Vimeo Help Guide

Vimeo’s own help centre, gathered into one screen-reader-friendly document

2026-07-31

Vimeo Help Guide

This guide gathers Vimeo’s official help centre. The text was taken from help.vimeo.com on 31 July 2026 and is Vimeo’s own; nothing has been summarised or rewritten.

Vimeo runs in a browser, in apps for iPhone, iPad and Android, on televisions, and through Vimeo OTT and Vimeo on Demand for people selling what they make. All of those are covered as Vimeo documents them.

This guide is incomplete, and here is exactly how. The gathering run stopped at its own limit with 220 addresses still waiting, so there are articles Vimeo publishes that are not here. What is here is complete in itself: every article is Vimeo’s full text.

The sections are Vimeo’s own, taken from the trail at the top of each article, in alphabetical order with Miscellaneous last.

What was left out. The Developers category – the interface, the player toolkit, access tokens – is developer documentation, which this collection leaves out everywhere; 2 articles went on that account.

Illustrations do not survive as pictures; where one carried a description it is kept as a short italic note. Tables have become lists.

Headings run six deep at most. Level one is this title, level two is a section, level three is an article, and anything below that came from inside the article itself.

Account and billing

About auto-renewal for users located in Germany

The article explains how customers based in Germany may be opted out of auto-renewal for their subscriptions under the German Fair Customer Contracts Act (FCAA), and provides instructions on how to check and manage auto-renewal settings.

Is my subscription eligible for auto-renewal?

As per the German Fair Customer Contracts Act (FCCA), your annual subscription may be opted out of auto-renewal if it was not purchased for business purposes.

On February 10, 2023, we sent e-mails to confirm if your account was purchased on behalf of a business.

If you are a “Consumer” with an annual subscription that started on or after March 1, 2022, your plan has been opted out of auto-renewal. However, you can opt for a one-time renewal from your settings to prevent your subscription from lapsing. You will need to opt in every year.

How can I tell if my account has been opted out of auto-renewal?

You can check if your account is opted out of auto-renewal on your billing settings page under ’Renewal’.It will state that auto-renewal is off for your account.

Screenshot: A billing settings table with columns titled ‘Title’, ‘Account usage’, ‘Renewal’, and ‘Payment method’. Below the headers, a single row displays the message: ‘Auto-renewal is off’.

Read how to disable auto-renewal at How do I disable auto-renewal for my Vimeo subscription plan?

About contacting Vimeo Support and response times

This article explains how to contact the Vimeo Support team for assistance and provides an overview of our expected response times.

Vimeo provides written support to anyone around the clock, seven days a week. Paying subscribers can expect a first response within a few hours, depending on the subscription level.

  • Contact form
  • Messaging support
  • Phone support
  • Initial Response Times
  • Follow-up response rate
  • Contacting us for special circumstances
  • Keep in touch
  • Contact sales
  • OTT support

Contact form

To receive the fastest support possible:

  1. Make sure you are logged in to your Vimeo account.
  2. Click Contact us at the top of the help center (or the blue chat box in the lower right corner).
  3. Once you type in your query, our Digital Assistant will first look for an answer to your question in our help center.
  4. If it’s unsuccessful, our Digital Assistant will prompt you to create a ticket within the chatbot widget. Follow the prompts until you receive a confirmation with your ticket number.

💡Tip: Include as much detailed information as you can in the form’s Description field so we can better investigate your issue from the beginning. Consider using Vimeo Record to demonstrate your issue and share the link with us.

Messaging support for Live events

Advanced, Premium, and Enterprise customers have access to live chat support for livestreaming issues 24/7. The chat option can be found by clicking Support at the bottom of any of your live events’ management pages.

Phone support

We offer phone support to our Enterprise customers. If you have an Enterprise contract with us, you should have received your phone PIN and instructions for contacting Enterprise Support during the onboarding process via email. If you cannot locate your phone PIN, contact your account manager to have it sent to you.

Initial Response Times

Enterprise

Enterprise accounts have access to 24/7 support via our contact form, Messaging, and phone. First response SLAs and phone hours vary depending on the support package you selected and the severity of your issue.

See the table below for Enterprise first response SLAs and phone hours:

    • Silver
  • Gold
  • Platinum
  • Minor issues
  • 6 business hours
  • 6 hours
  • 2 hours
  • Major issues
  • 3 business hours
  • 3 hours
  • 1 hour
  • Critical issues
  • 1 business hour
  • 1 hour
  • 30 minutes
  • Phone hours
  • 9 AM-9 PM ET or 9 AM-6 PM GMT* / 9 AM-9 PM AEST** *for customers based in Europe **for customers based in APAC
  • 24/7
  • 24/7
Self-serve plans

Our support team operates 24/7. Below are estimated response times for support tickets submitted through our Chatbot or contact form.

We also offer Messaging support for Business, Advanced, and Premium members.

  • Advanced:First response in 2 hours
  • Standard:First response in 6 hours
  • Starter:First response in 8 hours
  • Free:First response usually within 3 business days
Legacy self-serve plans

(Click here for more information about the transition to our new subscription model.)

  • Premium:First response in 2 hours
  • Business:First response in 4 hours
  • Pro:First response in 6 hours
  • Plus:First response in 8 hours
  • Basic:First response usually within 3 business days

Follow-up response rate

Follow-up response times may be longer than our first response time. Priority is assigned based on your plan as well as the nature of the issue.

Particularly complicated issues that require further investigation are often reassigned to a product specialist. Our specialists are trained to resolve issues as quickly as possible, but follow-up responses and resolutions can still take multiple days, especially if a given issue requires input from other teams, such as our developers.

Contacting us for special circumstances

Account owner is deceased or incapacitated

In the unfortunate event of the death or incapacity of a Vimeo member, Vimeo may, upon request of an appropriate person, and as required or permitted by law, deactivate or transfer the member’s Vimeo account. If you would like to read more about our policy or to submit a request, please visit our Deceased and Incapacitated User Policy Page.

Reporting a security vulnerability

If you are a security researcher who has found a vulnerability in one of our products, please report it here.

Keep in touch

The best way to stay current with news about Vimeo is to read our blog. You can also subscribe to ourstatus page for alerts on service outages.

Contact sales

If you are interested in Vimeo Enterprise, contact our sales team via the form on our Enterprise page. A representative will assess your needs further and determine the best package for you. Note that Vimeo Support cannot connect you to a sales representative via support contact channels.

If you have a question that was not answered here, please send our friendly support team a note via our Contact Form. Your feedback helps us continue to work better for you.

OTT support

Refer to the Vimeo OTT support article to know more.

About custom metadata fields for Enterprise videos

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Custom metadata fields let administrators define a structured schema — required fields, controlled vocabularies, defaults — that automatically applies to every video in scope, so every contributor uploads to the same standard. This article describes how the schema is configured, what field types are supported, how contributors fill values in, how mandatory fields block public sharing, and how to bulk-edit, backfill, filter, and surface non-compliant videos.

  • What to know before using custom metadata
  • Field types and required vs. optional
  • How an admin creates a custom metadata field
  • How contributors fill in custom metadata
  • Mandatory fields and public sharing
  • Bulk edit, backfill, and the admin compliance view
  • Filtering videos by custom metadata
  • API access
  • Frequently asked questions

What to know before using custom metadata

  • Plan requirement: custom metadata is included with Vimeo Enterprise at no extra charge. It is not included with Vimeo Custom.
  • Where it is configured:
  • For organizations with Workspaces, custom metadata is configured and enforced at the Workspace level. Each Workspace defines its own schema. See How to edit my Workspace’s settings.
  • For organizations without Workspaces, custom metadata is configured and enforced at the organization level.
  • Who can manage fields: only Workspace Administrators, Organization Owners, and Organization Administrators can create, edit, or delete custom metadata fields.
  • Who can fill values: any user with upload or edit access to a video can fill in custom metadata values on that video, at upload time or later from the video settings page.

Field types and required vs. optional

The following field types are supported:

  • Text — free-text input.
  • Integer — whole numbers.
  • Dropdown — single-select from a controlled vocabulary (allowed values).
  • Multi-select — multiple selections from a controlled vocabulary.
  • Boolean — true / false.
  • Date — a calendar date.

Each field can be marked required or optional. Dropdown and multi-select fields support up to 20 allowed values per field.

How an admin creates a custom metadata field

  1. Navigate to your Workspace (or Organization, if no Workspaces are configured) settings and open the Custom metadata section.
  2. Select Add field and configure:
  • Field name and (optional) description.
  • Field type (text, integer, dropdown, multi-select, boolean, or date).
  • For dropdown and multi-select: enter the allowed values (up to 20).
  • Mark as Required if it must be filled before a video can be shared publicly.
  • Default value (applied to new uploads).
  1. On the next step, choose how to handle existing videos:
  • Choose a backfill value for existing videos. This can differ from the default applied to new uploads.
  • Decide whether to override videos that already have a value for this field, or leave their existing values untouched.
  1. Save the field. It immediately becomes available on the video settings page for every video in scope.

You can edit a field’s name, description, allowed values, default, or required flag at any time. You can also delete a field — deleting removes it from the schema; videos retain their previously entered values unless you backfill or replace them. Changing a field’s type is not supported for most type combinations.

How contributors fill in custom metadata

Custom metadata fields appear in a dedicated Custom metadata section on each video’s settings page, dynamically rendered from your schema. Contributors can fill values at upload time or anytime later from the video settings page.

Required fields are clearly marked. The video can be saved without them, but it cannot be shared publicly until they are completed (see below).

Mandatory fields and public sharing

When a contributor attempts to share a video publicly while one or more required fields are still empty, those fields are highlighted in red and the share action is blocked until all required values are provided. This applies to all public-share surfaces (public links, embeds, social, showcases).

Private sharing within the Workspace or Organization is not blocked by missing mandatory fields.

Bulk edit, backfill, and the admin compliance view

  • Bulk edit: from the admin settings page, administrators can bulk-edit custom metadata across multiple videos in one action — setting, replacing, or clearing values.
  • Backfill at field creation: when adding a new field, choose a backfill value and whether to override existing videos that already have a value for that field.
  • Admin compliance view: a dedicated section in admin settings lists all videos missing one or more mandatory fields. Use it to clean up legacy content without cluttering the main library.

Filtering videos by custom metadata

Once fields are defined, you can filter your library and search results by custom field and value (for example, Department = Marketing). Multi-select fields filter on any selected value; boolean and date fields filter on exact match.

API access

All custom metadata operations are available via the Vimeo API:

  • Create, read, update, and delete custom metadata field definitions.
  • Get and set custom metadata values on video objects programmatically.

For developer documentation, see Vimeo Developers.

Frequently asked questions

Can I require certain custom fields before a video can be shared?

Yes. Mark a field as required, and videos cannot be shared publicly until all required fields are completed.

What field types are supported?

Text, integer, dropdown, multi-select, boolean, and date. Dropdown and multi-select support controlled vocabularies of up to 20 allowed values per field.

Can I edit or delete a custom field after creating it?

Yes. You can edit the name, description, allowed values, default, and required flag at any time. Changing the field type is not supported for most combinations. Deleting a field removes it from the schema; existing videos keep their previously entered values unless you backfill or replace them.

Can I set a different default value for new videos vs. existing videos during backfill?

Yes. The default value (applied to new uploads) and the backfill value (applied to existing videos) are configured independently in the two-step field creation flow.

What happens if I remove an option from a dropdown or multi-select?

You will see a warning before the change is applied. If you continue, any videos that had that option selected will no longer have it.

What happens if I rename a dropdown or multi-select option?

All videos using that option are automatically updated with the new name.

Can I use custom metadata to drive automation (auto-categorize, trigger approvals)?

Automation rules driven by custom metadata are not part of this release. You can build the same logic yourself today using the Vimeo API.

About Data Residency with Vimeo Enterprise

Vimeo is committed to providing customers with a secure and flexible video hosting solution that meets the needs of customers with specific data residency requirements. To support organizations that prioritize storing data within the European Union (EU), we now offer EU Data Residency. This is an optional feature that allows Enterprise customers to store video content on servers located within the EU.

  • How does EU Data Residency work?
  • How to enable EU Data Residency
  • Next steps

How does EU Data Residency work?

With EU Data Residency, your video content is stored on servers within the EU, specifically in Germany and Belgium. While we continue expanding EU-based storage capabilities, the following types of data are currently stored within the EU:

  • Stored in the region
  • Stored outside the region
  • Video source files and transcoded versions Transcripts and captions Search index Video thumbnails User profile pictures Live streams
  • Video metadata Vimeo user profiles Enterprise account information Analytics and logs Notifications, comments, and interactions

To take advantage of EU Data Residency, your team must access your Vimeo account through a custom subdomain (e.g., yourcompany.vimeo.work). This subdomain provides a dedicated and secure access point for your team, ensuring that videos stored in your account are stored within the EU.

Read about using Custom Subdomains with Vimeo Enterprise at ‘How to set up a custom subdomain for my Vimeo Enterprise account’.

How to enable EU Data Residency

To enable EU Data Residency for your Enterprise account, contact your Vimeo Success Team. They will guide you through the setup process, which includes:

  1. Confirming your desired subdomain (e.g., yourcompany.vimeo.work).
  2. Enabling EU Data Residency:This will ensure all new video uploads are stored within the EU.
  3. Accessing your account: Use your custom subdomain (e.g., yourcompany.vimeo.work) to log in.

What happens next

After you’ve enabled EU Data Residency:

  • New videos you upload will be stored in the EU.
  • All of your existing data will remain stored in EU.
  • Videos stored in the EU can be played back globally unless restricted by your video privacy settings.
  • Your Vimeo Enterprise account remains unchanged—you will not need to create a new account.
  • Read more about the experience of switching over to custom subdomains at How to set up a custom subdomain for my Vimeo Enterprise account

About disabling SSO for certain members on my team

It is recommended that all users in your organization use SSO for security purposes. However, you can disable specific users from logging in with SSO if they do not have SSO login credentials with your IdP, like a contractor or a service account.

Reach out to your Account Manager or the Support team with the email address of the user that you’d like to disable SSO. In the future, you can also reach out to re-enable SSO for one of these users.

About managing your Vimeo profile page

Your Vimeo profile is what viewers see when they click on the profile photo displayed on one of your videos. This article discusses how to manage your profile page and the various customization options available.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: When an account is converted to a Workspace, the ability to manage the Profile Page is lost. For more information, visit Troubleshooting: I can’t visit my Profile Page after becoming a Workspace

  • How to access my Vimeo profile page
  • Basic profile information overview
  • About adding for-hire information to my profile
  • About creating a custom URL for my profile page
  • How to add a cover video to the top of my profile
  • How to remove or replace my cover video
  • How to choose which videos are shown on my profile
  • How do I switch between horizontal-only and masonry grid layouts?
  • How can I view profile videos?
  • Can I hide my profile page?

How to access my Vimeo profile page

You can customize your profile page for cohesive branding. Below is the profile associated with the Vimeo Staff account:

Screenshot: Vimeo staff profile page

To access your profile page, follow the steps below:

  1. Select your profile photo in the upper right corner of the page.
  2. Below your name, choose View profile.

Basic profile information overview

On the left side of your profile, you will see the following basic information fields.

  • Profile pictures (recommended dimensions are 600x600)
  • Account Name
  • Location
  • Pronouns
  • Add bio (2000 characters max)
  • Add email
  • Add link (Available for Plus and above)
  • Enter the profile URL from that account and the link will display your username for that account. You can also enter your website URL.
  • Up to five (5) will be displayed before visitors are prompted to View all which will expand the panel to show all of your listed links.

Edit a field by clicking on it, making a change, then clicking out of it. Screenshot: Profile panel with mouse hovering over fields to edit.

About adding for-hire information to my profile

Underneath your basic information fields are the following fields that you can fill out related to your employment availability status.

  • For hire status (Available for Plus and above): Let others know if you’re available to be hired. You can further edit the specific roles you specialize in and projects you are interested in. Selecting “No” will hide this section from your profile.
  • For hire rate: Choose your rate range. You can opt to hide this on your profile by clicking the eyeball icon.
  • Clients: List out clients who have hired you in the past, separated by a comma. You can opt to hide this on your profile by clicking the eyeball icon.
  • Collaborators: Other users that you’ve added credits for in your videos will be listed here.
  • Activity: Other information or content within your account including:
  • Your public or password-protected showcases (Note: viewers need the password to enter the showcase)
  • Followers
  • Who you’re following
  • Other collections
  • Membership tier
  • How long you’ve been a member
  • The last time you were active on Vimeo

About creating a custom URL for my profile page

If you have a paid account on Vimeo, you can create a custom URL (like vimeo.com/staff) for your profile page. To do so, head to the Profile tab in your account settings and scroll down to Vimeo URL.

Note that custom URLs can only include letters and numbers.

How to add a cover video to the top of my profile

You can add a customcover videoto the top of your Vimeo profile. It can be an entire video or just a clip, and it will play silently on loop.

To add a cover video to your Vimeo profile, follow these steps:

  1. Click Add a cover videoat the top of the page.
  2. Choose a video - private or public - that you’d like to feature on your profile. If you know the video’s name you can search for it using the bar at the top of the module.
  3. Click Next. You will see this screen: Screenshot: Cover video editor
  4. Drag and drop the crop rectangle vertically to choose which portion will show on your page.
  • Note: This crop of your video has a max aspect ratio of 1:3:33 (eg. 1920x540), but will change based on the width of the browser being used to view your profile.
  1. If you’d like to trim your video so only a clip of it loops on your profile, click and drag the blue in and out indicators below the player. If you want the whole video to play, don’t do anything.
  2. Click Done.

How to remove or replace my cover video

If you ever want to change or remove your cover video, follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to your profile page by selecting your profile icon in the upper right corner after logging into Vimeo.
  2. In the upper right corner, select either Replace to open the module and choose a different video, or Remove to remove the cover video (don’t worry, this won’t delete your video from your account). Screenshot: Remove and replace options highlighted

⚠️Note: Cover videos are supported on most desktop browsers but are not supported on mobile browsers.

How to choose which videos are shown on my profile

By default, all of your public videos will be added to your profile page automatically. To disable this setting and customize the videos that show up on your profile, follow these steps:

  1. Hover your cursor between your video rows and select Add video. Screenshot: Add video and create section options on the profile page
  2. In the lower-left corner of the module that opens, toggle off Automatically add public videos.
  3. Under My public videos, click the checkbox next to each video you want to add to your profile. You can also select videos from the Credited videostab, which contains videos that another person has credited you in. Screenshot: Pop-up to select videos to add to profile page
  4. To remove a video from your profile page, hover your cursor over it and click the slash symbol in the upper left corner of the video preview. It will not be deleted from your account.

How do I switch between horizontal-only and masonry grid layouts?

To display your entire profile, you have the option to use a horizontal-only grid layout or a masonry grid that supports vertical and square formats. You can switch between the two layouts using the overlay menu in the lower right corner. This menu also includes a preview icon, allowing you to see your profile from another user’s point of view.

Screenshot: Grid view on profile page highlighted

Note: At this time, it’s not possible to add new videos and sections if you are in the masonry view. Switch to the grid view to add these to your profile.

How can I view profile videos?

You can view videos directly from the profile page. Click on the video you want to watch and it will expand across your screen. The title and description will appear to the right of the player. You can click into the next or previous video using the buttons below the player.

To return to the profile page, click the X in the upper right corner of the screen.

Screenshot: Pop-up of profile video when clicked on

Can I hide my profile page?

  • You can hide your profile page by enabling Private Mode on your account. This feature requires a Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise plan.
  • You can also toggle off visibility by navigating to your account settings > Profile > General and toggling off Allow others to see your profile.

About member roles on Vimeo

This feature requires a paid plan.

When you invite members to join you on Vimeo, you can assign roles to determine what each member can see and do. This article explains each role so you can choose the right ones for your members.

  • Roles on Vimeo
  • Folder and video access
  • Full role comparison

Roles on Vimeo

Roles define what members can (and can’t) do. Vimeo offers the following roles:

  • Viewer
  • Viewers can access content that has been shared with them and can be granted Can view or Can comment permission only. They cannot edit or make changes to videos they have access to.
  • Contributor
  • Contributors can access content that has been shared with them and can be granted Can view , Can comment , or Can edit permission. They can also upload, create, edit, and share their own videos and showcases.
  • Admin
  • Admins can access all content on the account, including videos created by other members, and have Can manage access by default. They can also use all features and tools, manage settings, brand kits, and add and remove members. They cannot handle billing or change the plan.
  • Owner
  • There is only one owner. This person has full control, including accessing all content with Can manage access, and managing billing, plans, brand kits, and all account settings, including connected social accounts and API integrations.
Additional roles on Enterprise plans
  • Contributor Plus
  • Contributor Plus members can do everything contributors can do, plus create and manage events, brand kits, and interactive videos.

Additional notes for Enterprise accounts:

  • For Enterprise plans that include multiple workspaces, there is also an organization owner and organization admins. Read more at About user roles and permissions for Organizations and Workspaces
  • If you have a large number of users that you’d like to grant the Viewer role, you can provide us with a CSV of their email addresses so we can add them for you. To do this, contact your account manager.
  • You can also grant viewer access by specifying a domain for SSO. Viewers that you grant access to via SSO will not receive an invite email.
Additional roles on legacy plans

On Pro, Business, and Premium plans, there is one additional role:

  • Uploader
  • Uploaders can only upload videos. They can do this from their upload page. Any videos an uploader adds are private, but admins or the owner can change the privacy after upload .

Folder and video access

What a member can actually do with shared content depends on which permissions they are granted.

When videos or folders are shared, members can be granted Can view, Can comment, Can edit, or Can manageaccess.

Admins and the owner can always have Can manage access to all content on the account, including content created by other members. All other roles need to be explicitly granted access to a folder or video.

Overview of folder sharing

When a folder is shared, the member it’s been shared with can access all the videos in the folder (and in any subfolders) with the permission they were granted at the folder level.

If you share a folder with someone and give them Can edit access, they can edit any videos inside the folder.

Contributors (and Enterprise members with the Contributor Plus role) can be granted the Can manage permission on folders. This allows them to create videos within a folder, delete videos, and create new subfolders.

Visit Folder role permissions for Enterprise accounts for a more detailed breakdown.

About monthly plan options on Vimeo

This article explains the available Vimeo subscription plans on a monthly payment schedule, detailing options for both our current and legacy plan offerings.

About the monthly plan subscription

Vimeo Starter, Standard, and Advanced plans are available on a monthly or yearly subscription basis.

Enterprise plans can only be purchased through our sales team. These custom plans are not available on a month-to-month payment basis.

If you are a long-time customer on our legacy suite of plans, Vimeo Plus is available monthly or yearly. Vimeo Pro, Business, and Premium plans are only available as yearly subscriptions.

However, these legacy plans (Plus, Pro, Business, and Premium) are no longer offered to new customers. If you have downgraded from a legacy plan, you will only be able to purchase one of our current plans if you choose to upgrade in the future.

To learn about the features of each plan and to purchase, visit our pricing page.

About Organizations and Workspaces

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

Organizations and Workspaces offer a structured approach to collaboration, centralizing user and content management while maintaining distinct work areas. This article provides a high-level overview of what Organizations and Workspaces are.

  • About Organizations
  • About Workspaces
  • How to add Organizations and Workspaces to your Enterprise account

About Organizations

An Organization is the top-level structure in Vimeo for Enterprise customers with Workspaces.

Organizations:

  • Provide a single, centralized view of all users, Workspaces, and billing under one umbrella.
  • Do not store content directly; instead, it lives inside Workspaces.

By managing membership, permissions, and payments at the Organization level, admins can govern multiple Workspaces and teams more easily.

About Workspaces

A Workspace is a collaborative space within an Organization where teams create, manage, and share content.

Workspaces:

  • Can be set up for different brands, departments, or projects.
  • Keep users and content delineated and separate to provide greater data partitioning and security.

Workspaces provide each group with its own environment to organize videos, control permissions, and collaborate—while still being governed by the parent Organization. You can think of this as a “child account” of the Organization. Screenshot: An organizational chart illustrating an account’s structure. At the highest level is the “Organization,” which branches into “Workspace 1” and “Workspace 2.” Each of these workspaces then contains four identical sub-sections: “My Library,” “Team library,” “Showcases,” and “Events.”

How to add Organizations and Workspaces to your Enterprise account

If you are an existing Vimeo Enterprise client, contact your account manager for more information on how to add Organizations Workspaces to your account.

If you are not on a Vimeo Enterprise plan, visit Vimeo Enterprise for information on how to contact our sales team.

About recommended SSO configurations

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Vimeo Enterprise offers flexible SSO configuration options so you can manage user provisioning and authentication in whichever way you need.

This article discusses the various SSO configuration options available for Vimeo Enterprise, including user provisioning and authentication methods tailored for organizational needs.

  • SSO for everyone in your organization
  • Provision all your users with SCIM
  • Only for current members of your Vimeo account
  • Multiple domains for one identity provider
  • Multiple identity providers

SSO for everyone in your organization

If you’d like everyone with your company email address to log into your Vimeo account with SSO, we recommend the following settings:

  • Set up a SAML connection
  • Claim your company domain
  • Enable JIT Provisioning

The next time your users go to log in with Vimeo, they will be redirected to your IdP login gate and provisioned to your Vimeo account. We also recommend setting up Vimeo as a gallery app using IdP-Initiated SSO so that your users can easily access it.

Provision all your users with SCIM

If you’d like to allow users to be provisioned and de-provisioned from Vimeo automatically based on the up-to-date members of your organization, we recommend the following settings:

  • Set up a SAML connection
  • Create a SCIM API app
  • Claim a domain

Claiming a domain is a critical step when configuring SSO for your enterprise on Vimeo, as it ensures a seamless and secure user management experience.

When a domain is claimed, any Vimeo user with an email address matching that domain is automatically recognized as part of your enterprise. By claiming your domain, you can simplify user provisioning, maintain tighter control over team membership, and reduce friction for your employees when setting up SSO.

⚠️Note: Not all IdPs offer SCIM, so check with your IdP if you can leverage this feature.

Only for current members of your Vimeo account

If you’d only like to allow users already on your Vimeo account to log in with SSO and not set up automatic provisioning, we recommend the following settings:

  • Set up a SAML connection
  • Enable Team-based SSO
  • Alternatively, but optionally, you can set up SCIM and provision users granularly on the IdP side.

To provision new users to your account with Team-Based SSO, you should send each of them an email invite. Claiming a domain and enabling JIT provisioning is not recommended in this use case, as only your users who are invited manually will log in with SSO.

Multiple domains for one identity provider

If your company uses one IdP but manages multiple domains, you can support all your users with your single Vimeo Enterprise account.

You can set up one IdP with multiple claimed domains. Therefore, when a user goes to log into vimeo.com, all users with all your claimed domains in their email addresses will be redirected to the IdP login gate your organization uses.

  • Set up a SAML connection
  • Claim your desired amount of domains
  • Enable JIT provisioning

Multiple identity providers

If your company has multiple IdPs and you need to set up multiple SAML connections, you can support all your users with your single Vimeo Enterprise account.

You can set up multiple IdPs with different claimed domains for each of them. Therefore, when a user goes to log into vimeo.com, they will be redirected to the IdP login gate for the SAML connection you created which has claimed their domain. We recommend the following settings:

  • Set up a SAML connection

  • Claim a domain

  • Set up a second SAML connection

  • Claim a second domain

  • Set up a second SAML connection

  • Claim a second domain (Continue for all your SAML connections)

  • Enable JIT provisioning

For a more advanced configuration, you can also set up multiple IdPs where up to one account uses team-based or SCIM-based SSO.

  • Set up a SAML connection
  • Don’t claim a domain
  • Set up a second SAML connection
  • Claim a domain
  • Set up a third SAML connection
  • Claim another domain (Continue for all your SAML connections)
  • Enable JIT provisioning
  • Enable team-based SSO

In this case, users with a claimed domain will be redirected to the IdP corresponding to their claimed domain. Users on your team without a claimed domain will be redirected to IdP login gate for the third SAML connection.

What is the Free plan on Vimeo?

The Free plan is unpaid and offers limited access to Vimeo tools and features. Only one seat is available for Free plans assigned to you (the account Owner).

What’s included in the Free plan?

The Free plan includes:

  • No ads before, after, or on your video
  • 4K, HDR, & Dolby Vision support
  • Playback speed controls
  • Limited video-making & editing tools, including templates, add text and sticker animations and trimming tools
  • Screen and webcam recordings up to 30 minutes each
  • GIF maker and embed GIFs in the email (Gmail only)
  • Create folders and subfolders
  • Basic viewer analytics
  • Native publishing across social channels
  • Embed videos anywhere
  • Create up to three (3) video showcases, one (1) channel, and one (1) group
  • The ability to download converted files

Our pricing page shows more information about the Free plan and compares it with others available.

How many videos can I upload or create on a Free plan?

When you create a Free account, you may upload or create up to 1 GB of content for the account’s lifetime, unless you upgrade.

⚠️Note: If you created your Vimeo account before June 17, 2024, you may have different video storage limitations on the Free plan. Check your sign-up date in the upper left-hand corner of your account settings or the lower left corner of your homepage or library to track your available video storage.

These video storage limitations are in place for the lifetime of the free account and do not reset or renew. After you reach the free video limit, upgrade your account to upload or create more videos.

Will my Free plan ever expire?

A free plan on Vimeo stays free forever. If you follow our guidelines and log in periodically, your account will remain active.

We consider accounts not used for a full year inactive and reserve the right to remove inactive accounts.

We’ll notify you in advance if your account is in danger of deletion due to inactivity and you’ll have an opportunity to reactivate it.

About types of provisioning

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Using SSO with Vimeo Enterprise, you can provision users in several ways depending on your use case and needs.

This article discusses various methods of user provisioning with Vimeo Enterprise using SSO, including Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning, team-based access, and SCIM integration for user management.

  • JIT Provisioning
  • Team-based
  • SCIM

JIT Provisioning

Just-In-Time (JIT) Provisioning allows users to be added to your account as soon as they successfully authenticate with your IdP for the first time.

  • For example, if you claim your company’s email domain for a SAML connection, all users with that domain in their email will be redirected to that IDP login gate, where they will authenticate and be provisioned to Vimeo after their first successful login.
  • Additionally, if you set up Vimeo as a gallery app within a page in your IdP listing all the apps your users have access to, all users who access Vimeo using IdP-initiated SSO will be provisioned to Vimeo after their first login.
  • Finally, JIT provisioning can also be enabled to automatically provision users to your account after they authenticate using your test URL, linked within the SAML connection modal.

To set up JIT provisioning, ensure you’ve enabled the JIT provisioning flag. You can also request your company’s email domain be verified for your SAML connection. As soon as the domain is verified, users with that domain will be redirected to log in with SSO using the corresponding SAML connection.

If there have been users manually removed from your team, you can toggle on the Allow reprovisioningtool on the SSO settings page to allow them to be reprovisioned automatically with JIT.

Team-based

Team-based SSO allows only users who are already on your account to log in with SSO. This option is ideal for accounts of small teams of users if many other people in your company want to continue logging into their separate Vimeo accounts without SSO. Team-based SSO does not provide a way to automatically provision users from your company. If you use Team-based SSO, users would have to be manually invited to your account in order to access it.

SCIM

SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) is an open standard that allows you to automatically provision users to Vimeo without requiring them to log in or be invited to Vimeo. SCIM also ensures your user memberships stay up to date and allows you to send push groups.

SCIM relies on an API connection that connects your IDP to Vimeo and talks to each other in the background. When enabling SCIM, all your current users will be provisioned at once after they are pushed to Vimeo. Then, when a new employee joins the company, they will automatically be created in your account on Vimeo. When an employee leaves the company, they will be removed from your Vimeo account without you having to manually remove them.

Only account owners can set up SCIM.

About user roles and permissions for Organizations and Workspaces

This article discusses the different user roles and their permissions within an Organization.

  • Organization roles and permissions
  • Workspace roles and permissions

Organization roles and permissions

There are three types of roles in an Organization: Organization Owner, Organization Admin,and Organization Member.

Organization Owner

When an Enterprise account is migrated to Workspaces, the Account Owner becomes an Organization Owner.

Their permissions include:

  • Access to the Organization’s Billing and Settings
  • Access to all of the Workspaces within the Organization.
  • Can change all settings, invite users, and view analytics in the Organization and all Workspaces.
  • The ability to allocate AI Credits
  • Organization Owners are automatically added as Workspace Admins to each Workspace within an Organization and cannot be removed.
Organization Admins

An Organization Admin has the second-highest level of permissions within the entire Organization.

Their permissions include:

  • Access to the Organization’s Billing and Settings
  • Managing all users, Workspaces, data, and settings across the Organization.
  • Access to all of the Workspaces within the Organization.
  • Organization Admins are automatically added as Workspace Admins to each Workspace within an Organization and cannot be removed.
Organization Members

Organization members are team members who can be assigned to Workspaces. They can be assigned to one or more Workspaces with these roles:

  • Workspace Admin
  • Workspace Contributor Plus
  • Workspace Contributor
  • Workspace Viewer

Learn how to add team members to your Organization at How to add and manage team members in my Organization.

Workspace roles and permissions

There are multiple roles in a Workspace: Workspace Admin, Workspace Contributor Plus, Workspace Contributor,and Workspace Viewer.

Workspace Admin

Can view and manage all videos, folders, team members, analytics, and live events (for Enterprise accounts with Live Events) on the account.

Workspace Contributor Plus

Can view, comment, upload, edit, share videos, and view clip analytics inside folders that have been shared with them. Additionally, they can use advanced creation tools and create and manage live events (for Enterprise accounts with Live Events).

Workspace Contributor

Can view, comment, upload, edit, share videos, and view clip analytics inside folders that have been shared with them.

Workspace Viewer

Can view and comment on videos that have been shared with them.

Learn how to add team members to your Workspace at How to add members and manage permissions in my Workspace.

About Vimeo accounts created via Facebook

It is no longer possible to create a new Vimeo account via Facebook credentials.

If you joined Vimeo via Facebook, you will need to set a password for your Vimeo account before performing any actions on the site that require a Vimeo password, such as deleting videos, deleting your account, or signing in from different devices.

This step is required to ensure that you’ll be able to maintain access to your Vimeo account separately from Facebook in the future. Once you set a password, you won’t need to be logged in to Facebook to use any Vimeo feature.

To set a password:

  1. Go to your account settings.
  2. Click Password on the left sidebar.
  3. Once there, click on the Change Password link.
  4. You will be prompted to enter a new password and confirm it.

Accepted payment methods overview

This article provides a comprehensive reference guide to all accepted payment methods for Vimeo plans, VOD, and purchases, detailing specific card types and any geographical or purchase-type exceptions.

  • What payment methods do you accept?
  • Do you accept checks, invoices, or purchase orders?
  • I keep getting an error when trying to make a purchase

What payment methods do you accept?

We currently accept the following methods for all plans, VOD, and purchases:

  • Visa
  • MasterCard
  • American Express
  • Discover
  • JCB
  • *PayPal
  • PayPal is not supported in the following scenarios:
  • Add-on seat purchases
  • Any purchase made from India

We currently accept the following international payment methods:

  • Carte Bleue
  • CartaSi
  • Dankort
  • China UnionPay

Through our Vimeo and Vimeo Create apps, you may also use iTunes/App Store or Google Play for purchases. However, if you are looking to purchase multiple seats, you will need to do so via vimeo.com, as multiple-seat purchases are not supported on our apps.

Do you accept checks, invoices, or purchase orders?

We cannot accept checks, invoices, or purchase orders for Vimeo memberships.

I keep getting an error when trying to make a purchase

If you are having payment issues, see our troubleshooting guide.

Add key contacts to manage Enterprise account payment details

The primary contact listed for a Custom or Enterprise account can add, edit, or remove additional key contacts to receive invoices.

If you are the primary contact and want to add a key contact to your account:

  1. Log into the payment portal.
  2. Navigate to the top right of the portal’s site header and select Settings.
  3. Click Account Information.
  4. Under the Contacts section, click on +Add a Contact.
  5. Once their details have been added, click Submit.

If you’d like to send invoices to other members of your team who do not need portal access:

  1. Navigate to the top right of the portal’s site header and select Settings.
  2. Click Account Information.
  3. Under Account Details, add any additional email addresses to which invoices should be sent.
  4. Click Update Information. Screenshot: image2.png

Change the email address associated with your Vimeo OTT account

Change the email address associated with your Vimeo OTT account on Vimeo OTT’s Account Settings page.

  1. VisitAccount Settings.
  2. Enter the new email address in the Emailfield.
  3. Enter your current password in the box at bottom of the page and click Save. Screenshot: mceclip0.png
  4. Your previous email address will receive an email with further instructions on confirming your email address change.

⚠️ Note: In order for the updated settings on this page to take effect, you will need to enter your current password, and click Save.

If you are unable to change your email address after following these steps, please contact us

Changes to Vimeo Messages

In March 2026, the Vimeo team investigated the use of Messages. In addition to being a largely unused feature, it also introduced unnecessary complexity and risk. As a result, Vimeo is discontinuing the Messages feature used for direct messaging between users.

The Message button has been removed from user profile pages, and the Compose Message button has been removed from the Messages page. Because of these changes, it is no longer possible to send new direct messages to other Vimeo users.

You can still view your existing message history at messages for a limited time. A notice on the Messages page will also inform that Vimeo Messages will no longer be supported starting April 15, 2026.

On April 15, 2026, the Messages feature will be fully discontinued. At that time, the messages page and all message history will be permanently removed.

If there is information in your messages you would like to keep, we recommend saving it before this date.

Claiming a Domain

Claiming your company’s domain will allow you to ensure all the members of your organization with a company email are required to log in with SSO. With JIT provisioning, it will also force all your users to be provisioned to your Enterprise account after they’ve successfully authenticated. By claiming a domain, you can also ensure no other employees at your company can create new Vimeo accounts independently from your Enterprise account.

To force all users with your company’s domain to log in with SSO into your Enterprise account, you should claim your domain for your SAML connection and also enable JIT provisioning. You have to request your domain be verified by Vimeo before your domain can be claimed.

  1. Create a new SAML connection
  2. We recommend testing your SAML connection using the test URL to ensure SSO is working properly before claiming your domain and forcing all your employees to log in with SSO into Vimeo
  3. In the “Claim your domain” section, enter the domain you wish to claim and click “Request verification”. You must request verification using an email address that contains the domain you’re trying to claim.
  • If you’d like to request verification of a domain that does not match the email address of your account, submit a support ticket from an account with an email that contains the domain you are trying to claim.
  1. Vimeo will notify you once the domain has been claimed
  2. Once the domain has been claimed, all users with the domain in their email address will be required to log in with SSO.

If you need to add another domain to that SAML connection, you can easily request it to be added to your list of claimed domains. You can associate multiple domains with a single SAML connection.

💡Tip: You can also claim multiple domains for different IdPs.

If you need to remove your domain from a SAML connection, simply delete that domain from the list of claimed domains. After the domain has been removed, users with that domain will no longer be forced to sign in with SSO to your account. If you wish to remove the user entirely, you will have to manually remove the user from your team.

Common issues with setting up SAML

If you’ve set up your SAML connection but are getting an error message, there are several common issues you can easily troubleshoot. This article contains information about common SAML errors and how to troubleshoot them.

If you’re getting an error on your IdP

Access Not Granted to your Vimeo SAML App

You may not have been given access to the Vimeo SAML app you’ve set up in your IdP. Reach out to your IT team to ensure you’ve been given access to the Vimeo SAML app so you can log in.

Unauthorized Device

If your organization requires your device to be registered with the company in order to use SSO, you may get an error trying to access Vimeo from an unregistered device (like a personal computer or phone). This could also occur if your organization requires you to access your company network or VPN. Ensure you’re logging into Vimeo while abiding by all the rules of your organization in order to get access to Vimeo using SSO.e2q

If you’re getting an error on vimeo.com

Vimeo Entity ID & ACS URL copied incorrectly

Ensure that you copy and paste the Vimeo Entity ID & ACS URL correctly from Vimeo into your SAML app in your identity provider. You can use the clipboard icon to ensure you copy the entire value before pasting it in your IdP. You may have also swapped these values and pasted them in the incorrect fields - check out our articles for common IdPs to make sure you’re following the correct steps.

SAML attributes not mapped correctly

Ensure that you’ve set up the correct SAML attributes for Vimeo using the following exact syntax:

  • firstName
  • lastName
  • email
  • groups (optional)

If you’re not able to set up custom attributes in your IdP, you can map your fixed attributes to Vimeo’s necessary attributes using the attribute mapping section in the Admin SSO Console. Creating an attribute mapping on Vimeo is optional.

IdP certificate not pasted correctly

Ensure that you’ve uploaded or pasted the entire SAML certificate from your IdP. Your certificate must include the necessary header and footer.

You should also ensure that you upload the certificate file and not the full metadata file.

IdP sign-in URL not pasted correctly

Ensure that you’ve copied and pasted the correct sign-in URL from your IdP into Vimeo. Users will be redirected to this URL to authenticate using your IdP.

Provisioning set up incorrectly

Ensure that you’ve set up the correct provisioning settings for your use case. Read here about Recommended SSO Configurations. If users aren’t being provisioned, ensure you’ve either claimed the domain in their email, set up SCIM provisioning correctly, or manually invited them to the team.

Configure SCIM on Vimeo

Enterprise accounts with SSO enabled can use SCIM to create and manage team member accounts and user groups on Vimeo. SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) is a standard for automating the exchange of user identity information between identity domains or IT systems.

This guide will walk through how to set up a SCIM connection with Vimeo for your organization; you can check configuring with IdP (Identity Provider) Okta and Azure. The instructions for configuring with other providers (OneLogin, GSuite, Azure, etc.) should be similar.

If you’re an existing Vimeo Enterprise customer and don’t have SCIM, please contact your Account Manager for more information. If you are not a Vimeo Enterprise customer yet and are interested in SCIM, please contact us.

  • Glossary
  • Why use SCIM?
  • Prerequisites
  • Get an API Token from Vimeo

Glossary

  • SCIM - System for Cross-domain Identity Management is a standard for automating the exchange of user identity information between identity domains, or IT systems.
  • Identity provider (IdP or IDP) is a system entity that creates, maintains, and manages identity information for principals and also provides authentication services to dependent applications within a federation or distributed network.
  • Service provider (SP) - is usually a SaaS application, like Vimeo, that needs a subset of information from IdP.

Why use SCIM?

If you’re new to SCIM, here are a few examples of how it can be helpful and how your IdP (Identity Provider, such as Okta, OneLogin, GSuite, etc.) can interact with your Vimeo account:

  • Push Users: When an employee joins your organization, they will automatically have a Vimeo account created with respective group membership information and personalized content.
  • Deactivate Users: When an employee leaves your organization, their account is automatically deactivated to ensure they don’t have access to your Vimeo account, and that they’re not taking any of the seats you’re paying for.
  • Update User Attributes: When an employee changes their name or email address, their respective Vimeo account will get updated immediately. Also, When you’ve reassigned an employee to a different department and changed their group membership, their group membership is immediately updated on the Vimeo account, which updates what content they can access on Vimeo.
  • Push Groups:New groups created through Okta will also be created on Vimeo.
  • Import Users: New users created in Vimeo can be downloaded in the Import tab of the App and turned into new AppUser objects, for matching against existing Okta users.
  • Import Groups: New groups created in Vimeo can be downloaded in the Import tab of the App and turned into new AppUser objects, for matching against existing Okta groups.
  • In general, if you need to manage thousands of accounts, SCIM is the most practical way to do this.

Prerequisites

To use SCIM with your Vimeo account:

  • Your Vimeo account should have an Enterprise membership and SSO enabled.
  • SSO should be configured and enabled on the IdP side.
  • IdP must support SCIM version 2; Vimeo does not support SCIM version 1.

When setting up SCIM provisioning for an Enterprise account, Vimeo takes extra precautions to ensure existing Vimeo users being provisioned to the Enterprise account are aware of their transition to a new team. If the existing user’s account does not have a domain claimed by the Enterprise, they will be required to accept a verification email before they can be successfully provisioned to the team. During this process, their status will appear as ‘Pending’ on the team management page until they accept the invitation. However, if the user’s email domain has already been claimed by the enterprise, no verification is required, as the domain claim confirms their affiliation with the company. This ensures a secure and seamless SCIM provisioning experience.

Get an API Token from Vimeo

You will need to get an API token from Vimeo to get started. You must log in to the Owner account in order to do this; team members cannot access API.

  1. Open developer.vimeo
  2. Select Get startedor New app.
  3. Fill out the form, then select Create App. ⚠️Note: For the question asking if other users will access your app, select No.
  4. Scroll down to the Generate an access token section.
  5. Select Authenticated (you).
  6. Select Private, then Scim scopes.
  7. Click Generate. Screenshot: image4.png
  8. Copy or save the newly generated token somewhere, such as a note-taking application. Do not skip this step; you will need it later.Screenshot: image5.png

Please work with your Vimeo success team to enable SCIM on your Vimeo Enterprise account, and contact scim-support@vimeo.com if you have further technical questions related to SCIM.

FAQ: Consolidating existing Vimeo accounts into my new Vimeo Enterprise account

This article applies to customers onboarding to Vimeo Enterprise. If you are a self-serve customer (Free, Starter, Standard, Advanced) looking to migrate content to another self-serve account, work with our Support team to complete this.

If you have one or more existing Vimeo accounts associated with your domain, our implementation team can help you consolidate them into your Vimeo Enterprise account. This article explains how this process works and what to expect when consolidating other Vimeo accounts into a single Vimeo Enterprise account.

  • Which accounts can be migrated to my new Vimeo Enterprise accounts?
  • Can my accounts be converted to Workspaces within an Enterprise Organization?
  • What will migrate into the new account?
  • What will NOT migrate into the new account?
  • Will my team members migrate?
  • What can I expect to see post-migration?
  • I’ve read this article and understand what migrates and what doesn’t. How do I proceed with consolidating my accounts?

Which accounts can be migrated to my new Vimeo Enterprise accounts?

Account consolidations typically apply only to paid Vimeo accounts. Here’s how we determine which accounts will migrate:

  1. Your Implementation Manager will provide you with a list of Vimeo accounts associated with your organization’s domain(s) so you can review and determine which accounts to consolidate.
  2. Vimeo will retain your original video IDs. This means that video links and embeds will continue to work post-migration.
  3. Our team will inform you of any videos that may be impacted by privacy hash enforcement, which impacts older embedded videos using the Unlisted privacy setting.
  4. After your approval, your Implementation Manager will complete the consolidation within two weeks.

Can my accounts be converted to Workspaces within an Enterprise Organization?

If you are interested in converting your existing Vimeo accounts into Workspaces under an Enterprise Organization account, contact your account manager for next steps.

What will migrate into the new account?

  • Video ID
  • Title
  • Description
  • Tags
  • Original Video Upload
  • Video Transcodes
  • Version History
  • Review Comments
  • User Comments
  • Transcripts/Captions
  • Interactive Elements
  • Interactivity Elements (chapters, cards, forms)
  • Associated Folders & Sub-folders
  • Privacy Settings / Embed Domain Restrictions
  • Thumbnail
  • Date Added
  • Vimeo Create Elements (non-editable)

What will NOT migrate into the new account?

  • Video Analytics
  • Upcoming Live Events
  • Associated Showcases/Channels/Portfolios
  • Player Embed Presets
  • Review Page URLs
  • Download URLs
  • API Apps
  • Vimeo Create Projects
  • Vimeo on Demand Pages
  • Videos with 0:00 duration
  • Deleted videos
  • Custom URLs

Will my team members migrate?

The Implementation Manager can provide a list of team members (if applicable) from the source accounts and, with your approval, transfer them to the Enterprise account.

What can I expect to see post-migration?

Here’s what you will see in your Enterprise account after the migration is completed:

  • A new folder will be created in your destination Enterprise account for each source account.
  • All folders from each source account will be copied as subfolders in the corresponding folder in the destination account.
  • The account owner of each source account will be added as a Contributor to the corresponding folder in the destination account.
  • All videos from each source account will be moved to the destination account and removed from the original source accounts..
  • Your videos will retain their original ID, ensuring links and embeds remain active.
  • Deleted or 0:00 duration videos will not be transferred to the Enterprise account

I’ve read this article and understand what migrates and what doesn’t. How do I proceed with consolidating my accounts?

When you are ready to proceed with consolidating your Vimeo accounts, contact your onboarding team to begin the process.

Are discounts available for non-profit organizations?

Vimeo currently offers discounts to non-profit organizations in the United States. Our support team cannot fulfill additional discount requests.
