Can I receive a Vimeo subscription for free?

Vimeo currently offers free trials for our paid memberships, excluding Enterprise. You can access this via our Upgrade page. Outside of this, our support team cannot fulfill requests for free access to paid Vimeo subscriptions.

Does Vimeo have any subscription discounts that work on renewals?

At this time, Vimeo’s promo codes are valid for one purchase only. We do not have any promotional codes for recurring or permanently discounted subscriptions.

Does Vimeo provide discounts to students and teachers?

Vimeo currently offers discounts to students and teachers located in the United States.

Vimeo provides a one-time discount promo code for your purchase. This promo code is available for verified teachers and students who have provided their email address.

Where can I read more about promotions and offers?

For other promotions and offers, we recommend opting in to the “Cool Deals” emails under Vimeo News Notification Settings.

FAQ: Lapsing from a paid account to a Basic account

Are you lapsing from Starter, Standard, or Advanced? Read this instead.

If you choose not to renew your Plus, Pro, Business, or Premium subscription on Vimeo and it expires, your account will downgrade to a Basic plan. This article answers the most common questions about lapsing to the Basic plan on Vimeo.

  • What features do I lose when I lapse to Basic?
  • What happens to my team members if I lapse to Basic?
  • How is video storage handled when my account lapses to Basic?
  • What is my weekly upload limit when my account lapses?
  • What happens to my stored source files when my account lapses?
  • How are privacy and embed settings impacted when my account lapses?
  • What happens to my collections when my account lapses?
  • Do I lose access to developer tools and the API if my account lapses?

What features do I lose when I lapse to Basic?

If your paid membership lapses to Basic, you will lose access to certain features, depending on the membership type:

  • Vimeo Premiumaccounts that lapse will lose access to all livestreaming features,Google Analytics, team collaboration, lead generation, priority conversion, VIP and chat support, advanced analytics, custom embed settings, automatic closed captions, domain-level privacy, Portfolios, Review Pages, SEO support for Showcases, and Vimeo On Demand.
  • Vimeo Business accounts that lapse will lose access to Google Analytics, team collaboration, lead generation, priority conversion, VIP support, advanced analytics, custom embed settings, automatic closed captions, domain-level privacy, Portfolios, Review Pages, SEO support for Showcases, and Vimeo On Demand.
  • Vimeo Pro accounts that lapse will lose access to priority conversion, VIP support, advanced analytics, custom embed settings, automatic closed captions, domain-level privacy, Portfolios, Review Pages, and Vimeo On Demand.
  • Vimeo Plus accounts that lapse to Basic will lose access to priority conversion, priority support, advanced analytics, custom embed settings, automatic closed captions, domain-level privacy, and the ability to set a password for videos.

What happens to team members on my account if I lapse to Basic?

If your account lapses to Basic, team members will no longer have access to the team account. However, they will retain their own free personal accounts that were created when they accepted the team invitation.

If you move back to a paid plan with multiple seats for team members, your team will regain access to the team account with data and access grants preserved.

How is video storage handled when my account lapses to Basic?

If you downgrade from a paid plan to Basic, your storage allowance will reflect the entitlements of your new plan. If your library is larger than the Basic plan’s 5 GB limit, some of your videos will be restricted until you either reduce your library size or upgrade to a plan with the necessary storage allowance.

Restricted videos are not deleted — they remain in your account and will reappear as fully accessible the moment your library fits inside the cap (whether by upgrading or by deleting other videos to free up space). However, while restricted:

  • The videos cannot be played, edited, or downloaded.
  • Their clip pages and embeds will stop working, and any links you have shared will no longer play.
Which of my videos count toward the limit?

All videos in your library count, regardless of their privacy setting — public, unlisted, and private videos all take up space against your plan’s allowance. Many customers are surprised by this: even videos that are not shared anywhere still count toward the cap.

To see your total usage, hover over the storage tracker in the bottom-left corner of your library. It reflects every video in the account.

Which of my videos get restricted first?

Videos are restricted in reverse upload order — newest first. If your library is over the cap:

  • Your most recent uploads are the first to become restricted.
  • Your oldest videos stay accessible for as long as the rest of your library fits within your plan’s allowance.
  • Restriction continues backwards through your library, one upload at a time, until what remains fits inside the cap.

If you delete videos to free up space, the next restricted video in line will be unlocked automatically as soon as there is enough room for it. This means deleting (or downloading-then-deleting) a few of your newest large uploads is usually the fastest way to bring an older video you want to keep back online — without needing to upgrade.

How do I get a restricted video back?

You have two options:

  • Upgrade to a plan with more storage at upgrade. If the new plan’s cap covers your full library, every restricted video is immediately unlocked, including its original links and embeds.
  • Reduce your library by deleting videos you no longer need. As soon as the remainder fits within the cap, the next restricted video in line is unlocked automatically.

You can check your current usage at any time in account settings, or in the lower-left corner of your library.

What is my weekly upload limit when my account lapses?

  • After your account lapses, you will have a weekly upload limit of 500MB up to 5GB total account storage.
  • If your total video storage exceeds 5GB, you will lose the ability to upload new content upon lapsing.
  • You can free up storage on your existing account by deleting some of your older videos, rough cuts, or backups until you are under the 5GB cap.

What happens to my stored source files when my account lapses?

  • Because storing source files is costly, we only offer that service to paying members. If your paid membership lapses to Basic, any source files stored on Vimeo will be deleted after 60 days and cannot be recovered.
  • The HD and SD versions of your videos will remain available.

How are privacy and embed settings impacted when my account lapses?

  • Videos set to the Unlisted and Embed only privacy settings will be switched to Private instead.
  • If your account is in Private Mode and you lapse, all your videos will be set to Private.
  • Videos with a password will keep the password until you change your settings, but passwords cannot be added to videos once you’re on a Basic account.
  • Any videos with player customizations will revert to the default player appearance options for Basic accounts.
  • If you have domain-level privacy set on your video, your embed privacy setting will be changed to “Nowhere.” You must change the setting to “Anywhere” to keep it embedded.
  • Your advanced settings will automatically be restored if you renew your paid membership. Any videos you haven’t modified since lapsing will return to how they were before your account lapsed to Basic.

What happens to my collections when my account lapses?

  • You will keep and be able to edit the groups, channels, and showcases you created as a paid member, but you will not be able to create new ones beyond the Basic limits.

Do I lose access to developer tools and the API if my account lapses?

  • Access to the Vimeo API, your account’s API apps, and authentication tokens will remain valid even if your membership status lapses or expires.
  • That said, you will no longer be able to use the API to access specific account features, such as retrieving direct file links or setting domain-level embed privacy.

FAQ: Lapsing from a paid account to a Free account

This article is for customers lapsing from Starter, Standard, or Advanced plans. If you are lapsing from Plus, Pro, Business, or Premium, read this instead.

Unsure which Vimeo plan type you have? Check “Membership” in the upper left corner of your account settings.

If you turn off auto-renewal for your Starter, Standard, or Advanced plan on Vimeo, your account will downgrade to the Free plan once your subscription expires. This article discusses what will change in your account when you cancel your subscription and downgrade to Free.

  • What features do I lose when I lapse to Free?
  • What happens to my team members if I lapse to Free?
  • What happens to my videos when my paid plan lapses to Free?
  • What happens to videos that team members uploaded to my account?
  • Do I get everything back if I restore to a paid plan?
  • How are privacy and embed settings impacted when my account lapses?
  • What happens to my collections when my account lapses?
  • Do I lose access to developer tools and the API if my account lapses?

What features do I lose when I lapse to Free?

You may not be able to add more videos to your account when you lapse to Free, depending on how much you uploaded while on a paid plan. Read more at How much video content can I store on my Vimeo account? In addition, the features you lose access to depend on which plan you were on before lapsing:

  • If you lapse from the Advanced plan:You will lose all features related to streaming virtual events, including broadcast tools, webinar hosting and registration, event analytics, live Q&A, polls, and audience chat, stream health monitoring, and marketing integrations (Constant Contact, Mailchimp, Hubspot, Campaign Monitor, Heap). Note that all videos that are archives of live events will move into our archive storage.
  • If you lapse from the Standard plan:You will lose access to stock media for video creation and editing, video and player branding options, custom call-to-actions & end cards, lead capture with custom forms, and Vimeo On Demand. Any VOD titles you have for sale or rental will no longer be available.
  • If you lapse from the Starter plan: You will lose access to player customization options, automatic closed captions and transcript editing, version history & video replacement, video chaptering & SEO, shared team workspaces, video review tools, password protection and unlisted link sharing, and advanced video analytics.

What happens to my team members if I lapse to Free?

When added to a team on your account, team members are provided their own free Vimeo account.

If your account lapses to Free, team members will no longer have access to the team account. However, they will retain their own free personal accounts.

If you move back to a paid plan with multiple seats for team members, your team will regain access to the team account with data and access grants preserved.

What happens to my videos when my paid plan lapses to Free?

If you downgrade from a paid plan to Free, your storage allowance will reflect the entitlements of your new plan. If your library is larger than the Free plan’s 1 GB limit, some of your videos will be restricted until you either reduce your library size or upgrade to a plan with the necessary storage allowance.

Restricted videos are not deleted — they remain in your account and will reappear as fully accessible the moment your library fits inside the cap (whether by upgrading or by deleting other videos to free up space). However, while restricted:

  • The videos cannot be played, edited, or downloaded.
  • Their clip pages and embeds will stop working, and any links you have shared will no longer play.
Which of my videos count toward the limit?

All videos in your library count, regardless of their privacy setting — public, unlisted, and private videos all take up space against your plan’s allowance. Many customers are surprised by this: even videos that are not shared anywhere still count toward the cap.

To see your total usage, hover over the storage tracker in the bottom-left corner of your library. It reflects every video in the account.

Which of my videos get restricted first?

Videos are restricted in reverse upload order — newest first. If your library is over the cap:

  • Your most recent uploads are the first to become restricted.
  • Your oldest videos stay accessible for as long as the rest of your library fits within your plan’s allowance.
  • Restriction continues backwards through your library, one upload at a time, until what remains fits inside the cap.

If you delete videos to free up space, the next restricted video in line will be unlocked automatically as soon as there is enough room for it. Deleting a few of your newest, largest uploads is usually the fastest way to bring an older video you want to keep back online — without needing to upgrade.

Deleting a restricted video is permanent. Unlike other videos, a restricted video you delete does not move to Recently deleted and cannot be recovered from there. Because restricted videos also cannot be downloaded, you cannot save a copy first — so only delete a restricted video if you are certain you no longer need it.

How do I get a restricted video back?

You have two options:

  • Upgrade to a plan with more storage at upgrade. If the new plan’s cap covers your full library, every restricted video is immediately unlocked, including its original links and embeds.
  • Reduce your library by deleting videos you no longer need. As soon as the remainder fits within the cap, the next restricted video in line is unlocked automatically. Remember that deleting a restricted video is permanent — it will not appear in Recently deleted.

You can check your current usage at any time in account settings, or in the lower-left corner of your library.

What happens to videos that team members uploaded to my account?

Videos your team members add are tied to the account, not the person who uploaded them. When the account lapses to the Free plan, those videos will remain with the owner’s account, either actively available or in archive storage as described above. They do not transition to the team member’s personal account.

Do I get everything back if I restore to a paid plan?

If you upgrade to a paid plan within a year of lapsing, any of your videos moved to our archive storage will be restored (please note that it may take some time for the videos to be moved from our archive storage back into your account).

How are privacy and player customization settings impacted when my account lapses?

A few settings will change when you lapse:

  • Videos set to the Unlisted and Embed only privacy settings will be switched to Private instead.
  • If your account is in Private Mode and you lapse, all your videos will be set to the Private setting.
  • Videos with a password will keep the password until you change your settings, but passwords cannot be added to videos once you’re on a Free account.
  • Any videos with player customizations will revert to the default player appearance options for Free accounts.
  • If you have domain-level privacy set on your video, your embed privacy setting will be changed to “Nowhere.” You must change the setting to “Anywhere” to keep it embedded.
  • Your custom settings will automatically be restored if you renew your paid membership. Any videos you haven’t modified since lapsing will return to how they were before your account lapsed to Free.

What happens to my collections when my account lapses?

You will keep and be able to edit the groups, channels, and showcases you created as a paid member, but you will not be able to create new ones beyond the limits in place for Free accounts.

Do I lose access to developer tools and the API if my account lapses?

Access to the Vimeo API, your account’s API apps, and authentication tokens will remain valid even if your membership status lapses or expires. However, you will no longer be able to use the API to access specific account features, such as retrieving direct file links or setting domain-level embed privacy.

FAQ: Managing mobile in-app subscriptions

This article provides answers to common questions about managing subscriptions purchased using a mobile app.

  • I purchased my Vimeo subscription in an app via my Apple or Google Play account. Can I manage that subscription on the Vimeo website?
  • How do I cancel my subscription if I purchased via Apple or Google?
  • If I delete the Vimeo app from my device, will that cancel my subscription?
  • If I delete my Vimeo account, will that cancel my subscription with Apple or Google?
  • Can I upgrade my subscription if it was purchased via Apple or Google Play?

I purchased my Vimeo subscription in an app via my Apple or Google Play account. Can I manage that subscription on the Vimeo website?

If you purchased your Vimeo subscription via your Apple or Google Play account in the Vimeo app, Vimeo Create app, Mevo app, or the Magisto app, you can only manage that recurring subscription in your Apple Account Subscriptions settings (for iOS) or in your Google Play Store Subscriptions (for Android).

You cannot manage your subscription on the Vimeo website if you purchased via Apple or Google. This is because the transaction did not occur on vimeo.com.

How do I cancel my subscription if I purchased via Apple or Google?

When you purchase a subscription via the mobile app, the transaction likely occurred either in the Apple App Store or Google Play, depending on your device type.

  • If you purchased on an iOS device, Apple provides detailed instructions for canceling in-app subscriptions purchased via Apple on its support site.
  • If you purchased on an Android device, Google provides detailed instructions for canceling in-app subscriptions purchased via Google on its support site.

If you cannot find your Vimeo subscription in your device’s subscription settings section, log into your Vimeo account on a web browser using the email associated with the account being billed and check your billing settings page for the option to cancel.

If I delete the Vimeo app from my device, will that cancel my subscription?

Deleting the app that you used to purchase your Vimeo subscription from your mobile device will not cancel your Vimeo subscription. This must be done directly via the platform you used to purchase your subscription as described above.

If I delete my Vimeo account, will that cancel my subscription with Apple or Google?

Deleting your Vimeo account does not affect your subscription status with Apple or Google. You must cancel directly via the platform you used to purchase your subscription as described above.

Can I upgrade my subscription if it was purchased via Apple or Google Play?

If you purchased your Vimeo subscription via Apple or Google Play and wish to upgrade, your ability to do so depends on which plan you previously purchased.

  • If you purchased Plus via the Vimeo app, you can upgrade to Pro via prompts in the Vimeo app or your device’s subscription management section. You cannot upgrade via vimeo.com.
  • If you purchased Pro, it is not possible to upgrade to Business or Premium in the Vimeo app.
  • You would need to cancel your app subscription in the appropriate App Store, wait for your subscription to lapse, then re-purchase via vimeo.
  • Your videos may briefly move into our archive storage in between subscriptions, but they will be restored upon purchasing the new plan.
  • If you purchased Starter or Standard, you can upgrade your subscription via the app; follow the Upgrade prompts in the Vimeo app to do so.
  • Subscriptions initially purchased via Apple or Google Play cannot be upgraded via vimeo.com.
  • If you purchased Advanced, you would need to speak with our sales team to upgrade to Enterprise, regardless of where you purchased your subscription.

FAQ: Migrating content to my Vimeo Enterprise account

This article applies to customers onboarding to Vimeo Enterprise.

If you are new to Vimeo and need to migrate your content from a previous platform to your Vimeo Enterprise account, our team can help you with that. This article answers the most common questions from new Enterprise customers about moving content to Vimeo.

  • I have existing content that I would like to add to my new Vimeo Enterprise account. Will I need to upload each individually?
  • I already use a Vimeo account. How can I migrate my videos into my new Enterprise account or merge my accounts?
  • What if I’m moving onto Vimeo from a previous video provider?

I have existing content that I would like to add to my new Vimeo Enterprise account. Will I need to upload each individually?

Not necessarily. The Vimeo Implementation team can help you migrate your content from either a previous provider or another Vimeo account (using publicly accessible URLs) to your new Vimeo Enterprise account. We will work with you to coordinate the ingestion of your content depending on how your existing library is stored.

I already use a Vimeo account. How can I migrate my videos into my new Enterprise account or merge my accounts?

We can either perform a clip transfer or proceed with a full account consolidation.

  • If you’d like to transfer a small subset of clips, we will move the videos from the original account to the new account. All videos will be located in the new account and will no longer appear in the original account. Take note that analytics will not be migrated over. To proceed, provide your implementation team with:
  • The email address of the source account that you’d like to migrate videos from
  • The URLs of the videos that you’d like to move over.
  • If you need to merge your whole Vimeo account(with all its videos and folders) with your new Enterprise account, see our account consolidation process for existing Vimeo accounts.
  • If you are migrating to a Vimeo Enterprise organization account with multiple workspaces added, discuss your content organization needs with your account manager.

What if I’m moving onto Vimeo from a previous video provider?

If you currently have content hosted by a third party, we can migrate this content as long as you have a publicly accessible URL where the files are hosted.

To run this process, your implementation team will need a CSV containing a list of videos, including columns for:

  • (Required) Source URL - A publicly accessible or signed URL where the file is hosted
  • (Optional) Title
  • (Optional) Description
  • (Optional) Tags - A list of up to 20 tags separated by pipe characters (“|”). Individual tags may not exceed 32 characters. Tags are a good way of retaining your previous provider’s video ID.
  • (Optional) Thumbnail URL - A publicly accessible link to directly download an image that can be used as a thumbnail for the video
  • (Optional) Folder ID - If you would like to move this video into a specific folder instead of just to the root folder, you can add the folder ID in this column. You can grab the folder ID from the URL of the folder page in the video manager
  • (Optional) Text Track URL - A publicly accessible link to directly download an English subtitle text track provided in a valid WebVTT format
  • (Optional) Privacy - The privacy setting you would like to apply for the video being uploaded. Use one of the following:
  • 0 - Anyone can access the video (aka “public”)
  • 0 - The video is embeddable, but it’s hidden on Vimeo and can’t be viewed on vimeo.com (aka “embed only”)
  • 0 - Only the account owner and team members on your account can access the video (aka “private”)
  • 0 - Only those with the password can access the video (aka “password”)
  • 0 - Only those with the private link can access the video (aka “unlisted”)

⚠️Note: Some video providers only allow the video download links to be available for a limited time. Be sure to coordinate the timing with your Implementation Manager or ask your provider to extend the duration of the download link so the links are valid at the time we run your migration.

Once you’ve put together your CSV, please send this over to your Implementation Manager, and we can kick off your migration with the timelines they communicate to you. We normally process 5,000 videos per day using this process.

FAQ: Refunds for Vimeo subscriptions

This article addresses the most commonly asked questions about requesting a refund and Vimeo’s refund policy.

  • What is Vimeo’s refund policy?
  • How do I request a refund for my subscription?
  • How do I request a refund if I purchased my subscription through the Apple App Store or Google Play?
  • Can I get a refund for an add-on purchase, such as seats or AI credits?
  • Can I get a partial refund?
  • I was told a refund was issued, but I don’t see it yet. How long does it normally take?
  • It’s past the suggested time, and I still don’t see my refund. What can I do?
  • Why does the refunded amount not match what I originally paid?

What is Vimeo’s refund policy?

Vimeo full refund policy is described in our Terms of Service. The key points to know are:

  • Monthly subscriptions can be refunded up to 3 days after your initial purchase
  • Yearly subscriptions can be refunded up to 14 days after your initial purchase

How do I request a refund for my subscription?

If you purchased your subscription from the Vimeo website, contact support to request a refund. Our team will review your request and respond as quickly as possible.

How do I request a refund if I purchased my subscription through the Apple App Store or Google Play?

  • Apple: We are unable to process refunds for purchases made through Apple iTunes or the App Store. To request a refund for a subscription purchased through Apple, contact Apple Support. Since the purchase was made through Apple’s app platform, it is subject to their refund policy and must be handled by Apple’s support team.
  • Google Play: For purchases made via Google Play, you can either contact us to request a refund or request a refund through Google Play support.

Can I get a refund for an add-on purchase, such as seats or AI credits?

We cannot accommodate refunds for add-on purchases, such as additional seats or AI credits.

The only exception is for seats added alongside your initial subscription purchase; in this case, if your subscription is eligible for a refund, all seats included in that purchase would be refunded alongside the subscription refund. Be sure to remove any team members from those seats before requesting a refund, as we won’t be able to process it if the seats are in use.

Can I get a partial refund?

We cannot accommodate any partial or pro-rated refund requests.

I was told a refund was issued, but I don’t see it yet. How long does it normally take?

While it typically takes up to 10 business days to process a refund, it may take longer depending on your banking institution. We advise waiting for one entire billing cycle (about one month) for the refund to be posted back to the account.

It’s past the suggested time, and I still don’t see my refund. What can I do?

We suggest reaching out to your bank for additional assistance using your receipt reflecting the refund. You can access your receipts in your account settings.

Why does the refunded amount not match what I originally paid?

If we support your local currency, your refund will be the same amount that was originally transacted.

In cases when your local currency must default to USD, you may have paid a different rate due to exchange rate fluctuations. This also applies to refunds in different amounts due to exchange rate fluctuations.

FAQ: Renew my Vimeo account subscription

Not sure what plan type you have? Check Membership in the upper-left corner of your Account Settings.

This article discusses how to renew your Vimeo Subscription. By default, Vimeo subscriptions automatically renew at the end of each cycle (yearly or monthly) to ensure uninterrupted service.

  • When does my subscription renew?
  • Why did my subscription not auto-renew when I enabled auto-renew?
  • Can I change my subscription plan?

When does my subscription renew?

By default, your membership renews automatically on the renewal date listed on your billing settings page unless you cancel automatic renewals before your renewal date.

If you would rather cancel your subscription, read how at ‘Cancel my subscription’.

Why did my subscription not auto-renew when I enabled auto-renew?

If you have enabled automatic renewal of your subscription, the payment method provided must be up to date to ensure successful charging. For example, we will not be able to charge an expired payment method. As a first step, please ensure your payment method details are correct.

⚠️Note:Under the German Fair Customer Contracts Act (FCCA), users located in Germany may be opted out of auto-renewal for their annual subscription if it was not purchased for business purposes. Read more at Will my account auto-renew if I am based in Germany?

If you’re experiencing issues with the transaction, it’s best to contact your bank or card issuer for further assistance.

If you are updating your payment method, our system will charge you immediately for a renewal.

Can I change my subscription plan?

You can upgrade your subscription plan on your own to access additional features and helpful tools. You can also compare Vimeo plans.

If you need further assistance, please Contact Support.

FAQ: Sales tax, VAT, and GST collection and exemptions for Vimeo purchases

This article answers the most frequently asked questions regarding tax collection and exemption.

  • Do I need to pay sales tax or VAT on my Vimeo Subscription?
  • In which U.S. states does Vimeo collect sales tax?
  • In which countries does Vimeo apply VAT or GST?
  • Is my U.S. nonprofit organization eligible for tax exemption?
  • Does my VAT ID or GST ID make me eligible for tax exemption?
  • How do I provide my VAT ID or GST ID to create a tax exemption?
  • How do I edit my VAT ID?
  • I am tax/VAT exempt, but I was charged tax/VAT on my purchase. How can I resolve this?
  • Is my purchase made in the Vimeo app eligible for tax exemption?
  • My country’s VAT ID is not accepted by your system. How can I get it added?

Do I need to pay sales tax or VAT on my Vimeo Subscription?

Whether you pay tax on your Vimeo plan and stock purchases depends on your state or country.

In which U.S. states does Vimeo collect sales tax?

For Vimeo subscription purchases, we collect U.S. sales tax in these states and districts:

  • West Virginia

The sales tax charged for users in the same state may vary based on zip code.

In which countries does Vimeo apply VAT or GST?

VAT (value-added tax) or GST (goods and services tax) will be applied to Vimeo subscription purchases made in the following countries:

  • Armenia

Is my U.S. nonprofit organization eligible for tax exemption?

Non-profit organizations are eligible for tax refunds on their Vimeo purchases.

If your tax-exempt organization was charged sales tax,contact us and include documentation showing your organization’s tax-exempt status in your initial message to expedite the process. We can then grant the exemption and issue a tax refund.

If you need additional assistance regarding your organization’s tax-exempt status, consult with a tax professional.

Does my VAT ID or GST ID make me eligible for tax exemption?

Your VAT ID may allow for a tax exemption if your ID is valid for cross-border transactions. Contact the appropriate authorities in your country for clarification on your VAT ID status.

Take note that we are not able to provide tax exemptions for VAT charges for the following countries:

  • Bahrain
  • Japan
  • Malaysia
  • Nigeria
  • Russia
  • Serbia
  • South Africa
  • South Korea
  • Switzerland
  • Taiwan

How do I provide my VAT ID or GST ID to create a tax exemption?

If you are VAT-exempt but live in a country where Vimeo collects VAT, you can enter a VAT ID while making new purchases or saving a credit card to your account.

How to add a VAT ID during the purchase
  1. Select the plan you’d like to purchase from ourupgrade page.
  2. On the checkout page, select your country. You’ll then see a button below the country name that says Add VAT ID.
  3. Click the button and enter your VAT ID. Once your ID has been verified, VAT will be automatically removed from your purchase price.

If you do not see this option, pleasecontact us for further assistance.

How to add a VAT ID for your plan renewal

If you’ve already made a purchase without a VAT ID and you want an exemption to be applied to your plan renewal, you’ll need to add a new payment method to your billing settings and delete your old billing methods:

  1. Log in to Vimeo and visit thePayment methods tab of your Billing settings.
  2. Select X to delete any saved credit cards that aren’t currently being used for renewal.
  3. Select + Add a new card
  4. If you choose a country where Vimeo collects VAT, a link will appear that says Have a VAT ID?
  5. Select Have a VAT ID?, then enter and validate your VAT ID.
  6. Choose Add payment method
  7. Now select the new payment method in the drop-down menu in the plan section.
  8. Select the X next to your previous card in the Payment Methods area if applicable. (It should be the only one with the X next to it if you followed each of the steps above.)

How do I edit my VAT ID?

To update your VAT ID, you can either update your payment method and add the VAT ID, orcontact us to update your VAT ID.

I am tax/VAT exempt, but I was charged tax/VAT on my purchase. How can I resolve this?

If you are a tax/VAT-exempt business but were charged tax or VAT on your purchase, it’s likely because you did not provide your documentation or VAT ID before purchasing. You cancontact us for a tax refund. Be sure to include your full VAT ID in the message (or for U.S. purchases, your exemption documentation).

Is my purchase made in the Vimeo app eligible for tax exemption?

To request a tax exemption for mobile in-app subscriptions, we’d recommend reaching out toApple Support orGoogle Play Support.

My country’s VAT ID is not accepted by your system. How can I get it added?

If you are not prompted to enter your VAT ID upon purchase, you will need tocontact us directly to send us your VAT ID, as we’ll need to manually add it to your account. This is required for the following countries:

  • Australia
  • Canada
  • Colombia
  • India
  • New Zealand
  • Serbia
  • Singapore
  • Turkey
  • United Arab Emirates (UAE)
  • United Kingdom (UK)
  • Uzbekistan

Folder role permissions for Enterprise accounts

If you have an Enterprise account, you can take advantage of advanced folder management features, including folder-specific permissions.

  • Folder-specific permissions
  • How to change a team member’s folder permissions
  • ‘Can manage’ folder permission
  • Workspace member types and permissions

Folder-specific permissions

The layered folder permission system ensures that access is consistently managed across different levels of the account.

Admins and Owners can grant their team members the following permissions based on their role and resource type:

  • Role
  • Resource Permission Scopes
  • Notes
  • Owner
  • Folder: Can manage Video: Can manage Events: Can manage Showcases: Can manage
  • Owners can only be assigned can manage .
  • Admin
  • Folder: Can manage Video: can manage Events: Can manage Showcases: Can manage
  • Admins can only be assigned can manage .
  • Contributor/Contributor+
  • Folder: Can manage, Can edit, Can view, Can comment Video: Can edit, Can view, Can comment Event: Can edit, Can view Showcase: Can edit, Can view
  • Contributors can never be assigned can manage on a video. If you add a Contributor to a folder that has subfolders, the team member will also have the permission to access the contents of the subfolders.
  • Viewer
  • Folder: Can view, Can comment Video: Can view, Can comment Event: Can view Showcases: Can view
  • Viewers can be assigned can view or can comment .
  • Uploader
  • Folder: n/a Video: n/a
  • Uploaders cannot be granted access to resources. They can only view public and unlisted videos.
  • Groups
  • Folder: Can view, can comment, can edit Video: Can view, can comment, can edit
  • Applies to SSO groups and the ‘All group’ for Enterprise teams.

How to change a team member’s folder permissions

To change a team member’s access, follow these steps:

  1. From the Library, select the folder.
  2. Open the folder share modal in the upper right section of the folder page.
  3. Either type in a new team member’s name and set their permission, then click Send invite, or…
  4. Alternatively, find an existing team member in the folder and click their role to open the dropdown menu and select the appropriate permission. The role change will save automatically.

‘Can manage’ folder permission

Changing a team member’s permissions from ‘Can edit’ to ‘Can manage’ will grant the team member permission to delete any videos within the folder from the team account, as well as permission to invite other team members to the folder.

A Contributor (Can edit) can be assigned to the ‘Can manage’ role in the main folder or in a subfolder. When a Contributor is assigned the ‘Can manage’ role in a top-level folder, they will also have admin permissions in all of the subfolders that live within that folder and can create new subfolders. But when a Contributor is assigned the ‘Can manage’ role in a subfolder, they will only have admin permissions in that particular subfolder. Members with ‘Can manage’ access will have access to creating and deleting subfolders.

See a full role comparison in Team member types.

Workspace member types and permissions

For detailed information, read How to add members and manage permissions in my Workspace.

Getting Started with Vimeo OTT

Once you’ve created your Vimeo OTT account, there are a few steps that need to be taken in order to publish your site and begin transacting. Before publishing, your site will not be viewable by anyone who is not a site member or admin. The list of the required steps, seen below, can be found by opening the Getting Started toggle in the bottom left corner of the admin.

Screenshot: Screen_Shot_2022-08-22_at_4.40.25_PM.png

The ability to publish your site and make it available to your audience will not be unlocked until each step of the checklist has been completed. These steps are:

  • Create a product- you will need to create at least one subscription (SVOD) or transactional (TVOD) product to get started.
  • Upload videos - you will need to upload at least one video. Here’s how.
  • Create a collection - create a collection to organize your videos into- either a playlist, series, or movie.
  • Create a category - create a category to organize all of your content - similar to parent folders in a filing system. For example, you could make a category for every genre of your content.
  • Complete setup - add a price to your product and make it available for sale.
  • Add billing information - you will need to add a bank account to get paid and a credit card for billing. See our instructions for setting up, verifying, and updating your payout information and find more information on adding a credit card and what charges to expect here.

Note: while it’s not a required to publish, we do highly recommend that you write your customer agreements as soon as possible. See our policy articles for guidance.

Once all steps have been completed, you will see the option to publish your site:

Screenshot: Screen_Shot_2022-08-22_at_4.42.10_PM.png

After you are published and have started selling, if you decide to shut down your OTT service, you will need to reach out to our support team for next steps.

How are profile videos organized on mobile sites and mobile apps

If you’re looking at your profile videos on the mobile site, you’ll notice that they appear in reverse-chronological order according to the upload date. If you’re logged in to your own account, you’ll also see your own private videos in reverse-chronological order.

In the Android and iOS apps, you’ll see profile videos in the creator’s specified order.

⚠️Note: The order of videos appearing on the Android and iOS mobile app is different from mobile browser web pages and these cannot be synced.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: When an account is converted to a Workspace, the ability to manage the Profile Page is lost. For more information, visit Troubleshooting: I can’t visit my Profile Page after becoming a Workspace

How can I turn my public profile page on or off?

You can enable or disable access to your public profile page on vimeo.

⚠️Note: This only changes public access to your Vimeo profile page. If you wish to make your entire account private, including disabling access to your profile via Vimeo’s API, enable private mode for your account.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: When an account is converted to a Workspace, the ability to manage the Profile Page is lost. For more information, visit Troubleshooting: I can’t visit my Profile Page after becoming a Workspace

To turn your public profile page on or off:

  1. Navigate to your profile icon in the upper-right corner of the page.
  2. Select Settingsto open your account settings.
  3. Go to Profile and then General to access your profile page settings.
  4. Use theVisibilitytoggle to allow others to see your profile or to hide this option.

How do I add Vimeo videos to my OTT site?

Vimeo OTT users can leverage their existing Vimeo videos to distribute as content for their customers. This will allow you to directly add the Vimeo videos to your OTT site without re-uploading them.

To add videos from Vimeo to your Vimeo OTT site:

To begin, make sure your OTT site is connected to your Vimeo account.

  • If you have created your OTT Site from Vimeo, you’re all set.
  • If you have created your OTT site another way, be sure to read the instructions on how to connect your accounts.

Once you’ve connected your Vimeo account, you can add your Vimeo content directly from the Content page of your OTT Admin if you are signed in as the site owner

  1. In the navigation bar, click Content > Videos.
  2. Once you’re on the Videos page, you’ll see a dropdown on the left with an option to Add Vimeo Videos.

Screenshot: mceclip1.png

  1. Click Add Vimeo Videos and you’ll see a window appear that lists all of your existing Vimeo videos.

⚠️Note: Currently, your Vimeo folders will not appear in this interface; use the search bar to find a specific video you’re looking for.

Select the video(s) you would like to distribute to your customers, then click the Add to OTT button. You’ll see a success message and your Vimeo videos will be linked to your OTT site.

Screenshot: mceclip2.png

  1. Keep in mind that OTT does not have a copy of your video; this is the same video that resides in your Vimeo account. Deleting the video on Vimeo would remove the video on OTT as well.

Now you’re ready to start configuring your newly added videos for distribution. For instructions on the next steps, refer to our guides on Creating Collections or Creating Categories.

How do I connect my Vimeo account to my OTT account?

If you are the site owner of an OTT site (vhx.tv) and have an account on Vimeo (vimeo), you can connect both accounts. Doing so will allow you to access your site from your Vimeo account, import videos from your Vimeo account to your Vimeo OTT site, and simulcast live events on Vimeo to a Vimeo OTT audience.

Note: You can connect your Vimeo and OTT accounts even if they have different email addresses.

  1. Navigate to your OTT account settings.
  2. You will see an option to connect your accounts.

  1. Click on Connect. You will be prompted to log in in case you are not logged into Vimeo.

Screenshot: mceclip4.png

  1. You will be prompted to confirm your connection; click Allow to continue.

Screenshot: connect-cta-explainer.jpg

  1. Upon successful connection of your accounts, you will be redirected to your OTT account settings with a status of “Connected”.

Screenshot: mceclip2.pngAnother way to connect is under Live Events in the Content menu. If you have not previously connected to Vimeo, you will see a button that allows you to connect the two services.

How do I upgrade my Vimeo subscription?

Not sure which plan type you have? Check “Membership” in the upper left corner of your Account Settings.

If you need more storage or features than your current Vimeo plan includes, you will need to purchase a higher subscription on Vimeo. This article discusses how to upgrade your plan on Vimeo.

  • How to purchase or upgrade a Vimeo subscription
  • How do I purchase Vimeo Enterprise?
  • I’m already on a paid plan. Will I be credited for an active previous purchase if I upgrade to a higher tier?

How to purchase or upgrade a Vimeo subscription

To purchase or upgrade a Vimeo subscription:

  1. Visit the Vimeo pricing page or select any Upgrade prompt on the Vimeo site or Vimeo app.
  2. Choose the plan that fits your needs and whether you wish to be billed monthly or yearly.
  • Annual plans are charged in full upfront, whereas monthly plans are billed every 30 days.
  1. Provide your payment details. See our accepted payment methods.
  2. Depending on your location, you may see a checkbox authorizing the storage of your payment method. You will need to select this checkbox to proceed.
  3. Select Complete purchase. By doing so, you agree to our Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and automatic renewal.
  4. You may be prompted to complete an additional authentication check per local regulations. If so, follow the onscreen prompts to verify your payment method and complete your purchase.

How do I purchase Vimeo Enterprise?

If you are interested in Vimeo Enterprise, contact our sales team via the form on our Enterprise page. A representative will assess your needs further and determine the best package for you. Note that Vimeo Support cannot connect you to a sales representative via support contact channels.

I’m already on a paid plan. Will I be credited for an active previous purchase if I upgrade to a higher tier?

We automatically prorate your purchase when you upgrade from your current paid subscription to a higher tier.

For example, if you’re halfway through your annual subscription and want to upgrade to a higher plan, we would apply what you’ve already paid for the remaining half of your subscription toward the cost of your higher subscription tier.

How many team members can I add to my Vimeo account?

The number of team members you can add to your account depends on which plan you purchased and, in some cases, how many seats you have purchased for your plan. See the table below for how many seats are available with each plan type:

  • Plan type
  • Number of team members
  • Plus
  • 1 (owner only)
  • Pro
  • 3 included, no add ons
  • Business
  • 10 included, no add ons
  • Premium
  • 10 included, no add ons
  • Starter
  • Add u p to 200
  • Standard
  • Add u p to 200 5 seats included
  • Advanced
  • Add u p to 200 10 seats included
  • Enterprise
  • Based on your contract

You can always purchase more seats from your billing settings page (note that you can add team members as Viewers at no extra cost, but they do count toward your 200-seat limit).

💡Tip: Build your team using our guided onboarding workflow.

⚠️Note for Enterprise Accounts: If you enable SSO on your Vimeo account, you can use SAML or SCIM to add and remove individual team members as well as groups. If you don’t have SSO and/or SCIM configured, contact your account manager for more information.

What is a paid seat?

A paid seat refers to an individual seat on a Starter, Standard, or Advanced account that you can assign to someone on your team who will be actively working on your Vimeo account. Specifically, Contributor and Admin roles count as paid seats.

While Viewers can be added at no additional charge, they do count towards your account’s total seat limit.

Note that these seats can be purchased as needed from your billing settings page.

How to accept an invitation to join a team or Workspace

This article discusses how to accept an invite from a team owner or admin. If you are a team owner or administrator, please see How to add team members to my account.

For Enterprise Users with Workspaces: These settings can be managed by a Workspace Administrator for the specific Workspace or an Organization Administrator for the Organization. The Organization’s settings will take precedence.

How to join a team or Workspace

Follow these steps to accept an invitation to join a team or Workspace:

  1. Once you have been invited to join a team or Workspace, you will receive an email from Vimeo with a message from the account owner or admin who invited you. Be sure to check your spam folder if you have not received the invite in your inbox.
  2. Select Get started to be redirected to vimeo. If you haven’t already created an account, you will be prompted to do so.
  3. After you’re logged in/created an account, you will be directly taken to your team’s library.

These same steps apply when accepting an invite for folder or video access.

What if I am unable to join a team or Workspace?

If you are having trouble accepting the invite, reach out to the team owner or admin to verify which email address should be used for the team account. They may need to re-invite you to the team or Workspace if there is an error.

How to access the Vimeo payment portal

The following applies to customers with contracts. For self-serve subscription plans, proceedto our guides on paying and managing your subscription.

As a customer who worked with one of our sales representatives and executed an individualized agreement, you will need to set up an account in our payment portal to manage your billing information and pay invoices. This article discusses how to set up and access the invoice payment portal.

Video overview

The video below offers an introduction to accessing Vimeo’s payment portal.

What to know before accessing the payment portal

  • This payment portal is only for customers who worked with a sales representative and executed an individualized agreement. Self-serve customers (who signed up and paid online without the involvement of our sales team) should continue to manage their billing preferences in their account settings.

How to access the payment portal

To set up your payment portal account:

How to add and manage team members in my Organization

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

As anOrganization Owner or Admin, you can invite new members to your Organization. manage their roles and permissions, and control their access to Workspaces. This article explains how to perform all member management tasks for your Organization.

  • What to know before you add and manage team members
  • How to invite new team members to your Organization
  • How to manage an existing member’s role and access
  • How to remove a member from an Organization
  • How to export your Organization member roster as a CSV

What to know before you add and manage team members

  • Admin Permissions: Only users with the Organization Owner or Organization Admin role can invite and manage members at the Organization level.
  • Organization Roles: There are three main roles at the Organization level:
  • Organization Owner:Organization Admins can manage all users, settings, and data across the entire Organization and within all Workspaces. They are automatically made a Workspace Admin in every Workspace. Additionally, they can access billing settings.
  • Organization Admin: Organization Admins can manage all users, settings, and data across the entire Organization and within all Workspaces. They are automatically made a Workspace Admin in every Workspace.
  • Organization Member: This is the standard role for users in your Organization. An Organization Member must be assigned to at least one Workspace to access content.
  • Workspace Roles:Organization Members assigned to a Workspace must have a role in that Workspace. You can read more about managing Workspace roles at: Those roles are:
  • Admin: Can view and manage all videos, folders, people, analytics, and live events on the account.
  • Contributor Plus:Can do everything Contributor members can do, plus use advanced creation tools, and create and manage live events (depending on the team’s membership plan).
  • Contributor: Can view, comment, upload, edit, share videos, and view clip analytics inside folders that have been shared with them.
  • Viewer: Can view and comment on videos that have been shared with them.
  • You can manage team members individually or in bulk. To manage them in bulk, select the checkboxes to the left of each team member’s name.

How to invite new team members to your Organization

You can invite new people to join your Organization and assign them to Workspaces in a single workflow. To do so:

  1. Navigate to your Organization Settings and select the Members tab.
  2. Select the Invite button in the upper-right corner.
  3. In the modal window that appears, enter the email address of the person you wish to invite. You can add multiple emails at once (up to 10 in each batch).
  4. Choose their role for the Organization:
  • Organization Admin:Select this to grant them full administrative access to the entire Organization. They will automatically be added to all Workspaces as a Workspace Admin.
  • Organization Member: Select this for non-Organization Admin users.
  • If you selected Organization Member, you must then add them to one or more Workspaces. Select “Add to Workspaces” and choose the desired Workspaces, along with the role they should have in each (e.g., Workspace Admin, Contributor, Viewer). Learn about Workspace member permissions at
  1. Select Send invitation. The team member will receive an email prompting them to join your Organization.
  2. Finally, you’ll have the optional chance to share Workspace-specific folders with the newly invited team members.

How to manage an existing member’s role and access

You can change a member’s role or adjust their Workspace access at any time from the Members list. To manage an existing member’s role and access:

  1. Navigate to the Members tab in your Organization Settings.
  2. Find the user in the member list and select the vertical ellipses (⋮)button to the right of their name.
  3. From the dropdown menu, choose one of the following options:
  • Make Organization Admin / Remove from Organization Admins: This option promotes a standard Organization Member to an Organization Admin or demotes an Organization Admin back to a standard Organization Member.
  • Manage Workspace access: This opens a new window where you can add the member to new Workspaces or remove them from Workspaces they are already in. You can also change their specific role within each Workspace from this view.
  • Turn off SSO:Activate or deactivate a user’s SSO access to your Workspace.
  • Remove from Organization:Removing a member from the Organization will revoke their access to all Workspaces and content within them.

How to remove a member from the Organization

Removing a member from the Organization will revoke their access to all Workspaces and content within them. To remove a member:

  1. Navigate to the Members tab in your Organization Settings.
  2. Find the user in the member list and select the vertical ellipses (⋮)button to the right of their name.
  3. Select Remove from Organization.
  4. A confirmation window will appear with the following message: “ will lose access to all content and Workspaces in . Any videos added by this member to shared folders and comments added to shared videos will still be accessible to other Workspace members.”
  5. Select the Remove button to permanently remove the member from your Organization.

How to export your Organization member roster as a CSV

Organization Owners and Organization Admins can export the full Organization member roster as a CSV file. The file is generated asynchronously and delivered to you when ready — you can download it directly or receive it by email.

  1. Navigate to the Members tab in your Organization Settings.
  2. Select Export as CSV.
  3. Choose how you want to receive the file when it’s ready: Download or Email.

The exported CSV includes the following information for each member:

  • Email address
  • Name
  • Organization role
  • Date added
  • Status (accepted or pending invitation)
  • SSO status
  • For each Workspace the member belongs to, a row with the Workspace name and the member’s Workspace role

💡 Tip: If a member is assigned to multiple Workspaces, the CSV contains one row per Workspace assignment so you can see every Workspace and role each member holds.

How to add members and manage permissions in my Workspace

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

Workspace Administrators, along with Organization Owners and Administrators, can invite new team members to a Workspace, assign their roles, and remove users directly through the Workspace settings. This article outlines how to add and manage members within your Workspace.

  • What to know before you add Workspace members
  • How to invite members to a Workspace
  • How to manage an existing Workspace member’s role
  • How to remove a member from a Workspace
  • How to export your Workspace member roster as a CSV

What to know before you add Workspace members

  • Administrator Permissions: You must be a Workspace Administrator, Organization Owner, or Organization Administrator to add, manage, or remove members from a Workspace.
  • Organization Owners and Admins can learn how to add team members to their Organization and Workspaces at How to add and manage team members in my Organization
  • Organization Owners and Admins will become Workspace admins for all workspaces and cannot be removed at the Workspace level.
  • Workspace Roles: There are several roles you can assign to members within a Workspace:
  • Workspace Administrator: Can view and manage all videos, folders, people, analytics, and live events on the account.
  • Contributor Plus: Can do everything Contributor members can do, plus use advanced creation tools, and create and manage live events (if the Organization also has Live Events).
  • Contributor: Can view, comment, upload, edit, share videos, and view clip analytics inside folders that have been shared with them.
  • Viewer: Can view and comment on videos that have been shared with them.

How to invite team members to a Workspace

You can invite new people to your Workspace, which will also add them to your Organization if they are not already members. To invite a member:

  1. Ensure that you are in the workspace you want to manage. Learn how to switch Workspaces at How to switch between multiple Workspaces.
  2. Select the name of your active Workspace from the top-right corner of the Vimeo homepage.
  3. Select Settings.
  4. On the Workspace settings page, select Members.
  5. On the Members page, select the “Invite”button located on the right side of the page.
  6. In the Invite members window that appears, enter the email address of the person you wish to invite. You can add multiple emails at once (up to 10 in each batch).
  7. Select their role for the Workspace from the dropdown menu:
  8. Select Invite. The team member will receive an email prompting them to join your Workspace.
  9. Finally, you’ll have the optional chance to share Workspace-specific folders with the newly invited team members.

Until the team member accepts the invitation, they will appear as ‘Pending’on the team member’s list. To manage their invitation, select the vertical ellipses (⋮) to the right of their name. Here, you can resend the invite, copy the invite link, share Workspace folders with the team member, manage which groups they’re part of, or remove them from the Workspace.

Screenshot: The “more options” menu for a “Pending” member invitation is open. It contains a list of actions including “Resend invite,” “Copy invite link,” “Share folders,” “Manage groups,” and “Remove from workspace.”

How to manage an existing Workspace member’s role

You can change a member’s role and permissions at any time from the Workspace Members list. To change a member’s role:

  1. Navigate to the Members tab in your Workspace Settings.
  2. Find the user in the member list.
  3. To the right of the user’s name, select the dropdown menu under their current role.
  4. Select the new role you want to assign to that user. The change is saved automatically.

How to remove a team member from a Workspace

Removing a member from a Workspace will revoke their access to the content within it, but they will remain a member of your Organization. Additionally, any content added by this member will still be accessible to other Workspace members after they are removed from the Workspace.

To remove a member:

  1. Navigate to the Members tab in your Workspace Settings.
  2. Find the user in the member list and select the vertical ellipses (⋮) button to the right of their name.
  3. Select Remove from Workspace.
  4. A confirmation window will appear. Select the final confirmation button to remove the member from the Workspace.

How to export your Workspace member roster as a CSV

Workspace Administrators (as well as Organization Owners and Organization Admins) can export the full Workspace member roster as a CSV file. The file is generated asynchronously and delivered to you when ready — you can download it directly or receive it by email.

  1. Navigate to the Members tab in your Workspace Settings.
  2. Select Export as CSV.
  3. Choose how you want to receive the file when it’s ready: Download or Email.

The exported CSV includes the following information for each member:

  • Email address
  • Name
  • Workspace role
  • Date added
  • Status (accepted or pending invitation)
  • SSO status

How to add team members to my account

The article explains how to invite team members to manage videos and folders in your account, including troubleshooting tips for common issues that may arise during the process.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:If you are seeking information on how to invite users to an Organization or Workspace, visit How to add and manage team members in my Organizationor How to add members and manage permissions in my Workspace.

  • How to invite a team member to my account
  • What isn’t my team member being added after sending an invite?
  • Suggested next steps

How to invite a team member to my account

You can invite team members to your account to help upload and manage your videos, events, and collections. You can also add team members to your account by sharing a video with them; see How to share videos with your team to learn how.

Team Owners and Admins can add new team members to the account. To add a team member to your account, follow these steps:

  1. Select the Manage Team tab in your Account Settings to access the team management page. You’ll see all your existing team members on this page (by default, it’ll only list you).
  • You can also invite someone to your team by selecting your profile photo and choosing the Invite members option. You’ll see the pop-up modal where you can invite your team members. Screenshot: Account menu with Invite members highlighted
  1. Select the + Invite button on the right side of the page.
  2. In the module that opens, enter your team member’s email address, then select their role from the dropdown menu. Note: If you are on a Starter, Standard, or Advanced plan and have run out of seats, select Purchase seatsto buy more seats for your account. Only the owner can purchase seats.
  3. To add more than one team member, you can type or paste up to 10 email addresses at a time, separated by commas. All team members invited at the same time will have the same role.
  4. Type in the message field to add a note to the email invites that your team members will receive.
  5. Select Invite to send the invitation(s).
  6. You will see a Pending indicator below their name and role on the team management page until they accept the invitation.

What isn’t my team member being added after sending an invite?

  • If the person you’ve added hasn’t responded to your invite, you can send them a reminder. Hover over the Pending status on the team management page and select the Send reminder link that appears. We will also send them a reminder automatically if they have not responded within 24 hours.
  • If your team member is having trouble receiving the invitation email, you can send them a direct invitation URL by hovering over the Pending status, selecting the Copy invite link button, and sending it directly to your team member.
  • Please note that this link is unique to each team member and cannot be used to invite others to the account. Once a team member accepts the invitation, the Copy invite link option will not appear any longer.
  • If the team member already has a Vimeo account that they would like to link, ensure you use the correct email address.
  • If the team member is still having trouble, try removing and re-inviting them from the team settings page.

Suggested next steps

  • You can also add team members to specific folder(s) by sharing. For more information about this, refer to How to share folders and videos with your team.

How to audit your team members’ content access

This feature requires a paid plan.

Using the View access feature, you can audit the content and permissions that a team member has access to for both the Team library and My library. From this view, Owners and Admins can click into the specific resource to execute management actions including: changing access grants, moving content, deleting content, and modifying the data (title, description, tags).

Follow the steps below to access and use this feature:

  1. Log into your Vimeo account and navigate to the team management page.
  2. Select the options menu (…) to the right of the team member role dropdown menu.
  3. Select View accessto see which folders and content the team member has access to.
  4. The View access page will default you to audit the user’s Team library access. Hover next to any item to Manage the resource.
  5. The View access page also contains a tab for My library where you can audit the user’s My library contents. Hover next to any item to Manage the resource.

⚠️Note:For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: Organization Admins can view audit data for the entire organization, while Workspace Admins see data for their specific Workspace.

How to cancel my Vimeo subscription

This article applies to all paid memberships other than Enterprise. Enterprise accounts are subject to our Enterprise terms. If you would like to suspend your Enterprise contract, please contact your account manager.

If you decide you no longer need paid features included with your Vimeo plan, you can cancel your subscription in your account settings at any time. This article explains how to cancel your subscription via desktop and what happens when you do so.

  • What to know before canceling a Vimeo subscription
  • How to cancel my Vimeo subscription or free trial
  • Why don’t I see the option to cancel?
  • Can I cancel my subscription at any time?
  • Can I get a refund if I cancel my membership?
  • Does canceling my Vimeo subscription delete my Vimeo account?

What to know before canceling a Vimeo subscription

  • When you cancel your subscription, you will still have access to your paid features until the end of your current billing cycle.
  • You will then lapse to a Basic or Free plan, meaning you will lose access to paid features such as additional storage, player customization, additional privacy settings, and any VOD titles you sell will no longer be available.
  • Refunds are not automatically issued upon cancellation. See About refunds for Vimeo subscriptions to understand our refund policy and how to request one.

How to cancel my Vimeo subscription or free trial

To cancel the automatic renewal of your subscription or free trial:

  1. Go to your billing settings page.
  • ⚠️Note: The billing settings page is only accessible if you are logged into an account enrolled in an active subscription or active trial. Otherwise, you will see a prompt to renew your subscription.
  1. Select Membership plan. Screenshot: Settings left navigation menu with the Membership plan option highlighted.
  2. On the left side, select Billing.
  3. In the lower right corner, select Cancel subscription. Screenshot: Billing settings page with the cancel subscription option highlighted. It’s located in the lower right corner of the page.
  4. Confirm your cancellation.

Why don’t I see the option to cancel?

  • If your Vimeo subscription was purchased via a mobile app using an Apple App Store or Google Play account, then you will not see the option to cancel in your billing settings on vimeo.com. You must manage the subscription via the relevant mobile platform.
  • Visit Apple Support or Google Support for steps on how to cancel mobile-purchased subscriptions.
  • If you are on a Free or Basic plan, you will not see the option to cancel.
  • You may choose to delete your account instead.
  • If you are on an Enterprise account, contact your account manager.

Can I cancel my subscription at any time?

You can cancel your subscription at any time before the renewal date listed on your billing settings page. You will not be charged for the next billing period if you cancel in advance. Instead of canceling your subscription, you can also choose to downgrade to a lower paid plan.

Can I get a refund if I cancel my membership?

Refunds are not automatic upon cancellation; however, in some cases, you may be eligible for a refund. Read about refund eligibility and how to request one at Refunds for Vimeo subscriptions.

Does canceling my Vimeo subscription delete my Vimeo account?

No, your account will remain active, but lapse to the Free or Basic plan. If you no longer have any need or desire to keep your Vimeo account in any capacity, you can delete it.

How to change a payment method

This article discusses how to change or edit your card information and switch your payment method.

  • How do I change the card on file for my subscription?
  • Why can’t I switch payment method to PayPal?
  • Suggested next steps

How do I change the card on file for my subscription?

When you purchase a subscription on Vimeo.com, your payment method is saved automatically. To update your payment method

  1. Go to the Membership Plan page in your Billing Settings. ⚠️Note: The Billing Settings page is accessible if you are logged into an account enrolled in an active paid subscription or active trial plan. Otherwise, you will be prompted to renew or upgrade your account.
  2. Open the dropdown menu below the Payment method where your current payment method is listed, and click Add a new card.
  3. Depending on your location, you may see a checkbox authorizing the storage of your payment method. You will need to select this checkbox to proceed.
  4. You may be prompted to complete an additional authentication check per local regulations. If so, follow the onscreen prompts to verify and submit your payment method.
  5. Enter your new payment information on this page.
  6. Once submitted, you can navigate to the Membership Plan page and select your desired payment method from the same dropdown menu.

Refer to the troubleshooting payment issues article if you are unable to add, change, or save your payment method.

Refer to the Accepted payment methods article to learn about all the payment instruments that are accepted on the Vimeo platform.

Why can’t I switch payment method to PayPal?

While we are unable to offer a direct way to switch your payment method from credit card to PayPal during an active subscription, it is possible to change payment methods when renewing a subscription or signing up again.

In that case, you can select PayPal as the payment option when signing up for a new membership (i.e. re-purchasing a membership once your older one lapses) or renew an existing subscription early, before it lapses.

If you purchased multiple seats as part of your initial plan purchase, we can refund that purchase in full if it’s within our terms. You could then re-purchase your plan with the desired number of seats. To proceed with this, please contact our support team.

If you want to change the current PayPal account to another PayPal account, you will have to cancel the auto-renew of your subscription, then let the account lapse, and then make a new purchase.

Suggested next steps

  • Now that your payment method is updated, view your purchase history and payment methods.
  • If your payment failed, Troubleshooting: Payment fails when purchasing or renewing a Vimeo plan.

How to change account ownership

How can I change account ownership?

If you are the current account owner of a team account and would like to transfer account ownership to a different team member on your account, follow the steps below. If you’d like to transfer ownership to an email address not associated with a Vimeo account, skip to step 4.

  1. Change the account password of your team account to a temporary one that you can give to the team member whom you’d like to make the new account owner.
  2. Remove the team member you’d like to make the new account owner from your account.
  3. Have the removed team member delete their account completely from Vimeo, as an email address can only be linked to one Vimeo account. (Alternatively, the new owner could change the email address on their personal account to a different email).
  4. Log in to the team account (via the current email address), and head to your Account Settings page.
  5. Click Edit next to your current email address.
  6. Enter the email address of the new account owner. After you change the email address associated with your Vimeo account, a notification email will be sent to both the old and new email addresses.

Once that is done, you can hand the new credentials off to the new account member and they can log into the account and update the temporary password. Make sure to have them update the billing information as well if needed.

What if I am not the account owner?

If the owner of the account has left your company or is otherwise unable to log in to Vimeo, please contact us. A member of our support team will assist in validating the new account owner.

How to configure SCIM for Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

You can configure SCIM to create and manage team accounts and user groups. This article discusses how you can set up a SCIM connection with Vimeo for your organization using Microsoft Entra ID as your IdP (Identity Provider).

If you’re an existing Vimeo Enterprise customer and don’t have SCIM, please contact your Account Manager for more information. If you are not a Vimeo Enterprise customer yet and are interested in SCIM, please contact us.
