How to prepare the Vimeo API application

  1. Open developer.vimeo
  2. Log in as a team owner.
  3. Select Get started or New app.
  4. Fill out the form, then select Create App.
  5. Scroll down to the Generate an access token section.
  6. Select Authenticated (you).
  7. Select Private, then SCIM scopes.
  8. Press Generate button.
  9. Copy or save newly generated token somewhere, such as a note-taking application.

Screenshot: App token page on vimeo developer page

How to configure the Entra ID App

  1. Go to your existing Vimeo application that is used for Vimeo.
  2. Go to Provisioning-> Update credentials -> Open Admin credentials.
  3. Set tenant URL as 0 where “1234567” is the Vimeo team owner’s* User ID (see Prerequisites).
  4. Set the Secret token from the section above (Preparing Vimeo API application).
  5. Select Test Connection.
  6. Save configuration.
  7. OpenMappings.
  8. Go to Provision Microsoft Entra ID Groups.
  9. Set up like on the screenshot below and Save.

Screenshot: Attribute mapping page within Entra ID platform

How to provision users from Entra ID to Vimeo

  1. Select Start provisioning button in the Entra ID Enterprise application.
  2. After that, every user you assign to the application under Users and groups will be provisioned into Vimeo.
  3. After provisioning is initiated you can check the Team Management page for those provisioned users.

About supported user attributes for SCIM configuration

When you change a user, keep UserName and Email attributes identical. Vimeo supports the below user attributes:

  • schemas (read-only, required by SCIM specification)
  • id (read-only, required by SCIM specification)
  • Username (mutable, requires the same value for email)
  • Name (mutable)
  • name.formatted (same as givenName+familyName)
  • name.givenName
  • name.familyName
  • displayName (same as givenName+familyName)
  • Active (mutable)
  • emails (only type=work and primary=true) (mutable)
  • profileUrl (read-only)
  • locale (mutable)
  • groups (read-only, mutable from /Groups endpoint)
  • meta (read-only)

Please contact scim-support@vimeo.com if you have any issues.

How to configure SCIM for Okta

This guide will walk through how Enterprise users can set up a SCIM connection with Vimeo for their organization using Okta as their IdP (Identity Provider).

If you’re an existing Vimeo Enterprise customer and don’t have SCIM, please contact your Account Manager for more information. If you are not a Vimeo Enterprise customer yet and are interested in SCIM, please contact us.

  • Configuring the Okta App
  • Provisioning users Okta to Vimeo
  • Processing failed SCIM attempts
  • Restrictions
  • Support attributes (mapping)

Configuring the Okta App

  1. Go to your existing SAML application that is used for Vimeo.
  2. In the General tab, edit App settings.
  3. Change Provisioning from None to SCIM.Screenshot: Okta general settings highlighing the Provisioning settings with the radio button labeled SCIM selected.
  4. There should now be a Provisioning area or tab in the application: Screenshot: A row of tabs, highlighting the tab labeled ‘Provisioning,’ third from the left.
  5. Go to the Provisioningtab > Settings> Integration> select Edit.
  6. Enter the SCIM connector base URL using this URL format: 0, where 12345678* is the Vimeo team owner’s User ID; you can find it in the upper left corner of the Vimeo Account Settings page.
  7. In the Unique identifier field for users field, enter userName.
  8. Enable all the supported provisioning actions that are listed here.
  9. In the Authentication Mode menu, select HTTP Header.
  10. For Authorization, paste the generated API token from Vimeo.
  11. Click Save.
  12. Next, go to the Provisioning tab > Settings > To App.
  13. Enable Create users, Update user attributes, and Deactivate users.Screenshot: Okta provisioning settings page, showing the ‘To App’ section with Create users, Update user attributes, and deactivate users options all enabled.
  14. Select Save.

Provisioning users Okta to Vimeo

The initial step to start provisioning in Okta is assigning users to the SAML application. If you just created a SAML application to set up SSO and SCIM, you can assign users and they will be provisioned automatically.

Screenshot: Assignments settings page in Okta, showing a list of example users.

If you already have a SAML application with assigned users, they won’t be provisioned once the provision is enabled. You have two options in Okta:

  • You can unassign and assign users again, or
  • You can contact Okta support and ask to enable a feature called Provision out of sync users which would add a Provision now button next to each user that is not provisioned after provisioning is enabled.

After you’ve initiated provisioning, you can see on your team settings page that team members have been added to your Vimeo account.

You can now also push Groups from your IdP into Vimeo if you need:

Screenshot: Okta Push Groups settings page, showing an example group that is being pushed to Vimeo.

Processing failed SCIM attempts

There are cases where users can’t be migrated via SCIM, such as:

  • A user with the same email address already exists on Vimeo and is not on this Enterprise team
  • Your account reached its seat cap
  • Connection errors

In these cases, you can go to your team settings page and download a list of failed migrations where you see the error message.

Screenshot: Vimeo manage team settings page, showing an error message that says ‘There is an error migrating some users. Download a list of errors.’ with a link to download a list of errors.

In most cases, to address them, it’s best to contact your Account Manager: some of them can be handled by migrating Vimeo users to your Enterprise account, others by purchasing additional seats.

Restrictions

When you change a user’s information in your IdP, be sure to keep the Username and Email identical.

Support attributes (mapping)

We do not support all SCIM out-of-the-box user attributes. Currently, Vimeo supports these user attributes:

  • schemas (read-only, required by SCIM specification)
  • id (read-only, required by SCIM specification)
  • userName (mutable, requires the same value for email)
  • Name (mutable)
  • displayName (same as givenName+familyName)
  • Active (mutable)
  • emails (only type=work and primary=true) (mutable)
  • profileUrl (read-only)
  • locale (mutable)
  • groups (read-only, mutable from /Groups endpoint)
  • meta (read-only)

Please contact scim-support@vimeo.com if you have any issues.

How to connect your Vimeo account to social media accounts

This article discusses how to connect and manage Vimeo with various social media platforms.

You can connect your Vimeo account to Facebook Pages, YouTube, Twitter, LinkedIn, Shopify, and Tumblr on your Connected apps setting page. Click Connect next to the corresponding provider to connect your accounts.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Organizations may limit the ability for Workspaces to publish to social.

Once you connect to an account, you can choose to publish certain actions automatically (such as new uploads and likes).

  • Click the Settings link corresponding to any connected account and then select the actions you’d like Vimeo to automatically post about each account.
  • Note that some providers only connect to publish to social and simulcasting and may not have additional settings to configure.

To disconnect from any of these accounts, hover your cursor over the Connected button and click it to disconnect. You can always reconnect your account or connect to a different Facebook account if you wish.

Note: If you encounter any issues with your selected social media connection, try troubleshooting by disconnecting and then reconnecting it.

If you connect to a Facebook account, please be advised of the following:

  • As of August 1, 2018, you can no longer connect and post your Vimeo activity to Facebook profiles. You can still connect and post your Vimeo activity to Facebook Pages.
  • A profile is a personal Facebook account for an individual, whereas a Facebook Page is a public profile for businesses, brands, organizations, and public figures.
  • Please note that anything that was posted before August 1, 2018, on your Facebook profile will not be affected and will remain unless you choose to manually delete it.
  • This also affects Publish to Social, as you will no longer be able to publish Vimeo videos to the native Facebook player on your profile. You can still publish your videos to the native Facebook player via your Facebook Pages.

How to control session duration on your team

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

This article provides a guide for Admins and Owners on managing session durations, forcing logouts, and enabling SSO single logout for team members on an Enterprise account.

As an Admin or Owner on an Enterprise team, you can control session duration for all team members on your account. Using this feature, team members will be required to reauthenticate after a specified number of days, hours, or minutes, or after a set period of inactivity. You can also manually force log out all team members at any time.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

  • How to control session duration
  • How to force log out team members
  • How to enable SSO single logout

How to control session duration

To learn how to turn on session duration, see these steps:

  1. Navigate to your team management page by selecting your profile icon, then Manage team.
  2. Select Settingsfrom the lefthand panel.
  3. Next to ‘Session duration’, select’Edit’.
  4. You can choose to log out team members after a period of inactivity or after a set amount of time.
  5. From the dropdown menu, choose Minutes, Hours, or Days. Enter the number of minutes, hours, or days in the field to the left.
  6. Select‘Save and log out team’ to apply the settings to your account.

How to force log out team members

As an Admin or Owner on an Enterprise account, you can force yourself and all team members to log out. After a few minutes, this will end active sessions for all users and require them to authenticate again.

Follow these steps to learn how:

  1. Navigate to your team management page by selecting your profile icon, then Manage team.
  2. Select Settingsfrom the lefthand panel.
  3. Next toLog out all team members, select Force log out.
  4. Select Force log out on the modal that will appear to confirm this action.

How to enable SSO single logout

To turn on SSO single logout, you must be an Owner or Admin on an Enterprise account.

When SSO single logout is enabled, all team members on your account will be logged out of Vimeo as soon as they’re logged out of your identity provider. This ensures that Vimeo sessions are consistent with IdP session policies and that other users cannot breach accounts on the same device.

Follow these steps to enable SSO single logout for your team:

  1. Select your profile icon, then navigate to Manage team > Settings> Single sign-on (SSO) to open the SSO settings in team management.
  2. Set up a SAML connection if you have not done so already.
  3. Within the SAML connection modal, navigate to the Vimeo metadata section. Copy the Single Logout URL and paste it into the corresponding field in your IdP.
  4. Then, scroll down to the Identity Provider Metadata section. Grab the SAML Single Logout URL provided by your IdP and enter it in the Single Logout URL (Optional) field. ⚠️Note: If you leave this field blank, Vimeo will default to the URL in theSign In URL field.
  5. Save your changes to the SAML connection.

  1. You will be prompted to answer a few questions that help us get to know what our customers use Vimeo for. Proceed through the survey (you can also skip it).

How to create an allowlist for my Vimeo Enterprise account

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Owners and Admins of Vimeo Enterprise accounts with custom subdomains have the option to restrict access to certain administrative features by specifying allowed IP addresses, ranges, or CIDR blocks. When enabled, this setting blocks login attempts to admin functions from IP addresses that are not explicitly permitted. This article explains how to create and manage your IP allowlist.

Screenshot: A full-screen error message is displayed in a dialog box. The message reads, ‘You can’t access this account from your current IP address.’ Below the message, it advises, ‘Contact your organization’s admin for help’.

  • What to know before setting up your allowlist
  • How to create an allowlist
  • How to add IP addresses to the allowlist
  • How to import IP addresses using a .csv file.
  • IPv4 address formatting guidelines

What to know before setting up your allowlist

Before setting up your IP allowlist, note the following:

  • This feature is designed to add an extra layer of access control, helping safeguard sensitive management functionalities on your account, complementing Vimeo’s existing identity and access management tools.
  • Note: This feature does not guarantee complete protection against unauthorized access and should be used in conjunction with other recommended security practices. Vimeo is not responsible for access gained through misconfigured settings or circumvention of IP restrictions.
  • On Vimeo, an allowlist refers to a list of IP addresses, ranges, or CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) blocks that are approved to access Admin features on an Enterprise account.
  • You must be an account owner or admin on a Vimeo Enterprise account to create an allowlist.
  • The Vimeo Enterprise account must havea custom subdomain.
  • You’ll need a list of IP addresses, ranges, or CIDR blocks for approved users.
  • You can either upload them manually one by one, add them in bulk as a comma- or line-separated list, or upload a .csv file.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

How to create an allowlist

Once the addresses are identified, Enterprise account Owners and Admins can add them through the account settings page of the Enterprise account to set up the allowlist.

To create an allowlist:

  1. From the account settings page of the Enterprise account, select Allowlist Screenshot: The settings page of a Vimeo Enterprise account. A Vimeo settings page displays ‘Authentication’ options. Within this section, the ‘Allowlist’ entry is selected, highlighted by a red outline. The description states: ‘Restrict access to this account by allowing only trusted IP addresses.’
  2. If it is your first time creating an allowlist, select Create allowlist.
  3. The first IP address added to the allow list must belong to the Owner or Admin on the account. Select Add IP addressto add it to the list.
  4. In the Add IP Address pop-up, add a single IP address, range, or CIDR block accessible to the account owner or administrator.
  5. Provide an optional nickname to help you identify it. For example, use the name of the Admin that an IP address corresponds with, or label the office location associated with an IP range.
  6. Confirm the details and select Add IP.

How to add IP addresses to an allowlist

The Owner or Admin can add additional IP Addresses, ranges, and CIDRs to the allowlist to restrict access. These can be added one at a time or in bulk as a comma-separated list.

To add IP addresses to an allowlist:

  1. From the allowlist page on the Enterprise account’s settings page, select the Add IP Addressbutton on the right side of the page.
  2. Add an IP address, range, or CIDR block. Provide an optional nickname so that you’ll be able to identify it.
  3. Review the addresses added and select Add IP.

You can add multiple IP addresses, ranges, or CIDR blocks separated by commas or lines.

How to import IP addresses by using a .csv file.

You can also upload a .csv file of IP addresses, ranges, and CIDR blocks.

To import IP addresses by using a .csv file:

  1. From the allowlist page on the Enterprise account’s settings page, select Import > Download CSV templateon the right side of the page.
  2. Format your list according to the CSV template and save it to your local device.
  3. Select Import > Import CSV.
  4. Select and upload your formatted .csv template file.

If your import fails, check that your CSV file is formatted correctly as per the CSV template and the IPv4 formatting guidelines.

About IPv4 address formatting guidelines

When developing your allowlist, note that IPv4 addresses must be formatted accordingly. Refer to the table below that describes the formatting criteria and provides examples of both correctly and incorrectly formatted IPv4 addresses.

  • Criteria
  • Description
  • Correctly Formatted
  • Incorrectly Formatted
  • Allowed Characters
  • Only numbers, periods, and slashes.
  • 192.168.1.1/24
  • 192.168.1.1a
  • CIDR Mask Formatting
  • CIDR masks must be between /0 and /32.
  • 192.168.1.0/24
  • 192.168.1.0/37
  • Decimal Numbers
  • Four decimal numbers,
  • 10.0.0.255
  • 10.0.0
  • IP Range Formatting
  • Ranges must have the lower IP address first
  • 192.168.1.0 - 192.168.1.100
  • 192.168.1.100-192.168.1.0
  • IP Range Size
  • Must be within (/0 - /32) .
  • 192.168.1.1-192.168.1.10
  • 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255
  • Negative Numbers
  • Must not contain any negative numbers.
  • 172.16.0.1
  • -1.0.0.0
  • Numerical Range
  • Each number must be between 0 and 255.
  • 10.0.0.255
  • 256.0.0.3000

If you get an error indicating that your IPv4 address is incorrectly formatted, verify the address and reformat it as needed.

How to customize the Vimeo player’s language settings

If you watch a video embedded outside of vimeo, your Vimeo account settings will not be reflected in the player. The embedded player detects the language settings configured in your browser to customize your experience.

See below for how to update your preferred language in certain browsers:

  • Change the language of your Chrome browser
  • Change the language your Mac uses (Safari)
  • Use Firefox in another language
  • Use Microsoft Edge in another language

The language configured in your browser will impact text within the player. The setting menus will be translated; however, text from the video or interactive features will not be impacted.

As a video creator, you can build interactive and lead-capture tools in native languages. Our captions can also be configured in a wide range of available languages in addition to the localization that occurs within the player itself.

To read more about captions, subtitles, and translation tools on vimeo see the following articles:

  • Available languages on the Vimeo website
  • How to add captions or subtitles to your video
  • How do I use Vimeo AI to translate my video into another language?
  • How to enable or disable captions and subtitles while viewing a video

How to delete my account

This article covers how to delete your Vimeo account and the implications of doing so. We strongly recommend exercising caution when considering whether and when to delete your account.

  • What to know before deleting your account
  • How to delete your account
  • How to delete an account created via a third party (Google, Facebook, Apple)
  • How to remove specific content from your account

What to know before deleting your account

  • Deleting your account (or anything else, like a video or comment) will remove it from public view on Vimeo.
  • After it’s deleted, we may retain some of your information and activity on our internal servers for a time in case you wish to restore it or for certain legal purposes.
  • Your account will not be viewable to the public. Please note that deleting videos, profile pictures, comments, or descriptions may not ensure complete or comprehensive removal because third parties may have reposted your material, and search engines may have indexed or cached it before you deleted it. We have no control over third-party sites or search engine results.
  • If your goal is simply to stop paying, you shouldCancel my subscription. Instead, this will revert your account to a free plan at the end of your billing cycle without deleting your content.

⚠️Note: Once an account is deleted, we cannot guarantee that any information is retained, which means we will not be able to restore account details, assets, or activity. If you have questions related to restoring your account, contact us.

How to delete your account

If you’re sure you’d like to permanently delete your Vimeo account and all content associated with it,follow these steps:

  1. Log in to your Vimeo account.
  2. Select your avatar in the upper right corner to open the main menu, scroll down to select Settings.

💡Tip: You can follow this Settings link to go to the page directly. 3. Select the Privacy tab. 4. Click Delete your account and follow the on-screen instructions.

This will permanently remove your account on Vimeo and all your videos, collections, likes, comments, etc. from Vimeo. Here’s what else deleting your account does:

How to unsubscribe an account created via a third party (Google, Facebook, Apple)

If you signed up for a Vimeo account via a third party like Google, you will need to create a Vimeo password to unsubscribe your account. See the steps at How to update your password to create a password before attempting to delete your account. Then, follow the steps above.

How to remove specific content from your account

If you don’t want to permanently delete your entire account, you can remove individual items. See the guides below for more information on deleting specific content:

  • Videos
  • Comments
  • Channels
  • Groups

How to downgrade my subscription

Not sure which plan type you have? Check “Membership” in the upper left corner of your account settings.

This article explains how to downgrade your subscription from your current paid plan to a lower-tier paid plan. Downgrading allows you to switch to a different paid plan with fewer features

  • What to know before downgrading your subscription
  • How do I downgrade my subscription to another paid tier?
  • Downgrade Enterprise or Custom plan
  • Can I downgrade my subscription early and receive a refund?

What to know before downgrading your subscription

Before you change your plan, please know that downgrades can only happen on or after your account’s next renewal date, which you can view on the membership plan page.

Below you’ll find a breakdown of how your access to certain features and storage would change with a downgrade from one paid subscription tier to a lower paid tier.

Current plans

  • Subscription Tier - Current
  • Subscription Tier - New
  • Features changed
  • Standard
  • Starter
  • Video storage: 4TB reduced to 2TB Team Collaboration: 10 seats reduced to 1 seat (unless additional seats were purchased). Player customization is limited . Features such as branding your player, custom cards, call-to-actions, lead capturing, and third-party player support are only available with Standard and higher. Selection of Vimeo video templates is reduced, and you will lose access to stock assets. No monetization capabilities . Access to sell your videos on Vimeo on Demand is limited to Standard and higher. No customizable portfolios . Showcase features such as SEO and connected Roku apps require Standard and higher.
  • Advanced
  • Standard
  • Video storage: 7TB reduced to 4TB . Team Collaboration: 10 seats reduced to 5 seats (unless additional seats were purchased). No virtual events or webinars. No marketing integrations . Connecting to apps such as Constant Contact, Hubspot, Mailchimp, Heap, and Campaign Monitor requires an Advanced plan. Lose access to live chat support .

Legacy plans

  • Subscription Tier - Current
  • Subscription Tier - New
  • Features Changed
  • Pro
  • Plus
  • Video storage: 4TB reduced to 2TB . Lose collaboration features , such as the ability to add team members to your account, review & approval tools, and the ability to see version history. No monetization capabilities . Access to sell your videos on Vimeo On Demand is limited to Pro and higher. No customizable portfolios, showcases, or chapters . Selection of Vimeo video templates is reduced, and you will lose access to stock assets. No ability to get a direct link to your video file for third-party players.
  • Business
  • Pro
  • Video storage: 7TB reduced to 4TB . Team Collaboration: 10 seats reduced to 3 seats. Marketing tools and integrations are not available on Pro; more on those tools here . Access to our Creator Marketplace , where you can find professional video creators to help make your next video, is not included in Pro. The ability to add your branding to videos made on Vimeo is limited to Business and above.
  • Premium
  • Business
  • Lose access to live chat support . Lose access to all virtual event and livestreaming features

How do I downgrade my subscription to another paid tier?

  1. Go to your billing settings.
  2. Cancel yoursubscription to disable auto-renewal. Wait for your account to reach its subscription end date.
  3. Once your account has expired, you can purchase a new plan at the lower tier you want.

Downgrade Enterprise or Custom plan

For Custom and Enterprise Plans, contact your Account Manager, Renewal Manager, or Customer Success Manager to downgrade your subscription.

Can I downgrade my subscription early and receive a refund?

Please check our refunds article to confirm if you are eligible for a refund. If your purchase is eligible for a refund, you may request it through our contact form.

How to edit my Organization’s settings

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

As an Organization Owner or Admin, you can manage users, view analytics, set security protocols, add branding, and view AI Credit and Bandwidth usage for your entire company in a centralized location.

This article provides an overview of the Organization Settings page and outlines the tasks you can accomplish there.

  • What to know before you edit your Organization’s settings
  • Organization Settings

What to know before you edit your Organization’s settings

Before you begin, please note the following:

  • Permissions: Only users with theOrganization Owneror Organization Admin role can access and manage Organization Settings.
  • Navigation: To access your Organization Settings, select your profile icon from the top navigation bar. SelectManage Organizationfrom the dropdown menu.

Screenshot: A user’s profile menu is expanded, illustrating the path to organization settings. In the header, the ‘Harth & Co.’ account button is highlighted with a red box. In the menu below, the ‘Manage organization’ option is also highlighted.

Organization settings

Your Organization Settings are organized into several tabs, which can be selected from the left-side toolbar.

Screenshot: The main navigation sidebar for an Organization. Available options are Members, Groups, Workspaces, Security and data, Brand kits, Usage, Analytics, and Billing.

Members

The Members tab displays a complete roster of every user across all Workspaces in your Organization. From here, you can invite new users, manage Admin roles, remove users from the Organization, and assign members to specific Workspaces.

Learn how at: How to add and manage team members in my Organization.

Groups

In the Groups tab, you can view alluser groups in your Organization, including those managed through SSO and custom-created groups.

Workspaces

The Workspaces tab provides a list of all Workspaces within your Organization. It provides a high-level view of the number of admins and members in each Workspace. It allows Admins to navigate directly to a specific Workspace for content and settings management.

Learn how at: How to edit my Workspace’s settings

Security and data

This section contains all Organization-wide security and data governance settings. Here, you can configure SSO, set privacy restrictions, manage data retention policies, and view audit logs for your Organization.

Brand kits

From the Brand kits tab, you can create and manage branding elements for your entire Organization in the form of logos and color palettes. Brand kits created here are inherited by all Workspaces, ensuring brand consistency.

Usage

The Usage dashboard provides visibility into your Organization’s total consumption of AI credits and storage. You can also view a breakdown of usage by each Workspace to monitor resource allocation.

Learn how at: How to Monitor Content Storage and AI Usage for my Organization

Analytics

The Analytics tab provides a centralized view of your Organization’s combined video analytics. This allows you to see performance across all Workspaces at a glance and filter down to a specific Workspace for more detailed insights.

Learn how at: How to view my Organization’s analytics

Billing

The Billing tab provides a direct link to your Organization’s billing page, where you can view and pay all invoices.

How to edit my Workspace’s settings

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

Workspace Administrators can customize their Workspace by changing its name, setting default privacy for uploads, managing branding, and enabling specific features for their team. This article provides a guide to all the settings available for managing your Workspace.

  • What to know before you edit your settings
  • Workspace Settings overview

What to know before you edit your settings

  • Administrator Permissions: Only users with the Workspace Administrator, Organization Owner, or Organization Administrator role can access and edit Workspace settings.
  • Settings inheritance:Any settings or restrictions set at the Organization level for the account that the Workspace is a part of will be inherited by the Workspace and cannot be overridden. Read more at How to edit my Organization’s settings.
  • Navigation: To access your Workspace’s settings, select your profile icon from the top navigation bar and choose Settings from the dropdown menu. If you are part of multiple Workspaces, use the drop-down menu to select the Workspace that you’re part of.

Workspace Settings

Your Workspace settings are organized into several tabs on the left side of the page. Below is a description of each tab, along with the actions you can perform within it.

Basics

This page contains the fundamental details of your Workspace. Here you can edit the Workspace name, upload a Workspace logo, and set default upload and privacy settings that will apply to all new videos added to the Workspace.

Additionally, to track events on all Vimeo players embedded on your own site, you’ll find the code to copy and paste below the Google Analytics script in the HTML of your website. Read more at Integrate the Vimeo player with Google Analytics.

Members

This tab displays the roster of all users with access to the Workspace. From here, you can invite new members, remove members, and change their roles and permissions within the Workspace.

Learn how at How to Add Members and Manage Permissions in my Workspace

Groups

The Groups tab displays a list of all user groups, such as those managed via SSO, that have been assigned to this Workspace.

You can create groups to more easily manage users, roles, and permissions. You can create a custom group or import groups from your identity provider into Vimeo through single sign-on (SSO) or SCIM provisioning. Read more at SSO Group permissions for Enterprise teams

Security and data

This page contains security settings specific to the Workspace, such as privacy restrictions and audit logs.

⚠️Note:Any security restrictions set at the Organization level will be inherited by the Workspace and cannot be overridden.

Brand kits

This section lets you manage branding for your Workspace. You can add brand kits that are specific to this Workspace, and any kits created at the Organization level will also appear here for your team to use.

Custom metadata

This tab lets administrators define the custom metadata schema that applies to every video in the Workspace — required and optional fields, controlled vocabularies, default values, and backfill behavior for existing videos. The same section also surfaces the admin compliance view (videos missing mandatory fields) and bulk-edit actions across multiple videos.

Read more at About custom metadata fields for Enterprise videos.

Vimeo AI

This page allows you to control which AI features are available to members of your Workspace. You can activate or deactivate tools like the AI script generator and the text-based video editor.

Learn how at About the Vimeo AI settings page

E-learning

If you use a Learning Management System (LMS), this is where you can configure and manage the integration for your Workspace to track and analyze online learning.

Read more at Vimeo integration with LMS (SCORM and xAPI)

How to manage custom groups, group members, and group roles

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

You can create and manage your user groups and assign specific roles to all team members, streamlining administration and ensuring the right people have the right access across your organization using the custom groups feature.

  • What to know before creating custom groups
  • How to create a custom group
  • How to add members to my group
  • How to assign a group role
  • How to invite a group into a workspace
  • Making the most out of groups

What to know before creating custom groups

  • If your account is an Enterprise organization with multiple workspaces, you must be an Organization admin to create and manage custom groups.
  • Workspace admins can then invite groups to an individual workspace.
  • If the above doesn’t apply to you, you have a single-workspace Enterprise account. In that case, you must be either the account owner or an admin to manage custom groups.

How to create a custom group

  1. After logging into Vimeo, open the account dropdown menu on the top right of the screen.
  2. Select the option that says either Manage team or Manage organization.
  3. From the left sidebar, select Groupsto create a new group or to view existing.
  4. Click on the New group button to create a new group.
  5. When a prompt appears on your screen, type your desired group name.
  6. Add the names of the members you want to include in the group and select Create group.

How to add members to my group

You have the ability to add members to your new or existing groups. Please note that you can only add current team members to your groups.

Manual search

  1. Select the three dots (…) menu and choose Manage members.
  2. At the top of the pop-up modal, select the Add members icon. ’
  3. Type in the name or email of the team member you’d like to add to your group.

Upload CSV

  1. After selecting Add members, choose the Upload CSV option at the bottom left corner of the modal.
  2. Upload your CSV file.
  • Ensure the CSV file contains a list of only the email addresses associated with the team members you’d like to add to your group.
  1. Once your file has been uploaded, a message will appear stating, Your CSV is being uploaded. Please come back later.
  2. Check back after a few minutes to make sure all team members have been successfully added to your group.

How to assign a group role

Assign a role to all current and future users inside your user group.

  1. Click on the options menu icon. Select Set default role.
  2. Click on the dropdown to assign a role.

How to invite a group into a workspace

If your Enterprise account is an organization with multiple workspaces, you have an additional layer of permission management. Organization admins can create and manage groups at the organization level as described above or using SSO.

In addition, if you are a workspace admin, you can invite any group in the org to your workspace. To do so:

  1. Open the account dropdown menu in the upper right corner, then select Settings.
  2. On the left-hand side, select Groups.
  3. Select Invite group.
  4. Search the group name, hover over it, and select Invite.
  5. Choose a role for that group: Admin, Contributor, or Viewer. All members of that group will be given that permission within that workspace unless they were individually given a different permission level.
  6. Select Invite.
  7. All members of that group will now have the assigned role in your workspace.

Making the most out of groups

  • If your Enterprise team uses SSO to log into Vimeo, you can create groups automatically using SAML and SCIM.

How to manage entries on the allowlist for my Vimeo Enterprise account

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Owners and Admins of Vimeo Enterprise accounts with custom subdomains can create an allowlist to restrict access to certain administrative features by specifying allowed IP addresses, ranges, or CIDR blocks. When activated, this setting blocks login attempts to admin functions from IP addresses that are not explicitly permitted.

This article discusses how to edit an allowlist by updating the nicknames of entries or removing them from the list.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

  • How to edit nicknames on the allowlist
  • How to remove addresses from the allowlist

How to edit nicknames

You can edit the nickname of your IP address. Due to verification needed for IP addresses, you cannot edit the IP address itself. You will need to remove the address and re-add it if you need to edit the number.

To edit the nickname for an IP address from the allowlist:

  1. Select the overflow menu(⋮) at the right of the IP address you want to edit the nickname for.
  2. Select Edit.
  3. Edit the nickname and select Save.

How to remove addresses from the allowlist:

You can remove IP addresses from the allowlist at any time. Note that you will not be able to remove your own IP address that you’ve added to the allowlist. Another Admin or the account owner will be able to.

To remove an IP address from the allowlist:

  1. Select the overflow menu(⋮) at the right of the IP address you want to remove.
  2. Select Removefrom the menu.
  3. The entry will remove automatically.

If you want to restrict access temporarily, learn how at How to start and stop IP restrictions on the allowlist for my Vimeo Enterprise account.

How to manage SSO Groups

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

You can pass group information to Vimeo via your Identity Provider using SAML or SCIM, allowing you to grant access to your content with specific departments or groups within your team.

This article discusses how to pass this group information from your IdP and how to manage those groups on Vimeo.

  • What are SSO Groups?
  • How to pass group information using SAML
  • How to pass group information with SCIM
  • If I use SSO to create groups, how can I manage them?
  • How can I see which groups someone on my team is in?

What are SSO Groups?

Using groups from your Identity Provider (IdP; such as Okta, OneLogin, Google, etc.) allows you to restrict access to content, personalize content for particular departments, and grant the ability to manage content to certain individuals. Vimeo will identify your groups and keep your groups and group membership information up to date using your IdP, either with SAML metadata or with SCIM.

How to pass group information using SAML

To pass group membership information using SAML metadata, you need to add a custom SAML attribute named “groups” that contains a comma-separated list of groups a specific user is a member of; this image shows Okta settings, but this step applies to all Identity Providers (IdPs) using SAML.

Screenshot: Screenshot from Okta attribute page with the word groups filled in under the Name space

How to pass group information with SCIM

To pass group information with SCIM:

  1. You first need to add your users within your IdP (using Entra ID (formerly Azure) or Okta).
  2. Once you’ve added the users, you can create your desired groups, then provision the users and groups.
  3. After you’ve initiated provisioning, navigate to your team settings page.
  4. Locate the Groups tab. You will see your groups have been added to your account.

If I use SSO to create groups, how can I manage them?

While your SSO groups will be created and updated automatically via your IdP, you can get information about those groups within Vimeo.

The Groups management page can be found by opening the account menu in the upper right corner and selecting Manage team or Manage organization. This is where you, as an owner, account admin, or organization admin (if your account is an organization with multiple workspaces), can see and do the following:

  • List all the SSO groups and group members synced onto your account. You can access and search any groups (including custom groups) and group members by name.
  • You can click on any of the groups and view all the members in that group.
  • Clicking the arrow next to ‘Name’ will sort the group names alphabetically.

Screenshot: Groups page with a list of groups

How can I see which groups someone on my team is in?

You can access the Manage Groups option for each member from the options (•••) icon on the team management page to view all the group memberships of that individual.

Screenshot: Team management page with Manage groups selected for specific team member

How to manage which emails I receive from Vimeo

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

There are a variety of email notifications you can receive from Vimeo about activity on your account or updates about Vimeo in general. This article discusses how to find your email notification settings and which ones you can turn on and off.

  • What to know about email notifications
  • How to update my email notification preferences
  • What types of emails can I turn on and off?
  • Suggested next steps

What to know about email notifications

  • Some types of emails cannot be turned off. You will always receive emails from Vimeo regarding your subscription purchase or renewal, lapse date, or updates to our legal policies.
  • Any email notification that can be turned off will include an ‘Unsubscribe’ option at the bottom of the message, which will also update your settings for that type of email.
  • Opting out of any of these notifications is not permanent; you can always turn them back on if you change your mind.

How to update my email notification preferences

To update your notification settings:

  1. After logging into Vimeo, open your account menu in the upper right corner, then select Settings.
  2. In the left side navigation menu, select Notifications.
  3. The Notifications settings page will open, showing all the types of emails you can receive. Select your preferences using the corresponding radio buttons.
  • For Comments, choose one of the options presented (select None to opt out of emails).
  • For all other categories, choose Yes to receive that type of email or No to opt out of receiving that email.
  1. When you’ve finished adjusting your preferences, scroll to the bottom and select Save.
  2. Your email preferences have been updated.
  • Keep in mind that for Vimeo News, it may take 2-3 business days for your preference update to take effect.

What types of emails can I turn on and off?

There are eight broad categories of emails that Vimeo sends that you can opt in and out of on the Notifications settings page, defined and detailed in the table below.

  • Comments
  • What the emails are about: Comments that others add to your videos
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Choose one of the following: All comments on videos Only replies or comments that mention you None ⚠️Note : This is a default setting. You can also adjust this on individual videos .
  • Team activity
  • What the emails are about: Actions that members of your Vimeo team take on the account
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Someone adds you to a folder Member adds a video Member views a video for the first time Anonymous user views a video Someone adds, restores, or deletes a version of your video
  • Upload activity
  • What the emails are about: Status updates for your new upload or video created in the video editor
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Video is uploaded (i.e. the upload is complete) My Create preview is ready (i.e. the video created in the editor has rendered)
  • Public activity
  • What the emails are about: Public engagement with your Vimeo account or content
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Likes Follows Messages Job shared with you Video shared with you Someone credited you in a video Someone added your video to a collection Someone’s video you added to your collection was removed ⚠️ Note : You can opt to have these emails sent only if they are related to an account or collection you follow on Vimeo.
  • Data retention activity
  • What the emails are about: Enterprise only . If your organization enacts a data retention policy, these emails inform if a video will soon be impacted by it.
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Video you’ve uploaded will be deleted per the data retention policy Any video uploaded by your team members will be deleted per the data retention policy
  • Vimeo On Demand
  • What the emails are about: Emails about either title purchases on Vimeo On Demand (VOD), or titles you sell on Vimeo On Demand.
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Purchase confirmations for VOD titles A new video was added to a VOD title you purchased. Someone purchased your VOD title. Daily and weekly performance summaries of your VOD title. Monthly and annual performance summaries of your VOD title
  • Analytics
  • What the emails are about: Summary of analytics for all videos on your Vimeo account
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Weekly summary of your account’s video analytics
  • Vimeo News
  • What the emails are about: Updates about Vimeo’s products, or activities on Vimeo about accounts and collections you follow. ⚠️Note : Any changes you make to these emails may take 2-3 business days to take effect.
  • Specific emails you can turn on and off: Daily Digest (your latest stats, new videos in your feed, updates from people you follow) Newsletters Product updates Cool offers

Suggested next steps

  • Understand more about on-site notifications
  • Navigate to other settings on your Vimeo account

How to monitor content storage and AI usage for my Organization

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

As an Organization Owner or Organization Administrator, you can monitor your company’s total consumption of storage and AI credits from a centralized dashboard. This article explains how to access and interpret the Usage dashboard for your Organization.

  • How to access the usage dashboard
  • Understanding the usage dashboard
  • AI Credit monitoring
  • How to manage usage limits
  • What happens when I approach a limit?

How to access the Usage dashboard

You can find the usage data for your entire Organization within your Organization Settings.

  1. From the top navigation menu, select your profile icon.
  2. From the dropdown menu, select “Manage Organization.”
  3. On the left-hand navigation panel, select Usage.

Understanding the Usage dashboard

The Usage dashboard provides a comprehensive view of resource consumption across your Organization. At the top of the page, you will see the total AI credits and storage used against your Organization’s limit.

Below the main overview, you will find a table that breaks down usage by each individual Workspace. You can toggle the view in this table between AI credits and Storage using the Usage type dropdown menu on the right.

Screenshot: The “Usage” dashboard, with a red box highlighting the “Usage type” filter. The filter is currently set to “AI credits,” and the table below is showing the AI credit usage for each workspace.

AI Credit Monitoring

There are two potential ways AI credits are monitored. This depends on how your account is set up with your Account Manager

  • Shared Pool: In this version, all Workspaces draw from your Organization’s total pool of AI credits. The dashboard table shows the total credits used by each Workspace.
  • Workspace Limits: In this version, specific credit limits have been set for each Workspace. The dashboard table displays additional columns for AI credits allocated and Percentage used. A colored progress bar next to the percentage indicates how close each Workspace is to its specific limit.
  • Blue bar: Greater than 0% used.
  • Orange bar: Greater than 75% used.
  • Red bar: Greater than 90% used.

How to manage usage limits

All storage and AI credit limits are managed in partnership with your Account Manager at Vimeo. To purchase additional resources, adjust your total limits, or set specific AI credit limits for individual Workspaces, please contact your Account Manager for assistance.

What happens when I approach a limit?

When your Organization reaches 90% of its AI credits limit, a banner will appear at the top of the dashboard. This banner will prompt you to contact your Account Manager to request an increase in your limits.

How to move a Live Event between Workspaces

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

If you need to reorganize your content, you can transfer alive eventfrom one Workspace to another. This article explains the process and the important consequences of moving a live event.

If you are looking for instructions on how to move your videos between Workspaces, visit

  • What to know before you transfer a live event between Workspaces
  • How to move a live event

What to know before you transfer your live event between Workspaces.

  • Administrator Permissions:
  • You must be an Organization Administrator or a Workspace Administrator in both the original Workspace and the destination Workspace to move a live event.
  • Types: The following types of events are movable:
  • Live Production and RTMP Mode if they are not live.

⚠️Note: Moving live events is a permanent and irreversible action that will impact the following. This may include loss of data. Our Support Team will not be able to recover these changes. Note these considerations before moving a live event.

  • Analytics:

  • Transferred Live Events will lose all previously collected analytics.

  • Auto Closed Captions:

  • Events will use the Auto CC minutes that are associated with the destination Workspace.

  • Engagement Data: Transferred Live Events will lose all previously collected Chat, Polls, and Q&A.

  • Extended Streaming (24/7): Available if the destination Workspace has Extended Streaming. For a workaround, visit

  • Videos added to live events:

  • Videos added to live events do not transfer with the event when it is moved from one Workspace to another.

  • For a workaround, visit

  • Videos of Live Events added toplaylists:

  • This playlist does not move to the destination Workspace when the Event is transferred.

  • Simulcasting integrations:

  • Simulcast integrations that were connected are now disconnected in the new Workspace. They will need to be reconnected. To learn how, visit About the integrations hub. Integrations are managed on a per-user basis, allowing for Workspace Admins, Contributors, and Contributor Plus users to manage marketing connections

Additionally, the following impacts are made to Event Registrations:

  • Registrant data, customized emails, and customized registration forms will transfer with live events to the destination workspaces.
  • Customized emails and the registration form will transfer to the destination workspace.
  • Users must reconnect to email lists as the connections will disconnect.

How to move a live event

If you are an administrator in both Workspaces, you can move a live event between Workspaces. The process for moving a live event is similar to moving other content from your library.

  1. Navigate to your library and select the Events folder.
  2. Select the vertical ellipses (⋮) to the right of the title of your live event and select Move Event(or Move Venue).

Screenshot: The “more options” menu for a “Test event” is open. Red boxes highlight both the three-dot icon that opens the menu and the “Move event…” option within it, showing the path to this action.

  1. In the window that appears, select the destination Workspace for the event.
  2. A final confirmation window will appear, warning you of the consequences of moving your Live Event.. You must acknowledge this warning to proceed.
  3. Select the Move button to complete the transfer

How to navigate my Vimeo account

To navigate to your account settings, click on the icon with your profile image in the top right corner of the top navigation bar.

Key features available

  • You can view the social media account you are using to log into Vimeo.
  • Invite members:Use this button to invite members to your account.
  • Settings:The settings option allows you to customize various aspects of your account, including privacy settings, notification preferences, billing, and other account-related configurations.
  • Manage team:If you are part of a collaborative environment, the Manage Team feature enables you to oversee and administer team members’ access and permissionswithin the platform and also add/remove members from your account.
  • Watch:Find your Staff Picks, Watch later, Liked videos, Collections (Portfolios, Showcases, Groups), Categories, and Channels.
  • More:Navigate to Vimeo OTT, On Demand, Purchases, Stock, Vimeo Experts, For Hire, and Messages.
  • Dark mode: Toggle the button to enable dark mode. This feature offers a visually comfortable alternative to the default light mode for users who prefer a darker interface.

Additional information

  • Additional options: The account menu provides access to other essential options such as legal information, and the ability to log out.
  • On demand:If you have VODs for sale, you can find them under Watch > Collections > Your stuff > On Demand pages. See Add videos to your On Demand page for more information.
  • My videos:You can find all of your uploaded videos in your Library.
  • Analytics: You can use this link to find your advanced analytics: Vimeo Analytics Dashboard. See How to access advanced analytics for more information.

How to organize the videos on my profile page

Although it is not possible to automatically sort the videos on your profile page, there are several ways to customize the arrangement of your videos. Visit What is the logic behind the order of videos displayed on my profile page? to read more.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: When an account is converted to a Workspace, the ability to manage the Profile Page is lost. For more information, visit Troubleshooting: I can’t visit my Profile Page after becoming a Workspace

  • How to drag and drop videos on the profile page
  • How to group videos on the profile page

How to drag and drop videos on the profile page

  1. You can move a video to another location on your profile by clicking on the six dots in the upper-right corner of the video
  2. Now, you can drag and drop the selected video.

How to group videos on the profile page

You can move a video to another location on your profile by clicking on the six dots in the upper right corner of the video, then dragging and dropping it.

You can also create sections to group your videos.

  1. To create a section, hover your cursor over the space between your video rows and select Create section.
  2. Give your section a title and drag and drop videos into it.
  3. Move a section up or down using the arrows on the top right.
  4. You can also select the slash symbol to the right of the arrows to delete the section.

⚠️ Note: When someone views your profile page, they see your sectioned videos first. If they want to load more videos, they can do so by clicking“Load more” at the bottom of the page, which will load up to ten videos at a time, as long as there are more videos to display.

⚠️Note: The labels at the top of the page originate from the categories you set for each of your videos.

⚠️Note:Videos added to My library may not appear on your profile page. Consider moving to the Team Library to make them visible.

How to purchase more video upload hours on Vimeo OTT

This article discusses ways to purchase more video upload hours on Vimeo OTT. When you purchase upload hours on OTT, you will be charged on the basis of the length of the video content that you intend to upload to OTT and not on the time that it takes to upload the content.

In this article:

How much does it cost to upload videos to Vimeo OTT? How do I purchase more upload hours? Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to upload videos to Vimeo OTT?

Our pricing depends on how many hours of video you upload to Vimeo OTT.

  • Plan
  • Number of Hours
  • Starter
  • 1 hour
  • Enterprise
  • Contact Sales

You can always purchase more upload hours for a set price. The breakdown looks like this:

  • Upload up to 1 hour of video
  • FREE
  • Upload up to 10 hours of video
  • $99 purchase as needed
  • Upload up to 25 hours of video
  • $149 purchase as needed
  • Upload up to 50 hours of video
  • $199 purchase as needed

These hours are pay-as-you-go and never expire, so any additional purchases are added to the hours of video you’ve already paid for.

Note that upload hours apply to your site and not your overall account. If you manage multiple sites on Vimeo OTT, you will need to purchase upload hours for each individual site. There is currently no way to transfer upload hours from one site to another.

How do I purchase more upload hours?

You can purchase more upload hours at any time on your Vimeo OTT site’s admin upload page (under the Content tab). Just click the Upload button, then choose to Buy more hours under the video upload time bar.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Is the cost related to how long the videos are or how long it takes to upload them?
  • The upload fee is related to the length of the video content that you are uploading, not how long it takes to upload them.
  • Does deleting videos create more upload space and grant me more hours on my account?
  • Deleting videos at this time does not return upload hours. While upload hours are non-refundable, please contact Support if you have any issues with uploading.
  • Does the “Replace Video” option count towards my hours purchased or is it in addition to that?
  • If you replace a video, it does take away from the overall allotment, since it begins transcoding immediately. So the best thing to do is make sure you have the final version ready to go before uploading.
  • Say we uploaded 10 hours for $99 and then had ANOTHER 10 to upload in 6 months. Would we pay another 99 or just the difference ($50) between the $99 we already paid and the next level <25 Hours?
  • You’d have to pay an additional $99 in that case. If you know that you will eventually be uploading over 25 hours of content we recommend buying the $149 package.
  • Does this mean we incur these fees PLUS Vimeo OTT taking a percentage of our sales?
  • The upload fee is in addition to the percentage of sales, which has not changed.
  • Does this mean that for every video that we upload which is shorter than 1 hour, we do not have to pay any fees? Or that the total of our videos is less than 1 hour long?
  • It’s one hour of total uploading that is free.
  • Why did you start charging for uploads?
  • Video on the internet is an expensive proposition, especially if you want to do it right. Our publishers are making amazing videos, so we built the Vimeo OTT player to give customers the best video-watching experience possible. That means that, for every video file that is uploaded to our platform, we transcode multiple unique versions that work across every device and adjust automatically depending on streaming performance. By charging for uploads, we will be able to continue to provide the best service across all devices. We spent a lot of time talking to current Vimeo OTT publishers about pricing before making these changes. And we developed this upfront payment structure so you don’t have to worry about ongoing incremental costs.

How to re-enable auto-renewal for my canceled Vimeo subscription

These instructions apply to all plans purchased through our site. If you are on an Enterprise account, please review our Enterprise terms and contact your account manager with any payment-related questions.

By default, your Vimeo subscription renews automatically on the renewal date listed on your billing settings page unless you cancel your subscription. If you canceled your subscription but change your mind before it expires, you can re-enable auto-renewal to avoid lapsing. This article explains how to re-enable auto-renewal for your Vimeo subscription.

  • What to know before re-enabling auto-renewal
  • How to re-enable my subscription’s auto-renewal

What to know before re-enabling auto-renewal

  • You will only see this option if your subscription hasn’t lapsed yet.
  • If your subscription has lapsed, you will need to re-purchase from our pricing page instead.

How to re-enable my subscription’s auto-renewal

To turn on auto-renewal for your canceled subscription:

  1. Navigate to yourbilling settings page.
  2. Select the Membership Plan tab to view the details of your current plan.
