How to securely share internal videos using SSO

This feature requires a Vimeo Enterprise account with single sign-on enabled.

On Vimeo Enterprise, you have the ability to share videos behind a single sign-on (SSO) gate so that your employees are required to be authenticated in order to access the content.

You can share videos behind SSO via a direct link or even via the embed code. This article discusses how to set up the SSO gate on your videos.

  • How to share my videos internally using SSO
  • How to access a video that was shared using SSO
  • Multiple identity providers

How to share my videos internally using SSO

Leveraging SSO on your videos allows you ensure that your content is extra secure and can’t be accessed by anyone outside of the organization.

You can also track and analyze team analytics for your colleagues who have authenticated with SSO before viewing your content. Follow the instructions below on how to do this.

  1. Set up SSO

First, enable SSO on your account. If you’d like to share videos with all users at your company with SSO, we recommend you set up just-in-time provisioning as part of your SSO configuration.

⚠️Note: You have the ability to set up SSO for one SAML connection or for multiple SAML connections, depending on how your organization is structured and manages user identity.

  • If you’ve only set up one SAML connection, the gate on your videos will simply direct you to that specific IdP.
  • If you’ve set up multiple SAML connections, your users will have to type in their email so Vimeo knows which SAML connection they should be authenticated with.
  1. Set your video to Private

After setting up SSO, navigate to your video and set the privacy setting to Private. Private only allows users on your Vimeo account to access the content, so after you’ve set up SSO on your account, the video will prompt your team member to authenticate using your company SSO.

See our privacy settings overview for a full breakdown of all video privacy settings.

💡Tip: If you want multiple videos on your team’s Vimeo account to have an SSO gate, you can bulk update videos in your library to the Private setting. If you are the owner, you can change this for all videos in your account settings. 3. Provide folder or content permissions

After users authenticate with SSO, they must also have permission to view that specific video. Otherwise, they will still not be authorized to access.

Therefore, you must ensure that you’ve granted permission to the content for your intended audience. This might be meant for all users, a specific group, or a specific person.

If your Enterprise organization has multiple workspaces, the intended viewers must have access to the workspace the video lives in as well.

You can either navigate into the folder that contains the video or into the video directly and select Share. Then, give permission to the correct user or user group. If you want to share with everyone in your organization, type in “All”. 4. Share or embed the video

Now that SSO has been enabled and you’ve updated permissions on the video, you can grab the link or embed code and share it with your audience.

How to access a video that was shared using SSO

Below we describe what the user experience is like for logging into a shared video with SSO when your account has been set up with one SAML connection.

Logging in with SSO into a video link

  1. Open the link to your video in your web browser.
  2. Click Sign in with SSO.
  3. Authenticate with your identity provider.
  4. After you’ve authenticated, you’ll be redirected to the Vimeo page to watch the video.

Logging in with SSO into an embedded video

⚠️Note: Currently, you can only log in with SSO onto an embedded video on demand. The ability to log into an embedded live event will be coming soon. For more information, reach out to your account manager.

  1. Open the page where the video is embedded. If this video is being viewed internally, your organization may require you to authenticate with your company SSO in order to access the page first.
  2. Find the embedded Vimeo video on the page. Click Sign in and then Continue.
  • ⚠️Note: Ensure you’ve enabled cookies in your web browser in order to take the most advantage of Vimeo embeds.
  1. A modal will open for you to log into Vimeo. If you’ve already logged in with SSO to view the internal page, the active IdP session will automatically authenticate you into Vimeo and automatically close out without requiring you to take any action.
  2. After you’ve authenticated, the player will refresh and you’ll be able to watch the video.

Multiple identity providers

If your company has multiple IdPs and you’ve therefore set up multiple SAML connections, you will have to type your email address into the Vimeo login form since Vimeo won’t automatically know which IdP to redirect you to. The experience will be as follows:

  1. Click Sign in.
  2. Type your email address into the login form that appears. The form will hide the password field after you’ve typed in the correct email address. You should then click Log in with SSO.
  3. You will be redirected to the SAML connection that your email address is associated with, where you will authenticate with your identity provider.
  4. After you’ve authenticated, you’ll be redirected to the Vimeo page (or the embedded video will refresh) so you can watch the video.

How to set up a custom subdomain for my Vimeo Enterprise account

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

A custom subdomain for your Vimeo account allows you to access Vimeo through a dedicated, branded subdomain of vimeo.work. This article explains what a custom subdomain is, the benefits of using a custom subdomain, and how to set up a custom subdomain for your Vimeo Enterprise account.

  • What is a custom subdomain?
  • Key benefits of using a custom subdomain
  • What to expect when implementing a custom subdomain
  • Additional considerations when using a custom subdomain
  • How to set up my custom subdomain on Vimeo

What is a custom subdomain?

A custom subdomain allows you to access your Vimeo Enterprise account at a URL like \0, providing a more secure and customized experience for your enterprise content.

Key benefits of using a custom subdomain

  • Network compatibility: Some strict corporate networks or school systems have disabled vimeo.com due to the public nature of the website. Your custom subdomain is only used for your enterprise content, so you can ensure {yourcompany}.vimeo.work is enabled on relevant networks while leaving vimeo.com blocked
  • Regional availability:Some countries, like Indonesia, have blocked vimeo.com. Since your custom subdomain is only for your enterprise content, your videos can now be viewed from these countries.
  • Custom experience: In addition to more branded URLs, your custom subdomain provides a branded login portal for your users to log in instead of going through the general vimeo.com login experience.

What to expect when implementing a custom subdomain

  • You will be accessing the same Vimeo Enterprise account with all your existing videos and data, just on a new domain.
  • All admin page URLs, video URLs, and embed codes generated on your custom subdomain will use the new \0 subdomain. Plus, since Video IDs remain unchanged, the URL structure of video clips will stay the same - you can basically substitute the vimeo.com domain with {yourcompany}.vimeo.work to easily switch over
  • Your team members can access the account via the new subdomain using their existing login credentials. If you’re using single sign-on, you will just have to configure a new SAML connection for the new custom subdomain.
  • While on your custom subdomain, you will not have access to public Vimeo pages like Staff Picks or the Watch page. The search bar on your custom subdomain will only display videos within your Vimeo Enterprise account, so you will not be able to search for or find other users’ content on your custom subdomain. To find other public content, you should continue to access these on vimeo.com.
  • The “public” privacy setting is not available on custom subdomains. You can use privacy settings like “unlisted,” “embed only,” “password,” and “private.” You can publish to external audiences without authentication by using “unlisted” and “embed only”, but these videos will simply not be searchable and discoverable on the vimeo.com website.
  • Existing embed codes from vimeo.com will continue to work, so you can ensure your embedded content doesn’t break once you switch over. We can also enable clip URL redirects so that any links shared with your users continue working

Additional considerations when using a custom subdomain

  • Ensure your chosen subdomain aligns with your company’s brand and that you have the necessary permissions to use it.
  • If you have videos you wish to publish publicly on vimeo.com, consider storing them in a separate Vimeo account.
  • Venues and the Vimeo mobile app are not compatible with custom subdomains.

How to set up my custom subdomain on Vimeo

  1. Choose Your Subdomain: Decide on the subdomain you want to use (e.g., \0). This should reflect your company’s brand and be something you have the rights to use. Please note that changing this subdomain later can be complex, so choose carefully.
  2. Contact Your Vimeo Success Team: Reach out to your Vimeo success team to confirm your chosen subdomain. They will then enable the subdomain on your account.
  3. SSO Configuration (If Applicable): If you use Single Sign-On (SSO), you will need to set up a new SSO SAML connection for your custom subdomain.
  • Navigate to your SSO console and create a new SAML connection.
  • Toggle on the Custom domain setting.
  • Set up the new SAML connection with your Identity Provider (IdP) using the provided SAML settings, paying attention to the \0 domain in the URLs.
  1. Access Your New Subdomain: Once your Vimeo success team confirms the subdomain is active, navigate to your custom subdomain (e.g., \0) and log in with SSO or your email and password, depending on your authentication settings.
  2. Turn off Public privacy settings: Your success team will coordinate with you on a time when they will migrate any “public” videos over to “private” or another privacy setting of your choosing. Then, we will also disable the ‘public’ privacy setting so that it cannot be used in the future. We will also enable clip URL redirects so any straggling videos already shared do not break.
  3. Turn off vimeo.com entirely: Finally, we will disable your account access from vimeo.com. You should use {yourcompany}.vimeo.work to log in and access your account going forward.

If you have any questions or need further assistance, contact your Vimeo success team.

How to set up my Organization’s Brand Kit

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

To ensure brand consistency across your entire company, Organization Owners and Admins can create a central Brand Kit. This article explains how to set up and manage your Organization’s branding, which is then automatically applied to all Workspaces.

  • What to know before you set up your Organization’s brand kit
  • How to create an Organization Brand Kit
  • How to add logos to my Organization
  • How to set brand colors for my Organization
  • How to manage my Organization’s Brand Kit

What to know before you set up your Organization’s brand kit

  • Admin Permissions: Only users with the Organization Owner or Organization Admin role can create and manage Brand Kits for the Organization.
  • Automatic Application: The Organization Brand Kit is automatically inherited by all Workspaces. While Workspaces can have their own Brand Kits, the Organization’s branding takes precedence.
  • Asset Requirements: Before you begin, make sure your brand assets are ready. The recommended file types are as follows:
  • Supported file formats include JPG, JPEG, PNG, and WEBP.
  • File sizes are limited to 10 MB.
  • Branding Updates:
  • If you edit or remove assets from a Brand Kit, videos that used those original assets will still display what was added at the time the video was created.

How to create a Brand Kit for my Organization

Your Brand Kit allows you to set default logos and colors across your Organization. To create your Brand Kit:

  1. Navigate to your Organization Settings and select the Brand kits tab.
  2. Select New Brand Kit (or Create Brand Kitif this is your first time creating a Brand Kit for your Organization).
  3. Name your Brand Kit (e.g., “Company Primary Brand”) and select Create.
  4. You will now be on the main configuration page for your new Brand Kit.

How to add logos to my Organization

You can upload logos for your Brand Kit. To do so:

  1. In the Logos section of the Brand Kit, select the “Add” button (a grey square with a plus sign).
  2. Select your logo file from your device.
  3. This will add the logo to your Brand Kit.

To manage the logo in your Organization’s Brand Kit, select the vertical ellipses (⋮) under the logo. Here, you can rename, download,or delete your Organization’s logo.

How to set brand colors for my Organization

Define a color palette to match your company’s. To do so:

  1. In the Colors section of the Brand Kit, select the + icon to add a new color.
  2. You can enter a specific hex code or use the color picker.
  3. Add all of your brand’s colors.

To manage the colors in your Organization’s Brand Kit, select the vertical ellipses (⋮) under the color swatch. Here, you can renameor delete the color swatch.

How to manage your Brand Kit

Once your Brand Kit is created, you can edit, rename, or delete it at any time.

  1. Find the Brand Kit you wish to manage in the list.
  2. Select the vertical ellipses (⋮) button to the right of the Brand Kit’s name.
  3. From the dropdown menu, choose one of the following options:
  • Rename:Change the name of the Brand Kit.
  • Delete: Permanently removes the Brand Kit.

How to set up payment for Custom & Enterprise account invoices

The following applies to customers who worked with a sales representative and executed an individualized agreement. For self-serve plans, please proceed to our list of accepted payment methods.

We accept the following payment methods for invoices within the payment portal:

  • PayPal
  • Credit card
  • ACH

While it is possible to set up the initial payment method within the portal yourself, it is not possible to switch to a different payment method yourself after that. If you need to switch to another payment method, please reach out to ar@vimeo.com to have a member of our Accounts Receivable team assist you.

PayPal

  1. Upon logging into the payment portal, you should see a PayPal option.
  2. From there, click on PayPal checkout.
  3. This will open a new window and prompt you to log into your existing PayPal account to finish setup.

Credit Card and ACH

  1. At the top of the page, navigate to Payments and then toManage Payment Methods.
  2. When you click on + Add New Payment Method, a new window will pop up where you’ll have the option to select Credit Card or ACH.
  3. Ensure that your credit card information is up to date, or if using ACH that you have double-checked your bank account details.
  4. If you have any issues setting up payment via credit card, contact the financial institution that issued your credit card in case of any security blocks.

If you wish to use an alternative payment, such as a wire transfer or check, please reach out to ar@vimeo.com so that our team can assist in setting this up for you.

How to set up SAML SSO with Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

This article discusses the configuration process for SAML single sign-on (SSO) with Vimeo Enterprise using Entra ID.

For an overview of how SSO works with Vimeo Enterprise and the first steps of this process, please head to our Setting Up SSO guide.

⚠️Note: Only the paid versions of Entra ID are supported; the Vimeo SSO solution does not support the free Entra ID tier. To configure SAML single sign-on for a non-gallery application without writing code, you need to have a subscription or Entra ID Premium.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

  • How to add a non-gallery application
  • How to configure user sign-in properties
  • How to edit the basic SAML configuration
  • How to configure my user attributes and claims
  • How to obtain the SAML signing certificate
  • Where can I retrieve my Entra ID SSO URL?
  • Suggested next steps

How to add a non-gallery application

Vimeo Enterprise will be added as a “non-gallery” application to your Entra ID portal. This means it isn’t a listed third-party integration available to all Entra ID administrators.

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center using your Microsoft Identity platform administrator account.
  2. Follow the steps on how to create your own application.
  3. Enter the display name for your new application as Vimeo Enterprise.
  4. Select the third option Integrate any other application you don’t find in the gallery (Non-gallery).
  5. Select Create. The application Overview page will open.

How to configure user sign-in properties

  1. Follow these steps to navigate to the application properties page.
  2. Configure how users who are assigned or unassigned to the application can sign into the application, and if a user can see the application in the access panel.
  • Enabled for users to sign-in determines whether users assigned to the application can sign in.
  • User assignment required determines whether users who aren’t assigned to the application can sign in.
  • Visible to user determines whether users assigned to an app can see it in the access panel and O365 launcher.
  1. Optionally, you can add a custom logo.
  2. When you’re finished, select Save.

How to edit the basic SAML configuration

  1. Follow these steps to navigate to the Set up Single Sign-On with SAML - Preview page.
  2. To edit the basic SAML configuration options, select Edit (the pencil icon) in the upper-right corner of the Basic SAML Configuration section.
  3. Enter the following settings:
  • Field
  • Value
  • Identifier (Entity Id)
  • Paste the Entity ID from Vimeo
  • Reply URL
  • Paste the ACS URL from Vimeo
  • Sign-on URL
  • Optional. Please leave this blank.
  • Relay State
  • Optional. Please leave this blank.
  • Logout URL
  • Optional. Please leave this blank.

How to configure my user attributes and claims

When a user authenticates via Entra ID SSO, your Entra ID account sends some basic information about the user to Vimeo. You will need to configure these values.

  1. In the Set up Single Sign-on with SAML page, scroll to the User Attributes & Claims section and select Edit (the pencil icon) in the upper-right corner.
  2. Configure these attributes as the following:
  • Name
  • Value
  • firstName
  • user.givenname
  • lastName
  • user.surname
  • email
  • user.email
  1. Remove the namespace schema URL from the mapping attributes; ensure that the Claim name column matches the Name column above.

To configure group claims, select Add group claimin the User Attributes & Claims section. For details, see Configure group claims.

More on assigning users and groups

  • How to manage SSO Groups
  • How to share and manage content with Groups
  • Assign users or groups to the application in Microsoft
  • Configure automatic user account provisioning in Microsoft

How to obtain the SAML signing certificate

  1. On the Set up Single Sign-on with SAML page, scroll to the SAML Certificates section.
  2. Configure the following settings for the certificate by selecting Edit (the pencil icon):
  • Expiration: Set for the maximum duration, three years from today’s date
  • Signing Algorithm: SHA-256
  • Notification Email: The email address of someone in your organization responsible for administering your Entra ID account
  1. Download the Base64 version of the certificate. This should be a .pem or .crt file.
  2. Upload your certificate to the IdP certificate section on Vimeo.

Where can I retrieve my Entra ID SSO URL?

In the Set up Vimeo Enterprise section, you can find the the SSO Login URL which Vimeo requires to link to your Identity Provider. We do not need the Microsoft Entra Identifier or the Logout URL.

Screenshot: Set up section with login URL option highlighted

Paste the URL into the Sign-In URL field on Vimeo.

Save your SAML connection, test login, and complete your SSO setup. Make sure you’ve also assigned your users in Entra ID to the Vimeo app so they can log in through your IdP.

Suggested next steps

  • After you’ve set up SAML SSO with Entra ID, you can set up SCIM.

How to set up SSO on Vimeo

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

This article discusses the setup and benefits of single sign-on (SSO) for Vimeo Enterprise users, detailing the process for creating a SAML connection, testing it, and managing user provisioning.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

⚠️Note: The new SSO on Vimeo is initially for new customers. If you set up SSO before April 2024, you’ll get it later this year, along with a guide to switch to the new experience. Contact your Account Manager for more information.

  • What is SSO?
  • Key terms and definitions
  • How to set up my SSO
  • Making the most out of SSO

What is SSO?

On Vimeo Enterprise, you can set up single sign-on (SSO) to allow your users to authenticate into Vimeo using a single credential across all your company apps. SSO allows you to manage your team’s access and keep your content more secure.

Vimeo’s SSO settings allow you to set up several different automated user provisioning methods. This will allow you to manage user access to Vimeo without having to invite every single user to your account.

Vimeo’s SSO settings are flexible, accommodating various IdPs and user provisioning methods.

Vimeo supports the following:

  • SAML 2.0
  • Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning
  • SCIM provisioning
  • Service Provider-initiated SSO
  • Identity Provider-initiated SSO

Key terms and definitions

  • SAML - Vimeo uses the SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) 2.0 standard to safely pass authentication credentials between your identity provider and your service provider.
  • Identity Provider (IdP) - Your Identity Provider is the single service your company uses for SSO across all your employees. Your users will use a single credential with your IdP to log into every app that has SSO.
  • Service Provider (SP) - In this case, Vimeo is the Service Provider to which your IdP passes the login credentials to authorize access.

How to set up my SSO

You can set up your SSO using the SSO admin console via your team settings page.

⚠️Note:Only Account Owners and Admins have access to the SSO admin console.

Step 1 - Create your SAML connection

  1. Select your profile photo located in the top right corner.
  2. Navigate to Manage team >Settings>Single Sign-On (SSO)
  3. Select the +Create Connection button Screenshot: Single sign on settings page with ‘create connection’ highlighted
  4. Enter a new SAML connection name
  • This is just a record for the connection and doesn’t need to match any specific IdP or account values. For example, this might be a useful record if you need to set up multiple IdPs for different business units or want to remember which IdP you use.
  1. Copy the Entity ID & ACS URL from Vimeo and save it for later. You will add this to your IdP in a later step.
  • Do not close the SSO console page. Keep it open until the SSO setup is finalized, as closing the window will cause the Entity ID and ACS URL links to be regenerated. ⚠️Note:Here you will also see yourSingle Logout URL. SSO single logout is an optional setting that ends Vimeo sessions for all team members as soon as they’re logged out of your identity provider.
  1. Go into your IdP & create a new SAML app for Vimeo.
  2. Paste the Entity ID & ACS URL into your IdP.
  3. In your IdP, set up the necessary SAML settings with the correct syntax, which are: email, firstName, and lastName
  • If you want to send a user group membership through SAML, you can also send a group attribute.
  • If you can’t set up custom attributes in your IdP, you can map your IdP attributes to Vimeo’s required attribute by entering your IdP attribute values in the SAML connection modal attribute mapping section.
  1. After saving the SAML connection in your IdP, now add your IDP information to Vimeo:
  • If your IdP allows you to export a metadata file, you can upload an XML file, and Vimeo will parse out the sign-in URL and cert.
  • Alternatively, you can paste items individually:
  1. Paste your sign-in URL
  2. Paste or upload your signing certificate (must be .pem, .crt, or .cert file extension).
  3. Optionally, you can enter your Single Logout URL as well.
  4. Save your SAML settings.
  • We will not force any SSO authentication at this time. You can save the SAML connection now, test it out, and then activate it later.

Step 2 - Test & Claim Domain

  • While in Step 2 of the SAML connection modal, test your SAML connection by pasting the test link into another tab (i.e., an incognito window) and try logging in.
  • Note: Test users must already be on your team. To have a user authenticate and be provisioned automatically using the test URL, activate JIT provisioning from the settings.
  • We recommend testing with a small group of users (preferably 5-10) before considering your testing complete.
  • If you encounter an issue logging in, verify the values you entered in the Vimeo SAML connection modal and your IdP. There are also other common issues that could be the cause.
  • Once you’ve validated that SAML is working, you can either close the modal and return later or you can request to claim your domain for that SAML connection if you want to force all users with your company’s domain to use SSO. Vimeo will review it and notify you once we’ve claimed the domain, which will force all users from your company to log in with SSO into Vimeo. Your approved domain claim will appear with a Claimedstatus.
  • You have the ability to claim multiple domains.
  • It is only possible to claim domains that your organization owns.

Step 3 - Set up your Provisioning options

Read our Types of Provisioning & Recommend SSO Configurations sections for info on which provisioning settings you should activate in this section.

  • If you’d like users with your company domain to sign in with SSO and be automatically provisioned, activate JIT provisioning.
  • If you’d only like users already on your Vimeo account to sign in with SSO and not set up automatic provisioning, activate team-based SSO.
  • If you’d like users to be provisioned with SCIM, set up a SCIM app and activate SCIM provisioning.
  • If there are users that were removed manually from the team, you can use the Allow reprovisioningtool to allow those users to be automatically reprovisioned with JIT provisioning.

💡Tip:You can also set up multiple options at once - check out ’Recommended SSO Configurations’ to ensure you set up SSO to best match your use case.

Step 4 - Set up SSO Settings

Activate the settings relevant to your use case:

  • Force SSO - Prevents users from logging in with email/password and disables password resets (strongly recommended).
  • This feature will be activated by default once you claim your company domain or activate team-only SSO.
  • Default role - Assign a default role to all new users created via JIT provisioning or SCIM.
  • Logout redirect URL - Specify a URL to which your users will be redirected after logging out of Vimeo.

Making the most out of SSO

To have more control over how long users on your team are logged in and precisely when they’re logged out, you can control the session duration, which includes the ability to force log outall team members.

How to share content with groups

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

You can share folders and videos with groups you’ve created and manage their access permissions for specific groups. This article discusses how to share with those groups and the different permissions you can assign.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: To use this feature, the content and groups must be located in the same Workspace where you are performing this action.

  • How to share folders with groups
  • How to share videos with groups
  • How to share showcases with groups
  • Comparison of group and individual content-level permissions

How to share folders with groups

Once you have created groups within your IdP to push them to Vimeo or use the custom groups feature, you can permit those groups to access specific folders and subfolders with either Can view, Can comment, Can edit,or Can manageaccess.

Folders can include multiple groups with different access permissions. Like individuals, groups can be given access to a folder by either the Owner, Admins, or a Contributor with “Can manage” access.

To share a folder with a group:

  1. Navigate to the Library, select the folder, and select Share in the upper-right corner.
  2. Search the group name and select what level of permissions you’d like the group to have:
  • Can view or Can comment:All users in the group will receive Viewer permissions, allowing them to watch or comment on all content in that folder.
  • Can edit: All users in the group can edit and change settings for videos in that folder.
  • Can manage: All users in the group will get the appropriate Contributor permissions with Can manage rights, allowing them to create subfolders, move content, and adjust video settings within that folder.
  1. After you’ve selected the group permission, select Share. If you would like to notify the Group via email, you can check the “Send an email notification” check box.
  2. Once you invite the group to a folder, it will appear within the Share modal alongside its permissions.

When a team member logs into the home page, they can view the folders and groups to which they have access. They can also view other folders accessible through individual permissions and those shared to the “All” group, which is created by default.

How to share videos with groups

You can also share individual videos with your created groups with ‘Can view’, ‘Can comment’, or ‘Can edit’.

  1. Navigate to your Library and select the Share button on the desired video.
  2. Select Add people
  3. Search for your group name.
  4. Once the group appears, a permission drop-down will be displayed next to the group name. Select the appropriate group permission level.
  5. Select the Share button to share your videos.

How to share showcases with groups

You can also share showcases with your created groups with Can view’, ‘Can comment’, ‘Can edit’, or ‘Can manage’ permissions. To do so:

  1. Navigate to your Library.
  2. Select the Showcase that you would like to share with your groups.
  3. Select the Share button in the top-right corner.
  4. In the share modal, search for your group name.
  5. Once the group appears, a permission drop-down will be displayed next to the group name. Select the appropriate group permission level. Screenshot: A “Share with” dialog box showing permissions for “Group 1” set to “Can view.” An expanded dropdown menu shows three options: “Can view,” “Can edit,” and “Can manage,” with “Can view” currently selected.
  • Can view:All users in the group will receive Viewer permissions, allowing them to watch or comment on all content in that showcase.
  • Can edit:All users in the group can edit and change settings for the showcase.
  • Can manage:All users in the group will receive the appropriate Contributor permissions with Can manage rights, enabling them to create subfolders, move content, and adjust video settings within the showcase.
  1. Select the Share button to share your showcase.

Comparison of group and individual content-level permissions

If a user is granted access to a folder or video through a group but also as an individual, their permissions will behave as follows:

  • Account Level Role

  • Individual Permission

  • Group Permission

  • That user’s access

  • Viewer

  • Can view or Can comment

  • Can edit

  • Can view or Can comment

  • Contributor

  • Can edit

  • Can view or Can comment

  • Can edit

  • Contributor

  • Can manage

  • Can view, Can comment, or Can edit

  • Can manage

  • Contributor

  • Can view or Can comment

  • Can edit

  • Can edit

  • Contributor

  • Can view or Can comment or Can edit

  • Can manage

  • Can manage

  • Team Owners and Admins will automatically have Can manage access to each folder; being added through a Group will not affect their permissions.

  • If a Group is added to a folder, all of the subfolders within that folder will inherit the same Group permissions.

  • You can always give higher permissions in a subfolder than in the parent folder; however, you cannot lower or remove permissions in a subfolder that are inherited from the parent folder.

  • As a TeamorWorkspace/Organization Account Owner or Administrator, you can also revoke a group’s permission from a folder. This is also true from an IdP standpoint.

  • In other words, if a group assigned to a folder has been removed from the IdP, the users in that group lose access to that folder as soon as the IdP is synced up with Vimeo, unless they had also been added individually.

  • If a team member uses the search bar in the video library or homepage, they will only see content to which they have view or edit permissions in the results. Videos and folders are hidden from search results if the team member does not have access to the folder in which they reside.

How to share folders and videos with your team

This feature requires a Pro, Premium, Starter, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: To use this feature, the video must be located in the same Workspace where you are performing this action. To learn how to transfer content between Workspaces, visit How to Move Videos Between Workspaces.

As a team Contributor, Admin, or Owner, you can share and manage access to content within your library, making collaborating with teammates easier than ever. You must have can manage or can editpermission on the resource to share it.

If you want to get feedback on your content from individuals outside of your Vimeo team, you can create a review link for either your folder or an individual video.

  • How to share a video with a team member
  • How to share a folder with a team member
  • How to share multiple folders with a team member

How to share a video with a team member

You can share a video directly with your team members if you havecan edit permission on the video. Further, you can manage access on an ongoing basis by modifying team members’ resource permissions or revoking access.

  1. Select the video you would like to share from your library and then select the Share button at the top right.
  2. A panel will appear on the right side with options for sharing, embedding, and changing the privacy settings for the video. Select Add people to give access to a team member. Screenshot: The right side panel on the video settings pages is open with various share options. At the bottom, second from the left, is the Add people option which is highlighted here.
  3. You can share the video with an existing team member by entering their name or email address. Begin typing to find the team member and select them from the dropdown.
  4. Once you have selected the team member, you have the option to send them an email notification and add a message.
  5. Select Send inviteto share the video. The recipient will be notified of the shared video via the activity bell on their Vimeo homepage.
  6. You can also use the Copy link button on the bottom right to get the link to the folder to share with an existing member of your team.

How to share a folder with a team member

You can share a folder directly with your team members if you have can manage or can editpermissions on the folder. Further, you can manage access on an ongoing basis by modifying team member’s resource permissions or revoking access.

You will not be able to directly share folders or govern access if you only have can view access.

  1. From your team library, hover next to the folder name you would like to share to open the options menu (…). Screenshot: The options menu for one folder is open with the Share option highlighted. It’s at the top of the opened menu.
  2. Select Sharefrom the dropdown menu to open the Share modal. Screenshot: The share modal for folders. It shows the Sharing tab open by default, a list of people with access, the ability to type in a name, group, or email, and the ability to copy the folder link for team members who have access.
  3. You can share the folder with an existing team member by entering their name or email address. Begin typing to find the team member and select them from the dropdown.
  4. Once you have selected the team member, you have the option to send them an email notification and add a message.
  5. SelectSend inviteto share the folder. The recipient will be notified of the shared folder via the activity bell on their Vimeo homepage.
  6. If you have an Enterprise membership, after adding your team member(s), you can use the Copy link button in the bottom right corner to share the folder link with them.

How to share multiple folders with a team member

Account owners and admins on any paid plan can invite team members to multiple folders simultaneously. Follow the steps below to add a team member to folders in bulk:

  1. On the Team Management page, locate the team member you would like to add to an existing folder.
  2. Select the options (…)menu next to the team member’s name and then select Share folders from the dropdown menu.
  3. A new modal will appear listing your folders. You may also search your Library for folders here.
  4. Select thecheckboxes next to the relevant folder names.
  5. You may choose to edit the team member’s permission for the selected folder(s) by using the dropdown menu to the right of the search bar.
  6. Select the blue Share button on the bottom right to share the folders.

How to sort and filter your team members

On theteam management page, team Owners and Admins can filter team members by their role and invite status. Owners and Admins may also sort team members by Name and Role on this page. To learn how, see the steps below:

  1. Log into your Vimeo account and navigate to the team management page.
  2. You will see the following dropdown menus to the right of the page with options to filter by role and invitation status.
  3. Select Role or Status dropdown menu and check off which options you would like to filter the list by:
  • For Role, you can select Admin, Contributor, and/or Viewer
  • For Status, you can select Accepted or Pending
  1. Select Applyto apply the filter.
  2. Use the sort options above the list of team members to see members grouped by Name and Role.

For more information about managing your team, see How to add team members to your account.

How to start and stop IP restrictions on the allowlist for my Vimeo Enterprise account

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Owners and Admins of Vimeo Enterprise accounts with custom subdomains have the option to restrict access to certain administrative features by specifying allowed IP addresses, ranges, or CIDR blocks. When enabled, this setting blocks login attempts to admin functions from IP addresses that are not explicitly permitted.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

  • What to know before starting or stopping IP restrictions
  • How to start or stop restrictions for an individual address
  • How to start or stop restrictions for the entire allowlist

What to know before starting or stopping IP restrictions

Before you use the allowlist to start or stop IP restrictions, take note of the following:

This feature does not guarantee complete protection against unauthorized access and should be used in conjunction with other recommended security practices. Vimeo is not responsible for access gained through misconfigured settings or circumvention of IP restrictions.

Allowlists are designed to add an extra layer of access control, helping safeguard sensitive management functionalities on your account, complementing Vimeo’s existing identity and access management tools.

How to start or stop restrictions for an individual address

You can temporarily restrict access to individual entries on the allowlist.

To start or stop restrictions for an individual address or range:

  1. From the account’s settings page, select Allowlist.
  2. On the allowlist, at the right of the user’s address or range, select the overflowmenu (⋮).
  3. Select pause access. Screenshot: The ‘Allowlist’ settings page displays a table of IP addresses with their nicknames, status, and other details. An overflow menu (three vertical dots) for a specific IP address entry is open, and the ‘Pause access’ option within this menu is highlighted, indicating the action to temporarily restrict access for that IP.
  4. The address status will switch to Paused. Users logging into the Enterprise account from a paused IP address will be blocked and receive the same error message as users not on the allowlist.
  5. To unpause access, select the overflow menu (⋮) again and choose Resume access. This will restore access for the IP address. Screenshot: The ‘Allowlist’ settings page displays a table of IP addresses, showing one entry with a status of ‘Paused’. The overflow menu (three vertical dots) for this paused entry is open, and the ‘Resume access’ option is highlighted, indicating the action to restore access for that IP.

How to start or stop restrictions for the entire allowlist

In addition to each entry, you can also start or stop restrictions for the entire allowlist. The Admin & the Owner are both subject to the IP restrictions; however, they do have the ability to manage the allow list and disable this feature.

To pause or resume restrictions for the entire allowlist:

  1. To restrict access for the whole allowlist, select the Restrict Accesstoggle at the top of the allowlist. This will prevent all users on the allowlist from accessing the Admin features on the account.
  2. Untoggle to resume access for the whole allowlist.

How to switch between multiple Workspaces

If you are a member of multiple Workspaces, you can navigate between them using the Workspace switcher. This article explains how to switch your view between Workspaces.

  • What to know before you switch Workspaces
  • How to switch between Workspaces

What to know before you switch Workspaces

  • The option to switch Workspaces will only appear if you are a member of more than one Workspace.
  • Switching your Workspace changes the entire context of your account, displaying the videos, folders, and settings specific to the selected Workspace.

How to switch between Workspaces

  1. From any page on Vimeo, select the name of your current Workspace in the top-right corner of the navigation bar.
  2. Select the dropdown menu under your name from the menu. A list of all the Workspaces you are a member of will appear.
  3. Select the name of the Workspace you wish to switch to.
  4. After you select a new Workspace, the page will reload, and you will now be in the selected Workspace.

How to switch Vimeo plan billing from monthly to annual

You may switch to another monthly plan or upgrade to an annual plan. To change the payment frequency:

  1. Go to Billing settings.
  2. Select Upgrade.
  3. Toggle to choose between an annual plan or a monthly upgrade under the desired subscription.

Important: If you already have an annual plan, you will not be able to switch to a monthly plan. The plan needs to lapse first so that you can choose the payment frequency for your next subscription.

How to tell if I am logged into Vimeo or Vimeo OTT

If you’re unsure which Vimeo product you’re using, this article will help you identify whether you’re on Vimeo Core orVimeo OTT.

  • Overview
  • How to identify my product?

Overview

  • Vimeo is a video experience platform designed for creating, hosting, and sharing videos.
  • Vimeo OTT is a solution for content creators to monetize their video content and offer subscriptions to viewers.

How to identify my product?

To identify if you are using Vimeo or Vimeo OTT, follow these steps:

Using the URL:
  • If your browser displays \0 in the address bar while you’re logged in, you are using Vimeo Core. *Screenshot: screenshot of an url showing 0
  • If the URL shows \0, you are using Vimeo OTT. *Screenshot: Screenshot showing an URL for Vimeo OTT 0
Using the Login Page

For Vimeo Core users:

  • You will log in at the standard Vimeo login page. Screenshot: Vimeo homepage with the headline “Share your videos everywhere with Vimeo.”
  • To confirm your membership, log in and check the Membership Plan section in your Billing settings. If you can view your account details and plan there, you are using Vimeo Core.
  • For more information on managing your profile, refer to Manage your Vimeo Profile.

For Vimeo OTT users:

  • You will use a different login page specifically for Vimeo OTT. Screenshot: Vimeo OTT landing page promoting “Start your OTT platform now,” showing devices with video content.
  • To confirm your membership with Vimeo OTT, visit the Vimeo OTT Pricing page. If the features listed there match what you use, you are logged into Vimeo OTT.

Suggested next steps

How to transfer videos between Workspaces

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

If you are a member of multiple Workspaces, you can move videos from one Workspace to another. This article explains the process and important consequences of moving videos between Workspaces. To learn about transferring Live Events between Workspaces, visit How to transfer a live event between Workspaces

  • What to know before you transfer videos between Workspaces
  • How to move videos or folders between Workspaces

What to know before you transfer videos between Workspaces

Moving content between Workspaces is a permanent actionwith significant impacts on the video’s data and settings. Before proceeding, please review the following requirements and consequences.

  • Permanent Changes:
  • ⚠️Note:Moving content is an irreversible action that will result in the permanent loss of the following data and associations for the moved content. Our Support Team will not be able to recover these changes.
  • Analytics will permanently reset to zero.
  • Members of the original Workspace will lose access unless they are also in the destination Workspace.
  • Defaults or restrictions set in the destination Workspace may override existing settings.
  • Review links will break.
  • Administrator Permissions: You must be a Workspace Administrator in both the original Workspace (where the content currently is) and the destination Workspace, or an Organization Owner/Administrator for the Organization that both Workspaces belong to.
  • Quantity Limits: You can move a maximum of 50 videos at one time, or 1 folder at a time.

How to move videos or folders between Workspaces

  1. Navigate to the Workspace containing the content you wish to move.
  2. From your library, hover over the thumbnails of the video(s) or folder that you want to move and select the checkbox that appears in the top-left corner for each.
  3. Once your content is selected, a menu bar will appear at the bottom of the screen. Select Move.
  4. In the “Move” window that appears, select the destination Workspace from the list. You can also move the video(s) to a specific folder in the Workspace.
  5. Select Move.
  6. A confirmation window will appear, summarizing the irreversible changes that will be made. Carefully review them.
  7. Select Move anyway to permanently transfer the content to the new Workspace.

Screenshot: A confirmation dialog warns of the permanent consequences of moving a video to another workspace. The message lists impacts including “Analytics will be permanently reset” and “Review links will break.” The “Move anyway” button is highlighted, indicating the final step to confirm the action.

How to transfer videos from one account to another

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

This article explains how to transfer videos between two self-serve Vimeo accounts

  • What to know before transferring videos
  • How to transfer videos between accounts

What to know before transferring videos

Before requesting a transfer, please take note of the following limitations and requirements:

  • For Enterprise users:This process described in this article applies to Vimeo self-serve plans. If you are migrating one or more Vimeo self-serve accounts to an Enterprise account, you will work with our Implementation team.
  • When videos are moved to the new account, they will no longer be available on the old account.
  • We require both the profile URLs and the login email addresses tied to your account to complete the Transfer Agreement.
  • For security purposes, we will CC the email addresses for both accounts on our correspondence with you after receiving your support ticket.
  • The following are not transferable between accounts:
  • Analytics: Your videos will lose their existing Analytics and will start from scratch in the new account.
  • Collections: We cannot move collections between accounts (Channels, Groups, Showcases, Folders, etc.), nor can we transfer videos between collections.
  • Purchases: We cannot transfer purchases (paid memberships, AI Credits, or VODs) between accounts.
  • Review pages: Your review page URLs will change and include the username of the account where your videos are being transferred.
  • VOD (Vimeo On Demand):If the videos you want to transfer are active VOD titles, you must unpublish and delete the container page where people can buy and watch your VODs before we transfer the videos. If you wish to continue selling the videos, you will need to create a new VOD page after they are transferred.
  • Live events:We cannot transfer live events or settings for live events between accounts.

How to transfer videos between accounts

We can transfer videos from one account to another with proper verification by submitting a Support ticket. When choosing the feature, select Managing videos, then select Downloading videos for the category.

To initiate the transfer, copy and paste the agreement below into the body of a support ticket and fill in the applicable information as follows:

Vimeo Transfer Agreement

My name is [FULL NAME], and I would like to transfer videos between two accounts that I own.

Please move videos out of this account: [PROFILE URL] + [MAIN EMAIL]

Please move the videos into this account: [PROFILE URL] + [MAIN EMAIL]

I would like to move the following videos: [SPECIFIC VIDEO IDS or STATE “ALL VIDEOS UNDER FIRST ACCOUNT”]

I understand all the terms of the video transfer, including the fact that all of my current video stats will be lost.

Once we’ve received this agreement from you, we can proceed with assisting in the video transfer.

How to update billing information on Vimeo OTT

This article discusses how to update your bank account information in the Billing section of the Vimeo OTT Admin.

How do I update my bank account information in the Billing section?

If you need to add or update your payout or charge information on your Vimeo OTT account:

  1. Navigate to Manage > Billing. Screenshot: An image showing Manage option highlighted in red and a drop down from that highlighting the Billing tab
  2. The Payouts tab will open by default.
  3. You can update your bank information at any time; however, other details, such as your Business name and Tax ID, will need to be handled by contacting our support team.
  4. Select the Charges tab toupdate your billing information for anything we may need to bill you for, such as fees and purchases.

How to update my email address and password

To log in to your Vimeo account, you need to use the email address associated with your account and a password. This article guides you on how to update your email address and password.

  • How to update my email address
  • How to update my password
  • What is the password requirement?
  • How to create a password
  • How to update my password if I can’t log in
  • Can I have two Vimeo accounts with the same email address?
  • Suggested next steps

How to update my email address

To update your email address:

  1. Go to your Account Settings.
  2. Select Edit next to your email address.
  3. In the window that pops up, enter the new address and your current password to confirm.
  4. Once you do this, the new email address can be used to log in to your account, and your previous address can no longer be used.

How to update my password

You can update your password by following the steps below:

  1. After logging in, select your profile photo and choose Settings.
  2. Select Password on the left sidebar to access the Password Settings page.
  3. Enter your previous password, then your new one.
  4. Select Save.

What is the password requirement?

The password requirements are as follows:

  • 8 characters minimum
  • One uppercase
  • One lowercase
  • One special character

How to create a password

If you created your account via a third party by logging in to Vimeo via Facebook, Google, or Apple,you will need to set a password to access certain features. Follow these steps to set a password:

  1. Go to your account settings.
  2. SelectPassword on the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Change Password link.
  4. You will be prompted to enter a new password and confirm it.

How to update my password if I can’t log in

If you forgot your password or your password isn’t being recognized, you’ll need to reset it using the main email address on your account.

  1. Navigate to your account settings page.
  2. Select Password on the left sidebar.
  3. Choose Forgot your password. You must be logged out of your Vimeo account to access this page.
  4. Enter the email address you used to sign up for Vimeo. Allow for a few minutes for the password reset email to be delivered.
  5. Once you receive the email, click the link, and that will allow you to choose a new password for your account.

Can I have two Vimeo accounts with the same email address?

You cannot add an email address to your account that is already associated with another Vimeo account. If you want to use an email that is already registered to another account, you’ll either need to delete the other account or change the email on that account first.

Suggested next steps

For issues related to account access, find information on I can’t access my account.

How to update my SAML connection

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

This article discusses how to manage and update SSO settings for existing SAML connections, including actions such as disabling connections, replacing certificates, and updating sign-in URLs.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

After you’ve set up SSO, you can update your existing SAML connections by returning to your SSO Settings page and selecting the Edit button.

Common actions include:

  • Disabling or deleting a SAML connection
  • You can disable a SAML connection that is no longer in use by toggling it off from the SSO Settings page.
  • To permanently delete the SAML connection, click Edit on the SAML connection, scroll to the bottom of the modal, and click Delete. Only do this when you’re ready to delete the connection.
  • Replacing a certificate
  • Your signing certificate will expire every few years. To replace it with a new certificate, open your SAML connection and either upload a new file or replace the existing certificate text. Ensure you include the necessary header & footer, then click Save.
  • Replacing a sign-in URL
  • If your company updates its IdP with a new provider, you may also need to change your sign-in URL. Copy your SAML connection and paste your new sign-in URL in the field. Click Save when you’re done. ⚠️Note: If you update your IdP, you likely need to replace the certificate as well.

How to use permission scopes to collaborate with my team

You can use granular permissions for individual videos or an entire folder. This article covers how to grant resource-level permissions to your team members to collaborate more effectively.

  • Video-level permissions
  • Folder-level permissions

Video-level permissions

To grant specific permissions to a team member for a video, follow these steps:

  1. From the video settings page, select the Share button in the top right corner.
  2. Find the team member in the list of ‘People with access’ or invite them to the video.
  3. Choose the appropriate permission scope by selecting the dropdown menu next to their name or email address.
  4. You can also Remove access here if necessary.

On a per-video basis, you can invite team members to the resource with the following permission scopes:

  • Can edit: Allows the recipient to edit the video and its settings.
  • Can comment: Allows the recipient to leave internal feedback via collaboration comments.
  • Can view:Allows the recipient to view the video page.

Folder-level permissions

To grant specific permissions to a team member for all videos within a folder, follow these steps:

  1. From the folder page, select the Share button in the top right corner.
  2. Find the team member in the list of ‘People with access’ or invite them to the video.
  3. Choose the appropriate permission scope by selecting the dropdown menu next to their name or email address.
  4. You can also Remove access here if necessary.

When granting the following permissions to a folder, the recipient will have access to all content within the folder:

  • Can manage: Allows the recipient to invite others, change access, create and delete folder content.
  • Can edit: Allows the recipient to edit videos within the folder and change video settings.
  • Can comment: Allows the recipient to leave internal feedback via collaboration comments on all videos within the folder.
  • Can view:Allows the recipient to watch videos within the folder.

How to view my Organization’s analytics

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Workspaces feature added.

The Organization Analytics dashboard provides a centralized, aggregate view of video performance across all Workspaces in your company. This allows Organization Administrators to track key metrics, identify trends, and understand the overall impact of their video content from a single location. This article provides an overview of the dashboard and the reports available for access.

  • How to access Organization Analytics
  • Navigating the Analytics dashboard
  • Filtering your data
  • Available reports

How to access my Organization’s analytics

Your Organization’s analytics can be found in your Organization’s settings page.

  1. From the top navigation menu, select your profile icon.
  2. From the dropdown menu, select “Manage Organization.”
  3. On the left-hand navigation panel, select Analytics. This will open the analytics dashboard in a new browser tab.

Navigating the analytics dashboard

The Organization Analytics dashboard is an interactive report that aggregates data from all Workspaces within your Organization. You can view the dashboard and reports as a holistic view of your overall Organization or filter by Workspaces. You can also download your analytics dashboard as a .csv file.

Screenshot: A video analytics dashboard for an organization. It shows key metrics like 4,934 views and over 15 hours of total time watched. A central line graph tracks trends for views, impressions, and unique viewers over time. Below the graph, widgets display top regions and top devices.

Filtering data:

At the top of the dashboard, you will find several powerful filtering options to refine your data:

  • Workspace Filter: The first dropdown on the left allows you to view data for all Workspaces at once or drill down to see the analytics for a single, specific Workspace.
  • Date Range: Select a preset or custom date range to analyze performance over a specific time period.
  • Content Filters: You can further refine your results by filtering for specific Content, Source, Device, Regions, and Types.

Available reports

From the main dashboard, you can navigate to several specific reports listed on the left-hand sidebar. Each report offers a more in-depth examination of a specific aspect of your Organization’s video performance and can be viewed comprehensively or by Workspace.

  • Video: Analyze video performance by tracking key metrics like views, impressions, watch time, and finishes. You can visualize engagement trends in a graph and view a detailed breakdown in a table to compare individual videos
  • Region: View metrics pertaining to the views of your videos by region within the time frame that you have selected.
  • Source: See where your viewers watched your video based on the URL of where it was posted..
  • Device: View metrics about your videos by the device type of the viewer.
  • Date: View metrics about your videos for dates within a selected time frame.
  • Team: See which members of your Organization have watched your videos, including information about video consumption and engagement.
  • Social video: View metrics about your videos filtered by the social platforms where you have shared them.
  • Social platform:Compare the analytics of all videos by social platform.

You can set the primary metric view and breakdown view for reports.

You can change the primary metric displayed in the report’s graph by selecting the dropdown menu at the top left of the chart. This allows you to switch between different data views, such as Views, Impressions, and Total time watched.

To change how the data is grouped in the table below the graph, select the View breakdown by button to choose from a variety of dimensions, including Date, Device, and Source URL.

How to view my Workspace’s analytics

You can track key metrics and identify trends for all the videos within your Workspace using the Analytics dashboard. The analytics you see are specific to the Workspace you are currently in. You will not see data from other Workspaces. This article provides an overview of how to access the dashboard and the reports available to you.

  • How to access your Workspace’s analytics
  • Navigating the Workspace analytics dashboard
  • Available reports

How to access your Workspace’s analytics

  1. Ensure you are currently switched to the correct Workspace. Learn how at How to switch between multiple Workspaces.
  2. From the Vimeo homepage, select the Analytics button from the main navigation toolbar on the left side of the page.

Navigating the Wprkspace analytics dashboard

The Analytics dashboard provides an interactive report of your Workspace’s video performance. The main dashboard gives you a high-level overview of key metrics.

  • Highlight Metrics: At a glance, you can see totals for Views, Unique viewers, and Total time watched.
  • Performance Graph: A graph tracks video performance over time, allowing you to visualize trends for views, impressions, and unique viewers.
  • Detailed Reports: Below the graph, you can find modules that highlight Top regions and Top devices, helping you understand where and how your audience is watching.

Available reports

From the main dashboard, you can navigate to several specific reports listed on the left-hand sidebar. Each report provides a more in-depth examination of a specific aspect of your Workspace’s video performance.

  • Video: Analyze performance by tracking key metrics like views, impressions, and watch time.
  • Region: See metrics related to where your videos are being viewed.
  • Source: See where your viewers watched your video based on the URL where it was posted.
  • Device: View metrics about your videos by the viewer’s device type.
  • Date: View metrics about your videos for specific dates within a selected time frame.
  • Team: See which members of your Organization have watched your videos, including information about video consumption and engagement.
  • Social video: View metrics about your videos filtered by the social platforms where you have shared them.
  • Social platform:Compare the analytics of all videos by social platform.

I can’t sign up for a Vimeo account

If you are attempting to create a Vimeo account on vimeo.com and see an error message, it’s possible our bot protection system is detecting that you may be a bot rather than a human.

Vimeo uses CAPTCHA to protect our site from spam, abuse, and other malicious intents often driven by bots. Most users will not see our CAPTCHA prompt, but our system may ask you to tick a box confirming that you are not a robot in order to proceed with creating a Vimeo account.

If you see an error message after ticking the box as prompted:

  1. Disconnect from any VPN or proxy networks.
  2. Navigate back to the Vimeo sign-up page and try creating an account again.

If you have tried these steps and still see an error message when trying to create a Vimeo account, contact us for further assistance.

Issuing refunds for web purchases

As a seller, you have a direct relationship with your customers; occasionally, your customers may reach out to you to request a refund. If you determine a refund is warranted, you can issue a refund directly through your OTT Admin for any purchases made via your OTT website.

  • Video
  • How to issue a refund
  • FAQ

Video

Here’s a video walkthrough of how to issue refunds for web purchases:

How to issue a refund

  1. Navigate to your Customers Page - Customers > All Customers
  2. Use the search bar in the upper right corner and enter the email of the customer requesting a refund.
  3. Click on the Customer’s record
  4. On theleft navigation, click on the tab Transaction history
  5. You will see rows for each web payment.
  6. Click on the … to the far right of the payment **Only users with Admin/Owner permissions role will be able to issue refunds**
  • Selecting “Refund and Disable” will refund this purchase and revoke their access to the product. If the purchase was for your subscription, their subscription will be canceled and they will not renew.
  • Selecting “Refund only” will refund this purchase but the customer will still have access to the product. If they purchase your subscription, they will still be subscribed and will be charged again on their next billing date.
  • Selecting “Send Receipt to Buyer” will send a receipt of the transaction to the email list for this customer. If a transaction has been refunded, this option will send a receipt of the refund.
  • Selecting “Send Receipt to Me”will send a receipt of the transaction to the email of the Admin user currently logged into the OTT dashboard. If a transaction has been refunded, this option will send a receipt of the refund.
  1. The Customer will receive the funds back to their credit/debit card in 3-5 business days and they will receive an email with refund confirmation information.

FAQ

Can I refund Subscription (SVOD) and Purchase/Rental (TVOD) purchases?Yes, you can issue refunds for any purchase made on the web, whether it was an SVOD or TVOD purchase.

Who can issue refunds? Only members of your team with Admin/Owner roles permissions can issue refunds. Users with the Member role will not see this feature.

What is the difference between “Refund and Disable” and “Refund Only”? Selecting “Refund and Disable” will refund this purchase and revoke their access to the product. If the purchase was for your subscription, their subscription will be canceled and they will not renew. Selecting “Refund only” will refund this purchase but the customer will still have access to the product. If they purchase your subscription, they will still be subscribed and will be charged again on their next billing date.

If I have apps, am I able to refund app purchases? You are only able to issue refunds for purchases that occur through your Vimeo OTT website and not through your apps. App platforms bill your customers directly, you will need to direct the customer to reach out to the platform where they purchased for a refund. You can provide them with this help document with instructions specific to each app platform.

Is there a time limit on how long I can issue a refund? Yes, you will only be able to issue a refund to purchases that occurred in the previous 30 days. If you want to issue a refund for purchases made more than 30 days prior, please reach out to our Support Team.

I am not seeing the … next to a purchase on the Customer’s record, why not?The purchase is probably more than 30 days old or not a web transaction.
