Add Google Tag Manager ID to your Vimeo OTT site

Google Tag Manager is a tag management system (TMS) that allows you to quickly and easily update measurement codes and related code fragments collectively known as tags on your website or mobile app. It allows you to manage third-party tags in the same place as your Google tags. Read more about Google Tag Manager Overview.

This article discusses how to add Google Tag Manager ID to your OTT site.

How do I add a Google Tag Manager ID?

If you are an Enterprise seller on Vimeo OTT, you can add tags and triggers for tracking various activities across your site without needing to add code to be deployed to your site using Google Tag Manager (GTM).

Adding the tag will automatically add your GTM container to the site which will begin tracking data immediately. Similar to other tracking on Vimeo OTT sites, this will be disabled for sellers that are Made For Kids and customers who have requested that they not be tracked per GDPR regulations.

Once you set up Google Tag Manager, go to the Workspace section of your Tag Manager to find your container ID (it will look like “GTM-XXXXXXX”).

💡Tip:If you have issues setting up GTM, consider installing the Google Tag Assistant extension, which can help you troubleshoot the issue. If you see a 404 error, make sure your container is published even if there is nothing published within it yet.

In your OTT site admin, navigate to Manage > Site.

Screenshot: manage___site.png

Select the Tracking tab. Paste your ID under Google Tag Manager Container ID. Be sure to save your settings.

Screenshot: tracking.png

You can only add a single GTM Container ID, as Google recommends only using one container per web domain. If you feel you need more, reach out to your account manager.

Add tracking pixels to your Vimeo OTT checkout page

We offer support for adding conversion tracking pixels from services like Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), or AdWords to your checkout page. A pixel tracks certain events (like when someone makes a purchase through your site, etc); when the events you’re tracking are triggered, the pixel sends the data over to your analytics.

While the pixel is installed on the OTT site, the conversion data (i.e., whether customers took the actions you’re tracking) for each pixel will be viewable on each platform’s end (i.e., the data for your Facebook pixel will be available in your Facebook account.

⚠️Note:If your site is marked ‘Made for Kids,’ pixels can only be enabled for conversion tracking, not page tracking.

How do I add Facebook Pixels to my Vimeo OTT site?

Facebook requires domain verification, which you can learn how to do for your OTT site here.

To add Facebook Pixels to your Vimeo OTT project/site:

  1. From the main admin menu, navigate to Settings > Site > Tracking
  2. In the Facebook section, add your Facebook Pixel ID (this is included from Facebook when you complete setting up your ad).
  3. Select a product to attach it to under Associated Product. You can also select All Products for your site.
  4. If you have multiple pixels, click the (+) button to the right of the Associated Product.
  5. Be sure to click Save in the upper right corner of the page.

Screenshot: facebook_pixel.png

After you’ve installed your Facebook Pixel, you can check if it’s working correctly by using Facebook’s Pixel Helper extension for Google Chrome. You’ll find that in Facebook’s help documents guide.

Pixel Events

By default, the Facebook pixel is set to track the following events:

  • PageView: sent for all non-video playback pages of your site
  • InitiateCheckout: sent whenever a customer views the checkout form
  • Purchase: sent after a customer successfully signs up and begins a free trial or subscription (Paid subscription sites only)
  • Complete Registration: sent after a user successfully signs up for your site (Free subscription sites only)

How do I add X Pixels to my Vimeo OTT Site?

On X’s side, the pixel is referred to as a “tag,” but it performs the same function. To add X Pixels to your Vimeo OTT site:

  1. From the main admin menu, navigate to Settings > Site > Tracking.
  2. Add yourX Pixel ID (this is included from X when you complete setting up your ad).
  3. Select a product to attach it to under Associated Product. You can also select All Products for your site.
  4. Be sure to click Save in the upper right corner of the page.

Screenshot: twitter_pixel.png

After you’ve installed your X tag, you can verify to see if it’s working by using X’s Pixel Helper browser extension for Google Chrome. You’ll find that in the “How to verify website tags are working” section of this help document on X’s side.

Pixel Events

By default the X pixel is set to track the following event:

  • PageView: sent for all non-video playback pages of your site
  • InitiateCheckout: sent whenever a customer views the checkout form
  • Purchase: sent after a customer successfully signs up and begins a free trial or subscription (Paid subscription sites only)
  • CompleteRegistration: sent after a user successfully signs up for your site (Free subscription sites only)

How do I add Google Adwords Pixels to my Vimeo OTT Site?

Adding Google Adwords Pixels to your Vimeo OTT site is also easy. Once you have a Google Adwords account, you can generate a pixel ID, which is what you’ll need to enter into the Vimeo OTT settings page.

  1. From the main admin menu, navigate to Settings > Site > Tracking.
  2. Add your Google Adwords Pixel ID & Label (this is included in Google Adwords when you complete setting up your ad).
  3. Select a product to attach it to under Associated Product. You can also select All Products for your site.
  4. Be sure to click Save in the upper right corner of the page.

Screenshot: google_adwords_pixel.png

Once you’ve set up your Google Adwords pixel, you can check to make sure it’s working correctly by validating it with the Tag Assistant extension for the Google Chrome browser.

Pixel Events

By default your Adword Pixel is set to track the following event:

  • Purchase: sent whenever a customer successfully subscribes or purchases from your site

Adobe Premiere Pro integration with Vimeo

The Adobe Premiere Pro integration with Vimeo allows you to upload videos from Adobe to your Vimeo account and manage quick video actions all in Adobe. You can access the integration here: Vimeo Panel on Adobe.

  • How to upload a video from Adobe Premiere Pro to Vimeo

How to upload a video from Adobe Premiere Pro to Vimeo

Follow the instructions below to export a video from Adobe to Vimeo:

  1. Connect to the Adobe Premiere Pro integration in Vimeo > Settings > Connected Apps. It will take you to the Adobe app listing page.
  2. Install the Vimeo Panel from Adobe Creative Cloud by selectingFree.
  3. Once installed and logged into, Adobe Premiere Pro, select Window > Extensions > Vimeo.
  4. You will be prompted to allow and activate the integration. Select Activate and proceed to log in to your Vimeo account. The integration supports logging in with SSO, a social account, or an email address.
  5. Select Allowfrom the next modal window.
  6. After logging in, you must enter an Activation code to verify your account.
  7. Once your account has been successfully linked, you can upload content from Adobe to Vimeo. Select Upload to Vimeofrom the modal in the center of the screen. ⚠️Note:This will only show your uploads from Adobe to Vimeo.

  11. Once you have updated its settings, select Upload.

  13. Select the stacked dot menu to edit settings, copy link, copy review page link, export markers as comments, import comments as markers, view comments, download video to timeline, replace video, or delete from Vimeo.

How to use review tools with Adobe Premiere Pro

Within Adobe Premiere Pro, you can access and resolve comments, @mention team members, and download your video onto the timeline. Review tools are available with a paid plan on Vimeo - Pro, Standard, or above.

Review comments
  • Select thecomments box under the video to review comments for each video.
  • You can access all your time-coded comments from Vimeo directly in Adobe Premiere Pro and @mention people on your team to review comments. ⚠️Note:Currently, you cannot leave time-coded comments within Adobe, however, time-coded comments from Vimeo will sync into Adobe.
Download your video

Once you receive comments and are ready to start editing, you can download your video onto your Adobe Premiere Pro timeline and import your comments as markers.

  1. Select the stacked dot menu to the right of the video in your Library.
  2. SelectDownload to timeline.
  3. Next, select Import comments as markers.
  4. Time–coded comments will appear as markers within your timeline.
  5. When you’re done, you can resolve comments directly within Adobe.
Switch Vimeo team on Adobe

If you are part of more than one team on Vimeo, you can access each of your team libraries from within Adobe Premiere Pro.

  1. Navigate to your different Vimeo team library by selecting your Team logo in the upper right corner of the modal.
  2. Select the team you would like to access from the dropdown menu.
  3. Once you’ve navigated to the desired team account, you can access the same folder library structure within Adobe Premiere Pro that you have configured in Vimeo.

Google Tag Manager Integration

⚠️Note:Google Tag Manager is only available to Sellers on the Enterprise OTT Plan. If you are interested in learning more please contact our Sales Team.

Google Tag Manager (GTM) is a tag management system that allows you to track the usage of your website and easily trigger both Google and third-party code snippets (generally referred to as “tags”) without having to modify the source code of your site. While Vimeo has quite a few native OTT integrations, GTM expands the platform to software that we might not support out of the box.

This article discusses how to add a Google Tag Manager Container ID to your OTT site.

First, you’ll create a container for your OTT Site and then, using Google’s web-based interface, you can add tags and then define rules for when each tag should fire.

Some examples of what you can add via GTM:

  • Google AdWords Conversion Tracking
  • ⚠️Note: OTT also offers a native Google Ads integration
  • Remarketing and/or Conversion Tracking
  • Custom HTML and Javascript

If you are new to GTM, we recommend reading about Google Tag Manager here.

How do I add a Google Tag Manager Container ID?

You’ll need to create a Google Tag Manager account here if you haven’t already done so. Be sure to select Web for your target platform, as Vimeo OTT does not currently support GTM in our Branded Apps.

Once you’ve created an account, go to the Workspace section of your Tag Manager to find your container ID (it will look like GTM-XXXXXXX).

Now you’ll need to add that ID to your Vimeo OTT Site. In your OTT site admin,

  1. Navigate to Manage > Site > Tracking tab.
  2. Paste the full container ID under the Google Tag Manager Container ID.
  3. Saveyour settings.

Adding the tag will automatically add your GTM container to your OTT site which will begin tracking data immediately. Similar to other tracking on Vimeo OTT sites, this will be disabled for sellers who are Made For Kids and customers who have requested that they not be tracked per GDPR regulations. You can only add a single GTM Container ID, as Google recommends only using one container per web domain.

Verifying that Google Tag Manager is installed

If you’d like to confirm that Google Tag Manager is installed properly, you can use either of the following tools to help troubleshoot the issue:

  • Preview Mode in Google Tag Manager
  • The Google Tag Assistant (Legacy) Chrome Extension.

Tracking Events in Google Tag Manager

Tags are configured to send data when an event occurs, such as page views, video plays, or purchases. Tag Manager uses triggers to specify what events to track and “listens” for that event to occur. When the event occurs, the tag fires and sends associated data, such as an item value or transaction ID, to the specified destination.

⚠️Note: For these data layer events to be populated on your OTT Site, you must have also added your GA4 tracking code in Vimeo OTT.

GTM Events

Below is a list of some of the most commonly tracked Events in Vimeo OTT

  • Event
  • Description
  • page_view
  • When the page loads or the browser history state is changed by the active site.
  • login
  • When a user completes login from the login page.
  • Search
  • When a user types a searchable term in the site’s content search field.
  • begin_checkout
  • When a user lands on a checkout page with a payment form.
  • sign_up
  • When a new customer record is created via checkout or FVOD registration.
  • purchase
  • When a checkout transaction is completed.

GTM Variables

These are the OTT parameters that you can create as variables in GTM

  • Variable Name
  • Description
  • site
  • Numerical Site Key #
  • user_id
  • Unique User #ID. Only available when Customer is logged in
  • search_term
  • When a user types a searchable term in the site’s content search field.
  • checkout_method
  • Payment method type (Credit Card, Google Pay, etc)
  • checkout_type
  • payment_element or card_element
  • coupon
  • Promo code or coupon used, if applicable
  • currency
  • 3-letter currency code (e.g. USD, GBP)
  • discount
  • Discount amount, if any
  • items
  • An array of the items that have been purchased, includes: Coupon Currency Discount Item_category (e.g. buy/subscription/gift) Item_category2 (e.g. purchase/rent / monthly/yearly) Item_id Item_name price
  • page_title
  • Name of the page
  • tax
  • Tax amount, if any
  • transaction_id
  • Unique identifier for the transaction
  • value
  • Amount paid in viewer’s currency, excluding taxes and discounts

Creating Triggers, Variables & Tags

Every Vimeo OTT event that you want tracked must be created as an Event Tag in Google Tag Manager.

For each Event, you need first to create a Trigger that listens for certain events to happen such as a button click or page view. The trigger tells the tag to fire when the event is detected. Then, in the Variables tab, you will create the custom parameters associated with each event.

Setting up your Triggers

  1. Login to Google Tag Manager

  2. Click Triggers in the left-side navigation, and then click the New button

  3. Select Trigger Configuration

  4. Choose the Trigger Type. This could be a Page View, a Click, or a Custom Event

  5. If you imagine a tag being triggered on all pages choose All Pages, or you can choose Some Page Views and enter a page path (e.g. /browse)

  6. Give the Event a name.

  7. Save

Defining Variables in GTM

We automatically push several events into GTM as customers navigate through your OTT Channel but to leverage them in your tags or triggers, you must first define them as Variables. This is an essential step.

To create a Variable in Google Tag Manager, follow these steps:

  1. Login to Google Tag Manager

  2. Click Variables in the left side navigation, and then in the User-Defined Variable section, click the New button

  3. Click on the Variable Configuration box and under Variable Type

  4. Select Data Layer Variable

  5. Describe your Variable at thetop left and then add the Name of the Variable based on the above list of Parameters available in the Vimeo OTT data layer. These are Data Layer Variables that are part of the eventModel in the JSON object, so all variables will follow the format: eventModel.[VARIABLE NAME].

  6. You’ll want to create Variables for as many of the Vimeo OTT parameters that you would like to track. Your user-defined variables should look similar to this:

Creating Tags

Now that you have defined both the triggers and variables, you can create a Tag that fires based on the trigger and sends the appropriate parameter.

  1. Login to your Google Tag Manager account

  2. Click Tags in the left side navigation, click the New button, and then click Tag Configuration

  3. Give the tag a name

  4. Choose the type of Tag. For third-party integrations, this will often be “Custom HTML” or “Custom Image” but there are many other tags to choose from

  5. Complete the integration steps

  • This will vary depending on the integration.
  1. Edit Triggering
  2. Select the corresponding trigger that you’d set up previously to determine when the tag should fire.
  3. Click Save

Publish Your Container Changes

Google Tag Manager does not automatically send these changes out until you Publish.

Click Submit in the top right of the page once you have configured your Triggers and Tags.

How to add support for Roku search feed

Roku Search Feed feature unlocks a powerful new way for users to discover your content. With Roku Search Feed, your app’s video content will appear directly in the Roku platform search results.

  • Increased Discoverability: Attract new users by exposing your content to a wider audience through Roku’s platform-wide search.
  • Streamlined User Experience: Simplify content discovery for existing users by allowing them to find and access your videos quickly and easily without needing to navigate directly to your app.
  • App Download Prompts: If a user finds content they like and doesn’t have your app, Roku will prompt them to download it, driving new installations.

If you do not have a Roku app, reach out to your Account Manager or OTT Sales Team for more info on adding a Roku app to your site.

  • Adding required metadata
  • Episodes
  • Series
  • Seasons
  • Movies
  • Enabling the Roku feed

Adding required metadata

Roku Search Feed will only index your content if you have added specific pieces of required metadata. In your OTT admin site, click on the “Content” dropdown and navigate to a collection or individual video. Metadata fields are found on the General, Distribution, and Discovery tabs of videos and collections. For each piece of content, specific metadata is required:

Episodes
  • Subscription Plans: A plan must be added to an episode. Episodes without plans will not appear.
  • Media Type:The Media Type field must be set to Episode
  • Episode Number: Episode number needs to be assigned.
  • Genre: At least one genre must be assigned, choose the closest fit to your content type from the pre-defined genre list.
  • Rating:You must set a value for each rating sub-field.
  • Rating: e.g. ‘TV-PG’
  • Location: US or no location
  • Rating Board: e.g. ‘USA Parental Rating’
  • Release Date:Date the video was released and location.
  • Location: US or no location
Series
  • Visibility - The series must be set to published
  • Thumbnail - You need to set a Thumbnail for the series
  • Contain Minimum One Season - The series must contain a minimum of one published season with at least one episode (see Episode required fields)
Seasons
  • Visibility - Season must be set to published
  • Contain Minimum One Episode: The season must contain least one episode (see Episode required fields)
  • Season Number: The season must specify the season number.
Movies
  • Visibility - The Movie must be set to published and the Primary video of the Movie must be added to a subscription plan. Movies without plans will not appear in the Roku search.
  • Thumbnail: You need to set a 16:9 Thumbnail for the episode
  • Media Type:The Media Type field must be set to Movie
  • Genre: At least one genre must be assigned. Choose the closest fit to your content type from the pre-defined genre list.
  • Rating:You must set a value for each rating sub-field.
  • Rating: e.g. ‘TV-PG’
  • Location: US or no location
  • Rating Board: e.g. ‘USA Parental Rating’
  • Release Date:Date the video was released and location.
  • Location: US or no location

Enabling the Roku feed

Once you have added the required metadata to your videos, contact your Account Manager and ask them to enroll you in the Roku Feed program. They will coordinate with the Vimeo OTT Apps team who will then update your Roku app to include the feed. App updates and resubmission to Roku typically take ~2-3 weeks. Once your app update is approved and live, search updates typically take 24 hours to start appearing in Roku Search.

Roku search looks across all channels so your videos may not show for generic searches like “yoga” or “horror movies”. The more informative and specific you can make your title and description the more easily your content will be found in Roku’s search feed.

How to live stream Vimeo events using the XSplit Broadcaster integration

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

Vimeo’s native integration with XSplit Broadcaster enables you to stream to Vimeo from XSplit Broadcaster directly, without the need for your event’s RTMP URL and stream key. This article explains what XSplit Broadcaster is and how to connect your Vimeo account to XSplit Broadcaster.

  • Video overview
  • What is XSplit Broadcaster?
  • How to set up XSplit to stream to Vimeo

Video overview

Watch the video below for a demo of the Vimeo integration with XSplit.

What is XSplit Broadcaster?

XSplit Broadcaster is a software-based livestreaming encoder that can be installed on Windows systems. You can log in to your Vimeo account in XSplit Broadcaster and choose which event to stream to within the application.

How to set up XSplit to stream to Vimeo

💡Tip: See XSplit’s help center for their instructions on using XSplit with Vimeo.

  1. Download XSplit.

  2. Open XSplit and open the stream settings dropdown above the stream preview.

  3. Select Vimeo.

  4. Select Authenticate XSplit to use Vimeo.

  5. Log in to your Vimeo account.

  6. If you are a member of multiple teams or Workspaces, choose the correct team where you would like to stream your live event.

  7. When you are ready to start your broadcast, a dialogue box will appear that allows you to select from the live events in the selected Vimeo team account. Choose your preferred option and select Start broadcast.

  8. Once your stream has ended, your recording will be saved to your team library.

How to order captions and subtitles with Rev

Vimeo partners with Rev to simplify the transcription process for your Vimeo videos. Read more about Vimeo’s integration with Rev.

You can order human-generated subtitles and captions from Rev on the settings page of your videos in the Languages menu.

To order captions and subtitles with Rev:

  1. Select your video from your Library.
  2. Select the Languages button from the toolbar on the left.
  3. At the bottom of the Languages menu, select “Order captions and subtitles perfected by Rev’s team of experts”.
  4. Select Order captions with Rev.
  5. Select the options you need for your video. 💡Tip:Rev can transcribe videos in English and Spanish.
  6. Once you’ve finalized your order details, click Checkout. You will be prompted to log in to your Rev account or create a new one to proceed.
  7. After you have signed in to Rev, you’ll be taken to the Payment screen. Once your order has been placed, Rev will email you a copy of your receipt (which you can also find in your Rev account).
  8. You will see the option to link your Rev and Vimeo accounts. Doing so will enable Rev to send your caption file directly to your Vimeo video. ⚠️Note: Make sure the checkbox “Automatically deliver files back to Vimeo” is selected to ensure that your caption/subtitle file is automatically uploaded to your video .
  9. When Rev’s team has finished creating your captions or subtitles, the transcription file will be automatically added to your video if you have linked your Rev and Vimeo Accounts (turnaround time varies based on the languages requested and the length of your video, but typically will be between 24 and 48 hours.)

For more information from Rev Support, see Rev’s guide at How Do I Use the Vimeo Integration?

How to publish my video on social media

This article discusses the benefits and process of publishing videos from Vimeo directly to various social media platforms.

Publishing to social is a way for Vimeo members to share their videos directly on social platforms (Facebook Pages, YouTube, Twitter, LinkedIn Company Pages, Shopify Product Pages, and TikTok ads) from the Library in one easy step.

Publishing to social platforms differs from sharing a link on those platforms, as the video is uploaded as a native video, making the experience seamless for your viewers. Since different audiences exist on various platforms, this feature will enable you to track your video’s performance across multiple platforms directly from a dashboard within your Vimeo account.

See relevant restrictions and requirements for publishing to social media at Restrictions and requirements for publishing to social.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:While connections to social sites are user-specific, the ability to share andprivacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit “How to edit my Organization’s settings” or”How to edit my Workspace’s settings“.

  • How to publish your videos to social
  • Analytics
  • Why publish on social?
  • Replacing or deleting videos

How to publish your videos to social

Contributor, Contributor+, and Admin team members can publish videos on their connected social accounts. To do so:

  1. Log in to your Vimeo account, then go to your Library.
  2. Once there, select the video you want to share to a social platform.
  3. Select the Share button in the video settings page.
  4. Now select the Publish icon at the bottom.
  5. A new modal will open with your connected accounts. If you haven’t connected your social accounts to Vimeo, you’ll need to connect each platform you want to use. Select the Connect button to go to your account settings.
  6. Select the social account you want to use, and then follow the directions to authorize Vimeo to publish your videos.

Once you’re connected, you’ll be able to publish videos directly to Facebook Pages, YouTube, Twitter, LinkedIn Company Pages, and Shopify Product Pages as native videos, while keeping track of their statistics (views, engagements, and shares) from Vimeo. This enables you to see how your videos perform on each platform. You’ll be able to edit your privacy settings in the publish to the social module, which means that you’ll always have control over where your posts are shared.

Analytics

After you’ve published a video to social, you can navigate to Analyticson the right side of the video page to see how it’s performing.

You’ll be able to check on the following aspects under Engagement:

  • Views (i.e., how many people saw your video and watched it)
  • Likes (i.e., how many people clicked the “Like” button on the social platform)
  • Comments (i.e., the number of comments left on your video on the social platform)

Please note that on Facebook, analytics will only reflect if the video was shared to a page, rather than to someone’s timeline.

Our Library won’t show analytics for videos shared on Twitter, or Shopify, unfortunately. You’ll be able to see specific engagement analytics on Twitter’s side, however, which will include retweets and likes but not video analytics.

Why publish on social?

Video plays a large role in the way people consume content on social media — wherever you turn, across platforms, people are watching videos. As a video creator, there are many reasons you might want to incorporate publishing to social platforms directly from Vimeo into your workflow.

First, each social platform is different — it has a distinct audience and people interact with video in various ways — so in many cases, it is best practice to publish different video cuts optimized for each platform. This has the added benefit of allowing you to track the performance of each version in its intended environment over time. Publishing to social can also be a way for you or your team to showcase a teaser or trailer for a longer-form video that lives on Vimeo.

Additionally, it can help you make platform-specific decisions about your marketing strategy.

Finally, there are benefits to publishing videos on each platform — that is, videos uploaded directly to the platform rather than being linked to or embedded on it. For example, Facebook tends to favor videos that are uploaded natively to its platform due to the algorithms in place. Features like auto-play for native videos also help with increased view rates and overall engagement.

Replacing or deleting videos

Deleting a video on Vimeo will not remove it from any platforms you’ve already published to. To delete a video, you must remove it from each social platform individually.

Similarly, replacing a video on Vimeo will not remove it from other platforms. If you’ve replaced a video, you’ll need to republish it to any social platform.

How to publish to TikTok for Business

Vimeo has partnered with TikTok to empower small businesses to quickly build high-impact TikTok video ads in seconds, allowing you to reach new customers, engage audiences, and make your brand stand out. You can choose one of our TikTok templates within our video creation tool and customize them with your branding, stock photos and videos, and commercially licensed music. You can then publish your video ads directly from Vimeo to TikTok’s ad manager and start running your campaigns.

This article discusses how to publish your Vimeo video to TikTok for Business.

Visit the TikTok hub page to read more about this integration.

How to start publishing to TikTok

  1. First, you will need to connect your Vimeo account to your TikTok for Business account. To do this, go to your account settings and navigate to Connected apps.
  2. Locate TikTok for Business, then click the corresponding Connect button.
  3. Once that’s done, you can choose a template (click the template, then click Customize), or start from scratch to create a video for TikTok.
  4. Edit your video as desired, then select Save in the upper right corner to be brought to the video settings page.
  5. Select the downward arrow beside the Share button in the upper right corner of the video settings page and then select Publish > Publish to social. Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-09-02 at 1.31.05 PM.png
  6. Select TikTok For Business at the bottom of the list. If you have not yet connected your accounts, you can do so from here.
  7. Input the title for TikTok and then select the advertiser ID (which you can find in your TikTok ads manager) from the dropdown menu, then click Next.
  8. Verify where your video is being published, and then click Publish when you’re ready.
  9. After a moment, you should find your video in your TikTok Ads Manager under Assets > Videos.

Questions about advertising on TikTok? See TikTok’s detailed support documentation at TikTok Business Help Center.

How to record and upload your Zoom meetings to Vimeo

The Vimeo app for Zoom allows you to back up your Zoom cloud recordings directly to your Vimeo account—no more downloading to your computer, then logging in to Vimeo to upload. Once your recording is on Vimeo, you’ll have access to our video player, collaboration tools, customizable privacy, embed settings, and much more.

See theZoom hub page to read more about this integration.

⚠️Note: If you delete a video that is stored both in Zoom and Vimeo in one location (e.g., Zoom), it will NOT simultaneously be deleted in the other location (e.g., Vimeo). This goes both ways.

  • How to connect Zoom to my Vimeo account
  • Zoom Recordings on your preferred team and folder destination
  • Upload defaults
  • Zoom recording privacy settings
  • Can I connect multiple Zoom accounts to one Vimeo account?
  • How to uninstall the Zoom app
  • Membership Tiers and Folder Selection Defaults

How to connect Zoom to my Vimeo account

  1. To set up the Vimeo app for Zoom, you’ll need to have an account on Vimeo and recording permissions on your Zoom account. If you do not have recording permissions enabled, contact the owner of your Zoom account.
  2. Click here to install the Vimeo App for Zoom.
  3. Go through the setup flow, accept the terms, and then you’ll see the installation confirmation page. After installation success, you’ll land on your Zoom Recordings folder (or assigned folder during installation).
  4. Once installed, you’ll be able to select Record to cloud on your Zoom meeting. This cloud recording will transcode and upload to your connected Vimeo account after your meeting recording ends.
  5. After your video finishes transcoding, it will appear in the Zoom Recordings Folder on Vimeo, where you’ll be able to access all our tools for sharing and collaboration.

⚠️Note: If you are a team member on an Enterprise account, your recordings will upload to your My library folder by default. You can then edit any settings on it before moving it to another folder on the account as desired. If you are a team member on a non-Enterprise account, your recordings will upload to the assigned folder during installation.

Zoom Recordings on your preferred team and folder destination

In order to select the preferred team and folder destination for your Zoom recordings, you will be prompted to make this selection while first installing the Vimeo App for Zoom.

Upload defaults

You will be able to change your preferred team and folder destination for all of your Zoom recordings from your existing settings by navigating to Zoom integration settings or via your Vimeo account settings and then choosing your preferred default settings

At this time, it is not possible to choose which meeting view of your Zoom meeting is recorded and uploaded to Vimeo. The view is chosen automatically in the following priority order:

  1. Shared screen with speaker view
  2. Share screen with gallery view
  3. Active speaker
  4. Gallery view
  5. Shared screen

Zoom recording privacy settings

All videos uploaded from Zoom will have the default privacy setting Private. You can update the recording’s privacy setting after it uploads to your Vimeo account.

Can I connect multiple Zoom accounts to one Vimeo account?

It’s only possible to link multiple Zoom accounts into one Vimeo team account if you have a Vimeo Enterprise account with Video Library enabled. In that instance, a Zoom Recordings folder will be created in each team member’s ‘Private to Me’ folder after they install the Vimeo app on Zoom and record a meeting. Those recordings can then be edited and moved into another team folder in the Vimeo team account.

If you do not have Vimeo Enterprise with Video Library, then installing the Vimeo app on Zoom ties one Zoom account to one Vimeo account, with each Vimeo account having its own Zoom Recordings folder.

How to uninstall the Zoom app

  1. Go to your Zoom Integration settings.
  2. Find the Zoom app listed and toggle to Disconnect.

For detailed uninstallation instructions, please refer to Zoom’s documentation at Installing and uninstalling apps from Marketplace.

Membership Tiers and Folder Selection Defaults

Enterprise account with Private to Me

  • You will see the team switcher
  • You will see the Zoom Recordings folder nested underPrivate to Me
  • You can click next
  • You can skip

Enterprise account without Private to Me

  • You will see the team switcher
  • You will see the folder selection (but not the default Zoom Recordings folder)
  • You cannot click next until you select a folder
  • You can skip

Paid Tier account with My Videos

  • You will see the team switcher
  • You will see the Zoom Recordings folder nested underMy Videos
  • You can click next
  • You can skip

Free Tier account

  • You will see the team switcher
  • You will see the Zoom Recordings folder nested under Library
  • You can click next
  • You can skip

Email notifications

You will receive an automated email once the app is installed on Vimeo. TheGo to my Zoom settings button will take you to Zoom, where you can update your Zoom profile and other settings. Screenshot: Screen_Shot_2022-11-29_at_2.15.48_PM.png

Once your Zoom meeting ends and the cloud recording is fully uploaded to Vimeo, you will receive an email notification that the Zoom recording is available on Vimeo. You can select Go to video to view your Zoom recording on Vimeo. You can trim, share, and add comments to your Zoom recording just like any other video on Vimeo.

Upload quality

Read about how Zoom determines the resolution of the recording from Zoom support at ‘Resolution of Recorded Video’.

What can I do if only the speaker’s view is being recorded?

If your Zoom meeting recordings only show the active speaker’s video and not the shared screens, go to your Zoom recording settings and enable the “Record active speaker with shared screen” option. This will ensure that future recordings capture both the speaker and any shared content, providing a complete record of your meetings.

How to record with Vimeo in Jira and GitHhub

When you install the Vimeo Record extension in Google Chrome, you can record video messages and embed them directly within Jira and GitHub issues. This is supported by both issue descriptions and comments.

Once the extension is installed:

  1. Open Jira or GitHub, and either select an existing issue or create a new issue.
  2. Click into either a Description or Comment field. Click the Record Video button that appears below it. Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-06-09_at_6.25.26_PM.png Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-06-09_at_6.25.00_PM.png
  3. The Vimeo Record extension will open. Select your recording destination and settings, then click Start recording.
  4. Record your message, then click the Stop button.
  5. The video will be uploaded to your Vimeo account, and the embedded player will automatically be inserted into the issue description or comment, allowing others to click play and watch your recording directly within the issue.

How to record with Vimeo on Asana

Teams that use Asana to collaborate can use video messaging powered by Vimeo Record to add visual context to shared projects. Vimeo Record allows you to record your screen and/or camera with audio to help asynchronously communicate with your team in a more engaging and effective way.

Additionally, our integration with Asana allows teams to embed videos from Vimeo into their project briefs, task comments, and task descriptions by pasting the link to your Vimeo video.

Visit the Asana hub page to read more about this integration.

Connecting your Vimeo account to Asana

As an Asana user, you can record up to two videos from within Asana without logging into Vimeo. After two recordings, you will be required to sign up for a Vimeo account or log into an existing account to continue using Vimeo Record in Asana.

If you run into issues or have any questions about using Vimeo Record on Asana, please contact Vimeo Support.

Record videos on Asana

Navigate to any project task within Asana and you will find a Record button. Click the Record button to configure if you want to record your screen, camera, or both, and then start your recording. All video recordings will take place within Asana. After you add two recordings, you will be prompted to log into Vimeo or create a new account to continue using the integration.

See Vimeo and Asana Product Guide for more details about using Vimeo Record in Asana.

Embed videos on Asana

While using Asana, you can paste a URL to display a video on Vimeo in these sections:

  • Task description
  • Task comment
  • Product brief (go to project > overview > key resources > brief)

You can also add a Vimeo URL that will unfurl in these areas by selecting theplus sign (+) menu, selectingvideo, and then entering the video URL.

See Asana’s guide for more detailed steps on embedding media in your Asana projects.

How to record with Vimeo on ProductPlan

With the Vimeo Record integration on ProductPlan, you can create screen recordings of product roadmaps and share them with your team. Visit ProductPlan’s overview here for more information.

How to add the integration to ProductPlan

How to use the Canva integration with my Vimeo account

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can import and export your Vimeo videos to and from Canva, enabling you the ability to leverage Vimeo as your primary platform for storage and delivery of video and Canva for video creation. This article discusses how to connect your Vimeo account to Canva, import Vimeo videos to Canva, and export videos from Canva to Vimeo.

  • What to know before using the Canva integration
  • How to install the Vimeo app for Canva and connect my accounts
  • How to import my Vimeo videos to Canva
  • How to export videos from Canva to Vimeo

What to know before using the Canva integration

There are some limitations with the Canva integration to be aware of:

  • Each export from Canva to Vimeo will create a new file in Vimeo. There is no support for a replace functionality at this time.
  • Canva currently only supports video files up to 1GB in size.

How to install the Vimeo app for Canva and connect my accounts

The first step for using Vimeo and Canva is to install the Vimeo app for Canva. To do so:

  1. In your web browser, navigate to canva and log in or create a new Canva account.
  2. Start a new Video or Social Media project.
  • This integration works best with these project types in Canva, as these are the video output formats that Canva supports.
  1. In the left side navigation bar within Canva, select Apps.
  2. Search for the Vimeo app and install it.
  3. Once installed, the app will appear in your project side navigation bar.
  4. Select the Vimeo app, then select Connect.
  5. Log in to your Vimeo account.
  6. Once you are logged in, Canva will be connected to your Vimeo account, and you will see your Vimeo content within the Vimeo app.

How to import my Vimeo videos to Canva

After connecting your Vimeo account, you can import your Vimeo videos into your Canva project. To do so:

  1. Within the Vimeo app in Canva, choose the Vimeo team where your video content lives.
  2. Browse or search for the desired folder.
  3. When you’ve chosen the desired video, select Add to design to import the video into your Canva project.
  4. Now you can edit your videos in Canva. Add graphics, stock videos, add scenes (pages), and more. See more tips for editing and designing in Canva’s Help Center.

How to export videos from Canva to Vimeo

You can export your final Canva project or select specific scenes or pages to export as a video to Vimeo. To do so:

  1. Open the Vimeo app in the left navigation bar within Canva.
  2. Choose a folder to export to in Vimeo.
  • The format defaults to MP4.
  1. Once you select Export, you will see a video export success message.
  2. You can now log in to your Vimeo account in a separate browser window and check the folder you exported to and find your exported video.
  • You can also find the exported video in the Recents section of your Vimeo home page.

How to use the Google Meet autoarchive integration with Vimeo

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans with Contributor+ roles

The Google Meet Autoarchive integration automatically imports recorded meetings to Vimeo, organizes them in folders, and provides access to Vimeo’s editing and collaboration tools. This article summarizes where and how you can connect your Google Meet account, outlines the upload behavior, and explains how to manage or disconnect the integration.

  • Feature availability
  • Prerequisites
  • Connect via the Import button
  • Connect via the Integrations center
  • Manage imported recordings
  • Disconnect the integration

Feature availability

Google Meet integration is available on:

  • Vimeo Contributor+ roles
  • Google Workspace Business Starter, Business Standard, Business Plus, or Enterprise accounts

If you’re on a free Google Meet plan, your recordings won’t automatically upload. However, the integration setup will still be available.

Prerequisites

  • You must be a Contributor or higher in your Vimeo team to upload videos.
  • Your Google Meet account must support cloud recording.
  • You must be signed in to both Google and Vimeo accounts.

Connect via the Import button

Follow these steps to connect Google Meet from the Import CTA on the homepage:

  1. Click theImport button on the Vimeo home page.
  2. Under Import to Vimeo, select Connectnext to Google Meet.
  3. Sign in using your Google account.
  4. Grant access by clicking Allow on the permissions screen.
  5. Choose Select allto proceed.
  6. Choose a default team and folder for where your Google Meet recordings will be uploaded. If you don’t have any existing folders, a folder named Google Meet Recordings will be created under the My Library tab. A new This can be changed later in your Upload defaults.
  7. You’ll see a success message: “You are now connected to Google Meet”.

Connect via the Integrations center

You can also connect Google Meet through your Vimeo account settings:

  1. Go to Settings > Connected Apps.
  2. Locate Google Meetand click Connect. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-10-06 at 8.36.46 PM.png
  3. Sign in to your Google account.
  4. Authorize access and click Allow.
  5. Choose your default folder for uploads.
  6. A confirmation message will appear once the integration is successful.

Manage imported recordings

Once connected:

  • All cloud recordings from Google Meet will be saved to the selected folder.
  • You can change your default folder underVideos >Upload defaults.
  • After each meeting, Vimeo will automatically upload your video and notify you via email.
  • You can use Vimeo’s editing tools and AI features to enhance recordings.

Disconnect the integration

To disconnect the integration:

  1. Go to Settings > Connected Apps

  2. Find Google Meet and click Disconnect.

You will receive an email confirming the disconnection. If the token expires, you will also receive an email with a CTA to reconnect.

How to use the Integrations Center

The Integrations Center is a centralized hub where you can search, filter, and browse apps. Each app has its own listing page that highlights its key features and benefits. You can also manage your integrations and integration settings directly within the Integrations Center.

  • What to know before using the Integrations Center
  • How to use the Integrations Center
  • What happens if I remove an integration?
  • Making the most out of the Integrations Center

What to know before using the Integrations Center

Before browsing or managing apps, take note of the following:

  • The Integrations Center is a centralized location for all app integrations.
  • You can search, filter, and browse apps to find what suits your needs.

How to use the Integrations Center

You can browse, add, and manage apps in the Integrations Center. To do so:

  1. From your Home page, navigate to Settings > Connected Apps > Integrations Center.
  2. Browse through available apps or use the search bar to look for specific apps.
  3. Select an app to open its listing page. Here, you can view its features and benefits.
  4. To manage an installed app, go to Connectedand select the app you want to configure.
  5. Admins can configure or disconnect apps from the Manage app tab in the listing page.

What happens if I remove an integration?

If you disconnect an app, it will no longer be active in your account. You can always reconnect it later by returning to the Integrations center.

Making the most out of the Integrations Center

  • Use search and filter options to quickly locate relevant apps.
  • Review app listing pages to understand the benefits before installing.
  • Leverage admin-level controls for secure and efficient management of integrations.

How to use the Kapwing integration with my Vimeo account

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

This article explains what Kapwing is, how to export videos from Kapwing to Vimeo, and how to import videos from Vimeo to Kapwing.

  • Kapwing integration overview
  • What to know before using the Kapwing integration
  • How to connect my Vimeo account to Kapwing
  • How to export videos from Kapwing to Vimeo
  • How to import videos from Vimeo into Kapwing

Kapwing integration overview

Kapwing is a video creation tool that enables users to create and edit videos in the cloud and to leverage AI to enhance videos. Kapwing also provides users with tools to repurpose and reformat video content, as well as automatically generate highlight clips from video content.

This integration allows you to import and export videos between Kapwing and Vimeo for advanced content editing and creation.

What to know before using the Kapwing integration

You will need a paid plan on Kapwing to use this integration.

How to connect my Vimeo account to Kapwing

To connect your Vimeo account to Kapwing:

  1. Go to Vimeo’s Kapwing integration page.
  2. Select Connect on Kapwing.
  3. Log in to your Kapwing account and allow the connection.

Alternatively, you can connect Kapwing to Vimeo when you go to export a video to Vimeo, as described below, and are prompted to log in.

How to export videos from Kapwing to Vimeo

To export a video from Kapwing to Vimeo:

  1. Upload or create a video in your Kapwing account.
  2. Select Export Project when you are finished editing.
  3. In the export panel, select Share. Screenshot: The Kapwing Export panel with various options shown. The Share butotn is between the Download and Embed options.
  4. Select Vimeo. Log in to your Vimeo account if prompted.
  5. Choose the desired Team, Folder, Privacy Settings, and input any other key information you want to be displayed about your video.
  6. Select Post to Vimeo.
  7. You will see a confirmation message that your video has been uploaded to your Vimeo account. You will also be given the option to manage your video in Vimeo, which will take you to the video settings page, or copy your video link to share with your audience.

How to import videos from Vimeo into Kapwing

To import videos from your Vimeo account into a Kapwing project:

  1. In a Kapwing project, select Add Media.
  2. Open the Import From dropdown menu, then choose Vimeo.
  3. Select the appropriate Team and/or Folder, search, or browse the available videos in the modal window to find the video(s) you want to edit. Once highlighted, choose Select to upload your content to your Kapwing project.
  4. Your video will be added to the Media menu in your Kapwing project and can be edited using Kapwing’s advanced editing tools.

How to use the Microsoft Teams autoarchive integration with Vimeo

This feature requires a Vimeo Enterprise plan and Microsoft 365 Business Standard/Premium or, Office 365 E1, E3, or E5, or Microsoft 365 E3 or E5, or Microsoft 365 A3 or A5 (for education) plans.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Integrations are connected to your Organization for Microsoft Teams. An Organization Owner and Admin can install this feature for the Organization and its Workspaces.

The Microsoft Teams Autoarchive Integration with Vimeo is designed to streamline the saving and management of your Teams meeting recordings. With this integration, admins can install the app on behalf of all users, enabling an automated system where Teams meeting recordings are uploaded directly into a designated folder within your Vimeo video library.

This article discusses setting up and using this integration, as well as the features available to admins, owners, and users.

  • What does the integration offer?
  • Requirements to set up the integration
  • Setting up and managing the integration
  • Admin or Owner installation
  • Folder selection
  • Permissions management

What does the integration offer?

  • Automated Uploads: Teams meeting recordings are automatically uploaded to Vimeo.
  • Admin Management: Admins can control and manage which users can access the integration.
  • Folder Selection: Recordings are saved to a chosen folder in the Vimeo library.
  • Notifications: Users are notified in Microsoft Teams when their video upload is complete.
  • Suggestions: After uploading, users receive suggestions for actions, such as sharing, editing, or organizing their video.

Requirements to set up the integration

  • The user must be a Microsoft Teams admin and a Vimeo admin.
  • Confirm that Vimeo notifications are approved (unblocked) in Microsoft Teams admin portal(like in the screenshot below). You can control access for the organization or a specific group of users in the Microsoft app setup. Screenshot: Screenshot of the Microsoft Teams admin center, showing the ‘App setup policies’ page with ‘Global (Org-wide default)’ policy selected. The page has toggles for ‘Upload custom apps’ (Off) and ‘User pinning’ (On). Below, there’s a section for ‘Installed apps’ with an ‘Add apps’ button, and ‘Pinned apps’ displaying ‘Activity’ and ‘Chat’ as pinned to the app bar.

Setting up and managing the integration

Admin or Owner installation:

Follow these steps to install the app as an Admin or Owner. The user will also need to be an admin on Microsoft Teams:

  1. Navigate to theMicrosoft Teams Integration settings page.
  2. Install the app for your team and allow access to your Vimeo account.
  3. Choose a team to onboard
  4. Onboard yourself and allow access to your team’s accounts

You canmanage which folders or teams your videos are uploaded to, as well as disconnect from them.

Folder selection

Follow these steps to select the folder you want to save your recordings in:

  1. During setup, select the default folder in your Vimeo library where all meeting recordings will be stored.

  2. You can update this folder later in the app settings.

Permissions management

Follow these steps to manage your permissions:

  1. Navigate to the Microsoft Teams integrations settings.
  2. Click on Manage beside Microsoft Teams
  3. You will be able to disconnect yourself and your team and resend them the invite.
  4. Your team will receive a notification on their Microsoft Teams app.

Once a Teams meeting ends, the recording is automatically uploaded to the designated folder in Vimeo. Users will receive a notification in Microsoft Teams when the upload is complete, and they can easily play back the video directly in Microsoft Teams.

Notifications include suggestions for the next steps, such as sharing the video, editing it on Vimeo, or organizing it into a playlist.

The Microsoft Teams Autoarchive Integration with Vimeo simplifies video storage and management for organizations. Admins can ensure seamless collaboration by automating the upload process, while users save time with instant access and actionable notifications.

How to use the Vimeo integration with Slack

This article discusses how to integrate Vimeo with Slack for collaboration on video projects. It details the setup process, management of notifications, and the roles of app managers and administrators.

  • Before you begin
  • How to configure your Slack integration
  • How to disconnect your Slack integration
  • How to update your Slack app
  • User notifications
  • App Managers and Administrators
  • Additional information

Before you begin

Users must be an AdminorContributor/Contributor +and must have can manageor edit access to the Folder for the Team or Workspace, to set up Slack notifications. Vimeo’s Slack integration is supported for folders housed in theTeam library and a user’s Personal Space if configured on your account (My library).

How to configure your Slack integration

  1. Navigate to your My library or Team library
  2. Hover over a folder and select the options menu (⋯) to the right or navigate to the (⋯) from within the folder.
  3. Select Connect to Slack from the dropdown menu.
  4. A modal will appear prompting you to connect the folder to Slack. Select Connect to continue.
  5. On the next step, you will see a modal that includes (1) granting Vimeo’s Slack app with the appropriate permissions to send data from your Vimeo account to your Slack workspace (2) selecting the Slack Channel where you would like to receive notifications. Both steps are required for the connection to be valid. Once you have selected the Slack Channel, please click Allow to authorize the connection.
  6. Once connected, you can choose which type of updates get pushed to Slack and in what language.
  7. Once configured, click Save to preserve your configuration.
  8. You can manage the Slack connection for each folder after its initial configuration by selecting Slack settings from the folder options menu. These options include changing the Slack channel, modifying the notifications that are linked to Slack, or disconnecting it entirely.

How to disconnect your Slack integration

To disconnect your Slack integration navigate toapps

  1. Find the Slack integration listed on the page.
  2. Hover on the Connected button and toggle to Disconnect.
  3. You will see a prompt to confirm that you wish to disconnect Slack from the connected folders.
  4. Select Disconnect.

How to update your Slack app

Vimeo pushes updates to our Slack application to preserve the integrity of the product, adopt new Slack APIs and scopes, and maintain security protocols. Users with the Vimeo Slack App connected will receive notifications to prompt an upgrade. Slack App Managers are required to approve the application update for all users within their workspace.

User notifications

When Vimeo makes an update to our Slack integration, users who installed the app will receive this message via their connected Slack channels prompting them to upgrade:

Vimeo x Slack integration update

We’ve made some changes to our integration to reflect Slack’s latest API updates. Please contact your Slack App Manager to update your company’s Vimeo x Slack integration byfollowing these steps.

Users who are connecting their Slack integration to new folders will receive a prompt to reinstall the application. This workflow will require that the user submit a request to theirApp Managers to upgrade their application.

App Managers and Administrators

App Managers and administrators must upgrade the Vimeo Slack App on behalf of all users in their Slack workspace by following these steps:

  1. Navigate to Vimeo’s Slack App listing.
  2. Review the changes to the application listed on the page.
  3. Select Approve for Workspace.You will see a confirmation that the app has been Approved for [Workspace].

Additional information

Please note the following:

  • People in your connected Slack channel who are not on your team, or have not been granted access to the folder, may see updates for a video that they cannot access on Vimeo. Be sure to add them as a team member to your folder so that everyone can collaborate.
  • Please note that only Account Owners, Admins, and Contributors can access folder settings and manage access.

Record and upload your Webex meetings to Vimeo

The Vimeo App for Webex gives you the opportunity to back up your Webex cloud recordings directly in your Vimeo account – no more downloading to your computer, then logging into Vimeo to upload. Once your recording is on Vimeo, you’ll have access to our player, collaboration tools, customizable privacy, embed settings, and much more.

Visit the Webex hub page to read about this integration.

⚠️Note: If you delete a video that is stored both in Webex and Vimeo in one location (e.g. Webex), it will NOT simultaneously be deleted in the other location (e.g. Vimeo). This goes both ways.

How to install the app

  1. In order to set up the Vimeo app for Webex, you’ll need to have an account on Vimeo and have a Webex Business tier or higher; Webex does not offer cloud storage for meeting recordings on the Basic tier.
  2. Click here to install the Vimeo App for Webex.
  3. Go through the setup flow, accept the terms, and then you’ll see the installation confirmation page. After installation success, you’ll land on your Webex Recordings folder (or assigned folder during installation).
  4. Once installed, you’ll be able to select Record to cloud on your Webex meeting. This cloud recording will transcode and upload to your connected Vimeo account after your meeting recording ends.
  5. After your video finishes transcoding, it will appear in the Webex Recordings Folder on Vimeo, where you’ll be able to access all our tools for sharing and collaboration.

⚠️Note: If you are a team member on an Enterprise account, your recordings will upload to your Private to Me folder by default. You can then edit any settings on it before moving it to another folder on the account as desired. If you are a team member on a non-Enterprise account, your recordings will upload to the assigned folder during installation or to your personal account, rather than your team account.

Webex Recordings on your preferred team and folder destination

In order to select the preferred team and folder destination for your Webex recordings, you will be prompted to make this selection while first installing the Vimeo for Webex app.

Webex recording privacy settings

All videos uploaded from Webex will have the default privacy setting of “Private.” You can update the recording’s privacy setting after it uploads to your Vimeo account.

The Vimeo App for Webex ties one Webex account to one Vimeo account, with each Vimeo account having its own Webex Recordings folder.

Troubleshooting: Videos not being posted when using the publish to social feature

This article discusses the common reasons for publishing failures when sharing videos to social media and provides troubleshooting steps to resolve the issues. If your videos aren’t posting when using publish to social, there are some steps to try.

What is causing the post to fail?

These are the most common reasons publishing to social will fail, along with what to check for:

  • App is not synced to Vimeo: Disconnect the app, then reconnect it from your Integrations center.
  • Trying to post on a personal Facebook profile: If using Facebook, ensure your destination is not a personal profile. Publish to social will only work when posting to Facebook Pages, not profiles.
  • Not under the correct role: If you’re using LinkedIn, check your role on the LinkedIn account; only ‘super-admins’ roles can post to a company LinkedIn page.
  • Permissions denied to publish to social: For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces,Publish to social can be limited by Organization Owners and Admins. Read more at How to edit my Organization’s settings
  • Check for other restrictions and requirements for publishing to social.

Still having issues?

Contact our support team and be sure to include the following information:

  • Link to the video that isn’t posting
  • Link to the social media page you’re trying to post to

Using Facebook Ads Manager with Vimeo OTT

Facebook Ads Manager is Facebook’s tool for managing and running ads on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, or Audience Network. It’s an all-in-one tool for creating ads, managing when and where they’ll run, and tracking how well your campaigns are performing.

How do I use Facebook Ads Manager with Vimeo OTT?

Using this tool you can measure the effectiveness of your ad campaigns for Web, iOS mobile, and Android mobile devices. You can calculate metrics such as the average cost per install, and the average cost per conversion.

Web events should be configured using the Facebook Pixel. This guide documents the web events we support.

For iOS & Android mobile, we support the following Facebook events:

  • Event Name
  • Event Trigger
  • Install
  • The user has installed the app
  • Initiate Checkout
  • The user initiates the purchase by selecting a subscription plan
  • Purchase
  • The purchase is successful and Apple/Google has confirmed the receipt
  • Complete Registration
  • The user’s account was created successfully (event fired only if the user is logged out & is a new user)

⚠️Note:

  • By default, Facebook Ads Manager will aggregate Web and Mobile App metrics. Be sure to look at “Website” vs. “Mobile App” events separately if you are marketing across multiple platforms.
  • If your app is a Made for Kids app, these tracking Events are disabled and not sent.
  • Reach out to your Ads Manager to access the data on your iOS and Android apps

Using Google Analytics 4 on Vimeo OTT

Google Analytics (GA4) provides valuable insight into user activity on your Vimeo OTT Site + Apps! Within this article, you will find the steps to create a GA4 property and add it to your Vimeo OTT account.

⚠️Note:This article covers setting up GA4 on your OTT website. To link your GA4 Account to your Vimeo OTT Branded Apps, please visit this article.

  • Summary
  • Terms to Understand
  • Configuring your Google Analytics 4 property
  • Adding your Google Analytics 4 property to your Vimeo OTT Site
  • Tracked Events in Google Analytics

Summary

This is a long support article but only because we want to be as detailed as possible to walk you through these important steps. The process is very simple and can be finished in just a few minutes. You’ll be creating a new Google Analytics 4 property (1 min), configuring it with optimized settings (3 min), and then copying a number into your OTT Site (1 min). You’ll be using GA4 in no time!

Terms to Understand

  • Google Analytics 4: often referred to simply as “GA4”; this is the next generation of Analytics and insights to understand your traffic and your customers.
  • GA4 Property: a “property” is a collection of destinations. You have a Vimeo OTT website and you may have an iOS app or Android app. All three together are showing the same content and are considered the same property with three different data streams.
  • Data Stream: a destination for viewing your content. Google Analytics supports three types of data streams; a website, an iOS app, and an Android app. Vimeo OTT supports the website data stream.

Configuring your Google Analytics 4 property

Many of the default Google Analytics 4 configurations will work great with Vimeo OTT but there are a number of optimizations that we recommend.

  1. Go to analytics.google.com

  2. Choose yourproperty from thetop dropdown menu, and select Admin in the lower left panel.

  3. Choose Setup Assistantfrom the middle Property column.

  4. In the Setup Assistant, find the Data Collection section with the Collect website and app data option.

  5. Click the arrow on the far right and choose Manage Data Streams.

You’ll see a list of your data streams with a filter along the top for iOS, Android, and Web.

  1. Click on the Web data stream and a large panel will slide out with all of your web data stream properties.

  2. In the Enhanced Measurement section and make sure the toggle is enabled to the ON position.

  3. Click on the Gear icon to enable additional measurements.

In the side panel that opens; we recommend enabling all of the available options except for Scrolls. You may enable Scrolls if you feel this information will be useful. Be sure to click Save once the toggles are in the ON position.

Now you’re ready to add your Google Analytics 4 property to your Vimeo OTT site!

Adding your Google Analytics 4 property to your Vimeo OTT Site

Add your Google Analytics 4 property to your Vimeo OTT Site:

  1. Go to analytics.google.com, choose your property from the top dropdown menu, and select Admin in the lower left panel.
  2. Click on Data Streams from the middle Property column. You’ll see a list of your data streams with a filter along the top for iOS, Android, and Web.
  3. Click on the Web data stream and a large panel will slide out with all of your web data stream properties.
  4. Select the Measurement ID shown in the top right.
  5. Click the Copy icon next to the ID.

Now your Measurement ID is copied to your clipboard.

  1. In a new tab, open up your Vimeo OTT Site Settings and click on Manage> Site.

  2. In Site settings, click on Tracking in the left sidebar.

  3. Click on the Google Analytics 4 Measurement ID.

  4. Paste the ID you just copied into this field and click Save.

Now your site is configured for GA4 and will start automatically populating data for your Acquisition, Engagement, and Monetization reports.

Tracked Events in Google Analytics

  • Event name
  • Event Trigger
  • page_view
  • each time the page loads or the browser history state is changed by the active site
  • scroll
  • the first time a user reaches the bottom of each page
  • session_start
  • when a user engages the app or website
  • user_engagement
  • when the webpage is in focus for at least one second
  • view_search_results
  • each time a user performs a site search, indicated by the presence of a URL query parameter
  • first_visit
  • the first time a user visits a website
  • form_start
  • the first time a user interacts with a form in a session
  • form_submit
  • when the user submits a form
  • file_download
  • when a user clicks a link leading to a file with a common file extension
  • click
  • each time a user clicks a link that leads away from the current domain
  • purchase
  • when a user’s purchase succeeds
  • begin_checkout
  • when a user loads the checkout page
  • sign_up
  • when a user begins a transaction and the new Customer record is created
  • login
  • when a user has successfully logged in
  • search
  • when a user has completed a content search

Using Segment with Vimeo OTT

Segment.com is a third-party service designed to receive large amounts of data and simultaneously re-route it to a myriad of destinations. Many Sellers have different needs for user management and data insights that can’t all be directly integrated into the Vimeo OTT platform. With Segment, they can leverage an almost infinite amount of additional third-party integrations for data insights.

  • What Does Segment Support?

  • Creating a Segment Integration

  • What Events Are Sent?

  • Native Segment Events

  • Platform Events

  • Video Events

  • Platform Events Properties

  • Video Events Properties

Segment supports hundreds of integrations. If you’re using a specific set of tools and you’d like it to collect data from OTT, check out the Segment Catalog to see if your software is supported. If it is, you can create a Segment account and start sending data to it right away.

Vimeo OTT supports sending data to Segment from our branded iOS, tvOS, Android, Android TV, Amazon Fire TV apps as well as from the Web. Vimeo OTT also supports sending data to Segment from our branded Roku app, though this program with Segment is still in alpha, as noted here.

Creating a Segment Integration

  • Navigate to Segment.com
  • Enter your name, email, and password. These don’t need to be the same as your Vimeo OTT credentials, but Segment does expect it to match the domain of your site URL.
  • Once signed up, you’ll need to add a Source.
  • Sources are locations where your data is coming into Segment. This may be an iOS or Android app or, for the below example, the Web.
  • Choose Website / Javascript.*
  • Click “Connect” from the sidebar.
  • Give the Source a name or leave it as “Javascript.”
  • Enter your website on OTT.
  • This can be either yoursubdomain.vhx.tv OR your full custom domain.
  • Once the source is added, head to the ‘Sources’ page and click “Settings” in the top navigation.
  • Click “API Keys” in the left navigation.
  • Copy the “Write Key.”
  • Navigate to Settings > Site > Advanced.
  • Paste the API Write Key into the Segment Key field.
  • Save your settings.

Now data will start sending to your Segment account. To see it flowing in, you can click on the “Source” and then choose the “Debugger” tab to see each event being fired.

* Note: If you’re an OTT Enterprise client and you’re configuring Segment to use multiple sources for your applications; you would choose the appropriate “Source” per platform.

The API Keys generated from each of the Sources below will be integrated with your application by coordinating with your Account Manager.

  • “iOS” for Apple iPhone and Apple TV applications
  • “Android” for Android Mobile and Android TV
  • “Android” (Second Source) for Amazon Fire TV
  • “Roku” for Roku devices

The events will include a ‘device’ property they can use to distinguish between two apps that share the same source.

What Events Are Sent?

Vimeo OTT will send a lot of data over to the Segment account. Below you will find tables of numerous events that are sent from the integration that will help you filter and understand the data coming in. These tables also indicate which platforms send each type of event, as not all events apply to every platform.

The primary event names in Segment are purposefully explicit and descriptive to help easily understand what event is taking place. Each of these events contains many additional attributes and properties to further describe the action taken; these are only the top-level events being sent.

Native Segment Events

The following events are provided by the Segment Analytics SDK.

Application Installed

Description: A user has opened your application after installation. This is a native Segment application event automatically collected by the Segment SDK.

Trigger: This event fires when a user first opens your mobile application.

Verifying my Vimeo OTT domain for Facebook

Due to Apple iOS 14 privacy policy updates, Facebook requires that anyone advertising on their platform must verify their domain. You can do this directly from your OTT site without needing to edit your DNS record.

How do I verify my domain for Facebook?

  1. In your OTT site admin, navigate to Manage > Site.

Screenshot: image1.png

  1. Select the Tracking tab. In the Facebook section, you will see a Domain Verification input. In order to get the proper value for this field, you will need to go into your Facebook Business Manager and follow the instructions outlined in this guide. Once you have a metadata tag it should look something like this
  1. You will want to copy only the content value (e.g. “123abc” above) and paste it into the domain verification code input. Be sure to save your settings.

Screenshot: Screen_Shot_2021-08-02_at_1.59.16_PM.png

  1. Adding this value will automatically add a metadata tag to the section in the HTML of your site’s homepage.
  2. You can then click Verify at the bottom of the Meta Tag Verification tab in your Facebook Business Manager and Facebook will be able to successfully verify your domain.

Vimeo integration on Constant Contact

Vimeo can integrate with the online marketing tool Constant Contact to provide you with a one-stop solution for your video needs. If you have a Constant Contact account, you’ll be able to use Vimeo’s video player to embed videos in your emails and website pages, plus you can create and distribute marketing videos. By bringing Vimeo’s video player right into your Constant Contact email and landing pages, you can increase your site’s engagement and visual appeal, improving its overall performance.

See the Constant Contact hub page to read more about this integration.

  • Setting up the integration
  • Connecting your Vimeo account to Constant Contact

Setting up the integration

To connect your Vimeo account with your Constant Contact account, follow the step-by-step directions at Connect your Constant Contact account with Vimeo from Constant Contact’s Help Center.

Check out Constant Contact’s documentation for how to insert a video into your email or website landing pages.

  • Create a Vimeo video in your Library
  • Insert a video into a custom code email
  • Insert a video into a campaign
  • View results of a video in a landing page

Connecting your Vimeo account to Constant Contact

When you’re creating an email using Constant Contact’s Cross Device Editor, a Shoppable or Custom Landing Page, or a Survey Page, you can easily insert a video from your Vimeo account.

Don’t have a Constant Contact account? Visit Constant Contact to learn how to grow your business or nonprofit with email marketing and more.

Vimeo OTT & AppsFlyer Integration

AppsFlyer is a third-party tool that helps you track your marketing campaigns to better attribute referrals and conversions made via your branded apps and analyze the data inside your AppsFlyer account.

How to enable this integration

To utilize this integration, your organization will need an account on Vimeo OTT with branded apps as well as an account with AppsFlyer.

You can sign up for an AppsFlyer account through this page.

  1. Log in to your AppsFlyer Account.
  2. Follow the step-by-step instructions at Adding an app to AppsFlyer to add apps for each of your corresponding Vimeo OTT-powered apps.
  3. If your apps are already live, you will need to input the app store listing URLs for each platform. You can get the URLs by visiting your OTT Admin and selecting Manage > Platforms. Then, select the Live button corresponding to each platform. This will open the store listing for the platform. Copy the store listing URL and paste it into the AppsFlyer admin’s app configuration. If your apps are not yet live, reach out to your Account Manager, and they will be able to provide you with the required values to input into AppsFlyer for each app.
  4. Click on App Settingsin the sidebar.
  5. Copy the Dev key for each platform and send this to your Account Manager. You may find that AppsFlyer provides you with the same Dev key for each platform, or they can differ, depending on your specific configuration.
  6. Vimeo’s apps team will rebuild your apps, and data will start flowing into your AppsFlyer account.

Enabling OneLink deep linking
