Vimeo OTT & Branch.io

branch is a mobile measure platform (MMP) that is integrated into the Vimeo OTT Branded Apps. It allows you to create deep links into your apps, and to monitor attribution and link analytics on the Branch side. If you have an Enterprise-level account with Vimeo OTT, you’ll be able to work with your account manager to enable Branch on your OTT site.

  • Supported devices
  • What is a deep link?
  • Connecting Branch to your Vimeo OTT account
  • Creating a deep link in Branch
  • What events are sent?

Supported devices

The Branch SDK is natively installed in the following OTT branded app platforms, but requires a linked Branch account in order to be activated:

Mobile

  • iOS
  • Android
  • Fire Tablet

CTV

  • tvOS
  • Android TV
  • Amazon Fire TV
  • Roku

What is a deep link?

Deep links are app-specific links that send a user “deeper” into the app, or into a specific part of the app, from your targeted campaign. i.e., instead of sending your customer to the home screen of your app, you might deep link them directly to a video or collection page. Linking the user to the correct contextual page from your campaign has incredible benefits from a marketing perspective—if the user doesn’t have to search around for what they need, they can get right to the content they came for, and hopefully convert. Deep links can be used to direct the user from an email, ad, or other marketing apparatus right to the desired page in your app.

Branch’s deep links store contextual information about where a user wants to go, where the link was clicked, who originally shared the link and other custom data. Read more in the Branch’s documentation about the types of analytics you’ll be able to access once the integration is enabled.

Connecting Branch to your Vimeo OTT account

This is a hands-on collaborative process with your Account Manager and the Vimeo OTT Branded Apps team. To enable Branch deep-linking and attribution your Account Manager will typically recommend Branch.io and, once your account is setup, can initiate the process with our Branded Apps team.

To get started:

  1. Create an account on branch.
  2. Send our team all three of the following key and link values:
  • Branch Key- This can be found on the Account Settings > Profile page in the Branch admin.
  • Branch Link- This can be found on the bottom of the Link Settings page under Link Domain in the Branch admin.
  • Branch Alternate Link- This can be found on the bottom of the Link Settings page under Link Domain in the Branch admin
  1. You or your Account Manager can open a Live App Change Request with our Branded Apps team and provide this information.
  2. Invite our Branded Apps team (apps@vhx.tv) to your Branch account as an Admin through theTeam tab in the Account Settings page so that they can configure other app details in your admin to ensure links will function correctly. You can remove access after setup if you prefer. Alternatively, you can do this step yourself and the Branded Apps Team can provide the values needed.
  3. You should set a name for your app in the Branch Account Settings page under the About Your App section in the App Name field. This should match the name of your apps with Vimeo OTT.
  4. A new version of the app will need to be built and published before Branch links can be set up and used. You will be notified when the new version is released, usually about 2-3 weeks.

Creating a deep link in Branch

Once you’ve connected your Vimeo OTT and Branch accounts, you will need to add a custom Key/Value Pair on the Link Data screen to make your links work:

  • If you want to link to a collection:
  • Key 0 : value 1
  • If you want to link to a video:
  • Key 0: value 1

The collectionID and videoID values indicated above are the auto-generated numbers found in the URL when you view a collection or a video, respectively, in the Vimeo OTT Admin.

  • If you navigate to your collection within the OTT Admin, you will see a URL in your browser similar to this:
  • 0
  • In this example, 0is 123456.
  • If you navigate to your video within the OTT Admin, you will see a URL in your browser similar to this:
  • 0
  • In this example, 0 is 0987654.

Refer to Branch’s documentation for further instructions on how to create your link.

Vimeo OTT & Tessitura Integration

At a time when performances, concerts, and other cultural events are increasingly making their way online, the integration between Vimeo OTT and Tessitura can help your organization easily bring incredible content right to your viewers. The integration connects Vimeo OTT with Tessitura so that your viewers can seamlessly access gated content (videos, live streams, etc); it’s useful for any arts or cultural organizations that are already using Tessitura as their service provider for member management, or who might like to do so.

By enabling this integration, you can ensure that your existing users in the Tessitura environment will be able to leverage their status as arts donors and gain access to your products on Vimeo OTT. For instance, you’d be able to offer a virtual season ticket, and host your entire season on your Vimeo OTT site. This will allow you to open up your programming to a range of new users.

If you’re interested in learning more about this, please reach out to us.

  • How do I enable this integration?
  • How does this integration work?

How do I enable this integration?

To utilize this integration, your organization will need both an account on Vimeo OTT and Tessitura version 15.1.16+. Once you have both of those in place, reach out to your Vimeo Onboarding Team to enable this integration. If you are no longer in onboarding, you can reach out to your Account Manager to enable this integration. OTT sellers will work with an onboarding team at Tessitura to test out the integration before it’s turned on.

If you are a self-serve OTT seller and don’t have an Enterprise contract, please reach out to accounts+tessitura@vimeo.com to enable this integration.

How does this integration work?

The Vimeo OTT + Tessitura Integration works with both SVOD (subscription video on demand) and TVOD (transactional video on demand) Vimeo OTT products.

For SVOD, customers access your Vimeo OTT subscription (SVOD product) based on constituencies applied to Tessitura accounts. Constituencies can be applied based on Tessitura ticket purchases, contributions, memberships, or manually.

For TVOD, Tessitura events are linked to Vimeo OTT products in a 1-1 relationship. A sale of an event in Tessitura will trigger the integration to add the corresponding Vimeo OTT product to a managed Vimeo OTT account.

Once this integration is enabled, your Tessitura users will receive an email prompting them to sign into your Vimeo OTT site. We recommend using the passwordless method, as detailed in this article.

You can read more about this integration in this guide.. Please note that you need to be signed in to your Tessitura account to view this help article.

Please note that Tessitura charges a fee in order to enable the integration. See this guide for more information on their pricing.

About AI credits

This feature requires a paid plan.

On Vimeo, AI credits are used to pay for AI-powered translations of your video’s subtitles and/or audio, as well as for live auto-captions and their translations during live events. This article provides an overview of AI credits, who can use them, and how to check your balance.

  • Who can purchase and use AI credits?

Who can use AI credits?

If you are the account owner or a team member with edit rights, you can use AI credits to translate your videos’ subtitles and/or audio, and to power live auto-captions on your live events.

Team owners and admins can control their team’s access to AI tools on the AI settings page.

Vimeo Enterprise with Workspaces:Vimeo AI credits and access to AI tools are managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins.

API usage: AI credits are also consumed when you trigger AI actions through the Vimeo AI API (Enterprise only). API requests draw from the same credit pool at the same rates.

Who can buy additional AI credits?

Paid plans, excluding Enterprise, cannot pre-purchase AI credit bundles, but can purchase credits when translating videos.

If you are an Enterprise account owner, speak to your account manager to buy additional AI credits.

Read more at AI credits rates and policies.

How much do AI credits cost?

Credit prices are visible in the Vimeo AI section on our plan comparison page by hovering over ⓘ ” Buy AI Credits. The price is also displayed during the translation process under the number of credits needed to complete your translation project.

The cost to use credits is:

  • AI Service
  • Cost
  • Subtitle translation only
  • 10 credits per minute of video per language
  • Audio and Subtitles translation
  • 20 credits per minute of video per language
  • Live auto-captions
  • 10 credits per minute
  • Live caption translations
  • 20 credits per minute per language

We also offer a limited number of free AI creditsto let you try our AI tools.

About available data for my interactive videos

This article discusses the interactive analytics panel for video and the metrics that could be viewed there. When you open the interactive analytics panel on the interactive editor page, you will see aggregate data showing the performance of your video.

In the upper right corner of the panel, you can select which view of the interactive dashboard you’d like to see and your desired time range. All time will be selected by default.

Once your time range is set, you have three views you can choose from.

  • Headlines
  • Interactions
  • Clickouts

Headlines

Headlines is a high-level dashboard of your video’s performance. It’s includes the following metrics:

  • Hotspot interactions per viewer: Calculated as number of total interactions / viewers.
  • Total interactions: Total number of times a hotspot was clicked or tapped.
  • Amount of overlay time per viewer: Average amount of time a viewer stayed inside your overlays.
  • Most popular hotspot: This will show the name of the hotspot on your video with the highest number of total interactions.
  • Clicks vs touches: Differentiates interactions on desktop (clicks) vs. interactions on mobile devices (touches), so you know how your viewers are seeing your video.

Screenshot: dashboard.png

Interactions

The Interactions view displays a table showing all of your video’s hotspots and the number of interactions each has. Each row displays:

  • Hotspot name: The name of your hotspots
  • Clicks: The number of interactions with the hotspot on desktop
  • Touches: The number of interactions with the hotspot on mobile
  • Total: Total number of interactions (clicks + touches)

Screenshot: interactions.png

Clickouts

The Clickouts view displays a table of the URLs that your viewers can click out to from either a hotspot or an overlay. Each row displays:

  • Destination URL: The URL clicked out to either from a hotspot or an overlay
  • Clickout: Number of times the URL was clicked on

Screenshot: clickouts.png

How often are these metrics updated?

The interactive analytics will refresh every 10 minutes.

About channels

Free and Basic accounts are limited to one channel. Multiple channels are available with paid plans.

This feature is not available in some regions.

You can create channels on Vimeo, which are destinations for video viewing. Viewers can subscribe to your channel and the videos you add will show up in their feed. This article discusses how create and customize channels.

What to consider before using channels

Before using channels, take note of the following:

  • For individual users, only the channel creator and moderators can add videos to a channel. To add moderators to your channel, click Settings on your channel page and follow the instructions in the Membership tab.
  • For team accounts, Contributors and Admins can add and remove the owner’s videos from a channel.
  • Owners or admins of the account who own the channel cannot be added as moderators.
  • You might not be able to add every video you want to your channel. That’s because Vimeo users can choose not to allow their videos to be added to groups, channels, and showcases.
  • Password-protected videos can only be added to and deleted from channels by account Owners.

How to access and create channels

To access your channels or create a new one, follow the steps below:

  1. Select your profile picture in the top right corner to open the dropdown menu.
  2. Select Watch from the drop-down, then choose Collections.
  3. Scroll down on the page to find Channels.
  4. Select + Create new channel to create a new one.
  • You can also create a channel by visiting the Channels page and then clicking the + Create a Channel button at the top of the page.

About configuring channel settings

You can customize your channel in its settings, which you can access by clicking on the Settings button on the right side of your channel page.

In theBasictab, you can change the following for your channel:

  • Title
  • Description
  • Custom URL
  • Category

In the Appearance tab, you can do the following:

  • Choose a thumbnail that will represent your channel around the site (search, your Collections page, etc.)
  • Upload a header image that will appear at the top of your channel page.

Note: Remember to hit Save after you make changes.

How to add videos to my channel

Once you’ve created your channel, you can add videos to it by following the steps below. For team accounts, only Owners and Admins can add videos to collections.

  1. From your Library, select the video you would like to add to your channel to open the video settings page.
  2. Select Sharein the upper righthand corner of the page to open the share side panel.
  3. In the share side panel, select Publish.
  4. Select Channel. This will open a pop-up modal that lists your created channels.
  • You can also create a new channel by selecting New channel at the bottom left of the modal.
  1. In the modal window that opens, choose your channel and then Confirm.

If you are watching a video on vimeo.com, you can select the Collectionsicon below the player to add it to your channel, if permitted by the video owner.

How to arrange the order of videos on my channel

You can customize the order of videos in your channel by following these steps:

  1. Go to your channel page and choose Settings.
  2. Select the Videos tab.
  3. Choose an arrangement method from the drop-down menu next toAlways arrange by.
  4. If you choose to arrange your videos manually, you can drag and drop up to 100 videos in the order you’d like.
  5. Save your changes.

How to share my channel

To share a channel, follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to the channel.
  2. Select Share under the channel banner image. Screenshot: Staff Picks channel page with the Share button highlighted
  3. Enter the email addresses or Vimeo user names of the people you’d like to share your channel with.

Note: If viewers are located in the United Kingdom or European Union and are not logged into a Vimeo account, they will be prompted to log in to watch an unrated video or a video rated “Mature” on vimeo.com.

How to remove videos from my channel

To remove a video from your channel, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the Videos tab in the channel’s settings.
  2. Click the red X in the video’s thumbnail.
  3. Save your changes.

⚠️Note: If a video that was previously removed is added back to a channel, the video will return to its original spot in the channel. For example, if your channel is sorted by Most Recent, the video’s placement will be based on the time it was originally added, not the time you re-added it.

How to delete my channel

To delete your channel, follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to your channel’s settings page.
  2. Select the Advancedtab.
  3. Choose Delete this channel.

Channel privacy overview

You can choose who can view your channel by clicking the Settings button and then the Membership tab. You can select from the following privacy options:

  • Anyone — Everyone in the whole world can view your channel.
  • Only moderators — Only the moderators you have added to your channel can view that channel.
  • Only moderators and the people I choose — You can add people to share your channel with by clicking the Add or remove people link below these options.

⚠️Note: Setting your channel privacy to anything other than Anyone will remove all current subscribers who are not moderators or people you have specifically chosen.

For more information about video privacy within a channel, refer to About privacy of videos in collections and review pages.

Making the most out of channels

  • If you’re looking for channels to follow, you can search for channels by using the search box at the top of your screen. We also recommend visiting the Channels homepage to peruse our featured channels.
  • If you want to stop following a channel, go to that channel and click the Unfollow button.

About content ratings

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

Apply content ratings to your videos and live events to inform viewers about the material they contain. This article provides an overview of content ratings, explaining why they are essential for compliance and discoverability.

  • What are content ratings?
  • Why should I rate my content?
  • What happens if I misrate my video?
  • Can I appeal a rating decision made by a moderator?
  • Suggested next steps

What are content ratings?

Content ratings are labels that inform viewers whether your content contains mature content or advertising.

  • Mature content:
  • We ask that you rate all your videos and live events to inform viewers about any content that may include nudity, violence, profanity, or illegal substances. If your video contains any of these elements, it should be rated for Mature Audiences.
  • Advertisements
  • An advertisement is defined as any content meant to influence a viewer’s choice or opinion about a product or service. Even if you’re uploading content to showcase your portfolio, you must mark it as containing an advertisement if it was made for that purpose.
  • As a video-sharing platform, we are legally required to ask users to declare whether a video they upload contains an advertisement. This ensures that anyone watching the footage knows they are being exposed to this type of content.

Finally, we ask you to disclose whether your video contains AI-generated content. Read more at How to label my videos to show they contain AI-generated content.

Why should I rate my content?

Rating your content helps viewers make informed decisions and ensures your videos are compliant and discoverable.

  • Due to local regulations in regions such as the UK and the EU, public videos and live events without ratings require viewers to log in to a Vimeo account to watch them. Rating your content ensures the broadest possible audience can access it.
  • Videos with accurate ratings are more likely to appear in relevant search results.
  • Clear ratings help prevent negative comments and complaints from viewers.

What happens if I misrate my video?

If a Vimeo moderator finds a misrated video, the rating may be changed and locked. If we believe that you’re intentionally misrating your videos to shock or confuse people, your account may be restricted or closed.

Can I appeal a rating decision made by a moderator?

If you disagree with a rating decision made by one of our moderators, you can contact our support team for the decision to be reviewed. Please be sure to include the link to the relevant video in your message.

Suggested next steps

  • How to apply content ratings to my videos
  • How to apply content ratings to my live events

About disclosing videos as AI-generated or AI-enhanced

We require that creators disclose when realistic videos are created with altered or synthetic media, including generative AI. This article explains our policy, when to apply a label, and what happens if you don’t.

  • What is the disclosure policy for videos that are AI-generated or AI-enhanced?
  • When to disclose content that is AI-generated or AI-enhanced
  • What are the risks of not disclosing?
  • What are the consequences for violations?
  • Suggested next steps

What is the disclosure policy for videos that are AI-generated or AI-enhanced?

Generally, Creators must label content that:

  • Portrays a real person saying or doing something they did not
  • Alters footage of an actual event or location
  • Creates a lifelike scene that did not actually occur

This includes content that creators have partially or completely altered or created using audio, video, or image editing tools. Realistic content and major modifications must be disclosed; however, unrealistic or minor edits do not require disclosure.

Minor edits are mainly cosmetic and do not alter the content in a way that could mislead viewers about what actually occurred.

A label disclosing that the video has AI-generated content appears on both the video page, under the video title, and in the embedded video player. However, if the video title is hidden in the embedded player’s settings, the label will not appear in the player. It will still appear on the video’s page on Vimeo.

If a creator generates or enhances a video using one of our AI tools, we’ll automatically add a label to the video disclosing its usage.

When to disclose content that is AI-generated or AI-enhanced

Below are examples of content that typically require disclosure and those that do not, to help distinguish between AI content that is realistic or has had major modifications and AI content that is unrealistic or is considered minor edits.

Examples of content requiring disclosure include:

  • Manipulated footage of a politician to make it seem like they made a controversial statement they didn’t actually say.
  • Edited footage of a natural disaster to make it appear more severe than it actually was.
  • A lifelike depiction of a famous historical event that never happened.
  • Cloned voices that are used for a voiceover.

Examples of content not requiring disclosure include:

  • Animation featuring fictional characters in a fantasy setting.
  • Obvious special effects are used to show a person flying through the air.
  • Beauty filters.
  • Enhanced audio to remove background noise and improve clarity.

What are the risks of not disclosing?

Failing to reveal altered or synthetic content carries various risks, including misleading viewers and undermining their trust in creators. It can result in legal repercussions and raise ethical concerns about manipulation and exploitation.

Non-disclosure may lead to misunderstandings, legal disputes, and erosion of trust between creators and their audience. Additionally, it can contribute to the spread of fake news and undermine public discourse.

Compliance with regulatory requirements and ethical standards is crucial for mitigating these risks and maintaining integrity in media creation and consumption. Transparency in disclosing altered or synthetic content is essential to upholding trust, integrity, and responsible media practices.

What are the consequences for not labeling my content on Vimeo?

When meaningfully altered or synthetically generated content is undisclosed, we may, in appropriate cases, take action to reduce the risk of harm to viewers by proactively applying a label that creators cannot remove.

For high-severity violations, such as misleading information that creates a serious risk of material harm to a person, group, or the general public, we may remove the content entirely. Creators who consistently choose not to disclose this information may be subject to penalties from Vimeo, including removal of content or account termination.

If you believe that your content was labeled or removed, or your account was terminated in error, you can submit an appeal. Visit our Community Guidelines for additional information regarding appeals.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn how to label your videos to indicate they contain AI-generated or enhanced content.
  • Learn how to tell if a video on Vimeo was generated with or enhanced by using AI.

About end screens

End screens overview

Among other options, you can display more videos, loop your video, or add a call to action after it finishes playing using an end screen.

  • All end screen options can be found by navigating to your video’s settings page > Interactivity > End screen. Screenshot: Interactivity tab with end screen option highlighted
  • Learn about customizing these settings at How to change my video’s end screen.
  • End screens will only be reflected when your video is embedded on another web page, or on-site if your video is set to Unlisted or Password-protected. Public video pages on vimeo.com will use the default settings.

Registration overview

You may also use a registration form to connect with your viewers.

  • Display a customized form screen at the beginning or end of your video, with the option to add a custom message. Learn how to add a registration form to your video at How to add registration to your video.

About customizable end screens

You can drive engagement and conversions with the following customizable end screen options. For a detailed breakdown of end screen compatibility with different player environments, refer to Player environment requirements for end screens.

  • More videos: Group together three of your public videos or the latest three videos from one of your channels, groups, or showcases. You also have the option to add a background image to your video’s end screen. The videos shown in this end screen will automatically load and play in your current embedded player.
  • Share options: Display social share icons and the video URL after the video finishes playing. You also have the option to add a background image to your video’s end screen.
  • Custom image: Display an image after the video finishes playing. You also have the option to make the custom image a clickable link.

About simple end screens

  • Empty: Your video will not show anything after it finishes playing.
  • Loop: Your video will loop infinitely after it finishes playing.

💡Tip:Except for the Thumbnail and Loop options, a replay button is located in the bottom left corner of every end screen.

About engagement analytics

The Engagement tab in your Analytics module gives you a detailed view of how viewers interact with your videos — including how long they watch, where they drop off, and how many finish the video.

You can analyse a single video in depth or view aggregated engagement data across multiple videos at once.

Accessing engagement analytics

  1. Go to Analytics from the main navigation.
  2. Select the Engagement tab.
  3. Use the date range picker and video filter to choose which videos and time period you want to analyse.

The retention graph

The retention graph shows the percentage of views remaining at each point in your video, from the very start (0%) to the end (100%). A sharp drop at any point indicates that many viewers stopped watching there.

When you select multiple videos, each video is divided into 100 equal segments regardless of its actual duration. Views are aggregated by matching percentage position, which lets you compare engagement patterns across videos of different lengths.

  • Y-axis: Number of views at each point.
  • X-axis: Percentage point of the video (0–100%).

The engagement table

Below the graph, a table shows key engagement metrics for each video, as well as aggregate totals across all selected videos.

  • Views
  • What it shows: The number of sessions in which the video starts playing
  • Average % watched
  • What it shows: Total watch time divided by the video’s length
  • Average completion rate
  • What it shows: The proportion of views in which the video was watched to completion (within 2 seconds of the end)
  • Views at 1%
  • What it shows: Views recorded at the 1% point of the video
  • Views at 25%
  • What it shows: Views recorded at the 25% point
  • Views at 50%
  • What it shows: Views recorded at the 50% point
  • Views at 75%
  • What it shows: Views recorded at the 75% point
  • Views at 100%
  • What it shows: Views recorded at the end of the video

How completion rate is calculated

Completion rate is the total number of finishes divided by the total number of views — not an average of individual video completion rates.

For example:

  • Video A: 5 views, 5 finishes → 100% completion
  • Video B: 5,000 views, 4,000 finishes → 80% completion
  • Combined completion rate: ~80% (not 90%)

Exporting engagement data

You can export the engagement table as a CSV file. Select Export at the top right of the Engagement tab. The CSV will include all rows and columns currently visible in the table.

Things to know

  • Engagement measures views at a point in the video, not unique viewers. If the same viewer watches a segment more than once (for example, by scrubbing back), each watch is counted separately.
  • Engagement analytics are not available via the Vimeo public API.
  • Engagement analytics are available to any user or Enterprise organisation with access to the Analytics section of Vimeo.

About free AI credits

This feature requires a paid plan.

This article addresses frequently asked questions about the limited number of free AI credits offered by Vimeo, which users can utilize to test AI translation features. For general information about AI credits, visit ‘About AI Credits’.

  • How many free credits does Vimeo provide?
  • How do I access my free credits?
  • Do my free credits expire?
  • How can I purchase additional credits?

How many free credits does Vimeo provide?

The number of credits that Vimeo provides depends on your account type.

  • Free/Basic/Trial:Free credits are not provided to users on Free accounts, Basic accounts, or accounts enrolled in a trial membership.
  • Paid Plans:250 credits.
  • Enterprise:Users on Vimeo Enterprise have a certain number of AI credits as part of their plan. If your plan does not include AI credits, please contact your account manager.

If you are on a paid plan and your account downgrades to a Free or Basic plan, you cannot access AI features.

How do I access my free credits?

Free credits are automatically added to your Vimeo account. As this feature is being gradually released, you may not receive your credits immediately. You will receive an email when credits are added to your account and are available to use.

You can use these credits at any time for AI translations. Read more at ‘How do I translate my video using AI?’

You can view your credit balance in the billing menu of your account settings.

Will my free credits expire?

Yes, Vimeo grants free credits that expire 30 days after being granted. The number of days remaining on your free credits is displayed in the bottom-left corner of the Vimeo home page.

Will I lose access to my free credits if I downgrade my account?

Yes. If you are on a paid account that downgrades to a Free or Basic plan, you will not have access to AI features.

How can I purchase additional credits?

Account Owners and Admins can purchase additional credits by translating a video, subtitles and/or audio. You can purchase the number of credits needed for that translation. You cannot pre-purchase credits in bulk.

About grab-nets

Interactive is only available with custom Enterprise accounts. Please contact your account manager if you are interested in creating interactive experiences with your videos.

When adding a hotspot to your videos on interactive, you will have to first adjust the position and size of the grab-net. A grab-net is the invisible click area of a hotspot, but if you’re adding a sticky hotspot, it also defines the pixel area of the object for accurate motion tracking.

What does a grab-net do?

This will be the invisible click area while adding a hotspot. If you’re adding a sticky hotspot, it also defines the pixel area of the object for accurate motion tracking so it is necessarily worth spending a little time getting your grab-net just right.

Will the grab-net appear on my final video?

No, the grab-net is only seen in the video editor as a guide to where you want to make it clickable, it will not be shown on your final interactive video.

Why is my hotspot not sticking to the object I want it to?

To improve the tracking of an object make sure to keep the grab-net tight around the required item, this will ensure the tracking engine identifies the correct item you are aiming to stick to for the hotspot. Make sure the entire object is within the grab-net, and avoid trying to track a small part of a larger object. The objects with high contrast to the background within the video will be easier to track.

About iframe background color for embeds

The transparency discussed here is referring specifically to the iframe (the containing web element), not transparency in any videos you upload. Vimeo does not include alpha channel support at this time.

  • Transparent Background
  • Turn off the transparent background
  • Apply a custom iframe background color

Transparent Background

By default, the background of the player iframe is transparent on Vimeo. All player elements (playbar, buttons, etc) are pinned to the video image, not the actual size of the iframe.

To avoid blank space in an embed, we recommend choosing a player size that matches your video’s native aspect ratio. For example, if the original video has an aspect ratio of 16:9, you’ll want to embed the video with dimensions that yield an aspect ratio of 16:9, such as 800 x 450.

⚠️Note:The dimensions of the embedded player can also be influenced by the CSS styling established by your webpage. For videos embedded in a responsive design, make sure the height and width are both adjusted to maintain your video’s native aspect ratio.

Turn off the transparent background

If your player displays differently than what you originally intended, you can disable the transparent background.

  • To turn off the transparent background, add ?transparent=0 to the end of the player URL in your embed code. This parameter will force a black iframe background and pin the player elements to the iframe, instead of the video image.

Example embed code:

0

⚠️Note:If your video is set to the Unlisted privacy setting, the any other parameter must be added after the privacy hash (?h=913052c8ff) at the end of the URL using & instead of ?. Here’s an example of an unlisted video’s iframe code with using the transparent parameter:

`

This is not supported :

0? quality=720p

Some examples of applications that only support Vimeo URLs are social media posts, WordPress themes and plugins, Wix plugins, Squarespace plugins, and other miscellaneous video embed tools within web page builders. Some tools may allow you to adjust player preferences (like autoplay, for instance) directly in their UI.

If you need help adding a player parameter, please contact usand provide the embed code you use for faster troubleshooting.

How do I estimate the amount of storage my video file will use up on my Vimeo account?

Video storage usage on your Vimeo account is determined by the size of the original source file at the time of upload. For example, a 200MB source file will use 200MB of your total storage limit. Plans that are measured by video count are not impacted by video file size.

We understand you may want to try to calculate your video’s file size before exporting or compressing it. To get an almost accurate calculation of the video file size, it can be approximately determined by the bitrate rather than just the video resolution.

Bitrate is the most important factor in determining a video file’s size. Technically speaking, you can have a 4K video with a lower bitrate than a 720p video. However, in this instance, the 4K video quality would appear poor but take less space when compared to a 720p video. If your video contains audio, that track has its own bitrate as well.

Here is a chart for your reference: Screenshot: A table that shows examples of different resolutions, bitrate, and duration, and the size of one minute of video. For example, a 720p resolution at a bitrate of one megabyte per second is 20 megabytes in size and has a 50 minute recording duration per GB.

The above table is for heuristic estimation and references only. There are a lot of other factors that influence the actual video file size, such as compression ratio, variable bitrate, and color depth.

Video length alone isn’t a reliable determinant of how many GB it’ll use up. It can be impacted by:

  • The quality of the footage.
  • Whether the footage files have supplementary metadata files attached to them.
  • The amount and quality of audio tracks in the editing timeline prior to export as a singular file.
  • The size of a video file itself is largely impacted by how it’s being edited and exported. Each video editing software has a myriad of different export settings, all of which have complex impacts on the quality, size, and playback speed of the final file that is ultimately exported.

How do I make an audio-only recording in the Record Studio?

Users on a paid Vimeo plan can record a maximum of 120 minutes per audio recording. Users on a Free or Basic plan can record a maximum of 30 minutes per audio recording.

You can use the Record Studio to make an audio-only recording.

To make an audio-only recording

  1. Navigate to the Record Studio.
  2. From the bottom toolbar, make sure that your camera is turned off and your microphone is powered on. You can use the arrow to the right of the microphone icon to select your microphone if you have multiple audio input sources.
  3. This will display a black recording canvas.
  4. Select the Start Recordingbutton in the top-right corner of the screen to begin your recording.
  5. When you are done recording your audio, select the red Stopbutton.
  6. Your audio recording will be saved to your Library.

To display or hide the soundwave, select the arrow icon to the right of the microphone icon in the bottom toolbar. Select Show audio waveform.

Learn how to further customize the appearance of your audio-only recording at How do I customize the appearance of my audio-only recording?

How do I make my video interactive?

Classic interactive is currently only available with custom Enterprise accounts. Please contact your account manager if you are interested in creating interactive experiences with your videos.

Any video on your Vimeo account can become an interactive video, including uploads, archived events, videos made with Vimeo Create, and videos made with Vimeo Record.

  1. From yourLibrary, select your video.
  2. On the video edit page, select Interactivity on the left side menu. ⚠️Important: If this is your first time clicking Interactivity for that video, the video will need to go through an additional processing step to make it ready for interactivity. You will be prompted to watch some how-to videos as this process takes place in the background. This only happens the first time you enter the interactive editor for each video.
  3. Once your video has been processed for interactivity, click Start creating to enter the interactive editor.

How long does it take to process my video for interactivity?

Typically, the processing step for making your video interactive takes about one-third of the duration of the video. Note that the process will continue running in the backend if you happen to leave the page.

Troubleshooting: I clicked ‘Interactivity’ and all I see is a spinning wheel

If you attempt to enter the interactive editor for a video the first time and only see a spinning wheel, try the following:

  • Clear your browser’s cookies for *.wirewax.com
  • Clear your browser’s cache

How do I modify videos made in the video editor?

To modify a video in the video editor:

How do I mute/unmute my video’s original audio in the Vimeo mobile apps?

When creating a video in the Vimeo Android app, the Vimeo iOS app, or the Create apps for Android and iOS, you can choose to keep your uploaded footage’s original audio in your video or you can mute it to allow for other audio in the scene, such asa music track.

  • How to mute or unmute in the Timeline
  • How to mute or unmute in the storyboard

To mute or unmute the original footage audio in the Timeline:

  1. Select the scene containing the footage with audio in the timeline.
  2. Once the timeline is highlighted in blue, you can scroll to the left to find the Audiobutton on the toolbar.
  • If the audio is not muted, the icon will display as a speaker with soundwaves.
  • If the audio is muted, it will show as a speaker with an ‘x’.

To mute or unmute the original footage audio from the storyboard:

  1. Open the storyboard by selecting the Storyboardbutton at the top of the editor. It has two overlapping rectangles with the number of scenes in your video.
  2. Open the Scene Optionsmenu of a scene and select Muteor Unmute.
  • Android:Select the scene thumbnail to open the menu.
  • iOS:Select the ••• menu in the top-right corner of the scene’s preview thumbnail.

How do I prevent images from being cut off in my video?

Vimeo’s editing workflow use an Artificial Intelligence engine to highlight images in your video. Typically the engine will detect a face or subject and zoom in on it. Sometimes the AI engine will zoom in on an image with text or an edited graphic that may result in images getting cut off.

To avoid this:

  • Turn off the zoom feature in the media inspector toolbar in the editor. Read how at ‘How do I use the inspector toolbar in the editor?’. Select Motion Effectand select None.
  • Avoid mixing portrait and landscape media in the same video

How do I record a video in the Record Studio?

Users on a paid Vimeo plan can record a maximum of 120 minutes per video. Users on a Freeor Basicplan can record a maximum of 30 minutes per video.

You can use the Record Studio to record a video using Vimeo. In the studio, you can record your camera, microphone, or your screen. Your recording will save to your Library, where you can share it as is or further enhance it using Vimeo AIor the Editor.

Setting up your recording

You can use the input control toolbar in the Record Studio to record your camera, microphone, or share all or part of your screen. You can set up a teleprompter to read your script or talking points directly from the screen. You can customize the layout or background of your recording canvas.

To read about navigating the features in the Record Studio, visit ‘What is the Record Studio?’.

To read about customizing the appearance of your recording, such as adjusting the aspect ratio or layout, visit ’How do I customize the appearance of my recording in the Record Studio?’

Recording a video

To record a video in the Record Studio:

⚠️Note:Record Studio delivers recordings with up to 2K quality visuals.

  1. After entering the Record Studio, select which camera and microphone you would like to use in your recording from the input control bar under the canvas.

  2. If you would like to share your screen, select the Share Screen button. Here, you can select which screen, window, or browser tab you would like to record.

  3. If you would like to write a script to use for the teleprompter in your recording, select the Teleprompter button. Read how at ‘How do I use the teleprompter in the Record Studio?’

  4. To use the Picture-in-Picture feature, select the Picture-in-Picturebutton to display the pop-up window. Read about how the Picture-in-Picture feature works below.

  5. Choose your recording quality from the Settings icon. Select your preferred quality from the drop-down menu.

  6. After making your selections, select the Start Recordingbutton in the top right corner of the screen.

  7. A countdown screen will appear for you to prepare for recording. If you are using a teleprompter, the text will begin to scroll.

  8. When you have finished your record, select the Stop Recording in the top right corner. You can also select the pause button to pause or unpause the recording, the restartbutton to restart your recording, and the trashicon to delete your recording.

  9. Your video will be saved to your selected folder. While it is optimizing, if you decide that you would like to retake your recording, select the Retakebutton to return to the Record Studio.

Picture-in-Picture

⚠️Note: This feature is available when using the Studio onGoogle Chrome.

You can use the Picture-in-Picture feature in the Record Studio to open a resizable, repositionable window with tools from Record. This window will stay at the top of your screen, allowing you to navigate to other programs and control your recording without looking at the Record Studio screen.

To use Picture-in-Picture:

  1. Select the Picture-in-Picture button at the bottom toolbar in the Record Studio.
  2. A resizable, repositionable window will appear, showing a preview of your display for your recording. 💡Tip:If the Picture-in-Picture window is too small, you will be prompted to resize the window. Select and drag the corners of the window to resize it. f
  3. Select Start Recording to begin recording. A countdown will begin before your recording begins.
  4. A toolbar will appear at the bottom of the window that lets you:
  • Restart the recording
  • Delete the recording
  • Pause the recording
  • Stop the recording
  • View the timestamp of the recording
  1. When you are done recording, select the button displaying the timestamp of your recording. 💡Tip: If you are unable to see a preview of your recording in the Picture-in-Picture box, then the size of the box is too small. Resizing the box to make it larger will expand the preview.

How do I record a video in the video editor?

Users on a paid Vimeo plan can record a maximum of 120 minutes per video. Users on a Freeor Basicplan can record a maximum of 30 minutes per video.

The video editor allows you to record video, audio, and screen content directly within the platform, eliminating the need for external software. This recorded content can be added to your video’s Timeline for editing.

This article discusses how to record a video directly in the video editor. To do so:

  1. Select the Media button on the left-side toolbar.
  2. Select the Record button in the media menu to open the Record Studio.
  3. In the Record Studio, you can:
  • Choose to record your camera, microphone, and/ or screen.
  • Create an audio-only recording for voice-overs.
  • Write or generate a script for theteleprompter.
  1. Select Start Recordingto begin and Stop Recordingwhen finished.
  2. You’ll be redirected back to the video editor - your recording will be added to the Uploads tab of the Mediapanel.
  3. Select the thumbnail of the recording to add it to your Timeline at the playhead point or select and drag the thumbnail to a specific spot on the Timeline.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Your recording will be saved to the Workspace you’re logged into at the time of recording. If you’re part of multiple Workspaces, make sure you’re switched to the correct one.

How do I rename my video in the Vimeo mobile apps?

You can rename your video in the Create app in the My Videossection for both Androidand iOS.

You can rename your video in the Homeor Library sections of the the Vimeo Android appand the Vimeo iOS app.

To rename your video in the Vimeo app for Android/iOS

  1. From the Home screen of the app, select the video that you would like to rename.
  2. Select the Pencilicon to edit the title of your video.
  3. Change the name of your video. You can also add or change a description for the video below the title.
  4. Select Savewhen you’re done.

To rename your video in the Create app for Android/iOS:

  1. From the home screen of the Create app, select My Videos.
  2. Locate the video you’d like to rename in your video library and select the overflow menu (•••).
  3. In the overflow menu, select Settings.
  4. In the video settings menu, enter the new title of the video under the Title header and select Save.

How do I scale footage in the Vimeo mobile apps?

With the crop and fit feature, you can scale down your video’s footage to fit any layout and ratio in the Vimeo Android app, the Vimeo iOS app, or the Create apps for Android and iOS.

To scale media:

  1. In the editor, select the footage you want to scale from the canvas.
  2. Pinch the footage to zoom in or out.
  3. Select and drag the footage to reposition it in the scene.

If the footage size is smaller than the canvas, the remaining background will be the canvas’ background color.

How do I scale media in the editor?

Once you’ve added a photo or video to your video, you can adjust its size to best fit your media with other elements like text, graphics, or additional media.

If the resized media doesn’t fully cover the available space, the canvas’ background color will fill in the remaining area.

There are two ways to scale your media: manually, or utilizing the Fit/Fill feature.

Manual scaling

To resize a video or image on the canvas, select the photo or video to display its bounding box, and drag the corner anchor points in the direction you’d like to resize the element.

Screenshot: Media selected in a video. A rectangular bounding box with four anchor points that can be dragged to change its size and position is displayed.

Scaling using Fit/Fill.

To access the Fit/Fill tool, select a media element in your video.

The Fit Typesbutton will appear in the inspector toolbar - select to adjust how your media fits on the canvas.

Screenshot: Toolbar button for adjusting the fit of video content within the canvas. Options include ‘Fit’ and ‘Fill’.

  • Fit: Your media will be resized to fit within the canvas without any cropping.
  • Fill: Your media will be expanded to fill the entire canvas, which may result in some cropping.

Read about managing your media in the video editor at ‘How do I add and manage media in the video editor?’.

How do I select a color palette in the video editor?

You can choose from a variety of color palettes in the video editor from the Colorsmenu.

Color palettes appear in three rows: primary colors, secondary colors, and text.

Screenshot: A set of three color palettes. Each palette features a combination of three colors in horizontal stripes.

Changing a color palette will override any previously selected colors, including text colors. Color palettes are organized into three rows: primary colors, secondary colors, and text colors.

To select a color palette:

  1. Select the Colors button in the left-side panel.
  2. Scroll through the available palettes.
  3. Select the palette to apply it.

Creating Custom Color Palettes

Contributor Plus team members and above on teams with access to the Brand Kit can create custom color palettes.

To create a custom color palette:

  1. Open the Colors menu.
  2. In the Brand Colors section, click the Pencil icon.
  3. Choose colors from the menu or enter HEX codes.

You can also access and edit brand colors through the Brand Kit by clicking the Brand button in the left-side panel and selecting Colors.

How do I select my video’s aspect ratio in the Vimeo mobile apps?

The Vimeo Android app, Vimeo iOS app, and Create apps for Android and iOS automatically sets your video’s orientation based on the majority of your photos and video clips (51%).

For example, a video will be created in portrait mode if 51% of the media that you add to the video is in portrait mode.

Aspect ratios supported:

The apps support the following orientations and aspect ratios:

  • Landscape - 16:9 (1920×1080, 1280×720, etc.).
  • Portrait - 9:16 (1080x1920, 720x1280, etc.).
  • Square - 1:1 (1080x1080, 720x720, etc.).

However, you can also change the aspect ratio of the video manually:

To change the aspect ratio/orientation of your video:

  1. In the editor, select the Format button from the toolbar under the timeline.
  2. Select which aspect ratio you’d like to change your video to based on the shape of the rectangle.
  3. Select Done.

How do I set up domain-level privacy?

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

This article discusses how to set up domain-level privacy for video embedding.

With domain-level privacy, you can specify and manage up to 50 domains where your video can be embedded. Any sites that are not on your list will receive an error message when they attempt to embed it.

To set up domain-level privacy:

  1. Open the video settings page and select the Share button on the top of the page.
  2. Select the Embed option on the modal
  3. At the top of the panel, open the dropdown menu under Where can this be embedded? Select Specific domains.
  4. Add the domain names for the sites where you’d like your video to be embedded in the Allowed domains box.
  5. Select the (+) button or hit the enter key on your keyboard to save them.

💡Tip: For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Organization Owners and Administrators can set privacy restrictions for their Workspaces. Learn how at How to edit my Organization’s settings.

How do I share and manage videos from the Vimeo mobile apps?

You can share and manage your videos in the Create app for Android and iOS in the Video Optionsmenu.

You can share and manage your videos from the Video Settings menu in the Vimeo Android app or the Vimeo iOS app.

  • Share and manage your video from the Vimeo iOS app

  2. Select the overflow button for the video (⋮) to open the options menu. The options are:
  • Share: Share the link of the video, the review link, share the video file itself, or publish your video to social media.
  • Video Settings:Change the name of the video, its privacy setting, or edit the video.
  • Analytics:View the analytics for your video.
  • Edit video:Edit your video in the app in the editor.
  • Save to device:Save your video to your mobile device.
  • Add to an offline playlist
  • Move to folder:Move your video to another folder on your Vimeo account.
  • Watch Later

To share and manage videos from the Vimeo iOS app:

  2. Select the overflow button for the video (⋯) to open the video settings menu.

To share videos:

  1. From the video settings menu, select Share. 💡Tip:If your video’s privacy setting is not publicly viewable by default (e.g., Unlisted or Private), a popup menu will let you know. If you would still like to share the video, select Share Anyway. Read about video privacy settings at Overview of video privacy settings.
  2. Select from one of the share options:

  • Share review link:Share your video’s review page to collect feedback and securely share rough cuts. Read about the video review page at the Video review page.

To manage videos:

Select from one of the options from the video settings menu:

  • Add to Showcase
  • Save to Camera Roll: Saves your video to the Camera Roll of your iOS device.
  • Share:
  • Watch Later
  • Save video offline
  • Replace video
  • Edit thumbnail
  • Delete video

To share and manage your video from the Create app:

  1. Select My Videosfrom the home screen of the Create app.
  2. Select the three dots (•••) at the end of the row of the selected video to open the video options menu.

In the video options menu, you can:

  • Share link:Set the privacy settings for your video and select Share linkfor the direct URL to your video.
  • Share file:Downloads the video file to your mobile device and provides multiple locations where you can share your video file.
  • More share options:Access the embed code for the video, share a review link (for applicable accounts), or directly publish to Facebook, Instagram, YouTube.
  • Download:Downloads the video file to your mobile device.
  • Edit:Open the video in the Create app editor.

How do I trim my videos?

This article refers to the trimmer tool found on the video settings page for all uploaded Vimeo videos. Use the trimmer to remove unwanted sections from the beginning and end of your video.

To read more about the trimming feature in the editor, visit How do I use the Timeline in the video editor?

⚠️Note:If your account is Standard, Pro,orhigher, you’ll have access to the text-based video editor. Read more at ‘How do I use the text-based video editor?‘.

You can access the trimmer on the video settings page. Select Edit on the right-hand panel and then Trimmer.

To use the basic trimmer:

  1. Visit the video’s settings page and select the Editingbutton on the left-side panel. The button shows a pair of scissors.
  2. Select “Trimmer”from the panel that appears on the left.
  3. Select and drag the trimmer handles at the beginning and end of your video to shorten or lengthen the duration. 💡Tip:You can also untrim previously trimmed videos. Select the trimmer handles and drag in the opposite direction you used to trim to display the previously trimmed media.
  4. You can split your video into multiple clips by selecting and dragging the time indicator needle to the specified point in your video and selecting the Split button. ().
  5. The clip will be split into two separate clips on either side of the time indicator needle.
  • Each clip can be trimmed individually of the other or split further.
  • You can also delete a clip by selecting it and clicking the Deletebutton.

💡Tip:Use the zoom slider to zoom in and out of the timeline to help you make more exact trims.

How do I re-trim my video?

If you want to re-trim your video from a previous version, you can try the following steps.

  1. Click on the version dropdown menu on top of the screen
  2. In the Version History box, select the version of your video to which you’d like to restore it.
  3. Once selected, the version will be restored. Follow the instructions listed above to re-trim the restored version of your video.

This will restore your video to its previous version. Follow the instructions listed above to re-trim the restored version of your video.

If you are still unable to trim your video, please contact support for further assistance. Please include the URL for the video you would like to trim, along with the specific steps you used.

⚠️Notes:

  • Videos longer than 2 hours cannot be trimmed using the text-based video editor. However, they can be trimmed by using the trimming steps above.
  • Videos can be trimmed in units of 20 milliseconds (0:00:20) and above.
  • The tool is not enabled for 360-degree videos or videos uploaded to Vimeo before October 2013.
  • Currently, the trimmer is not enabled for VOD (video-on-demand) videos.
  • If you would like multiple trimmed clips to be saved as separate videos, you will need to re-upload your original video to trim it another time.

How do I upload custom fonts in the video editor?

The feature discussed below requires a Standard, Advanced, Business, Premium, or Enterprise account.

Team members can upload and manage brand fonts for all team members via the Brand Kit in the video editor. Upload permissions are based on the type of account that you are a team member of.

  • Enterprise: Contributor Plus, Owner, or Admins can upload and delete custom fonts.
  • Standard, Advanced, Business, or Premium: Contributors, Owners, and Admins can upload and delete fonts.

⚠️ Note: By uploading a font file, you confirm that you own the font or have obtained all necessary licenses to use and incorporate it into a video as required by our Terms of Service.

  • How to upload a brand font
  • How to select an existing font as a brand font
  • How to delete a brand font

To upload a brand font:

  1. Select the Brand button on the left-side panel in the video editor to open the Brand Kit.
  2. In the Brand Kit, select Fonts.
  3. Select + Add Brand Font.
  4. Select the Upload button at the bottom of the font list.
  5. Agree to the font submission terms.
  6. Select the font file (.ttfor.otf) from your device.
  7. Once uploaded, the font can be selected from the Brand Kit or the text inspector toolbar’s font menu.

To select an existing font as a brand font:

  1. Select the Brand button on the left-side panel in the video editor to open the Brand Kit.
  2. In the Brand Kit, select Fonts.
  3. Select + Add Brand Font.
  4. Scroll through the list of available fonts.
  5. When you find a font you want to use as a brand font, hover over the font name to display a circle with a plus sign in the middle. Select to add to brand fonts.

To delete a brand font:

To delete the font from your brand fonts, hover over the selected font in the Brand Fonts menu and select the minus icon to the right.

How do I use a template in the Vimeo mobile apps?

Templates are video creatives pre-made for your use. You can edit templates with your footage and more to customize it to fit the needs of your video.

To select a template in the Vimeo mobile app:

  1. From the editor, select ‘Pick a template’(Android) or ’Edit a Template’(iOS).
  2. Select a template that you would like to use as the foundation for your video. You will be able to preview it.
  3. Select ‘Edit template’ to customize the template for your use. This will bring it into the editing portion of the Create app.
  4. Edit the template to best fit your video’s needs. You can make changes such as adding your media or changing existing text.

How do I use the inspector toolbar in the editor?

The inspector toolbar is located above the canvas in the video editor.

It houses a set of tools for manipulating elements within your video. The toolbar’s buttons are dynamic, presenting only the relevant tools based on the currently selected element—media, text, or graphics.

Expand each section to learn which tools are available for various element types in your video:

Media inspector toolbar

The media inspector toolbar appears when you select video clips or images in your video. Read about working with media in your video at How do I add and manage media in the video editor?.

The tools in the Media Inspector Toolbar are:

Videos:

  • Media Sound -Adjust or mute the audio volume in your media.
  • Crop -Crop your video clip.
  • Fit types -Select whether your video should fit or fill the canvas.
  • Animation- Select an animation for how your media appears
  • Replace -Replace your video clip with a new one.

Photos:

  • Crop.
  • Fit types -Select whether your photo should fit or fill the canvas.
  • Animation
  • Replace

Text Inspector toolbar

The Text Inspector toolbar appears when you select a text box. Read about working with text in the video editor at ‘How do I add and edit text in the video editor?’

Tools in the Text Inspector Toolbar are:

  • Font
  • Font size
  • Background Color: Customize the fill color and opacity of the text box.
  • Highlight Color: Choose the color of the highlighter used within the text box.
  • Alignment: Align the text left, center, or right within the text box
  • Drop Shadow: Apply a soft, normal, or strong shadow effect to the text.
  • Animation: Add an animation effect that plays when the text box appears on the screen. Choose from animations that apply to the entire text box, each line, each word, or each character.
  • Edit: Open the text menu from the left-side panel to modify the text box content.

Graphics inspector toolbar

The graphics inspector toolbar appears when selecting a graphic in your video. Read about working with graphics at How do I add and manage graphics in the video editor?

Tools included in the graphics inspector toolbar are:

  • Color: Modify the color of the graphic (if available).
  • Rotation: Adjust the angle of the graphic.
  • Flip: Flip the graphic horizontally or vertically.
  • Opacity: Adjust the opacity of the graphic.
  • Animation: Apply special effects to the graphic

How do I use the teleprompter in the Record Studio?

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

You can write a script or talking points in the Record Studio to use as a teleprompter.

To write a script:

  1. In the Record Studio, select the Teleprompter button on the input control toolbar.
  2. The teleprompter window will appear. It is repositionable and resizable. In the textbox, write your script or the talking points for your video.
  3. The teleprompter box also has controls to change the speed of the text scroll and to increase or decrease the size of the font. 💡Tip: Auto speed uses voice recognition to match the speed of the text scrolling with your pace of talking.
  4. When you are happy with your script or talking points, select the Xbutton in the top-right corner of the teleprompter window to exit out.
  5. When you beginrecording your video, the teleprompter window will appear and text will begin to scroll, allowing you to read directly from the screen.

⚠️Note: You cannot share your screen while using the teleprompter as the teleprompter will appear in your final video.

💡Tip:The teleprompter window is both resizable and repositionable for you to customize the best fit. Select and drag the teleprompter window to move it to a new position on the screen. Select and drag the corners of the teleprompter window to resize it.

If you are on a paid Vimeo plan - Pro and above or Standard and above, you can utilize AI to generate a script in the Record Studio. Learn how at ‘How do I use AI to generate a script in the Record Studio?’.

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

How do I use the text-based editor in the Vimeo mobile apps?

If your video contains audio with spoken English, you can use the text-based editing feature with the trimmer to edit your video in the the Vimeo Android app or the Vimeo iOS app. Here, you can remove filler words such as ‘ums and uhs’, word gaps with no sound, and any other selection of individual words or longer sections of footage containing speech.

To use the text-based video editor:

  1. From the homescreen, select the Library button to view your video library.
  2. Select the video that you would like to use the text-based video editor with.
  3. Select Edit Video.
  4. Select Text-based editor.
  5. A transcript of the speech in your video will be generated.
  6. Double tap a word in the transcript to select it. The word will be highlighted when selected.
  • If you would like to delete the single word that is selected, select Delete
  • If you would like to select multiple words, select and drag the handles until all words that you would like to delete are highlighted.
  1. Select Deleteto delete the unwanted word(s).
  2. After selecting Deletethe word will be removed from your video.
  3. Select Save to save your video.

You can also use the text-based video editor to remove pauses, gaps, and portions with no sound from your video.

Portions without sounds will be represented in your transcript by a dot (●). You can select the dot (or series of dot) that you would like to remove from your video, similar to selecting words. Select Deleteto remove these gaps from your video.

Show/Hide Deleted Words

Select the Showdeleted words button to show or hide which words have been deleted from your video. It will also show much time is removed from your video when removing portions without sound.

AI editing

Select the AI editingbutton to use AI to detect gaps and filler words to remove in bulk. You can select whether the gaps and filler words should be removed.

Search transcript

Use the Search transcriptbutton to search your transcript for specific words.

How do I use the text-based video editor?

If your video has spoken English audio, the text-based editing feature can be used with the trimmer tool to edit out filler words, silent gaps, and other unwanted speech sections.

  • Using text-based video editing in the video editor

Using text-based video editing in the video editor

Text-based video editing tools are available for use in thevideo editor.

To use text-based video editing inthe video editor:

  1. Select the Transcript button above the Timeline.
  2. Select the Transcribebutton next to the video clips that the editor recognizes contain speech.
  3. This will extend the “Transcription” menu from the left-side toolbar.
  4. You can switch between transcriptions for all of the clips in your video by selecting the name and thumbnail preview in the transcription frame.

Searching the transcript

Select the search bar at the top of the transcription to search the transcript for specific words in your video. The keywords will be highlighted in your transcript.

Removing Filler Words and Word Gaps

Select the AI Sparkles to identify and bulk-remove all filler words (e.g., ums and uhs) at once, or identify and bulk-remove the total number of word gaps based on a minimum length you set.

Deleting Words

Show or Hide Deleted Words:

You can show or hide all deleted words from the transcript by toggling the Show/Hide deleted words button.

How do I use the Timeline in the video editor?

The Timeline, located below the canvas in the video editor, allows you to organize and modify the sequence and duration of elements in your video, such as media, text, music, and graphics.

Additionally, you can edit your video by using keyboard shortcuts.

Each element is represented by a color-coded block that can be moved, trimmed, or extended.

Screenshot: Multitrack video editing timeline with separate tracks for audio, video clips, and text elements.

The top of the timeline contains tools to facilitate text-based video editing, including splitting and deleting elements, as well as playing and pausing your video. You can also zoom in and out of the timeline or resize the timeline to fit your browser window.

The video editor supports multi-track editing, allowing for simultaneous playback of media and effects. For example, you can play multiple video clips alongside photos, or layer background music with an uploaded voiceover track.

⚠️Note: If you overlap multiple videos or photos, the topmost layer in the stack will be the top layer displayed in the video. However, if another layer’s media contains sound (e.g., a video clip of a cityscape with traffic sounds), the sounds will continue to play in the background.

How do I use the Timeline in the Vimeo mobile apps?

The timeline in the Vimeo Android app, the Vimeo iOS app, or the Create apps for Android and iOS helps you adjust the timing of scenes and elements that are added to scenes.

  • Adjust the duration of scenes
  • Adjust the duration of photos, stickers, and text
  • Split scenes
  • Enable auto duration (iOS only)

Adjusting the duration of scenes:

Scenes are represented in the timeline by a box containing a thumbnail of what the scene looks like. You can pinch/expand the timeline to zoom in on a scene’s portion in the timeline.

To adjust the duration of scenes in the timeline:

  1. Select the scene from the timeline. This will surround the scene in a blue box with a blue handle on the start and end points of the scene.
  2. Select and drag the handlebars to either lengthen or shorten the scene.

Adjusting the duration of photos, text, and stickers:

Photos, text, and stickers added to scenes are designated an orange box overlaying the timeline and by an orange bubble above the timeline that shows a preview of the photo, sticker, or text. These can be adjusted individually.

To adjust the duration of text, stickers, or photos:

  1. Select the scene that you’d like to edit.
  2. Select the element in the scene (text, sticker, or photo) that you would like to change the duration of. This will highlight the element in the timeline with a yellow box and a yellow handle on the start and end points of the element.
  3. Select and drag the orange handlebars to either lengthen or shorten the duration. 💡Tip:You can also select the entire orange box and drag and drop to change at which point the element appears in the scene.

Splitting scenes:

Scenes can be divided from one longer scene into two shorter scenes in the timeline.

Cutaway scenes cannot be split. Each resulting scene must be a minimum of 0.5 seconds long.

To split a scene:

  1. Select the scene that you would like to split in the timeline. This will surround the scene in a blue box in the timeline.
  2. Select and drag the needle indicator in the timeline to the point in your scene that you would like to divide into two scenes.
  3. Select Spliton the toolbar to divide the scene into two scenes.

Enabling auto duration (Create iOS only):

Auto duration automatically adjusts scene duration - including the length of time for text and stickers. This feature can be toggled on and off.

💡Tip:Currently, this feature is available for title scenes or scenes with photos in the Create app for iOS.

To enable/disable auto duration:

  1. Select a title scene or a scene containing photos.
  2. Select Durationfrom the toolbar.
  3. Select the toggle button to enable or disable auto duration.

How should I measure success for an interactive video?

When reviewing your interactive analytics, the benchmarks you measure against may vary depending on the type of video. Below are some general recommendations to look for to help give you some guidance on how engaged viewers were with your interactive videos.

Overlay time (seconds)

Per the IAB, the industry norm for dwell time on an overlay is 14.8 seconds. Based on this, we suggest the following benchmarks for success:

  • 0-15 seconds - Fair
  • 16-29 second - Good
  • 30-50 seconds - Very good
  • 50 seconds and above - Exceptional
