What permissions are required to access the Brand Kit?

  • If you are on a per-seat pricing plan, the Brand Kit is available with a Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise plan.
  • If you purchased your membership via vimeo.com or the Vimeo mobile apps, the Brand Kit is available with the Businessor Premiumplans.

In addition, Brand Kit permissions are based on which type ofteam member is working on the Brand Kit:

  • Standard, Advanced, Business, Premium
  • Role: Contributors, Owners, Admins
  • Brand Kit Permissions: Can upload and manage Brand Kit elements (fonts, logos, colors, etc.).
  • Example: An Admin can upload a custom font to the Brand Kit.
  • Enterprise
  • Role: Contributor Plus, Owner, Admin
  • Brand Kit Permissions: Can upload and manage Brand Kit elements.
  • Enterprise
  • Role: Contributor
  • Brand Kit Permissions: Can apply Brand Kit elements that an Owner or Admin previously uploaded. Cannot manage, upload, or remove brand elements.
  • Example: A Contributor can apply an uploaded font to their video but cannot upload a new custom font or remove existing ones.

How do I access the Brand Kit?

You can access the Brand Kit in various locations, depending on whether you are creating or editing your video.

To access the Brand Kit in the editor:
  1. Select your video.
  2. Click on the Editoption.
  3. Select Brand. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-11-19 at 4.26.00 PM.png
To access the Brand Kit in the mobile app:

You can access the Brand Kit in the mobile app’s editor.

  1. Select your video.
  2. Select the Brandbutton from the editor ribbon, located below the timeline.

Customizing the Brand Kit

The features that you can customize in the Brand Kit include:

  • Logo: Upload and set your brand’s logo.
  • Supported file formats include JPG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, and PNG.
  • Currently, a GIF file renders as a still image.
  • Switching the toggle next to the Logo in the Brand Kit menu will apply your logo to all scenes in the video.
  • Colors: Select the color palette that represents your brand. Set the Primary, Secondary,andText colors for your brand by using the color picker or by entering the hex code for that color.
  • Primary colors:Scene background and larger graphics.
  • Secondary colors:Media and text background.
  • Text:Color of text added.
  • Font: Select the font for your brand from a vast library of fonts. 💡Tip:Standard, Advanced, Business, Premium, and Enterprise accounts can upload custom fonts. Read how at ‘How to upload custom fonts in the video editor’
  • Intros and Outros:Upload previously created branded video clips for your organization to use as intros or outros in your videos. Read more at How to add an intro or outro to my video

Customizing the Brand Kit will apply the settings to your account. For example, if you customize the Brand Kit in the desktop editor, the settings will display in the Brand Kit within the mobile app.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:The Brand kit can be set at both the Organization level and the Workspace level. To read more, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings or How to edit my Workspace’s settings.

How to access my video’s direct links

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

This feature enables you to access your converted video files, hosted on Vimeo, for playback or download via a third-party player or web page. It also addresses important privacy and analytics considerations. This article explains how to access direct links for your videos.

  • What to know before accessing a video’s direct links
  • How to access my video’s direct links for third-party playback
  • How to access my video’s direct links for downloading
  • Making the most of third-party players
  • What happens if I downgrade my membership?
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before accessing a video’s direct links

Download links are permanent. Anyone with the link can download your videos. To prevent this, delete the video from Vimeo, or as an alternative, you can:

  • Use the Send file option. When sharing that page, you can always turn off the download links.
  • You can also shareyour video page with downloads temporarily enabled.
  • The direct links under both the Play the Video and Download the Video dropdown menus contain the same files. For downloads, we return a special header to instruct the browser to save the file to the local disk instead of playing it back. However, this does not prevent downloading the Play URL (or prevent playing back download URLs, if used in a player).

How to access my video’s direct links for third-party playback

To access direct links for your video that you can play in a third-party player or web page:

  1. Select a video from the Library.
  2. Click the3 vertical dotsin the top right corner of the video settings page.
  3. Select Video file linksfrom the dropdown menu.
  4. Choose Play the videofrom the dropdown menu.
  5. Select the Copy Linkoption.
  • We recommend open-source players like Dash.js and HLS.js for video playback. You’ll see these along with progressive MP4, HLS, andDASH links.
  • HLSis Apple’s adaptive streaming method, sending video overHTTPfor native playback on Apple devices. HLS.js can extend HLS playback to non-Apple platforms.
  • DASH(Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP) links are used for Vimeo-hosted files in other players, typically on non-Apple devices or environments. DASH supports more features and offers greater customization than other streaming protocols.
  • To tell if content is streaming via HLS or DASH:
  • HLS: Compatible with Apple devices (Apple TV, Safari, iOS).
  • DASH: Compatible with all browsers and environments except Apple products.

⚠️Note: Sharing a direct playback link shouldn’t allow video downloads, but Chrome browsers may offer a download option due to Chrome’s functionality, not Vimeo’s. Other browsers will not have this option.

How to access my video’s direct links for downloading

To access direct links for your video that you can play in a third-party player or web page:

  1. Select a video from the Library.
  2. Click the3 vertical dotsin the top right corner of the video settings page.
  3. Select Video file linksfrom the dropdown menu.
  4. Select Download the video from the dropdown menu.
  5. Select the Copy Link button for the version of the video you’d like the link for.

Making the most of third-party players

Privacy
  • Vimeo’s privacy and custom embed settings do not apply to third-party player links.
  • Third-party player links do not expire.
  • When sharing, copy the link directly from your video settings, not the redirected link in the browser.
  • Modifying the URL will result in a 403 error.
Analytics
  • Data gathering is limited for non-Vimeo players; only the approximate number of video file plays can be determined.
  • As of August 7, 2024, a separate metric called Third-party Impressions is provided, representing the number of times a video file is loaded via a third-party player.
  • Third-party view approximations are no longer included in the total views count in analytics.

What happens if I downgrade my membership?

If you downgrade to Free, Starter, Basic, or Plus, any direct links you’ve shared or embedded will stop working(for example, your embedded video will no longer load). If you decide to reupgrade to Standard, Pro, or a higher plan, your links will automatically reactivate.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn about creating a custom URL for your videos.

How to access registrant data

Please note that due to the Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA), viewers must opt-in to have their viewing data shared with the video owner. Thus, we will not collect or show any viewer-level analytics (watch time) for viewers who filled out a legacy contact form.

Follow these steps to download data from your registration forms:

  1. From the video page, select Interactivefrom the left-hand panel.
  2. Select Registration and then Manage registrants.
  3. You will see a list of registrants from the video. If you opened the registration page directly, you would see a list of your preset forms.
  4. Select Export CSV from the top-right corner to download your data.
  5. The CSV file will be saved to your desktop with the following values:
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Email
  • Registration Date (UTC)
  • Views
  • % Watched
  • Source Type
  • Source

Learn analytics terminology at the Analytics Glossary.

How to access the Date report

⚠️Note:All data in analytics reports are in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time).

This article explains how to effectively utilize the Date report in the Advanced Analytics dashboard on Vimeo to analyze video performance metrics within specific time frames. The date report is available within the Advanced Analytics dashboard.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Analytics are also available for both the Organization and its Workspaces. Organizations can view combined analytics from all Workspaces.

To access the date report:

  1. Log in to your Vimeo account and open theAdvanced Analytics dashboard.
  2. Select Date from the dashboard menu on the left side of the page to see a graph that will show you the overall views of your videos for each date within the selected time frame.
  3. The graph will display your impressions, views, finishes, and average percentage watched according to the specified date or range of dates from the filters. Screenshot: image (6).png
  4. Choose an option from the dropdown menu above the graph. It will show your impressions, finishes, downloads, unique viewers, unique impressions, avg. % watched, avg. time watched, or total time watched, per the given date or range of dates you’ve specified from the filters.
  5. You may also filter your data by timeframe using the dropdown menu at the top right of the graph.
  6. Under the graph is a table version of your data, sorted by date. You can use the Choose secondary dimensiondropdown menu at the top of the table to add another dimension to the date report. You will see the following options: video, device, region, source URL, or streaming type.
  7. Select the Export databutton at the top right of the table to export the video analytics as a CSV file.
  8. The report will be emailed to you once it is ready.

How to access the Device report

This article explains how to utilize the Device report in Vimeo’s Advanced Analytics dashboard to analyze video performance by device type.

⚠️Note:All data in analytics reports are in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time).

The Device report is available within the Advanced Analytics dashboard. To access the report:

  1. Log in to your Vimeo account and open theAdvanced analytics dashboard.
  2. Select “Device” from the dashboard menu on the left side of the page to view a graph that displays the overall views of your videos by device type within the selected time frame.
  3. Hovering over a point on the graph will display a statistical breakdown of up to 10 of your selected devices, with the highest performers displaying first.
  4. Below your graph on the Device Report table, you will find all your device-specific data synced from your videos for the selected time frame.

  7. Select the Export databutton at the top right of the table to export the video analytics as a CSV file.
  8. The report will be emailed to you once it is ready.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Analytics are also available for both an Organization and its Workspaces. Organization Admins can view combined analytics for all Workspaces.

How to activate dark mode on the Vimeo website

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can change the appearance of some pages on the Vimeo website by switching to dark mode for an alternative viewing and editing experience. This article explains how to activate dark mode for your account.

  • What to know before activating dark mode
  • How to activate dark mode

What to know before activating dark mode

Before you change your appearance settings, take note of the following:

  • Dark mode shows supported pages with a dark background and light text. Light mode shows a white background with dark text.
  • Supported pages: Dark mode is currently only available on the video upload page, the video editor, and private video recipient view pages.
  • Unsupported pages, such as the accounts settings page, will default to light mode.
  • If you are a member of a team or workspace, your setting will not impact the view settings for other team members.
  • Your selected mode will remain the default for all supported pages.

How to activate dark mode

You can customize your appearance settings from your profile menu or directly on supported pages. To do so:

From the profile menu:
  1. After logging into Vimeo, select your profile icon in the top right.
  2. Toggle the dark mode switch. Your viewing experience will change to dark mode on supported pages on the Vimeo website.
  3. Selecting the toggle again will switch the interface back to light mode.

Screenshot: A Vimeo profile menu showing the ‘Dark mode’ toggle switch located at the bottom of the menu list.

From a dark-mode supported page:
  1. Navigate to the upload page, video editor, or a private recipient page.
  2. Select the dark mode icon (a circle with a half-moon shape) in the lower corner of the screen. Your viewing experience will change to dark mode on supported pages on the Vimeo website.
  3. Selecting the icon again will switch the interface back to light mode.

How to activate or deactivate default automatic captions

This feature requires a paid plan.

You can manage whether automatically generated captions are available to viewers by default on new uploads or on a per-video basis. This article explains how to activate or deactivate automatic captions in your account settings and for individual videos.

  • What to know before updating settings for automatic captions
  • How to activate or deactivate automatic captions for new uploads

What to know before updating settings for automatic captions

Before you change your settings, take note of the following:

  • Automatic captioning is available to allpaid members for videos uploaded after May 25, 2022.
  • If your video was uploaded before May 25, 2022, re-uploading your video will generate automatic closed captions.
  • Automatic captions are activated on uploaded videos by default as long as your language on the Vimeo site is set to one that supports automatic captions.
  • Captions generated automatically are labeled as “Autogenerated” to inform viewers and distinguish them from manually uploaded captions.
  • Automatic captions are also available for live events.

How to activate or deactivate default captions for new uploads

You can turn off default automatic captions for all future uploads. To do so:

  1. Navigate to the Upload defaults section of your account settings.
  2. By default, the checkbox next to Allow viewers to enable automatically generated captionsis checked. Uncheck the box to turn this off.
  3. Select Save.

Your videos still transcribe on the backend, but the auto captions will not be available to your viewers unless you activate the setting.

How to activate or deactivate automatic captions on individual videos

You can activate and deactivate automated captions for an individual video on its settings page. To do so:

  1. Select your video from your library to open its settings page.
  2. Select Languages from the left-side toolbar.
  3. Select the toggle to activate or deactivate captions under each language header.

Suggested next steps

  • If you do not see automatic closed captions in the Languages panel, refer to Troubleshooting: Auto CC not generating in the correct language or at all.
  • Visit FAQ: Automatic captionsfor common questions about automatic captions.

How to add a Sentiment widget to videos

This feature is available on all paid plans (Self Serve and Enterprise).

The Sentiment widget lets you capture viewer reactions inside the video itself. Viewers respond with one click — no forms, no redirects — and you get aggregated feedback alongside the rest of your video analytics.

Sentiment is ideal for training, customer education, support, and internal-comms videos where you want to measure whether content is useful or engaging without sending viewers to an external survey.

⚠️Note: You can add one Sentiment widget per video. The two variants — thumbs up/down and 1–5 star rating — are mutually exclusive on a given video. Each viewer can respond once per session.

  • About the Sentiment widget
  • How to add a Sentiment widget to a video
  • Choosing a variant: thumbs up/down or star rating
  • Customizing the button label
  • The viewer experience
  • Editing or removing the widget on a published video
  • Adding a Sentiment widget to multiple videos at once
  • What happens when you replace the video file
  • Sentiment analytics
  • API support

About the Sentiment widget

Sentiment is an interactive component that renders inside the player at a timestamp you choose. Viewers see a short prompt and either thumbs up/down buttons or a 1–5 star scale. After they respond, voting is disabled for that session and their reaction is added to the aggregate.

How to add a Sentiment widget to a video

  1. Open your video from your Library.
  2. In the left panel of the managed video page, select Interactivity.
  3. In the Interactivity panel, choose Sentiment (alongside Cards, End screens, and other components).
  4. Pick a variant — Thumbs up/down or 1–5 star rating.
  5. Set the timestamp at which you want the widget to appear during playback.
  6. Enter a button label (up to 42 characters).
  7. Select Save.

Choosing a variant: thumbs up/down or star rating

  • Thumbs up/down — binary feedback. Best when you want a quick sense of whether the content landed.
  • 1–5 star rating — graded feedback. Best when you want to measure degree of usefulness or quality.

You can only use one variant per video. To switch, edit the existing widget rather than adding a second one.

Customizing the button label

The button label is the short prompt shown to viewers (for example, “Was this helpful?” or “Rate this lesson”). Labels can be up to 42 characters.

The viewer experience

At the configured timestamp, the widget appears in the player. The viewer clicks once — thumbs up/down, or a star — and their response is recorded. The UI then disables further voting for that session, so each viewer counts once per play.

Editing or removing the widget on a published video

Sentiment widgets can be added, edited, or removed on already-published videos without affecting viewer access. Existing responses are preserved when you edit the widget; removing the widget stops collection but does not delete previously collected data from your analytics.

Adding a Sentiment widget to multiple videos at once

You can apply a Sentiment widget to several videos in one action:

  1. Go to your Library.
  2. Select the videos you want to update.
  3. Apply the Sentiment component from the bulk-actions menu.

The current limit is 50 videos per bulk action, consistent with other bulk actions in the Library. We expect to raise this limit in the coming months.

What happens when you replace the video file

Your Sentiment widget configuration is preserved when you replace the source video, including the variant, label, and trigger timestamp. The one exception: if the trigger timestamp is later than the new video’s duration, the widget will not render. In that case, edit the widget and choose a timestamp that fits the new file.

Sentiment analytics

Single video: Open the video from your Library and select the Analytics panel on the left. The Sentiment section shows aggregate metrics for that video — for example, total responses, thumbs up rate, or average star rating, depending on the variant you chose.

Across videos: Sentiment data is also segmented and aggregated in the cross-video Analytics section, so you can compare performance across your library and identify which videos are landing best with your audience.

For broader context on the analytics panel, see About analytics on the Video page and the Analytics Glossary.

API support

The Sentiment component can be added, edited, or removed via the Vimeo API, and Sentiment analytics are exposed via the Analytics API. See the developer documentation on developer.vimeo for the relevant endpoints.

How to add an interactive quiz to your video

This feature requires an Enterprise plan. This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the New Interactive toolenabled to create quizzes, and learner seats are needed for SCORM integration and LMS tracking.

Interactive quizzes serve as a method for assessing learners’ grasp of the material and evaluating their understanding of the content within your videos. By integrating knowledge checks directly into the content, you ensure engagement and can provide immediate feedback.

This article outlines the steps to create and configure a quiz within your video, and how to use the Export to LMS option to pass those results to an external Learning Management System (LMS) using standards like SCORM or xAPI.

  • Things to know before you create an interactive quiz
  • How to create an interactive quiz?
  • What happens when a user interacts with the video?
  • Making the most of your interactive quiz

Things to know before you create an interactive quiz

  • Interactive quizzes can be created only in the New interactive editor.
  • For full visibility on quiz results, you’ll want to have an LMS that integrates with one of the standards Vimeo supports.

How to create an interactive quiz?

Follow the steps below to create an interactive quiz in the editor:

  1. Choose your video > Select Interactivity > Interactive editor.
  2. Select Polls and quizzes> create quizby adding questions and answers.
  3. Select the correct answer from the choices you have provided. Then, click on the star icon.
  4. Click on Preview from the top navigation bar to preview your video.
  5. Save your video. Use the Publish> Export to LMSoption after you add an interactive quiz to your video.
  6. Select the Quiz score option from the Scoring method dropdown. Export your video. This option ensures your video is formatted to be SCORM-compliant. You will receive a zip file that you can export.
  7. Take the exported zip file and upload it to your chosen LMS system.
  8. In your LMS system, launch the newly uploaded video lesson.
  9. Watch the video and answer the interactive questions as they appear. Example:Select the correct answers for the quiz questions within the video.
  10. Once you have answered the questions and completed the video lesson, finish or exit the lesson.

The system will communicate your results back to the LMS, and you will receive a completion success status, along with the tracked quiz score.

What happens when a user interacts with the video?

When a user interacts with the video, the following events are tracked and communicated via SCORM to your LMS:

  • Video Start/Finish: Confirmation of when the user begins and completes the content.
  • Percentage Watched: The total viewing time recorded.
  • Question Responses: Detailed records of the answers submitted by the learner.
  • Assessment Scores: Includes final scores, custom scorecards, and any detailed feedback.
  • Interactive Element Usage: Tracking of engagement with all interactive elements.
  • Learning Outcome Progress: General progress against defined learning objectives.

Making the most of your interactive quiz

Your interactive video supports two main tracking methods, depending on your setup and privacy requirements, and captures several key events transmitted back to your LMS.

Tracking Methods

Anonymous Tracking (No Vimeo SSO)

  • Requirements: No Vimeo Single Sign-On (SSO) is needed. The LMS must pass the learner ID to Vimeo.
  • Video Privacy Setting: Set the video privacy to Unlisted or Embed only.
  • Data Handling: No personal data is stored, ensuring the process is privacy-compliant.
  • Tracking Detail: Provides basic progress tracking.

Authenticated Tracking (With Vimeo SSO)

  • Requirements: Vimeo Single Sign-On (SSO) is required for user identification.
  • Video Privacy Setting: Set the video privacy to “Private”.
  • Data Handling: Enables enhanced user profile integration.
  • Tracking Detail: Allows for advanced analytics and personalization.

How to add media

  • Video file types: 3GP, AVI, MOV, MP4, MPG, MTS, M2TS, WebM

To add new media:
