⚠️Note: If you encounter a “Technical Difficulties” error while adding media, try again. If the issue persists, contact Support for further assistance.

You can also incorporate pre-designed elements into your video and customize them to suit your video’s needs. Learn more at ’How do I work with templates in the video editor?

How do I crop media?

The inspector toolbar allows for manual or ratio-based auto-cropping of media.

To crop media:

  1. Choose the media you want to crop on the canvas.
  2. Select “Crop” on the Inspector Toolbar.
  3. In Custom crop mode, drag the anchor points on the bounding box to adjust the crop area.
  4. Click the blue checkmark to finish.

Cropping by Ratio

To crop using a preset ratio (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), select “Ratio” mode in the Inspector Toolbar once more to activate the setting.

How do I duplicate media?

You can create exact copies of video clips, audio files, images, or other supported media types directly within the Timeline editing interface to quickly reuse media assets without needing to re-import or re-create them from scratch.

To duplicate media:

  1. Select the media element that you want to duplicate in the Timeline.
  2. Right-click the media and select Duplicate from the menu. Screenshot: A clip selected in the timeline. The Right-click menu is open with options to copy, duplicate, paste, delete, and replace the selected element. ‘Duplicate’ is highlighted.
  3. A copy of the media will appear above the original in the Timeline at the position of the playhead. Select and drag the media to the position you’d like it to play

💡Tip: You can also select Copy from the same menu and Paste the media on the Timeline in the position you’d like.

How to reorder media

To change the order of your media, select the corresponding element block on the timeline and drag it to a new spot on the timeline.

💡Tip: When you place media clips on top of each other so they are stacked on multi-tracks, they will overlap and play simultaneously. To ensure that your media plays in a sequence, arrange the clips horizontally along the timeline unless you would like multiple media to play simultaneously (e.g., you have multiple video clips playing simultaneously or are displaying photos while playing videos at the same time).

How to trim or extend media

You can trim or extend media in the Timeline.

To trim or extend media:

  1. Select the media clip in the Timeline to trim or extend. This will highlight the clip and display its adjustment handles. Screenshot: A selected video clip in the timeline with handles that can be dragged to trim or extend its duration.
  2. Drag the handles
  • Shortening the Clip: Select and drag the edge towards the center of the clip to reduce its duration.
  • Lengthening the Clip: Select and drag the edge away from the center of the clip to increase its duration. This will reveal more of the clip’s content in the Timeline.

Note: If you’ve previously shortened a clip, you can always lengthen it again up to its original duration.

How to split media

The Split button divides a single media block into multiple. The media that you would like to split must be longer than 0.5 seconds.

To split media:

  1. Select the media that you would like to divide in the Timeline
  2. Drag the time indicator needle to the position that you would like to split the media element.
  3. Select the Split button on the top-left of the Timeline or select the S key on your keyboard. Screenshot: A clip selected on the Timeline with the Split button highlighted. Use the ‘Split (S)’ button to divide into separate sections at the current playhead position.
  4. Your media will be divided into two parts.

💡Tip: The Split icon will be grayed out if the needle indicator is less than0.5 seconds from the beginning or end of the clip. Make sure to position the needle at least 0.5 seconds away from the edges to enable splitting.

How to remove media from the Timeline

Delete media from the Timeline by selecting the element block in the Timeline and selecting the Backspace/Delete key on your keyboard.

You can also delete media by right-clicking the element block and selecting Delete from the overflow menu.

How to delete gaps between media element blocks

If you have a space between media after rearranging or removing it, you can get rid of this space by selecting the Delete gap button when you hover over it.

Screenshot: In the video editor timeline, a gap is highlighted between two clips. Click the trash can icon labeled ‘Delete gap’ to remove the empty space and join the clips together.

This will delete the gap and place the clip directly next to the clip before the gap.

How to delete uploaded media

You can delete media you’ve uploaded to the video editor in the Uploads tab of the Media pane.

To delete uploaded media:

  1. Select Media from the left-side panel.
  2. Select Uploads.
  3. Hover over the thumbnail of your media to display the Expand button. Screenshot: Close-up of the ‘Expand’ button, indicated by two outward-facing arrows, on a video clip.
  4. Select the Expand button.
  5. Select the trash can icon in the lower right corner of the expanded menu.

How to fade the audio of the media in or out of scenes

You can adjust the fade-in and fade-out of your audio track, regardless of whether you’re using media from the Media Library or your own uploaded files. This can be adjusted in the inspector toolbar.

To adjust the audio fade in/fade out:

  1. Choose the media block containing the background audio you want to adjust.
  2. Select the Media Sound button in the Media Inspector toolbar to open the Media Sound menu.
  3. In the Media Sound menu, under the Fade In/Fade Out sections, drag the slider or enter the desired duration in seconds to set the fade-in and fade-out points for the audio.

Screenshot: The Media Sound menu for a selected video clip. Controls include volume, fade in, and fade out.

How to add autoplay and loop parameters to my video’s embed code

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can add autoplay and loop parameters to your video’s embed code. Your most recently uploaded Public videos (or recently set to Public) will autoplay first. This article explains how to add these parameters to your embed code.

  • How to add parameters to the embed code
  • How to add parameters for multiple videos
  • What happens if my video’s privacy is set to Unlisted?
  • Suggested next steps

How to add parameters to the embed code

To manually add parameters into your embed code to set your embedded videos to autoplay and/or loop:

  1. Find your existing Vimeo embed code
  2. Decide which parameters you need:
  • For looping:loop=1
  • For autoplay: autoplay=1
  1. Add your chosen parameter to the embed code.
  2. Replace the original embed code on your website with the new code containing the added parameters.

Example:

0autoplay=1&loop=1”1

How to add parameters for multiple videos

To add parameters to multiple videos:

  1. Find your existing Vimeo embed code.
  2. If you are embedding more than one video set to autoplay, you must include all three parameters:
  • For looping: loop=1
  • For autoplay: autoplay=1
  • For multiple videos on the same page: autopause=0
  1. Add all three parameters, separating them with an ampersand (&).
  2. Replace the original embed code on your website with the new code containing all necessary parameters.
  • Custom dimensions embed code:This creates a video player with a fixed, unchanging size (in pixels), regardless of the screen size. Example:

0

  • Responsive embed code:This creates a video player that automatically scales and adjusts its size to fit the user’s screen or device.

Example:

0player“>

What happens if my video’s privacy is set to Unlisted?

If your video’s privacy is set to Unlisted, the process for adding embed parameters changes slightly.

  • Privacy Hash: Your video’s URL will automatically include a special security code, known as the privacy hash, immediately following the video ID. This hash will be introduced by a question mark (?) and looks similar to this:?h=913062c8ff.
  • Syntax Change: Since the question mark (?) is already in use by the privacy hash, every playback parameter you wish to add (like autoplay=1 or loop=1) must be appended using the ampersand symbol (&) instead of a question mark.

Suggested next steps

  • For further details on potential restrictions that could hinder autoplay or loop functionality, refer toTroubleshooting: Autoplay restrictions.
  • Read moreabout player parameters.

How to add captions or subtitles to my video

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

This article discusses how to add captions or subtitles to your video using your own files as well as explain other features you can use.

  • How to add captions or subtitles with an existing file
  • Can I add captions or subtitles without a file?
  • Making the most out of captions and subtitles

How to add captions or subtitles with an existing file

Vimeo supportsSRTandWebVTT files for captions and subtitles. We recommend using WebVTT. To ensure special characters display correctly, caption files must be encoded in UTF-8 format.

To add captions or subtitles to your video:

  1. Navigate to your Library and open the desired video.
  2. Select the Languagesbutton in the toolbar to the left of the player.
  3. Select the +button at the top of the languages window.
  4. Upload your files from your computer.
  5. Use the dropdown menus next to the file name to select the Languageand Type (SubtitleorCaption).
  6. Select Upload.
  7. Once the file is uploaded, toggle it on to activate it.

Can I add captions or subtitles without a file?

If you don’t have captions or subtitles files for your video, you can purchase them through Rev, our trusted supplier. This option is also available in the Languages tab.

  • Rev (FAQs for captionsand subtitles)

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Support team. Include which type of caption or subtitle file you tried to upload, the link to the video you tried to upload the file to, and any further details that would help us troubleshoot.

Making the most out of captions and subtitles

  • Automatic subtitles: Creators on paid accountshave access to automated subtitle transcription. Read more at How to enable or disable default automated subtitles.
  • Translating videos with AI: Creators on paid Vimeo plans can use Vimeo AI to translate their video’s subtitles into other languages. Learn how at How to use Vimeo AI to translate my video’s subtitles.
  • Managing subtitles and captions: In addition to toggling your captions on and off, you can select the overflow menu next to each (represented by three vertical dots (⋮) to download, replace, delete, or edit your files from your video.

How to add cards to videos

This feature requires a Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

Cards are a customizable, notification-style layer that Vimeo members can set to appear during playback of their embedded or unlisted videos. You can make cards as simple as a headline or choose to flesh them out with a description, thumbnail, and link to any destination.

⚠️Note: Adding a card to your video disables the Like, Watch Later, and Share controls.

  • Setting up cards on your videos
  • Viewing cards
  • Engagement analytics for cards
  • Cards in showcases
  • Embed code for videos with cards
  • Best practices for sharing videos with cards on social platforms
  • Best practices for embedding videos with cards

Setting up cards on your videos

To add or edit cards for one of your videos, head to the Interactivetab on the left side. Select Add to […] to reveal the fields to fill out for your card.

At a minimum, you need to enter a title for your card and the timestamp for when you want it to first appear during your video. You also have the option to add a description, link, and thumbnail. As you’re editing your card, you’ll see the player preview update in real time. The shortest duration of time that cards can be added next to one another is six seconds.

Once you’re done editing your card, hit the Add button. You can add up to one card per second of your video. When you’re done editing all your embed settings, hit the Save button.

💡Tip:Custom thumbnail files cannot be larger than9600px wide or5400px tall. For best results, we recommend uploading an image with the same dimensions as your video (for example, uploading a 1920px x 1080px thumbnail file for a 1920 x 1080 video).

Viewing cards

The viewing experience for videos with cards will differ depending on the platform the video is shared on and the device being used to view it. ⚠️ Note:Cards will only display on players that are, at minimum, 600px wide on horizontal mode (standard players) and 225px wide on vertical mode (players where the height is greater than the width).

Cards stay in the top right corner of your video for the six seconds after they first appear, unless you’ve added another card to appear in that window. Videos with cards play in-line anywhere they’re embedded. They also appear on the video page on Vimeo if their privacy setting is “Private” or “Unlisted.”

Screenshot: cards.png

On sites like Wix, Squarespace, and WordPress, videos with cards play in-line on the mobile web. On Facebook and Twitter, mobile apps and mobile web will link to the vimeo.com video page.

Engagement analytics for cards

From the analytics panel on the video page, you can check the number of times all of its cards have been seen and clicked for the past 30 days. Read about analytics for video interaction tools at Video Settings analytics panel.

Cards in showcases

Cards, as well as any other video interaction tools that you previously added, will now be shown within your showcase. Once you’ve shared your showcase, your viewers will see your cards when viewing the showcase. Read more at Vimeo Showcases.

Embed code for videos with cards

The regular Vimeo embed code is a simple iframe. To support cards in all viewing environments, we add a javascript wrapper to the regular embed code. The new embed code is responsive, which allows the player to maintain its original aspect ratio whenever the browser window is resized. See the example embed code below, with the javascript wrapper in bold.

0

If you previously embedded a video that you’ve just added cards to, you’ll need to update the embed code on your site to include the javascript wrapper. You can access the new embed code after you’ve added cards to your video by clicking the gray Embed codebutton above the player preview in your embed settings.

Best practices for sharing videos with cards on social platforms

If you’re embedding a video with cards on social platforms like Twitter or LinkedIn, you can simply paste your Vimeo video page URL in your post instead of the Vimeo embed code.

If you’d like to share your video on Facebook or Twitter, but want your post to link back to your own site instead of the Vimeo video page, you’ll need to add some extra code to your website. Read how at ‘Optimize your website for posting to social media platforms’

Best practices for embedding videos with cards

If you’re embedding videos with cards through a website builder like Wix or Squarespace, you’ll want to make sure the javascript wrapper isn’t stripped out of the embed code. We also recommend avoiding using widgets to embed your videos.

If you’re embedding multiple videos with cards on one page, we recommend only adding the javascript tag ** to one of the videos on your page. All subsequent embeds should only include the new **** tag.

Including the javascript script tag multiple times may have an impact on your page’s performance.

To embed a video with cards using common website builders, please follow these steps:

  • Wix
  • Squarespace
  • WordPress
  • Tumblr

How to add credits to your video

This article will guide you through the process of adding credits to your video. You can credit yourself or anyone who follows your profile. You can also choose to list collaborators along with their professional contact information.

Account owners, admins, and contributors who have access to the video can add credits to a video.

  1. Select your video from the Library to open the video settings page.
  2. Scroll past the player to the Credits** section.**
  3. Select the plus sign icon +** to add a new credit.**
  4. SelectAdd credits to add a credit to your video.
  5. Search from your followers to select the Vimeo member you would like to credit. You also must be following the user who you would like to credit. Screenshot: add a credit.png

💡 Tip: If you would like to credit someone who does not have a Vimeo account, you may choose to use the Description or Tags fields instead. 6. You can choose to enter a role for the credit or leave the role field blank. 7. Select Save to save the credit. Your collaborator will now be listed on the video’s page on Vimeo.com. 8. You can remove a credit at any time by going back to the settings drawer and selecting the trash can icon when hovering over the credit’s name. These changes are also saved automatically.

⚠️Note: Adding credits is unavailable if your video is set to “Embed only” or “Unlisted.” The person who is credited will appear as a Collaborator on your profile page.

If you need further assistance adding credits to your video, pleasecontact Support.

How to add multiple audio tracks to my video

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

This article discusses how to add, edit, and manage multiple audio tracks on videos uploaded to Vimeo, including supported formats and plan limitations.

You can add additional audio tracks to videos you’ve uploaded to Vimeo. This is helpful for creators who want to add multiple language tracks to their videos.

If you want information on adding an audio track to a video in the video editor, visit ‘How do I add or upload an audio track to my video in the editor?’

  • How many additional language tracks can I add to my video?
  • Supported audio file formats for audio tracks
  • Add audio tracks to your video
  • How to edit or delete an audio track from your video

How many additional language tracks can I add to my video?

The number of additional language tracks that can be uploaded to your video depends on your Vimeo plan.

  • Free subscription: Up to 1 additional audio language track per uploaded video.
  • Starter: Up to 5 audio tracks per video
  • Standard:Up to10 audio tracksper video
  • Advanced: Up to15 audio tracksper video
  • Enterprise: Up to 50 audio tracks per uploaded video.

Supported audio file formats for audio tracks

Supported audio file formats for audio tracks include:

  • WAV
  • M4A
  • AAC
  • MP3

You can also upload video files such as MP4, but only the audio from the file will be uploaded.

Add audio tracks to your video

To add an audio track to your video:

  1. Select your video from your library to open the video settings page.
  2. Select Languages in the left-side toolbar.
  3. Select the ‘+’ plus sign in the top right corner of the Languageswindow.
  4. Choose Select Files or drag and drop your audio files to upload.
  5. Choose your file’sLanguageandType(Dubbed audio, Audio description, or Commentary) so viewers can distinguish each track.
  6. Select Upload.

Read about changing the audio track for a video in the player at ‘How to change the audio track of a Vimeo video’.

Download, replace, or delete an audio track from your video

To download, replace, or delete an audio track:

  1. Select your video from your library to open the video settings page.
  2. Select Languages in the left-side toolbar.
  3. Select the overflow menu represented by three vertical dots (⋮) to the right of the audio track.
  4. Choose whether to download, replace, or delete the track.

In addition, you can download language-specific versions of your video if it has multiple audio tracks in different languages. Learn how to do so at How to download language-specific versions of my videos

How to add registration to your video

To use marketing integrations with forms you need a Business, Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise membership. The in-product form is available for all paid plans.

With registration, you can capture a viewer’s email and other details. You can set up the form screen to appear before, during, or after your embedded videos, including videos in showcases. You can also enable registration for a showcase. You can then download your viewer information or sync it to your email service provider (e.g., MailChimp).

If you’re a Basic, Plus, Pro, Free, or Starter member, you’ll need to upgrade to Vimeo Business, Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise to unlock forms for the embedded player.

How to set up a registration form

Follow the steps below to configure registration on a video or showcase.

  1. First, select the video from yourlibrary, and then go to the Interactive tab on the left of the video settings page.
  • To turn on registration for a showcase, open your showcase from the showcase folder in your library.
  1. SelectRegistration, and then Turn on registration.
  2. From the Registration panel, select Customize.
  3. Here, you can configure which fields you would like to display on the registration form including name, email address, and custom text, dropdown, or checkbox fields.
  • You can add up to 20 custom fields each up to 240 characters in length, and your registrants can include answers up to 50 characters in length per text field.
  • For checkboxes,you can use the link button to add a URL to the field.
  1. Drag and drop the dot icon to the right of each field to re-arrange the order in which they appear.
  2. Select the options menu to the right to open the dropdown menu to find additional settings for each field. Here, you can make a field required or delete it from your form.
  3. Below the custom fields, you can provide a link to your organization’s privacy policy that will be accessible to viewers directly from the preview player, below the contact form.
  4. Select the Appearance tab on the right to change the layout, add your logo, or add background image or color.
  5. Use thePreview dropdown menu option to view your form, confirmation, and sign-on screen from your viewers’ perspective.
  6. Once you are happy with your form, select theback button in the top left corner to return to your event settings page. Your changes will be saved automatically.

How to add videos to a showcase

Once you have created a showcase you can start adding videos that you would like to display together. This article discusses how to add videos to your showcase.

  • What to know before adding videos to your showcase
  • How to add videos to a showcase
  • How to add videos to showcases in bulk from my Library
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before adding videos to your showcase

Before adding videos to your showcase, please take note of the following:

  • On team accounts, Contributors, Contributors+, Admins, and Owners can manage showcases.
  • If you add a nonpublic video to your showcase, that video’s visibility will depend on the privacy settings of your showcase. See Privacy of videos in showcases for more information.
  • While your videos can’t appear in more than one folder, you can add videos to more than one showcase.
  • While there is no limit to the number of videos one can add to a showcase, please note that at this point, it is not possible to custom-sort a showcase with more than 100 videos.
  • You cannot transfer videos from one showcase to another.
  • For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: Videos available for showcases are limited to those uploaded to the Workspace. Learn how to move videos between Workspaces at How to transfer videos between Workspaces.

How to add videos to a showcase

To add a video to a showcase, follow these steps:

From your showcase

  1. Open the showcase from your library.
  2. Select Add videos in the upper right corner.
  • You can search for videos within your Library as well as select each folder to find videos.
  1. Use the checkboxes within the modal window to choose which videos to add to your showcase.
  • If you’d like to add all videos within a folder to a showcase, select the checkbox under Location.
  1. Select Add to showcase to save your changes.

From Share modal

  1. Navigate to your video’s settings page
  • You can also select the Share button from your Library using the three dots (…).
  1. In the Share panel/modal, select Publish
  2. Choose Showcase and a pop-up will appear where you can choose which showcase you’d like to add your video to. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-10-09 at 1.21.55 PM.png

How to add videos to showcases in bulk from my Library

You can add videos individually or in bulk to a showcase. To do so:

  1. Navigate to your Library
  2. Select the videos in your Library using the checkboxes on the left side of the page.
  3. Select Add to showcase at the bottom of the page.
  4. Choose the specific showcase(s) you’d like to add those videos to.
  5. Select Confirm to save your changes.

Suggested next steps

  • After you’ve added videos to your showcase, you can arrange and customize them. Refer to How to arrange and remove videos within a showcase for more details.

How to apply content ratings to my videos

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can apply content ratings to individual videos or set a default rating for all your uploads, informing your audience about the video’s content. Learn about content ratings at ‘About Content Ratings’. This article explains how to apply a rating to a single video and how to set a default rating for future uploads.

  • What to know before you rate your videos
  • How to apply a content rating to a single video
  • How to set a default content rating for all uploads

What to know before you rate your videos

Before applying a rating to your videos, please be aware of the following:

  • Content ratings: We ask that you apply content ratings to your videos and live events, and disclose whether they contain an advertisement or AI-generated content. Learn about Content Ratings at About content ratings.
  • All Audiences v. Mature Audiences: If your video contains violence, profanity, nudity, or drug/alcohol use, your video should be rated for Mature Audiences.
  • Access in Certain Regions: If your video is unrated, viewers in some countries (such as those in the UK and EU) will be required to log intoa Vimeo account to watch, even if it is set to Public.
  • Finality: Once you select a rating for a video, you cannot change it back to “Not yet rated.”

How to apply a content rating to a single video

You can set a content rating for any individual video from its settings page.

  1. Navigate to your Library.
  2. Select the video you want to rate to open the video settings page.
  3. Scroll down to the Content section.
  4. Select the dropdown menu and choose All audiences or Mature.
  5. If you select Mature, checkboxes for specific warnings will appear; check all that apply to your video.
  6. If your video includes AI-generated content that appears real, select the box to disclose. Learn about disclosing AI-generated content in your videos at How to label my videos to indicate they contain AI-generated content.
  7. If your video contains an advertisement, select the box next to Contains advertisement.
  8. Your settings will save automatically.

How to set a default content rating for all uploads

You can set a default rating that will be applied to all videos you upload.

  1. Navigate to your accountSettings.
  2. Select the Videos tab, then choose the Upload defaults sub-tab.
  3. Under the Content rating heading, select the appropriate rating from the dropdown menu.
  4. If you select Mature, check the boxes for all applicable reasons.
  5. To apply this rating to all of your existing unrated videos, select the box next to Also apply to all existing unrated videos.
  6. Select Save.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:This feature can be managed by a Workspace Admin for all videos uploaded to the Workspace. For additional information, visit ’How to edit my Workspace’s settings’.

How to build and manage my custom vocabulary list

This feature requires a paid plan.

The custom vocabulary list helps improve the accuracy of transcription and translations when using Vimeo AI. This list helps the AI more accurately recognize words specific to your team or company when transcribing the video’s original language.

This article discusses how to add, manage, and replace words in your custom vocabulary list.

  • What to know before building the custom vocabulary list
  • How to build my custom vocabulary list
  • How to add and manage custom vocab from my video’s transcript

What to know before building the custom vocabulary list

Before building your custom vocabulary list, take note of the following:

  • This is not a translation dictionary. It only improves transcription accuracy for the video’s original language.
  • Account Owners and Admins can create and manage custom vocabulary lists.
  • For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Workspace admins can create and manage custom vocabulary lists for the Workspace.
  • Your custom vocabulary list can contain up to 50 keywords/phrases.
  • Vimeo Enterprise users can add up to 1000 keywords/phrases.
  • Keywords are limited to 34 characters.
  • Phrases are limited to 12 words.
  • Words and phrases are limited to letters in the English alphabet (a-z, A-Z). Special characters, numbers, and letters from other alphabets are currently not supported.
  • If your video has subtitles in multiple languages, replacing words or phrases in one file will not automatically replace them in the other language files. Each file must be updated individually for each language.

How to build my custom vocabulary list

You can manage your custom vocabulary list from two places: the AI Settings page for your team or the Languages menu on an individual video’s settings page.

Add or manage keywords from AI Settings

You can add, remove, or upload keywords from your team’s AI Settings page.

  1. Navigate to your team’s AI Settings page.
  2. Locate Custom Vocabulary under the General header and select Manage.
  3. In the pop-up window, add words or phrases that are unique to your company.
  • You can type a single word or phrase and press Enter, input a list of words separated by commas, or upload a CSV file.
  1. Select Save to save your custom list.

You can manage the keywords in the same menu.

  • Removing keywords: To remove a word or phrase from your list, select the X next to it on the vocab list.
  • Downloading keywords: To download your vocab list as a CSV file, select the download icon.
  • Delete the entire list: You can delete your entire vocab list by selecting the trash icon.

How to add and manage custom vocab from my video’s transcript

If a video already has a transcript, you can add words directly to your custom vocab list from the Languages menu on the video’s settings page. To do so:

  1. Select a video from your library to go to its settings page.
  2. Select Languages.
  3. Select the pencil icon next to the transcript.
  4. In the transcript, find and highlight the word or phrase you want to add to your custom vocab list.
  5. Select Add to Custom Vocabulary from the menu that appears.

How to bulk upload my videos on the Vimeo mobile app

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can upload and manage multiple videos simultaneously using the Vimeo Androidor iOS app on your mobile device. This article explains how to upload videos in bulk and perform bulk actions such as moving, deleting, renaming, and adjusting privacy settings.

  • What to know before bulk uploading
  • How to bulk upload videos
  • How to bulk manage videos

What to know before bulk uploading

Before you start, note the following:

  • Impact on Storage Capacity:Uploaded videos count towards your account’s storage capacity. Your storage capacity is dependent on the available space in your account. Read more at How much video content can I store on my Vimeo account?

How to bulk upload videos

You can upload multiple videos to a new or existing folder. To do so:

  1. From the home screen of the mobile app, tap the Upload icon.
  2. If you haven’t already allowed the Vimeo app access to files on your device, you’ll need to grant permission. For more details, see Google Support and Apple Support.
  • Android: Change app permissions on your Android phone
  • iOS: Control access to information in apps on iPhone’/‘Control access to information in apps on iPad’.
  1. Select all the videos you want to upload in the batch from your device.
  2. Select Next.
  3. On the next screen, confirm the videos you want to upload in the batch. You can also rename all videos in the batch, choose the folder on your Vimeo account for uploading, and set the privacy options.
  4. Use the dropdown menus to change the destination folder and privacy settings for the uploads.
  5. Select the pencil icon to edit the video’s name, if necessary.
  6. Your videos will begin uploading to the selected folder.
  7. Tap Save (Android) or Done(iOS) to finalize the process. Your videos will now be available in the designated folder.

How to bulk manage videos

You can perform a single action on multiple videos at once directly from your library. This includes renaming, deleting, or moving your videos to another folder, and more. To do so:

  1. Navigate to your Library and press and hold one of the videos you’d like to select. This will activate the bulk-management tool.
  2. Tap the bubble to the left of each video to choose all the videos you want to manage. You can also choose to Select Allor Deselect All.
  3. From the menu bar at the bottom of the screen that appears after selecting a video, choose one of these actions:
  • Move to: Select this to move the selected videos to a different folder.
  • Privacy: Select this to apply a new privacy setting to all selected videos.
  • Delete: Select this to delete the videos from your account permanently. You will be asked to confirm before the videos are deleted.
  1. Tap the ellipses … (more) icon at the bottom of the screen to open the action menu for additional management tools:
  • Add to showcase: Bulk add your videos to one of your showcases.
  • Rename: Select this to apply a new name to all selected videos. Videos will be renamed with the new name and a number to differentiate them, as shown below.
  • Save videos: Download your videos in bulk to your mobile device or save them for offline viewing within the app when you’re not connected to the internet.

How to change downloading permissions on my videos

This feature requires a paid plan.

Adjustable download permissions provide greater control over your Vimeo videos. This article outlines how to modify download settings for individual videos or apply changes to all current and future uploads.

  • What to know about downloading permissions
  • How to change downloading permissions for an individual video
  • How to change downloading permissions for future uploads
  • Suggested next steps

What to know about downloading permissions

Before you change download settings, take note of the following:

  • Viewers can only download your video from the video’s page on vimeo.com. It is not currently possible for viewers to download your video from the embedded player.
  • As the video owner, you will always see the download button on your video page, regardless of your download settings.
  • For Enterprise accounts withWorkspaces: This feature can be managed by a Workspace Admin for videos uploaded to the Workspace. Read more at ’How to edit my Workspace’s settings’.

How to change download settings for an individual video

You can allow or disallow downloads for a particular video. To do so:

  1. Navigate to your Library.
  2. Select the video you want to change to open its settings page.
  3. Select Share in the top-right corner. Screenshot: The ‘Share’ button, highlighted in the toolbar. The icon, currently a padlock, changes to reflect the video’s privacy status.
  4. In the Viewer permissions section, toggle the Downloads switch on or off.

How to change downloading permissions for future uploads

You can remove the ability to download for all your existing videos and/or future uploads. To do so:

  1. Visit the Upload Defaults page in yourAccount Settings.
  2. Under “What can people do with your videos?“, check or uncheck the box to the left of Download them.

Screenshot: Video privacy settings, with the ‘Download them’ checkbox highlighted. Other options include ‘Add them to collections’, a ‘Save’ button, and ‘Also apply to all existing videos.’

  1. When you check or uncheck the box, the menu will expand, allowing you to apply this setting to all your existing videos. Check or uncheck the box next to “Also apply to existing videos” to do so.
  2. Select Save.

Suggested next steps

  • Read aboutvideo privacy settings.
  • Learn how to share a video.

How to change my video’s end screen

This feature requires a Plus, Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced or Enterprise plan.

You can add end screens to your embedded videos in order to customize what plays after your videos end. This article discusses how to add and remove an end screen. Read more at About end screens.

  • How to add an end screen to my video
  • How to add an end screen for my embed preset
  • How do I delete an end screen?

How to add an end screen to my video

  1. To access end screens, select your video from the Library.
  2. Select the Interactivity tab on the panel to the left, and thenEnd Screen.
  3. Select the dropdown under theEnd screen menu.
  4. Choose which end screen option you would like to apply to your video and configure it as prompted.
  5. Select Save to finalize your changes.

How to add an end screen for my embed preset

  1. Go to Settings> Videos > Embed presets.
  2. Select an existing preset or create a new one by selecting theplus sign icon. On the selected embed preset page, scroll down to theAfter video section. Screenshot: End screen section in the embed preset settings page
  3. Choose from the options in the dropdown menu to configure your end screen.
  4. If you would like the end screen to be applied to all existing videos, select the corresponding checkbox at the bottom of the page.
  5. Select Save once you are satisfied with your end screen settings.

How do I delete an end screen?

To delete an end screen from one of your videos, change the end screen to Empty.

If you want to remove end screens from all your videos, you can apply a preset to all existing videos with Emptyselected from theAfter video dropdown.

How to change my video’s privacy settings

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

We offer a variety of ways to control who can access your videos and how they can do so. This article explains how to change a video’s privacy settings for individual videos as well as in bulk. To read more, visit Overview of video privacy settings.

  • How to change my video’s privacy
  • How to edit privacy settings in bulk
  • Can I manage the privacy settings for my embedded video?

How to change my video’s privacy

You can edit the privacy settings for each video by following the steps below.

  1. Log in to Vimeo and navigate to your Library.
  2. Select your video to open the video settings page.
  3. On the upper right-hand of the page, select the Sharebutton. Screenshot: Share button at the top of the video settings page
  4. A new modal will open on the right side. Select the drop-down arrow next to the current privacy setting under Privacy. Screenshot: Share modal with drop-down menu of privacy settings
  5. Select the desired privacy setting. The selection will save automatically.
  6. You can also change your privacy settings from the Video library by clicking on the (…) dots from your selected video and then choosing Share. This will also open up the modal to change your privacy settings. Screenshot: Team library view with dots overflow menu opened and Share option selected

💡Tip:You can also set your video’s viewing privacy before uploading.

How to edit privacy settings in bulk

You can follow these steps to edit the privacy settings of multiple videos at a time.

  1. Go to your Library to find the video(s) you would like to edit. Note that you cannot change privacy settings for VODs or Vimeo Stock.
  2. To select a video,check the box on the left side of its thumbnail/row (depending on whether you are in grid-view or list-view).
  3. Then, selectPrivacy. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-02-10 at 12.12.33 PM.png
  4. Choose your desired privacy settings and then Save.

Can I manage the privacy settings for my embedded video?

You can manage the privacy settings for an embedded video by setting where your video can be embedded. For more details, refer to How to embed my video.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Privacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings or How to edit my Workspace’s settings.

How to change the thumbnail image for my video

This article discusses how to change the thumbnail image for your video. When you create or upload a video, a frame from your video is automatically selected to serve as the thumbnail image.

After the video has been uploaded and optimized, you can manually change the thumbnail on the video settings page.

To add or edit the thumbnail image for your live event, refer to How to add a thumbnail for a live event.

  • Video overview
  • How to add a new thumbnail to my video
  • How to select a thumbnail
  • How to download or delete a thumbnail from my video
  • Uploading recommendations for custom thumbnails

Video overview

Watch the video below to learn how to select and change the thumbnail image for your videos.

How to add a new thumbnail to my video

  1. Navigate to the Library and select the video you want to change the thumbnail for.
  2. Scroll under the video player to the Thumbnailsection.
  3. Here, you can select a pre-selected thumbnail, upload a custom thumbnail, or select a thumbnail from the video.
  4. To choose a thumbnail from the video, start by playing it in the video player. Once you find a frame you wish to use as your thumbnail, click the Select this framebutton located in the top-left corner of the video player.
  5. Once you upload or choose a frame, select the newly created thumbnail from the thumbnails list to designate it as your video’s new thumbnail image. The chosen frame will shift to the top of the list, signaling that it is now the new thumbnail.

How to select a thumbnail

After adding or uploading a thumbnail for your video, you can choose the thumbnail you want to use from the list of available options.

Screenshot: Thumbnail section with one thumbnail selected

The thumbnail you select will move to the front of the list, outlined by a thin line, indicating that it is the current thumbnail for the video.

How to download or delete a thumbnail from my video

After adding a thumbnail, you can download or delete it from the video settings page. You may also download the default thumbnail.

  1. Scroll down to the Thumbnail section on the video settings page.
  2. Hover over a thumbnail image and select the options menu (…) in the upper left-hand corner.
  3. Select DownloadorDelete.The first thumbnail cannot be deleted.

Uploading recommendations for custom thumbnails

If you are adding a custom thumbnail for your video, please follow these recommendations:

  • Supported file types include: JPG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF,andPNG.
  • While GIF files are supported, animated GIF files are not currently supported.
  • Custom thumbnails uploaded undergo slight compression. For the best results, we recommend uploading an image with the exact dimensions of your video.
  • Example: If your video’s dimensions are 1280x720, we recommend uploading an image that is 1280px x 720px.
  • At a minimum, 80% of the image must have an alpha (transparency) level above 250. Google does not permit transparent thumbnails for video indexing. For further details, refer to Google Support at URL Inspection Tool: Video Indexing.

How to change the title of my video

This article discusses how to update the name of your video on Vimeo from a desktop device. The title of your video can be edited from the video’s settings page.

To change the title of your video:

  1. From the Library, select the video you would like to rename.
  2. Type your new title in the text box under the Titleheader. The Title header is under the video player.

Screenshot: The highlighted ‘Title’ input field, which reads “My Video” and shows a character count of 8/128. 3. After typing in the new title for the video, title, select Enter on your keyboard or click somewhere else on the page. 4. The changes will automatically be saved, and the title of your video will be updated.

To learn how to change the title of your video on a mobile device, visit How to rename my video in the Vimeo mobile apps.

How to connect your account to Mailchimp

This feature requires a Business, Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

You can connect your Vimeo account to Mailchimp, which is one of our supported email service providers. You’ll need a Vimeo paid plan to sync your registration forms with Mailchimp, and a Vimeo Enterprise plan to track viewer data within Mailchimp.

This article discusses the process of connecting a Vimeo account to Mailchimp. To do so:

  1. Hover over your Vimeo profile picture in the upper right corner of the website, and select Settingsin the dropdown menu.
  2. On the left-hand side of the page, select the Marketing tab.
  3. Scroll down toMailchimp and select the blue Connect button next to its name:
  4. You will be prompted to accept the following terms:
  • I will only use collected email addresses for marketing purposes.
  • I will not share these email addresses with others.
  • I will comply with CAN-SPAM, CASL, and any other applicable laws.
  • I will provide an unsubscribe mechanism and comply promptly with opt-out requests.
  1. After accepting the terms, you’ll see a pop-up window where you canlog in to Mailchimp.
  2. Once you’ve successfully logged in, select the list where you want the information captured by Vimeo to be sent, and then select the Sync button.
  3. Mailchimp is now connected, and the Marketing tab of your Account Settings should display the name of the list synced with Vimeo. ⚠️Note: The limit of Mailchimp lists that will appear in our integration is capped at 1,000. If a particular Mailchimp list of yours isn’t showing up in our integration, you will need to remove the lists you previously created in Mailchimp.

Now that you’ve connected your account to Mailchimp, you can enable registration forms on any of your embedded videos and automatically sync your viewers’ submissions to one or more of your mailing lists.

How to connect your Vimeo Account to HubSpot

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

You can connect your Vimeo account to HubSpot, one of our supported email service providers.

Connect to HubSpot CRM to add registration forms to videos/live events and sync list data. Connect to HubSpot Media Bridge to have access to your Vimeo video library in HubSpot and embed in emails, landing pages, and get analytics.

This article discusses how to connect your Vimeo account to HubSpot.

To connect to HubSpot:

  1. Hover over your Vimeo profile picture in the upper right corner of the website, and select Settings in the dropdown menu.
  2. On the left-hand side of the page, click on the Marketing tab.
  3. Scroll down to HubSpot and click the blue Connect button next to its name:
  4. You will be prompted to accept the following terms:
  • I will only use collected email addresses for marketing purposes.
  • I will not share these email addresses with others.
  • I will comply with CAN-SPAM, CASL, and any other applicable laws.
  • I will provide an unsubscribe mechanism and comply promptly with opt-out requests.
  1. After accepting the terms, you’ll see a pop-up window where you can log in to HubSpot.
  2. Once you’ve successfully logged in, select the list where you want the information captured by Vimeo to be sent, and then click the Sync button.
  3. HubSpot is now connected, and the Marketing tab of your Account Settings should display the name of the list synced with Vimeo. ⚠️Note: The maximum number of HubSpot lists shown in our integration is 250. If you have over 250 lists, they will be retrieved in a loop.

Now that you’ve connected your account to HubSpot, you can enable registration forms on any of your embedded videos and automatically sync your viewers’ submissions to one or more of your mailing lists.

How to create a custom URL for my video

This feature requires a paid Vimeo membership.

Using custom URLs can help brand and organize your content. This article discusses how to create a custom URL to share with your viewers.

  • How to create a custom URL
  • Which privacy settings are available for custom URLs?
  • Does the Vimeo app support custom URLs?

How to create a custom URL

You can create a custom URL from your video settings page. To do so:

  1. Navigate to the video settings page from your Library by clicking on the desired video.
  2. Select theShare button in the upper right of the video settings page. This will open the Share panel on the right-side of the screen.
  3. Select on the Edit option under the Link section. Screenshot: Share side panel with Link section highlighted
  4. In the field labeled Edit, enter the desired custom URL for your video, consisting of only letters or numbers. You will need to add the custom portion after your username.

⚠️Note:Custom video URLs cannot be embedded. 5. Select the Copy link button to copy the custom link to your clipboard.

💡Tip: The format of custom video URLs is vimeo.com/username/thecustompart. For example, a video on our staff account about the Vimeo player has the custom URL: vimeo.com/staff/player.

Which privacy settings are available for custom URLs?

Custom URLs work for all privacy settings. Keep in mind that depending on the privacy you choose, the link may not be sharable to others. For example, setting a video to Private still allows you to set up a custom URL but the link wouldn’t be sharable.

Does the Vimeo app support custom URLs?

On mobile devices, shared custom URLs will have to be opened in a mobile web browser rather than the Vimeo app.

⚠️Note: If you are a Basic or Free user, you do not have access to create new custom URLs or to edit previously existing ones. Instead, you will be prompted to upgrade your account to access this feature.

How to create a quiz results panel

This article discusses how to create quiz and poll results panels in interactive videos.

Once you’ve created all your questions and assigned values to each of the correct answers, you can then surface a results panel to show the viewer their quiz score within your interactive video.

  • How to create a quiz results panel
  • How to create an answer-level poll results panel

How to create a quiz results panel

To create a results panel at the end of your video, you’ll need to create a time-triggered overlay.

  1. In the interactive Editor, scrub near the end of your video.
  2. Create a Time Trigger and select the action Open overlay, then click Create overlay.
  3. In the overlay editor, design your results panel any way you want.
  4. To add the quiz results to the overlay, select Resultsfrom the left-hand menu.
  5. A dynamic text box will appear in your overlay. With the results box selected, you can change the font, color, and position as you see fit.
  6. Use the Results for?dropdown in the right-hand menu and then select Overall quiz results.
  7. In the Question result dropdown, choose one of the following results options to display in this box:
  • Total score
  • Total correct score
  • Total correct answers
  • Score as % of maximum
  • All questions answered
  • All questions answered correctly
  • Time to answer quiz
  • Demo results Screenshot: overall_quiz_results.png

If you want to display multiple results metrics within your overlay, you will need to add multiple Results elements by clicking the Resultsoption on the left-hand menu.

All questions answered before the results panel appears in your video will be included in the results overlay.

You can also use this to create progress overlays, showing viewers their progress as they advance through the video.

How to create an answer-level poll results panel

If you want to display results for a particular answer, i.e., “what percentage of viewers chose ‘red’ as their favorite color”, you can add answer-level results for your poll:

  1. SelectQuestion poll results in theResults for?dropdown menu.
  2. Select theanswer you would like to display results for on your panel.
  3. Next, choose from the options under Question result:
  • Total answered
  • % answered
  • Answered / participants Screenshot: question_result_options.png

⚠️Note:Your poll data can take up to 30 minutes to update.

How to create a showcase

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

With a showcase, you can organize videos together to share publicly or privately. A showcase is a great way to distribute a collection of videos to any audience. This article discusses how to create a new showcase.

  • How to create a showcase
  • Are showcases supported on the Vimeo mobile app?

How to create a showcase

Follow these steps to create a new showcase:

  1. Open your library and go to Showcases in the left-hand panel.
  • You can also select the +Create button at the top right-side of the page, then choose Showcase.
  1. Select New showcase in the upper-right corner of the page.
  2. A new page will open where you can input the showcase’s title and description, set its privacy level, and add videos as well as customize its appearance.
  3. To start setting up your showcase, see How to add videos to a showcase and How to customize your showcase.

Are showcases supported on the Vimeo mobile app?

You can view and share showcases from the Vimeo app for Android and iOS. Within the mobile app, select the Library tab at the bottom of the screen and then select Showcases.

How to create a video on Vimeo with the video editor

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

You can create new videos using Vimeo’s browser-based video editor using videos, photos, stock media, graphics, music, and more. This article explains how to start a new video project in the web-based video editor.

  • What to know before creating a video
  • How to create a new video using the video editor
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before creating a video

Before you begin, take note of the following:

  • Videos created with Vimeo cannot exceed 120 minutes in length if using the in-browser video editor.
  • Videos created with the Vimeo Android app or the Vimeo iOS app cannot exceed 10 minutes.
  • If you are a member of multiple teams or Workspaces, ensure that you are logged into the correct team or Workspace for which you have creator permissions.
  • Creating a video in the video editor may or may not count against your account’s video storage.
  • Visit What types of video content count towards my video storage allowance? for more information.

How to create a new video using the video editor

You can start a new video project from your Vimeo homepage. To do so:

  1. From the Vimeo homepage, start a new project in one of two ways:
  • Select + Createin the top navigation bar, then select Video projectfrom the dropdown menu.
  • Select Create new or from template from the quick start menu.

This will open a new project in the web-based video editor. From here, you can choose to build your video from scratch with media and design elements, or select a template. When saving a video, it will save to your Library.

Suggested next steps

  • Read more about the video editor
  • Learn how to use a templateto create a new video.
