How to create and add videos to folders

This article explains how to create a new folder in your Library and begin adding videos to it. To learn about customizing and organizing your folders, visit ‘Organize videos into folders’.

⚠️Note: For Workspace members, folders and their contents (videos) are exclusive to their respective Workspace.

  • How to create a folder
  • How to add videos to a folder
  • How to move videos into a folder
  • How to change the destination of a video before uploading

How to create a folder

To create a folder, follow these steps:

  1. Select theNew Folderbutton at the top right of your Team library. Alternatively, select the plus sign (+) icon next to Team Library.

  2. In the window that opens, add a name to your folder and invite any team members with whom you’d like to collaborate. You can also enable Slack integration from this page.

  3. Click Create. The folder will appear in your left navigation.

  4. When you create a new folder you will see the option toInvite people and Upload.

⚠️Note: Enterprise teams can also add folders and subfolders from their Video Library page.

How to add videos to a folder

After you create a folder, you can add videos to it by clicking Upload or Add videos or by dragging and dropping videos directly into it. You can add multiple videos to a folder at once by clicking their checkboxes and then dragging and dropping them to the desired folder.

To upload a video directly into a folder, open the folder in your library, then drag the video file from your File Explorer or Finder window into the browser window with that folder open. Alternatively, open the folder, then click New video > Upload to open your File Explorer or Finder window. Select the video file to start the upload.

You can also create a new video directly from the folder to save it to that folder. Read how at How to make a new video on the Vimeo website.

⚠️Note: It’s not possible to put one video into multiple folders.

How to move videos into a folder

To move a video from one folder to another, open the first folder, select the video you want to move, and drag and drop it into the other folder in the left panel. Moving a video will not impact the video’s share link or embed code.

To moveone or more videos at a time, you can perform bulk actions on a subset of videos in the Library or from search results within the Library.

  1. To select a video,check the box on the left side of its thumbnail/row (depending on if you are in grid-view or list-view).
  2. Then, selectMove. Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-12-05 at 1.12.25 PM.png
  3. Choose the folder destination for your videos and select Move. Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-12-05 at 1.15.03 PM.png

How to change the destination of a video before uploading

On the upload page, you can select the folder to which you want to upload a video. Select the dropdown menu to search the folders in your Team Library.

⚠️Note:It is not possible to change the default upload location for all of your videos.

How to create and apply appearance presets for videos

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

To apply the same custom embed or viewing page settings to multiple videos, you can create a preset under the Videos tab in your Account settings or the video settings page. Video page presets customize the appearance and behavior of the video player and some page elements on Vimeo’s video page while embed presets customize the Vimeo player where your videos are embedded.

This article discusses how to create, apply, and edit video page and embed presets on Vimeo.

  • What to know before creating an appearance preset
  • How to create an appearance preset from my account settings
  • How to apply and create an appearance preset on my video settings page
  • What customization options are available for appearance presets?
  • How to edit an appearance preset
  • Customization options for Organizations and Workspaces

What to know before creating an appearance preset

Before you create a page or embed preset, take note of the following:

  • To include an end screen in your embed preset, you must add it within your account settings first. If you try to add it after applying the preset to a video, the preset will be removed from that video.
  • End screens cannot be added to video page presets.
  • End screens can only be added to embed presets from the account settings page.
  • If you are a Viewer or Contributor team member, you will not be able to access the existing presets located in the account owner’s settings. Due to this, only the account owner or admin can apply an end screen to an embed preset.

How to create an appearance preset from my account settings

You can create an appearance preset from your account settings by following the steps below:

  1. Select your profile icon, then go toSettings and find the Videos section on the left
  2. Under videos, select Page presets or Embed presets
  3. Select + Add new preset
  4. Name your preset and apply your desired settings for the video page, including the End screen
  5. Select theSave button at the bottom of the page. You will have the option to apply your new preset to all your videos by checking the box next to Also apply to all existing videos.

How to apply and create an appearance preset on my video settings page

You can apply your new preset to an individual video by following these steps:

  1. Select your desired video from your library
  2. Select the Appearance button on the right panel
  3. Choose either the Embed or Video page tab Screenshot: Appearance panel in the video settings page
  4. Select the desired preset from the dropdown under Embed presetor Video page preset
  5. Hit theSave button
  6. To create a preset based on the settings you chose on this page, select +Save new preset. You will be able to name it and it will be saved to access from your account settings.
  7. To delete a preset from this page, select the Manage Presets button under the dropdown to open the embed or video page preset page within account settings. Select the ‘X’ icon next to the title of the preset.

What customization options are available for appearance presets?

For a comprehensive breakdown of settings, refer to Video appearance customization Comparison. The customization options available for appearance presets are:

  • Branding & Custom logo
  • Engagement
  • Details
  • Play button location and controls

How to edit an appearance preset

If you need to edit an existing preset, select the title from Page presets or Embed presets and then Save at the bottom of the page after making any changes.

If you want to delete a preset, click the ‘X’ icon next to the desired preset.

Screenshot: Embed presets page in account settings with ‘X’ icon highlighted

Customization options for Organizations and Workspaces

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Presets can be set and managed at both the Workspace level and the Organization level. Note that settings at the Organization level take precedence over those set at the Workspace level. To read more, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings or How to edit my Workspace’s settings.

How to create and customize my Portfolios

This feature requires a Vimeo Standard or higher or a Vimeo Pro or higher membership.

Portfolios are customizable websites that allow you to showcase your videos to viewers. You can create as many portfolios as you like, and customize them to your specific tastes without any Vimeo branding.

⚠️Note: Only team account OwnersandAdmins can add or remove videos in portfolios. Other team members on your Vimeo account will not be able to do so.

Read about the privacy of videos in portfolios at: ‘Privacy of videos in collections and review pages’

  • Create a portfolio
  • Customize portfolio settings
  • Add videos to your portfolio
  • Remove videos from your portfolio
  • Customize video arrangement
  • Customize a portfolio domain

Create a portfolio

To create a portfolio, follow these steps:

  1. Hover over your profile image in the top navigation bar and select Watch.
  2. Select Collections.
  3. Click Create a new portfolio.
  4. Add a title and description.
  5. If you’d like to make your portfolio private, check the box next to Password protect this portfolio.
  6. Click on the + at the top right corner of a video thumbnail to add that video to your Portfolio. After you click the + sign, it will change to a - sign to let you know the video has been selected.
  7. Click Create This Portfolio.

Customize portfolio settings

To customize a portfolio’s settings after you create it, follow these steps:

  1. Go to your Collections.
  2. Click the gear icon in the upper right corner of your portfolio thumbnail image. This will take you to your portfolio’s Settings page.
  3. Navigate to the Appearance tab. Here, you can do the following:
  • Choose from our available default Themes to give it a unique look and feel.
  • Control which details will be displayed along with your videos.
  • Customize the color scheme.
  • Upload abackground image and header logo.
  • Change any CSS on your portfolio pages.

Add videos to your portfolio

To add videos to a portfolio, follow these steps:

⚠️Note: Only owners and admins can add or remove a video from a portfolio.

  1. Go to your video page
  2. Select Publish in the top right corner
  3. Click on Add to Portfolio. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-02-07 at 12.20.19 PM.png

💡Tip: Learn about adding videos to showcase.

Remove videos from your portfolio

Account Owners, Contributors, and Admins can remove a video from portfolios by clicking the red X on the thumbnail of the video. A video can always be added back to the portfolio if you change your mind.

Note: If a previously removed video is added back to a portfolio, it will return to its original spot in the portfolio. For example, if your portfolio is sorted by Most Recent, the video’s placement will be based on the time it was originally added, not the time you re-added it.

Customize video arrangement

To customize the way the videos in your portfolio are arranged, follow these steps:

  1. Click on the Always arrange by dropdown menu.
  2. Select Manually.
  3. Drag and drop your videos into the order you want.
  4. Save your changes.

Customize a portfolio domain

As a Vimeo Pro member or higher, you are more than welcome to use a custom domain for your Portfolios. You can use a domain that you already own (http://my-rad-site.com), set up a subdomain on your existing website (http://portfolio.my-rad-site.com), or purchase a new domain to use (http://my-new-site.com).

  1. Set up your domain – Purchase a domain from a registrar such as DreamHost.com, name.com, or 1and1.com. Alternately, you can set up a subdomain on your existing site. (Contact your registrar or hosting service for instructions.)
  2. Update your CNAME Record or A Record – If you want your Portfolio to live on a subdomain (http://portfolio.my-rad-site.com), you will need to follow your registrar’s instructions for updating your CNAME Record so that it points to vimeopro.com. If you want your Portfolio to live on your main domain (http://my-rad-site.com), follow your domain registrar’s instructions to set the domain’s A-Record to 184.73.186.224. Note: It may take up to 72 hours for these changes to take effect.
  3. Update your Portfolio Settings – In your Portfolio Settings, enter your domain or subdomain under the “Portfolio URL” section, in the “Custom” field, then save your changes.
  • Note: Currently, when you set up your own custom domain on a portfolio page, the connection will be HTTP. Installing SSL for custom domains is something for which we do not currently have the infrastructure to support. For now, we can only support an HTTPS connection for Showcases, and over our own domains (e.g vimeoand vimeopro). Any portfolio page can be shared over HTTPS via the Vimeo URL provided.
  1. Test your new Portfolio domain – Open a new browser window and navigate to the domain or subdomain you just set up. You should now see your Portfolio! If you don’t see it, and it has been more than 72 hours since you updated your CNAME or A-Record, contact your domain registrar for further assistance.

How to create quiz question and answers using interactive hotspots

This feature discussed below requires an Enterprise plan.

Vimeo Interactive Quiz feature lets you assign values of correct or incorrect to a question from a hotspot or overlay element and manage a set of questions and answers that viewers interact with. You can provide feedback about the results at the end of your video. This feature allows you to create True/False, Multiple choice, and this-or-that scenarios.

Getting started

You will need:

  • An existing video or a newly uploaded video ready to be made interactive.
  • A list of questions and answers you wish to quiz your viewers on.

Follow these steps to create questions and answers using interactive hotspots:

  1. Find the point in your video where you want to add a hotspot.
  2. Create your hotspot as normal, picking or creating a design and define where it should be.
  3. Now decide on the action your hotspot will perform and the options include:
  • Open an overlaythat tells the player if they got the question correct or incorrect.
  • Jump to a time in the video where they see the result of their answer play.
  • Fire a custom payloadthat triggers an action on the webpage or records the response to tell the player.
  1. Below your hotspot action setting, you will find a toggle to make the hotspot an answer to the quiz question. Toggle it on.
  2. Now to link hotspot to an answer, click it to open the Question managermodal window. In the Question manager, you can create, edit, or delete questions to link back to your hotspot. This will inform the data you pull from the quiz metrics.
  3. Once you have your questions in the manager, choose the drop-down to select your question to the answer you are creating. After linking your question to the hotspot, you can fill in details for the answer, the score, and if the answer is correct.
  4. Once you have filled in all the details, click the Add button to save the data to the hotspot.
  5. Repeat these steps for other hotspots connected to the same question. Be sure to mark at least one as the correct answer to properly track quiz performance.

💡Tip: There is a wide range of quiz hotspot images in the template picker to help you get started.

How to create your own interactive overlay template

We have many interactive overlay templates to choose from. You can customize and edit an existing template to fit your needs or you can also start from scratch and design a custom overlay with the overlay editor.

If you create an overlay that you want to reuse later, you can save it as a template.

To create an interactive overlay template:

  1. After building your overlay, select the dropdown arrow next to Save Overlay.
  2. Select Save as template. Screenshot: overlay_save_as_template.png
  3. Name your template and save it.
  4. You can find your custom templates by opening the Templates menu, at the top of the list. Your custom template is only accessible to you and your team members.

What is the difference between “Save overlay” and “Save as template”

If you select Save overlay, that will only save that specific overlay for the hotspot or time trigger you are creating.

If you want to use a similarly designed overlay for future hotspots or time triggers, select Save as template to access and reuse your current design in the template menu.

How to customize caption appearance while viewing a video

If you have captions or subtitles enabled as a viewer, you can access the Customize menu within CC settings to edit font size, font color, font edge styling, background color, and background opacity. Follow these steps to learn how:

  1. Select the [CC] button below the player and then selectCustomize.
  2. The Font, Background, and Window menus each contain customizable settings. Make sure you have captions/subtitles turned on to see the changes as you make them.
  3. To revert the subtitles or captions to the classic presentation, select Reset all.

⚠️Note: The owner of the video cannot set a default on the appearance of the captions, customizing will be the viewer’s preference and the owner will not have control over it.

How to customize my showcase

You can customize your showcases to reflect the identity of your brand, project, or presentation. This article will cover what types of settings are available and how to customize your showcase’s appearance. To edit showcase privacy settings, see How to manage the privacy of your showcase.

  • Customizing showcases overview
  • How to preview my showcase
  • How to customize my showcase from the preview
  • How to customize the banner on my featured content showcase

Customizing showcases overview

Once you’ve created your showcase, you will see a panel on the left side of the showcase settings page with three sections: Settings, Layout,andPlayback.

WithinSettings, you can edit the following:

  • Title

  • Description

  • Privacy

  • Branding

  • Dark mode: Enable dark mode for an alternative viewing experience (available for Player view)

  • Color: Choose a primary color

  • Custom logo: Upload a custom logo

  • Vimeo logo: Show or hide Vimeo’s logo (available for Player view)

  • Registration

  • SEO

  • TV apps

In the Layout panel, your available options are based on the layout you choose. For example, the option to show or hide Vimeo’s app navigation only applies to the Featured content layout.

Within Layout, the following options are available:

  • Featured content
  • Navigation: Controls such as Vimeo navigation, Search, and Copy link.
  • Featured content: You can change the showcase featured banner image and text, and other text details.
  • Video grid: You can add or remove videos, create an Event and customize the video order as well as the appearance of the video cards’ display within the showcase.
  • Player view
  • Video grid: You can add videos to your embedded playlist or create an Event as well as customize the video order of your playlist.

Within Playback, you can customize the following:

  • Behavior (available for Player view)
  • Autoplay: Your videos will automatically play upon loading the showcase
  • Loop: The first video in your showcase will automatically play once the last video ends.
  • Engagement
  • Like: Add or remove the Like button from the video page.
  • Share: Add or remove the Share button from the video page.
  • Comments: Add or remove the comment section from the video page.
  • Download: Add or remove the Download button from the video page.
  • Now playing
  • Title: Add or remove the title from the video page.
  • Description: Add or remove the description.
  • Profile picture: Add or remove the profile photo.
  • Profile name: Add or remove the profile name.
  • Views: Add or remove the views from the video page.
  • Date added: Add or remove the date the video was added to the showcase.
  • Video grid
  • Video cards: You can choose to display the thumbnails or include the entire player for the videos within the showcase.
  • Grid size: Change the size of the video player within the showcase.
  • Video count: Add or remove the number of videos within the showcase.
  • Titles: Add or remove the titles of the videos within the showcase.
  • Profile pictures: Add or remove the profile photos from the videos within the showcase.
  • Profile names: Add or remove the profile names from the videos within the showcase.

How to preview my showcase

To preview your showcase customizations, you will need to save any changes, then follow these steps:

  1. Open your showcase from your Library.
  2. You will see a banner at the top of the page with options to switch between web and mobile views.
  3. Select the mobile icon to see the mobile view within the showcase settings page.
  4. To open a full webpage preview of your showcase in a tab, select the out-link icon at the top-right of the page.

How to customize my showcase from the preview

You can customize your showcase right from the preview screen by hovering over the area. To do so:

  1. Within your showcase settings, you’ll see the preview screen of your showcase.
  2. Hover over the top portion of the preview. A blue outline should appear with a Customize button on the right side.
  3. Select Customize.
  4. Repeat these steps for the Banner section at the bottom of the preview and the Video grid below that.
  5. You can customize the video grid or manage the videos within your showcase from there.

How to customize the banner on my featured content showcase

You can customize the banner background on your featured content showcase for a more personalized appearance. To do so:

  1. Within your showcase settings, select the Layout tab.
  2. Ensure the Featured content layout is selected then choose the Featured content tab.
  3. Under the Background section, select the drop-down.
  4. You can choose between None, Video thumbnail, or Custom image.
  • If you want to update the thumbnail of the featured video, you can do so from that video’s settings page.
  1. If you choose Video thumbnail, hover over the thumbnail photo and click Select from video. A pop-up modal will appear where you can pick which video or event you’d like to make the featured video in this Showcase.
  2. If you choose Custom image, you can upload your own branded banner by selecting Upload image.
  3. Under the Details section, you can use the toggles to show or hide the Title, Description, and Start watching button. In addition, you can set your text Alignment.
  4. The settings will save automatically.

⚠️Note: When a video or live event is featured, you can choose whether the banner displays the Showcase title and description or the Video title and description.

For example, if you feature a live event about ‘Product Launch’ in a showcase titled ‘Company Events,’ you can use this setting to have the banner display either ‘Company Events’ or ‘Product Launch’ as the main title.

How to customize the appearance of my recording in the Record Studio

Above the record preview in the Record Studio is the inspector toolbar. Here, you can customize the appearance of your recording, such as the layout of the elements on the canvas or the canvas color.

This article discusses various features and steps to customize recording layouts, aspect ratios, camera backgrounds, view shapes, cropping options, and canvas colors in the Record Studio.

  • How to customize the layout for your recording
  • How to change the aspect ratio for your recording
  • How to change the background effect of your camera
  • How to change your camera’s view shape
  • How to crop your shared screen or camera view
  • How to change the canvas color for your recording

How to customize the layout for your recording

You can customize the layout of your recording from pre-designed layouts.

To customize the layout for your recording in the Record Studio:

  1. Select the canvas.
  2. From the inspector toolbar above the canvas, select the Layoutbutton.
  3. Scroll through the selections of layouts. They are categorized by Camera Only, Screen Only, and Camera + Screen
  4. Select which layout you’d like to use and it will be applied to your recording.
  5. You can also choose to flip or mirror the orientation of the elements by selecting the flip buttons at the top of the layout window.

You can also select and drag elements of the recording to reposition them on the screen.

How to change the aspect ratio for your recording

You can change the aspect ratio of your recording in the Record Studio by selecting the Ratiobutton in the inspector toolbar above the canvas.

You can change the aspect ratio to:

  • Landscape (16:9)
  • Square (1:1)
  • Portrait (9:16)

Select the ratio you would like to change your recording to; the changes will apply automatically. You can further customize the layout of your recording based on the ratio selected.

How to change the background effect of your camera

You can change your camera’s background and add effects.

To change your camera’s background:

  1. Select your camera’s view from the record preview window.
  2. Select the Effectsbutton from the inspector toolbar.
  3. The effects window will pop up. Here, you can choose to mirror your camera, blur the background, make it transparent, or upload your own image as a background.

For best results when uploading a background image:

  • Use a high-quality image file up to 2560px x 1440px. A smaller image may appear lower quality based on your chosen layout.
  • Use a common image format such as JPG, GIF, PNG, or JPEG.
  • While GIF files are supported, animated GIFs are not supported at this time.

How to change your camera’s view shape

You can change the shape of your camera’s view in your recording.

To change the shape of your camera:

Select your camera preview on your canvas.

  1. Select the Shapebutton on the inspector toolbar above the canvas.
  2. Select the shape that you would like to change your camera’s view to from the toolbar to preview it
  3. When you’ve selected the shape you would like to change your camera’s view to, select the blue checkmark to apply it to your canvas.

How to crop your shared screen or camera view

You crop your shared screen or camera view on your canvas in two ways: manually or bycrop ratio.

To manually crop:

  1. Select your camera view or shared screen from your canvas.
  2. Select the Crop button from the inspector toolbar above the canvas.
  3. A crop bounding box will appear around your selected element. Select and drag the corners to crop your screen or camera view.
  4. Select theblue checkmark in the inspector toolbar to apply the crop.

To crop using the crop ratio:

  1. Select your camera view or shared screen from your canvas.
  2. Select the Crop button from the inspector toolbar above the canvas.
  3. Select the Crop Ratiodropdown menu.
  4. Select which crop ratio you would like to use - 16:9 (landscape), 1:1 (square), or 9:16 (portrait).
  5. Select the blue checkmark to apply the crop ratio to the canvas.

How to change the canvas color for your recording

If your layout does not fill the entire record window, you can customize the canvas color for the remaining space.

To customize the canvas color:

  1. Select the canvas of the record preview window.
  2. Select the Canvas Colorbutton on the top toolbar.
  3. Select the color that you would like to use for the remaining space of your canvas. You can select a solid color, a gradient, or a specific HEX color code.
  4. A preview will appear. Once you are satisfied with the color of your canvas, click outside the color box to apply it.

For more information on recording a video in the Record Studio, visit ‘How to record a video in the Record Studio’

How to customize the embedded player

This feature requires a paid plan.

You can customize the appearance and behavior of the video player when embedded on other websites. This article discusses various methods for customizing and managing player appearance settings for embedded Vimeo videos.

  • How to customize my embedded player
  • What customization options are available for the embedded player?
  • Interactivity overview
  • About small embedded players
  • About third-party players
  • Customization options for Organizations and Workspaces

How to customize my embedded player

There are two ways to edit the player appearance settings for your videos. You can edit the embedded settings for an individual video via the video settings page. You can also use an embed preset which you can apply to multiple videos to maintain consistent branding.

Any time you change the custom embed options for a particular video, it will automatically update on sites where it has already been embedded.

To access embed appearance settings from the video settings page:

  1. After selecting a video from your library, select theAppearance icon from the left-side panel of the video settings page. Ensure you are on the Embed tab of the Appearance panel.
  2. Apply your desired settings under the Branding, Engagement, Details, and Controls sections.
  3. Select Save when finished.
  • You can also select + Save new presetif you’d like to create a custom preset. To read more, visit How to create and apply appearance presets for videos.

What customization options are available for the embedded player?

For a comprehensive breakdown of settings, refer to Video appearance customization Comparison. The customization options available for the embedded player are:

  • Branding & Custom logo
  • Engagement
  • Details
  • Play button location and controls

⚠️Note: There is no way to include the video download button on the embedded player; this is only accessible from the video page on vimeo.

Interactivity overview

Interaction tools help you connect with your viewers and can help drive engagement and conversions. These will appear in both the embedded player and the video page. To add these to your video, select your video from the library and open the Interactivity tab on the right side.

Interaction tools include:

  • End screens
  • Registration
  • Chapters
  • Cards

About small embedded players

If your embedded video is less than 375px wide, some elements on the playbar will be hidden within an expandable menu.

Select the arrow icon on the player to access volume controls, captions and subtitle options, playback speed controls, picture-in-picture, and full-screen mode.

Screenshot: Small embedded playbar with expansion arrow icon highlighted with arrow pointing to it

⚠️Note: If your webpage is using a responsive design, the embedded player may automatically adhere to a smaller size on mobile. Some end screens will not appear if the player is smaller than 300px wide or 169px tall.

About third-party players

Vimeo’s embed and privacy settings only apply to the embedded Vimeo player. If you have a plan that includes third-party player links, Vimeo’s embed customizations will not apply. However, the third-party player might support its own set of customizations — check out their support documentation for more info.

Customization options for Organizations and Workspaces

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Presets can be set and managed at both the Workspace level and the Organization level. Note that settings at the Organization level take precedence over those set at the Workspace level. To read more, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings or How to edit my Workspace’s settings.

How to customize the video page

This article explains how to customize the appearance and settings of your Vimeo video page with presets and various customizable features.

You have control over the settings on your video’s page on vimeo. This is the page viewers will see when they access your video. From the Appearance panel on the video settings page, you can create reusable video page presets and embed presets with different settings for each viewing environment.

  • How to customize the video page
  • What settings can be customized on the video page?

How to customize the video page

Follow these steps to access Appearance settings on the video settings page:

  1. Select your video from your library.
  2. Navigate to the Appearance icon on the left-hand toolbar and choose the Video page tab. Screenshot: Appearance panel on video settings page with an arrow pointing to the video page tab
  3. Here, you may create or apply an existing presetfor the video page or select settings for this individual video using the dropdown menus in this panel.
  4. You will see options for Branding, Video details,Engagement, and Controls. Open each dropdown menu to toggle on or off specific features.
  5. After making any changes, select Save.
  6. Visit the video page to view all your customizations. You can get there by selecting Share > Copy linkfrom the upper right corner or by using theView on Vimeo link at the top of the Appearance panel.

What settings can be customized on the video page?

Below is a basic overview of the customization options available for video pages on vimeo. Custom color settings are only applied toUnlisted and Private videos. For a comprehensive breakdown of settings, refer to Video appearance customization Comparison.

Note that commenting settings within the Appearance panel only control the visibility of comments on the video page.

  • Custom logo
  • Engagement
  • Details
  • Play button location and controls

Interactivity overview

Interaction tools help you connect with your viewers and can help drive engagement and conversions. These will appear in both the embedded player and the video page. To add these to your video, select your video from the library and open the Interactivity tab on the right side.

Interaction tools include:

  • End screens
  • Registration
  • Chapters
  • Cards

⚠️Note:End screens are only reflected on the video page when the video privacy is UnlistedorPassword-protected. Public video pages on vimeo.com will use the default settings.

Customization options for Organizations and Workspaces

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Presets can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit ‘How to edit my Organization’s settings’ or’How to edit my Workspace’s settings’.

How to customize videos in my showcase

You can manage the content in your showcases to your preference by re-arranging, deleting, or adding more videos. This article discusses how to customize the videos within your showcase.

  • What to know before customizing videos within a showcase
  • How to arrange videos within a showcase
  • How to customize my video grid for the featured content layout
  • How to remove a video from a showcase
  • How to use bulk actions on showcases

What to know before customizing videos within a showcase

Before customizing videos within your showcase, take note of the following:

  • We don’t have a feature that allows for the creation of folders or sub-showcases within showcases.
  • It is also not possible to change the order in which your showcases appear on your showcase management page. They are organized by the date they were created.

How to arrange videos within a showcase

To arrange videos within a showcase, follow these steps:

  1. Open the showcase.
  2. Select the Layout tab.
  3. Choose your desired layout, then select the Video grid section.
  4. Under the Content tab, select the arrow icon on the right-side to open the drop-down menu and choose Custom.
  5. Drag and drop videos to arrange them in the order of your choosing.

You can sort videos by one of the following options in the dropdown menu:

  • Title A-Z
  • Title Z-A
  • Last added to Vimeo
  • First added to Vimeo
  • Most likes
  • Most plays
  • Most comments
  • Custom
  • Last Modified
  • First Modified

How to customize my video grid for the featured content layout

You can customize how the video cards appear on your showcase page when using the featured content layout.

  1. Open your showcase from the library.
  2. Select the Layout tab.
  3. Choose the Video grid option.
  4. Under the Customization tab, you can select the desired options.
  5. Select Save at the top of the page.

You can customize the following for the video grid display:

  • Video cards: You can choose to display the player or only the thumbnail of the videos.
  • Grid size: Control the size of the player appearance.
  • Video count: Display the number of videos within your showcase.
  • Video details: Choose if you’d like to include the video titles, profile pictures, and profile names.

How to remove a video from a showcase

To remove a video from a showcase, follow these steps:

  1. Open your showcase from the library.
  2. Select the Layout tab.
  3. Choose the Video grid option.
  4. Under the Content tab, select the three dots (…) to open the menu.
  5. Choose Remove.

💡Tip: Removing a video from a showcase won’t remove the video from your library.

How to use bulk actions on showcases

To remove multiple videos from a showcase, follow these steps:

  1. Open your showcase from the library.
  2. Select the Layout tab.
  3. Choose the Video grid option.
  4. Under the Content tab, use the checkboxes on the left-hand side of the page to select multiple videos.

At the bottom of the page, you will see the option to Remove from showcase.

How to delete a registration form

This article discusses how to remove registration from your videos. You can turn off registration or delete a registration form preset.

  • How to turn off registration
  • How to delete a preset form

How to turn off registration

If you would like to remove registration from your video, follow the steps below:

  1. Select the video from your Library to open the video settings page.
  2. Select the Interactive icon on the panel to the left, and then select Registration.
  3. Select Turn off registration. Your changes will be saved automatically.

How to delete a preset form

To delete a registration form preset entirely, follow these steps:

  1. Select Customize form from the Registration panel.
  2. Open the Preset dropdown and hover over the form’s name to find the trash can icon.
  3. After you select the trash can icon, a new modal will appear where you can select Delete to save your changes.

For more information, see How to manage registration form presets.

How to delete a showcase

Follow these steps to delete a showcase from your library:

  1. Open the showcase management page.
  2. Select the overflow (three-dot) menu to the right of the showcase that you want to delete.
  3. Select Delete.
  4. You will be asked to confirm your choice. Select Delete to continue.
  • You can also delete your showcase from the individual settings page. Select the three dot overflow at the top-right of the screen and choose Delete showcase.

⚠️Note: Once you delete a showcase, it won’t be available anywhere it’s embedded.

How to delete a video

When you delete a video, it isn’t gone for good right away — it moves to Recently deleted, where you can restore it for 30 days before it’s permanently removed.

Follow the below steps to delete your video:

  1. Log in to Vimeo and select your Library in the left navigation menu.
  2. Choose the video you want to delete.
  3. Select theoptions menu (…) in the top right corner of the video settings page.
  4. Select Delete video. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-09-09 at 5.30.44 PM.png

To learn why a video may have been deleted, see Why did my video get deleted?

How can I recover a deleted video?

Videos you delete yourself move to Recently deleted, where you can restore them for 30 days before they’re permanently removed. After 30 days, or for videos removed for other reasons, we can’t guarantee recovery — but our support team can assist if the video is still in our archived storage. Contact us for further assistance.

How to download a video from my library

This feature requires a paid plan on Vimeo.

The article discusses the process of downloading videos from your library.

What to know before downloading a video

  • If you are looking for instructions on how to download videos uploaded on Vimeo by other creators, visit How to download a video on Vimeo.
  • My library exclusively operates within the boundaries of your active or selected Workspace.
  • If you are the video owner or a team member on a paid account, you can download your own videos from the video settings page.

How to download a video from your library

Follow the steps below to download:

  1. Select your desired Workspace and navigate to your library.
  2. Select the video you would like to download.
  3. Select the downward arrow on the Share button in the top right corner of the video settings page to open the dropdown menu.
  4. SelectDownload.

💡Tip:If your video has multiple language audio tracks, you can download language-specific versions. Visit How to download language-specific versions of my videos for instructions.

Suggested next steps

Now that you have learned how to download a video

How to download a video on Vimeo

This feature requires a paid plan.

You can download videos from Vimeo if the owner has enabled downloads. Vimeo provides creators with the option to enable or disable downloads for their content. If a video owner has chosen to allow downloads, you will find a download button or link available on the video’s page. This article explains how to download a video fromVimeo.

  • Before you begin
  • How to download a video on Vimeo
  • Making the most of downloading
  • Suggested next steps

Before you begin

Things to keep in mind before you start downloading videos on Vimeo:

  • Ensure that you’re logged in to your Vimeo account to download source files from public videos.
  • Confirm that the Download option is enabled for the video.
  • Remember that bulk downloading is not supported.

How to download a video on Vimeo

To download a video on Vimeo:

  1. Select the Download button below the video player on the video page.
  2. A modal window will appear with different file sizes to choose from.
  3. Select the download icon next to the version you want to download. ⚠️Note: You must be logged in to download a source file for a Public video.
  4. You will be prompted to save the video to your device.
  5. Depending on your browser, selecting the download icon may result in the video opening in a new tab instead of downloading the file to your computer. If this occurs:
  • For Windows users: Right-click on the link and choose Save as or Save target as.
  • For Mac users: Hold down theControl key on your keyboard and click the link, then chooseSave link as or Download linked file.

Making the most of downloading

Downloading videos from Vimeo allows you to watch them offline or share approved content with collaborators, to make the most of it:

  • For presentations, opt for a higher-quality file. For quick playback or sharing, a smaller file size is recommended.
  • Store downloaded files securely to prevent unauthorised distribution.

Suggested next steps

  • If you want to download an On Demand video, refer toRent, buy, or subscribe to On Demand videos.
  • Learn how todownload captions or subtitles from a video.

How to download language-specific versions of my videos

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

This article explains how to download language-specific versions of your video (muxes) if they are available in multiple languages.

Your video will have multiple audio tracks in various languages if you’ve used AI to translate your video’s audio or if you’ve manually uploaded any additional audio tracks.

To download a language-specific version of your video:

  1. Select your video from your library.
  2. Select the vertical ellipses (⋮) > Downloadunder the thumbnail of your video.
  3. If your video has multiple language audio tracks, a dropdown menu will appear, showing all available languages.
  4. Select the language you’d like to download the video in.
  5. Select the download button to the right of the video resolution you want to download.

The download will include only the video and the audio in the selected language. To download subtitles or transcript files for the video, refer to “How to view or download my video’s transcript.”

You cannot bulk download videos.

How to download my analytics report

Tracking your video performance is key to understanding your audience. With Vimeo’s analytics, you can easily download reports to review engagement, viewer behavior, and more.

This article discusses how to access and download Vimeo’s analytics reports

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Analytics are available for both the Organization and its Workspaces. Organization Admins can view combined analytics from all Workspaces.

  • How to access the analytics report
  • How to download the analytics report
  • FAQs

How to access the analytics report

To access your analytics report, go to the Vimeo Analytics Dashboard or navigate to the Advanced dashboard by selecting Analyticsfrom the panel on the left side of the homepage after you log in to Vimeo.

How to download the analytics report

To download analytics, visit any of the following Report pages:

  • Video Report
  • Region Report
  • Source Report
  • Device Report
  • Date Report
  • Team Report

To download any report:

  1. You can download the type of report you want from the dashboard menu on the left side of the page.
  2. Use the filters at the top of the page to refine your report and select the specific data you need.
  3. Click on the Export databutton below the displayed graph.
  4. You can either directly download the report or have it emailed to you.

💡Tip: If you have an account with lots of videos/views, it is advisable to have the report emailed to your account.

⚠️Note: If you want the CSV file of all your uploaded videos, then please get in touch with support for the same.

  1. After starting the download, you will receive a test notification confirming whether your request is being processed or if an error has occurred.

Downloading your analytics report gives you the flexibility to review your performance data offline, share insights with stakeholders, and maintain historical records.

FAQs

  • Why are the total amounts in the video report and the downloaded CSV files different? The Report Total line on the analytics report may differ from the total in the downloaded CSV file because the system excludes deleted video analytics from the CSV file but includes them in the Report Total line.
  • Why is the report’s total for unique viewers/impressions different from the CSV file’s total? The Report’s total line for unique viewers and impressions will differ from totaling the downloaded CSV column because the CSV counts that data at a video level. The report’s total line will only total each unique viewer/impression. For example, if one viewer watches 4 different videos, the unique view/impression will be counted individually for each video row in the CSV report. The report total will only count this as 1 unique view/impression despite the viewer watching 4 different videos.
  • Why does the number of videos selected in the content filter not appear in my downloaded CSV file? The downloaded CSV file will not include lines of data where the video has no analytics. This is why, if you use the content filter and it displays a certain number of videos, but the number of lines in the CSV is less.

How to edit my video’s transcript

This feature requires a paid plan.

You can edit your video’s transcript in the Languagemenu on the video’s settings page. This article explains how to edit your video’s transcript.

  • How to edit a transcript
  • Can I use the API to add text tracks?

How to edit a transcript

You can edit your video’s most recent transcript directly on your video’s settings page. If your video has multiple language tracks, you can edit each file individually. To do so:

  1. Select your video from your library.
  2. Select Languages from the left-side toolbar.
  3. Select the overflow menu (⋮)to the right of the transcript that you want to edit,
  4. Select Edit to open the transcript.
  5. Once you have found a line of text to edit, select the text box and make any necessary changes.

Editing subtitle timestamps

You can also edit the start and end timestamps of individual subtitles directly in the transcript editor. You don’t need to download the file internally. To adjust a timestamp:

  1. Find the subtitle row you want to adjust.
  2. Select the start or end timestamp field on that row.
  3. Enter the new time value.
  4. The preview updates immediately, and your changes sync across all platforms.

Note: Timestamp editing is available only for VOD content. It is not supported for live event transcriptions. Timestamps must be edited one subtitle at a time; bulk editing is not available.

Can I use the API to add text tracks?

You can use the API to upload and manage text tracks for captions or subtitles in your video. Read more at Vimeo Developer: Working with Text Tracks.

How to edit overlay settings

Overlays are an effective way to enhance viewer engagement and provide additional information. This article will guide you through the process of editing overlay settings.

  • Video tutorial
  • Accessing Overlay settings
  • Background color
  • Close button options
  • Customizing the close button
  • When not to allow manual closure
  • Overlay animation
  • Preview animation

Video tutorial

This video explains how to edit overlay settings:

Accessing Overlay settings

To get started, open the Overlay editor. If you notice your video shining through the overlay when you first open it, i.e. depending on your template choice or starting point, the overlay’s background might be transparent by default.

Background color

You can customize the overlay’s background color and modify it to suit your video. Drag the color bar to modify the background.

Close button options

Next up are the close button settings. You have the choice to either hide the default close button or allow viewers to manually close the overlay. Typically, it’s a good idea to enable manual closure. This is particularly useful when your overlay contains additional information that viewers might want to explore, such as a bio or product details in a shoppable video. Offering viewers an intuitive way to exit the overlay and return to the main video contributes to a seamless experience.

Customizing the close button

You can customize the design of the close button. You can use your own branded “X” image or add custom text like Back or Return to Video.

⚠️Note: All overlays do not come with a default close button

When not to allow manual closure

While allowing manual closure is generally recommended, there are instances where you might opt for a different approach. For example, in cases where you have a mandatory quiz question or a branching experience where viewer choices determine the path, you might choose to disable the overlay’s default close button. This ensures viewers engage with the content as intended without accidentally bypassing it.

Overlay animation

You can add animation effects to elements as they appear and disappear on the screen. Animation type: There are 2 types of animation available: Fade In and Fade In Cascade.

Direction of Animation: Select the direction from which the animation effect will come.

If you opt for the Fade in Cascade style, you can further refine the animation. You can choose the Cascade order i.e. the order in which the elements will animate.

You can also set the delay between each element’s appearance with the Cascade delay option.

Preview animation

This allows you to see how your chosen animations play out and make adjustments according to your preferences.

For more guidance on creating interactive videos, visit the Vimeo Help Center.

How to edit subtitle timestamps

This feature is available to all users with access to AI transcription.

You can fine-tune when your subtitles appear and disappear directly in the transcript editor. No external tools needed. This is useful when subtitles display too quickly or too slowly, giving viewers more or less time to read them.

How to edit subtitle timestamps

  1. Select your video from your library.
  2. Select Languages from the left-side toolbar.
  3. Select the overflow menu (⋮) to the right of the transcript you want to edit.
  4. Select Edit to open the transcript editor.
  5. Find the subtitle row whose timing you want to adjust.
  6. Select the start or end timestamp field on that row.
  7. Enter the new time value.

The preview updates immediately. Your changes sync across all platforms automatically.

Limitations

  • Timestamp editing is available for VOD content only. It is not available for live event transcriptions.
  • Start and end times can be edited independently.
  • Bulk editing is not supported. Timestamps must be adjusted one subtitle at a time.

How to edit the dubbed audio on my AI-translated video

The feature discussed below requires an Enterprise plan and is gradually rolling out over the next few weeks. If you have questions on availability, please contact your account manager.

You can edit your dubbed videos to correct errors or refine the wording. The video’s dubbed audio and translated subtitles will update based on your changes.

This article explains how to edit the translated transcript to update both the subtitles and the dubbed audio for that language in your video.

  • What to know before editing the dubbed audio
  • How to edit my dubbed video

What to know before editing the dubbed audio

Before editing your dubbed video, please note the following:

  • Some languages are available for dubbed audio translations, while others are only available for subtitle translations.
  • About supported languages for Vimeo AI’s audio translations
  • About supported languages for Vimeo AI’s subtitle translations
  • Editing the text as outlined in this article to regenerate audio won’t result in extra credit charges at this time.
  • Editing the transcript will update both the subtitle text and regenerate the dubbed audio track for your translated videos.
  • AI dubbing is only editable for 30 days after creation. To meet the data protection commitments in our AI addendum, we delete dubbing project data from our third-party AI providers within 30 days. After this 30-day window, the dubbed audio can no longer be edited. Because the subtitles generated as part of the dubbing project are tied to it, those subtitles can’t be edited after 30 days either. Subtitles created on their own (not as part of AI dubbing) aren’t affected by this limit. To make changes after 30 days, you’ll need to create a new dub.

How to edit my dubbed audio

You can edit your dubbed audio by updating the translated transcript of your video. To do so:

  1. Select the video from your library.
  2. Select Manageunder the video player.
  3. From your video’s settings page, select the Languages icon from the left-hand navigation bar.
  4. In the Languagespanel, hover over the subtitles track for the language that you would like to edit. Select the Pencil icon corresponding to the language you wish to edit. Screenshot: The languages panel showing Spanish subtitles and Dubbed audio toggled on. There is a pencil icon to the right of the subtitles option and is labeled ’Edit
  5. In the transcript editor, select the line text you wish to change and make your edits.
  6. After you’ve made your changes to the transcript, select the Update subtitles and audio dubsbutton at the bottom of the Edit transcript panel. Screenshot: The transcript on the left panel shows a typing cursor editing text while the subtitles in the video show the original text. At the bottom of the transcript panel there is a button that says ’Update subtitles and audio dubs.”
  7. Your dubbed audio will regenerate to reflect these changes.

How to embed my video

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

Embedding your video allows you to extend its reach and increase its visibility. This article will guide you through the steps to embed your video on external sites as well as setting up your video’s embed privacy, ensuring a smooth integration.

  • How to embed my video
  • How to manage where my video can be embedded

How to embed my video

Follow these steps to embed your video outside of vimeo.com:

  1. Navigate to your Library and select a video to open the video settings page.
  2. In the upper right corner, select theShare button. Screenshot: Top right section in video settings page with the Share icon
  3. Select the Embed option at the bottom of the modal Screenshot: Share modal with Embed button highlighted
  4. A modal window will open with the HTML code.
  • By default, this code is for a Responsive player, but you can manually configure the embedded player’s size (in pixels) if you wish. To do so, select the Fixedoptionin the Sizesectionand enter your desired player size.
  • You can also customize the playback of your embedded video. Under the Playback section, you can enable Autoplay, Mute, and Loop. ⚠️Note:Custom video URLs cannot be embedded.
  1. Select Copy embed code to copy the HTML code to your clipboard, which you can then paste into your website’s HTML editor.
  • Any future changes you make to your video, such as its appearance settings, will automatically apply to the embedded player. You will not need to re-embed your video.

How to manage where my video can be embedded

You can control whether your video can be viewed elsewhere besides vimeo.com. All privacy settings except for Privateallow you to embed your video on other sites.

  1. Navigate to your Library and select a video to open the video settings page.
  2. On the upper right-hand corner of the page, select theSharebutton.
  3. Select the Embed option at the bottom of the modal.
  4. Under the Where can this be embedded section, select the drop-down and choose between Anywhere, Nowhere, and Specific domains. Screenshot: Embed privacy settings drop down titled ‘where can this be embedded?’
  • Anywhere: Anyone can embed your video onto any page on the internet.
  • Nowhere: No one, including you and your team members, can embed your video anywhere. It will only be viewable on vimeo.com.
  • Specific domains(Available for all plans except Free and Basic): After you select this option, add your website’s domain (mysite.com) or subdomain (subdomain.mysite.com) in the text field that appears below the dropdown menu; be sure to click the (+) to add it. You can specify and manage up to 50 domains where your video can be embedded.
  • Note that when adding a domain, such as vimeo.com, to the “specific domains” list, all subdomains directly under it, including project.vimeo.com, will be automatically included. However, subdomains at further levels, like example.project.vimeo.com, will not be covered by this setting.
  • Wildcard characters are not supported.
  1. Your selection will save automatically.

How to embed my showcase

How to enable account-level privacy restrictions

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

For Enterprise Users with Workspaces: These settings can be managed by a Workspace Administrator for the specific Workspace or an Organization Administrator for the Organization. The Organization’s settings will take precedence.

Account-level privacy restrictions give you more granular control over which privacy settings Admins, Contributors, and Owners can use. This ensures that the content on your account can only be shared content for intended internal use cases.

  • What to know before using account-level privacy restrictions
  • How to enable account-level privacy restrictions
  • What privacy settings can I restrict for my team members?
  • What do team members see if they have limited permissions?

What to know before using account-level privacy restrictions

  • Disabling a privacy setting for Admins will also disable the privacy setting for Contributors, as Admins cannot have fewer permissions than Contributors.
  • This means you can disable a privacy setting for Contributors and leave it enabled for Admins, but you cannot disable a privacy setting for Admins and leave it enabled for Contributors.
  • Disabling a privacy setting for Admins (and therefore all team members) will prompt you to confirm that any videos that previously had this privacy setting will be migrated to “Private” since you no longer want to use this privacy setting. By clicking Confirm, the migration will commence automatically. Any clips that previously had that privacy setting will soon have the Private privacy setting.

How to enable account-level privacy restrictions

  1. From the dropdown menu under your profile icon, navigate to Manage Team.
  2. On the team management page, select Settings.
  3. Scroll down to Privacy settings and select Privacy restrictions by role.You can enable or disable privacy settings per role based on your desired configuration. ⚠️Note:Privacy settings will be enabled by default unless you previously had the Public privacy disabled.
  4. Your changes will be saved automatically.

What privacy settings can I restrict for my team members?

  • Video privacy: You can restrict videos on your account to a specific privacy for your team members.
  • Publish to third-party websites: You can decide if your team members can share your content on social media and simulcasting events.
  • Update domain privacy: You can lock down the embed privacy settings applied to a video, including the approved domains.

What do team members see if they have limited permissions?

When a team member navigates to a video that they have can edit access to, they will only see the privacy settings that have been enabled for their role. Any privacy settings that are not enabled will not be visible.

There may be cases where a video cannot have its privacy setting changed by a Contributor. For example, if Admins are able to set videos to Public but Public is disabled for Contributors, Contributors will not be able to change the privacy setting for videos already set to Public.

How to turn on captions or subtitles

⚠️Note: Video creators can upload captions and subtitles to their videos. If you do not see your language, it probably means that the video has not yet been transcribed or translated. You may contact the video creator directly to inquire.

How to turn off captions or subtitles

  2. In the menu that appears, selectOff.

How to export a video from Adobe Premiere Pro for Vimeo

This article provides a brief overview of the steps required to export your final video from Adobe Premiere Pro, allowing it to be uploaded to Vimeo.

  • How to export a video from Adobe Premiere Pro
  • Suggested next steps

How to export a video from Adobe Premiere Pro

To export your video:

  1. Highlight your final sequence in the Premiere Pro timeline.
  2. Go to File > Export > Media.
  3. Under Export Settings, set your output format and preset.
  4. Click the Output Name to choose the file name and destination folder.
  5. Ensure Export Video and Export Audio are checked.
  6. Under the Effects tab, confirm your preferred options.
  7. Under the Video tab, click Match Source.
  8. Confirm your video settings.
  9. Under the Audio tab, confirm your audio settings.
  10. Under the Multiplexer tab, confirm your multiplexer settings.
  11. Leave the Captions settings as needed.
  12. At the bottom of the window, select Use Maximum Render Quality.
  13. Review the estimated file size and ensure you have sufficient storage space on the Vimeo upload page.
  14. Once all settings are confirmed, click Export.

After exporting, review your file to ensure the picture and sound quality are correct before uploading to Vimeo.

Suggested next steps

Learn in detail about recommended Adobe Premiere Pro export settings for Vimeo uploads.

How to export video from Final Cut

You can export your videos from Final Cut to Vimeo. This article discusses a few different ways to export your video from Final Cut to be uploaded on Vimeo.

  • About sending files to compressor
  • How to share as a master file to my computer
  • About sharing/uploading directly to Vimeo using the Mac OS App

About sending files to compressor

For the most fine-grained control over your video’s export settings, we recommend using method 1 to send the file to Compressor first, then adjust the compression settings there. (Compressor can be purchased from Mac App Store: Compressor). Compressor gives much more control over your video’s export settings than FCP alone.

If you want to upload your video in Dolby Vision using Final Cut Pro, our partners at Dolby have a tutorial at How-To: Editing Dolby Vision with Apple Final Cut Pro for Vimeo.

  • PROS
  • CONS
  • You’ll have more fine-tuned control over your compression settings.
  • There are more steps involved.
    • You’ll need to purchase Compressor.

Select your final sequence in Final Cut, then open File > Send to Compressor.

How to share as a master file to my computer

  • PROS
  • CONS
  • A simple way to export videos (good if you have limited knowledge of compression).
  • You’ll have less fine-tuned control over your compression settings.
  • You can view your final file before uploading.

Read about exporting the master file from FCP from Apple at ‘Export final mastering files with Final Cut Pro’.

  1. In the Destinations menu, select Add Destination, then double-click “Export File.” You can name this destination if desired (e.g. “Vimeo export”). Make sure to apply the following settings:
  • Format
  • Video and Audio
  • Video codec
  • H.264
  • Include chapter markers
  • Unchecked
  1. Leave the Destinations menu. Highlight your final sequence.
  2. Go to File > Share > Export File… (or select the name you gave your Destination).
  3. In the Info Tab, you have the option to adjust your video title, description, and tags. However, those will not apply to your video on Vimeo. Click Next to begin the export process.
  4. View your finished, compressed file to make sure it looks and sounds correct, then upload it to Vimeo. Read about uploading to Vimeo in the ‘Upload and video settings’ section of the Help Center.

About sharing/uploading directly to Vimeo using the Mac OS App

⚠️Note: macOS 10.12 Sierra or higher is required.

  • PROS
  • CONS
  • You can upload a file to Vimeo from Final Cut in one step, without ever having to open a browser.
  • You won’t be able to see this file before it’s uploaded to Vimeo.
  • You can set the exact title, description, tags, and video privacy settings to be used on Vimeo.

Using the Mac OS app, you can compress and upload videos to Vimeo in one simple step. To get started, you’ll need to install the Vimeo app from the Mac OS App Store at App Store: Vimeo.

Next, please follow the instructions outlined in the ‘Vimeo MacOS App’ article to set up your integration with Final Cut. Once you’ve connected the Mac OS app on your system to Final Cut, you can then upload directly to Vimeo using the advanced sharing destination.

Screenshot: A screenshot showing the destinations menu in Final Cut. The left panel has multiple destinations where you can export your video. Vimeo (advanced) is selected as the destination in the left panel. The right panel shows the export settings of Vimeo (advanced).

Please note that Apple also includes built-in integration with Vimeo, as shown here under new destinations:

Screenshot: A screenshot showing how to add export destinations in Final Cut. Select the ‘Add Destination’ button in the left panel. Select ‘Vimeo’ in the right panel.

This integration can also be used to upload directly to Vimeo from Final Cut without using the Vimeo Mac OS app, however, Vimeo’s support team will be unable to assist with any issues that arise.

How to format a .csv file to set regional availability for my video or live event

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Using a .csv file, video owners and event hosts can outline which regions their video or live event should be visible in or blocked from. This article discusses how to format your .csv file.

  • Formatting your .csv file for geoblocking/geoallowing
  • Formatting examples
  • Importing your .csv file

Formatting your .csv file for geoblocking/geoallowing

You can import a .csv file to set your allowed or blocked locations. You can only import one type of location data per CSV file. This means that you can import location data using Country/Region/State/City (US Cities Only), OR you can import location data using US ZIP Codes.

You cannot combine both types of location data in the same CSV file. Currently, city-level blocking and allowing is only supported within the US for US Cities only.

To format your .csv file:

Format your .csv file according to the following guidelines:

  • Header Row: The first row must contain the following headers (case-insensitive):

  • MODE

  • COUNTRY

  • REGION

  • CITY

  • ZIP CODE

  • MODEColumn: Specify whether to “allow” or “block” access for each location. Use the values:

  • allowed

  • blocked

  • Location Data Columns:

  • For Country/Region/State/City Imports:

  • COUNTRY: Use the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Read more from the International Organization for Standardization at ISO 3166

  • REGION: Use the ISO 3166-2 region code (if applicable).

  • CITY: Enter the US city name. Currently, city-level blocking and allowing is only supported within the US for US Cities only.

  • ZIP CODE: Leave this column empty.

  • For US ZIP Code Imports:

  • COUNTRY & REGION, CITY: You can leave these columns empty.

  • POSTAL CODE: Enter the 5-digit US ZIP code. The United States Postal Service’sZip Code Lookup can help you find Zip Codes. Enter one zip code per line.

  • File Encoding: Save your CSV file using UTF-8 encoding to ensure proper character handling.

Formatting examples

The two tables below provide examples of correctly formatting your .csv file using the instructions provided.

By Country/Region/State/City:

  • MODE
  • COUNTRY
  • REGION
  • CITY
  • ZIP CODE
  • allowed
  • US
  • US-CA
  • Los Angeles
  • allowed
  • US
  • US-CA
  • San Francisco
  • allowed
  • US
  • US-NY
  • New York City
  • allowed
  • GB
  • GB-ENG
  • allowed
  • GB
  • GB-SC
  • allowed
  • GB
  • GB-WLS

By Zip Code:

  • MODE
  • COUNTRY
  • REGION
  • CITY
  • ZIP CODE
  • blocked
  • US
  • 75204
  • blocked
  • US
  • 07008
  • blocked
  • US
  • 00966
  • blocked
  • US
  • 11201
  • blocked
  • US
  • 12304

Importing your .csv file

After formatting your .csv file, you can import it into the Manage regional availabilitywindow in your video’s settings page or your live event’s settings.

How to host a showcase on my website

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

Hosting a showcase on your own website allows you to share curated content from Vimeo with your audience without sacrificing any of your branding or other site features.

This article discusses how to set up a custom domain for your Vimeo Showcase while ensuring secure HTTPS connections and troubleshooting common connection issues.

  • Customizing a showcase domain
  • Troubleshooting my custom domain connection

Customizing a showcase domain

As a Vimeo member, you can use a custom domain for your Showcase. Vimeo supports adding another layer of security to your connected custom domain with HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure).

HTTPS transmits its data security using an encrypted connection, ensuring that the connection to your domain is encrypted and preventing potential attackers from accessing or impersonating your site. When you connect to an HTTPS-secured server, secure sites will automatically redirect you to the HTTPS version.

To set up a custom domain for your Showcase, you can use a domain that you already own (https://my-rad-site.com), set up a subdomain on your existing website (https://showcase.my-rad-site.com), or purchase a new domain to use (https://my-new-site.com). To do so:

  1. Set up your domain:Purchase a domain from a registrar such as 0, 1, or 2. Alternately, you can set up a subdomain on your existing site. Contact your registrar or hosting service for instructions.
  2. Update your CNAME Record or A Record: If you want your showcase to live on a subdomain (https://showcase.my-rad-site.com), you will need to follow your registrar’s instructions for updating your CNAME Record so that it points to vimeoshowcase.com. If you want your showcase to live on your main domain (https://my-rad-site.com), follow your domain registrar’s instructions to set the domain’s A-Record to 34.67.129.45.

💡Tip:If you currently have an HTTP connection set up, it will stay connected to your Showcase. If you’d prefer to use HTTPS, you’ll need to update the DNS records on your domain provider’s end. The DNS records to update on your domain provider’s end are:

  • CNAME: vimeoshowcase.com
  • A Record: 34.67.129.45

⚠️Note: It may take up to 72 hours for these changes to take effect. 3. Enter your domain name: Beforesharing your showcase, you can enter your domain name. After selecting the Share button, select Customize and then Custom domain. Enter your domain name and then Connect domain. 4. Test your new showcase domain: Open a new browser window and navigate to the domain or subdomain you just set up. You should now see your Showcase. If you don’t see it, and it has been more than 72 hours since you updated your CNAME or A-Record, contact your domain registrar for further assistance.

Troubleshooting my custom domain connection

If you’re having trouble connecting your custom domain, several factors may be contributing to the issue. The most common causes are:

  1. Your domain has expired. First, check with your domain registrar to ensure your domain is active and registered with them before proceeding. Then, ensure the domain is disconnected from your Showcase, and attempt to connect it again.
  2. We were unable to issue an SSL certificate to your domain. Sometimes certificates cannot be issued for a number of reasons. We recommend trying to disconnect the domain from your Showcase, then attempting to reconnect it, before completing further troubleshooting.
  3. Privacy settings:Visit Privacy of videos in showcasesto learn how video privacy settings can impact showcase visibility.

How to label my videos to indicate they contain AI-generated or AI-enhanced content

What to know before labeling videos as AI-generated or AI-enhanced

  • To strike a balance between creators’ innovative use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and viewers’ demand for transparency regarding the authenticity of the content they consume, we require creators to disclose when realistic videos are created with altered or synthetic media, including generative AI.
  • Visit Disclosing videos as AI-generated or AI-enhanced to read more about our policy.
  • Labeling a video containing AI-generated content won’t lower a video’s rating.
  • The indicator for AI-generated content appears under the player on the video page or in the embedded video player. This label does not display in embedded videos if the video creator hides the video title.

How to label videos as AI-generated or AI-enhanced

You can disclose videos that have been meaningfully altered or synthetically generated while you are uploading them or at a later time from the video settings page. To do so:

  1. Select your video from the Library to open the video’s settings page.
  • Or, if you are uploading your video, wait until the video settings page appears in the upload workflow.
  1. Scroll past the player to the Content section.
  2. Select the checkbox next to Includes AI-generated content that appears real.
  3. Select the checkbox for Audio or Visuals, or both.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn about our policy regarding when to disclose content as generated with or enhanced by using AI.
  • Learn how to tell if a video on Vimeo was generated with or enhanced by using AI.
