How to manage commenting permissions

Customizable commenting permissions give you more control over the functionality of your videos on Vimeo. This article includes steps for editing settings on an individual video or for all current and/or future uploads.

For Enterprise Users with Workspaces: This feature can be managed by a Workspace Admin for videos uploaded to the Workspace. For additional information, visit ’How to edit my Workspace’s settings’.

  • How to update commenting permissions on an individual video
  • How to change the commenting Appearance settings
  • How to change viewer commenting settings for all current and/or future uploads

How to update commenting permissions on an individual video

You can turn viewer comments on and off for your videos. To determine who can comment on your video, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to Vimeo and navigate to your library.
  2. Select your video to open the video settings page.
  3. Select theCommentsbutton in the upper right-hand corner of the page. A panel will open on the right of the page.
  4. Navigate to the gear icon and select Allow viewer comments.
  • If there is a check mark next to Allow viewer comments, viewers will be allowed to comment on the video page.

Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise members can also create semi-private, unlisted video review pages for sharing with clients or collaborators. Read more about configuring a video review page at ‘About video review pages’.

How to change the commenting Appearance settings

You can use presets and theComments toggle withinAppearance settings to update commenting visibility on the video page. See ‘How to use page presets’ to read more about creating and applying presets.

Within the Appearance panel, scroll down to the Engagement section to toggle Comments on or off. When Comments are toggled off, comments will be hidden from the video page, but are not fully disabled. Viewers can still leave comments via the mobile app or third-party integrations when the Comments toggle is disabled within a preset or in Appearance settings.

How to change viewer commenting settings for all current and/or future uploads

To disable viewer comments for your existing videos and/or future uploads:

  1. Navigate to the Upload defaults tab under the Video section in your Account Settings.
  2. UnderComments, toggle off Allow viewer comments.
  3. Select thecheckboxnext to “Also apply to all existing videos”.
  4. Save your changes to apply this setting to your videos.

How to manage comments on my video

As an account Owner, an eligible team member, or an eligible Workspace member, you can manage comments from the video settings page. This article discusses the difference between Viewer and Collaborator comments and how to navigate and review both types. Visit ‘How to manage commenting permissions’ for information about changing commenting settings on your videos.

  • What are the differences between Viewer and Collaborator comments?
  • How to navigate comments on the video settings page
  • How to resolve a comment
  • How to download comments
  • How to manage commenting permissions
  • How to update commenting permissions on an individual video

What are the differences between Viewer and Collaborator comments?

As a video Owner, an eligible team member, or an eligible Workspace member, you will see two tabs within the video settings page comments panel:Collaboratorsand Viewers.

From the video page, you can access collaborator comments by selecting either the Leave feedback or the Manage button under the video player, depending on your permissions.

See below for the main differences between these types of comments:

  • Viewer comments are shown on the video page and within the Viewer tab on the video settings page. Comments within the Collaborators tab are notshown on the video page.
  • Unlike Viewer comments, collaborator comments cannot be disabled.
  • To access collaborator comments, you must have ‘Can comment’, ‘Can manage’, or ‘Can edit’ permission to the video or have access to a Review link. Anyone with the video link can leave a viewer comment, provided viewer comments are enabled.

How to navigate comments on the video settings page

From the video settings page, you can view both viewer and collaboration comments. Read on for an overview of how to filter and search comments:

  • View viewer comments:To see all comments from the video page, navigate to the Viewers tab.
  • Search comments:Use the magnifying glass icon at the top of the panel to search comments by keyword or name.
  • Filter by team or replies:Select the filter icon to choose whether to see all comments, those left by your team or guests, or to see only replies and mentions that may need your attention.
  • Sort options:You can also sort by newest, oldest, or by the timecodes referenced in comments.
  • Disable viewer comments:You can disable viewer comments from thegear icon. See How to change commenting permissions on my video [new version] for more information.
  • Unfurl links:If a comment contains a Vimeo video, you can view it here or open it on a new page.

How to resolve a comment

If you’re an Enterprise team owner, a Contributor, or an Admin team member on an Enterprise team, you can resolve comments left on a video.

  • Hover over a comment and select the circle icon to resolve a comment. ⚠️ Note: If the comment has additional direct replies, resolving the initial comment will also resolve all subsequent replies. Your viewers can toggle on the option to see any resolved comments, but they won’t be able to interact with them.
  • You can select theeye icon at the top of the panel to show all previously resolved comments.

How to download comments

Downloading comments is available on the video settings page.

Select the geariconand then choose“Download as…” to download all comments, or onlyCollaboratororViewercomments.

How to manage registration form presets

Registration presets allow you to save and reuse form customizations for live events, videos, and showcases. You can manage preset registration forms via the registration page.

  • How to create a registration form preset
  • How to apply a registration form preset
  • How to access registration form presets

How to create a registration form preset

Once you have configured a registration form, you can save it as a preset so you can use it again on other videos, events, or showcases. Follow the steps below to learn how:

  1. From your library, select your event, video, or showcase.
  2. For videos or completed events, selectInteractive. For upcoming events and showcases, select Registration. Both of these options will be on the left side of the page.
  3. If not already enabled,Turn on registration.
  4. From the panel that opens, select Customize form.
  5. Configure the form as desired. See How to configure the registration form for more information.
  6. Select thePresetdropdown and then select +Save new preset.
  7. Enter a name for the preset and then Save.
  8. Your form preset will now appear on the registration page and within the Preset dropdown on other videos and events.

How to apply a registration form preset

To apply a preset that you have already created to another video, event, or showcase, see the steps below:

  1. From your library, select your event, video, or showcase.
  2. For videos or completed events, selectInteractive. For upcoming events and showcases, select Registration. Both of these options will be on the left side of the page.
  3. If not already enabled,Turn on registration.
  4. From the panel that opens, select Customize form.
  5. Select thePresetdropdown and choose the previously saved form from the list.
  6. Read the message in the modal that appears and then select Apply.
  7. You may make additional customizations to the form, which will not impact the preset on other videos.

⚠️Note: Your live event’s registration settings will be saved even after the event is completed. Viewers will see the same registration form once the event ends, however, registrants from the live event will not be carried over to the saved recording unless you sync both to the same CRM list.

How to access registration form presets

To see all preset forms and export a file with the registrant information you’ve collected across videos and events, go to your account settings > Marketing >Registration or use this link: Manage registration.

Delete a preset form

On the registration page, you will see a list of all preset forms that you have saved. You can delete a form by hovering on it and select the trash icon to the right. When you delete a form it will be removed from your list of presets. Any videos using the preset will no longer be linked, but will keep the settings from the preset.

Download CSV file of registration data

In the upper righthand corner of the registration page, you can select the Export CSVbutton to download a file with the registrant information you’ve collected across videos and events.

How to manage video versions and access history

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

Version management is a critical tool for maintaining an organized video production workflow. It helps you track, manage, and revert updates to your video file while preserving a clear record of all changes and associated feedback.

  • What to know before you start
  • How to manage your video versions
  • To view your version history
  • To replace your video file
  • To restore a previous version
  • To delete a previous version
  • To download a previous version
  • Collaborator and viewer comments
  • Mentions and notifications
  • Making the most of version management
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before you start

  • Availability: Version Management is available to all users on the Video Settings page.
  • Automatic History: Every time you replace a video file using the official method, a new version is automatically created and recorded in the history.
  • Comment Preservation: Restoring a previous video version will make its footage active. However, comments from other versions will not be deleted; all comments are retained within the Version History.
  • Review Status: The review status indicates the current stage of a video’s review or approval process. It appears in the video settings page and helps collaborators stay aligned during production.
  • In progress: The video is being edited, and feedback has not been requested yet.
  • Needs review: The video is ready for feedback and comments.
  • Approved: The video has been finalized and is ready to share.

How to manage your video versions

All version controls are accessible from the Video Settings page.

To view your version history:
  1. Navigate to the Video Settings page for your clip.
  2. Locate the video name at the top of the page. You will see a version indicator (e.g., V5) next to it.
  3. Click the version historyto open the full drop-down.
  4. Here, you can see a timeline listing all past versions of your video.
To replace your video file:
  1. Open the version history drop-down menu.
  2. Click the + New version. Screenshot: Video player screen showing a version history popup with V2 as the ‘Current’ version and V1 listed below it. A ‘New version’ button is at the bottom.
  3. Or select Replace from beside theShare button to replace with a new version.
  4. Select the replacement file from your computer and upload it.
  5. The new file will replace the previous one, and the version number will be incremented (e.g., V5 becomes V6).
To restore a previous version:
  1. Open the version history drop-down menu.
  2. Select the 3 dots beside the version you wish to revert to (e.g., V3).
  3. Select Restore. Screenshot: Video player screen showing the version history popup. The three-dot menu next to V1 is open, displaying ‘View,’ ‘Restore,’ ‘Download,’ and ‘Delete’ options, with ‘Restore’ highlighted.
  4. The system will create a new version (e.g., V6) that uses the footage from the restored version (V3), and this V6 will become the active version.
To delete a previous version:
  1. Open the version history drop-down menu.
  2. Select the 3 dots beside the version you wish to revert to (e.g., V3).
  3. Select Delete.
To download a previous version:
  1. Open the version history drop-down menu.
  2. Select the 3 dots beside the version you wish to download.
  3. Select Download.

Collaborator and viewer comments

Videos can include two types of comments, depending on where the video is shared: collaborator comments on review links and viewer comments on public video pages. Read in detail about managing comments on your videos.

  • Comment type
  • Visibility
  • Purpose
  • Who can view or manage it
  • Collaborator
  • Private. Visible only on review links and within the video settings page.
  • Used for time-coded feedback during the editing and review process.
  • Team members with Can Edit access can resolve, download, or delete comments. Team members with Can Comment access can reply from the video settings page. If comments are enabled on a review link, anyone with that link can add or reply to comments.
  • Viewer
  • Public. Visible on the main video page.
  • Used for general audience feedback and engagement.
  • Anyone with Can View access can comment. Viewer comments can be locked or disabled from the video settings page.

Screenshot: A dropdown menu for setting access permissions, showing three options: Viewers (Can view), Collaborators (Can comment), and Can edit, along with a Remove access option.

Mentions and notifications

Mentions and notification preferences help manage collaboration and communication across team members and guests. Read in detail about mentioning someone in a comment.

  • Feature
  • Description
  • @ Mentions
  • Tag any team member or guest who has previously commented on the video.
  • Guest commenting
  • Guests must provide their name and email before posting feedback. This enables them to be mentioned in later comments.
  • Notification preferences
  • Choose comment notification settings for each video: All comments , Only mentions and replies , or None . Team members are opted in to notifications by default.

Making the most of version management

  • Track Feedback: You can see all collaborator comments that were left on any past version, even after restoring a video. This provides a complete audit trail.
  • Review Content: You can click to view any previous version to remind yourself of the content and context of that clip.
  • Clean Slates: Use the Restore function when a version is approved, as it gives you a clean comment slate on the new version (V5 for the client, for example) while fully preserving the V4 comments in history.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn how to configure and manage review links for your videos.
  • Learn how to share a folder for external review.

How to modify videos not originally created in the video editor

This article discusses how to edit videos on Vimeo, even if they weren’t originally created using Vimeo’s video editor, including guidance on modifying videos presented as a single scene. Note that time limitations may apply, depending on your account type. Read more at ‘About Vimeo Plans’.

To modify a video not created in the video editor:

  1. Select your video from your personal or team Library. Team members with modification rights will be able to edit videos. Learn about team member types at About team member types
  2. On the video settings page, select the Editing buttonon the left of the video represented by a pair of scissors.
  3. Select Video Editorto open the video in the video editor. Screenshot: Video editing menu with the ‘Video editor’ option highlighted.
  4. Your video will open in the video editor as a single scene. Use the split and trim tools in the video editor to divide it into multiple scenes.

⚠️Note:Videos not originally made with the video editor on Vimeo will appear as a single scene when opened in the video editor. You can split this single scene into multiple scenes using the split and trim tools. Learn how at ‘How to use the Timeline in the video editor

How to move folders

This feature is available to Enterprise account owners, admins, and contributors with ‘Folder admin’ permissions. It is also available to owners and admins on all other paid membership types; contributors on non-Enterprise plans may only move folders within their ‘My library’ space.

To move a folder to another location:

  1. Locate the folder you wish to move in either My library or Team library.
  2. Select the options menu (•••) that corresponds to the folder. This can be found in three places:
  • The left side navigation when you hover over the folder name.
  • The right side of the folder within the library workspace.
  • The upper left corner of the folder page.
  1. Select Move folder. Screenshot: A folder in a team library with the options menu open, highlighting the Move folder option in the menu.
  2. A modal window will open, showing the folders you can move your folder into. ⚠️Note: The locations that appear depend on your role and permissions on the Vimeo account. Contact your account owner or admin if you do not see the location where you wish to move your folder.
  3. Select the destination for your folder, then select Move.
  4. Your folder and all the content within it, including subfolders, will move to the selected destination. You will see a confirmation message at the bottom of the screen.

How to organize and customize folders

This article discusses how to organize your video library, from creating subfolders to customizing your folder’s settings.

What to know before organizing and customizing your folders

Folders function differently depending on your membership type:

  • For Free, Basic, and Plus members, folders are not shareable, linkable, or visible to anyone but the account owner since these tiers do not include additional team seats. If you’d like to create groupings of videos to share, you’ll want to make a showcase, group, or channel.
  • For all other plan types, folders serve as workspaces for collaboration. Contributor team members added to a folder can upload, manage, replace, and embed videos within that specific folder.

How to rename a folder

To rename your folder:

  1. Select Folder settings from the three dots icon to open a new modal window. Screenshot: A screenshot of a video library in dark mode, with a red arrow pointing to the three-dot options menu on a folder named “Sunshine.”
  2. Within Folder settings, you will be able to rename your folder. Screenshot: The “Folder settings” window for renaming a folder.

How to delete a folder

Choosing Delete will bring up a confirmation module to delete the folder, with the option to delete the videos within the folder as well.

To delete a video:

  1. Go to your Library. Click on the three dots icon.
  2. Select the delete folder option to delete your folder.
  3. You can also click the gear icon in the upper-right section of the page to open the folder settings modal window. Below the names of your team members who have folder access, you’ll find a Delete folder button; note that only the owner and account admins have the ability to delete folders.

⚠️Note: For Enterprise Accounts, to rename an Enterprise video’s folder, you can also go to your Video Library home page and click on the options menu (•••) to the right to edit the folder name to the desired one.

Subfolders

You can further organize the videos within your folders by making subfolders. To create a subfolder, navigate to one of your folders. In the upper right section of the page, click the (+) New Folder button to create and name your subfolder.

Please note the following about subfolders:

  • You can create subfolders up to 10 levels deep within the main parent folder.
  • All subfolders will inherit the permissions of the parent folder.
  • When the top-level folder is shared with a member of the team, they will also have access to the subfolders.
  • If a new subfolder is added to a folder after sharing the folder with a team member, that individual will also have access to the newly created subfolder.
  • Team owners and Admins can also share a subfolder separately from its parent folder if you want to restrict access to some of the content in the parent folder.

Sort folders in the library

To customize the order of folders and content displayed in your library, you can use the dropdown menu towards the left of the page.

Screenshot: The “Modified” sort button in the video library, highlighted with a red box.

  1. Select the dropdown menu next to Modified or Addedto sort your folders by date modified or added to your library.
  2. Use the arrow to the right to switch between descending and ascending dates.
  3. You can also move folders into other folders to better organize your content.

Folder breadcrumbs on the video page

You can see which folder and subfolder a video is located in at the top left corner of the video page. You can navigate to the folders from these links as well.

Suggested next steps

Now that your folders are organized, here’s what you can do next:

How to password-protect a video

You can set a password for your video to help control who can watch it. This article explains how to set and remove password protection for your videos.

What to know before password-protecting a video

  • Password-protected videos can be embedded anywhere, and viewers do not need a Vimeo account to watch them.
  • To compare all available privacy options, visit About video privacy settings.
  • For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: Privacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence.

How to password-protect a video

If you would like to require viewers to enter a password to view your video, follow these steps:

  1. Select the video from your Library to open the video page.
  2. Select Shareat the top of the video page. It’ll have an icon of your video’s current privacy setting.
  3. In the expanded menu, select the privacy drop-down menu and choose the Password option.
  4. Enter a password for your video.
  5. Only share your video password with people you want to access it.

How to remove password protection from a video

You can also remove password protection from your video. To do so:

  1. Select the video from your Library to open the video page.
  2. Select Shareat the top of the video page.
  3. In the expanded menu, select the privacy drop-down menu
  4. Select any other privacy setting that is not the Password setting (such as Unlisted or Public).
  5. Once a new setting is selected, the password will be removed.

How to position, align, and layer elements of interactive overlays

When creating an overlay within interactive, there are multiple tools within the overlay editor that allow you to cleanly lay out and align elements of your overlay. These include rulers, grids, and layers.

To use the layout tools:

To access, select the View menu at the top of the overlay editor,

Screenshot: Top of the overlay editor, showing the view menu open.

You can enable or disable the following:

  • Add Grid: You can display a grid within the editor to help keep equal distances between multiple elements. The grid will only appear in the editor and not on your public video.
  • Add Rulers:Enabling rulers will display a ruler in pixels for both the height and width of your video to help you measure the distance between objects on your overlay.
  • Snap to grid: When enabled, dragging a panel or object will snap it to the nearest grid line. This takes into account the current grid size and will snap to all four sides.

You can also choose the size of your grid (by pixels) by entering it in the Grid Sizebox. The larger the number, the larger the grid square.

You can change the color used for displaying your grid by selecting Grid Color. You can select the color from the color picker or input its HEX or RGB values. An optional alpha channel is available to set the opacity (0 for transparent - 100 for an opaque grid).

Screenshot: View menu open showing Grid color selected and a color selector open.

Layers:

In addition to adjusting the view of your overlay canvas, the Layers option helps you track all of your overlay’s elements and where they fall on the canvas.

To open the Layers window, select the Layers button at the bottom of the sidebar menu.

Screenshot: Overlay editor highlighting the layers menu in the lower right corner

Screenshot: Overlay editor showing the layer menu open with multiple layers within it.

In the Layers window, you can:

  • Select, drag, and drop elements to adjust where they fall in order (or select the arrow keys at the bottom to move that layer up or down).
  • Edit the names of each element to provide an internal name that will not be shown in your video.
  • Select the lock icon to prevent further edits to that element.
  • Duplicate an element.
  • Delete an element.

How to remove the Vimeo watermark from my video

This article explains how to remove Vimeo watermarks from videos for users with a paid membership.

Before you begin:

  • If you are on a Free or Basic plan, you cannot remove watermarks from your videos.
  • To remove watermarks, you need to upgrade to a paid Vimeo membership.

To remove the Vimeo watermark:

How to search your Library

To search your Library, use the search bar on the top left of the page. If the player icon is selected to the right of the search bar, the results will only contain your content. You can search for video titles, folder names, transcripts, and more. For Workspace users, search results are restricted to the particular Workspace in which they are operating.

  • View and filter all results

View and filter all results

If you press the Enter key or select View on the Library search page… in the search dropdown, you will be taken to ourVideo Library search results page.To the right, you will find the option to sort the results by overall relevance, alphabetically, date modified, date added, or duration.

You can filter your content by:

  • Type: Filter by content type, i.e. videos or folders

How to search your Library for transcript mentions

You can search your Library to find videos that mention your search term. Here’s how:

  1. Go to your Library and begin typing to populate the results dropdown.
  2. You can search for keywords or phrases within your video transcripts using the search bar.
  3. Results from within a transcript will be marked with a timestamp indicating when the term was mentioned.
  4. Select “See all Library results” to see all results that contain the search term. If a transcript contains the search term more than once, this will be reflected in the dropdown with the number of results within the video.
  5. Select the dropdown menu under a single video result to see all the timestamps in that video containing the search term.
  6. Once you select a result, you will be redirected to the viewing page for that video with playback starting at the relevant timestamp.

Read more about theunified search experience to easily access your videos.

How to select a regional accent for my video’s AI-dubbed audio

The feature discussed below requires an Enterprise plan and is gradually rolling out over the next few weeks. If you have questions on availability, please contact your account manager.

You can enhance your AI-translated videos by selecting specific accents and voices for your dubbed audio. This article explains how to choose from a variety of voices and regional accents when translating audio for your video.

What to know before translating

Before translating, take note of the following:

  • Voice Options: You can choose between two main types of voices:
  • Original Voice: This option uses AI to replicate the original speaker’s voice in the new, translated language. Sometimes, a cloned voice might not be available, especially for specific regional accents.
  • AI Voice: These are high-quality, pre-recorded voices from professional voice actors that you can use for your translations.
  • Previews: Before committing to a complete translation, you can generate a free audio preview to hear how your selected voice sounds.

How to select a regional accent for your AI-dubbed audio

You can choose an accent when you translate your video for supported languages. To do so:

  1. From your video’s settings page, select the Vimeo AI button on the left-side toolbar.

  3. Select audioand subtitlesand Continue.

  • The voice cloning feature is not yet available for all regional accents.
  1. Once you have made your selections, you can either:
  • Select Preview to generate a short, free sample of the dubbed video.
  • Select Translate to begin the translation and dubbing process for the entire video.
  1. Once complete, the translated and dubbed video will be available. The regional accent will be displayed in the Languages menu of your video’s settings, where you can add additional translations if needed.

You can also edit your dubbed audio. Visit How to edit the dubbed audio on my AI-translated video to learn how.

Set your upload default privacy settings

How to set regional availability for my videos

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

This article discusses setting the regional availability for your video on Vimeo. To learn how to set the geo-availability for your live event, visit How do I set regional availability for my live events?

  • What is regional availability?
  • Setting regional availability by country/region
  • Setting regional availability by US-based city or zip code
  • Setting regional availability using a .csv file
  • What will my viewers experience?

What is regional availability?

Setting a video’s regional availability (also known as geo-blocking or geo-allowing) allows publishers to restrict video access based on viewers’ locations. Location is typically based on the viewer’s IP address.

When configuring Regional Availability for your videos, you can:

  • Allow Locations: Specify where the video can be viewed.
  • Deny Locations: Specify the locations where the video cannot be viewed.

Regional Availability helps content owners:

  • Comply with licensing agreements: Ensure that your content is only viewed in regions where you have the rights to show it.
  • Protect content: Prevent unauthorized access to your videos.

You can set a video’s regional availability by region or country. Regional availability for cities and zip codes based in the United States is also supported.

Setting regional availability by country or region

Owners, Admins, and Contributor + team members can set and manage regional availability on the Vimeo website. These settings are not available on the Vimeo mobile app.

To set regional availability for a video:

  1. Visit the video’s settings page.
  2. Scroll to Availabilityand select Manageto open the Manage regional availability window.
  3. Use the dropdown menu to select whether you want to Block in specific regionsor Allow in particular regions.
  4. Select the checkmark next to each region or country to allow or block, depending on your setting type. You can also use the search bar to find specific countries and regions.
  5. Select Applyto apply the settings.

Setting regional availability by US-based cities or zip codes

You can also set regional availability by using zip codes. Support for city and zip/postal codes is currently limited to cities and zip codes based in the United States of America.

To set the regional availability for your video by city or zip code:

  1. In the Manage Regional Availabilitywindow, select the Worldicon.
  2. Select Enter US zip codes.
  3. Enter each 5-digit ZIP code and press Enter.
  • You can add multiple ZIP codes by separating them by commas (e.g., 10001, 10002, 10003). Press Enterto apply.
  1. Select Applyto save your settings.
  2. You can download your list of regions as a .csv file by selecting the download button at the bottom left of the window.

Setting regional availability using a .csv file

In addition, you can bulk allow or block regions using a .csv file. Learn how to format your file at ‘How do I format a .csv file to set regional availability for my video or live event?’

To import your .csv file.

  1. Select the Upload a CSV icon in the bottom-left corner in the’ Manage regional availability’ window.
  2. Select the CSV file from your device to upload.
  3. Review the imported data.
  4. Click “Apply” to save the settings.

What will viewers experience?

Viewers in geo-allowed regions can watch your video normally, without any indication that regional access restrictions have been applied.

Viewers in restricted regions cannot view your video. They will receive an error message that it is unavailable in their region. Read more at ‘What does “This video is not available in your region” mean?’

How to share a chapter

You can share a link to a chapter of your video so that the recipient can begin playback at the most relevant part of the video. Follow these steps to share a chapter:

  1. Go to your Library and select the video to open the video page.
  2. Select the chapter icon on the bottom right of the player.
  3. Select the link icon next to the chapter title that you would like to share.
  4. The link will be copied to your clipboard. You can then share this link with the recipient.
  5. Video playback will begin at the beginning of the shared chapter. In the example below, the last chapter was shared:

Additional information

  • If your video privacy is set to Embed only,chapter links will not function. Viewers who access a link to a chapter will see an error message.
  • It is not possible to disable chapter sharing, however, you may hide chapters from viewers by going to Player > Controls > toggle off Chapters on the video page. Read more at Customize the video player.

How to share a folder of videos for external review

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

You can share a folder externally so recipients that are not members of your team can review the content. This article discusses how to create and share a review link for your folder.

For more information about video review links refer to How to use and manage video review links.

  • How to share my folder for external review
  • What customization options are available for the review links?

How to share my folder for external review

You can create a flexible and distinct review link for your folder. To do so:

  1. From your folder page, navigate to Share on the top right and select the Review tab in the pop-up modal. You can also find the Share button in your Library by hovering over the folder and selecting the Share icon.
  2. Select New review link.
  3. Name your review link and apply your desired settings for your link.
  4. Select Create link at the bottom of the modal. You will be able to create multiple links for one folder and those links will be listed under the review tab where you can manage them.

⚠️Note:Folders must be located within Team Library in order to be shared. It is not possible to share folders located in My Library.

What customization options are available for the review links?

Expiration date

  • You can set a date for the review link for your folder to expire anytime in the future or you can disable the expiration altogether.

  • Note: The expiration setting for links defaults to 30 days until it is changed or disabled.

Password protection

  • You have the choice to enable password protection for your review link.

Link permissions

  • You are able to manage recipient access for the following functions for videos within the folder: commenting, video downloads, adjusting the review page status, viewing resolved comments, and viewing previous versions of the video.

Appearance

How to share a segment of a video

  • How to share a video segment
  • How to share a link to start playback at a specific time

How to share a video segment

To share a video segment you can use thestart time andend time parameters together. If you share a video URL amended with both parameters, the recipient can view the video clip on its own, with the option to switch to watching the full video.

Example: By adding #t=1m30s&end=3m10s to the URL, after the video ID and before &share=copy, the link automatically triggers playback to begin 1 minute and 30 seconds into the video and end at 3 minutes and 10seconds.

https://vimeo.com/01234567890#t=1m30s&end=3m10s&share=copy

On the shared segment page, you can hover over the video player and select Watch full videoto be redirected to the full video page, which will retain the original embed settings.

The viewer can hover over the video player again and selectBack to clip to go back to the originally shared segment.

How to share a link to start playback at a specific time

To share a video link that will begin playback at a specific point, you can add the start time parameter end of the URL. Add #t= followed by the timecode of where you’d like playback to begin.

Example: By adding #t=1m42s to the URL, after the video ID and before &share=copy, the link automatically triggers playback to begin 1 minute and 42 seconds into the video.

https://vimeo.com/01234567890#t=1m42s&share=copy

How to share a video from the video page

You can share videos directly by email or by copying the link. To share using this method, make sure you are on the video page.

To learn about managing access to your videos, see How to share my video or How to share videos with your team.

How to share a video from the video page

Follow these steps to learn how to share a video with people on your team, people you’re following, or anyone else.

  1. From the video page onvimeo, select the Share button underneath the player.
  2. A modal will open with options for sharing and embedding. Start typing an email address in the dialogue box labeled Send the link.If you are on a team account, you can search for team members by name or group.
  • You may alternatively choose to use the Copy linkbutton to save the link to your clipboard. You can then paste the link in a message, email, or social media post to share it.
  • If permitted by the video owner, you can copy the embed code from this modal as well.
  1. Once you have entered the email address(s) you would like to share the video with you have the option to add a custom message.
  2. Select Send link to send the email.
  3. The recipient will receive the shared link via email. They will be able to click through the email to open the shared video page.

How to share a Vimeo video via mobile web

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can share a Vimeo video directly from your mobile browser without using the Vimeo app. This method allows you to copy the video link or share it using your device’s built-in sharing tools (such as Messages, Mail, or social apps).

  • Before you begin
  • Steps to share a Vimeo video via mobile web
  • Notes on privacy settings
  • Next steps

Before you begin

  • You do not need to be logged in to share a public video.
  • Private or password-protected videos can only be shared if you have access to them and if sharing is allowed in the video’s privacy settings.

Steps to share a Vimeo video via mobile web

  1. Open your mobile browser and go to vimeo.
  2. Locate the video you want to share.
  3. Once the video loads, tap the Share icon.
  4. A share menu will open with available options:
  • Copy Link: Copies the video’s URL to your clipboard.
  • Share via: Opens your device’s native share options (e.g., WhatsApp, Messages, Mail, AirDrop, etc.).

Choose your preferred method and complete the share using your selected app or tool.

Notes on privacy settings

  • If the video is set to private or password protected, recipients must have permission or the correct password to view it.
  • If you are the video owner, ensure your privacy settings allow sharing before sending the link.

Next steps

Read more about sharing and managing video via the Vimeo mobile app.

How to share my video

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

This article discusses the different methods you can use to share your video

  • How to share your video
  • Suggested next steps

How to share your video

Follow the steps below to share your video

  1. Select the video from your library to open the video settings page.
  2. Select the Share button in the top right corner of the page.
  3. A modal will appear on the right with options for sharing, embedding, and changing the privacy settings for your video.
  4. Select theCopy link button to copy the link and to share your video. 💡Tip: Hold CtrlandVkeys on a PC or Command (⌘)andVkeys on a Mac to paste a link.

Additional information

With a StarterorProplan orhigher, you can also share videos by email. If you would like to share an individual video with a team member, see How to share videos with your team. You may also share a video from the video page.

Suggested next steps

Now that you have shared your video, you might also want to:

  • Learn how to manage your privacy settings.
  • know how to track your video’s analytics to see where your views are coming from.

How to share videos with different privacy settings

You can share your videos with any privacy setting. The following rules apply based on the privacy setting:

  • Unlisted: Viewers can watch your video embedded on another website or with the unlisted vimeo link.
  • Password: Viewers can watch your video embedded on another website or the vimeo video page after entering the video’s password.
  • If you are a Basic or Free user, you must upgrade to a paid membership to password-protect your videos.
  • Embed only: Viewers can watch your video embedded on another website, but the vimeo video page will only be visible to you (as the video owner).
  • Private: Only you (the video owner) and your team members can watch your video embedded on another website or the internal video edit page.
  • All other viewers will be prompted to log in, and they will only have access to watch the video if you’ve added them to your team.
  • Password (shared via social or embedded): You need to provide the password to your recipients directly.
  • Password (shared via the Share button on vimeo): The password is included in the email to your chosen recipients.
  • Anyone at [Company] (Vimeo Enterprise only)
  • Anyone who is a member of your organisation and has the link can watch your video after logging in. Viewers don’t need to be individually invited — they only need to authenticate with their company account (via SSO or email and password).
  • Videos with this setting do not appear in search results or in your teammates’ Shared with Me folder until they open the link for the first time
  • This setting applies to videos and live events, but not to showcases or other content types.

💡Tip: You can also create review links to securely share your videos for feedback.

How to share videos with your team

This feature requires a Pro, Premium, Starter, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

As an Owner, Admin, Folder Admin, or Contributor on a team account (including Enterprise accounts with Workspaces), you can share videos with your team regardless of their folder permissions. You can also share videos with new team members, which will trigger an email to invite them to your team. Viewers can share videos from the video page.

Refer to How to share my video if you are trying to share your video with anyone who is not part of your team.

How to share a video with a team member

  1. Select the video you would like to share from your Library and then select Share. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-09-18 at 6.30.06 PM.png
  2. A new modal will appear on the right side with options for sharing, embedding, and changing the privacy settings for your video.
  3. Select Add people.Add your team member’s name or the email of a new team member. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-10-10 at 1.34.44 PM.png
  4. Choose their permission level from the dropdown menu: Can manage, Can view, or Can comment.
  5. Check or uncheck the box to decide whether you want to send an email notification to them.
  6. Click on share.
  7. As an Owner, Admin, Folder Admin, or Contributor on a team account, you can share with any existing team member by entering their name, group, or email address.
  8. Shared videos will appear in the team member’sShared with mefolder. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-09-30 at 3.06.00 PM.png

⚠️Note:When you invite a new team member using the Sharemodal they will receive an email with a direct link to the video.

💡Tip: To share multiple videos at the same time, add your team member as an Admin or Contributor.

How to tell if a video on Vimeo was generated with or enhanced by using AI

To balance creators’ innovative use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and viewers’ demands for transparency regarding the authenticity of the content they consume, we require creators to disclose when they use altered or synthetic media, including generative AI, in realistic videos.

After a creator discloses content that has been meaningfully altered or synthetically generated, a label will appear on the video page:

Screenshot: Vimeo video player interface for a video titled ‘Neighborhood’. The video has ‘Mature’ and ‘Includes AI’ tags. A tooltip explains the AI tag, stating ‘This video contains content that has been edited or generated using AI’.

On embedded videos, a label will appear in the video player:

Screenshot: A Vimeo video player showing a person at a snowy mountain basecamp. A banner at the top reads, ‘This video contains content that has been edited or generated using AI.’

⚠️Note:If a creator disables the display of their video’s title in an embedded player, the message stating that the footage contains AI content will not appear.

If you are a video creator, visit How to label my videos to indicate they contain AI-generated content to learn how to label your videos.

How to transcode and export from Compressor

You can transcode and export videos from Apple Compressor. This article discusses how to prepare your video for Vimeo using Compressor.

If you want to upload your video in Dolby Vision using Compressor, our partners at Dolby have a tutorial available at ‘How-To: Dolby Vision Encoding - Apple Compressor for Vimeo’.

  • How to prepare my video for Vimeo using Compressor
  • Compressor settings overview

How to prepare my video for Vimeo using Compressor

We have recommended specific settings below, however, we can’t guarantee that these settings or navigational steps are up-to-date or applicable to any third-party software. Always keep our main video and audio compression guidelines in mind and refer to Apple’s user guide for Compressor.

You can prepare your video within Compressor. To do so:

  1. If you imported your video into Compressor directly from Final Cut Pro, it should already be preloaded into the main window. Otherwise, import your file by clicking Add File in the lower panel. (Alternatively, you can navigate to File > Add File… Select your video file, then click Add.)
  2. Navigate to Window > Show Settings & Locations. (If the settings/locations menu is already shown, you can skip this step.)
  3. In the bottom-left corner, click the “+” symbol and select “New Setting.” Read about creating custom settings from Apple at ‘Create custom settings in Compressor’.
  4. In the Format dropdown, select MPEG-4. Give the setting a Name (for example: “Vimeo Export”) and a Description (e.g., “Export setting for Vimeo”). Then, click OK.
  5. In the settings panel on the left-hand side, select your new preset.
  6. On the right-hand side of the screen, under the General tab, choose the options shown at the bottom of this article. ⚠️Note: If the General tab is not appearing, select the equalizer icon ().
  7. Select the options under the Video tab as shown in the tables below (Video Properties, Cropping & Padding, Quality).
  8. Skip the Video Effectssection.
  9. Under the Audio tab, select the options in the table below (you can skip this step if your video does not contain audio).
  10. Skip theAudio Effects section.
  11. Your export preset is now ready. Choose Add next to the filename to apply your preset. Then select a destination on your computer to export your file to (such as your Desktop).
  12. You can also drag the Vimeo Export preset over your file to apply it.
  13. Once you’re ready, click Start Batch to begin the export process. You can watch the progress of your compression job in the Active tab.
  14. Once the compression process has finished, view your finished file to make sure it looks and sounds correct, and upload it to Vimeo via your web browser.

Compressor settings overview

  • General

  • Name

  • Leave as-is

  • Description

  • Leave as-is

  • Default location

  • None

  • Format

  • Video and Audio

  • Optimize for network use

  • Unchecked

  • Set duration to

  • 100% of source

  • Video Properties

  • Frame Size Vimeo uses some unique calculations to determine the available playback qualities for your video. Read how at ’ Determining playback resolution ’.

  • Choose your desired frame size from the list under “Manual.” If you aren’t sure what frame size to use, choose “Automatic.”

  • Pixel aspect ratio

  • Square

  • Frame rate You can enter a custom frame rate by choosing Automatic and entering your new frame rate value to the right of the dropdown. There are some situations where you’ll want to choose a frame rate different from the source: If your frame rate is higher than 60 FPS : Choose a factor of your frame rate that is between 15-60 FPS. For example, if your frame rate is 100 FPS, choose 60 FPS. If your frame rate is lower than 15FPS : Choose a multiple of your frame rate that is between 15-30 FPS. For example, if your frame rate is 8 FPS, choose 16 FPS. If you upload a frame rate that is higher than 60 FPS or lower than 15 FPS, Vimeo will automatically adjust the frame rate for you. However, we can’t guarantee the results will always look as expected. It’s best to do the conversion on your end prior to uploading.

  • Under “Manual,” choose your source video’s native frame rate. If you aren’t sure which frame rate to use, choose “Automatic.”

  • Field order (if applicable)

  • For HD footage, choose “High.” For SD footage, choose “Main.”

  • Entropy mode

  • Keyframe interval

  • Automatic

  • Data rate These data rates are suggested for average video files. If your video contains below-average visual complexity (such as a slideshow presentation), choose a lower data rate. If your video contains above-average visual complexity (such as a video with high levels of grain), increase the data rate. Remember: Lower data rates lead to smaller file sizes and faster uploads! Experiment to pick the lowest data rate that yields acceptable image quality.

  • Custom. Use the slider to choose a value appropriate for your video. SD 2000 – 5000 kbps 720p 5000– 10,000 kbps 1080p 10000 – 20000 kbps 2K 20000 – 30000 kbps 4K 30000 – 60000 kbps 8K 50000 – 80000 kbps

  • Multi-pass

  • Unchecked

  • Checked

  • 360 Metadata

  • For standard, non-360 videos, set this value to “None” For 360 (e.g., spherical) videos that do not already have video metadata, set this value to “Spherical V1” or ” Spherical V2”. Read about working with 360 metadata from Apple at ’ View 360° video metadata using Compressor ’

How to translate subtitles and dub videos in bulk

You can generate AI subtitle translations and dubbed audio for multiple videos at once directly from your Vimeo Library. This lets you apply language translations across your entire library in a single action, instead of processing each video individually.

Who can use this feature

Subtitle translation in bulk: Available to any user who already has access to Vimeo AI subtitle translation.

Dubbing in bulk: Available to team members on select Vimeo Enterprise plans.

Translate subtitles for multiple videos

  1. In your Library, switch to list view or grid view.
  2. Check the box on the left side of each video thumbnail you want to include. To select all videos in a folder, click the folder and then select all.
  3. In the bulk actions toolbar that appears at the top of the page, select Translate subtitles.
  4. Choose one or more destination languages from the list.
  5. Select Start.

Vimeo AI will generate the subtitle translations in the background. You’ll receive a notification when they’re complete, and the translated subtitles will appear in the Languages section of each video’s settings.

Translate and dub multiple videos

  1. In your Library, check the box on the left side of each video you want to translate and dub, or open a folder and select all videos inside it.
  2. In the bulk actions toolbar, select Translate and dub.
  3. Choose one or more destination languages from the list.
  4. Select Start.

The translated subtitles and dubbed audio tracks will be generated in the background and added to each video automatically.

Note: Dubbing uses Vimeo AI credits. The number of credits used depends on the number of videos and the number of languages selected.

Things to know

We recommend reviewing AI-generated translations for accuracy. To edit a subtitle translation, open the video’s settings, select Languages, and click the translated track.

If you edit the original transcript of a video after generating translations, you’ll need to update each translated track manually — they won’t update automatically.

There is no limit on how many videos you can process in a single bulk action. For very large libraries, we recommend processing in chunks — for example, selecting one folder at a time. If you experience very slow performance, contact your Customer Success Manager or reach out to Support and we can run the operation on your behalf.

Please note that AI dubbing will only be editable for 30 days after creation.

For a full list of supported languages, see About supported languages for Vimeo AI’s subtitle translations.

Enterprise users can also use the Vimeo AI API to process videos programmatically. This approach is ideal for system integrators, content delivery platforms, and teams building custom workflows that need to translate or dub at scale.

How to upload and display a custom logo

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

This article discusses how to upload and display a custom logo.

With Vimeo paid plans, you have the option to upload and display your custom logo in the embedded video player. With a Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise plan, you can also display the logo on your embedded live events.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: Custom logos can be managed at the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings or How to edit my Workspace’s settings.

  • Upload your custom logo via the video settings page
  • Add or remove your logo from the video player
  • Custom logo for live events

Upload your custom logo via the video settings page

  1. When you select Custom logo while customizing the player for your video, you will see an option to upload a logo.
  2. Select any video from your Library, then select Appearanceon the left side.
  3. Under theCustomization menu, toggle the Custom logo. Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-09-02 at 12.44.34 PM.png
  4. A new modal will appear in the lower left corner. Select the Uploadbutton to upload an image file. We recommend a PNG file that is at least 200x200 pixels in size. Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-02-08 at 12.02.02 PM.png
  5. Although you upload the logo via one particular video, you can later use this logo on other videos on your account.

Note: Consider the following points while uploading a custom team logo:

  • If available, please prefer brandmarks over wordmarks.
  • If available, please use logo files with transparent backgrounds.
  • Recommended aspect ratio for logo: 1:3 >> square >> 3:1.

Add or remove your logo from the video player

  1. To add the custom logo you uploaded to the video player, select the desired video from your Library.
  2. On the video settings page, select the Appearancebutton.
  3. In the menu that opens up, toggle on or off the Custom logooption to choose whether your logo appears in the lower right corner of the player. Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-09-02 at 12.44.34 PM.png
  4. If you’ve uploaded more than one logo, you can click on the logo and use the arrows to switch between the images and choose the desired logo.

💡 Tip: If you want to add your custom logo to all of your existing videos, you can create an embed preset and bulk apply it to all of your videos. Read more at ‘Customize the video player’.

The logo will only appear on videos embedded on another website.

Custom logo for live events

Vimeo Premium, Advanced, and Enterprise members can include their custom logo on the live video player via the live broadcast settings page.

  1. On the live settings page, select the Appearance tab in the upper left corner.
  2. Scroll down to the Customization section, then toggle on the Display custom logo switch.
  3. When your logo is selected, you can also choose whether you want the logo displayed during playback and whether you want the logo to link to another URL, which you can input below the setting.
  4. When you share the event link or embed your live event, the logo will appear in the lower right corner of the player.

How to upload or select media for my video in the Vimeo mobile apps

Access to the Stock library is available with a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise account. Users on Free and Starter accounts who joined before July 17, 2024, also have access to the Stock library. Compare plan features at ’Compare Vimeo plans’

You can upload or select videos or photos to use as footage in the Create app for Android and iOSor the Vimeo Android app and Vimeo iOS app.

Create supports these file formats:

You can upload photos and videos from your mobile device, use stock footage, select media from Google Photos, or record live footage from your device’s camera or screen (iOS only).

Add a new scene with photos or videos:
