  2. Click on the Import button on your Vimeo homepage. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-08-13 at 3.19.05 PM.png
  3. Find Dropbox in the list of applications and click Connect Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-08-13 at 7.51.14 PM.png
  4. When prompted, log in to Dropbox and click Allow. Your Dropbox account will now be connected to Vimeo.
  5. Select the Dropbox folder where your videos will automatically upload to Vimeo.
  6. Select your team and folder where your Dropbox videos will automatically upload to. We will create a new Dropbox Recordingsfolder if you don’t have one.
  7. From this point on, any video files added to this directory will be automatically uploaded to your Vimeo account.

Please note:

  • Videos that exceed your account’s allotted storage will not appear on your Vimeo account.
  • Only videos in the root folder on Dropbox will be uploaded. Videos contained within subfolders will not be recognized for upload. If you’d like to upload from a subfolder, you’ll need to select that folder for automatic uploading within your account settings (apps).
  • If your videos are not transferring, try disconnecting/reconnecting to Dropbox in your Vimeo account settings, and then rename or remove/replace the video files in your auto-upload directory.If you continue to have trouble, don’t hesitate to contact us.

How to upload videos using the Vimeo mobile app

You can upload a video to your Vimeo account using the Vimeo iOS app or the Vimeo Android app. Videos uploaded through the app count towards your account’s number of videos or storage allowance.

This article discusses how to upload videos to your Vimeo account by using the Vimeo mobile apps. If you are searching for instructions on how to upload a video to the Vimeo website by using your computer, visit How to upload a video to Vimeo.

  • Upload using the Vimeo iOS app
  • Upload using the Vimeo Android app

Upload using the Vimeo iOS app

To upload a video on the Vimeo mobile app (iOS):

  1. From the Vimeo app homepage, select the “New Video” button - a blue rectangle with a black plus sign in the middle.
  2. Select Upload.
  3. Select the video that you would like to upload. 💡Tip: If Vimeo hasn’t accessed your camera roll previously, you’ll be prompted to allow this here and can later manage it in Settings. Read more from Apple Support at ’Control access to information in apps on iPhone/iPad’.
  4. After selecting a file to upload, you can give it a title, description, and set privacy settings. Use the Trim tool to remove unwanted sections by dragging handles on either side of the video.
  5. Select the Savebutton to upload your video to your Library.

Upload using the Android app

To upload a video using the Vimeo mobile app (Android).

  1. From the Vimeo app homepage, select the “New Video” button - a blue rectangle with a black plus sign in the middle.
  2. Select Upload a video from the menu.
  3. Select the video that you would like to upload. 💡Tip:If you have not given the Vimeo app access to your photos and videos on your device, you will be prompted to do so here. This can later be managed in the Appsmenu on your device. Learn how from Google Support at Change app permissions on your Android phone.
  4. Trim the beginning and end of the video if necessary by holding and dragging the blue handles on either side of the video.
  5. Select Done.
  6. Provide a title, a description, which folder you would like to save your video to, and set its privacy settings.
  7. Select Uploadto upload your video.

How to use a template in the video editor

Templates in the video editor provide a pre-designed framework, ensure professionalism with high-quality visuals, and offer customization options to add a personal touch.

Templates can also inspire creativity, simplify the editing process, and provide an accessible starting point for beginners.

Vimeo Enterprise users can also Team templates to maintain brand consistency. Read more at What are Team Templates? (Enterprise)

To use a template in your video:

  1. In the video editor, select Templates from the left-side panel.
  2. Browse templates by theme, search for a specific template, or filter by category or aspect ratio using the dropdown menus. 💡Tip:If you are part of an Enterprise team, select the Team Templates tab to view your team’s templates.
  3. To preview additional options, hover over the thumbnail image for the template and select the expand button in the upper right corner.

Templates are made up of multiple scenes. You can either add an individual scene by selecting the blue plus sign in the top-left corner of a theme thumbnail or select Use all scenes to add all scenes in a template to your video.

Screenshot: ‘Use all 6 scenes’ button displayed above a template set with customizable scenes for text and images.

⚠️Note: If you add a template to your video, any elements on your current timeline will be replaced with scenes in the template.

How to use AI to generate a script in the Record Studio

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

This article discusses how users with a paid Vimeo plan can utilize AI to create customized teleprompter scripts in the Record Studio. To do so:

  1. Select theTeleprompter button from the input control toolbar in the Record Studio to open the Teleprompter window.

  2. Select the AI Sparkles button in the lower-right corner of the teleprompter window.

  3. The AI panel will expand. You can select from pre-generated examples such as a product testimonial or training on a new feature. You can also type what you would like to AI to write a script about in the textbox.

  4. You can further customize your script by choosing the Duration—short, medium, or long—and selecting the Tone, such as Confident, Funny, Direct, Inspiring, Casual,or Formal.

  5. After selecting the duration and tone of your script, select the Generatebutton to use AI to generate the script.

  6. After your script is generated, you can choose to make the script longer, shorter, or try again with a new script.

  7. You can also make edits manually in the textbox.

  8. When you are happy with your script, select the Xbutton in the top-right corner of the teleprompter window. Begin recording your video to run the teleprompter.

⚠️Note: You cannot share your screen while using the teleprompter, as the teleprompter will appear in your final video.

To read about using the teleprompter, visit ‘How do I use the teleprompter in the Record Studio?’

💡Tip: Admins of Teams and Workspacescan control access to this feature for their team members through the Vimeo AI settings menu. For additional details, visit the ’About the Vimeo AI settings’ page.

How to use and manage video review links

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

Review Links offer a robust way to share videos for time-coded feedback and allows you to receive feedback for your videos on a custom review page that you can create for multiple recipients. This feature allows the seamless sharing of a review page with anyone, even those without a Vimeo account or a team seat, making the process of gathering precise and secure feedback straightforward.

  • What to know before you start
  • How to create and manage review links
  • To create a review link
  • To set an expiration date for a review link
  • To set a password for a review link
  • To set permissions and disable downloads
  • To save and share the review links
  • To manage a review link
  • To disable a review link
  • To change a link’s settings
  • To share the link with a Vimeo team member
  • Making the most of review links
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before you start

  • Purpose: Review Links are primarily for collecting private, time-coded feedback from collaborators.
  • Access: Review Links can be created for any video right from the Share panel on the Video Settings page.
  • Customization: You can create multiple review links for a single video, each with unique settings (e.g., one link allows download, another does not).
  • Guest Commenting: When a guest uses a review link, they are prompted to provide their name and email before posting feedback, which allows them to be mentioned in later comments.
  • Video Privacy:Your video’s privacy is not tied to the review links, meaning the recipient of the link will be able to view the video regardless of the video’s individual privacy.

How to create and manage review links

To get feedback on your video, you first have to create a review link. To do so:

To create a review link:
  1. Navigate to the Video Settings page for your video.
  2. Click the Share icon in the upper-right corner.
  3. Click on Create review linksfrom the window.
  4. Enter a descriptive Link name and configure other related settings as described below.
  5. Select Create link. Screenshot: The “Create review link” configuration screen showing fields for Link name, Expiration, Password, viewer permissions like Comment and Download, Appearance toggles, and the ‘Create link’ button highlighted.
To set an expiration date for a review link:
  1. In the Create Review Link window, click on the Expiration field.
  2. Select the specific date and time you want the link to stop working.

This ensures access is automatically revoked after your review deadline has passed.

To set a password for a review link:
  1. In the Create Review Link window, locate the Password field.
  2. Toggle the switch on to enable a password.
  3. Enter your desired password. Recipients will need to enter this to view the review page.
To set permissions and disable downloads:

In the Create Review Link window, under “What can people with this link do?”, you can configure recipient permissions.

  • To disable downloads: Ensure the Download option is toggled off.
  • To enable commenting: Ensure the Comment option is toggled on.
  • To enable status changes: Toggle the Change status option on. This allows reviewers to mark the video as Approved.
  • To view the history: Toggle the ‘View previous versions’ option on.
To save and share the review links:
  1. Click the Create link at the bottom of the configuration window.
  2. The new link will appear in the Share panel. Click the Copy link icon next to it to get the URL for sharing.
To manage a review link:
  1. Click on the Share button of your video.
  2. Select Manage review linksfrom the Share window to reconfigure your review link.
To disable a review link:
  1. Select Share > Manage review links.
  2. You can manually expire any active link by toggling the switch next to it off in the Share panel.
To change a link’s settings:
  1. Select Share > Manage review links.
  2. Select the version you would like to configure in the Review linkspanel.
  3. Click Manage. Screenshot: Review links” screen showing the creation date, expiration date, a ‘Copy link’ button, a link icon, a three-dot menu, and a toggle switch.
To share the link with a Vimeo team member:
  1. Select Add people from the Sharepanel.
  2. Enter the name/email address of your team members.

This sends them an email invitation and gives them direct comment access based on their team role.

Making the most of review links

  • Custom Branding: In the link creation window, use the Appearance settings to replace the Vimeo logo with your team’s logo for a professional, branded review experience.
  • Easy Review: Recipients can play the video, view all time-coded comments on the timeline, and jump to specific points of feedback by clicking a comment.
  • Guest Tagging: Guests who have previously left feedback on the video can be @ mentioned in future comments for seamless communication.

Suggested next steps

  • Ensure the Comment permission is always enabled if you need specific, time-coded feedback.
  • Use the Version Management tools to replace the clip with a new edit once you’ve collected all your feedback.
  • Learn how to share a folder for external reviews.

How to use chapters

This feature requires a Pro, Business, Premium, Starter, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

Chapters are ideal for long-form content like lessons, training sessions, sermons, recitals, sports games, and narrative storytelling. Adding chapters helps your viewer create a self-guided viewing experience and allows them to easily navigate to relevant segments to find content faster.

You’ll also be able to see which chapters get the highest engagement and track engagement rates by chapter. This article discusses how to add and edit chapters.

  • What to know before using chapters
  • How to add chapters to my video
  • How to edit chapters
  • How to remove chapters
  • Can I view chapters on mobile?
  • About analytics for chapters

What to know before using chapters

  • One Vimeo video has a limit of 80 chapters.
  • Chapter titles are limited to 50 characters.
  • Chapters are restricted to the Vimeo player and won’t function on any other publishing site.

How to add chapters to my video

You can add chapters that will appear during the playback of your embedded videos and in showcases, as well as on Vimeo.com. To do so:

  1. Select the video from your Library to open the video settings page.
  2. Select theInteractive tab to the left of the video player. Then, choose Chapters.
  3. Under the Chapters section, select + Add a chapter.
  4. You can name your chapter by selecting the options menu (…)to the right.
  5. After selecting the options menu (…) you may enter the new title.
  6. Select Add chapter to keep going. You can add up to one chapter per second to your video.
  7. Once you’re done adding your chapters, select the Save button.

💡Tip:You can hover over chapter segments to see timestamps and chapter titles.

How to edit chapters

You can edit an existing chapter after it has been created. To do so:

  1. Select the options menu (…)next to the chapter name.
  2. Edit the name or timestamp of the chapter.
  3. Select Closeto save your settings and close the menu.

How to remove chapters

You can delete chapters from the same menu where you edit existing chapters.

  1. In the Edit Chaptermenu, select the trash icon in the top right corner of the modal that appears.
  2. The chapter will be deleted as soon as you select the trash icon.

💡Tip:Replacing a videowith a shorter one will delete all chapters and timestamps that come after the end of the new video. However, if the replacement video has the same length as the original, the chapters and timestamps will remain.

Can I view chapters on mobile?

Chapters are only supported on a Desktop viewing experience. The chapter markers aren’t visible on mobile devices and iPads; only the chapters menu is.

About analytics for chapters

To see analytics on a video, select the graph icon in the top right corner of the video page. Chapters appear withinviewer retention stats so that you can see which chapters your users are engaging with the most.

The chapters are shown along the video playbar, and the viewer retention graph shows viewership at each second of the video. By comparing the peaks in the graph with your chapter markers, you can see what percentage of viewers are being retained for each chapter.

You can read more about analytics at Advanced Analytics.

How to use community groups

Free and Basic accounts are limited to one group. Unlimited groups are available with paid plans. This feature is not available in some regions.

Community groups are mini-communities within Vimeo that allow members to share, discuss, and collaborate on videos with each other.

If you’re looking for help on SSO Groups on Enterprise accounts, see SSO Group permissions for Enterprise teams.

  • Access and create groups
  • Configure group settings
  • Add a video to a group
  • Remove a video from a group
  • Invite people to your group
  • Join or leave a group
  • Transfer group ownership
  • Delete a group
  • Group albums
  • Troubleshoot adding videos to groups

Access and create community groups

To access your groups, click on your profile picture in the top right corner and hover over Watch. Then, select Collections from the list. To create a group, head to the groups page and click Create a Group, then follow the steps to customize it to your liking.

Configure community group settings

You can configure your group’s settings by clicking Settingsfrom your group page, then editing the fields to your liking. Click Save Changes when you’re done.

To make your group private, follow these steps:

  1. Click Settingson your group page
  2. Go to the Membership tab.
  3. Under Group Privacy Settings you can choose to make your group visible to anyone or limit it to members of the group.

Note: If you opt to make your group private, anyone who’s not a member of the group who navigates to it will see a message stating that this is a private group that they do not have permission to view. This privacy setting will also hide the group from your profile page.

Add a video to a community group

Once you’ve created your group, you can add videos to it by following these steps:

  1. Navigate to the video settings page for the video you’d like to add to your group.
  • Or, from your Library, select the three dots (…) on the right-side of the screen and choose Share.
  1. Select the Share button on the top right side of the page. This will open the Share panel.
  2. Choose Publish button at the bottom of the side panel.
  3. Select Group. Screenshot: Publish panel with group highlighted.
  4. Check the groups that you’d like to add your video to.
  5. Select Confirm.

⚠️Note: You can add each of your videos to a maximum of 10 groups.

⚠️Note: If you’ve applied privacy settings to your individual videos, the group privacy generally overrides the video’s privacy setting, with the exception of videos marked Unlisted or Embed only, which will not be visible in a group. Videos with all other privacy settings will show in the group.

Remove a video from a community group

To remove a video from a group, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the video’s page.
  2. Select the Share button on the top right side of the page. This will open the Share panel.
  3. Choose Publish button at the bottom of the side panel.
  4. Select Group.
  5. Uncheck the groups you would like to remove that video from.

Note: If a video that was previously removed is added back to a group, the video will return to its original spot in the group. For example, if your group is sorted by Most Recent, the video’s placement will be based on the time it was originally added, not the time you re-added it.

Invite people to your community group

You can invite people to your group by clicking Invite on your group’s homepage. Then add people by Vimeo screen name or email address.

Note: If you are a new Basic member, you have to wait 3 months before inviting other users to join your group.

Join or leave a community group

To find groups you may want to join, you can check out the Group Directory or peruse the Groups page. If you no longer want to be in a group, simply click Leave Group from that group’s homepage.

Transfer community group ownership

If you are the moderator of a group and decide to leave the group, you will need to transfer ownership to another moderator or group member. If you don’t, the group will be orphaned. To transfer ownership to another user, go to your Group Settings, then click the Ownershiptab.

Delete a group

To delete a group, go to the Settings tab and click Delete this group. The group will be permanently removed from Vimeo.

Community group albums

You can organize the videos within your group using albums. You can create a group album if you’re a moderator for that group.

To create a group album, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the settings page for your group and navigate to the Videotab.
  2. Click the Manage your group Albums link.
  3. Click Create a New Albumbutton under the green Browse Albumsheading.

If you organize your group videos into Albums, you can choose the order in which you’d like them to appear. To do so, follow these steps:

  1. Go to your group’s settings and click Manage your group Albumsin the Videos tab.
  2. Click the gear icon to go to Settings.
  3. Choose from the dropdown menu how you’d like to arrange your videos.
  • If you choose Manually, drag and drop up to 100 videos in any order you want and save your changes.

Troubleshoot adding videos to community groups

If you’re having trouble adding your video to a specific group, here are some tips:

  • Make sure you’re logged in to your account and verify that you are indeed a member of the group. For team accounts, only Owners and Admins can add videos to groups.
  • Check the Privacy Settings of your video to make sure you have enabled it to be added to collections like Groups, Channels, and Albums. Keep in mind you can add your video to a maximum amount of 10 groups!
  • ⚠️Note: If viewers are located in the United Kingdom or European Union and are not logged into a Vimeo account, they will be prompted to log in to watch an unrated video or a video rated “Mature” on vimeo.com.
  • Finally, take into consideration the Privacy Settings for the group itself. Certain moderators choose not to allow other people to add videos to their group. Other groups require that a moderator approve videos before they actually show up on the group page.

How to use Enterprise data retention tool

This feature requires an Enterprise account.

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

You can use the Data Retention tool to set schedules to delete content according to the policies you create. This article discusses how to create new policies and apply them to your folders and groups.

  • Data retention tool overview
  • How to create a data retention policy
  • Applying policies to folders and groups overview
  • Making the most out of applying a policy
  • About overlapping data retention policies
  • How to review the policy summary
  • How to edit a data retention policy
  • Recovering a video and Viewing History overview

Data retention tool overview

To access the data retention tool, Enterprise Account owners and admins should navigate to the Settings tab within your team management page.

Screenshot: Data retention settings page

On the data retention policy page, you can see a list of all the retention policies created in the account. The following information is included in this list:

  • The duration of the retention policy schedule (days, months, years)
  • The date the policy was created on
  • The status (if the policy is enabled or disabled). Here, you can toggle this on or off
  • The default policy is specified (Note: you can only set one policy as your default)

Select “Details” to see the title, description, and folders/groups to which the policy has been applied. You can now create a new policy or edit an existing one.

How to create a data retention policy

Screenshot: Create a new retention policy page

  1. Navigate to the data retention page within your team management settings.
  2. Select Create policy to open the data retention wizard.
  3. Enter your policy details. This includes the policy name, description (optional), and schedule duration (months, days, or years). 💡Tip: The duration is the number of days, months, or years after the video has been uploaded on Vimeo when you would like it to be deleted.
  4. You also have the option to specify if the policy is an account-wide default.If the default is selected, this will apply to all content uploaded into the account unless it is overridden by another data retention policy applied to a certain folder or group.
  5. Click Next.

⚠️Note:If you are creating a default policy, both existing and new content will be affected (i.e. videos older than X years will be automatically deleted). If you would like to retain older content, you can set different policies for the folders and/or groups that it belongs to.

Applying policies to folders and groups overview

Screenshot: Choose location section for the policy with a team folder and a group checked off

  • If the policy is not the default, you will continue to a page where you can select the team folders and user groups to which the policy will apply.

⚠️Note: You can select top-level parent folders only. All videos and subfolders contained within this parent folder will have the policy applied to them.

  • If you select a group, the policy will apply to all the Private To Mefolders of team members in that group.
  • These are the SSO groups that can be synced to Vimeo via SAML/SCIM or created using the custom groups feature.
  • If you have a user that is in multiple groups with different retention policies, the retention policy that has a longer duration will win and be applied to that user’s “Private to me” folder.
  • You will not be able to select folders or groups that already have data retention policies applied to them.

If the policy is the default, you can skip selecting folders and groups and move ahead to the summary.

Making the most out of applying a policy

  • Retention policies can be applied to folders or groups’ Private to me folders. Therefore, assigning a policy to a group does not mean that all uploads by users in that group have the policy applied. It will only be used for videos in those users’ Private to me folders.
  • When setting up a policy, you can only select top-level parent folders. All subfolders within the parent folder will have that retention policy applied to them.
  • Retention policies can be created for a minimum of 7 days or more.

About overlapping data retention policies

There may be several cases where data retention policies overlap. Here’s how those are handled:

  • If you have a default data retention policy, any additional policies you’ve applied to folders or groups will override the default (regardless of duration).
  • If a user is in multiple groups with different retention policies, the policy with the longer retention period will win. Hence, the videos will be deleted at the schedule of the longer retention policy applied to the group the user is a part of.

How to review the policy summary

  1. Ensure your policy has the correct duration and is applied to the correct folders and groups.
  2. Feel free to go back to edit the policy or locations.
  3. Click “Finish & save” to enable your policy and be redirected back to the data retention page.

How to edit a Data Retention policy

  1. On the data retention page, click “Edit” next to a policy you wish to edit.
  2. Navigate through the wizard to change the title, description, duration, or location of the policy.
  3. Review your new policy summary and click “Finish & save” to update your policy.
  4. After saving, new retention schedules will be calculated for the folders & groups to which this policy applies.

Recovering a video and viewing historyoverview

For details on how to view your deleted video history and recovering videos refer to How to view history and recover videos deleted by data retention.

⚠️Note: The videos that have been deleted longer than 30 days ago will be permanently deleted.

How to use HandBrake

HandBrake is a free program that can be used to compress and prepare MP4 videos for upload to Vimeo. It can be downloaded for Windows or Mac on HandBrake’s downloads page.

Be sure to reference our compression guidelines when encoding your video. We include setting recommendations specific to HandBrake below based on non-exhaustive testing and user feedback; newer options that HandBrake has added may not all be noted below.

If you have a question about using HandBrake, or are running into an error, please check out HandBrake’s Support FAQ.

  • Compress with HandBrake
  • Export with HandBrake
  • Recommended settings
  • Summary tab
  • Dimensions tab
  • Filters tab
  • Video tab
  • Audio tab

Compress with HandBrake

  1. When you open HandBrake, you will be prompted to select your source file. This is the original file you are looking to compress. If you accidentally bypass this step, you can also access the file selection menu by clicking File > Open Source, or by clicking the Open sourcebutton in the upper left-hand corner of the application.
  2. Select the file that you want to work with, then click Open. HandBrake will scan the source file, which may take several seconds.
  3. Once your file is ready to go, Handbrake will automatically load in some default information found in the Summary tab.
  4. We list recommended settings for additional tabs in HandBrake within the tables included below.
  5. You can skip the Subtitles and Chapterstabs. These aren’t required for most Vimeo videos.
  6. Once you are done with compression settings, you can move on to exporting your video.

Export with HandBrake

  1. Click the Start button at the top of the application to begin the encoding process. Screenshot: A screenshot showing the interfact of HandBrake. The ‘Start’ button is at the top row, in the middle. It is represented by a green circular button with a black triangle pointed to the right. Under the circle, a label reads ‘Start’.
  2. Once the video has been exported, view your finished, compressed, file (via VLC or QuickTime) to make sure it looks and sounds correct, then upload it to Vimeo. Having trouble with uploading? Please visit this troubleshooting guide.

Recommended settings

Summary tab
  • Title, Angle, Range, Chapters
  • Handbrake will automatically load this information from your original file. Leave as-is
  • Preset
  • Handbrake will automatically choose an encoding preset, but once you begin editing, it will automatically adjust the default to “Modified”. You can ignore this section for now.
  • Format
  • Set to MP4 File (the default). Web optimized, iPod 5G support, and Align A/V start should all remain unchecked.
  • Save as:
  • This is the name and destination path of your output file. You can enter a new file name or path manually, or select “Browse” to choose a new destination.
Dimensions tab
  • Storage size/ Display Size
  • Default. These values should default to your source file’s original dimensions.
  • Keep aspect ratio
  • Checked
  • PAR
  • Default. Should be 1 x 1
  • Anamorphic
  • Off
  • Modulus
  • Default (2)
  • Cropping
  • Automatic
Filters tab
  • Detelecine
  • Off
  • Interlace Detection
  • Off *If you are de-interlacing your video (as described below), you can check this option to detect interlaced frames of video.
  • Deinterlace
  • Off *If your source file is interlaced you can select Yadif but we only recommend this if you are comfortable using Handbrake. If you are not sure what type of source you have, it’s best to choose Off. You can read more about deinterlacing with Handbrake at ’ How to Deinterlace Video with HandBrake ’ .
  • Color
  • Keep “Grayscale” unchecked (unless you want to convert your video to black & white)
  • Rotate
  • 0°, Keep “Flip” unchecked *If your source file is upside down, you can experiment with other values to fix it.
  • Deblock
  • Off *If your source footage is low quality, you may want to enable this feature to remove blocking artifacts. Use with caution.
  • Denoise
  • Off
  • Sharpen
  • Off
Video tab
  • Video encoder
  • H.264 (x264) *If your video is HDR or above 4K (e.g 5K, 8K, etc), we recommend using H.265 (x265)
  • Framerate (FPS)
  • Same as source *Although rare, there are some situations where you’ll want to choose a frame rate different from the source: If the frame rate of your file is higher than 60 FPS: Choose a factor of your frame rate that is between 15-60 FPS. For example, if your frame rate is 100 FPS, choose 60 FPS. If your frame rate is lower than 15 FPS: Choose a multiple of your frame rate that is between 15-30 FPS. For example, if your frame rate is 8 FPS, choose 16 FPS.
  • Variable / Constant Framerate
  • Constant Framerate
  • Quality
  • Select Average Bitrate (kbps). Then, enter the average bitrate appropriate to your video file: SD: 2000-5000 kbps 720p: 5000-10000 kbps 1080p: 10000-20000 kbps 2K: 20000-30000 kbps 4K: 30000-60000 kbps 5K or higher: 50000- 80000 kbps *These data rates are suggested for average video files. If your video contains below average visual complexity (such as a slideshow presentation), choose a lower data rate. If your video contains above average visual complexity (such as a video with high levels of grain), increase the data rate. 💡 Remember: Lower data rates lead to smaller file sizes and faster uploads! Experiment to pick the lowest data rate that yields acceptable image quality.

How to use the Brand Kits

The Brand Kits are designed for marketers and teams who want brand consistency across all touchpoints, from embedded players to webinar pages. This article summarizes how to use the Brand Kits, a centralized hub where you can manage your logos and brand color for consistent branding across Vimeo’s product surfaces.

  • What to know before using the Brand Kits
  • How to use the Brand Kits
  • How to use the Brand Kits in player appearance
  • FAQs and troubleshooting
  • Making the most of the Brand Kits

What to know before using the Brand Kits

Before you begin, keep the following in mind:

  • The Brand Kits are available at both the account level and team level.
  • You can now create and manage multiple brand kits per team or workspace.
  • For Enterprise accounts that have workspaces enabled, a parent brand kit can be defined at the account level and inherited by all workspaces.
  • The Brand Kits connect to several areas across Vimeo:
  • Player appearance
  • Registration forms
  • Showcases
  • Video tools include Live, Record, Editor, and Simplified Interactive Editor.
  • Brand kits include logos and colors.
  • Permissions to manage brand kits are available to Admins and Owners.

How to use the Brand Kits

Follow these steps to use the kits:

  1. Navigate toManage Workspacevia your avatar drop-down.
  2. Select the Brand kits from the left panel.
  3. Navigate from Brand kits > Your Default Brand kit. ⚠️Note:New users or those who haven’t previously used player logos willnotsee Your Default Brand Kit. In this case, you will need to create a New brand kit to get started.
  4. Select and upload your logo and colors. Screenshot: A dark-themed web page for a “Brand kit” named “PARTY”. The page is divided into two main sections: “Logos” and “Colors”. Both sections are currently empty, each showing a large dark card with a plus sign icon, indicating where a user can click to upload or add new items.
  5. You can rename or delete previously created logos and colors from the three-dot menu at the bottom.

How to use the Brand Kits in player appearance

To use the Brand Kits to modify the appearance of your player:

  1. Select your video, and click on Appearance from the left menu.
  2. Switch between the Embed and Video page at the top to customize each view.
  3. From the Branding section, choose and apply your brand colors and logo.
  4. Click Save to apply your changes.

FAQs and troubleshooting

  • What happens to my existing presets or branding?

Your previously uploaded player logos will automatically be included in the Brand Kits.

  • Why is Vimeo consolidating branding settings?

The Brand Kits reduce time spent reconfiguring settings and ensure your brand is unified across all customer-facing experiences.

  • Do I need to update anything manually?

To take advantage of new features like brand-wide color syncing, you’ll need to visit the Brand Kits and configure those settings. Otherwise, your existing branding will continue to apply where possible.

Making the most of the Brand Kits

Here are a few tips to get the most out of your branding setup:

  • Unify your touchpoints: Ensure your logo and color choices are consistent across embedded players, registration forms, and webinars to reflect your brand.
  • Use brand-consistent CTAs: Align button styles and player behavior with your brand tone using the preset editor.
  • Preview changes often: Use the in-app previews before publishing your brand kit to avoid unexpected color clashes or layout issues.
  • Communicate with your teams: If you’re managing branding at the team level, ensure each team knows where to find and apply your new brand kit settings.

How to use the Vimeo Enterprise Legal Hold tool

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

With Vimeo’s Legal tool, Enterprise account owners and admins can apply a legal hold on specific videos to prevent them from being deleted. This tool helps you preserve your videos while being reviewed in any ongoing litigation.

Enterprise account owners and admins can upload a CSV to apply the legal hold to a set of videos. While videos are under legal hold, they cannot be deleted by a user or by a data retention policy. Once litigation has ended, the legal hold can be removed, and then the Enterprise account owners or admins can remove videos one at a time or upload a CSV to remove the legal hold from the batch of videos.

  • How to access the Legal Hold tool
  • How to apply Legal Hold to your videos
  • How to remove Legal Hold from your videos
  • How to Download CSV

How to access the Legal Hold tool

Navigate to the Settings tab on your team management pageand select Legal Hold to access the tool. Legal Hold can be applied to videos by uploading CSVs of your clip URLs.

How to apply Legal Hold to your videos

  1. To start, set up your CSV.
  • The header should be video_url.
  • You can grab the URLs from the video share link or the video settings page, or the advanced settings page. (You can also add the clip ID if you have that handy)
  • Create the list of videos you’d like to apply a legal hold to and save.
  1. Select “Upload CSV” in the top right corner. Select “Apply legal hold” and choose your CSV.
  2. After you’ve uploaded your CSV, the videos will be suspended in legal hold indefinitely.
  3. While videos have legal hold applied to them, they cannot be deleted by any user on your team or by a data retention policy.

How to remove Legal Hold from your videos

To remove the legal hold for individual clips:

    1. Find the clip on the list and click the three dots over on the right.

Select Remove from legal hold. Screenshot: A screenshot showing the Legal Hold section of the Team Management page. The button with three horizontal dots at the right of a row pertaining to a specific video is selected. When selected, it shows the option ‘Remove from legal hold’.To remove the legal hold for a batch of clips:

  1. Create your CSV. The header should be video_urland create a list of your video links.
  2. Select Upload CSV. Select Remove legal holdand find your CSV from the desktop browser.
  3. After uploading your CSV, the list of videos in the CSV will be removed from the legal hold page.

How to Download CSV

  • Select Download CSV to download a list of clip IDs for all the videos that have legal hold applied to them.

How to use the Vimeo Record extension for Google Chrome

About the Vimeo Record extension

The Vimeo Record Chrome extension now opens the Record Studio in a new browser tab when launched from the browser toolbar. This change, implemented in October 2024, replaces the previous in-browser widget experience and allows users to record their screen, webcam, or both.

What happens when I click the extension?

Record Studio now launches in a new tab when you click the extension icon. The previous pop-up widget is no longer in use.

Can I record using the extension?

Yes, the Vimeo Record extension stays in your Chrome toolbar. Clicking it opens Record Studio, offering these features:

  • Record: Capture your screen and/or webcam.
  • Enhance: Utilize tools such as a teleprompter and AI-supported scripts (if available).
  • Upload: Directly transfer your video to your Vimeo account.

Get detailed information about the Record Studio.

What are the benefits of using Record Studio?

  • Browser-flexible experience - Works across any supported browsers.
  • Expanded recording tools - A wider range of recording options and tools.
  • Performance improvements - Seamless recording and faster uploads.
  • Streamlined workflow- Start recording hassle-free and quickly.

Suggested next steps

Learn about how to install or uninstall the Record Chrome extension.

How to use transcript view

Adding the transcript view to the embedded player helps viewers find relevant sections within a video. This feature gives viewers a comprehensive overview of the video’s content, making it easier to identify specific sections they want to explore. This view is available for embedded videos and on mobile.

If you are creating a video and want to know more about how transcripts/closed captions work, refer to ‘How do I add captions or subtitles to my video?’.

To use transcript view:

  1. Click on the captions icon on the player
  2. Use the Transcript Panel with the Transcript Search to find and follow along as the video plays.

This applies to all the videos that have transcripts created from both auto CC and uploaded captions. If the video’s owner disabled a captions track, the associated transcript will also be disabled.

⚠️Note: If you are getting an error message and your transcript is not loading, reach out to support using this contact form.

How to use Vimeo AI to ask questions about videos

Activating this feature is available to account Owners on select Vimeo Enterprise plans. Please contact your account manager to gain access.

This article discusses how to ask questions and find answers onAI-eligible videos

Viewers can determine which videos support questions and answers by checking if the Vimeo AI button is displayed under the video player. If a video does not have the Vimeo AI button under the player or in the player’s top-right corner, you cannot ask questions about the video.

  • How can I activate Ask AI on videos I upload?
  • How to use Ask AI on Vimeo.com
  • How to use Ask AI on an embedded video

How can I activate Ask AI on videos I upload?

Ask AI can be activated onAI-eligible videos.

Account Owners on selectVimeo Enterprise plans can activate Ask AI on the AI settings page. Learn how at About the Vimeo AI settings page

All viewers of the video can ask questions that are not limited to what appears in the transcript of your video. For example, they are about scenes, objects, or slides of a presentation that appear in the video.

How do I use Ask AI on a video on Vimeo.com?

All viewers can use Ask AI on videos where the feature is activated. You can use Ask AI by selecting the Vimeo AI button under the video player. To do so:

  1. Select the Vimeo AI button under the video player and title of eligible videos to open the Vimeo AI module.

Screenshot: A Vimeo video player. Below the player, a title reads Break down language barriers with Vimeo AI: Translate your videos in minutes.’ The ‘Vimeo AI’ button, located to the right of the title is prominently outlined in red. 2. In the questions and answers box, select from a pre-generated question or type your own in the textbox. You may have to wait a few moments for Ask AI to activate. 3. To view or ask questions in another language, select the dropdown and choose a supported language or type the question in your preferred language. Ask AI will respond in the language asked. 4. Vimeo AI will generate the answer to your question and provide quick links to points in the video where the answer is given. You can select the play button next to each point to jump to that point in the video. Screenshot: A Vimeo AI answer interface displays a response to ‘What is the video about?’, explaining Vimeo AI’s video translation capabilities, language support, and features for global accessibility. Below the detailed text answer, three rectangular buttons are outlined in red, providing related links or topics. These are selectable, pointing the user to the point(s) in the video where the answer is given.

How to use Ask AI on an embedded video

If a video uploaded to Vimeo is embedded on another site and the video has Ask AI activated, viewers can ask questions about the video. To do so:

  1. Hover over the video player and select the Ask Vimeo AI button.
  2. Select or type the question in the expanded panel.
  3. After the answer to your question is generated, select the play button under the answer to play the moment in the video that discusses the answer.

How to use Vimeo AI to generate chapters for my video

This feature requires an Advanced, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

This article explains how to use Vimeo AI to create chapters for your video

Owners on paid plans, Advanced, Premium, and up, as well as team members on select Vimeo Enterprise plans, can use Vimeo AI to generate chapters.

To use Vimeo AI to generate chapters for your videos:

  1. Select the Vimeo AI button from the left-side toolbar of the video settings page.
  2. Select Generate Chapters.
  3. Chapters will be generated for your video. Chapters consist of the title of the chapter, a thumbnail from your video, and the duration of your chapter.
  4. Select Saveto save your generated chapters (or select “Replace” if chapters already existed for your video).
  5. If you want to customize the beginning and ending points of your chapters, you can edit them manually using the Interactivebutton on the left-side toolbar.

How to use Vimeo AI to generate details about my video

This feature requires an Advanced, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

This article explains how to use Vimeo AI to generate details (such as a title, summary, and tags) for your video. Owners on paid plans, Advanced, Premium, and up, as well as team members on select Vimeo Enterprise plans, can access this feature once the team Owner activates it.

For Enterprise Users with Workspaces: This feature can be managed by a Workspace Admin for videos uploaded to the Workspace. For more information, visit How to edit my Workspace’s settings

To use Vimeo AI to create video details:

  1. Select the video that you want to generate details for from your Library.
  2. Select the Vimeo AI button on the left-side toolbar of the video settings page.

How to use Vimeo AI to generate highlights

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

A highlight reel is a short recap or a series of video moments that Vimeo AI creates from a longer AI-eligible video, based on a text prompt you provide.

This article explains how to use Vimeo AI to create a highlight reel for your video. Team members on select Vimeo Enterprise plans can access this feature once the team Owneractivates it.

For Enterprise Users with Workspaces: This feature can be managed by a Workspace Admin for videos uploaded to the Workspace. For additional information, visit ’How to edit my Workspace’s settings’.

To use Vimeo AI to generate a highlight reel:

  1. Select the Vimeo AI sparkles button from the left-side toolbar of the video settings page.
  2. Select Generate highlights.
  3. In the prompt box, describe the highlight reel you’d like Vimeo AI to create. The box rotates through example prompts for inspiration, such as:
  • “Create a 30-second summary of the video using the best moments.”
  • “Turn this video into a short recap with the top business takeaways.”
  • “Find the strongest quotes and supporting moments for a testimonial clip.”
  1. Select Generate highlight reel. This button stays greyed out until you enter a prompt, so a prompt is required to generate a highlight reel.
  2. Vimeo AI creates a highlight reel based on your prompt. You’ll see status updates while it works, until your highlight reel is ready.
  3. Preview the highlight reel. From there, you can Save as a new video or Copy link to share it.
  4. To refine the result, use Ask for edits to request changes (for example, “make it shorter” or “focus on the customer testimonial”), or select Clear chat to start over with a new prompt.
  5. Once saved as a new video, your highlight reel can be further customized using the Editor.

How to use Vimeo AI to translate my video’s audio and subtitles

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

This article explains how to utilize Vimeo AI for translating both the audio and subtitles of your video.

Team members on select Vimeo Enterprise plans can use Vimeo AI credits to both translate the subtitles and audio of their AI-eligible video. The Enterprise account Owner must activate this feature before team members can access it.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces: Workspace Admins can manage access to this feature for videos uploaded to the Workspace. For additional information, visit About the Vimeo AI settings page.

  • How translations are priced
  • Translating your video’s audio and subtitles
  • When to add translation to your video workflow
  • What if my translation attempt fails?

How translations are priced

The total cost of your translation is calculated as: 20 credits per minute x Video length (minutes) x Number of languages selected

Example:A 2-minute video translated into three languages

20 credits per minute x 2 minutes x 3 languages

Total cost = 120 credits

Translating your video’s audio and subtitles

You can translate your videos and subtitles into multiple languages.

To translate your video’s subtitles:

  1. Select the Vimeo AI button from the left-side toolbar.
  • You can also access it by selecting “Languages”from a video’s page and selecting”Generate.”
  1. Select Translate video.
  2. Select Audio/Subtitles.
  3. Select the languages that you would like to translate your video into.
  4. Confirm the cost of your translation. You can begin the translation process if you have enough credits left in your AI credit balance. If you do not, you will be prompted to purchase the required AI credits.

The time it takes for your video to translate is roughly proportional to its length. For instance, a 5-minute video will take approximately 5 minutes to generate a translation.

You can edit the video’s description from the Languagesmenu of the video’s settings.

After, you can download language-specific versions of your video if it has multiple audio tracks in different languages. Learn how to do so at How to download language-specific versions of my videos.

When to add translation to your video workflow

We recommend translating your video once you are confident that no further edits are needed.

If you edit your video’s script after using AI translation, you must manually edit the transcript for each text track in the Languagesmenu of the video’s subtitles. They will not update automatically.

Additionally, if you edit your video using the following tools, you will need to re-translate it, as translations are not updated automatically.

  • Editor
  • Trimmer
  • Text-based video editor
  • If you replace your video

You will not receive a refund for additional translations required to reflect changes made to your video after the original translation process is completed.

Translate and dub multiple videos at once

You can generate subtitle translations and dubbed audio for multiple videos in a single action directly from your Library.

  1. In your Library, check the box next to each video you want to translate and dub, or select a folder to include all videos in it.
  2. In the bulk actions toolbar that appears, select Translate and dub.
  3. Choose the language or languages you want to translate and dub into.
  4. Select Start to begin generating the translations and dubbed audio tracks.

The translations and dubbed audio will process in the background. You’ll receive a notification when they’re ready.

What if my translation attempt fails?

For help with translation issues, check out Troubleshooting: Failed AI Translations.

Automate audio dubbing and translation via API — Enterprise users can also trigger audio translations and dubbing via the Vimeo AI API. This is useful for building automated localization pipelines. See How to use the Vimeo AI API for details.

How to use Vimeo AI to translate my video’s subtitles

This feature requires a paid plan.

If your video’s original audio is in a supported language and has a transcript, you can use Vimeo AI Credits to translate its subtitles. This article explains how to utilize Vimeo AI for translating the subtitles of your video.

  • What to know before translating subtitles
  • How to translate your video’s subtitles
  • What if my translation attempt fails?
  • Making the most out of AI translations
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before translating subtitles

Before you translate your video’s subtitles, take note of the following:

  • You can pay for translations using AI credits. Translation costs are calculated as: 10 credits per minute x Video length (minutes) x Number of languages selected.
  • We recommend translating your video at the end of your workflow when you are confident that you will not need to make additional edits to its content.
  • If you edit your video’s original subtitle transcript after using AI translation, you must manually edit the transcript for each language. The translated subtitles will not update automatically.
  • If you modify your video using the Video Editor, Trimmer, Text-based video editor, or if you replace your video, you must re-translate it. This will cost additional AI credits.
  • Using AI to translate videos on Vimeo is currently not supported on Vimeo mobile apps.
  • Team owners and admins can manage access to this feature for their teams. For additional information, visit About the Vimeo AI settings page.

How to translate your video’s subtitles

To translate your video’s subtitles using Vimeo AI:

  1. Select your video from your Library
  2. Select theVimeo AI button from the left-side toolbar of the video’s settings page.
  3. Select Translate Video. Screenshot: A video’s settings page. On the left, a side navigation menu includes icons for Appearance, Languages, Interactivity, Editing, Analytics, and Vimeo AI, with ‘Vimeo AI’ highlighted. On the right, the main ‘Vimeo AI’ panel lists options including ‘Translate video’, ‘Generate video details’, ‘Generate chapters’, ‘Generate highlights’, and ‘Ask about this video’. The ‘Translate video’ option is also highlighted.
  4. Select Subtitles Onlyand Continue.
  5. Select the language(s) that you want to translate the video into. The cost of the translation will display. If you do not have enough credits, you will be prompted to purchase more.
  6. Select Finish and Saveto begin the translation.

The time it takes is approximately proportional to the video’s length. After the translation is complete, you can manually edit your video’s transcript from the Languages menu of the video’s settings page.

Screenshot: A video’s settings page. On the left, a side navigation menu includes icons for Appearance, Languages, Interactivity, Editing, Analytics, and Vimeo AI, with ‘Languages’ highlighted. The expanded ‘Languages’ panel shows ‘English (original)’ and ‘Spanish’ entries, each with a ‘Subtitles (AI)’ toggle. A ‘Translate’ button is below them. A pencil-shaped edit icon on the ‘Spanish’ row is also highlighted with a tooltip displaying as ‘Edit’.

Translate subtitles for multiple videos at once

You can generate subtitle translations for multiple videos in a single action directly from your Library.

  1. In your Library, check the box next to each video you want to translate, or select a folder to include all videos in it.
  2. In the bulk actions toolbar that appears, select Translate subtitles.
  3. Choose the language or languages you want to translate into.
  4. Select Start to begin generating the translations.

Translations will process in the background. You’ll receive a notification when they’re ready, and the subtitles will appear in the Languages section of each video’s settings.

What if my translation attempt fails?

If you encounter issues with your translation, visit Troubleshooting: Failed AI Translations for additional troubleshooting information.

Making the most out of AI translations

  • We strongly recommend manually reviewing translated subtitles for accuracy and clarity. AI is an experimental technology and may produce inaccurate or unsuitable translations.
  • To help the AI capture phrases or words specific to your team, company, or industry, consider adding them to your team’s custom vocabulary list.
  • Vimeo Enterprise users can also use Vimeo AI credits to translate their video’s audio. Learn how at ‘How to use Vimeo AI to translate my video’s audio and subtitles’.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn aboutAI credits.

Translate subtitles programmatically — Enterprise users can also trigger subtitle translations via the Vimeo AI API. This is useful for automating translation workflows. See How to use the Vimeo AI API for details.
