How to view quiz and poll data in your interactive videos

If you’ve integrated quizzes and polls into your videos, you can see how your audience engages with your content. You can access and analyze this data, to gain valuable insights into participant performance without compromising their privacy.

This guide will walk you through viewing and interpreting quiz and poll data.

  • Video tutorial
  • Accessing Quiz and Poll Data
  • Downloading Data
  • Understanding Overall Quiz Results
  • Analyzing Question Quiz Results
  • Examining Session Quiz Results

Video tutorial

This video explains how to view quiz and poll data in your interactive videos:

Accessing Quiz and Poll Data

  1. Log in to your Vimeo account and navigate to the video containing the quizzes or polls you wish to analyze.
  2. Click on the Interactive Studio tab located at the top of the video player.

Downloading Data

  1. Within the Interactive Studio, select the Quiz and Poll Data button at the top.

  2. Downloadthe spreadsheet containing comprehensive information about the quiz results.

Understanding Overall Quiz Results

  • TheOverall Quiz Results tab in the downloaded spreadsheet gives a comprehensive overview of participants’ performance.
  • The Participants column indicates the number of participants who completed all questions.
  • The Average score shows the total score divided by the number of people taking the quiz. The average score percentage shows the total score divided by the maximum score possible in your quiz.
  • The maximum score is the maximum score possible on your quiz.
  • Total correctshows the number of total correct answers registered by the quiz
  • The Not Complete column shows the count of participants who didn’t answer every single question.

Analyzing Question Quiz Results

  • The Question Quiz Results tab within the spreadsheet gives access to aggregated data for each question.
  • The Question Name column identifies the specific quiz questions.
  • The People Answered column, displays the number of participants who responded to each question.
  • The Correctcolumn shows how many participants answered each question correctly.
  • The Incorrectcolumn shows information about the number of participants who answered each question incorrectly.
  • TheCorrect Answer column shows the correct answer for each question

You can calculate the Accuracy Percentage by dividing the number of correct answers by the total number of answers and then multiplying by 100.

Examining Session Quiz Results

  • The Session Quiz Resultstab within the spreadsheet delves into individual quiz-taker insights.
  • The Session ID column assigns a unique identifier to each quiz-taking session.
  • The Correct column shows the number of questions the participant answered correctly.
  • The Incorrect column shows the number of questions the participant answered incorrectly.
  • The Duration column gauges the time participants take to complete the quiz in seconds.
  • The quiz percent correct is the participant’s number of correct answers divided by the total number of questions multiplied by 100
  • The Completed column determines if the participant answered all questions.
  • The Scorecolumn provides a participant’s score based on correct answers out of the total possible score.
  • The Submitted column shows the exact date and time when quiz results were submitted.

By following these steps, you’ll be able to effectively access, analyze, and interpret quiz and poll data within your videos. Visit the Vimeo help center for further guidance on creating interactive videos.

I reached my total storage, video usage, or upload quota limit. What can I do?

If you see that you have or will soon reach your account’s video limit, steps you can take to free up or add space depend on which type of plan you have and how it measures storage allowance. This article will outline steps you can take depending on what type of storage allowance your plan has.

Total storage (most plans)

If you have reached your total storage limit, you can:

  • Compress your source file to reduce the file size (e.g. use a lower bitrate or resolution)
  • Delete previous versions of videos you’ve replaced using version history.
  • Delete videos you don’t need to store anymore. You can also delete videos in bulk from your Library.
  • Upgrade your account to get more storage.

Video usage (Free, Starter, Standard, Advanced accounts created before June 17, 2024 and maintained a paid subscription) You can check your sign-up date in the upper left-hand corner of your account settings.

If you hit your video usage cap, you can:

  • Delete any video(s) that were added within the last 24 hours of hitting your cap to open up more video space (consider downloading it first). You can also delete videos in bulk from your Library.
  • Upgrade your account to increase your video allowance.

Weekly upload quota (Some Plus and Pro accounts)

We have started migrating Plus and Pro users to total storage in lieu of weekly quota. You can check your plan’s storage using the tracker in the lower left-hand corner of your account’s home page, library, or video upload page.

If you have reached your weekly upload quota limit, you can:

  • Compress your source file to reduce the file size (e.g. use a lower bitrate or resolution).
  • Wait for your weekly quota to reset (hover over the tracker in the lower left corner of your library page to see when that occurs).
  • It is not possible to temporarily increase your quota or reset your quota early.
  • Delete a video that was uploaded since your last quota reset to free up space in your current quota week. Deleting videos that were uploaded prior to that reset will not free up space for your current quota. You can also delete videos in bulk from your Library.
  • Upgrade your account to get more storage.

I was blocked from saving my video. What should I do next?

The most frequently used feature that may have caused the inability to save your video is Stock footage(available for Standard members and higheror Pro members and higher).

To amend your video so you may download or share it, either go back to the editing stage and remove/replace this feature on your video orupgrade to use it in your video and in future projects.

Immersive and spatial video format support overview

You can upload and play spatial, VR180, 360 & Apple Project Media Profile 180/360 videos on Vimeo. This article discusses the formats we support and information about uploading.

  • About uploading 180 & 360 videos to Vimeo
  • How do I capture spatial videos?
  • About uploading spatial videos to Vimeo
  • Unsupported Features

About uploading 180 & 360 videos to Vimeo

Vimeo supports the uploading of 180 & 360 videos from the Vimeo apps for iPhone, iPad and Android, Mac, Vision Pro, and the vimeo.com website. Uploads require the following video specifications:

For VR180 & 360:

  • Spherical Video V2
  • Side-by-side OR top-and-bottom
  • Monoscopic or Stereoscopic
  • Projection: Equirectangular

For more detailed information, see Upload 360 video

For APMP 180 & 360:

  • HEVC for mono or frame packed stereo / MV-HEVC for layered
  • stereo
  • Side-by-side, top-and-bottom / Layered Stereo (MV-HEVC)
  • Monoscopic or Stereoscopic
  • Projection: Equirectangular
  • Color Depth: 10-bit

When a supported format above is uploaded, Vimeo will produce:

  • Spherical V2 h.264
  • APMP 10-bit, HEVC or MV-HEVC

Note: Vimeo does not currently support upload or playback of APMP Wide Field of View (APMP WFoV) or Apple Immersive Video (AIV).

Playing immersive 180 & 360 videos

Immersive videos can be watched in 3D on the Vimeo App for Vision Pro, and in 2D on other supported Vimeo mobile apps and vimeo.

If you encounter any issues around playback while using a browser, check out this article for possible fixes: Troubleshoot 360 Playback.

How do I capture spatial videos?

Spatial video can be captured using supported iPhones and Vision Pro devices. These can then be uploaded to Vimeo.

About uploading spatial videos to Vimeo

  • Vimeo supports the upload of spatial videos from the Vimeo apps for iPhone, iPad and Android, Mac, Vision Pro, and the vimeo.com website.
  • Spatial video uploads require the following:
  • MV-HEVC
  • Stereoscopic
  • Projection: Rectilinear
  • Field of View: 90 degrees
  • Color Depth: 8-bit

When a supported format above is uploaded, Vimeo will produce:

  • APMP 8-bit, MV-HEVC

Playing spatial videos

Spatial videos can be watched in 3D on the Vimeo App for Vision Pro, and in 2D on other supported Vimeo mobile apps and vimeo. The full 180 or 360 field of view of the video is visible on all devices.

Unsupported Features

Immersive and spatial videos do not support the following Vimeo features:

  • Vimeo’s video editor on web or mobile apps
  • Review pages
  • Vimeo does not currently support upload or playback of APMP Wide Field of View (APMP WFoV) or Apple Immersive Video (AIV)

Integrate the Vimeo player with Google Analytics

This feature requires a Business, Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

As a Vimeo user, you can use Google Analytics to track events on all Vimeo players embedded on your site, except for Vimeo Live. Google Analytics is not available to Vimeo live players.

You can find more detailed information at theGoogle Analytics help center.

  • How to add the Vimeo tracking script to your site
  • Which events on my Vimeo videos does Google Analytics 4 track?

How to add the Vimeo tracking script to your site

  1. Go to the Marketing tab in your Vimeo Account Settings.
  2. Scroll down below the email service providers to find the Google Analytics heading, where there are two tracking codes:Google Analytics 4 and Legacy, which is the now-deprecated Universal Analytics tracking code.
  3. Highlight and copy the code you need to your clipboard. ⚠️Note: While the legacy Google UA tracking code is still available for use, be mindful that it is a deprecated Google product that is no longer supported.
  4. Paste the code into your website’s HTML editor. It must be inserted somewhere in your site after the embedded video player.This ensures that the analytics script can successfully locate your embedded video.
  5. Save your website’s changes.
  6. Events on the embedded Vimeo player on your site will now be tracked in Google Analytics.

⚠️Note: We can’t provide support for specific questions about your third-party tracking service. We strongly recommend visiting the Google Analytics help center for further assistance with this integration.

Which events on my Vimeo videos does Google Analytics 4 track?

When you insert the Google Analytics 4 (GA4) script into your site and you’ve embedded videos from your Vimeo account on that site, you can track certain events for those videos. These events include:

  • Event names
  • Definition
  • video_load
  • This event occurs when the video is able to begin playback (but the play button has not yet been clicked).
  • video_play
  • This event occurs when playback begins
  • video_ended
  • During playback, when the end of the video is reached.
  • video_timeupdate (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%)
  • These events are logged when a viewer has played past the specific point in time of the video’s duration (1st quartile, midpoint, 3rd quartile, completed)

Each event that is tracked will be labeled with the following video metadata:

  • Metadata parameters
  • Definition
  • video_provider
  • The provider that hosts the video (i.e. “Vimeo”).
  • video_url
  • The clip URL of the embedded video (i.e. this is the URL if you were to visit or share the video’s page on Vimeo.com.)
  • video_title
  • The title of the embedded video.
  • video_id
  • Vimeo’s automatically generated unique ID for your video; this is also found in your video’s clip URL and embed code.
  • video_current_time
  • The time within the video when the event was recorded.
  • video_duration
  • The total length of the video (in seconds).
  • video_percent
  • The amount of the video that was viewed.

Is classic interactive SCORM compliant?

Classic interactive is not available in a SCORM wrapper.

If you’re looking to record certain events per user, you can use the Vimeo Player API to track user behavior by conflating your user-level data with interactive events from the player, such as completion, etc.

Library, My Library, and Team Library: what’s changing and how it works

This applies only to paid users who aren’t part of a team. If you’re on a team, nothing changes — you keep My Library and Team Library as they are. This feature is also being rolled out to a limited number of users. This article is only for you if you’ve seen the pop-up below in your account.

What’s changing and what it means for you

For users on a paid plan without a team, your two separate spaces — My Library and Team Library — are being combined into one unified Library, where all your content lives together.

Previously, upgrading to a paid plan automatically moved your content into a shared Team library, which created confusion over what was personal versus shared. That’s no longer the case:

  • If you use Vimeo on your own, you work in a single space — your Library.
  • The split between personal and shared content (My Libraryvs Team Library) appears only when you choose to collaborate by creating a team.

Depending on your account, this may have already happened or may be coming soon. You don’t need to do anything.

What happens to your content
  • Nothing is deleted. Every folder and video stays in one place instead of two.
  • Privacy never changes. Public, password, and private links stay exactly as you set them.
  • Want a team later? Invite someone and a Team Library comes back automatically.
The libraries at a glance
  • Library
  • When you see it: When you use Vimeo on your own
  • What it’s for: A single space for all your content
  • My Library
  • When you see it: When you’re part of a team
  • What it’s for: Your personal content, kept separate from the team’s
  • Team Library
  • When you see it: When you’re part of a team
  • What it’s for: Content shared with the people on your team
If you use Vimeo on your own: your Library

When you work on your own, you have a single space: your Library.

  • Everything you upload goes here.
  • You don’t need to create a team to use Vimeo: upgrading to a paid plan no longer forces you to.
  • You keep a simple experience, with no separate team library, until you choose to create one.

Working with a team: what you can do

Creating a team: My Library and Team Library

The moment you decide to collaborate with others, you create a team. From then on, your space splits in two:

  • My Library → your personal space. This is where the content you want to keep to yourself stays.
  • Team Library → the space shared with your team members, designed for working together on the same content.

The Team Library isn’t just “another personal folder”: it exists specifically for sharing and collaboration. That’s why it only appears once a team actually exists.

Good to know: creating a team isn’t a permanent decision. If you change your mind later and you want to continue solo, you can go back to a single Library.

How to create a team and start collaborating
  1. Open your Library
  2. Select Start your team
  3. Follow the steps to set up your team
  4. When you’re done, your Team Library is ready: from then on, you’ll see My Library and Team Library as two separate spaces
  5. Invite the people you want to collaborate with
How to add content to the Team Library
  • Upload new content directly to the Team Library, or move the content you want to share into the Team Library.
  • The content you want to keep to yourself stays in your My Library.
Going back to a single library

If you’re an admin and you remove your last collaborator, you can decide whether to merge the libraries back into one for a cleaner setup, or keep them divided in case you want to re-invite collaborators later without losing the split.

Either way, you can merge them later from the merge option in your Library.

If you merge, all the content from your My Library and Team Library comes together inside the Library, at the same level — there are no longer two separate spaces, and your content all lives in one place.

FAQs

  • Do I need to create a team to use a paid plan?

No. Creating a team is optional. If you work on your own, you keep using your Library just like before, even on a paid plan.

  • What’s the difference between My Library and Team Library?

Your My Library is your personal space. The Team Library is the space shared with the people on your team, designed for collaboration. You only see both when you’re part of a team.

  • Is the content in My Library visible to others?

Your My Library is your personal space and isn’t shown to the others within your team.

  • What happens to my content when I create a team?

Nothing happens automatically. They can then be fixed up and organized between My Library (your personal content) and Team Library (shared content). You decide what to share with the team.

  • Does moving a video between libraries change who can see it?

Externally no, your privacy settings will stay exactly the same. Internally yes, the video will be visible to your team members, where before it wasn’t, to allow collaboration on the same file.

Don’t hesitate to Contact us for further assistance.

Live caption hours are becoming AI credits

Starting on June 1st, 2026, your yearly live caption hours convert into AI credits. Your captioning experience doesn’t change — you’ll just use the same credits you already use for other AI features (like translations and dubbing) to power live auto-captions.

New to AI credits? Start with About AI credits for a quick primer.

  • What’s changing
  • How your hours convert into credits
  • What happens if you run out of credits during a live event
  • When this happens
  • What you need to do
  • A note for accounts with Unlimited Live Caption Hours add-on
  • Questions

What’s changing

After June 1, there’s just one pool: AI credits. They cover live auto-captions and every other AI feature on Vimeo. For a full breakdown of how credits are consumed across features, see AI credits rates and guidelines.

What stays the same:

  • Auto-captioning works the same way it does today in your live events.
  • You don’t need to enable or configure anything new.
  • Your existing AI credit balance and entitlement stay intact — we’re adding to it, not replacing it.

Heads up: Automatic closed captions can be enabled at the event level even if they appear off elsewhere. Because live auto-captions now consume AI credits, check the Automatic closed captions toggle under Optional features before you go live if you want to avoid consuming credits. For a recurring event, update the setting on the event itself.

How your hours convert into credits

Every minute of live auto-captioning consumes 10 AI credits. Your yearly caption-hour entitlement converts at that same rate, on top of the AI credits you already get:

  • Your current entitlement
  • What you’ll get
  • 2 hours / year of live captions
  • +1,200 AI credits / year
  • 30 hours / year of live captions
  • +18,000 AI credits / year

These credits renew yearly, just like your caption hours did. Because it’s all one pool now, you can spend them on whatever AI feature you need — live captions, VOD translations, dubbing, and anything we ship next.

What happens if you run out of credits during a live event

Captions don’t cut out mid-stream. Your event keeps running.

  • Self-Serve accounts: Credits consumed beyond your entitlement are billed at the end of the day. For details, see About AI credits.
  • Enterprise accounts: Captions keep running. If you regularly exceed your entitlement, your Account Manager will reach out to discuss an AI credits add-on.

When this happens

Starting on June 1st, 2026: Migration happens automatically. No action required on your end.

What you need to do

Nothing. The migration is automatic.

For Enterprise accounts: If you want to get ahead of it, check your AI credits balance and usage and explore the other AI features your credits can now power.

A note for accounts with Unlimited Live Caption Hours add-on

If your account has the Unlimited Live Caption Hours add-on, nothing changes for you on June 1st. You’ll keep using the live caption hours system as today. Your Account Manager will walk you through the transition to AI credits when the time comes.

Questions

How do I avoid being charged for live auto-captions? Live auto-captioning only consumes credits when the Automatic closed captions toggle is on for that event (under Optional features). Toggle it off before going live, or for a recurring event, disable it on the event’s settings. Note that this toggle is set per event, so confirm it each time.

Can I use these new credits for other AI features? Yes. Once migrated, all your AI credits — whether granted, purchased, or converted from caption hours — live in a single pool you can spend across any AI feature. See the AI Credits section of our Help Center for everything you can do with them.

Do my existing AI credits expire when the new ones are added? No. We’re adding the converted credits to your existing entitlement. Your regular AI credits entitlement and any add-on credits you’ve purchased keep their existing expiration rules — see About AI credits for the full expiration policy.

Where can I see my AI credit usage?

  • For Enterprise Accounts: You can track organization-wide usage and balances by following our guide: How to monitor content storage and AI usage for your Organization.
  • For Self-Serve Paid Accounts: You can view your remaining credit balance directly from your live event settings. Look at the Automatic closed captions toggle area under Optional features to view your available credits.

Manage Vimeo Stock

Vimeo Stock videos are no longer available to purchase as of April 1, 2025. Your purchased Vimeo Stock videos are still available in your Vimeo Library, and none of your videos using Vimeo Stock videos have been impacted.

We previously partnered with world-class creators from our community to exclusively license their collections for sale through Vimeo Stock. Since all of our stock clips are royalty-free and cleared for commercial use, you can use each licensed clip in an unlimited number of video projects, such as narrative films, documentary films, and commercials, as well as on websites and in corporate videos.

Please review our standard license for permitted uses.

  • Manage your stock clips on Vimeo
  • Downloading and using your stock clips

Manage your stock clips on Vimeo

Your purchased stock clips appear alongside your uploaded videos in the Library with the privacy setting “Stock footage.” Admins added to your account will be able to view and download stock footage you’ve purchased, but they will not be able to purchase stock footage on your behalf.

Screenshot: stock_purchased.png

You can edit the title of your stock clip in its settings like any other video, but you won’t be able to change the privacy and embedding settings as you would for a normal video on your account. Unlike your uploaded videos, stock clips don’t count against your account’s video storage, and they cannot be embedded.

You don’t have to pay any royalties based on plays or the number of video projects. Please note that the licenses are non-transferable and non-refundable. You can view the license for any of your stock clips on the Purchases page.

Download and use your stock clips

To download your stock clip, navigate to its clip page by selecting its title in your Library, then select the Download button beneath the video player.

For 4K and HD-only footage, we provide the original source file for download, which may either be ProRes (most common) or H.264, depending on what the creator uploaded as the original format (this information was provided when you purchased the stock clip). The source will always be marked as “original” in the download box on the clip page.

⚠️Note: It’s important to always select Original when downloading purchased stock files (if available). For 4K footage purchased in HD quality, the original file download option will not be available. In this case, select the highest quality available in the download box.

Managing the Enterprise Home page

This article provides a guide on utilizing the widgets on the Enterprise home page, offering insights for optimizing your experience.

  • Team view
  • Setting a featured video
  • Setting a featured folder
  • Recents widget
  • Analytics widget
  • My feed widget
  • Starred folder

Team view

Owners and admins of an Enterprise account can control their team members’ home page with the Team view button. This appears on the top right corner of the home page, which helps enable or disable content team members see on their home page. If any of the content is turned off by the admin/owner, it disappears from the feed of the entire team.

Screenshot: Image shows the upper right hand corner of an Enterprise Owner or Admins’ homepage, which has a Team view dropdown menu. The menu is open showing toggles for four options: Featured content, Featured folders, My feed, and Watch.

Setting a featured video

Owners and Admins can set the featured video on the Home page. The Manage video button lets you scroll through the entire library and choose any video or event you want to feature here.

To set a featured video:

  1. Click on the Manage video button
  2. A modal will open allowing you to search among your videos and live events. Select the video or event you want to pin to the top of the home page.
  3. When you’ve chosen your content, click on Add video.

💡Tip: Ensure you are logged into your account, otherwise you will not see your team’s homepage.

As team owner or admin, you can preview your featured video/event by navigating to the home page of your enterprise account. If you have set a live event as your featured video, you can navigate to the event settings page by clicking the Manage videobutton.

If the next event has not yet been scheduled, team admins can also opt to show the latest archived clip on the home page instead of the upcoming scheduled one.

Anyone on the team who clicks on the featured video or live event on the homepage will be brought to the video / live event page. If the home page features an in-progress live event, team members will see a play button across the header that they can click to navigate to the live broadcast. If the event is scheduled for later, they will see the event schedule and status.

The options on the private video / live event page vary depending on the team member’s permission on the video’s folder. Viewers can only comment, whereas Contributors can adjust the video’s settings in addition to commenting. The comment panel includes the ability to leave time-coded notes, video comments, and other review tools.

The featured content shown on the library home page will be available for all team members to view, even if that content is located in a folder that not everyone can access.

Clicking the back arrow in the upper left corner will navigate you to the folder that the video lives in, whereas clicking the team logo will bring you back to the homepage.

Setting a featured folder

Featured folders contain all the pinned videos. Enterprise owners and admins with pinned folders for their teams will appear in this folder.

To create a featured folder:

  1. Click on Select folders to choose the folder you want to feature
  2. ClickUpdate.
  3. The featured folder will then appear on the home page.

Recents widget

Viewers, Contributors, Contributor Plus, Admins, and Ownerswill see the Recents widget. Videos that have been recently modified will appear in this folder. It is not specific to any individual user, but the videos will be filtered for each user according to their access to the videos. Not every team member will see every recent video.

Analytics widget

This is the data collected from the Analytics dashboard that appears on the home page.

My feed widget

This widget will appear only if the Team admin/owner gives a team member access to it. This is specific to each user. Users will be automatically subscribed to Staff picks and can additionally choose to subscribe to updates from creators or channels of their choice.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-02-05 at 5.26.47 PM.png

Starred folder

Hover on any video or folder to add to the Starred folder by clicking the star icon. The Starred folder appears on the left navigation panel.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-02-05 at 5.33.05 PM.png

Navigating the interactive overlay editor

When creating an overlay, you can either start from a template or build your own overlay from scratch. Regardless of which creation pathway you choose, you will use the overlay editor to customize your overlays. Below is what the overlay editor looks like:

Screenshot: overlay_editor_full_view.png

Change the general overlay style settings

On the right-hand side of the page is an Overlay menu. Here you can:

  • Change the background color: Underneath your overlay, you can have a color cover your video. Click the box to choose a color and adjust its opacity using the sliders. You can also input the hex code into the text box.
  • Hide close button: Make the close button not visible to the viewer
  • Allow overlay to close: Choose whether or not to allow your viewer to be able to close the overlay.
  • Animation: Choose how your overlay animates into view.
  • Direction of animation: Choose the direction from which your overlay’s animation starts

New interactive Overlays

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Vimeo’s new interactive video overlays allow you to embed hotspots, text, media, and polls directly into your videos. These interactive layers enable you to provide additional details, boost audience engagement, and encourage specific actions such as purchases and registrations. This article summarizes how to create overlays in Vimeo’s new interactive environment using an easy drag-and-drop builder with customizable preset designs.

  • How to apply overlays to my timeline
  • How to apply an overlay via hotspot

How to apply overlays to my timeline

To apply an overlay to your video timeline:

  1. Select your video and click theInteractivitybutton on the left side panel.
  2. Choose theNew Interactive editor.
  3. Select Overlaysfrom the left navigation menu and choose from available preset designs.
  4. You can also click on the + sign at the top to create a new overlay.
  5. Drag and drop overlays, hotspots, polls, media, text, or graphics to add them to your video. You can also embed videos or a URL into your video.
  6. To save your overlay, click the Save overlay button in the top right corner. Alternatively, you can save it as a template using the dropdown menu associated with the same button.

How to apply an overlay via hotspot

To apply overlays via hotspot:

  1. Select Hotspotsfrom the left side panel.
  2. You can choose from the available categories from the drop-down menu or upload one of your choice.
  3. Click on the hotspot on your video to edit your Hotspot settings and select Open overlayfrom the Action on clickdrop-down.
  4. You can now create a new overlay for your video.
  5. Once you apply and save your new overlay, click on the hotspot, scroll down to Edit overlay on the pop-up window.
  6. Click on the three-dot menu to edit your overlay.

Using the new overlay builder, you can quickly add interactive elements to your videos with drag-and-drop ease. Customize overlays to enhance viewer engagement and deliver a more dynamic video experience.

Call to action
  • The title in the CTA end screen will be hidden when the player is smaller than 360px wide and 203px tall.
  • The description in the CTA end screen will be hidden when the player is smaller than 415px wide and 234px tall
  • The CTA is only visible when accessing the Unlisted video on the mobile browser and not on the Vimeo app.
  • Each field displays a character limit count. Note that the title font size is larger than the description font size, and the font cannot currently be customized.
More videos
  • The last video in the more videos end screen will be hidden when the player is smaller than 375px wide
  • If you select Showcase under More Videos, ensure that both the showcase itself and the videos within it are set to Public. Otherwise, the end screen will not display the selected showcase videos and will instead show random videos from the library.

Private Mode for your account

This feature requires a Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

Private Mode allows you to prevent your profile page and all of your videos from appearing on vimeo.com.

  • Disclaimer about Private Mode
  • Enable and disable Private Mode
  • Share videos in Private Mode
  • Use Showcases in Private Mode
  • Deactivate Private Mode

Disclaimer about Private Mode

Entering Private Mode will remove all your activity on vimeo.com, forever. You should only use this account setting if you’re certain you never want any of your viewers to access your content on a vimeo.com web page. They will be able to watch your content exclusively on your website or within Vimeo portfolios or review pages. (Read below for more information on sharing videos in Private Mode.)

Specifically, Private Mode hides your profile page, locks all of your videos into the Embed only privacy setting, and prevents you from using groups or channels. Any messages, comments, likes, groups, or channels you created before entering Private Mode will also be removed. This action cannot be reversed.

Be advised that Private Mode does not remove your profile information from vimeo.com. For example, you can still share other videos and comment and like other videos on vimeo.com; doing so will allow others to see your profile name and profile picture.

You can also consider adjusting your video privacy settings instead of using Private Mode.

Enable Private Mode

Vimeo Basic, Plus, Free, and Starter members need to upgrade their plans to unlock Private Mode.

If you’re a Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise member, you can activate Private Mode by following these steps:

  1. Navigate to the Privacy tab of your Account Settings.
  2. Click Enable Private Mode.
  3. You’ll need to review all the changes that will be made to your account, then re-enter your account password to enable Private Mode. Note: All of your videos must still comply with our Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Community Guidelines, even in Private Mode.

Share videos in Private Mode

In Private Mode, your videos will not be publicly visible on Vimeo.com and you’re not able to use Groups or Channels. However, you can still use Vimeo to host, organize and share your videos in the following ways:

  • Embed your videos on your website or other places around the web (You can even add domain-level privacy.)
  • Showcase your videos in a beautiful Pro Portfolio
  • Share videos with clients using Video Review Pages

Use Showcases in Private Mode

In Private Mode, you can still use showcases to organize your videos into different collections. However, only you will be able to access your own showcases. You cannot share showcases with other viewers in Private Mode or add to your team’s showcases. Additionally, you won’t be able to optimize your collection using the SEO tool. This is because Google cannot index private showcases.

Disable Private Mode

To disable Private Mode, head back to the Account tab of your Account Settings and click the Disable Private Mode button. Remember, disabling Private Mode will not bring back any of your previous activity (comments, likes, messages, etc.).

If you choose to deactivate Private Mode, and you’re still a Pro or Standard member or higher, the privacy settings of your videos will stay the same (Embed only, Unlisted, or Password). If your account is lapsing to Basic or Free, then any videos that are set to “Hide this from Vimeo.com” will update to “Private”.

Recently deleted: how to recover your videos

When you delete a video, it isn’t gone for good right away. From now on it moves to Recently deleted, where it stays recoverable for 30 days before it’s permanently removed. So if you change your mind, or delete something by mistake, you can put it back in seconds. This article explains what Recently deleted is, how to restore your content, and how to free up space whenever you want.

What “Recently deleted” is

Recently deleted is a section of your library that works like a safety net: it collects the videos you delete and keeps them for 30 days. While they’re here, you can restore them to their original location or delete them permanently to free up space. You’ll find it in your library’s side navigation, below your folders.

How it works, in short

  • When you delete a video, it’s moved to Recently deleted rather than erased right away.
  • The item stays there for 30 days, then it’s automatically and permanently removed.
  • At any point within those 30 days you can restore it or delete it permanently.
  • Items in Recently deleted still count toward your storage until they’re permanently removed, either when you delete them yourself or automatically after 30 days.

At a glance

  • You delete a video
  • What happens: It moves to Recently deleted and stays recoverable for 30 days
  • You restore an item
  • What happens: It returns to its original folder (or to the top level of your library if that folder no longer exists)
  • You delete it permanently
  • What happens: It’s removed for good and can’t be recovered
  • You do nothing for 30 days
  • What happens: It’s automatically and permanently removed

How to delete a video

When you delete a video from your library, you’ll see a confirmation: “[Item name]” will be deleted forever after 30 days. Once you confirm, the item moves to Recently deleted and a notification appears.

How to restore a video

  1. Open Recently deleted from the side navigation.
  2. Find the video and hover over its row.
  3. Select Restore.

The item returns to its original folder. If that folder has been deleted in the meantime, the item is restored to the top level of your library. You can also select multiple items and restore them all at once.

On Enterprise accounts, only owners and admins can see Recently deleted and restore items (see “Who can see and manage Recently deleted” below).

Good to know: a restored video keeps its title, description, tags, privacy settings, and embeds.

How to free up space (permanent deletion)

Videos in Recently deleted still count toward your storage. To free it up right away, you have two options:

  • A single item: hover over its row and select Delete forever.
  • Everything at once: use Empty trash from the banner at the top of the page (available to owners and admins only).

Permanent deletion can’t be undone: you’ll be asked to confirm, and once it’s done the item can no longer be recovered.

Who can see and manage Recently deleted

Visibility and available actions depend on your account type and your role.

Personal and team accounts (self-serve)
  • See the Recently deleted tab
  • Who can use it: All users
  • Restore and permanently delete
  • Who can use it: All users (items they have permission to manage)
  • Empty trash
  • Who can use it: Owners and admins only

The rule is “if you can delete it, you can restore it” — that’s why the tab is visible to everyone. Emptying the trash, being a destructive action, stays limited to owners and admins.

Enterprise accounts
  • Delete content
  • Who can use it: All members
  • See the Recently deleted tab and restore
  • Who can use it: Owners and admins only

On Enterprise, all members can delete content, but only owners and admins see the Recently deleted section and can restore items. The retention period is 30 days.

Recently deleted and Data Retention (Enterprise only)

If your Enterprise plan includes the Data Retention module, owners and admins get a direct link between the two areas: from the side navigation you can reach the Data Retention page in settings, and from the Data Retention page a banner links back to Recently deleted. This link is visible to owners and admins only.

Note: not every Enterprise plan includes Data Retention (for example, Essentials doesn’t, while Base Suite and Marketing Suite do). If your plan doesn’t have the module, the Data Retention reference isn’t shown.

FAQs

How long does a video stay in Recently deleted?

Deleted videos stay recoverable for 30 days from the moment you delete them. After that, they’re automatically and permanently removed.

Can I recover a video after 30 days?

No. Once 30 days have passed, or if you’ve deleted it permanently with Delete forever, the deletion is final and the video can no longer be recovered.

Do videos in Recently deleted use up storage?

Yes. Items in Recently deleted keep counting toward your storage as long as they’re there. To free up space, delete them permanently with Delete forever or clear everything with Empty trash.

Where does a video go when I restore it?

It returns to its original folder. If that folder has been deleted in the meantime, the video is restored to the top level of your library.

I can’t see the Recently deleted section. Why?

On personal and team accounts the tab is visible to everyone. On Enterprise accounts, however, Recently deleted is visible to owners and admins only — if you don’t have that role, you won’t see the tab. To recover content, contact an owner or admin on your account.

Does deleting a video break embeds on external sites?

While the video is in Recently deleted, its embeds on external sites won’t work. When you restore it, they work again, because the video’s ID and URL are preserved.

Still have questions?

If something isn’t clear or you need help, you can contact our support team: help.vimeo.

Search Engine Optimization (SEO) with showcases

This feature requires a Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

Vimeo members can use Vimeo’s SEO tool to help their showcases get discovered by new audiences online. If you opt in, Google will be able to index your public showcases, and they will become discoverable via search queries and gain a wider viewership. Without SEO, the only way for new viewers to find your videos is via a direct link.

⚠️Note: If you are a Basic, Free, Plus, Pro, or Starter member, you can preview this tool when working on your Showcase. However, you must upgrade to at least Business or Standard to use it.

  • What is search engine optimization?
  • Get started with SEO
  • Showcase privacy settings

What is search engine optimization?

Search engine optimization, commonly referred to as SEO, is the process of optimizing your website to get organic traffic from search engines (Google, Yahoo, Bing, etc). By making small changes to your website’s appearance and content, you can make it more attractive to search engines, which causes your site to gain higher placement in search results. SEO also means that search engines deliver high-quality results that are relevant to what searchers are looking for.

By improving your SEO, you will expand your visibility online, helping you reach and engage with a wider audience. You can read more about search engine optimization here.

Get started with SEO

To set up the SEO feature for a showcase, follow these steps:

  1. Open your showcase and then navigate to settings by selecting the gear icon to the left.
  2. Select SEO to open SEO settings within the panel.
  3. Start customizing your showcase’s metadata. By adding an SEO title and meta description, you can edit how your showcase appears in a Google search. ⚠️Note: If you decide not to customize your Showcase’s title or description, Google will show the default title and description.
  4. Be sure to add keywords describing the content of your collection. Google uses that information to determine which content is relevant to a particular search query and how the page should rank in searches for a particular term. Essentially, that’s what gives a web page its search ranking.
  5. Select Appearance to customize the visual elements of your showcase. ⚠️Note: At a minimum, 80% of the Featured Contentthumbnail image must have an alpha (transparency) level above 250. Google does not permit transparent thumbnails for video indexing. For further details, refer to Google Support at URL Inspection Tool: Video Indexing.

Showcase privacy settings

Search engine optimization is only available for Showcases with the privacy setting Anyone, i.e., public showcases. This is because Google cannot index private or hidden Showcases. Any private videos you’ve added to your public showcase, including Stock clips, will only be viewable by you, the account holder. Additionally, users currently in Private Mode cannot utilize this feature.

Send a showcase to a custom TV channel (Roku, Amazon Fire TV)

This feature requires a Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

Vimeo members can create customized Roku Channels and Fire TV apps where they can send their showcases.

Note: This feature is only available with Roku and Amazon Fire TV at this time. It is not currently possible to send showcases to Apple TV, Samsung, mobile apps, or any other TV apps. It’s also not possible to distribute live events via a TV app.

  • Get a feed URL
  • Roku channel set up
  • Access your channel
  • Privacy
  • Sell videos in TV apps
  • Updates to your showcase
  • Troubleshooting

Get a feed URL

The feed URL is a file generated from Vimeo that contains information about your showcase and the videos inside it.

You’ll need to enter a feed URL during the setup process for your TV apps or channels.

To obtain a feed URL, open showcase settings and then select TV apps. Next, choose the Roku or Amazon Fire TV tab.

For Roku, you’ll need to enter a provider name, the language of your channel, and genres before copying your feed URL.

For Amazon Fire TV, select thelink button to copy the URL to your clipboard.

Roku channel set up

As of January 2024, you will need to convert your Direct Publisher channel to Scenegraph per Roku’s announcement here: Roku to sunset Direct Publisher early 2024.

Access your channel

Once your channel is published, it will appear in the Roku Channel or Fire TV store. You and your viewers will be able to download the channel and access the videos in your Showcase from a Roku or Fire TV device. You can find instructions for installing channels below:

  • How to add apps to your Roku streaming device
  • Download apps on your Fire TV

Please note that the feed URL for Fire TV apps does not support custom sorting—meaning your videos may appear in a different order than how they appear in your showcase on vimeo.com. The default order on Fire TV will display the most recent videos first.

Privacy

Please note that only public videos and showcases can be shown on TV apps. For example, you’ll need to set both your videos and showcase to “Anyone” can view.

Sell videos in TV apps

We do not support integrating Vimeo On Demand videos into Showcase feeds for TV apps in order to sell your content.

You may be able to monetize with ads through the developer platforms provided by Roku, however, this process is not controlled nor managed by Vimeo. You can find more information on the ad monetization programs provided by each developer platform below:

  • Roku- direct publisher monetization
  • Amazon Fire TV - monetization

If you’re interested in selling videos through a custom TV app, please check out Vimeo OTT (home). Vimeo OTT is a service that allows users to launch a subscription using custom branded apps and webpages. For more information on selling videos through Vimeo OTT, you can reach out to the team by selecting “contact” at help.vhx.

Updates to your showcase

The content of your showcase will be automatically updated on your Roku channel once it’s published. This means that even if you need to update your videos on Vimeo (for example, if you need to add/remove a video in your Showcase, or change a title or video thumbnail), you won’t need to make any manual changes on Roku’s end—just keep in mind that it make take some time for your changes to be reflected.

Any updates or customization to the apps themselves (general app images, layouts, app descriptions, categories, etc) must be done through Roku’s interface. Vimeo only supplies the video content of your showcase.

Troubleshooting

Vimeo’s support team is always happy to help with any content-related issues that arise (for example, videos not appearing in your TV app). However, if you’re specifically having trouble with your Roku developer account we suggest contacting Roku Support (index) they will be best positioned to assist you with any issues. You can find support for Fire TV here.

Set a default quality for embedded videos

This feature requires a paid plan on Vimeo.

Embedded videos default to Auto mode, which picks the best quality video for each viewer’s playback environment. Vimeo paid members can default an embedded video to a specific quality on desktop and mobile by adding the quality parameter to the end of the player URL in the embed code.

⚠️Note:The quality parameter is not currently supported for live events.

  • Quality parameter examples
  • Limitations

Quality parameter examples

For example, if you want to default the embed to 1080p, you would add:

0

You can combine multiple URL parameters using an ampersand (&). For example:

0

The following qualities are supported by the quality parameter: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. If you select a quality that doesn’t exist for your particular video, the quality parameter will be ignored, and the embed will default to Auto.

Limitations

  • Using this parameter will default your embed to the selected quality on page load. Viewers will still have the option to manually switch back to Auto or different playback quality.
  • Please note that the playback quality settings are unavailable on iOS devices running version 17.0 or below. This is because video playback on these versions occurs in the device’s native player, which does not support quality selection. As a result, users may only experience audio playback, and the option to change video quality will not be visible. To access full playback features, we recommend using the iOS device version 17.0 or above
  • Please use caution when implementing this parameter. Not everyone can easily stream high-definition video, especially 2K and 4K. Defaulting to a particular quality may result in excessive buffering and choppy playback for your viewers.

Shared with me

This feature requires a Pro, Business, Premium, Starter, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise membership.

We have introduced a new space called Shared with me. This space shows all videos directly shared with you by a team member. You can access this space via your side navigation panel.

When someone on your team shares a video with you, it will appear in your Shared with me section. The default sort for Shared with me is “Last shared” - so the latest videos will appear at the top of the list. You can see who shared the video with you, when they shared it, and what team they are on. You have additional sort options for this space and can view it in either grid or list view.

Previously, if you were a Contributor or Viewer on a team account, shared videos appeared in your Team library root. We have cleaned this up and all of these videos will now appear in Shared with me. Shared with me only shows videos - shared folders will still appear in your Team Library.

If you are part of multiple teams on Vimeo, Shared with me will show all shared videos in one place - regardless of which team you’re switched into. If you want to see videos shared with you from a specific team, you can use the filter on this page to narrow shared videos down to one team.

If you share a video with another team member, they will see it in their Shared with me section with you as the sharer and the date you shared the video.

Showcases: feature access by account type

With a showcase, you can organize videos together to share publicly or privately. Read on to learn which showcase features are available at each membership level.

  • Set showcase privacy to Public, Private, or Password

Standard, Pro, Advanced, Business, Premium, and Enterprise

Premium and Enterprise

Store your source files on Vimeo

This feature requires a paid plan on Vimeo.

If you have a paid Vimeo account, you can choose to store your source files (the original file and the initial version of the video that you uploaded) on Vimeo.

  • Enable source file storage
  • Download your source files
  • Lost source files

Enable source file storage

To enable source file storage, follow these steps:

  1. Go to your Account Settings and click the Videos tab.
  2. Under Upload Defaults, scroll to the heading “Video preferences.”
  3. Check the box next to Keep source video files.
  4. Click Save. Once that’s done, your source files will be stored on any uploads you make going forward.

⚠️Note: Checking the box will not restore any files that have already been removed. The same goes for when you upgrade — once your membership is at Plus or above, you’ll have to go and manually enable this setting.

Download your source files

If you store your source files, you will be able to download them at any time. If you enable downloads on your videos, any of your viewers will also be able to download your source file in addition to any Vimeo versions (HD, etc.)

💡Tip: The Vimeo HD versions of your videos are often smaller than your source files, even though the quality is not noticeably different. We recommend having viewers download your Vimeo HD versions to minimize download time without sacrificing quality.

Lost source files

  • By default, your source file will be permanently deleted if you are a Free or Basic member or if you are a paid member but haven’t enabled source file storage in your account settings as described above.
  • While Basic or Free members can indeed download the source files made available by any paid members, they do not have the ability to permanently store or share their own source files on Vimeo.
  • You also must maintain your paid membership to keep your source files. If your subscription ends or the feature is disabled, your source files may be deleted and may not be recoverable.
  • We recommend keeping your own independent backups. This ensures you always have access to your files, even if they’re removed from Vimeo in the future.

⚠️Note: Any source files uploaded via an API pull application (like Dropbox, Google Drive, One Drive, Custom App, etc.) prior to September 2016 cannot be downloaded, regardless of whether you enabled the setting in your video preferences.

Technical FAQs: Vimeo AI

Last updated: December 4, 2025

  • What is Vimeo AI?
  • When using Vimeo AI, who owns the inputs and outputs?
  • Will my videos be used to train any generative AI models?
  • How will Vimeo use the outputs generated by Vimeo AI?
  • How is access to Vimeo AI administered and controlled?
  • Is my content shared with third parties?
  • How do Vimeo’s third-party service providers use my data?
  • How does Vimeo address inclusivity and fairness in AI?
  • How does Vimeo communicate its use of AI in a transparent and clear way?
  • Can I access Vimeo AI features through the API?

What is Vimeo AI?

Vimeo’s AI capabilities include features that speed up workflows, extract insights, and get more out of existing content by auto-generating titles, tags, and chapters. They also recap content through text summaries and turn videos into a two-way dialogue, enabling viewers to ask questions directly about the video. Vimeo’s AI tools also enable users to translate their videos.

We strive to leverage our AI capabilities as a complementary asset to enhance, assist, and complement workflows, making it easier to accomplish your day-to-day tasks. Our video AI suggestions and outputs can be further edited through our video editing tool. Vimeo AI runs on Vimeo’s trusted infrastructure and upholds the security practices and compliance standards that our customers expect. Enterprise users can also trigger these AI features programmatically through the Vimeo AI API.

When using Vimeo AI, who owns the inputs and outputs?

Between you and Vimeo, you retain all rights to the inputs you provide to our services, and you own any output you rightfully receive from our services to the extent permitted by law.

Will my videos be used to train generative AI models?

Vimeo does not use and does not permit third parties to use your videos to train or improve the underlying generative AI or large language models. Read more about our position on AI.

How will Vimeo use the outputs generated by Vimeo AI?

We use outputs solely to provide, support, and maintain our services. We may use user interactions and customer feedback to improve or develop our services. For more information, please see our AI Addendum.

How is access to Vimeo AI administered and controlled for teams?

Team Owners and Admins can control Vimeo AI settings for their team on the AI Settings page. Learn how at About the Vimeo AI settings page

Is my content shared with third parties?

Some of our AI features utilize software from third-party service providers. Vimeo only partners with third parties whose security policies and privacy commitments align with ours.

Below is an overview of the third-party service providers we work with today for specific AI capabilities, along with how data may be shared with them. Our primary third-party service provider is Microsoft Corporation, which uses the Azure infrastructure, which features a wide array of security tools and capabilities. To learn how Microsoft secures the Azure infrastructure, visit Microsoft: Azure infrastructure security.

We may add additional third-party providers to enhance our AI capabilities in the future. As additional partners are added, we will update this section of the help center article.

  • AI feature
  • Description
  • Third-Party Service
  • Data Shared
  • Transcription
  • Transcribe videos into a text transcript
  • ElevenLabs and Google Cloud
  • Audio portion of the video file
  • AI script generator
  • Generate a script based on a text prompt and indication of tone and length preferences
  • Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service
  • Text prompts
  • AI-generated video details
  • Automatically generate video titles, tags, text summaries, and chapters
  • Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service
  • Text transcript
  • Interactive Q&A
  • Enable editors and viewers of a video to ask questions through pre-generated or open-ended Q&A
  • Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service
  • Text transcript
  • AI Translation
  • Translate video, audio, and captions into dozens of languages
  • ElevenLabs (audio) and Google Cloud
  • Audio portion of the video file

You can find a complete list of Vimeo’s sub-processors here.

How do Vimeo’s third-party service providers use my data?

Our third-party service providers are only permitted to store and process data to provide the service to us and to monitor for uses that violate the applicable product terms. Microsoft fully controls the Azure OpenAI Service; Microsoft hosts the OpenAI models in Microsoft’s Azure environment, and the Service does NOT interact with any services operated by OpenAI (e.g., ChatGPT or the OpenAI API).

Your inputs and outputs:

  • are NOT available to other customers.
  • are NOT available to OpenAI.
  • are NOT used to improve OpenAI models.
  • are NOT used to improve any Microsoft or 3rd party products or services.
  • are NOT used to automatically improve Azure OpenAI models.

How does Vimeo address inclusivity and fairness in AI?

We’re committed to making sure our AI features are implemented responsibly. We only work with vendors who have developed controls designed to monitor and eliminate biases in their models. Additionally, our automatic transcript generation feature promotes inclusivity and accessibility by enabling individuals with hearing, visual, and other impairments to access videos.

If you experience a critical error or issue that does not align with our commitment and significantly impacts your experience with our AI features, please contact our support team.

How does Vimeo communicate its use of AI transparently and clearly?

Vimeo provides tools for creators to transparently label videos containing realistic AI-generated content with clear disclosures visible on the video page and player. This functionality and automatic labeling for Vimeo’s AI tools help inform viewers about the presence of synthetic media hosted on Vimeo. For more details, visit ‘How can I tell if a video on Vimeo was generated with or enhanced by using AI?’.

Can I access Vimeo AI features through the API?

Yes. Enterprise users can use the Vimeo AI API to trigger transcription, subtitle translation, audio dubbing, and AskAI on their videos programmatically. See How to use the Vimeo AI API to get started.

Tips for designing an interactive overlay

Below are some tips and best practices on designing your interactive overlay in Vimeo Interactive.

Be a storyteller

Remember the story you’re trying to tell (or sell)

Brand it

Stick with your organization’s aesthetic. Try taking design notes from your own website and brand guidelines.

Animation & movement

Videos can be used as background. You can also use the animation option in the right-hand menu and try out different options for animating the overlay into view.

Space is good

Keep it simple and don’t clutter your overlay with too many elements or text.

Complex shapes

Complex shapes or text can be exported from a design tool as PNG or SVGs

Image size

Keep images high-res but under 2MB.

Default close button

Turn off the default close button in the settings and upload your own design and turn it into a close button.

Minimum copy

Keep copy to a minimum when possible. Viewers are attracted to images and videos.

Troubleshoot Legal Hold issues

If you are facing issues while applying legal hold on your videos, here are some common error messages you can come across and steps you can take for troubleshooting them:

  • “Something went wrong. Our system timed out. Please re-upload your file.”
  • “System detects legal hold page is open in two browser tabs. Please close other tab.”
  • “Something went wrong. Please check your network connection and try your upload again.”
  • “Something went wrong. Invalid file type.”
  • “Something went wrong. Invalid user and video URLs found.”

“Something went wrong. Our system timed out. Please re-upload your file.”

If you’re seeing this error message, we suggest you try uploading again with multiple sets of smaller CSV files.

“System detects legal hold page is open in two browser tabs. Please close other tab.”

If you’re seeing this error message, try closing additional browser tabs, we suggest using only one browser tab while applying the legal hold.

“Something went wrong. Please check your network connection and try your upload again.”

If you’re seeing this error message, your browser or computer has lost connection. Check and refresh your network connection to make sure it’s up and running. Once reconnected try uploading the CSV.

“Something went wrong. Invalid file type.”

If you’re seeing this error message, you might have tried uploading a non-CSV file. Only CSV files are supported for legal hold.

“Something went wrong. Invalid user and video URLs found.”

If you’re seeing this error message, check for your user id. Try accessing the videos from your registered users ids.

Troubleshooting: Auto CC not generating in the correct language or at all

This article discusses common reasons why auto-generated captions would not generate for an uploaded video, and provides solutions to resolve the issues.

What is causing the Auto CC to fail?

These are the most common reasons Auto CC will not appear on videos, along with what to check for to fix the issue in the video file.

  • Audio is missing or difficult to hear: Check if the audio is present and clear in your source video file.
  • Multiple audio channels in the video file: If there are large gaps in the transcript, be sure to check that the video doesn’t have multiple audio channels by using editing software such as Adobe Premiere.
  • If so, try condensing the multiple audio channels into one and re-exporting the video.
  • Language detection failed: Check if there is spoken word within the first 30 seconds in the desired language. The language detection uses the first 30 seconds of the video to determine the set language.
  • Upload date: Ensure that the video was uploaded afterMay 2022; any videos that were uploaded before then will not have Auto CC generated. You can re-upload the video if you would like to generate Auto CC for it.

How to solve Auto CC failing

If you’ve identified one of the above as the cause of your Auto CC failing, adjust your video or settings as needed, then replace or re-upload your video to allow the captions to regenerate.

If you still have issues, contact our support team and be sure to include the following information:

  • Links to all impacted videos (or let us know if it’s all videos)
  • The desired language for Auto CC

Troubleshooting: Autoplay restrictions

If the autoplay parameter is present, the Vimeo player will attempt to begin playback automatically. However, some browsers specifically block autoplay. This article details each browser’s restrictions by expanding each panel below.

Safari version 11+ (Desktop)

  • Autoplaying videos must be muted.
  • Viewers can block or allow unmuted autoplay for specific domains on their setup.
  • Read more information from Apple at ‘Stop autoplay videos in Safari on Mac.’
  • Learn in detail about WebKit: Auto-Play Policy Changes for macOS

Chrome version 66+ (Desktop/Mobile)

  • Autoplaying videos must be muted.
  • Videos frequently visited by the viewer are permitted to autoplay with sound (based on Google’s scoring system).
  • Learn in detail about Google Chrome for Developers: Autoplay policy in Chrome.

If your video still isn’t playing, you may need to add the allow=autoplay parameterto the Vimeo iframe and any iframe in your webpage that the player is contained in.

This parameter is included in our default embed code, but if you’re working in another embed application or with multiple iframes, you may need to add it manually.

Example:

Please see Google’s Autoplay Policy for more information on the allow=autoplayparameter.

iOS (Safari, other mobile browsers, apps)

  • Autoplaying videos must be muted.
  • Autoplay is disabled when the iPhone or iPad is in Low Power Mode.
  • Learn in detail about WebKit: New

Firefox 66+ (Desktop/Mobile)

  • Firefox blocks videos with sound from playing automatically.
  • Viewers can block or allow unmuted autoplay for specific domains on their setup.
  • Learn in detail about Mozilla Support: Allow or block media autoplay in Firefox

Troubleshooting: Caption and subtitle issues

This article covers the most common issues you may come across when attempting to upload or playback caption and/or subtitle files.

  • Uploading
  • Unexpected Text Track Upload Type
  • Invalid Caption File
  • Playback
  • Replacing and deleting files
  • Can I enable more than one caption or subtitle file?

Uploading

If you encounter an error while uploading subtitles or captions to the website, please ensure that you are uploading a supported file type (SRT or WebVTT). You may receive one of the two following error messages if you attempt to upload a file type that isn’t supported (e.g., “.txt” or “.csv”), or if there are formatting issues within your file (e.g., HTML code or improper syntax).

Unexpected Text Track Upload Type

If you receive the “Unexpected Text Track Upload Type” error, double-check to make sure that you are uploading a file type we accept (SRT or WebVTT. After converting your document to an accepted file type, try uploading it again.

Invalid Caption File

If your file type is one of the supported file types, and you still receive the “Invalid Caption File” error message, please follow these troubleshooting steps to get your file ready to upload.

If you are using an SRT file, please convert it to a WebVTT file using the TextEdit (Mac) or Notepad (PC) application. You can follow these steps to convert your file:

  • Add the header WEBVTT followed by a line break at the top of the file.
  • Find (ctrl-F/cmd-F) the comma character (,) and Replace-All with the period character (.)
  • Copy-and-paste the content of the WebVTT file into this validator: Live WebVTT Validatoror use Happy Scribe for SRT files (without converting them to WebVTT format).
  • Make the appropriate changes for any errors the validator reports back.

Here are some examples:

Screenshot: hc-captionst-1.png

In this example, the “cue identifier” is the beginning timestamp and the ending timestamp. An error will be registered in the file if you add a line break after the timestamps.

Screenshot: hc-captionst-2.png

The beginning and ending timestamps must be written on the same line of text or you’ll see an error like the first one displayed in red above.

Additionally, the ending timestamp for a cue should not precede the beginning timestamp or you’ll see the second error message.

Finally, the beginning timestamp for a cue should not be equal to or earlier than the ending timestamp of the preceding cue. In the example above, the ending timestamp for line 3 is the same as the opening timestamp for line 4 (00:18.000), resulting in the error message.

Playback

If your subtitles or captions don’t appear during playback, make sure you’ve activated the caption file by toggling it on. You can toggle on the file by clicking the CC button underneath the video. Once it’s blue, the file has been activated.

If your file is active and you’re still not able to see your subtitles/captions, or if they are not showing as expected, please try these troubleshooting tips.

  1. First, download the file from the video’s settings page.
  2. If you get a 404 Not Found error, the file is not valid because the file was not uploaded completely or was not accepted by the system. Please delete the existing file and re-upload it.
  3. If you are able to download the file from the system, convert the file into a WebVTT file using the directions above. Then, paste the content of the file into the validator site.
  4. Once you’ve done that, make the appropriate changes in your document for any errors the validator reports back.

We recommend using TextEdit (Mac) or Notepad (PC) to make updates to your document. Here are some examples of common issues we’ve come across with subtitle/caption files:

Screenshot: hc-captionst-3.png

Screenshot: hc-captionst-4.png

Replacing and deleting files

Error message: “Something went wrong. Please try deleting your file again.”or“Something went wrong. Please try replacing your file again.”

  • You may see an error message if there was a loss in network connection while attempting to either delete or replace a file.
  • To resolve this issue, reset your network connection and try again.

Error message: “A caption or subtitle file with that name already exists, please rename the file and try again.”

  • If you attempt to upload a file with the exact same name as another caption or subtitle file that is already uploaded to your video, you will see this error message.
  • To resolve this issue, either rename the new file orreplacethe existing file with the new one.

Can I enable more than one caption or subtitle file?

You will see the error message “Please activate only one text track of a language and type” if you attempt to activate more than one caption or subtitle file. It is not possible to enable your own caption file as well as Vimeo’s autogenerated captions at the same time.

Troubleshooting: Caption file types

This article contains specifications for each common caption file type. If you are experiencing errors with your captions, check to make sure your file meets the requirements below. In this article:

  • WebVTT
  • SRT

WebVTT

Specs:

  • Files must begin with a valid signature (WEBVTT)
  • Timecode is represented as 00:00:00.000
  • Cues often (but do not have to) include a numeral identifier (e.g. 1, 2, 3, …)
  • Cues must have a content line (even if empty) followed by a break line

SRT

Specs:

  • Files must begin with the first cue’s numerical identifier (e.g. 1, 2, 3, …)
  • Timecode is represented as 00:00:00,000
  • Hours, minutes, and seconds are always written as two characters (07 not 7). Milliseconds are always written as three characters.
  • Cues must have a content line (even if empty) followed by a break line

What is causing extra voices or a change in pitch in AI-translated dubbed?

The most common reason you may notice an extra voice or change in pitch or tone is that the system is detecting extra voices when auto-detecting the number of speakers.

How to fix extra voices or a change in pitch in AI-translated dubbed audio

You can try to manually set the number of speakers when creating AI-translated dubbed audio, then re-run the translation.

To manually set the number of speakers being translated:

Screenshot: The translate video settings panel showing the Number of speakers dropdown open with the ability to select a number of speakers in the video. It’s the second dropdown menu in the panel.
  5. Proceed with running the AI translation.

Still having issues?

Troubleshooting: Failed AI Translations

This feature requires a paid plan.

If your Vimeo AI translations fail, you may see one of the following error messages:

  • AI Translation is not supported for this video’s language.
  • You can view the supported languages at What languages are supported by Vimeo AI subtitle translation? or What languages are supported by Vimeo AI’s audio translation?
  • Unable to process this translation; please try again.

If the Translate from drop-down field doesn’t populate anything, it typically means there is no transcript available for the system to translate. To fix this, you can:

  • Upload your own caption file in the video’s original language.
  • If there are already other AI translation files, be sure to set one of the files as the video’s original language.

If your video’s language isn’t supported, you’ll receive an error indicating that AI translation is unavailable. If the translation fails, you’ll be informed that Vimeo AI cannot process it.

Languages with successful translations will appear in the Languagesmenu on the video’s settings page.

If your translations continue to fail, please contact Support. In your message, please provide the following:

  • The link to your video.
  • The original language of your video.
  • The language(s) failing
  • Screenshots of any error messages you receive or any additional details to assist with troubleshooting.

Troubleshooting: Failed or slow video uploads

Several factors can affect the video upload process, including your internet connection, file format, and browser extensions. This article explains how to troubleshoot and solve common issues regarding failed or slow uploads.

  • How to fix failed uploads
  • How to improve the connection speed for slow uploads
  • Contacting Support for upload issues
  • Suggested next steps

How to fix failed uploads

If your video doesn’t upload completely, try uploading it again. If it fails a second time, try the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Ensure that you’re using the latest version of a supported browser.
  • Check that your file follows our compression guidelines.
  • Check for firewalls: If you are on a corporate or school network, ask your administrator to allowlist the following domains: *.vimeo.com, *.vimeocdn.com, *.akamaized.net, *.appspot.com, *.googleapis.com, *.google-analytics.com, and *.hopx.cedexis.com.

How to improve the connection speed for slow uploads

We do not limit upload speeds. If your upload is slower than expected, it may be due to local network traffic or ISP limitations.

Possible steps to improve connection speed include:

  • Turn off ad blockers or any extensions that might interfere with the upload.
  • Pause other bandwidth-heavy activities (e.g, streaming, gaming, etc.).
  • Rebooting your modem and router.
  • Switching from Wi-Fi to an Ethernet cable to rule out signal interference.
  • Use a speed test tool to check your upload bandwidth.
  • Internet speeds are measured in bits per second (Mbps), while file sizes are measured in bytes (MB). For example, a 500 MB file will take approximately 40 seconds to upload on a 100 Mbps connection.

💡Tip:Higher resolution videos may take longer to process. You may see standard definition versions first while the HD version finishes converting.

Contacting Support for upload issues

If none of these steps resolve your issue, please contact Support. Include the following information in your message:

  • A description of the upload issue you’re experiencing.
  • The size of your video file and its file format.
  • The troubleshooting steps you’ve already tried and their results.
  • A specific description of what happens when the upload fails.
  • A screenshot or link of the results of your speed test (if reporting slow uploads).

Suggested next steps

  • If your video is uploading but stuck in processing, refer to Troubleshooting: My video is stuck on the Optimization Pending screen.
  • Check theVimeo Status pagefor any site-wide issues.

Why can’t I see a download button on a video?

These are the most common reasons you may not see a download button on a video:

Troubleshooting: My account’s video storage usage increased suddenly after I changed plans

If you see your video usage suddenly increase after moving from the Plus plan to another plan such as Starter or Standard, it may be due to older versions of your videos becoming accessible in your new plan. This article will explain how to reduce your storage usage when this happens.

  • What is causing my video usage to suddenly increase?
  • How to fix the increase in my video storage

What is causing my video usage to suddenly increase?

If you ever replaced a video while on the Plus plan, you did not have access to that video’s previous versions, so they did not count toward your account’s storage usage. This feature is likely available on your new plan, making old versions of your video count towards your storage.

How to fix the increase in my video storage

To reduce your storage in this scenario, we recommend deleting old versions of videos that you no longer need stored on Vimeo.

If you need to keep these old versions accessible and stored on Vimeo, we have some other recommendations to help keep your storage in check when adding more videos to your account.

If your AI-translated video isn’t working as expected after your video processes, there are a few steps you can take to resolve the issue.

Troubleshooting steps
