Troubleshooting: My video didn’t convert properly when uploading

If you have successfully uploaded a video but it fails to convert or play properly, there may be an issue with the source file. This article explains common conversion errors and how to resolve them to ensure your video is accessible.

  • What causes conversion issues?
  • How to fix file corruption
  • How to fix variable frame rate and aspect ratio issues
  • Suggested next steps

What causes conversion issues?

Several technical factors can prevent a video from converting correctly after a successful upload. These include:

  • File Corruption: If the source file is damaged or corrupted, it can stop conversion or cause playback to fail mid-video.
  • Encoding Variations: Variable frame rates or non-square pixels can lead to sync discrepancies or unexpected aspect ratios.
  • Multiple Tracks:Files with more than one audio or video track can confuse the encoder, leading to random track selection.
  • Format Compatibility: Vimeo does not support the following file types for upload or conversion into a playable video:
  • PowerPoint or Keynote files (e.g., .key, .pptx, .ppt, .pptm)
  • Documents(e.g., .pdf, .txt, .doc, .docx, .xlsx, .xml)
  • DVD video disc information (e.g., .IFO, .ISO, .BUP)
  • Audio files(e.g., .mp3, .wav)
  • Project files (e.g., .wlmp, .prproj, .imovieproj, .camproj)
  • GoToMeeting files (e.g., .g2m)
  • Webex files(e.g., .arf or .wrf)

How to fix file corruption

Corruption can be introduced during shooting, editing, or exporting. To resolve this:

  1. Test the source file:Play your file in a player like QuickTime or VLC to see if it plays to the end without issue.
  2. Re-upload the video:If the file plays correctly on your computer, try re-uploading the video or replacing your video. Learn how to manage video versions and access history.
  3. Re-export or re-encode: If the error persists, re-export your video from your editing software or use a free tool like HandBrake to re-encode the file.

How to fix variable frame rate and aspect ratio issues

Vimeo converts all videos to a constant frame rate and square pixels. To prevent sync or display issues:

  • Set a constant frame rate:Ensure your editing software is set to export at a constant, rather than variable, frame rate.
  • Use square pixels:In your editor’s export settings, uncheck any options for “anamorphic” video to ensure your video displays with the correct aspect ratio (e.g, an HD 16:9 video displaying as SD 4:3).
  • Mix down tracks:Ensure you are uploading a single video and audio track by mixing them down in your editor before the final export.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn aboutcompression guidelines for optimal export settings.
  • Contact Support if you are still experiencing conversion failures. In your message, include the following:
  • A link to the video that you are experiencing issues with.
  • A summary of the unexpected behavior is in the video (preferably with timestamps), and what the expected behavior should be.
  • Check theVimeo Site Status page for site-wide issues.

Troubleshooting: My video editor is blank

If you encounter a blank video editor screen or are unable to proceed past the “preparing video for editing” screen, the following troubleshooting steps may assist.

  1. Verify Browser Compatibility: Ensure you’re using a supported browser (refer to the provided link for a list of compatible browsers).
  2. Whitelist Vimeo Domain: Confirm that “vimeo.magisto.com” is whitelisted within your network settings.

If the issue persists after completing these steps, please contact Vimeo Supportfor further assistance. In your message, please include additional information that will help our team best assist.

Troubleshooting: My video is stuck on the Optimization Pending screen

This article explains how to troubleshoot videos that remain on the Optimization Pending screen for an extended period when uploading or saving to the Library.

  • Why is my video stuck in Optimization Pending?

Why is my video stuck in Optimization Pending?

There isn’t a single universal cause, as the time a video spends in the Optimization Pending state varies due to multiple factors. The time required to complete video optimization is directly influenced by the source video’s or project’s size and encoding.

How to fix video optimization issues

If you notice that your video remains in the Optimization Pending state for more than 30 minutes, please verify that your video meets our compression guidelines. You can reupload your video if needed, or try saving it again from thevideo editor.

If reuploading or resaving your video doesn’t help and your video is stuck on the Optimization Pending screen for more than 30 minutes, please contact Support with the following information:

  • The video’s URL.
  • An estimate of how long the video was stuck on the Optimization Pending screen.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn how to troubleshoot uploading problems

Troubleshooting: Record issues

This article outlines common blockers with using Record and how to troubleshoot these issues.

  • Mac Recording Permissions
  • Windows Recording Permissions
  • Recording stuck in ‘Optimization Pending’
  • Record quality
  • No sound in the recording

Mac Recording Permissions

If you are using Mac OS Catalina or later, you may see the following error: “There was an error with screen capture. Check the permissions and try again, or visit the Help Center”.

To troubleshoot this issue, ensure that you are running the most current version of Chrome. If not, update your Chrome browser, restart, and try your recording once more.

If that doesn’t help, you may need to configure your system’s privacy & security settings.

  1. Open your System Settings.
  2. SelectPrivacy & Security, then select Screen and System Audio Recording.
  3. Ensure that Google Chrome is toggled on.
  4. Follow the same steps for the Microphone and Camera in Privacy & Security.
  5. You must quit and relaunch Chrome for the settings to take effect.

⚠️Note: If these settings are already on, try disabling these permissions for Google Chrome, saving your security settings, and then going back in and toggling it on for each again.

Windows Recording Permissions

Windows 10 users may encounter the error “There was an error with screen capture. Check the permissions and try again”.

Verify that your Windows system has granted recording permissions for both audio and video. For more information about app permissions, visit Microsoft Support at App permissions.

To check for permissions, refer to Microsoft Support for instructions on how to turn on app permissions for your microphone in Windows 10andmanage app permissions for your camera in Windows. Ensure that the Vimeo Record app can access your camera and microphone.

Recording Stuck in Optimization Pending

If your recording is showing ‘optimization pending’ and hasn’t completed uploading to your library, please reach out to Support for additional help or to request a recreation.

Record Quality

The video quality in a recording depends on your screen’s resolution and/or the maximum resolution of your webcam. After transcoding, the video is resized to fit the nearest resolution template, ensuring the best quality. The video will not be stretched to the highest resolution, such as 1080p, unless it matches the nearest resolution template.

Here are some tips on how to change your screen’s resolution to help maximize your recording potential:

Microsoft Support: Change your screen resolution in Windows

Apple Support: Change your Mac display’s resolution

Why doesn’t my recording have sound?

You must ensure that your browser is allowed access to your microphone. In some cases, you may see an error message stating that your browser blocks your microphone.

Visit the following links to read more about allowing your browser to record:

  • Firefox
  • Google Chrome
  • Microsoft Edge
  • Safari

You may also need to check that your device is not blocking your browser from recording.

Visit the following links to read more about allowing your device to record based on your operating system:

Microsoft Support: App permissions

Apple Support: Control access to the microphone on Mac

Still having issues?

If you continue to experience the same issues after trying the above steps or encounter an error message not mentioned, please contact customer support. Be sure to include the following information:

  • Screenshot of the error
  • Browser type and version
  • Device type and OS version

Troubleshooting: Remove white space above and below embedded video

When you are embedding a video using a responsive (default) embed code, you may encounter an issue where white space appears above and below your video player.

This white space is caused by the padding % at the front of the embed code. There are a few things you can do to remove this white space.

  • Custom dimensions: On the video settings page, select the privacy option from theShare button > Embed > Customize >toggle on Set custom dimensions You can edit the side of the player using the text boxes below the toggle.
  • Edit padding:You can manually edit the padding percentage in the embed code. If you know the height and width of the parent container, put the padding value as parentHeight/parentWidth %. Example: If the parent container is 5000 pixels x 10000 pixels, the padding would be 50%.

Below is a sample embed code with 50% padding:

<div style="padding:50% 0 0 0;position:relative;"><iframe src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/000?h=000&badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; gyroscope; accelerometer" style="position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:100%;" title="Tour of Ibiza"></iframe></div><script src="https://player.vimeo.com/api/player.js"></script>
  • Remove padding:You can entirely remove the padding from the default embed code if you wish by deleting the following from the beginning of the code: “padding:50% 0 0 0;position:relative;” Below is a sample embed code with no padding:
<div style= ><iframe src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/000?h=000&badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; gyroscope; accelerometer" style="position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:100%;" title="Tour of Ibiza"></iframe></div><script src="https://player.vimeo.com/api/player.js"></script>

If you continue to encounter issues with your embedded video, please contact our support team.

When contacting our support team for any embedding issues, include the following information in your support ticket:

  • URL of the embedded video
  • Link to the webpage where the video is embedded (along with any login information, if needed)
  • Method of embedding: Are you embedding the video using the HTML embed code or the video URL/direct file link?

Troubleshooting: Sharing video link results in the viewer being prompted to log in to watch my video

This article discusses how to troubleshoot log-in prompts or error messages when sharing video links. If you’re sharing a video link with a viewer and they’re seeing a prompt to log in or an error message, you can check a couple of things to resolve this issue.

What is causing the log-in prompt or error message?

This is the most common reason for this error message, and how to fix this issue.

  • Check if the video is missing a content rating. Videos without content ratings set may prompt viewers to log in before they can view the video due to regulatory requirements.
  • Add a content rating to your video to remove the login prompt for those viewers.
  • Check if the viewer has permission to view the video based on access.If your account is part of a team and/or a Workspace, and access to the video is for team members or Workspace members only, the viewer will need to log in to view the video.
  • Ensure that the video’s privacy and access settings are aligned with the viewer to whom you are sending the video. Visit these articles for more information:
  • About video privacy settings
  • How to enable account-level privacy restrictions

Still having issues?

Contact our support team and be sure to include the following information:

  • Links to the impacted videos
  • Screenshot/screen recording of the error message

Troubleshooting: Sharing videos from Vimeo to social media

If your videos aren’t displaying the correct thumbnail or title on social media platforms like Facebook or Twitter, an earlier version of your video was likely cached.

To resolve:

  1. To re-cache your video, run its URL through one of these tools:
  • Facebook: Link debugger
  • X (Twitter): Card validator
  1. Wait for about an hour, and then give your post another try.

⚠️Note:These debugger tools are intended to fix new posts moving forward. Posts created before using these tools will not be impacted.

Troubleshooting: Some Vimeo AI features are unavailable in my location

Some of our AI features are not available to users residing in the state of Illinois. These states have laws that prohibit the processing of biometric data without the individual’s express permission. Since Vimeo is unable to determine the identity of all individuals appearing in any given piece of content (some of which may not be Vimeo users), we cannot practically meet the requirements imposed by these regulations.

At this time, Vimeo AI features do not process “biometric data” to uniquely identify an individual (i.e., using data to identify the same individual across two different videos).

Troubleshooting: Source file unavailable to download

You must be logged in to Vimeo to download source files for Public videos. The source file option is not visible to logged-out users for Public videos. Logged-out users can instead download transcoded versions of Public videos in various sizes. For step-by-step instructions, see How to download a video.

Logged-out users can download source file links for Unlisted and Password-protected videos. If you would like to share a source file with someone who does not have a Vimeo account, you can change the privacy setting to Unlisted or Password. Or, you can send file links to download.

Troubleshooting: Why can’t I see the unmute button?

Here are a few conditions that dictate whether the unmute button appears on the video:

  • Video is muted
  • The video is auto-playing
  • Video can show controls (i.e. no background=1 or controls=0)
  • Video has audio

Unified Search

Vimeo’s search functionality has been upgraded to deliver a faster, more unified way to discover content. You can:

  • Search across both Library and public content from a single interface.
  • Easily toggle between My library, and Vimeo videos.
  • Refine results with advanced filters and sorting options.
  • Locate specific video moments using transcript-based keyword search.

This enhanced search experience helps streamline content discovery, whether you’re managing internal videos or exploring Vimeo’s broader video library.

Upload HDR, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision videos

High dynamic range (HDR) videos utilize a wider range of colors and luminance to deliver a high-quality image that mimics what the human eye can see. Standard digital videos are referred to as Standard Dynamic Range (SDR).

HDR and Dolby Vision videos can be uploaded to Vimeo in the same ways as any other type of video. However, your video needs to be edited and/or shot in HDR or Dolby Vision before upload to Vimeo.

  • Upload process for HDR and Dolby Vision
  • Source file requirements
  • Create videos in Dolby Vision
  • Create HDR and HDR10+ videos on Samsung

Upload process for HDR, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision

During the upload process, we will detect that your video is HDR or Dolby Vision based on metadata in your source file. Videos shot with HDR will only be transcoded to 4K even if the original video uploaded to Vimeo is 8K. The 8K playback quality will be available only if the uploaded video is in 8K Spatial format.

If a video is detected as Dolby Vision (Profile 8.4), it gets Dobly Vision and SDR renditions. If it’s detected as HDR10+, then it gets HDR10+ and SDR renditions. Otherwise, it gets regular HDR10 and SDR renditions. In each case, regular HDR displays will be able to fall back to static HDR metadata for displays that don’t support dynamic metadata.

The maximum output quality depends on the dimensions of your source file. Please note that Dolby Vision videos will not exceed 4K. If you would like to upgrade a video to Dolby Vision, you can use Apple Compressor to export a Dolby Vision file for upload.

Not seeing HDR or Dolby Vision after uploading

Please note that due to the multiple layers of transcoding required for HDR formats such as Dolby Vision, lower-quality files of your video will be available initially while additional transcoding takes place in the background. Be sure to allow extra time for your video to fully transcode to be available in Dolby Vision.

Source file requirements

In order to be considered HDR, your file must be tagged with color transfer characteristics and have a bit depth greater than or equal to 10.

We support both thePQ(SMPTE 2084) or HLG (AKA Hybrid Log Gamma or arib std-b67) transfer functions.

If using the PQ (SMPTE 2084) transfer function, please include the following metadata to ensure the most accurate display of your video’s colors on all devices (in SDR and HDR):

  • Mastering Display Color Volume (SMPTE 2086) —This metadata is typically added automatically in post-production and defines the color information about the screen on which your video was mastered.
  • Content Light Level (CEA 861.3) —This metadata is also included automatically in post-production and defines the peak brightness of your video sequence.

In order to be considered Dolby Vision, your file must be delivered as HEVC-10bit, HLG, and Dolby Vision 8.4. The Dolby Vision metadata is already included in the file.

⚠️Note: We only support Dolby Vision Profile 8.4, and we don’t support mixed Dolby Vision/HDR10+ videos.

Create videos in Dolby Vision

To create videos in Dolby Vision, you can capture, edit, and share your video with the iPhone 12, iPhone 13, and some iPad models. Visit our partners at Dolby to learn how to capture Dolby Vision and export Dolby Vision using an iPhone.

Creators can also create Dolby Vision content by capturing footage with an HDR-compatible camera and editing content using Final Cut Pro or other non-linear editing software. Apple Final Cut Pro and Apple Compressor can be used to export and convert existing HDR content in Dolby Vision. Please note that Dolby Vision export for Vimeo is not currently supported on Windows PCs.

Create HDR10+ videos on Samsung Galaxy

To read about creating HDR10+ videos on your mobile device, visit Samsung’s guide here.

Upload via FTP (Deprecated 2020)

You’ve arrived at this article because you were searching for information on uploading to Vimeo via FTP. As of December 2020, we’ve decided to deprecate this upload method.

There are several other ways to upload to Vimeo:

  • Using the upload page (upload).
  • Using a supported hosting service (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box). This option is suitable for those who store their videos in the cloud or are seeking a bulk uploading option.
  • Using a mobile app (iOS, Android, Windows Phone) or third-party software integrations (iOS, iMovie, Windows 10, and more). See how at Uploading Integrations
  • Using a custom-built application. This option is for unique uploading needs, and coding skills are required. Read more at our Developers Page

Use dynamic elements in interactive overlays

  • Introduction to Dynamic Elements
  • Get started with Dynamic Elements
  • Linking your API to elements in your overlay
  • Tips and Tricks for using dynamic elements

Introduction to Dynamic Elements

Dynamic Elements is a feature available in the interactive overlay panel to pull content from any open API and integrate it into the overlay. Dynamic Elements can also be linked to click-through URLs in element actions.

All elements will allow users to add their own content and mix it with content/action from the API. You can drop in an open API endpoint and immediately assign values to different overlay elements within your overlay.

Some benefits of using Dynamic Elements are:

  • Ingesting dynamic content into your overlays allows you to integrate deeper and connect more fully with your existing systems that manage your data, product, information, etc.
  • Building a more connected video asset
  • Always present your audience with the most accurate and up-to-date data and information available
  • Plug in any real-time, relevant data from a range of sources to your overlays
  • Scale up your interactive video production and save monumental amounts of time from manually updating your data and content

Get started with Dynamic Elements

To use Dynamic Elements, you’ll need two things:

  1. An open REST API returning JSON
  2. An interactive video that uses overlays

Once you have those, navigate to the Overlay Editor. You can find the Dynamic Elements button at the top of the page.

Clicking this will open the API manager where you can add, edit, and delete APIs associated with your interactive video.

To add an API:

  1. Click the Dynamic Elements button. The following modal window will open:
  2. Give your API a name
  3. Enter the URL to your API into the API URL field
  4. Click the + Add API button to add the API to your video.

You can add multiple APIs to your video, or, if your API supports it, filter the API responses by adding filtered API URLs.

Linking your API to elements in your overlay

To connect an overlay element to dynamic data from your API:

  1. Add a new or select an existing element of your overlay design. In the example shown below, a text element has been selected.
  2. In the right-hand menu, under the “Dynamic element” section, toggle the switch that says Link to API to reveal the Dynamic Element settings for that element.
  3. Select the API you want to link your element with from the API dropdown menu.
  4. Once you have selected an API, click + Add dynamic data.
  5. This will open the “Select a response” modal window. Here you can see the full API response called from the URL you entered. Use the arrows to reveal values from each of the items.
  6. Select the response from the API output by clicking the required field directly in the response, then click Confirm.
  7. In the case of the Dynamic Element feature for text, you’ll see the code shortcut generated in the text container while in edit mode. Note: On elements that are linked to an API, you will see the dynamic elements’ symbol displayed alongside the selection box.
  8. As soon as you exit editing mode for the text element the response will populate with the current data from the API value selected.

Tips and Tricks for using dynamic elements

  • If you don’t have an API or you need an API for a specific task that your current API does not support, look at tools such as Sheetlabs that can turn any spreadsheet into an API.
  • The Dynamic Element “interactive params” embed option is useful for customizing API queries, by passing certain queryParams you specify to call your dynamic elements APIs. For security reasons, please avoid using the interactive params feature to append API Keys. For more information, please visit our developer documentation.

Video and audio compression guidelines

This article provides best practices for video, color, and audio settings to use when compressing videos before uploading them to Vimeo. See the compression quickstart guide below for the most common settings.

⚠️Note: The best way to re-encode your file is to re-export it from the program you used to create it.

If your editing or encoding software does not offer export customizations (or you don’t have access to the software), you can use a free program like Handbrake (handbrake.fr) to re-encode your file. Read about How to use Handbraketo help avoid variation in upload quality.

  • Compression quickstart guide
  • Video guidelines
  • Color guidelines
  • Audio guidelines

Compression quickstart guide

This section provides a brief breakdown of recommended settings, but may not cover all use cases. See Video, Color, and Audio guidelines after this list for more exhaustive information.

  • Video Codecs:H.264, Apple ProRes 422 (HQ), or H.265 (HEVC)
  • Frame rate: Keep the native frame rate and choose a constant frame rate
  • Bit rate: Choose variable if possible and follow ranges based on your video’s definition
  • Resolution: Pixel aspect ratio of 1:1
  • Color Primaries and Matrix Coefficients: All accepted, but we recommend BT.2020 (Rec. 2020) or BT.709 (Rec. 709)
  • Color Transfer Characteristics: For HDR videos, we only support the PQ (SMPTE 2084) or HLG transfer function
  • Bit depth: 10 or greater
  • Scan type: Progressive, and recommend deinterlacing videos
  • Audio Codec: AAC-LC (Low Complexity AAC)
  • Data rate: 320 kb/s
  • Sample rate: 48 kHz

Video guidelines

Codecs

What is a Codec?

A codec is the technology that compresses (and can decompress) a file – in this case, a video file – so that its smaller size means faster uploads, downloads, and streaming playback over the internet. Most video production software will allow you to export your file using your choice of codec. Different codecs will compress a video file in different ways in order to most efficiently send the data over a network.

We accept files compressed using most major codecs, but for the best results, we recommend using one of the following:

H.264

H.264 is a standard codec that balances high visual quality with efficient file size. It’s a great starting point for encoding your videos as it ensures you’ll get the most out of your upload storage space while minimizing upload and conversion times. Be sure to choose the “High Profile” H.264 setting instead of “Main Profile.” Please note that the H.264 video codec only supports resolutions up to 4K.

Apple ProRes 422 (HQ)

This professional-quality codec ensures high quality for your encoded video but typically results in a much larger file size than H.264. If you notice quality issues with your H.264 videos and have ample storage space on your Vimeo account, using ProRes may produce a better result.

H.265 (HEVC)

H.265 or High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) is the successor to H.264, which offers a smaller-sized file with high visual quality at the cost of increased encoding time. The H.265 codec also supports resolutions up to 8K.

Frame rate

What is frame rate?

Frame rate is the measurement of how quickly several images (or frames) appear within a second, commonly referred to as FPS (frames per second). When preparing your video for upload, it’s best to maintain the video’s native frame rate when compressing your video. If your footage exceeds 60 FPS, we will automatically reduce the frame rate. If your video’s frame rate is automatically reduced, you may notice lower quality or choppy playback. Important: We recommend a constant frame rate throughout your entire video.

Always choose a constant frame rate rather than a variable frame rate. While we accept many frame rates (FPS), the most common ones are below:

  • 23.98
  • 24
  • 25
  • 29.97
  • 30
  • 50
  • 59.94
  • 60
Bit rate

What is the bit rate?

Bit rate (also known as data rate) determines the visual quality of the video and its file size by measuring the amount of data used to encode a single second of video.

If your video editing software gives you the option, choose a “variable” bit rate and select a value from the ranges below. You can experiment with different rates if your file is too large or if you’re not happy with the quality of your source file. Video quality and corresponding bit rates can be found in this table:

  • Quality
  • Bit rate (Mbps)*
  • SD
  • 2 – 5
  • 720p
  • 5 – 10
  • 1080p
  • 10 – 20
  • 2K
  • 20 – 30
  • 4K
  • 30 – 60
  • 8K
  • 50 – 80

We recommend setting the constant rate factor (CRF) to 18 or below. For ProRes, follow the standard presets in your video editor to export your file. For example, ProRes HQ for 1080p at 29.97 fps has a target bit rate of 220 Mbps in Final Cut. CRF is an encoding mode that adjusts the file data to achieve a selected quality level rather than a specific data rate.

Resolution

What is resolution?Your video’s resolution determines the level of detail - or pixels - in each frame. This can also affect the aspect ratio, or the shape of the frame itself. The more pixels, or dots, the more data an image contains. More data equals higher quality and a clearer picture.

Given the numerous kinds and sizes of screens on which your audience may be viewing your video, it’s important to consider the resolution. We recommend compressing your video with a pixel aspect ratio of 1:1, or square pixels.

Below are some of the most common formats:

  • Format
  • Resolution (px)
  • Standard Definition (SD) 4:3 aspect ratio
  • 640 × 480
  • Standard Definition (SD) 16:9 aspect ratio
  • 640 × 360
  • 720p HD 16:9 aspect ratio
  • 1280 × 720
  • 1080p HD 16:9 aspect ratio
  • 1920 × 1080
  • 2K 16:9 aspect ratio
  • 2560 × 1440
  • 4K UHD 16:9 aspect ratio
  • 3840 × 2160
  • DCI 4K UHD 17:9 aspect ratio
  • 4096 × 2160
  • 4K Monoscopic 360 2:1 aspect ratio
  • 4096 × 2048
  • 4K Stereoscopic 360 2:1 aspect ratio
  • 4096 × 2048*
  • 8K UHD 17:9 aspect ratio
  • 8192 × 4320

Stereoscopic video should be uploaded with the left and right views stacked on top of each other as 4096 x 1024 (4:1 aspect ratio) for each eye.

Color guidelines

What is color space?

Color space refers to the specific range of possible colors and luminance values within a video. During the transcoding process, color space informs how exact color values are reproduced.

For the most accurate color display on Vimeo, we recommend uploading a file that contains color space information using the settings described below.

⚠️Note: Some software may not offer control over your color settings.

Color primaries and matrix coefficients

What are color primaries and matrix coefficients?

Color primaries indicate the white point and the red, green, and blue primary color points for a video system. Matrix coefficients translate between RGB color space values and Y´CbCr values.

We support all color primaries and matrices, but we recommend BT.2020 (Rec. 2020) orBT.709 (Rec. 709). You can use the same value for both color primary and matrix coefficients. For Dolby Vision, set the color space to Rec. 2020 HLG.

Color transfer characteristics

About color transfer metadata and Dolby Vision

Color transfer metadata is usually added automatically in post-production. We further support the upload of encoded Dolby Vision files. Dolby Vision for Vimeo uses an HLG base layer with Rec. 2020 primaries and Dolby Vision dynamic metadata. Using Dolby Vision for Vimeo, the metadata is automatically included inside the file. There’s no additional metadata required for upload. The HLG transfer function enables backward compatibility with a range of non-Dolby Vision devices that support HLG playback.

We support a wide range of transfer characteristics for standard (SDR) videos, but for HDR videos, we only support the PQ (SMPTE 2084) or HLG transfer function. If using the PQ (SMPTE 2084) transfer function, please include the following metadata to ensure the most accurate display of your video’s colors on all devices:

  • Mastering Display Color Volume metadata (SMPTE 2086)
  • Content Light Level Information metadata (CEA 861.3).
Bit depth

What is bit depth?

Bit depth refers to the number of bits of data, expressed in 1s and 0s, used to record the color channels for each pixel of your video. A higher bit depth means that more shades of each color are available, while a lower bit depth means you are more likely to see sharp delineations between color changes in the images.

While we support various bit depths, we recommend a bit depth of 10 or greater for the highest quality results. For high dynamic range (HDR) and Dolby Vision videos, your file needs to have a bit depth of 10 or greater in order to be considered HDR on Vimeo.

Scan type

What is a progressive scan?

A progressive scan indicates the specific pattern in which lines of visual information are displayed across the viewer’s screen. With progressive scanning, all of the lines that make up a single frame are transmitted. With Interlaced scanning, lines of visual information are alternated, and only half of a frame’s visual information is transmitted at a time

Vimeo converts all videos to progressive for playback. For best results, we recommend deinterlacing videos prior to upload.

Audio guidelines

Similar to video codecs and compression, the codec you use to compress the audio of your video can affect how it sounds and the file size. Below, we’ve included our key recommended settings for encoding your audio.

Audio codec

For consistent results, we recommend using AAC-LC (Low Complexity AAC) for the audio codec.

Data rate

For consistent results, you may choose to encode your audio at 320 kb/s CBR, although this is higher than necessary to achieve transparent audio quality. Note that the appropriate data rate will depend on the number of channels, sample rate, and bit depth of your video file.

Sample rate

For best results, set your audio sample rate to48 kHz. The sample rate will be converted to 48 kHz if it is different in the uploaded file.

Video Settings analytics panel

This feature requires a paid plan on Vimeo.

The analytics panel in your video’s edit page shows you the most important analytics for your video from the past 30 days, helping you track performance and see how viewers are engaging with your videos.

  • Open the analytics panel
  • Overview of the analytics panel
  • Understand your view rate
  • Viewer retention stats

Open the analytics panel

You can open the analytics panel for any of your videos from your video’s edit page by clicking the Analytics button on the right side of the page.

Screenshot: analytics panel.png

The analytics panel will open from the right. To navigate to your full Advanced Analytics dashboard from the analytics panel, click Advanced report. Screenshot: advanced report.png

Overview of the analytics panel

Here’s a breakdown of everything in the analytics panel for Plus, Pro, Business, Premium, Starter, Standard, Advanced, and Enterprise members:

Live

If your video is an archived live event (Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise), you will see a Live section in your video analytics panel. The metrics in this section reflect viewership of your event when the stream was actively live.

  • Views: The number of times the live video started playing.
  • Peak viewers: The highest number of concurrent viewers during the stream.
  • Avg time watched: The average duration a viewer stayed on the live event.
  • Total time watched: The cumulative duration.

Video

The next section of the analytics panel is Video, which provides the following metrics about your video’s viewership from the last 30 days:

Screenshot: Example of video analytics over 30 days showing Views, Impressions, and View Rate

  • Views: The number of times the video started playing (in the last 30 days).
  • If the owner of the video is logged in while watching the video, then that is not counted as a view.
  • Impressions: The number of times your video was “loaded” on a Vimeo clip page or on a website it’s embedded on.
  • View rate: The rate at which a video is played after it is loaded on a clip page or embedded site.

Engagement

The last section of the panel is the Engagement section, which is available for members of the Business, Premium, Advanced, and Enterprise.

Screenshot: engagement_analytics.png

The metrics in this section allow you to track the performance of various interaction tools on your video, including:

  • Contact forms
  • Impressions: How many times the contact form screen was displayed
  • Submissions: How many times an email address was submitted
  • Rate: The number of submissions divided by the number of impressions
  • Cards
  • Impressions: How many times all cards on your video that included a link were displayed
  • Clicks: How many times any of the cards on your video that included a link were clicked
  • Rate: Number of clicks divided by the number of impressions
  • Call to action (CTA)
  • Impressions: How many times the CTA end screen was displayed
  • Clicks: How many times one of the links in your CTA end screen was clicked, with a breakdown of clicks for the primary button and secondary link
  • Rate: All clicks divided by impressions

Understand your view rate

The view rate for your video is your views divided by your impressions. We count an impression every time the Vimeo player loads your video, either on vimeo.com or embedded, and we count a view every time someone hits the play button on your video.

A video’s view rate can be significantly inflated or diluted by its audience and exposure. For example, if you share a personal wedding video with a close group of family and friends, it will likely have a high view rate because it is only exposed to people who have a strong interest in viewing it. On the other hand, if your video gains a lot of exposure from being embedded on a popular site, it will rack up a ton of impressions, which may dilute your view rate significantly.

⚠️Note: Vimeo does not display the view rate for your videos publicly.

Viewer retention stats

If you have a paid Vimeo membership, you can access viewer engagement stats when the Analytics drawer is open on the video page to learn more about how your video kept your viewers’ attention. Along the timeline of your video, you can see viewer retention stats along a line graph to help you determine what parts of a video are the most engaging. ⚠️Note:Viewer retention stats has moved from the old Classic Analytics Report and the old Video Settings page to the Analytics panel on the video page.

The following metrics are available for each timestamp:

  • Views: the number of times the video was played
  • % Watched: the number of viewers who watched a particular moment divided by the total viewers of the video

The graph and stats display the last 30 days of data, as does the rest of the information on the Analytics panel.

To learn more about viewer retention, see How to access your viewer retention stats.

Vimeo library overview

This feature is available for all Vimeo accounts, but specific options may vary based on your plan.

As a paid subscriber, you have two distinct libraries to help you manage your video content: My Library and Team Library. Each is designed for a specific purpose, providing you with a flexible and organized way to handle your personal and shared videos.

As a free user, you will have access to only one library. Upon upgrade, the library will become the Team Library, and you will gain access to a dedicated My Library space for your personal videos. This article summarizes the features of both libraries and how to use them.

  • What to know before using the library
  • My library
  • Team library
  • How to navigate to My library or the Team library
  • What actions can I perform in My library and the Team library?
  • Unified Search
  • Bulk changes
  • Individual changes
  • About additional features in My library and Team library
  • Making the most out of the Vimeo library
  • Sort your videos
  • Filter your videos
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before using the library

My library
  • My library is accessible to all users, both free and paid.
  • My library refers to a user’s private library within a specific Workspace. Workspace and Organization administrators can view these folders.
  • My library serves as a personal space where users can upload, create, manage, and save their content. This space cannot be renamed or deleted.
  • Owners, Admins, Contributors, and Contributor Plus (Enterprise only) can add content.
  • Videos uploaded, recorded, or saved to Vimeo go to My library by default unless chosen otherwise.
  • Users can share content, set privacy, move videos to the Team library, or keep them private for drafts.
  • Viewers can see My library, but they cannot add content until they are upgraded to Contributor or above.
Team library
  • The Team library is available for all paid plans, however, certain features require an Enterprise plan.
  • The Team library refers to a user’s team library within a specific Workspace.
  • The Team library, accessible from the home page, is for team collaboration, organising shared videos and folders, and knowledge sharing.
  • Owners and Admins can view all content uploaded by any team member within the Team library.
  • Contributor Plus (Enterprise only), Contributors, and Viewer roles need specific folder permissionsto access content in their Team library.
  • For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:If you are part of multiple Workspaces, your libraries’ content will match the Workspace you are currently logged into. To learn how to switch between Workspaces, visit How to switch between multiple Workspaces.

How to navigate to My library or the Team library

To navigate to either of the libraries:

  1. Click on the left navigation panel from your home page, within your selected Workspace.
  2. SelectMy libraryor Team library from the options.

What actions can I perform in My library and the Team library?

Unified Search

Vimeo’s search offers a unified and faster way to find content. You can:

  • Search both the Library and public content from a single interface.
  • Find specific video segments using keyword searches within transcripts.
  • Utilize filters and sorting options to refine results.
  • Easily switch between My library and public content views.

Read in detail about how to search your library.

Bulk changes

You can perform bulk actions on videos in your My library, Team library, or directly from search results within your Library. To select a video, check the box located on the left side of its thumbnail or row, depending on whether you are in grid-view or list-view.

Once you start selecting videos, the following bulk action options will appear:

  • Add to Showcase: Add selected videos to any of your existing showcases.
  • Move: Move up to 50 selected videos to a folder of your choice.
  • Read about folders at Organize videos into folders.
  • You can move videos from the Library to a folder.
  • You can move videos from one Library folder to another.
  • You cannot move videos back into the Library once they are moved out.
  • You can move folders to another folder or the library.
  • Privacy: Change privacy settings for up to 50 videos at a time. You can select Link privacy or Embed privacy as required. You can also choose to allow or disable downloads. Note that Vimeo Stock clips and Vimeo On Demand videos must remain private.
  • Delete: Permanently delete up to 100 selected videos from your account after entering your password (Only the Organization owner or admin can perform this action).
  • Translate subtitles and dub: Generate AI subtitle translations and/or dubbed audio in one or more languages for multiple selected videos at once. Available to team members on select Vimeo Enterprise plans. There is no hardcoded limit on how many videos can be processed in a single bulk action. For very large libraries, we recommend processing videos in chunks.
Individual changes

To make more detailed changes to an individual video, you can access its settings by clicking the video’s thumbnail in your Library. For more information, refer to Video settings overview.

  • Copy link: You can copy the link to your video and paste it wherever you want to share it.
  • Share:Click on share to open the video share modal to view who has access to the video and who can share it with others.
  • Video info: A side panel will appear on the right side of your screen. The panel will display a preview of your video, the title, team members with access, and Manage video button which will take you to the video settings page. There is also a Privacy section where you’re able to view the current video privacy as well as change it.
  • When in list mode, additional options for performing actions related to the video will become visible when you hover over it. In grid mode, they’ll appear in the top right corner of the video player.

About additional features in My library and Team library

Additional features are accessible from the Videos tab by clicking the ellipses (•••) icon. These features include:

  • Share: This icon, depicting an upward-pointing arrow, shares the video.
  • Copy link: Copies the video link.
  • Copy embed code: The </> icon copies the video’s embed code.
  • Analytics: A small graph icon leads to the analytics panel, displaying 30 days of data for the specific video. Further information is available at Vimeo Analytics.
  • Review links: Open the Review links modal tocreate and manage review links.
  • Download: Opens a modal for downloading all available versions of the video. This is not shareable.
  • Move: Relocates the video to a different folder.
  • Replace: Navigates to the Collaboration tab within the video’s settings, where the current file can be replaced with another. Versions can be compared on the Video review page.
  • Add to Starred: Stars the video/folder, ensuring it appears in the Starred folder on the left navigation panel of the home page.
  • Delete: Deletes the video.

Making the most out of the Vimeo library

Sort your videos
  1. Inside your library, select the Last modified dropdown in the top right corner.
  2. Choose from the options to sort your content by:
  • Title, A to Z
  • Title, Z to A
  • Last modified
  • First modified
  • Last added
  • First added
  • Longest
  • Shortest
Filter your videos

You can filter your videos by Type, Privacy, and Created by filters. You can use the Created by filter if you are on a team account and want to filter videos by creator in the Team library and folders.

  1. Go to your library from your Vimeo account and select the filter of your choice.
  2. To filter by Type, select your preference from the dropdown menu.
  3. To filter by Privacy, select one or more privacy options from the dropdown.

To filter your videos by theCreated by filter:

  1. From your home page, navigate to the Team library.
  2. Click on theCreated by filter dropdown.
  3. Select one or more team members from the dropdown menu.

Suggested next steps

  • You can create a manage folders within your library. For more information about this refer to About folder settings in the library.

Vimeo Player Cookies

The DNT parameter on a Vimeo Player Embed prevents us from setting any new cookies on your browser during that viewing session. However, it does not prevent your browser from sending cookies that were already stored from previous visits to Vimeo. Suppose you’ve previously watched a video without DNT enabled. In that case, your browser will automatically send those existing cookies with any new requests for Vimeo content, and this is a default browser action that we cannot control.

If you apply a DNT parameter to the player, the only cookies that will be set are player_clearance, cf_clearance, _cf_bm, and _cfuvid, as these cookies are considered essential to the secure operation of the player.

Vimeo’s embeddable video player sets the following cookies:

  • Cookie
  • Function
  • Expiration
  • vuid
  • Vimeo-generated ID used for generating analytics information for the video owner.
  • 2 years
  • player
  • Stores preferences for player controls (i.e. volume, stream quality, captions).
  • 1 year
  • flags
  • Specifies feature flags enabled by the video owner.
  • 1 year
  • [clip_id]_password
  • Stores an encoded password entered to authenticate a password-protected clip.
  • session
  • [webinar_uuid]_webinar_registrant
  • Stores the ID of a user who has registered for a webinar.
  • 7 days
  • lc_[hash]
  • Stores the ID of a user who has submitted information through a video registration form.
  • 7 days
  • player_clearance
  • Vimeo cookie used for bot prevention
  • 7 days
  • _cf_bm
  • Cloudflare bot manager manages incoming traffic that matches the criteria associated with bots.
  • 30 minutes
  • _cfuvid
  • Cloudflare cookie used to enforce rate-limiting rules.
  • session
  • cf_clearance
  • Cloudflare cookie used for bot prevention.
  • 1 year

You can find additional information on Cloudfare cookies in Cloudflare’s documentation.

What are playback segments?

You can choose to segment your video into parts that display a scrubber progress bar in the player relative to the duration of each part. For instance, if a playback segment contains the first 30 seconds of a video, your viewers will only see those 30 seconds reflected in the playbar while they are in that segment.

  • What are the benefits of using playback segments?
  • Getting started with playback segments
  • Tips and tricks for playback segments

What are the benefits of using playback segments?

  • Break your branching video down into segments for easier navigation of the playbar
  • Use alongside branching features (time triggers and hotspot actions) to create Playback Segments that can be navigated without allowing the viewer to see segments they shouldn’t
  • Use alongside chapters to create chapter segments for navigation of the timeline within each chapter

Getting started with playback segments

What will you need?

  • An interactive video
  • A list of the timestamps for all of the segments you want to create (you can compile this within the studio)

Use the segment editor

  • In the interactive editor, you can find the Playback segment button alongside the player controls.
  • Clicking this button will reveal the playback segmentation editor panel to the left, the segment timeline, and a dummy play bar that will show you how each segment will appear to viewers
  • In segmentation mode, you will see the video represented as one long segment, with the playbar representing the entire length of the video.

Create a second segment

  • Move the timeline needle (or manually enter the timecode) to where you wish the second segment to begin.
  • As you drag the needle, you’ll see the dummy playbar represent what the viewer would see with the current segmentation settings.
  • At the desired point in the video hit the ‘Add segment break at xx’ button to split the segment in two.
  • Notice the dummy playbar has now returned to the start. This is because you are now at the start of segment 2.
  • Continue to find the segment start points in your video, adding a segment break at each of these points until you have added all of the player segments required for your video

Delete a segment

  • You can delete any of your segments by hitting the trash icon alongside the segment time stamps. ⚠️Note: Any segments you delete will have an impact on the previous segment length.

Change a segment

  • You can change the start time of any segment by manually altering the time code in the segment start time input box.

Finish the segmentation

  • When you are finished creating your playback segments, hit the tick at the top of the playback segment panel.

Tips and tricks for playback segments

  • Segments must be more than 1 second in length.
  • At the end of each segment, the video will by default begin to play the next segment. If you want to keep your viewer inside a segment use time triggers with a pause or jump to actions at the end of each segment.
  • Chapters, time parameters, hotspots, and time triggers can move the viewer through segments.

What events do audit logs track?

This feature is available for Account Owners and Administrators on Enterprise accounts.

For Enterprise plans with Workspaces: audit logs at the Workspace level are limited to that Workspace; logs at the Organization level aggregate all Workspaces.

Audit logs give Enterprise admins a record of who did what, when, and to which asset across the account. This article lists the events your audit log tracks, explains how to read a log entry, and points you to the search and filter tools you’ll use to find what you need.

To open the log, go to Manage Team → Settings → Policies and Permissions → Audit logs. For step-by-step access instructions, see How to access and enable audit logs.

  • How to read an entry
  • Searching and filtering
  • What’s tracked
  • API parity

How to read an entry

Every entry shows the actor (with their avatar), the event, the affected object, and a precise timestamp (U.S. Eastern Time).

  • User avatars appear next to each entry so you can scan activity by person at a glance.
  • Clickable references let you jump straight from a log entry to the related asset — for example, the video page, folder, or showcase.
  • Privacy-change details are inlined: when a privacy setting changes, the entry shows exactly what it was changed to.
  • A “Vimeo impersonator” badge distinguishes actions taken by Vimeo employees in ModWorld from actions taken by your team. Use it to filter out vendor-side activity during incident reviews.

Searching and filtering

Two controls in the audit logs header help you focus on the records that matter:

  • User search — type a person’s name to see every action they took. Useful for off-boarding reviews, role-change investigations, or auditing a single team member’s activity over a date range.
  • Event-type filter — narrow the log to a single category (for example, only privacy changes or only downloads).

Both controls combine with the date range filter and the CSV export. See How do I filter and download my audit logs? for the full filter and export workflow.

What’s tracked

Audit logs cover the following event categories. Each category contains multiple specific events; the list below is a high-level summary.

Member management

  • Member invited, role changed, or removed
  • Hiring Committee and team-permission updates

Video lifecycle

  • Video uploaded, imported, published, replaced (new version), or deleted
  • Review-link created

Privacy and sharing

  • Video privacy changed (with the new value recorded)
  • Embed privacy changed
  • Video shared with a person, group, or via a link
  • Folder shared

Downloads and embeds

  • Video downloaded
  • Embed-related actions

Live events

  • Live event created, scheduled, started, finished
  • Live event privacy changed

Showcases

  • Showcase created, edited, deleted
  • Videos added to or removed from a showcase

⚠️Note: Audit logs do not contain activity that occurred before the feature was released or before your account was upgraded to Enterprise. Mobile video creation and download activity is not tracked.

API parity

Everything that’s API-applicable in the Audit Logs UI is also available through the Vimeo API. Specifically, on the API side we’ve:

  • Added new events — the API emits the full set of new event types tracked by the UI.
  • Added the ability to search the user of an action by email address or username.
  • Added the ability to filter by event name(s) — single or multiple.

If you care about the underlying log data and querying capabilities, you’re fully covered via API. The only things not exposed via API are presentation-layer improvements — user avatars, clickable references, the “Vimeo impersonator” badge, the redesigned layout — which wouldn’t make sense in an API response anyway.

For details, see How do I use the API to access audit logs? and the Vimeo Developer reference.

  • About Audit Logs
  • How to access and enable audit logs
  • How do I filter and download my audit logs?
  • How do I use the API to access audit logs?

What if my Vimeo membership purchased via the mobile app isn’t showing up on my account?

If you used the mobile app to purchase a membership (via Apple orGoogle Play), but it doesn’t appear in your Account Settings, and you keep seeing prompts to upgrade, it’s possible that your purchase hasn’t been updated on our backend yet.

To resolve this:

  1. Select your profile photo in the top-right corner of the app.
  2. On the profile menu, scroll down to the bottom of the page and select Restore (Android) / Restore purchase (iOS).
  3. This will actively fetch your purchase information and update it on your account.

If this doesn’t work, please contact Support and provide the exact steps you have taken so we can investigate further.

What interactive features are available with my plan?

Several features are available within the Interactivity panel on the video settings page. Your access to these features depends on your Vimeo plan type.

Open your video from your Library and select Interactive on the left of the page to open the Interactivitypanel.

The sections below contain a breakdown of which features are available by plan type.

  • Chapters
  • Forms
  • Cards
  • End screens
  • Interactive studio

Chapters

Chapters are available to Vimeo members with a Pro, Business, Premium, Starter, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise plan. See How to use chapters for more information.

Enterprise members also have access to automatic chapter suggestions.

Forms

Forms are available to all Vimeo members with a paid plan. If you have a Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced, or Enterprise plan you can use marketing integrations with contact forms. See How to add a contact form to your video for more information.

Cards

Cards are available to Vimeo members with a Business, Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise plan. See How to add cards to videos for more information.

End screens

End screens are available to Vimeo members with a Plus, Pro, Business, Premium, Standard, Advanced or Enterprise plan. Visit How to change my video’s end screen.

Interactive studio

Interactive studio contains a suite of features including hotspots, time triggers, and interactive overlays. You need an Enterprise plan to access this feature. Visit What is interactive video? to read more.

What is a custom payload for interactive videos, and how can I use it?

You can insert custom data into the custom payload field(s) inside a hotspot or an overlay element. Set up your hotspot or button action as you normally would, but toggle on Add custom payload data. This will allow you to then add keys & values as your primary action. This could be useful when looking to add additional tracking to your video.

When you listen to the interactive events in the Vimeo Player API (see documentation) you will be able to see the custom data surfaced and use it in whatever way you like.

What is a hotspot?

Interactive is only available with custom Enterprise accounts. Please contact your account manager if you are interested in creating interactive experiences with your videos.

When using interactive, a hotspot is a visible call to action on your video that acts as a ‘hitbox’ that when tapped triggers an action. You can add a hotspot to anything such as people, objects, or products to make your video interactive. You can choose to move your hotspot as your object does or set it to a fixed position.

Types of Hotspot

Interactive offers two types of hotspots.

  • Sticky Hotspots: These types of hotspots stick to people or objects as they move. You can see a higher viewer activity on sticky hotspots compared to static ones.
  • Static Hotspots: These are anchored to a fixed position in the video frame and don’t move. You can decide when you want them to appear on the video/image.

You can use the save interactive settings button to save the hotspots and overlays you’ve designed for a given project as a template for use later on.

Save Interactive settings

You can save elements from an interactive video (hotspots, overlays, and time triggers) as a template for future use. This feature will help you save time by reducing the need to design elements from scratch.

To save your video’s settings as a template:

  1. Select the Saved Settings option in the upper right-hand cornerof the screen.

  2. From here, you’ll be prompted to assign it a name before saving.

  3. You can apply your settings to a new video once you’ve saved your settings. When you open a new project in the studio, click on the Saved Settingsagain and select the Apply Saved Settings option.

  4. You can select the settings you want to apply to your video.

What is a time trigger?

This feature requires an Enterprise account.

Time trigger is a feature on interactive that allows you to specify points in the video when actions occur.

Time trigger actions happen when playback reaches a specific time and don’t require viewer interaction. These actions include:

  • Opening an overlay
  • Pausing the video
  • Jumping to a different point in the video.

Time triggers are ideal for automatically displaying overlays or pausing or looping the video while the viewer chooses a branching video.

⚠️Note: When comparing FPS to milliseconds, be aware that time-trigger input values may behave differently than expected due to variations in the rendering engine process.

Screenshot: mceclip1.png

What is classic interactive video?

This feature requires an Enterprise plan.

Classic interactive video allows you to take your videos to a new level of engagement by adding call-out areas that act when your audience clicks or taps on them. Any video on your account can become interactive.

⚠️Note: A video that is longer than 4 hours cannot be used in the Interactive studio.

You can add clickable hotspots that can open overlay panels, jump to other points in the video, or open other websites, all from within the interactive Vimeo player. You can also create time triggers, which perform a function at a given point in your video without your viewer needing to do anything, such as automatically pausing or looping the video, or displaying an overlay.

You can use the save interactive settings button to save the hotspots and overlays you’ve designed for a given project as a template for use later on. You can access your custom fonts in the interactive studio

Classic Interactive video is available as an option for Enterprise accounts. If you are on Vimeo Enterprise and interested in making your videos interactive, contact your account manager for the next steps.

What is my view rate?

The view rate for your video is your views divided by your impressions. We count an impression every time the Vimeo player loads your video, either on vimeo.com or embedded, and we count a view every time someone hits the play button on your video.

A video’s view rate can be significantly inflated or diluted by its audience and exposure. For example, if you share a personal wedding video with a close group of family and friends, it will likely have a high view rate because it is only exposed to people who have a strong interest in viewing it. On the other hand, if your video gains a lot of exposure from being embedded on a popular site, it will rack up a ton of impressions, which may dilute your view rate significantly.

⚠️Note: Vimeo does not display the view rate for your videos publicly.

What is the difference between upload quota, video usage, and total storage?

The amount of video content you are entitled to have on your Vimeo account is measured differently based on which plan type you have and, in some cases, when you first created your account. This article will outline the different ways video limits are measured based on the plan you have.

If you’re not sure which plan you are on or when you created your account, check the upper left-hand corner of your account settings.

Total storage (most plans)

Most plans–Starter, Standard, and Advanced accounts created on or after June 17, 2024; Plus, Pro, Pro Unlimited, Business, Premium–are granted a lifetime total storage cap, measured in gigabytes (GB) or terabytes (TB). This means you can store as much content as you want in any timeframe until you reach your plan’s total limit, as long as you are still subscribed to the plan.

  • You will not be able to upload any more videos once your account reaches the total storage limit.
  • The total storage does not reset or renew.

Video usage (Free, Starter, Standard, Advanced accounts created before June 17, 2024 and maintained a paid subscription) You can check your sign-up date in the upper left-hand corner of your account settings.

If you are on a Free, Starter, Standard, or Advanced plan and you created your account before June 17, 2024, you are granted a set number of videos that you can add to your account. These plans do not limit you by upload quota, storage, or file sizes. Once you’ve added the number of videos your account is allowed to have, you cannot add any more videos.

Weekly upload quota (some Plus and Pro accounts)

We have started migrating Plus and Pro users to total storage in lieu of weekly quota. You can check your plan’s storage using the tracker in the lower left-hand corner of your account’s home page, library, or video upload page.

A few legacy Plus and Pro plans are granted a specified amount of video storage you can upload per week. This quota resets every seven days, starting with the day you subscribed to the plan.

  • If you reach your upload limit within that seven-day period, you will not be able to upload until your quota resets. You can track when this occurs by hovering over the tracker in the lower left-hand corner of your library.
  • There is no total storage limit for the lifetime of Plus and Pro plans with weekly upload quota.

What is the Enterprise Data Retention Tool?

For Enterprise Accounts with Workspaces:This feature is managed at the Organization level by Organization Owners and Admins. For more information, visit How to edit my Organization’s settings.

Vimeo’s Enterprise Data Retention tool allows account owners and admins to apply data retention policies to folders and user groups in your account. The videos associated with these folders & groups will be automatically deleted after the duration specified by your data retention policy. The data retention tool helps you to get rid of any outdated and irrelevant videos based on your selected policy and duration, helping you better manage your video library as well as the risk associated with user-generated content.

Features of the Enterprise Data Retention Tool

  • Account owners and admins can create new and edit existing data retention policies. Contributors and viewers do not have access to the enterprise data retention tool.
  • Retention policies can be applied to folders and/or groups in the account. The videos uploaded in the “Private to me” folders by users in these groups will be deleted based on the duration set by the retention policies.
  • The videos in each folder/group will be deleted based on the duration set by the retention policy. The video will be deleted once that duration has elapsed after the video has been uploaded.
  • For new default policies, both existing and new content will be affected, meaning videos older than X days/years will be automatically deleted unless they are in a folder or owned by a group with a different policy.
  • Retention policies can be set for the desired time period of days, months, or years. You cannot create a policy of fewer than 7 days or more than 50 years.
  • Admins are able to recover videos that data retention policies have deleted in the last 30 days. They can also view a history of videos that have been deleted by data retention policies if they were deleted over 30 days ago.

Owners and Admins can also set a legal hold on specific videos that prevents them from being deleted (both by a user or by a retention policy) in case the video is being investigated for legal reasons.

What is the Record Studio?

Some features of the Record Studio require a paid Vimeo plan - Standard and above or Pro and above.

The Record Studio helps you record a video using your device’s camera, screen, or both within your web browser. In the Record Studio, you can also write or generate a script using AI and use the script on a teleprompter.

How to access the Record Studio

You can access the Record Studio by selecting the Record quickstart icon from the Vimeo homepage.

💡Tip: Enterprise users can find the Record Studio by selecting the “New” dropdown button at the top right of their Vimeo homepage and then selecting “Record Screen.”

Navigating the Record Studio

  • On the top bar of the Record Studio, you can select which team and folder to save your recording to. You can also view/change the privacy settings for your recordings or install the Record Studio Chrome extension. Selecting Start Recordingwill begin your recording session. ⚠️Note: Privacy settings for record studios default to Unlisted. You can change this setting at any time under privacy settings.
  • The canvas is in the middle of the Record Studio. This is where you can view the layout of your recording and customize its elements, such as your camera’s view and the screen you are sharing.
  • The Inspector toolbar is located above the canvas, centered in the Recording Studio. Here, you can set elements of your recording, such as the layout or background color, or change the aspect ratio of your video. The buttons in this toolbar are dynamic and can change based on your recording.
  • The input controls are at the bottom of the Record Studio, under the recording preview. Here, you can find the controls to select which camera and microphone to use for your recording. You can also select which screen you’d like to share and view a preview of your recording. Finally, you can show the teleprompter or start using the Picture-in-Picture setting.

Read more about using the Record Studio at:

What should I do if I received a copyright notice when posting my video made in the editor to social media?

Soundtracks in the stock music library are royalty-free and licensed for commercial use.

Videos made in the editor can be published on social media platforms (Facebook, YouTube, etc.) without a problem as long as they are published directly from Vimeo using thePublish to Socialfeature - this way Vimeo can ensure that the license is recognized.

When publishing a video directly from the Vimeo editor, Vimeo has the ability to add a “clearance” tag to the videos and whitelist it so that the algorithms on YouTube, Facebook, and other platforms won’t detect the soundtrack/content as a copyright infringement.

Once a video made in the editor is downloaded from Vimeo and then uploaded as a file, Vimeo does not have the ability to whitelist it. This is why those videos are prone to be detected as copyright infringement by the algorithms. Vimeo has no way of “clearing” a video that was downloaded from Vimeo and manually uploaded to a third-party platform.

As an alternative, you can also dispute the claim on that platform, informing them that the soundtrack was taken from Vimeo’s music library as part of the creation process.

In the rare case where your video was shared directly from Vimeo and you still received a copyright notice/claim (note that this might happen when the videos are shared in “private” mode), you can either dispute it and mention that you made the video using the Vimeo editor, or you can contact us and send us the following information, so we can release it for you:

  1. The link to your video on the third-party platform (YouTube, Facebook, etc.)
  2. The link to the video on Vimeo.
  3. A screenshot of the copyright claim.

Once we receive the required information, we’ll be able to take care of this with our music provider and the social platform.

⚠️Note: If the video was incorporated into a live stream video, Vimeo will not be able to clear/whitelist the soundtrack and you will need to dispute the claim on your own.

In addition, if you upload your own music, we won’t be able to provide you with a commercial license.

What should I do if my media takes too long to upload to the editor in the Editor?

  • Photo file formats: JPG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, PNG, non-animated GIF
  • Video file formats: 3GP, AVI, MOV, MP4, MPG, MTS, M2TS, WebM
  • Audio file formats: MP3, M4P, WMA, ADTS, OGG, WAV, WAVE

In case your file format is not supported, you may use any online format converter to convert it into one of the above formats.

Check your internet connection

Uploading footage, especially of a large size, requires a strong and stable internet connection.

An intermittent internet connection might slow down the uploading process or cause it to fail before it is completed. In this case, here’s how this can be resolved:

  • On the mobile apps: Turn off the Wi-FI and try uploading the footage using the Mobile Data.
  • On the Web platform: Switch to a different Wi-Fi network or try connecting with a LAN/Ethernet cable.
  • Check for pop up blockers/extensions (Web/desktop platform):If the browsing window does not open when trying to upload footage from your computer’s storage or if the footage is not being added, it is possible that you have certain pop-up blockers or extensions installed on your browser that are preventing this from being performed.
  • Try disabling those by following these instructions and then try uploading the footage again:
  • Chrome: Disabling pop-up blockers / managing extensions
  • Safari: Disabling pop-up blockers / managing extensions
  • ****⚠️Note: On Safari, the AutoPlay settings need to be configured to “Allow All Auto-Play” to avoid uploading issues.

Check if your footage is stored on iCloud (iOS)

On iOS devices, the iCloud backup is set as Active by default and your footage is being backed up to your iCloud account. When you try to add footage that is stored on iCloud to your video, the editor tries to download this footage to your local storage to be able to use it.

This situation might not be successful in cases of issues connecting to your iCloud account.

To resolve this situation, you may follow one of the below options to work around it:

  1. Download the footage you’d like to use in your video from iCloud, so you have a full copy of it stored locally on your device (see more from Apple Support atDownload iCloud photos and videos).
  • You can also choose the “Download and Keep Originals” option on your Photos settings to prevent this from happening in the future. Just note that this option requires that you have available storage on the device.
  1. Download the original footage from iCloud onto a regular desktop computer and make a movie using our website.

In case any of the above does not work, please contact our support team and share the exact steps taken in attempting to resolve the situation so we can further assist.

What type of images can I upload for a hotspot?

Interactive is only available with custom Enterprise accounts. Please contact your account manager if you are interested in creating interactive experiences with your videos.

Interactive supports hotspots in formats .jpg, .png, .gif, .svg (animated .gif and animated .svg). However, we recommend using SVG graphics due to the scaling capabilities of that image format. We also support customed designed hotspots created in Illustrator, Photoshop, or Figma.

We export custom hotspots as SVGs.

  • SVG’s are recommended if possible as they scale (JPG, PNG, and GIF will also work but might not scale as well on different screen sizes).
  • You can design for a normal state and a design for a hover/rollover state. This is a good way of letting the audience know that your video is interactive.

What types of video content count towards my video storage allowance?

Not all methods of adding videos to your account will count against your weekly quota, video usage, or total storage allowance. Which allowance type you have varies depending on which plan your account is on. This article outlines which types of video content count towards your video limit and what does not, depending on what type of storage allowance your plan has.

You can verify how your account measures video limitations by checking your account settings or the tracker in the lower left-hand corner of your library.

Total storage (most plans)

  • Uploading a new video: Yes
  • Making a video in the editor:
  • Starter, Standard, Advanced: Yes
  • Plus, Pro, Business, Premium: No
  • Recording a video: No
  • Streaming an event: Yes, when archived
  • Replacing a video: Yes

Video usage (Free, Starter, Standard, and Advanced accounts created before June 17, 2024, and maintained a paid subscription) You can check your sign-up date in the upper left-hand corner of your account settings.

  • Uploading a new video: Yes
  • Making a new video in the editor: Yes
  • Recording a video: No
  • Streaming an event: No
  • Replacing a video: No

Weekly upload quota (some Plus and Pro accounts)

  • Uploading a new video: Yes
  • Making a video in the editor: No
  • Recording a video: No
  • Replacing a video: Yes
  • ⚠️Note: If you replace a video, then later switch from Plus to another plan, you may notice your account’s storage usage suddenly increase. This is due to previous versions of your video now being accessible in your new plan.

What’s the difference between Vimeo impressions and third-party impressions?

Using the Vimeo player allows you to take advantage of advanced analytics that are recorded through the player. When the Vimeo player is not utilized (for example, using direct file links to play hosted videos in other players), advanced analytics tracking is not accessible through Vimeo.

As of August 7, 2024, Vimeo analytics will separate the counts of impressions and views from those generated by the Vimeo player and videos distributed on third-party players. Previously, impressions from third-party players were included in the Impressions metric, and view counts from third-party players were estimated based on these impressions.

Now, you will see a new metric called Third-party impressions in your Analytics Reports, which is the total count of impressions from videos loaded in third-party players using direct file links. Impressions and Views will only count analytics from the Vimeo player as of August 7, 2024.

Third-party impressions can be viewed and downloaded in Analytics reports, as well as accessed through the Analytics API.

Screenshot: third-party tooltip.png

Why am I being prompted to upgrade when saving a video?

While the video editor is available to all Vimeo members, certain features can be accessed only with specificmembership tiers. Those features include accessing our stock library, and brand kit, and hiding the Vimeo watermark.

When using a feature that is not included in your subscription, you will be prompted to either upgrade your account or continue working on your video and upgrade later.

Will Vimeo use my videos to train generative AI models?

Vimeo will not allow generative AI models to be trained using videos hosted on our platform without your explicit consent, even if you use our free offerings. We also prohibit unauthorized content scraping (by model companies) and continue to implement security protocols designed to protect user-generated content.

Read about Vimeo’s position on AI on our blog at ‘Vimeo’s position on AI’.
