Create coupon codes for transactional products on Vimeo OTT

You can offer all of your customers a fixed percentage on transactional products (TVOD) such as rentals and direct purchases, similar to subscription product promotions.

  • How do I create coupons for transactional products?
  • What are coupons?
  • Campaigns
  • Creating coupons
  • Editing a coupon
  • Deleting a coupon
  • Downloading random coupon codes
  • Redeeming a coupon code

How do I create coupons for transactional products?

Follow the steps in this video to create coupons for your transactional products

What are coupons?

Coupons let you offer discounts on transactional products and track how they’re being used. Here at Vimeo OTT, we use the term “coupons” exclusively to refer to promotions for TVOD (buy/rent) products.

You get 100 free coupons per month to give out. After that, they are $1 per redemption charged to your credit card.

Campaigns

Create codes for promotional partners, festivals, events, weekend specials, and more. Here’s what we’ve seen:

  1. Contests - Doing a contest for a giveaway on social media? Use coupons to give out the winnings.
  2. Weekend specials -Create a coupon for a weekend flash sale
  3. Festivals - Going to Sundance or SXSW? Give out custom codes there for a discount on your movie.
  4. Merchandise sales - Include free unique coupons in your physical merchandise so customers can also download the file from your site.

Creating coupons

  1. From your site’s admin page, go to your Products tab drop-down menu and select Promotions.
  2. You will be presented with managing several promotional tools; select Manage Coupons under Transactional Coupons
  3. The next page is where you can manage your existing and deactivated coupons. Select Create Coupons.
  4. Next, you’ll be presented with the following fields:

  • Campaign name: Name your campaign (e.g., Weekend Special)

  • Coupon Type: Select Custom or Random

  • RANDOM coupon codes will give you a list of unique codes that you will be able to mail or give out to a group of people. Each code is different from the others. These are great for including inside the DVD and Blu-ray cases of your movie for digital access.

  • CUSTOM coupon codes are fixed and set by you and can be used as many times as you specify. These custom codes are really nice for public giveaways or promos, with a set limit.

  • Note: Coupon codes must be alphanumeric and cannot contain special characters.

  • Quantity: the number of coupons you want to allow redeemed

  • Coupon code: this is what your customers will use to redeem at checkout, e.g. WKNDSPECIAL (If you selected Random, this will be grayed out.)

  • Redemption type: Select Purchase or Rental

  • Select if you want the redemption type to be for the rentalor the purchase of the product. If you only have one of these configured for your product, that will be automatically selected.

  • Discount: Select Discounted or Free. If discounted, set the amount of the discount

  • In order to accommodate international currencies, we no longer support a fixed dollar amount. However, if you previously created a coupon code with a fixed dollar amount, the codes will still be redeemable.

  1. When you are satisfied with all of your coupon settings, click Create. After doing so, you can only update the campaign name, increase the quantity, or delete it.

Screenshot: image1.png

Once the coupon is created, you will be directed to the general coupons page where you can check on your newly created coupon.

Screenshot: image2.png

Editing a coupon

  1. Navigate back to Promotionsand selectManage Coupons
  2. On the right side of the coupon, click the options icon (•••) to open a drop-down menu, then click Edit.
  3. On this edit page, you can:
  • Change the Campaign Name
  • Increase the Quantityof the coupon (you cannot decrease the number)
  • Delete the coupon. This will make all of the unredeemed codes no longer redeemable.

Deleting a coupon

  1. On the coupon manage page, hover over the options icon (•••) and click Delete on the drop-down menu.
  2. There will be a pop-up message to confirm the deletion; click OK.
  3. The coupon will be deleted and a confirmation banner will appear at the top of the page.

Downloading random coupon codes

If you created Random coupons, you can download the codes from the main coupon page:

  1. On the right side of the coupon, click the options icon (•••) for the drop-down menu, then select Download codes
  2. You will see a banner confirming that we will e-mail a .CSV file with the codes
  3. Check your e-mail for a message with the subject: Your CSV with coupon code data is ready!

Below is a preview of what your CSV can look like.

Screenshot: image3.png

Here is what each column provides:

  • Column
  • Definition
  • code
  • Random code that is generated to be used at check-out
  • active
  • TRUE - is available to redeem FALSE - not available to redeem
  • user_email
  • User email will populate here once the code is redeemed
  • redemption_link
  • Direct link to check out with the code redeemed

Tip: If you change the number of codes after downloading the initial CSV file, you will need to re-download the codes to get an updated CSV.

Redeeming a coupon code

If a customer needs help with redeeming a coupon code, here’s how they would do it:

  1. Go directly to the desired product to buy or rent.
  2. Ensure that the correct purchase type is selected.
  • For example, if you’ve advertised your coupon for Purchases only, then the customer should select the Buy option (instead of rent).
  1. The customer will need to enter their email address and payment information.
  2. Under the payment details, click the ☑ Promo Code. checkbox.
  3. Enter the coupon code and click APPLY.
  4. If the code is 100%, the customer can click Redeem Now and watch immediately without entering payment information.

Create promos for a subscription product on Vimeo OTT

Promos allow you to attract new customers by offering them a discount on your content, either for a set period of time or for as long as they remain subscribed.

A few things to keep in mind about subscription promos

  • You will be charged a subscription fee for viewers who subscribe through a 100% promo.

  • It is only possible to offer promos for subscriptions purchased via the web. If you offer branded apps, in-app purchases do not support promo codes at this time.

  • Promo codes can be applied both to subscriptions purchased directly and to gift subscriptions.

  • By default, Customers cannot use more than one promo at the same time. Customers have to wait until the current promo ends and then apply for the new one. If you would like to change this behavior, you can choose to Allow Queued Promo Codes

  • If you have set up both a free trial and a promo for your content, the promo will be applied after the free trial period.

  • How do I create a promo?

  • How do I extend a promo?

  • What are my actions and options for promos?

  • How do I allow for queued promo codes?

  • Applying a promo to a customer’s account

How do I create a promo?

Before creating a promo, you will need an available subscription product with videos within a Collection. Then follow these steps:

  1. Within the Vimeo OTT Admin, click Products > Promotions. Screenshot: image5.png
  2. Next to Subscription promos, click Manage promos. Screenshot: image3.png
  3. On the next screen, click + Create promo. Screenshot: image4.png
  4. Configure the settings of your new promo in the General tabof the Promo settings page: Screenshot: image2.png
  • Campaign Name: This is for internal use and will appear on the promo page in your site admin.
  • Promo Redemption:Choose which type of subscriber is eligible to use this promo (only new subscribers, only existing subscribers, or both).
  • If you are leveraging our Membership Subscription feature, you will also see eligibility options for users who are “upgrading” from the standard subscription tier.
  • Start date: Choose when this code will go live.
  • End date (optional):Choose when the code will expire. If you do not set an end date, the promo will end when the quantity runs out (set on the next page).
  1. Once you have saved your general promo settings, move on to the Details tab, where you can choose between Custom or Random for your promo code type.
  2. Click Custom to create a promo code for mass usage, then an alphanumeric string of up to 20 characters in the text box below. Screenshot: image1.png ⚠️ Note: Promo codes cannot contain special characters. Shorter codes are easier to remember.
  3. Click Random to create a set of auto-generated codes you can give out to individuals for one-time use.

Screenshot: image6.png

  • If you’d like, you can add a prefix to your code, which is 10 alphanumeric characters that would appear at the start of all of the codes generated. For example, if you were doing a Fall promo, you could make it FALL15, and all the promo codes would start with that prefix, followed by the randomly generated code.
  1. Configure the following:
  • Subscription Type:Select which subscription types the promo code applies to: Monthly, Annual, or both. If both are selected, the code can be used for either billing option.
  • Discount: There is an input field where you can input the discount percentage. You can select a partial discount (e.g. 15%) or Free (100% OFF)
  • Duration: Choose the number of months the discount will apply before renewing at the full price. You can also select “Forever”
  • Quantity: Custom promos determine how many subscribers should be allowed to use this code. If a viewer attempts to use a promo code after the maximum amount has been claimed, they will see a “Code expired” message at checkout.
  • The default amount is 100. For Random codes the maximum you can create is 10,000 codes per promotion, and for Custom codes the maximum is 30,000,000.

⚠️ Note: The subscription price with the promo applied cannot be less than $1.99/month or $12.99/year. You can see the Purchase price with your selected discount amount in the Promo summary section on the left-hand side of the page. If the Purchase price is lower than the minimum, you will not be able to create the promo and will need to set a smaller discount percentage.

  1. Click Save to save your promo details. Be sure to check the Promo summary on the left side to confirm your promo’s terms. You won’t be able to update these details once you’ve generated the codes! When you are satisfied, click Generate codes.
  • For Random codes, the button will switch after a moment to say Download CSV. Clicking it will prompt an email to be sent to you with a CSV file attached. Once you have your CSV of codes, you can distribute them however you see fit. Remember that the random codes can only be used once, so each recipient will need a unique code.

💡 Tip: Don’t see an email? Search your inbox for a message from help@vhx.tv and consider adding that address to your contacts or whitelist. Be sure to check your spam folder and all filters, and be sure you are checking the email that is associated with your Vimeo OTT account.

How do I extend a promo?

To extend a promo:

  1. Go to the Admin.
  2. Find the promo.
  3. Change the End datefor the promo.

What are my actions and options for promos?

After you have created a promo, you can click the actions dropdown on it to see options for sharing/editing:

  • Edit - Click this to edit your promo settings.
  • Promote on Homepage (Custom only) - Click this to feature the promo on your website so that anyone who lands on your homepage will know about the discount.
  • Warning: as soon as you select the promo in this drop-down, it will appear on the homepage of your Vimeo OTT site. To disable it, open the drop-down and select Remove from the homepage.
  • Copy promo URL (Custom only) - If you don’t want to promote it to everyone, you can simply click the “Copy promo URL” and share that link with a select audience. This is also a good way to test it out yourself before making it live.
  • Copy redemption URL (Custom only) - Use this if you want to send people directly to checkout with the code applied already. We have found in past experiences that the promo URL will be more effective at converting people, but figured it’d be handy for you to have both.
  • Deactivate - Click this anytime on an active Promo to disable it immediately.
  • Note that it is not possible to permanently delete a promo.
  • Scroll down on the promos page to find your inactive promos. If you wish to activate one, open the corresponding dropdown menu to the right and click Activate.

To see which customers used a promo code to purchase, download the transactions CSV file, which will include the code each customer used, if any, including codes set for existing customers.

How do I allow queued promo codes?

Promo Codes are designed to encourage a Customer to subscribe at a discount and then eventually pay full price. As such, the default behavior for all sites is that a Customer cannot redeem a new promo until their current promotion ends. If you would like to allow customers on an active discount to redeem a promo code for a future renewal, you can choose to allow queued promo codesin your Site Settings under General > Promotions.

Once this feature is enabled, subscribers will be able to enter a valid promo code on their Billing & Subscription page — even if they already have one active – and see that queued promo applied at their next renewal. They can remove the queued promo anytime before renewal. Only one promo code can be queued at a time, and promos must match the subscriber’s current billing cadence. If a subscriber switches plans, any queued promo codes will be cleared automatically. If you choose to enable this feature but later disable it, any promos that have already been queued will remain.

Applying a promo to a customer’s account

Sellers can apply a promo to a customer’s account directly through the OTT Admin to give a customer a discounted promotional rate on their existing subscription.

  1. Within the Vimeo OTT Admin, click Customer > All Customers
  2. In the Search field, enter a customer’s email address to pull up their record
  3. Click the … icon next to the customer’s record to open a dropdown
  • Apply promo option will only appear on customers who have an active paid subscription
  1. Select Apply Promotion, which will open a modal window
  2. Enter the promo code and click Apply
  • If the promo is applied successfully confirmation text will appear
  • If the promo is not applied successfully, red text will display why the promo could not be applied
  • Promos cannot be applied if the customer is currently on a promo unlessyou have activated the Queued Promos Feature in your Site Settings
  • Other reasons a Promo may not be applied: if the promo has previously been redeemed by the customer, if a subscriber is monthly and the promo is annual, if the promo is no longer active, if the promo is only applicable to new customers, or if the subscription is set to be canceled

Creating a purchase / rental product on Vimeo OTT

This article discusses how to create a purchase/rental product.

  • Create a purchase/rental product
  • How do I distribute my product?
  • Add videos to a released product

Create a purchase/rental product

You can create a new purchase/rental product on the Products page.

  1. Start by clicking + Create product at the top of the Products page

  2. Select Buy and rent

  3. Add information and assets under the Basic Info tab, including:

  • Title- Title the Product to describe what it contains. Example: “Purple Fitness - Weekend 1”
  • Description - Describe the Product your audience will be buying. Example: “Buy or Rent Weekend 1 of Purple Fitness’ Weekend Workouts!”
  • If you have a translated version of your product title and description, click Add translations, select the language(s), and type in the translation. These translations will appear for users who select the corresponding language anywhere on your site, including the checkout page.
  • Make sure you’ve enabled translations in your site settings in order for this to work.
  • Thumbnail - This image appears in customer emails, trailers, Facebook, Twitter, your website, and in Vimeo OTT Apps. Images should use a 16:9 ratio. We recommend 1920px × 1080px to ensure it scales well.
  • Additional thumbnails: These will be automatically generated based on your Thumbnail but you have the option to add custom assets when featuring this product in a different aspect or environment. Options here include a vertical, square, featured image, and featured mobile image.
  1. Next, head to the Distribution section to set the status of your video.
  • Choose Pre-orderIf you want this product to be set to pre-order mode. If you want to sell pre-orders, follow this guide.
  • Choose Ready to Sell if you’re ready to start selling once the product is all setup.
  • You can also choose to block or allow your content in specific countries.
  1. Next, add your Content.

  • If you’ve already uploaded your product’s trailer, click Choose trailer; otherwise, click the upload link below it to upload a new video as the trailer.

  • Below, add your main video(s), live events, or extras by clicking the Add Content button.

  • Click the checkbox next to the items you want to add. Be sure to click Add at the bottom of the window when you’re done.

  • Once added, you can Enable downloadsfor each video. Download options are not available for content in the Live Events or Extras tabs.

  1. Pricingis where you’ll set the purchase and/or rental price for your product.
  • Pay what you want- Enable Pay-What-You-Want pricing to allow customers to pay more than the base price.
  • Rental period - Establish the length your customers can rent the product for.
  • The default setting grants unlimited, non-expiring access, with optional limitations of 30 days or 14 days. ⚠️Note: Products that include live events cannot be made available for rent.
  • Tax model - This notifies you how your customers in certain countries will be taxed.
  • Buy price- Set your purchase price. Purchases include unlimited streaming and downloads for the viewers
  • Rental price- If you want to enable rentals, set your rental price.
  • Accept international currencies - Enable international pricing for your product.
  1. Next, you can add Extras to your product.
  • Click Add filesto choose from your uploaded extras and add them to the product. Selecting Upload will take you to your uploaded extras. This step is optional.
  1. In Advanced, you can customize the messaging we send when a customer makes a purchase. This is optional.
  • If you have translated versions of your message, click Add translations, choose your language, and enter the translated version of your message.
  • Customers who have translated your site into the corresponding language will see this version instead of the default English message.
  • Make sure you’ve enabled translations in your site settings in order for this to work.
  1. Finally, click Save to create the product and it will be available for purchase/rental. See below for how to share it and sell it.

Note that below your settings are two additional options:

  • Pause sales: This will take your product offline and make it so that new users cannot purchase it. Any existing users that have already purchased will continue to have access to your product.
  • Remove: This will take your product offline and make it so no one can buy it. Note that this is only an option if your product hasn’t had any sales. If you’ve had sales, you can only pause it.

⚠️Note: At least one product (subscription, purchase, or rental) must remain published for your site to stay online. If no products are available, your site will automatically be taken offline.

How do I distribute my product?

If you have the product available, you are now selling. Here are some next steps:

  • Share the checkout link so others can purchase / rent: Share it on Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, etc. To get to the checkout page of your product, click the View checkout button on the main Products page and it will be copied to your clipboard.

This is what the checkout page to purchase your product looks like for others: - Add your product to a category: Categories allow you to group together videos, events, collections (for subscriptions, such as series), and transactional products. For example, each category could be a different genre.

How do I add videos to a released product?

If you want to add videos to a product that has already been sold and released to your audience, here are the steps:

  1. Upload the videos you want to add to the videos page.
  2. Navigate to the product’s edit page and then to the Content tab.
  3. Choose between videos or live events and click the checkbox next to the video you want to add.
  4. Click Save on the product.

⚠️Note: If you’re adding new content to a transactional product, we recommend exporting a transaction CSV, sorting by the product in question, and then emailing the customers using your email client or a marketing email service (if you have one) to let them know there is new content available.

Creating and editing a subscription product on Vimeo OTT

  • What are subscriptions?
  • How do I set up a subscription product?
  • When do subscriptions get charged each month?
  • How does a subscriber cancel their subscription?

What are Subscriptions?

Subscriptions on Vimeo OTT let you charge your customers on a recurring monthly and/or yearly basis for streaming-only access to your content. You can add new work as often as you want. You control the branding, packaging, and pricing.

Vimeo OTT’s subscription fees are straightforward: $1 per subscriber per month, plus merchant fees. More on pricing.

How do I set up a subscription product on Vimeo OTT?

Once your videos are uploaded and you have Collections created, you can create a Subscription product. Note that you can only create one subscription product per site.

  1. Head to the Products page of the Vimeo OTT Admin.
  2. Click the Create Product button and select Subscription from the dropdown
  3. You will then be taken through the process of creating a subscription, first landing on the Settings tab where you can set:
  • Title - Set a name for the Subscription.
  • Description - Describe what your subscription is. This will be shown on the checkout form.
  • If you have a translated version of your product title and description, click Add translations, select the language(s), and type in the translation. These translations will appear for users who select the corresponding language anywhere on your site, including the checkout page.
  • Make sure you’ve enabled translations in your site settings in order for this to work.
  • Thumbnail - Provide a 16:9 ratio image (3840 x 2160 pixels works best) to represent your Subscription. This is the image that will appear in customer emails, trailers, Facebook, Twitter, when you share your website, and on your website.

Screenshot: subscriptoin_setup_page_showing_basic_info_fields_-_title__desciprtion__and_thumbnail.png

Next is the Content tab. Here you will set the following:

  • Trailer - this is a video that represents your Subscription. You may upload a new video here or choose a previously uploaded video.
  • Click Choose Trailer to see a list of your uploaded videos that you may select to use as your Subscription trailer.
  • Collections - from this tab you can quickly add or remove which Collections you have made available to your Subscribers.
  • Click + Add collectionsand select the checkbox for each one you’d like to add.

Next is the Pricing tab. Here you set the following:

  • Monthly Recurring Price - If you set this price, people get charged monthly. ($1.99 minimum)
  • Yearly Recurring Price- If you set this price, people get charged yearly. ($12.00 minimum)
  • Free-trials- If you want to give subscribers a free trial to watch your content before they are charged, you can set that here for 3, 7, 14, or 30 days.
  • International pricing- Pricing in the various currencies we offer natively to your viewers. Read more about international pricing in this article.

⚠️Note:You will not be charged the $1 price for a subscriber in a free trial. You will be charged once the customer has transitioned from the trial to a paid plan.

Screenshot: ott-multicurrency-setup.png

⚠️Important:A $1 holding charge will be processed on the customer’s card. These transactions will be reversed immediately and should disappear from accounts within 24 hours. The reason for this charge is to help prevent fraud. This hold will always be in USD, regardless if multi-currency is enabled.

In the Distributionsection, you can choose whether your videos are available worldwide, only in certain countries, or block specific countries.

In the Advanced menu, you can customize the messaging we send when a customer makes a purchase. This is optional.

If you have translated versions of your message, click Add translations, choose your language, and enter the translated version of your message. Customers who have translated your site into the corresponding language will see this version instead of the default English message. Make sure you’ve enabled translations in your site settings in order for this to work.

Below these settings are options to update the availability of your subscription product.

  • Pause subscription will make it so that new users cannot subscribe. Any existing subscribers will continue to renew as normal and will continue to have access to your product.
  • Cancel all subscriptions will revoke all current subscribers’ access to your product. They will no longer be charged for the subscription.

⚠️Note: At least one product (subscription, purchase, or rental) must remain published for your site to stay online. If no products are available, your site will automatically be taken offline.

Make sure you click Save when you’re done.

When do subscriptions get charged each month?

Subscriptions get charged on the same day each month/year that the user has subscribed. So, if they first subscribed on March 15th, they would next be charged on April 15th.

How does a subscriber cancel their subscription?

They can cancel at any time on their purchases settings page. When they cancel, they will have access to the content until their next billing cycle day.

Creating and managing categories on Vimeo OTT

This article discusses creating and managing categories for your videos. Categories must be assigned to at least one hub for content to display properly.

  • What are categories?
  • Create a category
  • Assigning categories to content hubs
  • General settings
  • Content settings
  • Distribution settings
  • Discovery settings
  • Content organization best practices

What are categories?

Categories are groups of videos, events, collections, and buy/rent products. Categories enable you to organize your content, much like parent folders in a filing system.

There are two types of categories:

  • Manual categories allow you to add specific pieces of content into a category. You can search for a video, collection, live event, or product, add it to the category, and manually arrange the display order. When you want to add more or rearrange content, you can manually add and rearrange at any time.
  • Dynamic categories enable you to establish rules for what content is included in a category and how it is displayed to the viewer. You set up filtering rules based on metadata (ie, tags, content type, video duration, etc.) for what content should get added to a category. Once you set up the filtering rules, content is added dynamically when it meets them. You set up sort rules to determine the order of content displayed to viewers (ie, random order, release date, number of views, etc.). You can read more about how to configure a Dynamic Category here. ⚠️Note: Currently, multiple categories can only be used when you sell a subscription product with Vimeo OTT. If you are only selling transactional products, however, you can still create a featured carousel for content that you’d like to highlight.

Create a category

To create a category:

  1. Navigate to Content > Categories.
  2. Click the + Add button next to the Categories section of the Content page or + New Category at the top of the page.
  3. A pop-up will open and prompt you to add the category title and choose if you want to create a Manual or Dynamic Category. Create a title, make your selection, and then select Add.

Assigning categories to content hubs

After creating a category, navigate to your Content hubs page and select the appropriate hub. You can also assign a category to more than one hub, so that it appears in the respective hubs’ browsing interface. Without assignment to a hub, categories will not appear in user facing hub pages.

General settings

After creating your category, you’ll be brought to the category’s settings page, starting with the General settings. Here, you can modify the category title, as well as add a Short description,a Full description, and a Thumbnail.You can also add multi-language translations for these text fields.

Content settings

Based on whether you chose a Manual or Dynamic category, this section will allow you to search and add content or set up rules for what content will get added. Read about creating Dynamic Category filters and sort rules.

Distribution settings

The Distribution tab allows you to control how your category is distributed and discovered across your platform. Settings you can configure here are:

  • You’ll be able to set its visibility to Published or Private.
  • You can also geo-block your category to make it available or unavailable in certain regions. The default option is Worldwide, but if you select Choose countries, you’ll need to specify which countries, and whether you’d like to limit your collection to only those countries, or if you’d like to prevent people in those countries from watching.
  • You can replace the category ID in your category’s URL with a custom URL specified here.
  • You can add Subtitles and captions, enable comments, add a screener, and download the video in multiple resolutions.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-07-26 at 4.39.51 PM.png

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-07-26 at 4.40.15 PM.png

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-07-26 at 4.40.29 PM.png

Discovery settings

The Discovery tab is for adding information about your category to make it more discoverable for search results. You can:

  • Designate the category to be your Featured category, pinning it to the top of the Browse page of your site and apps. This will add it to your featured carousel.
  • Mobile App Category appearance: choose from Default (16:9), Vertical (2:3), or Square (1:1) layouts for mobile categories.
  • Thumbnail size: choose to display standard or small thumbnails for mobile and TV apps
  • Item title display: show or hide text below thumbnails.
  • Overlay configuration: add Countdown overlays on the category row level for the first 10 assets within your category.
  • Add Tags to your category
  • Add Genres to your category
  • Add Cast, Crew, Release date, Rating, and Advisory to your category
  • Add aLicense to your category
  • Add a Media IDto your category
  • Add Advanced metadata(only applicable if you are using our API for data)
  • Add Image metadatafor images you upload
  • Add Custom metadata.

Click Save once you’ve made all your changes.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-07-26 at 4.40.58 PM.png

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-07-26 at 4.41.20 PM.png

Content organization best practices

Watch the video below to learn some tips for organizing your content.

Creating collections on Vimeo OTT

This article discusses how you can create collections.

  • What are collections?
  • Create a new collection
  • General settings
  • How do I add content to my collection?
  • Distribution settings
  • Discovery settings

What are collections?

Collections help you organize and curate your videos into groups and playlists to add to your subscription product. (TVOD or transactional products cannot be placed into collections.)

⚠️Note:Currently, collections are only used within subscriptions sold with Vimeo OTT. Create a collection of videos before you set up your subscription product.

Create a new collection

Within your Vimeo OTT Admin

  1. Click on Contentand scroll down to select CollectionScreenshot: Screenshot 2023-08-10 at 11.30.14 AM.png
  2. Click + New Collection.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-08-10 at 11.30.57 AM.png

You can create three different types of collections:

Movie - A Movie collection is ideal for a feature film with optional supporting content.

  • Playlist - A Playlist is used for any group of thematically similar videos that aren’t specifically a Movie or a Series.
  • Series - A Series collection is for a series where videos are episodes sorted into unique seasons.

Once you insert a title and click “Add,” you’ll be on your Collections settings page.

General settings

You will first see the General tab of your collection’s settings. Here, you can enter the following:

  • Title - Add or edit the name of the collection.
  • Short description - A short blurb that appears when the collection is in the Feature Carousel (more information below).
  • Full description- Add a paragraph description for the collection.
  • Thumbnail - Upload an image that will represent this collection in customer emails, trailers, Facebook, Twitter, and your website.
  • There are additional thumbnails below this for use with different devices; we automatically generate them based on your 16:9 upload but you can customize them as well. Read more at About thumbnail options for your Vimeo OTT videos

How do I add content to my collection?

Click on the Contenttab and begin to add your trailer and videos. Choose from existing videos, or upload a new one. You can also add extras, which are other file types meant to be supplementary to your content (i.e., mp3s, PDFs, images, etc). Screenshot: otthc-collections2.jpg

If you’ve selected “Series” as the type of collection, the Content tab is also where you’ll be able to create seasons.

⚠️Note:Continuous playback is auto-enabled for all collections and cannot be toggled.

Continuous playback is not supported on Xbox and Tizen apps

Click Add Season to create a Season. Enter a Season name and click Save. The Season will now appear in a list. Please note that your site can only display up to 50 seasons per collection.

Click into a Season’s Settings from the ellipsis (…) menu to add a Title, a Short Description (for the features carousel only),a Full description, a Season number, and Thumbnail.

⚠️Note: When grouping episodes into seasons, the name of each season should be unique, or else your viewers will be presented with a playback error. (i.e. seasons 1, 2, 3, etc.). There can’t be more than one of the same seasons.

Screenshot: otthc-collections3.png

💡 Tip: You can specify default settings for your new videos within your Site Settings. Visit How to edit your Vimeo OTT site settings to learn about setting Site Defaults.

Distribution settings

The next tab is Distribution, where you can control how your collection is distributed and who can see it. In this tab you can specify settings for:

  • Visibility: Toggle “Published” or “Private.” Published means that your paid subscribers will be able to see it; Private means only you can.
  • Regions: If you want to geo-block your film to make it available or unavailable in certain countries, you can do so here. The default option is “Worldwide,” but if you select “Choose countries,” you’ll need to specify which countries, and whether you’d like to limit your collection to only those countries, or if you’d like to prevent people in those countries from watching.
  • Custom URL:Use this space to set a custom URL for your collection. Think of something short, snappy, and linkable.

Discovery settings

Here’s where you’d add more information about your collection to make it more discoverable for search results. You can add:

    • Featured: Choose how you’d like to display your content on your site. Read Configure category appearance with row-level customization on Vimeo OTT to learn how.
  • Tags:Ad hoc hashtags that describe your content. These will be used to help your customers discover your content.
  • A Media ID:This is an internal identifier that can be leveraged for searching your own catalog or for generating reports with our API.
  • Advanced metadata:These fields are only available when using our API and are not surfaced in the Customer Experience or leveraged in Search.
  • Image metadata:Attach custom images to your Collection that can be retrieved via the API.
  • Custom metadata:Create arbitrary key/value pairs for your Collection that can be retrieved via the API.

Creating Terms and Policies for my Vimeo OTT site

As the operator of your OTT streaming service, you are responsible for providing your customers with transparent and comprehensive Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy. This article defines what these terms and policies are and how to add them to your Vimeo OTT site.

  • What are Terms of Service?
  • What is a Privacy Policy?
  • What is a Cookie Policy?
  • How do I create and edit my Vimeo OTT site’s terms and policies?

What are Terms of Service?

Your OTT streaming service, like any other online service, has a set of rules and guidelines that customers must agree to in order to access and use it. These rules, often called “Terms of Service” (Terms), are a legally binding contract between you and your customers.

The Terms define what customers can and cannot do on your Vimeo OTT site, covering things like account creation, content usage, subscription terms, and dispute resolution. They also outline your rights as the service provider and allocate risk between the parties.

It’s important to have clear and comprehensive Terms that reflect your organization’s business model and legal requirements.

What is a Privacy Policy?

When users interact with your apps or your site, certain information about them is recorded. For example:

  • When a user registers for a free trial or subscription, they provide an email address and payment information.
  • When a user views your content, information about their activity and device is recorded in order to deliver the best experience and to generate analytics.
  • Users might also reach out for customer support, and in doing so provide their name and email address.

Some of this information is considered “personal information.” As the operator of your OTT streaming service, it is your responsibility to provide your customers with a transparent notice of how you handle their personal information, commonly known as a “privacy policy.”

When crafting your privacy policy, consider the specific ways you use data, any additional methods you employ for data collection, whether your channel is designated as “Made for Kids,” and the relevant laws and regulations that apply to your business.

What is a Cookie Policy?

When users visit your OTT streaming service, small text files called “cookies” and other tracking technologies may be placed on their device. Cookies can serve various purposes, such as remembering preferences, providing in-product notifications, and measuring the effectiveness of advertising campaigns.

Your cookie policy should clearly explain what types of cookies and other tracking technologies you use, what they do, and how users can manage or disable them if they prefer.

By default, Vimeo sets a limited number of cookies on your OTT streaming service for essential and functional purposes. In addition, Vimeo supports various third-party integrations that involve adding tracking technologies to your site for purposes such as advertising and analytics.

If you connect any third-party services that involve the placement of additional trackers, you must adjust your cookie policy to include information about the additional purposes and third parties who will be able to collect information about your users through those tracking technologies.

How do I create and edit my Vimeo OTT site’s terms and policies?

You can find the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy directly in your OTT site.

  1. Log into your Vimeo OTT site.
  2. Navigate to Manage, then Site.
  3. Select the Customer Agreements tab on the left-hand sidebar.
  4. Add or edit the policies to reflect your business practices and legal obligations.
  5. Save your changes.

Vimeo may provide templates, which are for informational purposes only and are not legal advice. Legal requirements are complex and may change over time. Contact an attorney to obtain advice with respect to any particular legal matter.

You are the operator of your OTT streaming service and have a direct relationship with your customers. Vimeo merely provides the technology — the Vimeo OTT platform — to allow you to provide your service. You are responsible for publishing your own terms and policies in accordance with the Vimeo Seller Addendum.

FAQ: Transitioning from Vimeo OTT live events to Vimeo Events

An important update regarding streaming with live events on Vimeo OTT.

Vimeo OTT is enhancing its live streaming service by replacing the direct streaming option with Vimeo Events-powered live streaming. This upgrade maintains the familiar live capabilities while introducing new features to improve your overall streaming experience.

As a result, beginning February 1st, 2025, the Live Events tab will be removed from the OTT dashboard. Any further live streams must be conducted through Vimeo Events.

  • What are the benefits of streaming with Vimeo Events?
  • How can I prepare for this transition?
  • When is the deadline to make this change?
  • What happens if I don’t connect my accounts by the deadline?
  • Can I still stream via RTMP?
  • Where can I read about the Browser-Based Encoder?
  • What will happen to my past, recorded events?
  • Why is this change happening?

What are the benefits of streaming with Vimeo Events?

When streaming on Vimeo OTT with Vimeo Events, you’ll benefit from:

  • A simplified, yet powerful, web-based production suite in addition to RTMP streaming.
  • Faster video availability after your streams conclude.
  • Integrated live chat functionality.

How can I prepare for this transition?

To prepare for the transition to Vimeo Events, we strongly recommend completing the following steps as soon as possible. You will not be able to stream from the Live Events tab after February 1, 2025 and instead will use Vimeo Events.

Connect your Vimeo.com and Vimeo OTT accounts:

Connect your Vimeo.com and Vimeo OTT accounts to begin streaming with Vimeo Events. Find out how at ‘How do I connect my Vimeo account to my OTT account?’.

⚠️Note:Only theAccount Ownerof the Vimeo OTT account can connect the accounts. If you don’t have a Vimeo.com account, please reach out to your Account Manager or the OTT Sales Team for assistance.

Familiarize yourself with Vimeo Events:

After connecting your accounts, familiarize yourself with the features and capabilities of Vimeo Events. View how at ‘Broadcasting live events from Vimeo to Vimeo OTT’.

When is the deadline to make this change?

We strongly recommend connecting your accounts and familiarizing yourself with Vimeo Events before February 1, 2025.

What happens if I don’t connect my accounts by the deadline?

You can still connect your accounts after February 1st, 2025, however, you won’t be able to create new live events until you complete setting up this connection.

Can I still stream via RTMP?

Yes. With Vimeo Events you have all of the same capabilities you had previously, including the ability to stream from an external encoder connected to OTT via RTMP.

Where can I read about the Browser-Based Encoder?

You can read more at ‘Overview: Create and go live to an event’.

What will happen to my past, recorded events?

Prior live streams on your Vimeo OTT account are transcoded into on-demand videos and will remain in your OTT library.

Why is this change happening?

“Live Events” on Vimeo OTT are powered by livestream, a subsidiary of Vimeo.

To unify our products, Vimeo is sunsetting Livestream.com and has been building out powerful live-streaming capabilities inside of Vimeo.com. We’re bringing those new capabilities to Vimeo OTT by sunsetting “Live Events” and replacing them with Vimeo Events powered by Vimeo.com.

This change ensures that you continue to deliver high-quality content to your subscribers seamlessly.

Fees and taxes on Vimeo on Demand

When you sell a video using Vimeo on Demand (VOD), you will keep 90% of the gross revenue after transaction costs have been deducted. These transaction costs include:

  • Transaction fees from the buyer’s payment method

  • VAT/GST & US sales tax (where applicable)

  • Fees and taxes breakdown

  • More information on VAT

Fees and taxes breakdown

Transaction fees range from 4% to 17%, depending on factors such as the price you set for your work, the purchaser’s payment method, and the currency that the purchaser uses to purchase the VOD title.

Purchasers located in VAT/GST-applicable countries will see VAT-inclusive pricing, meaning that their local tax rate will be automatically deducted from the prices you’ve set. Tax will not be added separately to the listed prices on your VOD title.

That means the total price you set looks like this for tax-applicable countries: Price + Price*Tax = Total Price, or after some algebra, the equation can be reworked into: Price = Total Price / (1+Tax).

Here’s an example calculation using a 24% VAT rate:

Set VOD price: 9.90 EUR Exchange rate on that day: 1 USD = 0.81278 EUR Total Price (USD) = 9.90/0.81278 = 12.18 USD Price after 24% VAT rate: 12.18/(1+0.24) = 9.82 USD Tax in USD: 12.18 - 9.82 = 2.36 USD

After transaction fees and taxes have been deducted, Vimeo will then take 10% of the remaining revenue as a fee. The remaining amount is sent to the seller.

Gross Revenue - Transaction Cost - VAT - Vimeo Fee = Net Revenue

More information on VAT

VAT rates are available online by searching for the buyer’s country’s name and VAT.

In cases where a VOD purchase occurs in a VAT-applicable country, we are required to collect VAT on it because Vimeo is the merchant of record for all VOD transactions.

As such, we bear the responsibility of collecting VAT. In other words, because a sale itself is technically performed by Vimeo, VOD sellers aren’t selling directly to other countries - we are. In order to remain in compliance with VAT regulations, we therefore charge VAT on all sales made to purchasers in VAT-collecting countries.

It’s important to note that for these reasons mentioned, we collect VAT regardless of whether you’ve submitted a tax form. Please note that we are not able to return any of the taxes collected on sales of your VODs to you, even if you are a member of a tax exempt organization.

Any VAT that we collect is then remitted back to the appropriate tax authority in each country or region in a combined amount, along with all the other VAT collected during a given period (e.g. a quarterly remittance for the EU).

You’re welcome to adjust your current prices for currencies of VAT-collecting countries (currencies besides USD and CAD), since VAT will be taken out of the prices you charge viewers in those countries.

Find your Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for VOD payments

All Vimeo On Demand sellers must submit their tax forms as soon as possible. All Vimeo On Demand payments will be subject to a 24% withholding of gross sales if you do not have an approved tax form on file by the time your income is generated.

How do I determine my TIN?

Determining your Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) depends on where you are located as an individual or entity. Here’s how you can find it:

You will require your TIN to submit a W-9 or W-8 Form before receiving any Vimeo payments.

  • For U.S.-based individuals: Your TIN is the same as your social security number.
  • For U.S.-based entities (corporations, partnerships, LLCs, etc.): In general, your TIN is usually the entity’s Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN). In some cases (e.g., LLC, S-corp corporations, partnerships), however, the TIN may be that of the owner. Consult with a tax professional to determine what your TIN is.
  • For creators based outside the U.S.: If you are a U.S. citizen living abroad, you must provide a TIN. If you are a non-U.S. citizen residing outside of the U.S., you may either provide a W-9 (if you have a TIN) or provide a W-8 (if you do not have a TIN).

Get paid with Vimeo On Demand

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

Any purchases of your VOD titles will be accrued throughout each calendar month and then transferred to your PayPal account in one lump payment.

  • Requirements
  • Timeline
  • Currencies
  • Fees
  • Statements
  • Purchase notifications
  • Set up your PayPal account

Requirements

You will need a verified PayPal account to receive your earnings. Read more about PayPal’s verification process in PayPal’s help center.

Timeline

You will receive each payment approximately 30 days after the month’s end. For example, a payment for all sales made in the month of June will be transferred from Vimeo to your PayPal account on or around July 30. You will receive a detailed statement when the payment is processed, and the funds will appear in your PayPal account soon thereafter.

Currencies

All VOD payments are made in U.S. dollars. Sales made in currencies other then U.S. dollars will be converted to USD based on the final exchange rate of the day each purchase was made. (Daily rates provided by openexchangerates.)

Fees

You keep 90% of revenue after transaction costs and any applicable taxes. Read moreabout transaction costs.

Statements

When your monthly VOD payment is processed, a statement reflecting the amount paid will be sent to the primary email address associated with your Vimeo account and you will be able to download a CSV spreadsheet with more detail from the Payments section of your account settings.

Purchase notifications

Every day that someone purchases your work, we’ll send you an email. This email will be sent to the main email address associated with your Pro account (or higher). Please note that you won’t receive an email on days when no purchases have been made.

Set up your PayPal account

To connect your PayPal account to your VOD page, first be sure your account is verified — if it’s not, you will not be able to connect it to your Vimeo account. You will also need to make sure that you entered your first and last name exactly as they appear on your PayPal account.

Things should run smoothly, but sometimes you might miss a payment for one of these reasons:

  1. You did not connect your Vimeo account to your PayPal account
  2. There was an error when we tried to deposit the payment to your PayPal account

To resolve #1, head to your Payments settings page and click Connect your PayPal account. Once you’ve connected your account, you’re good to go.

To resolve #2, check your PayPal account to make sure that it’s set up to receive payments. If it already is, head to your Payments settings and click Edit your PayPal connection, and make sure the name and email address match the exact info on your PayPal account.

⚠️Note: Any missed payments get added to the next month’s payment. We make payments 30 days after the end of a particular month.

You can read all of the terms in our Payment Addendum.

Get started with Vimeo OTT Live

Vimeo OTT Live overview

Content creators can better engage with their audiences by adding live content to their OTT site’s on-demand library. This guide will walk you through what you need to add live content to your OTT site.

⚠️Note: To stream live events, you need a Vimeo OTT Enterprise plan with live streaming enabled and a Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise Vimeo.com account. Contact Vimeo OTT Sales or your Account Manager to add live streaming capabilities to your site.

In this article:
  • Prep your Vimeo OTT Account to go live
  • Pick & set up your live video encoder
  • Other best practices

Things to do before you go live on Vimeo OTT

Prep your Vimeo OTT account

To stream with Vimeo OTT, you need to have a Vimeo account enabled for live streaming capabilities or an Enterprise account set up. Additionally, make sure you have the following:

  1. Subscription Product live- Have your subscription product or transactional product all ready to go first.
  2. Active Category/Collection - If you have a subscription product create a Collection or Category that this live stream will live in for your customers. We recommend it living in the featured Carousel Category so viewers see it at the top of your Browse page.

Once you have covered the above steps, visit ‘Setting up a live stream on Vimeo OTT’ for instructions on how to set up a live stream.

Pick & set up your live video encoder

Vimeo OTT uses RTMP, which stands for real-timemessaging protocol. It provides for high-performance transmission of audio, video, and data from an encoder to a server, which distributes the signal across the Internet. Many streaming providers and encoder developers support RTMP streaming.

Which encoders support RTMP?

Encoders that can be used to stream to Vimeo OTT via RTMP include, but are not limited to:

  • Livestream Studio
  • OBS Studio
  • Wirecast
  • XSplit Broadcaster
  • NewTek TriCaster
Cloud transcoding

This feature also includes cloudtranscoding. This means you can stream a single bitrate from your encoder, which we convert into various lower bitrates in the cloud for you. For example, if you send your stream at 1920x1080 at a minimum bitrate of 4Mbps, the possible qualities viewers can watch are:

  • 1080p: 1920x1080, 5256kbps
  • 720p: 1280x720, 2756kbps
  • 540p: 854x480, 1756kbps
  • 360p: 640x360, 628kbps

Depending on that person’s internet connection speed, the player will automatically adjust which bitrate each viewer sees. This greatly reduces the required bandwidth you need in order to stream in multiple bitrates while also providing the best possible experience for your viewers.

Encoder setup recommendation

Vimeo OTT uses the incoming resolution to determine which qualities the cloud can transcode the video in. Lower incoming bitrates cannot be transcoded to higher qualities in the cloud; in other words, if you stream at a quality less than 720p, then your stream will not be available in 720p or 1080p.

To get the most out of the cloud transcoding feature, we recommend that you configure your encoder as follows:

  • Video bitrate: 5000kbps
  • Audio bitrate: 256kbps
  • Resolution:1920x1080
  • Frame rate: 30 frames per second
  • Keyframe interval: 2 seconds
Other best practices
Bandwidth recommendations

The most reliable Internet connection when streaming is connecting directly via Ethernet to a dedicated network. This means that no other computers or devices have access to that network. This connection type is less likely to experience bandwidth fluctuation than shared networks or wireless connections.

A general rule of thumb is having twice as much upload speed available as the bitrate you want to stream. An average bitrate of each preset quality is listed in the quality menu of most encoders:

The chart below from our friends at Livestream, which is a Vimeo company, gives a general guideline of the recommended upload speeds for some presets:

Note: Given the varying network environments and potential for network interruptions, we advise always making a local recording copy in the event the stream gets interrupted.

Firewall requirements

Your network needs to be able to maintain a back and forth communication with Livestream. In order of importance, the following Firewall ports on your network should be open to incoming and outgoing communication:

  • TCP 1935
  • TCP 80
  • TCP 443
  • UDP 53

How can I add Live Engagement to my live events on Vimeo OTT?

Vimeo Events on OTT support the ability to engage live with your viewers through Chat, Q&A, and Polls.

The first step to streaming on OTT is connecting a Vimeo.com account. Follow these simple steps to connect your Vimeo.com and OTT accounts. Once you have connected your Vimeo account and your Vimeo OTT Site, with a Vimeo account enabled with live streaming you are ready to broadcast your live events directly to your Vimeo OTT audience. You can monetize your live events as part of your subscription, one-time purchases (also known as Pay Per View), or both.

⚠️Note: To stream live events, you must be on a Vimeo OTT Enterprise plan with live streaming enabled and have a Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise account on Vimeo.com. Please contact Vimeo OTT Sales or your Account Manager to add live streaming capabilities to your site.

  • Configuring site-wide defaults for live engagement tools
  • Configuring live engagement tools on a specific event

Configuring site-wide defaults for live engagement tools

You can set defaults for your site that will apply to every new Vimeo Event you create. You can override the sitewide defaults at the individual event level.

  1. Log into your Vimeo OTT admin for your project and click Manage > Site > Content Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-01-08 at 11.28.15 AM.png
  2. Scroll to the section titled Live Engagement
  3. Include a live engagement room for all new live events—This toggle lets you choose whether all live events you create will have the option to enable live engagement tools. By default, this toggle will be disabled.
  • If enabled, the live event will show a section next to the video player where the live engagement tools will display when enabled.
  • If disabled, viewers will only see the video player. The live engagement section will not display for your event.
  1. Require users to log in to participate in live engagement for all new live events—This toggle allows you to choose whether to require users to log in before they can participate in the Live Engagement. By default, this toggle will be enabled.
  • If enabled viewers will be prompted to log in before they can see the contents of the live engagement module and participate
  • If disabled they will be able to see and participate in the live engagement even if they are not logged in to your site.

Configuring live engagement tools on a specific event

Each time you create a new Vimeo Events live stream, you will be able to configure the live engagement settings.

  1. Log into your Vimeo OTT admin for your project and click Content > Vimeo Events
  2. Click on any Vimeo Events you have already created or create a new event.
  3. On the General tab of the event, scroll down to the section titled Live Engagement Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-01-08 at 11.28.36 AM.png
  4. The options to include a live engagement room and to require users to log in to participate live will be inherited from the defaults you set via the sitewide options outlined above. You can configure the options for this event by enabling/disabling these per-event settings.
  5. You must enable Include a live engagement room for this event if you want to use Chat, Polls, or Q&A during your event.

How can I create a live stream?

Live streaming lets you share moments in real-time, build excitement, and interact with your viewers like never before. To stream on OTT, first connect your Vimeo.com and Vimeo OTT accounts. With a Vimeo account enabled for live streaming, you can broadcast live events directly to your Vimeo OTT audience and monetize them through subscriptions, one-time purchases, or both. ⚠️Note: To stream live events, you need a Vimeo OTT Enterprise plan with live streaming enabled and a Premium, Advanced, or Enterprise Vimeo.com account. Contact Vimeo OTT Sales or your Account Manager to add live streaming capabilities to your site.

To create a live stream:

  1. Log into your Vimeo OTT admin for your project and click Content > Vimeo Events
  • If you do not see the Vimeo Events option, you have not connected a Vimeo.com account to your OTT account, so you should follow the instructions outlined here.

  1. Click the blue New+ button in the upper left corner of this page and click Vimeo Events from the dropdown menu that appears.

  2. A popup will appear with fields to create your Vimeo Event

  3. Title - The title that will be displayed for this live event

  4. Scheduled Event - Click this button to set a date and time for the event to begin. Note the date and time are for appearance only; no matter what date and time you enter, your event won’t go live until you start going live from your encoder.

  5. Production mode

  • Stream with RTMP
  • Select this option to connect an external video encoder such as Open Broadcaster Software (OBS), Wirecast, XSplit Broadcaster, & Livestream Studio
  • Stream through your Browser
  • Select this option to stream directly from Vimeo’s browser based production studio
  • End of stream behavior
  • If you select this when your event ends, the VOD of your just concluded event will appear on the live event page so viewers can watch on demand.
  • If you are only running a one-time event and don’t plan on re-streaming this event, you should select this option.
  • If not selected, when your event ends, the event thumbnail will appear on the live event page and you will be ready to stream your next event.
  1. Click Create to go to the Live Event Details page.

💡Tip: Read about configuring the live settings and starting and ending a live stream here.

How can I enable and moderate live engagement tools during my stream

Once you have created your Vimeo Event and enabled it for Live Engagement you are ready to start your live stream, enable Chat, Polls, and/or QA, and manage your audience interactions.

You will enable the specific live engagement tools (Chat, Polls, and/or QA) and moderate them from your connected Vimeo.com account. Once enabled, the live engagement tools will appear inside a Live Engagement Room which will appear alongside or below the video player.

  1. Log into your Vimeo OTT admin for your project and click Manage > Site > Content
  2. Click on any Vimeo Events you have already created.
  3. On the General tab of the event, scroll down to the section titled Live Engagement
  4. Click the blue Manage Event button and a new tab will open taking you to the corresponding event on Vimeo.com
  • If you are not already logged in on the corresponding Vimeo.com account, you will be prompted to log in.
  • You will need to be added as a Team Member on the Vimeo.com account connected to your OTT account to access and moderate the Live Engagement tools.
  1. Inside the Vimeo.com event interface, you will be able to individually enable Chat, Polls, and/or QA functionality.
  2. The location of the Chat, Polls, and Q&A features is slightly different between RTMP and Browser Based Studio.

RTMP

Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-01-08 at 11.28.58 AM.png

Browser Based Studio

Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-01-08 at 11.30.00 AM.png

  • Chat is located on the right side of the screen. Enable by clicking the blue button Turn On inside of the chat module. You can read a full overview of moderating live chat here.
  • If streaming via a Browser Based Encoder, you can toggle between chatting with the audience and chatting with live-stream speakers.
  • The polls module is located on the left side of the screen. Enable by clicking the blue button “Create poll” inside of the polls module. You can read a full overview of creating and moderating polls here.
  • The QA module is located on the left side of the screen. Enable by clicking the blue button “Start Q&A” inside of the Q&A module. You can read a full overview of creating and moderating Q&A here.
  1. When the features are enabled on the Vimeo.com event, they will become visible to viewers in the Live Engagement Room to the right or below the video player on your site/apps.

How can my viewers cancel their subscriptions?

The steps to cancel will depend on how your viewersinitially signed up.

  1. If they signed up within an Apple iOS or Apple TV app, follow the steps here: HT202039
  2. If they signed up within a Google Play/Android app, follow the steps here: answer
  3. If they signed up within the Roku channel, follow the steps here: how do i manage or cancel a subscription
  4. If they signed up with Amazon, follow the steps here: nodeId=GDT2SXJJ7K49JKYE

If they signed up on the website, they can cancel their subscription by logging into their account and following the steps below:

⚠️Note:If they signed up and paid on the website, they can only cancel via the website (notvia apps).

  1. Navigate to the settings menu in the top right corner of the screen

  2. Click Manage Subscription within Billing and Subscriptionsettings

  3. Then click on the Cancel subscription

  4. This pop-up will appear. Choose an option and then select Continue.

  5. Note that choosing a Pauseoption will halt their automatic renewal for the selected amount of time.

  6. If they no longer wish to be charged, choose No thanks, I want to cancel, select Continue.

  7. They will then see a short, optional survey. To finalize the cancelation, select Confirm Cancellation.

  8. They will see a confirmation window indicating their subscription has been canceled.

  9. They will also receive an email confirmation. If they did not receive a confirmation, double-check that their subscription shows as ‘Canceled’ in their settings. When they cancel, their video access will exist until the next charging cycle, but they cannot be further charged.

⚠️Note: If they don’t see those options on the Manage subscription settings page or otherwise have trouble managing their subscription, contact us and provide the last four digits of the card currently being charged or the email registered in the account for us to help them further.

How can my viewers manage their account settings for my OTT site?

This article discusses how your viewers can manage their account settings from your OTT site.

  • How can my viewers log in?
  • What can my viewers do if they have trouble signing in?
  • How can my viewers reset their login password?

How can my viewers log in?

If your viewer has not purchased or subscribed yet, they will need to do so first.

The first time a viewer signs up, they will be prompted to set a password. To do so, they need to:

  1. Enter their email address on the login page.
  2. On the next page, enter the password and click Sign In.
  3. If they have already created a password, and it’s not working, they can reset or set a password to log in on that page or use the email link method below.

Viewers can try these steps to log in via the email sign-in link:

  1. They need to add ’support@vhx.tv’ to their contact list to ensure messages from us do not end up in their spam folder.
  2. Enter their email address on the login page
  3. If they are an active viewer, they will be immediately sent an email link that will log them in, once clicked.
  4. Next, they can open their email inbox, and click the login link.
  5. They will then be logged in to watch their purchased/rented/subscribed video content within their Vimeo OTT Library.

What can my viewers do if they have trouble signing in?

If a viewer is having trouble with their password, they can consider the following possibilities:

  • Did they sign up with a typo in their email address, or an address different than the one they are using to sign in? They can try to find the confirmation email from when they signed up to verify the address they should be using.
  • Punctuation makes a difference. If they signed up with email.email@gmail.com, but are trying to sign in with emailemail@gmail.com, our system will not consider those the same addresses.
  • The end of email address matters. For example, @gmail.com and @googlemail.com may be the same as Google, but our system will see them as different email addresses.

With those possibilities in mind, here are the ways to log in on the web:

If they don’t have a password, or their password isn’t working, here is how to set/reset it:

  1. Click Sign in in the top right corner of the page and enter their email address.
  2. Click Next.
  3. Underneath the password field, select Reset your password.
  4. Enter their email address on that page and select Reset Password.
  5. If they are an active viewer, they will be emailed a link to set a new password.
  6. Find the link in their inbox and click on it.

⚠️Note: If they do not receive an email to reset their password, they are likely using an incorrect email address. They can try with any other addresses they own. They can check all of their email inboxes for a ‘Start watching’ email from VHX (search for ‘Start watching VHX’).

If a password is not required:

  1. Click Sign in in the top right corner of the page
  2. Enter their email address. If they are an active viewer, they will be immediately emailed a link that will sign them in, once clicked. They can open their email inbox and click the sign-in link.
  3. They will then be signed in to watch their video content.

⚠️Note: If they do not receive an email to reset their password, they are likely using an incorrect email address. They can try with any other addresses they own. They can check all of their email inboxes for a ‘Start watching’ email from VHX (search for ‘Start watching VHX’).

How can my viewers reset their login password?

If the login page is asking for a password and they don’t have or remember theirs, here is how to reset it:

  1. Please add ‘support@vhx.tv’ to your contact list to ensure messages from us do not end up in your spam folder.
  2. Make sure they are logged out here.
  3. Visit the login page and enter your email address.
  4. Click Next.
  5. Underneath the password field, select Reset your password.
  6. Enter the email address on that page and select Reset Password.
  7. If they are an active viewer, they will be emailed a link to set a new password. Check the email inbox for that link.
  8. Click the link in the email and reset their password.

How can my viewers update their information?

This article discusses how your viewers can update their information such as credit card details and email addresses.

  • How can my viewers change their email addresses?
  • How can my viewers update their credit card information?

How can my viewers change their email addresses?

If your viewers can log in, they can change their email address by clicking the circular-shaped profile icon and selecting Account Settings from the drop-down menu.

They will need to click on Email, and then type in the new email and click Save.

How can my viewers update their credit card information?

Viewers can edit their billing information by going to the Billing Settings page.

  • First, sign in to their account.
  • Click the avatar or account link in the top right of the signed-in page.
  • Choose Account Settings from the dropdown.
  • Choose Billing & subscription from the settings page.
  • Choose Payment Method from the options on the page.
  • You can now enter your new payment information.
  • Click Save.

Keep in mind, that if they subscribed to another platform, such as iOS, Android, or Roku, they will need to update their payment information through the relevant app store.

⚠️Note: Visa Gift Cards and other kinds of pre-paid gift cards are not supported.

💡Tip: Learn about How can Vimeo OTT sellers assist viewers with common payment issues? To assist customers with payment issues.

How do I start and end a live stream on OTT?

When you are ready to start your event, simply go live in your encoding software or via the Web-Based Browser, and your stream will start on OTT. If you have enabled Notify Followers an email will go out notifying your subscribers your event is now live.

  • Starting a live stream
  • Ending a live stream

Starting a live stream

To start your stream via RTMP:

  1. Go Live in your Encoding Software and start your stream
  2. Your stream should start playing on OTT within 30 seconds

To start your stream via Web-Based Studio:

  1. Navigate to the General tab of the event
  2. Click the blue button Visit web-based studio
  3. You will be taken to Vimeo.com’s Web-Based Studio
  4. Start your Stream 💡Tip: Read about how to navigate the web-based production tool
  5. Your stream should start playing on OTT within 30 seconds

Ending a live stream

Once you are done live streaming, click End Eventin the live event setup panel and end the stream in your encoder.

If you end your event in your encoding source but do not click the End Event button in OTT, the stream will continue to retry connecting to the encoding source for five minutes before ending the event and kicking off the transcoding process.

Once your Vimeo Event transcodes to a VOD, it will appear in Content > Videos. If you selected the stream to be 24/7 there will be no VOD.

If you had enabled Preview mode, your VOD would not include the part of the stream while the setting was enabled.

💡Tip: Read about creating and configuring a live stream here.

How to access Livestream Studio with your Vimeo OTT account

Livestream Studio is a multi-camera livestreaming encoder developed by Vimeo. You get access to one license to Livestream Studio with a Vimeo OTT Growth plan, and three licenses with an Enterprise plan. You can learn how to download and install Studio here.

When you first launch the program, you will see a prompt to log in. You should have set up an account on vimeo as part of purchasing your plan on Vimeo OTT; select Vimeo and enter your email and password for that account here to unlock your license.

After you are logged in, you can stream to events on your Vimeo OTT site by navigating to the Stream tab and selecting RTMP as your streaming provider.

Screenshot: stream_tab_rtmp_hilit.png

On your OTT site admin, create a live event. Once you get to the Server URL and Stream Key, copy and paste them into their respective fields in Livestream Studio.

⚠️Note: If you only see one field, click the switch your view link below it to switch to a separate URL and Key field.

Screenshot: url_and_key_fields_in_studio.png

When you’re ready to start your event, click the Go Live link in the bottom right corner of the Studio interface. You should see your stream appear on the OTT admin.

If you enabled Preview Mode, your stream will only be visible to you and your OTT Team. You will need to click the “Go Live” option to exit Preview Mode and allow your Customers to see the stream.

From here, you can produce your event from Livestream Studio, which includes features such as graphics overlays and video playback. For more detailed guides on using Livestream Studio, visit the Livestream Help Center.

To stop the stream in Studio, click the red Streaming button in the lower right corner. Be sure to end the event in the OTT live event setup panel in your site admin as well.

If you have any issues or questions, contact us.

How to add a profile picture on a Vimeo OTT account via Gravatar

You can add a profile picture to your Vimeo OTT account using Gravatar. There is no direct option to upload a profile picture from your account settings — the only way is to create a Gravatar account and upload your picture there.

How to add videos to my Vimeo On Demand page

What to know before uploading new videos

Videos uploaded to your Vimeo On Demand page will be counted against your allowed video storage.

We strongly recommend exporting your video files according to our Video Compression Guidelines before uploading them. This will maximize your storage space and ensure that the videos will maintain high quality playback on Vimeo.

How to add existing videos to my Vimeo On Demand title
