Submit VOD tax forms

It is crucial for all Vimeo On Demand sellers to submit their tax forms as soon as possible. All Vimeo On Demand payments will be subject to 24% withholding of gross sales if you do not have an approved tax form on file by the time your payment is generated.

Read below to learn which form to submit, and how.

  • Instructions to change/update/remove your VAT ID number
  • Instructions for U.S. sellers
  • Instructions for sellers from other countries
  • Overview of different tax forms
  • W-9 Form
  • W-8 Form
  • 8233 Form
  • 1099-K Form
  • How to change/update/remove the tax exemption
  • Need help?

Instructions to change/update/remove your VAT ID number

You can only add VAT ID numbers from your payment method in your settings. You cannot change or remove the VAT ID number once it is validated. If you want to change your VAT ID number, you must reach out to support. To be able to remove it, you have to create a new account and Billing will gift you the leftover time.

Screenshot: Screenshot Screenshot: Screenshot

Screenshot: Screenshot

Instructions for U.S. sellers

U.S. residents and entities must submit a W-9 form and will not be subject to withholding once a valid form is submitted.

You can submit your form electronically on your Payment Settings.

Learn how to identify your taxpayer identification number (TIN).

Instructions for sellers from other countries

Residents of other countries must submit a U.S. W-8 tax form and will only be subject to withholding if it is legally required for your country.

Businesses and organizations: If you’re selling on behalf of a business or organization, you can submit a W-8BEN-E from your Payment Settings page on Vimeo.

Individuals: If you’re an individual seller, you must first check this IRS page to see if your country has a tax treaty with the U.S.

If your country is listed on the IRS page above, you will be not subject to any withholding from Vimeo if you submit a W-8BEN tax form with a valid tax treaty claim.

Download the form and then submit a completed copy to taxforms @ vimeo [dot] com.

If your country is not listed above, your net revenue will be subject to 30% withholding if you complete a valid W-8BEN form. You can submit all the necessary forms on your Payment Settings page.

Overview of different tax forms

Vimeo uses Tipalti, a third-party vendor which helps us collect and review tax paperwork. If Tipalti is unable to process the form you submit, you’ll be notified via email and asked to provide the required information.

If we do not have proper forms on file for your account when a monthly payment is processed, your payments might either be paused or subject to withholding of 24% of your gross sales.

W-9 Form

A W-9 form is the means by which U.S. taxpayers provide identifying information to services like Vimeo. A W-9 requires you to provide your name, address, and Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) (more on this below). If you are a United States-based creator you must submit a completed W-9 form before receiving payments from Vimeo.

W-8 Form

A W-8 form identifies a person in a foreign country that received money from a U.S. entity.

All non-U.S. creators (except those with a U.S. TIN) must provide this form prior to receiving payments from Vimeo. The most common types of W-8 forms are form W-8BEN (for individuals) and form W-8BEN-E (for companies).

If you live in a country that has an income tax treaty with the U.S., you can make that treaty claim on your W-8 form. This may reduce the amount that Vimeo needs to withhold.

Read this article to learn how to submit the proper form.

8233 Form

Some international sellers who begin filling out a W-8BEN form in their account settings may be asked to submit an 8233 form. At this time, there is no need to submit this form, and we are working to update our online tax form process to remove the 8233 form.

In the meantime, if you are prompted to submit an 8233 form, please do not submit any tax forms. Instead, follow these instructions to submit a W-8BEN tax form.

1099-K Form

If you are a U.S.-based creator, we will send you a 1099-K form if you meet both of the following requirements:

  1. You have earned more than $20,000 in gross revenue on Vimeo On Demand over the calendar year
  2. More than 200 transactions have occurred in relation to your Vimeo On Demand title(s)

⚠️Note: If you sell multiple titles on Vimeo On Demand, we aggregate your revenue and transactions across all of your titles to determine if you meet these thresholds. If you receive a 1099-K, note that it will report the “gross revenue” from your sales, not the revenue that Vimeo actually paid out to you.

If you do not meet these thresholds, we won’t send you a 1099-K form, but your Vimeo On Demand earnings will remain subject to U.S. taxes. We advise contacting a tax professional to determine your tax responsibilities.

How to change/update/remove the tax exemption

To make any changes to tax exemption, you will need to reach out to support. Support can also refund the user if VAT charges are incurred. Please contact us for assistance.

Need help?

Our team cannot provide legal or tax advice. However, we’re happy to help you through the process of submitting the proper form. Contact us and we’ll get back to you as soon as possible.

Subscribers Report on Vimeo OTT

The Subscribers report provides metrics that allow you to measure your subscription (SVOD) site’s growth and revenue over time.

  • Subscribers report overview
  • Set the duration and interval for the subscribers report
  • Metrics provided in the Subscribers report
  • Filtering and segmenting the Subscribers report

Subscribers report overview

Similar to the Viewership report, the Subscribers report is also represented in a graph plot, showing results for the duration you are searching for. To access the report from OTT Admin, click on the Analytics menu and select Subscribers. Refer to Types of data & analytics provided by Vimeo OTT to know more.

For example, a default Subscribers report below depicts the last 30 days of data on a per-day basis. The graph gives the total count of users based on Subscription and trials for that day.

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-03-01_at_2.47.04_PM.png

A table with this information will be available below. You can also download a CSV by clicking the download icon (downward arrow) in the upper right corner.

⚠️Note: Your payout statement includes all of the transactions that were made during the month in question. The count of subscribers in the Subscribers Report includes customers who were gifted subscriptions, added via the Add Customer tool or via the API (including users added via a branded app), who may not have processed a transaction. This could mean that the Subscribers Report may show a larger number of subscribers than the total transactions in your Payout Statement.

Set the duration and interval for the subscribers report

The report supports the following time durations:

  • Last 7 days
  • Last 30 days
  • Last 365
  • Custom date range

⚠️Note: When using the Custom range option, the selection has to be within a 365-day range.

Next to the duration dropdown, you can choose to plot the data on a monthly, weekly, daily, or hourly time interval. Please note that:

  • Hourly is only available when “Last 7 days” is selected as the duration. The date and time interval data are shown in UTC.
  • The weekly time interval begins from Monday 00:00:00 UTC, ends Sunday 23:59:59 UTC per week.

Historical data on the Subscribers report is accessible from January 1, 2018, onwards for the daily, weekly, and monthly time intervals. The hourly time interval data is available starting from January 1, 2020.

Data is current to the previous day (i.e. through 23:59:59 UTC off the previous day).

Metrics provided in the Subscribers report

The Subscribers report measures the following:

  • Total
  • Total number of active subscriptions and/or trials. Active is defined as enabled users with access to your content. This consists of user purchased subscriptions, gifted subscriptions, and API created subscriptions.
  • Gained
  • Total number of new activated subscriptions and/or trials.
  • Lost
  • Total number of subscriptions and/or trials that have been disabled and no longer have access to content.
  • Churn Rate
  • Churn Rate is the percentage of subscriptions that were disabled and lost access to your content. Metric is available only for the Subscriptions filter. It’s not applicable for Trials.
  • Average Revenue
  • The Average revenue is the average subscription revenue per subscriber on any platform. Metric is available only for the Subscriptions filter. It’s not applicable for Trials.
  • Lifetime Value
  • The Lifetime value is the average amount of subscription revenue a single subscriber can be expected to generate over their lifespan as a customer. Metric is available only for the Subscriptions filter. It’s not applicable for Trials.
  • Trial Conversion Rate
  • The Trial conversion rate is the percentage of customers who converted to a subscription after their trial period ended. Metric is available only for Trials filters. It’s not applicable for Subscriptions.

Filtering and segmenting the Subscribers report

The Subscriber report by default displays the total count of Subscriptions & Trials for the chosen metric. You can filter this to show Subscriptions only or Trialsonly.

For example: Set the metric to Gained. By default, you will see the combined value of subscription and trials gained over the chosen duration, but you can apply the filter to show only gained Subscriptions, or only gained Trials.

Additionally, you can adjust the report to break out the data into these two segments:

  1. Platform: See which platforms your subscribers and trials are using to sign up for your site. This is most useful if you have branded apps for your site.
  2. Country: See which countries your OTT site’s subscriber base is from.

⚠️Note: Some subscribers may have restrictions in place that do not allow us to collect location data. In these cases, their country will be listed as ’Others’. Since users cannot be forced to share their location data, you will always see some users whose country is marked as ‘Others’. 3. Billing Frequency: You can analyze your subscriber report metrics from the Segment dropdown by choosing Billing Frequency. You can apply Billing Frequency to the metrics of Total, Gained, Lost, Churn rate, and Trial conversion rate. It is not available for Average revenue and Lifetime value. When you apply the Billing Frequency segment, the data in the report will get segmented by three Billing Frequency values: Monthly, Yearly, and Custom.

⚠️Note: Billing Frequency data is only available from Sep 1st, 2022.

For example, if you want to generate a report for Total trials active within the desired duration, you can set the metric to Total, set the filter to Trials, and the report gets generated. You can further identify where those trials are mostly coming from by using the Segment dropdown, such as which Platform most customers are using to sign up (shown below).

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-03-01_at_2.56.54_PM.png

Note: The graph and data table can display up to 10 segments at a time.

  • For metrics that have a “Total” column in the data table, we will by default display the 10 segments with the highest Total value in descending order.
  • For metrics without a total column (e.g. Churn rate, Trial conversion rate), we will by default show the highest value based on the most recent date.

You can customise which segment items appear in the graph and data table. For example, if you segment your report by Country, you can choose to view subscription and trial data from specific countries. To do so:

  1. Scroll down to the data table and click the Search icon in the segment column. Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-03-01_at_2.56.43_PM.png
  2. Search or scroll for the desired segment item (e.g. country) and click the corresponding checkbox. Note that if you already have 10 items selected, you will need to deselect one in order to select a new one.
  3. Click Add, and the data table and graph will update with the newly selected segment items.

💡Tip: You can also remove segment items from the data table by hovering your cursor over them and clicking the corresponding Remove button to the right.

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-03-01_at_2.55.08_PM.png

Tax withholding for Vimeo On Demand

Vimeo On Demand transactions are sourced in the United States and are therefore subject to U.S. tax laws and withholding requirements.

Therefore, Vimeo is required to collect tax forms or automatically withhold funds from all VOD sellers, regardless of their home country, in order to be legally compliant.

After January 1, 2017, any Vimeo On Demand payments will be subject to 24% withholding of gross sales if you do not have an approved tax form on file. In these situations, the amount withheld will be immediately remitted to the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and cannot be returned to the seller.

If you’re a U.S. citizen or entity, we will not withhold any funds as long as you have a W-9 tax form on file by the time your payment is generated.

For sellers from other countries, your withholding rate may be up to 30% of your net revenue. However, many countries have tax treaties with the United States that will reduce this rate to 0%.

Learn how to submit your VOD tax forms

How your tax information is used: Vimeo uses Tipalti, a third-party vendor to help gather and maintain your tax information. We may use the information supplied on your W-8 or W-9 for end-of-year reporting purposes. For example, when it’s time to send 1042s to international creators, or 1099s to U.S. creators that meet the required thresholds, your information will be used to generate those forms.

Thumbnail badges on Vimeo OTT

Thumbnail badges let you automatically and manually overlay status labels on your content thumbnails across your website and branded apps. Badges like New, New Episode, and Leaving Soon appear automatically based on content dates, while badges like Top 10, Exclusive, and Original can be manually applied to individual videos and collections. This article explains how to configure global badge settings, enable or disable individual badges, and assign manual badges to your content.

  • What are thumbnail badges?
  • Types of thumbnail badges
  • How to configure global badge settings
  • How to enable or disable individual badges
  • How to customize individual badge appearance
  • How to assign manual badges to videos and collections
  • Badge display limits

What are thumbnail badges?

Thumbnail badges are small text overlays that appear on the corner of your content thumbnails. They help viewers quickly identify new, expiring, or highlighted content as they browse your site and apps. Badges are displayed across all platforms, including web, iOS, Android, and TV apps (Roku, Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV, and more).

You can manage all badge settings from your OTT admin under Content > Thumbnail Badges.

Types of thumbnail badges

There are two types of thumbnail badges:

Automatic badges are displayed based on content dates. Once enabled, they appear and disappear without any manual action required. Automatic badges include:

  • New — Appears on videos published within a number of days you define (e.g., the last 1 day).
  • New Episode — Appears on series (collections) that contain an episode published within the “New” threshold you define.
  • Leaving Soon — Appears on videos that are scheduled to be removed within a number of days you define (e.g., the next 30 days).

Manual badges must be assigned to individual videos or collections by the seller. Manual badges include:

  • Top 10 — Highlight top-performing content.
  • Exclusive — Display on exclusive or premium content.
  • Original — Display on original productions.

How to configure global badge settings

Global settings control the default appearance and behavior of all badges across your site. To configure them:

  1. In your OTT admin, navigate to Content > Thumbnail Badges.
  2. Under Global Settings, configure the following options:
  • Position: Choose whether badges appear in the Top Left or Top Right corner of the thumbnail.
  • Font Weight: Select Medium (500) or Bold (700).
  • Font Family: Customize using Google Fonts (Vimeo-hosted fonts).
  • Default Background Color and Default Label Color: Set the hex color values for your primary badge color scheme.
  • Alternative Background Color and Alternative Label Color: Set a secondary color scheme that you can apply to specific badges. A live preview will show how badges appear with the Default and Alternative color schemes.
  1. Set the thresholds for automatic badges:
  • “New” badge threshold (days): Enter the number of days after publishing during which the “New” badge should appear (e.g., 1 day).
  • “Leaving Soon” badge threshold (days): Enter the number of days before a video’s scheduled removal during which the “Leaving Soon” badge should appear (e.g., 30 days).
  1. Click Save to apply your changes.

How to enable or disable individual badges

Under Badge Settings on the Thumbnail Badges page, you can control which badges are active on your site.

  1. Navigate to Content > Thumbnail Badges and scroll down to Badge Settings.
  2. For each badge (New, New Episode, Leaving Soon, Top 10, Exclusive, Original), use the Enabled checkbox to turn it on or off.
  3. Click Save to apply your changes.

💡Tip: Automatic badges (New, New Episode, Leaving Soon) will begin appearing immediately once enabled — no further action is needed. Manual badges (Top 10, Exclusive, Original) require you to assign them to specific videos or collections (see below).

How to customize individual badge appearance

Each badge can have its own appearance settings, allowing you to visually differentiate badge types.

  1. In the Badge Settings section, click Toggle advanced options next to the badge you want to customize.
  2. Configure the following options:
  • Color Scheme: Choose from Default (uses Global Settings colors), Alternative (uses the alternative color scheme), or Custom (set unique colors for this badge).
  • Font Weight (optional): Override the global font weight for this specific badge, or select Use global weight to inherit the global setting.
  • Font Family (optional): Override the global font family for this specific badge, or leave as Use global font family to inherit the global setting.
  1. Click Save to apply your changes.

How to assign manual badges to videos and collections

Manual badges (Top 10, Exclusive, Original) need to be assigned individually to the videos or collections where you want them to appear.

  1. In your OTT admin, go to Content > Videos and select the video you want to badge. To badge a collection, go to Content > Collections and select the collection.
  2. On the edit page, scroll down to the Thumbnail Badges section under General settings.
  3. Select the manual badges you want to display on this content:
  • Top 10 — Display this badge to highlight top-performing content.
  • Exclusive — Display this badge for exclusive or premium content.
  • Original — Display this badge for original productions.
  1. Click Save in the upper right corner.

⚠️Note: Automatic badges (New, New Episode, Leaving Soon) are displayed based on content dates and cannot be manually assigned. They will appear automatically on eligible content when enabled.

Badge display limits

Each thumbnail can display a maximum of two (2) badges at the same time. If a video or collection qualifies for more than two badges (for example, it is both “New” and has been marked as “Exclusive” and “Original”), only two will be shown.

💡Tip: Keep this limit in mind when combining automatic and manual badges on the same content. For best results, apply manual badges selectively to avoid conflicts with automatic badges.

Troubleshooting: Account verification for selling VODs keeps getting declined after linking PayPal

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

If you’re having trouble getting through the VOD verification process and keep getting declined, check for these common issues.

What is causing the verification to decline?

These are the most common reasons your verification will decline and what you can do to fix it.

  • Submitted ID photo is a copy: Ensure you’re taking a physical photo of your ID and not a copy of your ID.
  • PayPal information doesn’t match: Verify your PayPal information matches the information you’re submitting, such as your name.
  • Information in submitted documents do not match: Be sure that your proof of address or supplemental documents match the information you’ve entered in Persona.

After checking these elements, you can re-try the verification.

Types of data & analytics provided by Vimeo OTT

Vimeo OTT provides you with data and analytics that you can use to help grow your business and drive sales. All data is contained within the Vimeo OTT Dashboard, which you’ll see when you log in to your Vimeo OTT site.

What are the types of data and analytics provided by Vimeo OTT?

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-04-12_at_11.40.17_AM.png

The data available to you include

  • Retrieving historical subscribers & viewership data from January 1, 2018, till date for the daily, weekly, and monthly time intervals in viewership and subscribers report.
  • Customer growth metrics in the form of the Subscribers report to gain real-time business insights on total and net gain/loss in subscribers and trials count, churn rate, lifetime customer value, and trends over time, including the ability to segment by platform or country.
  • Calculate the Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) or the gross revenue for payments processed by Vimeo OTT per month
  • All transaction activity of your customers and their data, including customer email addresses and geographic location of purchase. Customize the metrics and filter and export the CSV in one click. Check all the possible video product transactions in this guide.
  • Viewership report to review your content metrics such as time watched, views, finishes, and unique viewers across the entire site and branded apps for all VOD and Live videos with the ability to segment by Platform, Country, or Videos.
  • Real-time sales information for all available products to buy and rent. Filter by dates, products, or both.
  • Google Analytics integration for additional tracking.
  • Enterprise users can receive additional OTT template reports upon request from your account managers.

Understanding payout statements

This article discusses payout statements.

  • What are statements?
  • What is included in statements?
  • Sales by product
  • Sales by region
  • Non-USD Transactions

What are statements?

Statements are a report of your monthly sales. All gross sales, fee schedules, and geographic breakdowns are included in your statements. Reports will be available to view on the web, or you can download PDF or CSV reports with all transaction details. A sample statement looks like this:

Screenshot: top.png

What is included in statements?

  • Gross Sales: This is the sum of all purchases during the month.
  • Refund Fees: You’ll see this line item if a purchase from a prior month was refunded during the current month. The amount you’ll see here is the purchase price minus the fees you paid since we don’t charge you fees on transactions that are refunded.
  • Chargeback Fees: You’ll see this line item if a purchase from a prior month was charged back during the current month. The amount you’ll see here is the purchase price plus chargeback fee minus the OTT fees you paid since we don’t charge you fees on transactions that are charged back.
  • Vimeo OTT Fees: This includes the percent of sales as well as transaction fees, coupon fees or fulfillment fees.
  • 10% of transactions: sum of fees charged as a percentage of your sales price (Gross Sales sales x 10%)
  • 50 cents: sum of fees charged for each transaction completed (# of purchases x $0.50)
  • $1 per subscriber per month
  • $1 for API fulfillment
  • Coupon Fees: most coupons are free but some films will have expenses related to bulk coupons or special merchandise-related coupons
  • Net: This is the amount we will send to you this month. We calculate this amount by netting all fees out of the Gross Sales.

All calculations are made in USD, but the payout you receive will be converted to your account currency. The transacted currency will be converted to your payout settlement currency using the exchange rates at the time of the transaction, not the time of payout.

⚠️Note: Your payout statement includes all of the transactions that were made during the month in question. The count of subscribers in the Subscribers Report includes customers who were gifted subscriptions, added via the Add Customer tool or via the API (including users added via a branded app), who may not have processed a transaction. This could mean that the Subscribers Report may show a larger number of subscribers than the total transactions in your Payout Statement. The full report is available in the transactions.CSV. The payout statement only includes a summary.

Sales by product

This page shows a breakdown of sales per product.

Screenshot: 2_sales_by_product.png

Sales by region

This page shows a breakdown of sales that took place in each state of the United States as well as a breakdown per country.

Screenshot: 3_sales_by_region.png

Non-USD Transactions

Screenshot: OTT_Fees.png

If your product is available in multi-currency, our fees may be different due to the exchange rates. For example, if you offer a rental for $12 CAD, the standard transactional fee of 10% + .50¢ is applied in CAD and then converted to USD. Let’s consider the exchange rate at the time of the transaction is 0.712. 12 CAD (0.1) = $1.20 CAD 50¢ is converted to CAD so .50*0.712 = 0.356 The total fee for a $ 12 CAD transaction comes out to about $1.56 CAD and is converted to USD for $1.11.

Understanding privacy settings for VOD videos

VOD videos have specific privacy settings to support the VOD experience. These settings ensure content is accessible to customers as intended and cannot be modified through standard video editing tools.

  • How are privacy settings applied to my VOD videos?
  • Why can’t I edit my VOD video privacy settings?
  • How does Vimeo prevent the editing of my VOD videos?

How are privacy settings applied to my VOD videos?

When you upload a video as part of a VOD, a privacy setting that aligns with VOD requirements is automatically assigned. Unlike the standard Vimeo privacy options, these settings are essential for managing access and purchases.

Why can’t I edit my VOD video privacy settings?

Vimeo’s upload API does not support these VOD-specific privacy settings. If you attempt to edit a VOD video and save changes, the action will fail because the privacy setting cannot be modified. Changing it could disrupt the VOD experience, potentially affecting customers who have already purchased access.

How does Vimeo prevent the editing of my VOD videos?

To protect the integrity of your VOD videos, Vimeo restricts access to the Video Editor for these files, ensuring no accidental changes disrupt the viewing experience.

Due to technical limitations, VOD videos have unique privacy settings that cannot be edited. If you need to alter a VOD video, consider uploading a new version with the desired edits while maintaining the original privacy settings.

Understanding the Vimeo OTT Dashboard

This article helps you understand your Dashboard.

  • What is the dashboard?
  • What analytics are available on the dashboard?
  • Pause and Cancel Reasons

What is the dashboard?

The Dashboard is an organized and comprehensive analytics tool that streamlines the way Vimeo OTT records and scales data. You can access the dashboard from the OTT Admin either when you first log in, or by clicking on the Analytics menu, and selecting Dashboard from the drop-down menu.

Once inside your dashboard, you’ll see your monthly activity summary. This gives you a snapshot of the revenue your site processes, and what you can expect payments from Vimeo to be like in the current calendar month. You’ll see Revenue, Buy and Rent and two new reports - Subscribers and Viewership. Revenue and Buy and Rent statements can be retrieved by clicking on the View statement.

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-04-12_at_11.40.17_AM.png

⚠️Note:Data will not populate in the dashboard if you are browsing in incognito or private browser mode.

What analytics are available on the dashboard?
Revenue

This is all the revenue your video network has earned on Vimeo OTT over the past month. This doesn’t count revenue made on integrated platforms such as BigCommerce, branded apps, or through the API.

Click View Statements to find all the billing details, monthly statements, and invoices in the Payouts and Charges section. To know more about how the payout statement works, check out this article.

Buy and Rent

The Buy and Rent section of the Dashboard shows the total number of fulfillments of your transactional (TVOD) product units for the current calendar month. It does not include subscription (SVOD) products. Click Buy & Rent report to access the customizable report for additional insights.

TheUnits Over Time chart outlines product units sold/fulfilled over the time period selected. You can select a time period from the dropdown under the graph title, and choose from the Past Week, Past Month, Past 3 Months, Past 6 Months, Past Year, All Time, or a Custom date range.

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-04-11_at_2.07.27_PM.png

If you click on a given bar in the chart, you will see the breakdown for that selected time period (i.e., if you’ve filtered for “Past year” in the graph, and click on the bar for March, you’ll see the breakdown for the units sold and fulfilled in March).

This chart also displays a breakdown of the type of fulfillment — Web purchases, purchase via your branded apps (e.g. iOS, Android, Android TV), API, and Free.

You can download the data statement from the downward button in the top right corner.

Viewership Report

The Viewership section of the dashboard summarises the total views, hours watched, and total finishes within the calendar month. Click Viewership report to access the full customizable report.

From there, you will see data displayed in a graph plot for aggregate viewership metrics like Views, Total time watched, Finishes, and Unique viewers, across your entire site, including any branded applications.

To access the report from the OTT Admin click on the Analytics menu, and select Viewership. To know more about how to customize your data, you can refer to this Viewership Report article.

Subscribers Report

The next report on the dashboard is the Subscribers report, which shows you your paying subscribers, current free trialists, and the sum of both metrics. Click on the Subscribers report to access the full customizable report.

The Subscribers report provides you with a measure of your subscription (SVOD) site’s growth and revenue over time. You can access the report from OTT Admin, click on the Analytics menu, and select Subscribers. To download the CSV file, click on the downward arrow icon.

To know more about customization and report generation in detail, refer to this Subscribers Report article.

Pause & Cancel Reasons

Screenshot: Screenshot_2022-04-11_at_2.07.56_PM.png

You can find the Pause & Cancel Reasons in the drop-down Analytics menu of OTT admin which is represented as a graph for the reasons your subscribers are considering canceling or pausing their subscriptions. These numbers are captured from a user survey presented when someone pauses or cancels a web subscription via the settings/purchases page. The chart presents these numbers in a rolling 3-month timeframe.

They can ‘Pause’ due to reasons like ‘Vacation’, ‘Save money’, ‘Waiting for content’, and ‘Other’.

Or, Cancel subscription owing to reasons like ‘Price too high’, ‘needs videos’, ‘Lost interest’, or ‘Other’.

⚠️Note: Not all “set cancellations” will actually result in a cancellation, since subscribers can change their minds after the cancellation. This chart will still include these subscribers in its count of Cancels since they would’ve noted a reason when they initially canceled.

Uploading videos on Vimeo OTT

This article discusses how you can upload your videos to Vimeo OTT.

  • How do I upload videos to Vimeo OTT?
  • Can I batch-upload videos?
  • What’s the transcoding process like after the video is uploaded?
  • Are my uploaded videos private?
  • Can I download my uploaded videos?
  • Can I add my Vimeo videos to Vimeo OTT?
  • Known limitations for platforms

How do I upload videos to Vimeo OTT?

At the top of your Admin, you’ll see the Videostab under Content. All of your video content gets uploaded here.

Our pricing depends on how many hours of video you upload to Vimeo OTT. The breakdown is outlined in this guide.

Can I batch-upload videos?

You can batch-upload multiple videos at once by dragging & dropping the batch into the uploader.

  1. Once the file is selected or dragged into the window, it will begin uploading. You can track its progress on the Videos page.
  2. Once the video is uploaded, it will begin the transcoding process. You can also track that progress on the Videos page.
  3. You will be emailed when the video is finished processing and can then add it to a Subscription Collection or a Purchase/Rental Product.

⚠️Note: Batch uploading directly from your computer has a limit of 120GB at a time, and batch uploading from our Dropbox integration has a limit of 50GB at a time.

If you have a large amount of video content that is already hosted on another platform, we may be able to help you. Vimeo OTT supports importing via the below providers:

  • Amazon S3
  • Cyberduck (preferred FTP method)
  • Transmit

We do not accept hard drives or any other physical media. Please contact usfor more details. If interested in bulk uploading, reach out to your Account Manager or our Sales team for more information.

What is the transcoding process?

Once your video is uploaded, we transcode it to the various resolutions and bitrates for streaming and downloading (depending on your source file format):

  • 4K MP4 download
  • CONDITIONS: Source file must have a resolution of at least 3840x2160
  • 1080p MP4 download
  • CONDITIONS: Source file must have a resolution of at least 1920x1080
  • 720p MP4 download
  • CONDITIONS: Source file must have a resolution of at least 1280x720
  • 540p MP4 download
  • CONDITIONS: Always created
  • 360p MP4 download
  • CONDITIONS: Always created
  • Adaptive streaming file
  • CONDITIONS: Always created

⚠️Note:Deleting videos does NOTgrant you more upload hours. Also, if you replace a video, it does take away from the overall hours’ allotment, since it begins transcoding immediately. We recommend that you make sure you have the final version ready to go before uploading. More information is here.

Are my uploaded videos private?

Your uploaded videos are private until you place them in a Subscription Collection or Product for sale.

Can I download my uploaded videos?

To download videos that you have uploaded to OTT:

  1. Go to the Content > Videos
  2. Click on the video you want to download
  3. Click on the Distribution panel on the left side
  4. Scroll down and select Download

You will now be able to download your video from OTT.

Can I add my Vimeo videos to Vimeo OTT?

You have the option to connect your Vimeo account to your OTT account and add your videos on Vimeo to your OTT site. This will not require additional upload hours and will use your subscription storage instead.

Known limitations for platforms

Samsung Tizen TV has choppy playback of the video sources with 23.976 FPS. The affected model’s list can be found in this article.

Use OBS Studio to go live to your Vimeo OTT site

Open Broadcaster Software Studio(OBS) is a popular free application that can stream live video to many streaming platforms, including Vimeo OTT.

You can download and read more about OBS here. Please note that livestreaming events on your OTT site is only available for Growth and Enterprise sellers.

Start by creating your event on your Vimeo OTT site by going to Content > Create live event. In the live event Setup page, click the blue Create URL and Stream key button to get your event’s RTMP URL and Stream Key.

Screenshot: create_url_and_key.png

Launch OBS. The auto-configuration wizard may open automatically when you first launch OBS or you can navigate to Tools > Auto-Config Wizardto start setting up your stream.

The third step in the auto-config wizard will prompt you for your stream information. Select Custom… from the Service drop-down menu.

Copy and paste the RTMP URL from your OTT event setup page into the Server field and the stream key into the Stream Key field. We recommend leaving the checkbox next to Estimate bitrate with bandwidth test selected. Click Next.

Screenshot: url_and_key.png

The OBS bandwidth test will begin. Based on the results of the test, the auto-configuration wizard will recommend encoding and bitrate settings. You can use these settings by selecting Apply Settings.

To quickly test streaming with a built-in laptop camera or a webcam, click the + button beneath the Sources panel, and then select Video Capture Device.

Screenshot: obs_source.png

Choose Create New, give the source a name (e.g. “Webcam”), then click OK. In the next window, you can choose among your available devices to add as a video source to OBS, then click OK to see it in the Sources panel.

Once you see your video source (i.e. your camera), click Start Streaming to go live to your OTT site.

Use the Vimeo mobile app to stream live to your Vimeo OTT site

This feature requires a Vimeo Enterpriseaccount. You may be looking to simulcast Vimeo events to a product on your Vimeo OTT site. See Broadcasting live events from Vimeo to Vimeo OTT to read more.

You can utilize Vimeo’s mobile app and simulcast feature to live stream to your Vimeo OTT site from your mobile device.

  • Requirements to stream to Vimeo OTT from mobile
  • How to stream to Vimeo OTT from mobile

Requirements to stream to Vimeo OTT from mobile

To broadcast a live stream from a mobile device to a Vimeo OTT site, you will need the following:

  • Access to your accounts on both Vimeo (vimeo.com) and Vimeo OTT (ott.vimeo.com) via a desktop browser
  • The Vimeo mobile app
  • Requires iOS 13 or higher or Android 6 or higher
  • An internet connection on your mobile device (e.g. Wi-Fi, 4G/LTE)

⚠️Note: This requires an Enterprise contract with Vimeo. If you do not have access to an account on vimeo.com with the ability to go live, contact your account manager for next steps.

How to stream to Vimeo OTT from mobile

For clarity, “Vimeo Core” refers to your account on vimeo, whereas “Vimeo OTT” refers to your account hosted on vhx.tv.

  1. First, create an event on your Vimeo OTT site. Log into your OTT dashboard and navigate to Content > Create live event.

Screenshot: 0_new_video_menu.png

Tip: If you want the event to appear only on your OTT site, consider setting its Privacy to “Hidden from Vimeo” or “Only people with an unlisted link.”

  1. In the Destinations tab, find “RTMP” and click the corresponding Add button.

Screenshot: RTMP_add.png
