The viewer profile experience on Vimeo OTT

Here’s what your viewers see once profiles are on—useful for your own understanding and for guiding viewers who have questions.

  • Choosing a profile
  • Creating and managing profiles
  • Locking an adult profile with a PIN
  • The child profile experience
  • Switching profiles

Choosing a profile

  • After signing in, the viewer lands on the Choose Profile screen showing every profile on the account.
  • They select their profile. If it’s protected with a PIN, they enter it. They then enter the platform with that profile’s own history, My List, and recommendations.

Creating and managing profiles

  • Viewers add a profile from the Choose Profile screen (up to four total), pick an avatar, and name it (up to 15 characters).
  • From Manage profiles, a viewer can rename a profile, change its avatar, mark it as a kid profile, set or change a PIN, or delete it.
  • The Main profile can’t be deleted or made into a kid profile.

Locking an adult profile with a PIN

An adult profile can be protected with a four-digit PIN under the Profile Lock setting (“Require a PIN to access your profile”). Once set, anyone selecting that profile must enter the PIN first—handy for keeping a parent’s profile private on a shared device. Child profiles never use a PIN.

The Main profile can also choose to require the PIN before new viewer profiles can be created.

Setting, changing, or resetting a PIN requires the viewer to confirm their identity with a code sent to the account email. (After the PIN is set for the Main profile, the viewer can use that PIN to change it instead of email verification.) The same flow doubles as a forgot-PIN path: a viewer who can’t remember their PIN verifies by email and gets back in without being locked out.

The child profile experience

  • A child profile shows a kid-friendly version of your library—only the content you marked child-safe.
  • Search only returns child-safe results, and adult-only titles or pages can’t be reached even by direct link.
  • Settings and account management are hidden, and there’s no PIN to enter.
  • Community features are disabled for child profiles.

Switching profiles

Viewers can switch profiles at any time from within the app, without logging out. Each switch instantly loads that profile’s own personalized experience.

  • About Viewer Profiles on Vimeo OTT
  • Setting up Viewer Profiles on Vimeo OTT
  • Setting up the child-safe viewing experience on Vimeo OTT

Vimeo On Demand content ratings

Content Ratings help us keep Vimeo On Demand titles accessible to as many people as possible. In a content rating, we ask creators to tell us if their VOD works contain nudity, violence, profanity, or drug/alcohol references. Based on the categories selected — or not selected — one of the following badges will appear on the Vimeo On Demand page: All Audiences, Mature, or Not Yet Rated.

When setting up your VOD page, you will be asked to rate the work you’re selling. The rating you choose should apply to all the work you’re selling. Choose the appropriate rating (“All audiences” or “Mature”), then, if applicable, select one or more of the mature content categories. This rating will be applied to your VOD page. You can return to your VOD settings at any time to update your rating.

Vimeo On Demand promo codes

You can offer promo codes for free or discounted rentals, subscriptions, and purchases of your work. You choose the discount, either by percentage or specific U.S. dollar amount. You can also set custom start and end dates for each code — this is especially handy for press screeners or special sales.

You can create single promo codes, or create a batch of unique promo codes. You can also create VIP access codes for offering advance access or custom access to your title. You can read more about creating each type of code below.

  • Single codes
  • Batch codes
  • VIP access codes
  • Code Limits

Single codes

To add a single promo code:

  1. Select your profile picture that appears the top right of any vimeo.com page to expand the menu.
  2. Select Watch >> Collections >>On Demand pages.
  3. Find the title’s poster image, then select the gear iconto head to its settings page.
  4. On the left-hand side, select thePromotions tab, then select Add a new promo code.
  5. Under Type, select Single, and in the text field under Code, enter the exact text viewers should use to redeem your promo code. Codes are not case-sensitive, but they may only contain letters and numbers, and can include up to 32 characters.
  6. Under Total, specify how many times this particular promo code can be used by entering a number between 1 and 5,000.
  7. Under Discount, select what kind of discount you’d like to offer and whether it applies to rentals, purchases, or both. For the creators of a series, you have the option to offer promo codes toward rentals / purchases of single episodes*, toward a monthly subscription, or toward your entire series. (Please note: at this time, only percent-off promo codes can be applied toward purchases made in currencies other than USD.)
  8. Finally, you can decide when your promo code will be active. Under Start/End Dates, click the calendar icon to select a start date for your code. Check Expires to set an end date. All promo codes default to the setting Does not expire.
  9. When you’re all done, click Create promo code to save your code.

⚠️Note:Though you can set a promo code for single episodes within a series, you cannot specify which episode can be accessed with that code. If a viewer clicks the promo code link, the system will choose an episode for them. If a viewer wants to apply the promo code to a specific episode, they will need to open that specific episode and apply the code (not the link) at checkout.

Batch codes

The batch code option allows you to create a batch of unique, single-use codes. Once you create a batch promo code, we will automatically generate a downloadable .csv file that contains the individual codes for you to share with your viewers.

To create a batch code:

  1. Select your profile picture that appears the top right of any vimeo.com page to expand the menu.
  2. Select Watch >> Collections >>On Demand pages.
  3. Find the title’s poster image, then select the gear iconto head to its settings page.
  4. Select the Promotion tab, then clickAdd a new promo code.
  5. For type, select Batch, and enter a batch name for your promo code. Please note: the batch name is not what viewers will use to redeem their promo code — they must use a unique code from the .csv file that you can download once you create your code.
  6. Under Total, specify how many times this particular promo code can be used by entering a number between 1 and 5,000.
  7. Under Discount, select what kind of discount you’d like to offer and whether it applies to rentals, purchases, or both. For the creators of a series, you have the option to offer promo codes toward rentals / purchases of single episodes*, toward a monthly subscription, or toward your entire series. (Please note: at this time, only percent-off promo codes can be applied toward purchases made in currencies other than USD.)
  8. Finally, you can decide when your promo code will be active. UnderStart/End Dates, click the calendar icon to select a start date for your code. Check Expires to set an end date. All promo codes default to the setting Does not expire.
  9. Click Create promo code to save your code.
  10. Click Get codes to download a .csv containing your batch of unique codes (including unique code links), and share these individual codes with your viewers.

⚠️Note:Though you can set a promo code for single episodes within a series, you cannot specify which episode can be accessed with that code. Your viewers will be able to apply this code to the episode of their choosing.

VIP access codes

You can give people exclusive access to your title before (or after) it’s released to the general public with VIP access codes. These codes allow you to give advance access to any crowdfunding backers, press, or family and friends. Even after you release your title, you can still create VIP access codes as needed to give certain viewers exclusive, custom access to your title. For each code you create, you can specify the type of access you want to grant, regardless of the actual purchase options you offer for your title.

If you want to create a VIP access code while your title is in pre-order, you must have a main feature added to your Vimeo On Demand (if you’re selling a series, you must add at least one episode).

To create a VIP access code:

  1. Select your profile picture that appears the top right of any vimeo.com page to expand the menu.
  2. Select Watch >> Collections >>On Demand pages.
  3. Find the title’s poster image, then select the gear iconto head to its settings page.
  4. Select the Promotion tab, then click Add a new VIP access code.
  5. Enter a name for your VIP access code. Please note: this code name is not what viewers will use to redeem their VIP access code — they must use a unique code from the .csv file that you can download once you create your code.
  6. UnderLimit, specify how many VIP codes you want to be created by entering a number between 1 and 5,000.
  7. Under Access type, select how long you’d like to give your VIP viewers access to the VOD. Please note that you cannot change the access type for a code after you’ve created it.
  8. Finally, you can decide when your VIP code will be active. Under Start/End Dates, click the calendar icon to select a start date for your code. Check Expires to set an end date, which would be the last day a buyer can apply the code and receive the free access. All VIP codes default to the setting Does not expire.
  9. ClickCreate VIP access code to save your code.
  10. Click Get codes to download a .csv containing your corresponding list of VIP access codes (including direct code links), and share these individual codes with your VIP viewers.

⚠️Note:You may not sell promo or VIP codes or otherwise use them to distribute your film in exchange for payment or other consideration except in connection with crowdfunding or Vimeo’s prior written consent.

⚠️Note:OnlyVIP promo codes are applicable for gifting more than one month of free/discounted viewing with Subscription-VODs. Standard promo codes for those VODs are only applicable towards one month of free/discounted viewing. After that, buyers will be charged the normal monthly subscription price.

Code Limits

You can create up to 100 different codes per Vimeo On Demand title, and the total number of uses across all codes made for one VOD cannot exceed 5,000. Unused codes may be edited or deleted. Once a code has been used, it can be disabled but not deleted. When a code’s limit is hit, it will be disabled automatically.

Vimeo On Demand seller requirements: Verifying and displaying contact information

To comply with the Digital Services Act, all Vimeo On Demand Sellers must display their address, phone number, and email address to buyers. Sellers must verify by February 13, 2025, or their Vimeo On Demand titles will be unpublished and removed from sale globally.

  • Why is this necessary?
  • What happens if I don’t do this?
  • Can I avoid doing this if I’m not in the EU or do not wish to sell my content in that region?
  • What is Persona? Are they trustworthy?
  • What happens if my verification fails?
  • How can I troubleshoot verification issues?
  • What information do I need to complete the verification?
  • How can I update my contact information?
  • Do I have to use my personal contact information? Can I use a virtual office?
  • What contact information will be made visible on my VOD listings?
  • Why do I also need to log in with PayPal?
  • What documents are required for proof of business registration?
  • For how long is my identity verification data stored?
  • Can I switch my account from an individual to a business without disrupting my existing listings?

Why is this necessary?

Articles 30 and 31 of the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA) require Vimeo to verify and display the contact information of all Vimeo On Demand sellers. This includes your address, phone number, and email address, which will be shown to buyers on your Vimeo On Demand listing pages in the EU. This is part of an ongoing effort to ensure transparency and keep Vimeo users safe.

💡Tip: You can read more about the Digital Service Act here.

What happens if I don’t do this?

If you don’t complete the verification process by February 13, 2025:

  • Your Vimeo On Demand titles will be unpublished and removed from sale globally.
  • If you have paid subscribers to your Vimeo On Demand content, their subscriptions will be irreversibly canceled.
  • Unverified new sellers will not be able to publish Vimeo On Demand titles.

Can I avoid doing this if I’m not in the EU or do not wish to sell my content in that region?

Vimeo requires all sellers to verify regardless of their location or which regions they are selling in.

As of February 7, 2025, sellers can choose to not display their contact information and remove their listings from sale in the European Union.

This setting is available in two places.

The “verify to get paid” flow:

Under Settings > On Demand > Payments:

What is Persona? Are they trustworthy?

Persona is our trusted partner for handling identity verification. They are an identity verification platform that helps businesses confirm the identities of their users (individuals and businesses). Learn how Persona secures and protects your information and review Persona’s Privacy Policy.

What happens if my verification fails?

You can retry the verification process by clicking Verify now from the Vimeo On Demand Create new or Vimeo On Demand Payment Settings pages or contact our support team for assistance.

What information do I need to complete the verification process?

The below image represents how the verification process will look for an individual:

You’ll be guided through a simple verification process with Persona. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Authentication:You’ll first need to log in with PayPal.
  • Redirection: You’ll be redirected to Persona’s secure website.
  • Information: You’ll be asked to provide basic information to confirm your identity, such as your name, address, and a government-issued ID.
  • Confirmation: Confirm your email address and telephone number with a one-time code.
  • Verification: Persona will verify your information quickly and securely.
  • Completion: Once verified, you’ll be returned to Vimeo. You don’t need to create a separate Persona account.

How can I troubleshoot verification issues?

If you run into issues with the Persona module’s verification flow, you can check for a mismatch in information provided or click here to retry verifying. You can also refer to the Persona Help Center. Listed below are the articles most relevant to our integration with Persona:

  • Device handoff: continue verification on another device
  • I see a “Can’t access your camera” error.
  • Why isn’t the barcode being captured clearly?
  • I see a “Failed to capture screenshot and/or the Play icon” error when I take a photo.
  • How to scan your passport with NFC
  • Troubleshoot: Receiving SMS (text message)
  • Troubleshoot: Receiving email

How can I update my contact information?

If you need to update your contact information, here’s what to do:

To update your name, first update it on your PayPal account. Once complete, return to the Persona verification flow to re-verify the updated name.

If you need to change other details, you must go through the Persona verification process again. This typically requires providing supporting documentation to verify your updated information.

The verification process ensures your account remains secure and compliant. Be prepared to provide accurate and up-to-date documents during the process.

Do I have to use my personal contact information? Can I use a virtual office?

You don’t have to use your personal contact information, and you can generally use a virtual office. The most important thing is that the contact information you provide is accurate, and verifiable, and allows you to reliably receive correspondence from buyers. This means providing:

  • A valid email address: Make sure you have access to this email account.
  • A working phone number: This must be a phone number that can receive texts for phone number verification.
  • A reliable mailing address: This can be:
  • Your business address (if you have one)
  • A virtual office address that offers mail-receiving services
  • A P.O. Box

Please Note: While virtual offices and P.O. Boxes are generally acceptable, they must be locations where you can reliably receive mail and official correspondence. Simply providing a virtual office address or P.O. Box without a way to receive mail may not be sufficient for verification.

What contact information will be made visible on my VOD listings?

If you are verifying as an individual, the following information will be visible:

  • Individual name
  • Email
  • Phone Number
  • Address

If you are verifying as a business, the following information will be visible:

  • Business name
  • Business ID number
  • Email
  • Phone Number
  • Address

Your contact information is displayed to buyers in the EU in two places:

  • Listing Page: Select from the bottom-right corner, in the seller’s name box by clicking on Contact info.
  • Checkout: Select from the left side of the checkout window by clicking on Contact info.

Why do I also need to log in with PayPal?

Your PayPal payment information must match the identity information you verify in Persona. Logging in with PayPal is fast and secure.

What documents are required for proof of business registration?

We accept documents that meet the following criteria, regardless of their name or format, as these can vary by country or jurisdiction:

  1. Business Name: The document must display the business’s registered name.

  2. Business Registration Number: The document must include the official registration or identification number assigned to the business by the relevant authority.

Examples of such documents might include:

  • Business registration certificates
  • Tax registration documents
  • Articles of incorporation
  • Trade licenses

Please note that documents may be issued in various languages and formats depending on the country or jurisdiction. Ensure that the provided documents are originals and clearly show the required information.

All business documents must be issued by an official authority such as a federal/state/municipal government, public institution (tax authority, securities and exchange commission), chamber of commerce, business registry, etc.

For how long is my identity verification data stored?

Persona will store your verification data for as long as you remain a seller on Vimeo On Demand, and six months thereafter.

Vimeo uses Persona, a third-party identity verification service, to verify seller identities. The information you provide during this process, such as your ID document, proof of address documents, phone, and email address, is stored when you maintain an active seller account on Vimeo On Demand. After you stop selling on Vimeo On Demand, this verification data is retained for another six months. For details on how your data is secured, please refer to our full privacy policy.

Can I switch my account from an individual to a business without disrupting my existing listings?

Yes, you can change your account from an individual to a business account without affecting your current Vimeo On Demand listings. Here’s how:

  1. Navigate to settings: Go to the On Demand / Payments page within your Vimeo Settings.
  2. Start the verification process: You can begin the verification process again from this page.
  3. PayPal business name: To verify as a business, Persona, our verification provider, requires a business name. This name is obtained from your linked PayPal account. Therefore, confirm your business name is correctly listed within your PayPal account.
  4. Business verification: If your PayPal account provides a business name, you’ll be given the option to verify as a business in Persona.
  5. Safe transition: Your current individual verification remains active, and your listings will remain unaffected until you complete the business verification process.
  6. Confirmation: Once your business verification is successful, your account will reflect the change.

Your existing listings will continue to be available to your viewers throughout this process. If you encounter any difficulties, contact our support team for assistance.

The Vimeo OTT terms dictionary

Not sure what we mean by a certain word or phrase? We’ve defined the common ones here for you. Need more assistance? Please contact us.

Admin -This is your Vimeo OTT backend where you edit your videos, sites, products, and subscriptions. It’s the main hub of activity and all of your seller promotional tools.

API- Application Programming Interface. A set of functions, routines, and tools that allow anyone to incorporate aspects of a platform into their own software.Vimeo’s API will enable you to leverage our tools for serving video online to your audience.

Aspect ratio- Describing the width of a video compared to its height, typically expressed in a ratio. For example, the HD video standard is defined as 16:9. Other common ratios arelisted here.

AVOD (Available for Vimeo OTT Enterprise accountsonly) -Advertising-based video on demand. Vimeo OTT supports basic advertising integration so that you’re able to integrate pre-, post-, or mid-roll ads in your videos.

Captions -Provide a written description of what is occurring in your video for viewers who may be unable to hear or process the sound. Similar to subtitles, thesecan be added to your video.

Compression- Prepare your videos in the correct format prior to uploading them to Vimeo OTT. Video compression settings recommended for Vimeo can be found here.

Conversion rates -The percentage of users that take a desired action. The sales conversion on a seller’s Dashboard refers to the percentage of site visitors who purchase content.

Dashboard -The Dashboard is the first thing you will see upon logging in to your Vimeo OTT account. It is the main hub of activity where you can view metrics including daily sales and gross revenue.

Downloading -Transferring data from the internet to a device (e.g., laptop, mobile phone). When a customer purchases a Product, they have the option to download the video to view offline. Sellers have the option to disable downloads within a Product.

DRM- Digital Rights Management. A term describing a series of technologies that are applied to a digital file that prevent access to that file across devices. Vimeo OTT DRM utilizes multiple technologies includingApple Fairplay,Google Widevine, and Microsoft PlayReady.

EST- Electronic Sell Through. For a one-time fee, your customers will have unlimited access to the TVOD products that you set available to download.

FVOD - Free Video on Demand. Allow your audience to stream or download your content for free without a paywall.

Payout - A sum of your Vimeo OTT earnings paid to you, after we deduct applicable fees. Payout occurs on a monthly basis. Statements will provide you with additional information about your monthly payout.

Products -Products describe video content and any additional digital mediathat you are selling to your customers through Vimeo OTT. This includes subscriptions (SVOD) and content for transactional purchase/rental (TVOD).

Screeners- Streaming-only copies of your video that you can send to the press, partners, and friends. They are time-sensitive and you control how long someone has access to the video. You get 100 free Screeners to send out each month at no extra cost. After that, they cost you $1 for each additional Screener sent.

Statements - Statements area reportof your monthly sales. All gross sales, fee schedules, and geographic breakdowns are included in your statements. Reports will be available to view on the web, or downloadable as PDF or CSV reports.

Streaming -Viewing a video over the internet without downloading. SVOD (Subscription Video on Demand) networks and rental videos are only available via streaming.

Subscriptions/SVOD (Subscription Video on Demand) - Customers are charged a monthly or annual fee for unlimited streaming of your videos. Video content is not downloadable.

Subtitles -Captions that translate a video’s audio narrative into another language in written form. Vimeo OTT allows you to upload .SRT and .VTT files with your videos

Transactions -A sale, subscription, redemption, or fulfilment of your content on Vimeo OTT. Information about transactions can be found in your Transactions CSV and your monthly Payout statements.

Transcoding- The process of converting video files into their Internet-ready versions. We create multiple versions of your video based on the conditions of the source file so that it works well across all devices and connection speeds.

TVOD - Transactional Video On Demand. This refers to videos available for purchase or rental. TVOD videos have a different price structurethan subscription videos.

Uploading -The transfer of files from your computer to your Vimeo OTT site. Video content, subtitles, and bonus materials are all examples of content that would be uploaded to a site.

VAT -Value Added Tax. Businesses selling digital goods must pay VAT according to a customer’s location. Vimeo currently collects and remits tax/VAT/GST/JCT/DSTbased on location.

VHX - Our old name. We became Vimeo OTT in 2016. We are a platform for selling video online directly to your audience, whether for purchase or rental, live pay-per-view events, or subscriptions.

VOD Seller FAQs

This feature requires a Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, Premium, or Enterprise plan.

We’ve compiled a list of the most frequently asked questions and answers about Vimeo On Demand here to help you make the most of your VOD experience.

  • How do I get started?
  • Are there any fees to use VOD?
  • How many videos can I add to a VOD title?
  • When will I get paid?
  • Why did my payout fail?
  • Can you re-issue a failed payment before the end of the month?
  • How can I contact my customers?
  • Can I offer my VOD for free?
  • Can my buyers download my VOD to watch offline?
  • Can I have more VIP Promo Codes?
  • What happens if I want to switch my purchase type (Rent/Buy to Subscription VOD)?
  • Can I sell 360 videos with Vimeo on Demand?
  • How do comments, likes, and recommendations work for VODs?

How do I get started?

Vimeo On Demand lets you sell videos individually, or in a series. You’ll be prompted to select one of these two options when you’re setting up your Vimeo On Demand page. That means that you’ll be able to sell your film and your series on separate pages, and customize each page. You’re also able to designate your video as a rental, purchase, or subscription.

Before you get going, you’ll want to have a few things on hand:

  • Title & description
  • Pricing
  • Trailer video
  • Promotional poster
  • The video(s) you want to sell

When you’re ready to get started, we have a step-by-step guide to getting set up here that will walk you through the process:

Start selling with Vimeo On Demand

Are there any fees to use VOD?

When you sell a video on VOD, you keep 90% of the revenue after transaction costs have been deducted. These transaction costs include:

  • Transaction fees from the buyer’s payment method
  • VAT/GST & US sales tax (where applicable)

Fees and taxes on Vimeo on Demand

How many videos can I add to a VOD title?

A single VOD title can contain up to 600 videos.

When will I get paid?

You will receive each payout approximately 30 days after the month’s end. For example, a payment for all sales made in the month of June will be transferred from Vimeo to your PayPal account on or around July 30. You will receive a detailed statement when the payment is processed, and the funds will appear in your PayPal account soon thereafter.

Why did my payout fail?

There are a number of factors that could contribute to a payout failing. These issues most commonly stem from your PayPal account information.

To begin troubleshooting a failed payout, you’ll first want to head to your Payments settings page and make sure your PayPal account is connected. If it is not, click ‘Connect’ to connect your PayPal account on that page.

Note: Vimeo does not support Business PayPal accounts so you must use your Personal PayPal account for payments.

You’ll want to make sure that you’ve also verified your PayPal account as well (you can read about PayPal’s verification process in PayPal’s help center.).

Next, you’ll want to check your PayPal account to make sure that it’s set up to receive payments. If it already is, head to your Payments settings and click “Edit your PayPal connection,” and make sure the name and email address spelling match the exact info on your PayPal account.

Keep in mind: Any missed payments will get added to the next month’s payment.

Can you re-issue a failed payment before the end of the month?

Unfortunately, it takes PayPal’s system 30 days for the failed payment notice to bounce back. Because we can’t make payments until the previous ones have gone through that process, we won’t be able to make a successful revenue payment to you until the end of the following month. Any missed payments will get added to the following month’s payment once the issue that caused the payment to fail has been resolved.

How can I contact my customers?

For legal reasons, we are not able to provide sellers with the names or contact information of those who buy their work.

That said, Vimeo On Demand gives viewers the option to opt in to receive updates from any VOD seller. A “Receive Updates” button is displayed on all VOD pages, and this button is also presented once someone has made a Vimeo On Demand purchase (right after they complete the checkout process).

In the Audience tab of your VOD page’s Settings, you’ll see an “Export email addresses” button. This lets you download a .CSV file of email addresses from anyone who opted in to receive updates from you.

You’ll want to be sure to review the “Acceptable Use Email Policy” in your VOD Settings before updating your viewers.

Can I offer my VOD for free?

If you’re looking to grant free access to a Vimeo On Demand title, the best way to do so for one or more viewers is to create and distribute promo codes. There’s several different ways you can go about that, depending on whether you want just one code or several. You can find more information about promo codes at Vimeo On Demand promo codes.

That said, sellers also have the option to grant free streaming access to one or more episodes of a series VOD title. This can be done from the Videos section of a VOD’s settings by clicking on the price listed under an episode’s title. That brings up a lightbox where you can select the “Streamed for free” option from the dropdown menu under the “This video can be” heading. Keep in mind that this will make the episode free to stream for everyone. If you’d like to offer access to just some viewers, you’re better off issuing a promo code.

Can my buyers download my VOD to watch offline?

If you’re looking to grant your buyers an option to download your VOD to watch offline, you can enable downloading under the ‘Pricing’ tab on your VOD settings page. As a note, if you haven’t enabled the ‘download’ option for videos purchased using the ‘Buy’ option when your buyer purchases the VOD, enabling that after a purchase has been made won’t retroactively grant that kind of access for buyers.

Can I have more VIP Promo Codes?

At this time, the total number of redemptions across all codes associated with a single Vimeo On Demand page cannot exceed 5,000. That means you can create a batch of 5,000 individual, single-use codes (or 5 codes that can be redeemed 1,000 times each, or 50 codes that can each be redeemed 100 times, etc).

Unused codes may be edited or deleted. Once a code has been used, it can be disabled but not deleted. When a code’s limit is hit, it will be disabled automatically.

What happens if I want to switch my purchase type (Rent/Buy to Subscription VOD)?

Unfortunately, the only way to change your VOD’s distribution method is to create a new VOD page and select the desired option and delete the current VOD.

If you set up your VOD as a Subscription Video On Demand and ever want to sell it without a subscription option, you would need to make a new page and vice versa.

Can I sell 360 videos with Vimeo on Demand?

You can use Vimeo On Demand to sell 360 video—upload 360 trailers, episodes, features, and even bonus material.

How do comments, likes, and recommendations work for VODs?

Anyone can like and comment on a video. Most viewers leave positive comments, but if someone leaves a bad comment on your VOD title, you can remove it. Hover your cursor over the comment you’d like to delete, and a red Delete link should appear. Click that, and confirm your decision. If you feel that someone’s comment violates our Community Guidelines, please contact us so that we can take a look.

A recommendation is a little bit sweeter than a comment or like, because only those who have purchased a Vimeo On Demand title are able to recommend it. Buyers are prompted to make their recommendation during their viewing, so you know they’ve actually watched it.

Ways to sell on Vimeo OTT

You can customize how you package your videos on your Vimeo OTT site in the following ways:

  • Advertising-based (AVOD)
  • Free content (FVOD)
  • Pay-Per-View (PPV)
  • Transactional (TVOD) - Purchase/Rental
  • Subscription (SVOD)

Advertising-based (AVOD)

Vimeo OTT supports basic advertising integration, so you can integrate pre-, post-, or mid-roll ads.

⚠️Note:AVOD is available on Vimeo OTT Enterprise only and requires a Google Ad Manager account. Currently, post- or mid-roll ads are only available to sellers with a Google Ad Manager 360 account. For information on Vimeo OTT Enterprise, visit ‘Vimeo OTT Plans and Pricing’.

Free Content (FVOD)

Vimeo OTT provides multiple options for distributing free content without a paywall. Additional details are found at ‘Distribute videos for free with Vimeo OTT’.

Pay-per-View (PPV)

Pay-per-view through Vimeo OTT allows your customers to purchase access to a single live video event or an on-demand collection of past live events. Read on at ‘Selling live pay-per-view products’

Transactional (TVOD)

Once you’ve arranged your videos into products, you can set either a rental price, a purchase price, or both.

  • Purchasing—This allows your customer access to videos inside a product through streaming or direct downloading. Videos can be set to ‘streaming-only’, which disables downloads.
  • Rentals- Allow for unlimited streaming within a set time period with no access to direct downloads.

Optionally, videos can be set to streaming-only, which will disable downloading. Find out about products at ‘Introduction to products’

You can also provide free or discounted access to your videos using tools like Screeners or Coupons.

There is no limit to how often a user can stream or download your videos, and you will never be charged extra for bandwidth costs.

Subscription (SVOD)

Customers pay a recurring monthly or yearly fee to receive unlimited access to collections of video content through your branded Vimeo OTT website or app. Learn how to create a subscription product at ‘Creating a subscription product’.

You can also add customers to your Subscription product via the Customer’s page for $1 USD per customer per month.

In addition, you can create free trials for subscriptions for up to 30 days. Discover how to make a free subscription trial at ‘How to create a free trial’.

⚠️ Note: Subscription-based (SVOD) videos have pricing that differs from transactional (TVOD) videos. Visit ‘Vimeo OTT Pricing breakdown’ for full details.

What happens to my VODs if my account downgrades to Plus, Starter, Basic, or Free?

If your Vimeo account downgrades or lapses to a plan that does not include Vimeo On Demand, and you don’t delete your VOD titles beforehand, a few things happen depending on which plan you downgrade to. This article discusses what happens to your content contained in a VOD title after downgrading and how to avoid and resolve unwanted consequences.

If you lapse to Free or Basic:

  • You lose access to your videos attached to VOD titles, since most videos are moved to our archive storage for one year after you lapse.
  • Your VOD titles will be unpublished and no longer available for purchase.
  • Previous buyers will no longer be able to access their VOD purchase.

If you downgrade to Starter or Plus:

  • Your videos may still be accessible, depending on the amount of storage you are using.
  • Your VOD page will be unpublished and no longer available for purchase.
  • Previous buyers can still access their VOD purchase, but only if you didn’t delete the VOD title before downgrading.

To avoid your videos becoming inaccessible, delete your VOD titlebefore downgrading your account.

  • This will unpair your content from the VOD title.
  • It will also give your buyers a 30-day notice to download the content (if you allow it) or watch it before it’s no longer accessible.

If your account has already downgraded or lapsed and you are unable to access your VOD videos, you need to either:

  • Re-upgrade your Vimeo account to regain VOD access
  • Contact support to have the VOD title deleted

What is Vimeo OTT?

Vimeo OTTis the company’s dedicated over-the-top (OTT) platform, offering the essential technology and tools for launching a subscription service and building a sustainable business. This article provides an overview of the optimal ways to utilize Vimeo OTT for an enhanced user experience.

  • Ways to use Vimeo OTT
  • Making the most out of Vimeo OTT
  • Suggested next steps

Ways to use Vimeo OTT

You can use Vimeo OTT to do the following things:

  • Add new videos and metadata in seconds
  • Customize your website, apps, and checkout page
  • Own customer data in one central dashboard
  • Track analytics, including subscriber growth and churn
  • Offer your audiences a custom app that matches your brand’s look and feel and more.

Making the most out of Vimeo OTT

You can use the following available tools on Vimeo OTT to make the most of your content:

  • World-class video player: Your videos look pristine everywhere, with powerful CDNs that deliver adaptive streaming to customers.
  • Seamless payment processing: Accept credit cards and in-app subscriptions so customers can subscribe on any device. Vimeo usesStripe for payment processing, ensuring security for sensitive data. Read more aboutStripe’s security practices.
  • Integrated CMS: Manage your growing video library, from ingestion and transcoding to detailed metadata.
  • Comprehensive, human support: Ensure around-the-clock support for your viewers. Vimeo support takes care of them (and you) 24/7.
  • Advanced selling options: Test monetization strategies like ads and transactional sales, or implement digital rights management (DRM).
  • Branded apps everywhere (Enterprise): Deliver video on all major platforms. Your service matches your brand, wherever viewers are watching.
  • Live (Enterprise): Deliver live content to your audience on your branded apps.
  • Migration assistance (Enterprise): Easily move your existing service, videos, and customer data with Vimeo’s advanced account support.

Suggested next steps

For answers to common questions about using the Vimeo OTT platform, please refer to theVimeo OTT section within our Help Center.

For more information on the specifics of these features, contact our team.

What the customer sees on my Vimeo OTT site

Here is an example of what your customers experience, from clicking the “Complete purchase” button all the way to watching your videos.

The checkout page

Screenshot: Screenshot 2023-07-20 at 3.24.42 PM.png

When you sign up to sell on Vimeo OTT, upload your videos, and create a product, a checkout page is created. Every product on Vimeo OTT has a specific checkout page, where customers pay for access to your content, purchase gifts for other people, and redeem coupon codes.

Previewing the content

The checkout page includes your product description and a Play Trailer button that allows customers to watch the trailer you uploaded on the product settings page.

Screenshot: watch_trailer.png

Buying/Renting/Preordering/Subscribing

There are three sales modes that a Product can be in:

  1. SUBSCRIBE - Users can subscribe to your SVOD product and can stream your content anytime. They will be charged per month or per year (whichever they choose at checkout). ⚠️Note: If you enabled free trials, they will be entered in the set trial period before they are charged.
  2. Buy- Once the content is purchased, the customer can stream and watch forever. They now own the content. They can log into Vimeo OTT to view or download it anytime.
  • Pre-order - If the product being sold is in pre-order mode, the customer will enter their credit card information, and will not be charged until the release of the content specified by the seller. Once the seller releases the content, the customer will receive an email and will be able to watch it immediately.
  1. Rent- If you’ve enabled rentals on your product, this will be an option on the checkout page. Once the customer starts watching, they have a certain amount of hours to finish depending on the rental period you set for that video. On rentals, all downloads are disabled.
Buying with a credit card

Customers have the option to purchase using several different popular payment methods including credit cards orpayment wallets such as Google Pay and Apple Pay. The credit card option will always be available but other selections are dependent on the user’s browser configuration. For instance, if a Customer is using the Chrome browser and has an active Google wallet configured, the option for Google Pay will appear, or if the customer is using Safari with an active Apple wallet, the option for Apple Pay will appear. Customers will never see Apple Pay and Google Pay on the same checkout page as they are browser-specific. Additionally, customers can checkout with 1-Click via a Link account.

  1. On the checkout form, customers will be required to enter their email twice for confirmation. This is the address where the receipt and watch links will be sent. Customers will also use this to log in to your site in future sessions. ⚠️Note: When the customer enters their email address, if they have a Link account, they will receive a text with a verification code on the phone number associated with Link your account and will have to enter the verification code in the new field below the email address box and their payment information will auto-fill the payment fields. The customer needs to enter their CVV.
  2. If your customer is purchasing a “Buy or Rent” product, they will need to select between “Buy” or “Rent” options, individually. If your customers are purchasing a “Subscription” product, they will choose between frequency options; “Monthly” or “Yearly.” All of these option’s visibility depends on how the corresponding products have been configured. Screenshot: buy_or_rent.png
  3. Customers using a credit card will enter the name on their card, the card number, expiration date, CVC code, country, and postal code. This information helps ensure the transaction is not fraudulent.
  4. Customers selecting a payment wallet option such as Google Pay will see a window open in their browser that allows them to choose their pre-configured payment method and preview the configured price.
  5. Customers who choose to pay via Apple Pay will see a payment prompt appear on their screen
  6. After configuring their payment, Customers will see a fee breakdown of their payment that includes taxes and final payment amounts, where applicable. Fees are only noted when due, inclusive taxes are not itemized and free trials are explicitly noted as no payment due today. ⚠️Note: If a customer does not have an existing Link account, once they have added their credit card information, a new pre-selected checkbox will appear below the credit card field Save your info for secure 1-click checkout with Link. They can uncheck this box to opt out of Link.
  7. Customers will see an “Automatic Renewal Details” section. They should click on the checkbox here to authorize the automatic renewals Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-01-08 at 4.37.43 PM.png
  8. Customers will submit their payment, the transaction will process and, upon success, the receipt will load. The customer can then click the Start Watching link on the receipt to begin.
  9. Customers will also receive a copy of their receipt in their email with a summary of their payment and a link to start watching.

Gifting

Another feature of the checkout page is the gifting tool. If gifting is selected, the customer can enter an email address to gift the content to. They can also supply a short message to the recipient of the gift.

Once payment is complete, the recipient will receive an email on the selected delivery date to redeem the gift and start watching.

⚠️Note: If the gift is a preorder, the recipient will not be able to view the content until it’s released.

Redeeming Promo Codes

The checkout page also has a Promo code checkbox for entering promo coupon codes they may have received from the seller. These codes can be a certain percentage discount or can make the content totally free.

Screenshot: promo_checkbox.png

Screenshot: promo.png

The site experience

Once the purchase is complete, customers can access your content. They can navigate to the site’s Browse page where they can see your featured carousel at the top of the page and find all your categories and collections.

Screenshot: what_customer_sees_watching.png

Customers can also select Search at the top of your site to quickly find what they are looking for.

Opening a Movie or Series collection will bring them to the collection’s page with all the videos contained in it. Additionally for Series, users can sort which videos they see using the Season drop-down menu.

Screenshot: episodes.png

Watching

Once the customer clicks through to the watch page from the receipt, the video or live event will auto-play on the page.

Our video player uses adaptive streaming, meaning the load times are short, and the quality of the video will increase with internet speed. If the product purchased has more than one video in it, the other videos are listed lower down the page to be played.

Screenshot: tvod_watch_page.png

Downloading

If the content purchased has downloads enabled on the videos, there will be a download button within the player to download the different resolutions of the video to a computer to keep for later viewing.

Screenshot: tvod_downloads.png

Note:Rentals or Subscriptions do NOT have downloads enabled, and the viewer can only stream the content within the rental timeframe.

Enabling Subtitles

If the video has subtitles uploaded, the customer can select their language of choice from the CC dropdown. The subtitles will play along with the video right within the player. They can also be downloaded as an SRT file from the downloads dropdown below the player.

Screenshot: captions.png

Commenting

Every video’s watch page can have comments enabled to grow community engagement around the content. Anyone who has purchased can see all the comments and comment themselves if they’re enabled. The seller will be notified of each comment left on the videos. As a seller, it’s in your best interest to engage with the community in the comments section.

Screenshot: tvod_comment.png

Sharing

Every video on Vimeo OTT has a share button built into the player. This means the viewer can click on the icons for the below services to share what they are watching.

  • Facebook -Sharing on Facebook creates a pre-filled share for the customer to post on their wall, displaying what they are watching on Vimeo OTT with a link to the content’s homepage.
  • Twitter - Sharing on Twitter creates a pre-filled tweet for the customer to send, displaying what they are watching on Vimeo OTT with a link to the content’s homepage and an auto-loaded trailer of the content.
  • Embed code -This copies the embed code of the content’s trailer with a buy button that the customer can post on their own website to promote the work and drive sales.

Language

If you enabled and supplied translations for your site, customers can scroll to the very bottom of any page on the site and find a Language dropdown menu in the lower right corner. The languages you enabled will be listed and customers can select their desired language to be translated.

The translations will persist as they navigate between pages on your site. They can always go back to this menu and revert back to English (or choose another language) as they wish.

Why branded apps are a good investment for Vimeo OTT

With an Enterprise account, Vimeo OTT offers branded appson iOS, Android, Apple TV, Android TV, Roku, Amazon Fire (TV and tablet), Universal Windows Platform (Xbox), Tizen TV (Samsung), LG TV, and Vizio TV. Expanding your network beyond the web viewing experience has quite a few benefits. Having apps for your network not only increases the visibility and awareness of your brand but also helps you grow your subscriber base and reduce your churn.

  • Why should I use Branded apps?
  • What platform should I start with?

Why should I use Branded apps?

Having your brand appear in a platform’s app store can increase your visibility to prospective subscribers. If they’re looking for the type of content you offer — original programming, fitness, or instructional videos — being present in app stores is a great way to get discovered. If you’re offering a free trial, which we highly recommend, having an app can help increase your customer conversion rate. People are 33% more likely to sign up for a free app trial than on the web. In general, two-thirds of free trial sign-ups convert into paying customers. These conversions can be even higher with people who sign up through apps — we’ve seen up to a 72% conversion on these platforms.

Apps can help retain customers too. Customers who sign up via an app platform are less likely to churn because of an expired card since they use those accounts for other purchases. Apps can also help improve the lifetime value of your customers. 58% of customers who sign up via the web eventually add mobile or connected device (think TV or tablet) viewing to their watching habits.

Your customers can also access any transactional products you’d like to offer in most apps as well.

What platform should I start with?

Getting the full suite of apps we offer is great for attracting the largest number of prospective customers across all platforms, although if you want to start out slow with just one or two apps, you can do that too. The best platform to start with will be largely dependent on your audience’s demographics and viewing habits. For most sites, it makes sense to start with iOS. If you aren’t sure, contact us and we can help you determine which app is best for your network.

If you think you’re ready for branded apps on your network, contact our team for more information.

Policy, safety, and copyright

About Creative Commons licenses

Creative Commons licenses give video creators a standardized way to grant public permission to use their creative work under copyright law. From the reuser’s perspective, the presence of a license on a copyrighted work answers the question, What can I do with this work?

On the Upload defaults page within Settings, you will find the following options at the bottom to select the Creative Commons license you would like to apply to your videos:

  • Attribution: This license allows individuals to distribute, remix, adapt, and create derivative works from the material in any medium or format, so long as credit is given to the creator. The license allows for commercial use. View License Deed / View Legal Code for Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported.
  • Attribution Share Alike: This license allows individuals to distribute, remix, adapt, and create derivative works from the material in any medium or format, so long as credit is given to the creator. The license allows for commercial use. If you remix, adapt, or build upon the material, you must license the modified material under identical terms. View License Deed / View Legal Code for Creative Commons Attribution Share Alike 3.0 Unported.
  • Attribution No Derivatives: This license allows individuals to copy and distribute the material in any medium or format in its unaltered form only, and only so long as attribution is given to the creator. The license allows for commercial use. View License Deed / View Legal Code for Creative Commons Attribution No Derivatives 3.0 Unported.
  • Attribution Non-Commercial: This license allows individuals to distribute, remix, adapt, and create derivative works from the material in any medium or format for noncommercial purposes only, and only so long as attribution is given to the creator. View License Deed / View Legal Code for Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial 3.0 Unported.
  • Attribution Non-Commercial Share Alike: This license allows individuals to distribute, remix, adapt, and create derivative works from the material in any medium or format for noncommercial purposes only, and only so long as attribution is given to the creator. If you remix, adapt, or build upon the material, you must license the modified material under identical terms. View License Deed / View Legal Code for Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial Share Alike 3.0 Unported.
  • Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives: This license allows individuals to copy and distribute the material in any medium or format in its unaltered form only, for noncommercial purposes only, and only so long as attribution is given to the creator. View License Deed / View Legal Code for Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives 3.0 Unported.
  • Public Domain Dedication: This license is a public dedication tool, which allows creators to give up their copyright and put their works into the worldwide public domain. It allows individuals to distribute, remix, adapt, and build upon the material in any medium or format, with no conditions. View License Deed / View Legal Code.
  • No Creative Commons License: Does not add a Creative Commons license to your videos.

Applying any of these licenses will add your video to the relevant section(s) of our Creative Commons page.

For more in-depth information including license deeds and legal codes, please visit the Creative Commons About page.

About Vimeo Enterprise usage in healthcare

From interactive staff training to live and on-demand communication, Vimeo’s secure video platform helps healthcare organizations create, edit, share, and manage video content in one place.

Clinical Training As more businesses adapt to hybrid and global workforces, there’s a need for better communication tools and secure knowledge sharing for employee communications, training, collaboration, and team alignment. Encourage a learning culture by uploading and sharing educational videos on Vimeo. Measure and maintain your medical practitioners’ knowledge and expertise with interactive video quizzes and polls.

Patient Education Upload videos to spread awareness about disease prevention and management of chronic conditions. Empower your patients with the ability to access secure, password-protected videos from their homes, anytime and on any device. Create and publish videos with interactive overlays and time triggers to provide more information or additional resources for your patients.

Live Streaming and Events Healthcare companies with global customers may need secure and scalable resources to host and produce live events and webinars. Using a browser-based production studio alongside AI-powered video creation and editing tools with auto closed captioning and transcriptions can help you scale your events without stretching budgets or resources.

Marketing Content Embedding marketing videos on your website is a great way to generate awareness around your brand or offering. Hubspot reports that over 66% of consumers watch video to learn about a brand or product. Create your videos with AI-powered tools like one-take video creation or upload your latest branded video to Vimeo.

Preserve and Share Institutional Expertise Create a video library for organizational knowledge management and sharing. Provide access to the entire organization or restrict video access to relevant departments and teams with our privacy controls and folder restrictions.

Encourage Interactive Learning Leverage the power of video by making the live and on-demand training content interactive. Add quizzes and polls to evaluate your learners and to collect feedback or recommendations. You can also attach handouts or presentations with interactive overlays to your videos to provide additional resources.

If you want to use Vimeo in another way, contact us.

Can I search by Creative Commons licenses?

Yes. Enter your search term in the search bar on the top right of any page, then select “Search all of Vimeo” to search all content on the Vimeo site (rather than just your content). From your search results, click the More Filters button. Select a Creative Commons license under the License drop-down menu, and your search results will automatically update.

You can also search for content on our Creative Commons page, which is organized by license type.

Can I use someone else’s copyrighted work in my own work?

If you obtain permission (the legal term is a “license”), you can use another person’s copyrighted works as they’ve permitted. Section 1 of our Community Guidelines discusses this.

If your use of the material is protected by fair use, you don’t need the copyright holder’s permission.

Here are some more options for using content from other videos for your own:

  • Creative Commons, where creators apply for a license on their videos for re-use provided it’s used according to the license’s terms.
  • The Editor, which includes templates and stock images and video footage to create engaging social videos.

Can Vimeo tell me if my video counts as fair use?

We wish we could offer a clear answer, but determining fair use is complex and nuanced. Vimeo users are individually responsible for ensuring their videos do not infringe on copyright laws. While you may upload content that you think qualifies as fair use, it’s important to remember that this is done at your own risk. Careful consideration of fair use principles and how they apply to your content is essential.

That means you should consider the four factors of fair use and see if you can apply them to your videos.

A Comprehensive Guide: What Content You Can Upload to Vimeo

Vimeo is an online video platform that empowers you to showcase your creativity, engage your audience, and make a lasting impact. As you embark on your journey with Vimeo, it’s important to understand the guidelines and policies that govern the platform. This article will serve as your guide to using Vimeo effectively and ensuring your content meets the platform’s standards while providing a positive experience for all users.

We will dive into Vimeo’s terms of service and content guidelines to provide you with a comprehensive understanding of what kind of content is acceptable on Vimeo.

Vimeo Terms of Service

When using Vimeo, it’s important to familiarize yourself with the rules and regulations outlined in the terms of service. Here are the critical sections related to uploading content:

Ownership and Responsibility

You own the content you upload to Vimeo, but it’s your responsibility to ensure that you have all the necessary rights, licenses, and permissions to share it on the platform.

Prohibited Content

Vimeo strictly prohibits the upload of content that infringes upon intellectual property rights, promotes hate speech, contains explicit violence or pornography, harasses or defames individuals, or violates any local, national, or international laws.

Copyright Infringement

Vimeo respects copyright laws and takes copyright infringement seriously. Unless you have explicit permission or a legal basis, you cannot upload content that violates the copyrights of others.

Vimeo Content Guidelines

Third-Party rights

The content you upload should not infringe on any other third-party rights. This may include trademark rights and privacy rights.

Sexually Explicit Content

We do not allow pornography or other sexually explicit content. This includes content that.

  • depicts sexual acts in an explicit manner

  • contains sexualized nudity; or

  • is primarily intended to cause sexual stimulation, even if no sexual act or nudity is featured. We may allow videos that depict sexuality that serve a clear creative, artistic, aesthetic, or narrative purpose and non-sexual nudity. However, in these cases, you must rate the content properly..

Defamation

We do not allow content that makes provable false statements of fact about a person, regardless of their private or public status, that would harm their reputation. If the complaining figure is a public one, we will generally require evidence that the false statement was maliciously made to take down the content.

Harassment, bullying, and abuse

We do not allow content that seeks to threaten, intimidate, insult, shame, or hurt an individual or group, regardless of their private or public status. Threats, doxing, revenge porn, trolling, cyberbullying, and other forms of abuse will be removed. We may allow critical commentary of public figures as long as it does not constitute harassment or abuse.

Hateful and Discriminatory Speech

We do not allow hateful and discriminatory speech. We define this as any expression that (1) is directed to an individual or group of individuals based upon personal characteristics of that individual or group; (2) conveys a message of inferiority or contempt; and (3) would be considered extremely offensive to a reasonable person.

Promotes or supports terror or hate groups

We do not allow content from hate or terror groups that aim to spread propaganda designed to radicalize and recruit people or aid and abet attacks or provide instructions on how to assemble explosive/incendiary devices or homemade/improvised firearms.

Child Harm

We do not allow content that was created through the exploitation of children or that is harmful to children. Content featuring child nudity is not permitted. We will remove this type of content, regardless of who posted it or with what intention, to reduce the chances of others using it for unintended or harmful purposes. 💡Tip: If you intend to watch Vimeo with your kids or upload any content featuring them, please read our Parental Guidance for tips on how to keep them safe.

Depicts or encourages self-harm or suicide

We do not allow content that depicts or encourages self-harm or suicide. We do allow videos where users talk openly about depression, self-harm, suicide, or other mental health issues, or about their own experiences with these issues, to educate the public, raise awareness and help others.

Excessive Violence

We do not allow content that:

  • Incites violence

  • Show people being murdered, tortured, or physically or sexually abused

  • Depict self-mutilation or encourage it

  • Show animals being tortured or killed

  • Display shocking, disgusting, or gruesome images

Videos that depict violence in a way that complies with our Guidelines must be marked with a “Mature” content rating to be displayed on Vimeo.com.

Deceptive Schemes

We do not allow content that promotes:

  • Illegal schemes (like Pyramid/Ponzi schemes)

  • Businesses that promise wealth with little or no effort

  • Unregistered securities offerings (absent a legal basis)

  • Illegal products or services

  • Products or services (even if legal) using deceptive marketing practices

Health Misinformation

We do not allow health-related content that might cause people to take dangerous or unproven treatments or refrain from taking indicated precautions or treatments that the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) or World Health Organization (WHO) recommend. We also do not allow claims that an epidemic or pandemic (such as COVID-19) is a conspiracy.

Vaccine Misinformation

We do not allow claims that vaccines are unsafe for a general population unless the CDC or WHO has substantiated the claim. In addition, we do not allow content that promotes an agent or treatment for use to vaccinate against a particular infectious disease if it has not been specifically approved by a governmental body.

Abortion Misinformation

We do not allow content that seeks to provide false or misleading information regarding the safety and availability of abortion care.

Voter Suppression

We do not allow content that spreads false or misleading information on voter eligibility, voter registration, and the voting process (e.g., time, place, manner, requirements) in a manner that might cause a reasonable voter to fail to take an action that would allow that person to effectively vote. We also do not allow content that seeks to intimidate or harass voters.

Election Interference

We do not allow content that: calls for violence over voting or an election; seeks to intimidate or harass persons who administer voting or elections; or encourages others to do any of the foregoing or to interfere with or obstruct the voting or election process.

Misinformation about Elections Results

We do not allow content that

  • contains an explicit or implicit call for violence or unlawful activity.

  • defames, intimidates, or harasses people or companies involved in administering elections.

  • is part of an apparent campaign to spread disinformation on Vimeo.com (e.g., multiple accounts created to spread the content or other coordinated behavior).

Candidate Eligibility

We do not allow content that spreads false or misleading information about a candidate’s technical eligibility requirements for an elected office (e.g., age, citizenship, address).

False and Misleading Content

We do not allow:

  • Claims that established events such as genocides, school shootings, or terrorist attacks did not happen.

  • Claims that a disaster or other emergency did occur when no such event happened.

  • Fake news, highly deceptive manipulated media (e.g., deep fakes), propaganda, conspiracy theory-related content, or any other false and misleading information that creates a serious risk of real-world-harms to individuals, groups, and the general public.

Vimeo provides a platform for creators and businesses to share their videos with a global audience. By understanding and adhering to Vimeo’s terms of service and content guidelines, you can maintain a positive and compliant presence on the platform. Following these guidelines ensures that your content aligns with Vimeo’s standards and contributes to a vibrant and respectful community of creators.

Digital Rights Management (DRM) for my videos

This feature is available as an add-on with the Enterprise plan.

Digital Rights Management (DRM) is a technology that helps protect your videos from unauthorized copying, sharing, and misuse. It helps ensure that only authorized viewers can access your content while enforcing rules on how it can be used.

  • How does DRM work?
  • How can I enable DRM?
  • DRM video playback restrictions
  • Browser and device compatibility
  • How can I update old embed codes for DRM?
  • Next steps

How does DRM work?

DRM works by encrypting your video content with a special key. Only users with the correct license can decrypt and play the video. This license also sets restrictions on how the video can be used, such as:

  • Prevents sharing: DRM ensures that viewers cannot share your videos.
  • Controlling Usage: Actions like screen recording and taking screenshots can be restricted.

How can I enable DRM?

You can enable DRM protection via a toggle under Privacy in your Team Settings.

  • DRM technology: To protect your videos, we use industry-standard DRM technologies like Google Widevine, Microsoft PlayReady, and Apple FairPlay.
  • Enabling DRM at the Team Level: You can turn on DRM for your account in your Team Settings:settings. When this setting is toggled on, it will override all the existing video settings you have and turn DRM on for all of your videos. Additionally, the default for new videos will be DRM enabled. When this setting is toggled off, it will override all the existing video settings you have and turn DRM off for all of your existing videos. Additionally, the default for new videos will be DRM turned off.
  • Enabling DRM at the video level: You can turn DRM on and off on the video settings page. This setting will default to whatever your team’s DRM setting is. This setting will never affect your team’s DRM setting
  • HLS and DASH downloads are disabled: Please note that you cannot download Play files when DRM is active.
  • Text tracks are not encrypted: Text tracks, transcripts, and thumbnails will not be encrypted by DRM.
  • If using Edge or Chrome and Permissions-Policy is set on the page, then old embed codes will need to be updated to include encrypted-media as a value in the allow attribute list.

DRM video playback restrictions

Playback restrictions are as follows:

  • Download restrictions: Viewers will not be able to download DRM-protected videos.
  • Screen recording prevention: DRM helps prevent screen recording on supported devices and browsers.
  • 360-degree playback is not supported.
  • Maximum resolution may be limited: Playback may be capped at 720p in certain environments to comply with HDCP content protection requirements.

Browser and device compatibility

  • Latest Browsers Recommended: For the best playback experience, viewers should use the latest version of their web browser. Older browsers may experience playback issues.
  • Startup Time: DRM may have a slight impact on video startup time due to encryption and licensing verification.
  • Third-Party Players: DRM-protected videos will not work on third-party players.
  • Mobile Apps: DRM playback is supported on Vimeo’s native iOS and Android apps.

How can I update old embed codes for DRM?

If you are using Edge or Chrome and your page has a Permissions-Policy set, old embed codes may need to be updated. Ensure that encrypted-media is included in the allow attribute list of the embed code for proper DRM functionality.

By enabling DRM for your videos, you ensure that your content remains secure, is only accessible by authorized viewers, and cannot be easily shared or misused.

Next steps

Read more about troubleshooting video playback and DRM issues on Chrome.

Do I need permission to use another person’s trademark?

Not necessarily. Trademark infringement only occurs when there is alikelihood of confusion.

Reference to a trademark isn’t infringement. For example, you might need to refer to a trademark when describing a good or service. The doctrine of “nominative fair use” permits this kind of use, so long as the trademark isn’t used more than is necessary.

We cannot advise you on whether or not your proposed use might be considered infringing or non-infringing, as each case is different and will depend upon a number of factors. If you have doubts, the best practice is either to obtain the trademark holder’s written permission or to not use the trademark material at all.

Do trademark owners also own the custom URL for their trademarked terms on Vimeo?

Vimeo custom URLs are issued on a first-come, first-served basis. With few restrictions, Vimeo users can select any unregistered term and use it as a custom URL for their profile, videos, groups, or channels.

When selecting custom URLs for your own account, we recommend you use terms that are clearly related to you and your content, such as your name, a common web handle, your video titles, or your business. Avoid choosing terms that may infringe on a trademark.

You should be aware that owning a trademark for Acme Inc. does not necessarily give you the exclusive right to vimeo.com/acme as your URL. We will allow anyone to use that URL so long as their use isn’t likely to be considered trademark infringement.

If you believe that your trademark is being infringed, you can report it.

Does Fair Use apply if I credit the artist or mention fair use in my video description?

Writing “Copyrighted material used under fair use” or “No copyright infringement intended” in your video description or in the credits does not strengthen your fair use claim.

Attributing the original artist(s) in your video description or credits also does not impact the fair use analysis.

Does fair use apply to the background music in my video?

We strongly advise against using a commercial music recording as the background song of your video or live event, particularly if you’re just looking to enhance the impact of your video. However, if the visual accompaniment to the song somehow “transforms” the original work to create something wholly new and unique, you may have a stronger claim to fair use.

Please also note that purchasing music from digital music platforms does not constitute a license to use the copyrighted material in your personal works. Copyright owners reserve the right to submit a DMCA takedown request for such uses.

If you are looking to license music for your video, consider one of the following websites:

  • Musicbed
  • Marmoset
  • Song Freedom
  • Filmstro

Also, if you use Vimeo’s creation and editing tool to make your video, you can choose from a library of commercially licensed music.

Does fair use give me free reign to reuse any material I want without getting permission?

No. “Fair Use” is not a magic phrase you can invoke to excuse your use of someone else’s creative work. You cannot copy someone else’s work and then claim fair use.

What is considered “fair use” depends on the circumstances. Fair use protects creators who reuse copyrighted content in a few ways. Some oversimplified examples include:

  • When the new work directly critiques and comments on existing works
  • For educational or scholarly purposes
  • To transform the source material into something new.

Determining fair use is more complicated than just a few general use-case examples, and we urge you to educate yourself before determining if you can claim fair use in your work.

Does Vimeo allow copyright enforcement agencies to scan my private videos for copyright infringement?

Vimeo does not provide copyright enforcement agencies (or anyone else) with backdoor access to your account or videos.

That said, there are a number of ways that copyright owners or their agents can find and send takedown notices for videos that currently have a restricted privacy setting:

  • The video was not always private and they detected it before the setting was changed
  • The video was embedded on a third-party site to which they had access
  • The video was placed in a collection with a less restrictive privacy setting, which would override the native video setting.
  • The video was reported to them by someone with the password or who otherwise had access
  • The user who uploaded the video did not actually choose a restricted privacy setting

Be advised that it is a violation of our rules to upload any video for which you don’t have all the necessary rights and permissions, no matter what privacy setting you select.

Does Vimeo offer a Data Processing Agreement?

Vimeo includes a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) in our standard Terms for Enterprise and Vimeo OTT customers. We do not offer a DPA for self-serve users. If you use Vimeo’s embeddable player, you may enter into controller-controller standard contractual clauses with Vimeo to address the transfer of information of your site visitors using this webform: 0

Does Vimeo participate in the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF)?

Vimeo and its subsidiaries are active participants in the EU-U.S. DPF, the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and the Swiss-U.S. DPF. You can view our listing and certifications on the official DPF website.

Being certified signifies that Vimeo not only currently meets but is also committed to continuously adhering to the stringent data protection requirements set by European authorities. This commitment ensures the secure transfer of personal data from the EU, UK, and Switzerland to Vimeo in the United States.

For more information, please review the section titled “International Data Transfers and Certain User Rights” in our Privacy Policy.

Does Vimeo sell my data?

Vimeo recognizes that users in certain jurisdictions have the right to opt out of the sale of their personal information, and to request information about whether we have sold their personal information in the past 12 months. When you use our services, we may share your personal information with advertising partners in a way that may constitute a sale under the CCPA.

You may opt out via the link provided on the relevant page or app. If we do not provide an opt-out mechanism, it is because we have a good faith belief that personal information collected from that property is not being sold. For more information, please review our Privacy Policy.

FAQ: Copyright strikes

We know the Digital Millenium Copy Act (DMCA) takedown experience is unpleasant for our creators. To provide as much transparency as possible to our community, we’ve compiled answers to the most frequent questions we get regarding copyright strikes.

  • What is a copyright strike?
  • How do I avoid getting copyright strikes?
  • How do I have a copyright strike removed?
  • Where can I see the strikes on my account?
  • I had a license to use the content in my video. What can I do?
  • What happens if I get too many strikes?
  • Why is Vimeo threatening me with account termination after getting two strikes?
  • I have two strikes and don’t want my account disabled. Can I get a grace period to review my videos?
  • Why am I getting a strike now for a video I uploaded years ago?
  • I have one or more strikes but I never received notifications of them.
  • The number of claims on my DMCA notices page doesn’t match the number of strikes. Why is that?

What is a copyright strike?

When Vimeo removes a video from your account in response to a DMCA takedown notice, Vimeo records a copyright strike against your account. We keep track of copyright strikes as part of our Repeat Infringer Policy.

How do I avoid getting copyright strikes?

The best way to avoid claims of copyright infringement is to be extremely careful with the videos you upload. Make sure that they do not include any material that you don’t have all the necessary rights and permissions, including any applicable music licenses.

You should also review all your uploads and fully delete any that might have copyright issues.
