How can my viewers watch past streams of a recurring event?

You can configure your live broadcast or webinar to display a playlist of all past streams of that event within the event player. This allows your audience to access all archived streams of that event and watch them within a single player without requiring you to embed each archive’s video manually.

To display the playlist option on your live event player:

  1. First, create your event or select an event from your library.
  2. In the left navigation menu, select Player, then Customize Player.
  3. A new page will open. Your settings will appear in the left side panel with a preview of your event’s player in the middle of the page. Find the Playlist section in the panel (below Before event settings). Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-05-10 at 12.19.37 PM.png
  4. Toggle on Playlist. An overlay will appear in the upper left corner of the player.
  5. If desired, you can also toggle on Autoplay next video to automatically play the next archived stream in the playlist, and Loop playlist to restart the playlist once a viewer reaches the end.
  6. When you are done configuring your settings, select Save in the upper right corner of the page.
  7. Viewers can use the arrow buttons in the overlay to navigate between videos from your event. This applies to both your event embed and the player on your event page on vimeo.com.

Alternatively, you could share or embed the individual videos that are automatically saved in your library when an event ends. This works just like sharing any video from your Vimeo account.

⚠️Note: It is not possible to add/remove previous streams from the post-event playlist.

How do I directly reply to questions in my event’s live Q&A session?

This feature is available on Advanced, Premium, and Enterprise accounts with the Events feature added.

Owners, Admins, and Contributor roles on your Vimeo account can reply in line to Q&A questions submitted through the Q&A engagement tool in events. Audience members can view the replies to their questions and other attendees’ questions. This allows you to enhance the Q&A experience, and event engagement, and help viewers and broadcasters better understand the questions and topics of importance.

Direct replying is supported on all event types with Q&A, including venues, as well as with moderated Q&A sessions.

  • Replying to questions
  • Deleting responses
  • Viewing responses
  • Additional information

Replying to questions

You can reply to questions posed in the Q&A tool directly via text. To do so:

  1. Select the question or the reply icon, found above the question on the right side of the Q&A panel.
  2. Type your response into the reply field, then click the arrow button to post your reply.
  • ⚠️Note: For events with moderated Q&A, you can reply to approved questions as well as questions that are still pending approval. Replying to a pending question will also approve the question, making it visible to the audience.
  1. The reply will be displayed for all audience members beneath the question.

Deleting responses

Currently, replies cannot be edited, but as an event organizer, you can make any changes by deleting the original reply and replying again. To delete your reply:

  1. Hover over your answer.
  2. Select the Delete icon in the upper right corner of your reply.

Viewing responses

Audience members can view organizers’ replies to questions directly within the Q&A panel. Replies are located below each question for easy access and understanding.

Additional information

  • Both organizers and viewers can sort questions to easily find the newest, oldest, or most popular questions. Replies will also be visible when questions are sorted.
  • At the end of a session, event organizers can easily export Q&A history for the session for record-keeping and analysis. The Q&A export includes both questions and answers.

How Do I Know if My GPU Supports NVENC and NVDEC?

In order to be able to use the hardware encoding and hardware decoding features in Livestream Studio, you must have the proper hardware installed on your computer. One of these options is via NVENC (encoding) and NVDEC (decoding), which process the video via a supported NVIDIA GeForce graphics card.

The first sign of knowing whether your PC supports these features is to go into Studio and check Settings: StreamingforHardware Encoding, then check Settings: AdvancedforHardware Decoding. If these options do not appear in these menus, then, unfortunately, you do not have the supported hardware.

We have successfully tested the following NVIDIA GeForce models:

  • GTX1050
  • GTX950
  • GT730 (GK208-400-A1 - other versions of this model have been reported to not work)
  • GTX650

To find out if a specific model supports these features, visit the NVIDIA GPU Support Matrix. The first table on this page represents cards that support hardware encoding (NVENC); the second table (below) is for cards that support hardware decoding (NVDEC). Below each of these tables are three green buttons which are different NVIDIA product lines; clicking all of these will expand and complete each respective list.

Search for the the model name of the GPU on your system (e.g. GTX 1050). The quickest way to do this is to hold CTRL+F (Windows) or CMD+F (Mac) and type the model name into the page search. The browser will jump to the first matching result.

If your model name is on the first set of tables and lists “YES” under the H.264 (AVCHD) YUV 4:2:0column, then your GPU supports hardware encoding in Livestream Studio.

If it appears in the second set of tables and lists “YES” under the H.264 (AVCHD) column, then it supports hardware decoding.

If your NVIDIA card falls outside of these parameters, then NVENC and/or NVDEC may not be supported on that card

How Do I Know if My Intel Processor Includes Quick Sync?

In order to be able to use the hardware encoding feature in Livestream Studio, you must have the proper hardware installed on your computer. One of these options is having a processor that include Intel Quick Sync. (The other is NVENC via NVIDIA GeForce GPUs.)

Intel Quick Sync is Intel’s version of dedicated video encoding and decoding hardware core. Rather than using a general GPU, this core is located on the processor die and is dedicated just for video processing.

Studio will automatically detect if you have the proper hardware or not. You can quickly check this by going to the Settings: Streaming menu. If Hardware Encoding does not appear at the top of the menu, then you do not have the GPU hardware.

To determine if your processor includes Quick Sync, first you need to determine your CPU model.

  • Windows 7: Open the Start menu, right-click Computer, then click Properties.
  • Windows 8 & 10: Right-click the Start menu, then click System.

If you are running Studio on a Mac, to find the exact CPU model you will need to open the Terminal application. Enter the following command, then press the Return key:

<p>sysctl -nmachdep.cpu.brand_string</p>

Click to copy

Your CPU model will be displayed underneath.

In a web browser, navigate to this list and find your CPU model (Tip: Use the CTRL+F/CMD+F search function in your browser and type in the model ID).

If you do not see the CPU model that you are searching for on this Intel product specification page, scroll down to click on Show more.

If your CPU does not appear in the list, then you do not have Intel Quick Sync available with your computer’s processor.

How To Access Livestream Studio

Full access to three (3) licenses of Livestream Studio is available with a Vimeo Enterprise account. Advanced and Premium users have access to one (1) license.

Download Livestream Studio on your computer.

  • Download onto Windows
  • Download onto Mac

Follow the on-screen steps to install the software, after which it will automatically launch.

Studio will prompt you to log into either a Livestream or Vimeo account. As of January 30, Livestream is no longer supported. If you do not have a Vimeo account, you can sign up by selecting Vimeo at the bottom of the prompt.

Once your account is created and subscribed to Vimeo, you may then log into Studio using your account credentials. Studio will indicate that your full access has been unlocked.

A few things to note:

  • Because Studio needs to authenticate your login, you will need an internet connection to access the software. If you lose your internet connection, you can continue to use Studio in offline mode for up to 7 days before being required to reconnect your account.
  • If you exceed your Studio license limit (i.e. try to run more Studio instances simultaneously than your subscription allows), you will get a warning message every five minutes within Studio to close other instances. Not following your Studio license limit may lead to account suspension.
  • While Livestream Studio has the ability to stream to various providers, a paid Livestream account does not allow you to stream to Vimeo, and a Vimeo account does not include the ability to stream to Livestream.

If you have a legacy USB Dongle and want to use your subscription to access Studio instead, close Studio, then disconnect your dongle. After disconnecting the dongle, re-launch Studio and you will see the prompt to log in.

How to access Livestream Studio after migrating to Vimeo

This feature requires an Advanced, Premium, or Enterprise account with the Events feature enabled.

If you previously used a Livestream account to access Livestream Studio and have since migrated your account to Vimeo, you will need to log out of Studio and log back in using your Vimeo account credentials to continue accessing Studio.

How to log out of Livestream and connect Studio to Vimeo

  1. In the Studio application, select the gearwheel icon in the upper right corner to open the Settings menu.
  2. Select My accounttowards the bottom of the left sidebar.
  3. You should see that you are logged into your Livestream account. Select Log out.
  4. You will then see a login window. Select Log in with Vimeo.
  5. A browser window will open. Log into Vimeo if necessary.
  6. You will see a prompt to connect Studio to your Vimeo account. Select Allow. Once connected, you will be redirected back to the Studio application.
  7. If you are a team member on multiple Vimeo accounts, you may be prompted to select which account to log in to; choose the desired account, then select Next.
  8. You will see a prompt indicating your license has been unlocked. Select Use Studio to proceed with using Studio.

I am being prompted to Activate a Livestream Account in Livestream Studio

If you launch Livestream Studio and see a prompt to “Activate a Livestream Account” after migrating to Vimeo, select the person icon next to the Livestream logo to log out of Livestream. You will then see the option to log in to Vimeo.

Additional troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with logging in or accessing your Studio license, you may need to update your Studio version. Close and relaunch Studio, ensuring you have an internet connection, and run any updates if you are prompted.

How to access viewer-level analytics in showcases

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

User-level analytics are available via a CSV download in your showcases. Analytics results will only appear for logged-in team members (not for signed-out viewers). This is a useful feature for when you’re broadcasting internal meetings and want to gain an understanding of team-wide participation.

Follow these steps to access your showcase analytics:

  1. First, navigate to your showcase from your library.
  2. Select Analytics from the top-right corner of the page.
  3. Choose a date range from the dropdown menu. The default rate is the past 30 days.
  4. Select Download CSV to download the CSV with analytics data for your chosen date range.

Here are the columns with data that surface in this report and their definitions:

  • Play ending point: Play ending point is recorded in seconds, noting when the user stopped watching.
  • Video duration: Total video duration in seconds.
  • Number of plays: A play is recorded whenever someone clicks the play button on the video player. Multiple views will be counted if the browser page is refreshed in between views.
  • Play starting point: Play starting point is also seconds, so most of these users start at 0 seconds but you can also see if a user started at the 30-second mark on the video.
  • User: The team member’s email address.
  • Time last viewed: Date and time the team member last viewed the video.
  • Loads: Recorded when the viewer navigates to the video page so the player has loaded and the viewer hasn’t pressed play yet.
  • Finishes: The number of times the user played the video to the end. The video must play the very last frame and stop (or repeat) in order for a finish to be counted.
  • Video: The video title is associated with the report.
  • Database Key: An internal identity that represents User ID|Video ID.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:Analytics are also available for both the Organization and its Workspaces. Organization Admins can view combined analytics for all Workspaces.

How to activate Bonjour Service for remote camera sources

In order to use remote cameras in Livestream Studio, you must make sure you have Bonjour service installed and activated on your Windows computer. Remote cameras will not work without Bonjour running.

Bonjour is pre-installed on Studio hardware units (e.g. HD31, HD51, HD550, etc.) and is always running on Mac systems. Customers using a Studio license on their own Windows PC may have gotten a prompt.

If you need to install Bonjour manually:

  1. Go to Apple’s support site and click Download.
  2. Once the software has finished downloading, open the installation wizard.
  3. Follow the on-screen prompts to complete the installation.

To ensure Bonjour is running, first make sure Studio is closed. Then open the start menu and type Services. Click the Services icon that appears at the top of the menu.

Screenshot: Windows start menu with Services desktop app highlighted

Find Bonjour Service in the menu. Right-click on it and select Restart.

Screenshot: bonjour service menu opened with restart highlighted

Close out the menu and relaunch Studio. Remote cameras on your network should now be detected by Studio.

How to activate, deactivate, and moderate live chat from the web studio

This article discusses how to activate, deactivate, and moderate live chat from the web-based production studio for live events.

The live chat feature on your event page or site allows viewers to interact and discuss your virtual event. You can moderate these interactions by deleting comments or blocking users. Chat moderation is only accessible through a desktop browser and is not supported on the mobile app.

  • About chat for live events
  • Activating and deactivating chat
  • Moderating chat
  • Exporting your chat transcript

About chat for live events

During your event, the browser will display only the 100 most recent messages to you and your viewers to prevent playback buffering and system slowdown.

Chat is active for your event as soon as you activate it. Viewers can start chatting, even if you haven’t gone live yet. The chat will remain active until you finish your stream (unless you deactivate it prior).

Viewers can share the following:

  • Emojis and messages are limited to 240 characters in length.
  • Links pasted in chat will appear as clickable hyperlinks.
  • Chat participants can delete their messages (but not those of others).

While one event can accommodate an unlimited number of viewers, chat, polls, and Q&A are limited to80,000 participants. If the number of participants reaches 80,000, new viewers will be unable to access these features. However, existing participants will retain their access.

Activating and Deactivating chat

Audience chat is off by default. However, you can turn chat capabilities on or off through the web studio.

To turn chat for live events on and off:

  1. Select the chat button from the web studio interface at the top right of the screen.
  2. Select the overflow menu (⋮) at the top-right of the chat module.
  3. Select the toggle next to Audience chatto turn the chat feature on or off.

After it’s activated, your chat will be available on the Vimeo event page, and the engagement tools will be embedded.

Moderating chat

During your event, you can delete individual comments or ban a user entirely via the Chat tab, the web-based production tool, or your stream’s Vimeo public page.

To delete a comment or block a user:

  1. From the chat window in the web studio, hover your cursor over their message.
  2. You can delete a comment by selecting the trash can icon. However, you cannot recover a deleted comment.
  3. Select the block icon, which is shaped like a circle with a line through it, to block a user. Select it again to unblock the user.

Blocking a user hides their comments from everyone except themselves. They can still comment, but others in the chat won’t see them.

⚠️Note:Blocks are event-specific. If the user returns to a future event, you must re-block them.

Exporting your chat transcript:

The chat feature will deactivate once your event concludes. Following the event, you can download a transcript of the event’s chat as a .txt file. The system will store this transcript for 30 days.

To export your chat’s transcript:

  1. Select the chat icon from the top-right of the page.
  2. Select the overflow menu ( ⋮ ).
  3. Select Download.
  4. Select either the ‘Current’ session for the event you just streamed or select your event’s date for a previous stream.

How to add a custom thumbnail for a live event

When you create a live event, it will provide a default image (color bars) to use as a thumbnail image.

However, you can change the thumbnail for your live event on the Customize player page.

To change the thumbnail image for your video:

  1. Select the gear icon on the top right of the page to open Settings.
  2. Select Destinations, and then next to the Vimeo logo, select Customize. Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-02-11 at 11.55.09 AM.png
  3. A new page will open. Scroll down to the Customization section to find the Thumbnailoption.
  4. Hover on the image next to Thumbnail and select the pencil icon that appears.
  5. Select “Upload” to select the desired image as your thumbnail.

How to add attendees to your live event or webinar via CSV file, CRM, or MAP

This article explains the process for adding registrants to your live event by uploading a CSV file or importing a list from your CRM or MAP. Both methods can be used to manually add attendees once you’ve turned on Registration for your event.

  • How to upload a CSV file of attendees
  • How to import attendees from your CRM or MAP
  • Analytics for attendees

How to upload a CSV file of attendees

You can upload a CSV of registrants for your webinar by following these steps:

  1. After creating your live event or webinar, you can turn on registration any point before it ends:
  • Navigate to the Settings gear from the top-right of the event settings page.
  • Then, select Registration from the righthand panel andTurn on registration.
  1. SelectManage registrants.
  2. Select Upload CSV in the top right corner.
  3. Next, select the file you want to upload. ⚠️Note: We only support CSVs with up to 1000 rows. If your CSV is larger you will need to break it up into multiple files and upload them separately.
  4. Check the box at the bottom of the screen to confirm that all contacts listed have registered for your event or are expecting to receive related communications, then select Next.
  5. On the next screen, match the columns in your CSV to the columns in the Vimeo attendee table by clicking on the dropdowns under the CSV column header and selecting the corresponding column. When you are done, select Submit.

Please note the following about your CSV upload:

  • Emails that are uploaded will not be cleansed or checked for spam so users should ensure that things email domains like X@test.com are stripped before uploading as Vimeo will not sanitize these.
  • Registration does not support non-English characters at the moment. Please strip all non-English characters like ñ or ø before uploading.
  • Attendees that you register via CSV will not receive a registration confirmation email. However, they will receive reminder and follow-up emails.

How to import attendees from your CRM or MAP

You may import contacts from your CRM or MAP list to register them as attendees of your webinar. Vimeo will receive your registrant information and send back viewer-level analytics to the CRM or marketing platform.

  1. After creating your live event or webinar, you can turn on registration any point before it ends:
  • Navigate to the Settings gear from the top-right of the event settings page.
  • Then, select Registration from the righthand panel andTurn on registration.
  1. SelectManage registrants.
  2. On the upper righthand corner of the next page, select Sync from email list. You will be prompted to connect to your provider if you have not already done so.
  3. Once you have connected and selected your CRM or MAP, you can choose your list in the dropdown menu.
  4. Select Next to continue and then Done once it has finished uploading.
  5. Your list will populate on the Attendees page. ⚠️Note: Duplicate information in your list will override the Vimeo attendee table (i.e. if any of your attendees have already registered).
  6. To remove an uploaded list, hover over it and select the options menu (⋯) and choose Disconnect list. ⚠️Note: Attendees that you register via the list will not receive a registration confirmation email. However, they will receive reminder and follow-up emails.

Analytics for attendees

Viewer-level analytics are automatically pushed to the CRM once the event is complete. For Marketo, Custom Fields will be created for Viewer Level Analytics passed from Vimeo. Those custom fields include:

  • Watch Time Percentage
  • Vimeo Events - QnA
  • Vimeo Events - Polls
  • The attendee status if they attended will also change to Attended Live

How to add full screen graphics to events

Full-screen graphics are images that cover the entire screen while you are live. This is useful for displaying information before any action taking place, or during any breaks in your event.

⚠️ Note: Graphics overlays on the Vimeo platform are only supported if you select Stream through your browser. If you are using an external encoder, see How to add graphics to events while using an external encoder. If you are using Livestream Studio, see the Livestream Help Center to learn about its graphics overlay functionality.

Full-screen graphics when streaming with Vimeo

When you create a recurring event or webinar and select Stream with Vimeofrom the setup page, you will be brought to our web-based production tool where you can add all the production elements for your event from your browser.

On the left side of the broadcast page, select the graphics icon. Select Add image.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2025-03-19 at 10.58.48 AM.png

This will open your File Explorer or Finder window and allow you to upload your image.

  • We recommend PNG or JPGs at a maximum of 1920x1080 and 5MB in size.
  • If your image has a transparent background, that will apply when uploading it to your Vimeo event. If you truly want to fill the screen, make sure the background is filled.
  • Images that are not 16:9 in aspect ratio will be cropped or zoomed to fit the window.

Once your image is added, you can add optional primary and secondary text (e.g. “The event will begin soon.”) When finished, select Save.

To use this image as a full-screen graphic, you need to add it to a scene by itself. To do this:

  1. Below the preview player, select Add to scene.
  2. Select it again to select that blank scene.
  3. In the Images panel, select the ••• menu on the desired image, then Add to scene.Screenshot: image_add_to_scene.png
  4. Alternatively, you can drag and drop the image into the preview player to add the image to the scene.

⚠️Note: If you add any other production elements to the scene (e.g. speakers’ cameras), they will overlay on top of your image. To use an image as a standalone full-screen graphic, it should be in a scene by itself.

To show the full-screen graphics in the player:

  1. Below the preview player, select the scene with the graphic.
  2. Select Send to stream. Screenshot: image_scene_send_to_stream.png
  3. The image will appear in the player alone with no other audio.

You can add as many images as you wish, but only one image can be added to a scene at a time.

To remove an image from a scene, hover over it in the Images panel, select ••• then select Remove from the scene.

If you no longer need the image for your event, select Remove from the event.

Additional notes:

  • Graphics for recurring virtual events will be retained on those events. However, new events will need new graphics created each time.
  • Additionally, while your graphic will save to your recurring event, your graphic will not display automatically each time you stream. Select the corresponding eye icon in the panel to display your graphic overlays.

How to add graphics to events while using an external encoder

If you are streaming your event via an external encoder (such as Livestream Studio, OBS, or Teradek devices) and wish to add graphics overlays to your stream, you will need to do so using the graphics features built into most software encoders. The graphics in external software encoders are generally more flexible and have more advanced options than the graphics features previously provided for RTMP streams on the Vimeo platform.

If you are streaming using Livestream Studio, refer to Livestream Studio: Graphic Overlaysor watch the video below.

If you are using different software (OBS, Wirecast, etc.), consult with its developer on how to add graphics overlays into your stream. Any graphics included in your stream’s output will appear as part of your stream on Vimeo.

If you are using a hardware encoder to stream your event, you can use a software encoder to receive a signal and send it over to the Vimeo platform. If you would like to use Studio Desktop for that purpose, refer to Setting Up Studio as an RTMP Server for the setup process.

You can also stream via Vimeo’s web-based production tool and use the graphics options in there. Read how at How to navigate the web-based production tool.

How to add logo graphic overlays to events

A logo is a small icon that appears in the lower right corner of the player and is a subtle way to keep your brand visible at all times during your event.

The image you upload to use as your logo should be a square at 200x200 pixels and no more than 5MB in size.

⚠️ Note: Graphics overlays on the Vimeo platform are only supported if you select Stream through your browser. If you are using an external encoder, see How to add graphics to events while using an external encoder. If you are using Livestream Studio, see the Livestream Help Center to learn about its graphics overlay functionality.

Logo graphic overlays when streaming with Vimeo

When you create a live broadcast or webinar and select Stream with your browserfrom the setup page, you will be brought to our web-based production tool page where you can add all the production elements for your event from your browser.

To add a logo to your stream from the web-based production tool page:

  1. Click the Brand icon on the left side of the page.
  2. At the top of the panel will be a Logo section. If your team’s logo is not already on your account, click Upload to upload your logo. You can upload multiple logos, but only one can be selected for your event.
  3. You can click the logo you’d like to use to select it.
  4. By default, the toggle next to the Show logo on all scenes will be turned on. This will display your logo in the bottom right corner of the player regardless of which scene is active.

Unlike other production elements, the logo does not get added to individual scenes. If you do not want it displayed during your stream at any point, disable the Show logo on all scenes toggle switch in the Brand panel. You can re-enable it at any point during your event to show your logo.

⚠️Note: Please consider the below points while uploading a custom team logo:

  • If available, please prefer brandmarks over wordmarks.
  • If available, please use logo files with transparent backgrounds.
  • The recommended aspect ratio for the logo is 1:3 >> square >> 3:1.

How to add lower-third graphics to live events

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can add lower-third graphics to your virtual broadcast in the web-based production tool. This article explains how to create, customize, and display these graphics using the web-based production tool.

  • What to know before adding lower third graphics
  • How to create a lower-third graphic
  • How to customize your lower-third graphics to match your brand
  • How to add a lower-third graphic to a scene
  • How to manage lower-third graphics for scenes
  • How to display lower-third graphics during the live event
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before adding lower third graphics

Before adding lower-third graphics to your event, take note of the following:

  • Supported production mode: Lower-third graphics are supported when using the in-browser production studio when selecting the Stream through your browserproduction mode. Screenshot: The Production mode menu expanded from the Go live button, displaying options for Stream from your browser, Prerecorded event, Recording only, and Use an external encoder. The ‘Stream from your browser’ option is selected and highlighted with a red box.
  • If you are using an external encoder, refer to How to add graphics to events while using an external encoder. If you are using Livestream Studio, refer to Livestream Studio: Graphic Overlays.
  • Automatic creation: A lower third graphic will automatically be created for the broadcaster and every guest speaker. It’ll display their names and title, but will not have images.
  • Default graphics:Polls and Q&A have default lower-third graphics, such as poll results and submitted questions.
  • Recurring live events: Graphics for recurring virtual events will be retained; however, your graphics will not display automatically each time you stream. You will still need to show/hideit during the scene.

How to create a lower-third graphic

You can create custom lower-third graphics for your scenes. To do so:

  1. From the web-based production tool, select the Graphics icon on the left navigation menu.
  2. Select + Add lower third.
  3. Enter the Primary text for your graphic, an image, and optional secondary text.
  4. Select Save. Screenshot: Left-side toolbar in the production studio with the Graphics icon highlighted in a red box. In the main ‘Lower thirds’ panel, the + Add lower third button is also highlighted in a red box

How to customize lower-third graphics to match a brand

You can adjust the colors for all your event’s lower third graphics to match your brand if you have access to the Brand Kit. To do so:

  1. Select the Brand icon on the left-side toolbar.
  2. Select the Primary color or Secondary color to open the color window.
  3. Drag and drop the color selector or insert your brand’s exact HEX color codes.
  4. Select Save to apply your brand colors. Screenshot: Left-side toolbar with the Brand icon highlighted in a red box. In the ‘Colors’ section, the color selection swatches on the right are highlighted in a red box, and the Save button at the bottom is also highlighted in a red box.

How to add a lower-third graphic to a scene

Once created, you must add graphics to a scene to display them during your live event. To do so:

  1. Select Graphics on the left-side toolbar.
  2. Select the Scenes tab.
  3. Select the+ iconnext to the graphic to add it to the scene.

How to manage lower-third graphics for scenes

After adding a graphic to a scene, you can manually edit or remove it from your live event. To do so:

  1. Select the Graphics button from the left-side toolbar.
  2. Select the Scene tab within the Graphics panel.
  3. Select the vertical ellipsis button to open the overflow menu. Here, you can edit the lower-third’s appearance or remove it from the live event entirely. Screenshot: Lower thirds list item with the options menu expanded. The three-dot menu icon and the dropdown list containing Edit and Remove from event are highlighted in a red box.

How to manage lower-third graphics for speakers

The other tab in the graphics menu is for Speakers. These lower-third graphics are automatically created for the broadcaster and any guest speaker added to your event. To edit these:

  1. Hover your cursor over the lower third.
  2. Select the pencil icon. Screenshot: Lower thirds configuration panel with the Speakers tab selected and highlighted. The edit icon (pencil) next to ‘Speaker #1’ is highlighted in a red box, and the corresponding Speaker form on the right, showing Name and Title fields, is also highlighted.
  3. Edit the speaker’s name and title. These lower thirds do not include image fields.
  4. Your changes will save automatically.

How to display lower-third graphics during the live event

After creating and editing the appearance of your lower-third graphic, you will need to display it during the scene to your audience. To display them:

  1. When a scene is in the stream output, hover over the output preview in the center of the web-based production studio.
  2. Select Showto show the lower-third graphic.
  3. To hide the lower-third graphic, hover over the stage once more and select Hide.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn how to add guests to your live event.

How to add Remote Guests in Livestream Studio

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can add a live webcam or desktop source from another location into yourLivestream Studio project using the Remote Guests feature. This article discusses how to invite guests, manage their settings, and add them to your stream.

  • Video overview
  • What to know before inviting Remote Guests
  • How to invite and show Remote Guests in Studio
  • Making the most out of the Remote Guests feature
  • Suggested next steps

Video overview

Watch the video below to see an overview of the Remote Guest feature.

What to know before inviting Remote Guests

Before adding guests to your production, take note of the following:

  • Vimeo Enterprise accounts can invite up to 10 guests. Users on Advanced and Premium plans can invite up to 5 guests.
  • Remote Guests do not need a Vimeo account to join your stream.
  • Browser requirements: Remote Guests can only join your stream via Google Chrome.
  • View our hardware and network recommendations for remote guests.

How to invite and show Remote Guests in Livestream Studio

To generate a link to send to your Remote Guests and add them to your production:

  1. After opening Livestream Studio, navigate to the Guests tab.
  2. Select Add Input > Remote Guests > Add remote guests.
  3. Select the Settings sub-tab in the Guest tab.
  4. Copy the displayed Guest link and send it to your guests (via email, messaging app, etc.).
  • This guest link will stay the same for the project in Livestream Studio, unless you select Reset guest link.
  1. When the Remote guest joins, a thumbnail with their camera feed will be added to the Guests tab.
  2. Select + Add As Inputon the individual guest to add them as a standalone input for your event.
  • Alternatively, select + Add As GFX to create a gallery-view graphics overlay that includes all guests and the first Studio input.

When a guest is switched into the event, they will see a red “On Air” indicator in their browser.

Making the most out of the Remote Guests feature

The Guests panel provides additional tools for automating and communicating between hosts and guests.

  • Guest Settings:Select the Settings tab to access automation tools.
  • Autopush: Automatically updates the gallery graphic in a selected GFX channel to reflect the current number of guest inputs.
  • Auto switch: Automatically switches to the guest who is currently speaking in the Program Output. To manually configure switching thresholds (e.g., check interval, Switch delay, Activation margin), select Manual adjustment.
  • Chat: Select the Chat tab on the left side of the Guests panel to access the event chat.
  • Removing guests: To disconnect a guest, hover over their image in the Guests tab and select the trash can icon. The guest will receive a notification that the host ended their session.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn how Remote Guests can join a live event. How to join a live event as a Remote Guest.
  • If your guest is having trouble connecting, refer to Troubleshooting: Remote Guest’s camera and microphone not appearing.

How to apply content ratings to my live events

This feature is included with all Vimeo plans.

You can apply content ratings to your live events to ensure viewers are aware of the content and to prevent access issues in certain regions. This article explains how to add a content rating to a new or existing live event.

  • What to know before you apply a content rating to your live event
  • How to apply a content rating to a live event

What to know before you apply a content rating to your live event

Before rating your live event, please be aware of the following:

  • Content ratings: We ask that you apply content ratings to your videosand live events and disclose whether they contain an advertisement. Learn about Content Ratings at About content ratings.
  • All Audiences v. Mature Audiences: If your live event contains violence, profanity, nudity, or drug/alcohol use, your live event should be rated for Mature Audiences.
  • Access in Certain Regions: If your event is unrated, viewers in certain countries (such as the UK and EU) will be required to log intoa Vimeo account to watch, even if the event is set to Public.
  • Finality: Once you select a rating for a live event, you cannot change it back to “Not yet rated.”

How to apply a content rating to a live event

You can add a content rating from the event page. To do so:

  1. Navigate to your live event’s settings page by either creating a new event or opening an existing one from the Live Events folder in your Library.
  2. On the page for the Live Event, select the Settings gear icon at the top-right of the page to open the Settings menu.
  3. In the Settings menu, on the right side of the page, expand the Privacyheader.
  4. Scroll down toSelect content rating.
  5. Select the dropdown menu and select either All audiences or Mature.
  6. If you select Mature, additional checkboxes for specific warnings will appear; be sure to check all that apply.
  7. If your event contains sponsored content, check the box next to This video contains an advertisement.
  8. Your changes are saved automatically.

How to change the settings for my live event

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article explains how to select and update settings for your live event within the web-based production tool. Each section below highlights which settings can be changed from the settings menu.

  • Opening the settings menu
  • Basics
  • Privacy
  • Schedule
  • Production
  • Registration
  • Destination

Opening the settings menu

The settings menu is located in the top-right corner of the web-based studio and is represented by a gear. This will expand the settings panel on the right of your screen.

Basics

You can change the following in the basic settings pane:

  • Title of your event
  • Description:The description of the live event. The description will appear on your event page on Vimeo.

Privacy

You can change the following settings in the Privacy pane:

  • Link privacy: Change the privacy setting of your link. Read about the different types of privacy settings at About privacy settings for live events
  • Embed privacy:Change the embed privacysetting for your event and select where your event can be embedded online.
  • Content rating: Content ratings are required. They help keep Vimeo safe and ensure your intended audience can view your video. Read more at Content ratings.
  • Additionally, indicate whether the stream or videos within the stream contain advertisements.

Schedule

  • Select the start and end dates and times for your event.
  • Select the time zone in which your event is being held. Viewers will see their corresponding local times based on their locations.
  • Select whether your event is recurring and specify the recurring dates.

Production

  • Choose the latency for your event.
  • Toggle the Automatic closed captions on or off.
  • Add keywords in advance to assist in automatic speech detection (e.g., products, names, and terms that will be mentioned during your event).
  • Toggle recording on or off.
  • Recorded events are stored in your Library for you to view on demand later.
  • If recording is disabled for a recurring event, none of your future streams will be archived.
  • Toggle DVR on or off.
  • Viewers can watch in real time or pause and rewind to catch up during the live event.
  • Toggle Extended stream on or off.
  • Read more about extended streaming at How to enable extended streaming

Registration

  • Turn registration on or off for your event.
  • Customize the registration form or apply a preset registration form.

Destination

  • Customize the live event player
  • Choose simulcasting destinations for your event

How to change your stream’s production mode

This article discusses the different production modes available when streaming on Vimeo and how to change your mode in the browser-based production studio.

  • How do I change my stream’s production mode?
  • What are the different production modes available for selection?

How do I change my stream’s production mode?

You can change your stream’s production mode in the browser-based production studio.

To change your stream’s production mode:

  1. Access the browser-based production studio by creating a new event or selecting an existing one.
  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to the Go Live button in the top-right corner of the studio.
  3. Select which production mode you’d like - the studio will update accordingly.

What are the different production modes available for selection?

The different production modes in the browser-based production studio are:

  • Stream from your browser
  • Host and manage your live event directly from the browser-based production studio.
  • Prerecorded event
  • Stream a pre-recorded video or event with your audience.
  • Recording only
  • Record a video without an audience
  • Use an external encoder
  • Use an external encoder to stream your live event with RTMP/RTMPS or SRT.

How to configure DVR for my live events

This feature requires a Premium or Advanced plan, or an Enterprise account with the Event features enabled.

The DVR (Digital Video Recording) feature allows your viewers to rewatch, catch up on missed content, or pause the live stream to resume watching it later while it is streaming.

For live broadcasts, the organizers can enable or disable DVR alongside the rest of the event settings.

To enable or disable DVR:

  1. Create a live broadcast or webinar, or select an event you’ve already created from your library.
  2. On the event settings page, select the Settings gear in the upper righthand corner, then Production.
  3. Toward the bottom of the panel, toggle DVRon or off. Note that by default, DVR will be toggled on.

Additional information:

  • With DVR enabled, viewers can rewind up to the most recent four hours of your stream while it’s live. Rest assured that events longer than four hours will be fully archived and available for playback in their entirety after the event ends.
  • For Enterprise clients with eCDN enabled for their team/organization, enabling DVR on live events will decrease the efficiency of peering with these solutions.

How to configure the registration form for your live event or webinar

You can customize your event’s registration form and link your email marketing provider to help stay in touch with your webinar’s attendees. Your live event’s registration settings will be saved even after the event is completed. Viewers will see the same registration form once the event ends, however, registrants from the live event will not be carried over to the saved recording unless you sync both to the same CRM list.

To configure the registration form:

  1. While setting up your live event, toggle on Registration under Optional features. If you missed this step, you can still turn on registration for your event at any point before it ends:
  • Navigate to the Settings gear from the top-right of the event settings page.
  • Then, select Registration from the righthand panel andTurn on registration.
  1. From the Registration panel, select Customize.
  2. Here, you can configure which fields you would like to display on the registration form including name, email address, and custom text, dropdown, or checkbox fields.
  • You can add up to 20 custom fields each up to 240 characters in length, and your registrants can include answers up to 50 characters in length per text field.
  • For checkboxes,you can use the link button to add a URL to the field.
  1. Drag and drop the dot icon to the right of each field to re-arrange the order in which they appear.
  2. Select the options menu to the right to open the dropdown menu to find additional settings for each field. Here, you can make a field required or delete it from your form.
  3. Below the custom fields, you can provide a link to your organization’s privacy policy that will be accessible to viewers directly from the preview player, below the contact form.
  4. Select the Appearance tab on the right to change the layout, add your logo, or add background image or color.
  5. Use thePreview dropdown menu option to view your form, confirmation, and sign-on screen from your viewers’ perspective.
  6. Once you are happy with your form, select theback button in the top left corner to return to your event settings page. Your changes will be saved automatically.

Additional information

  • Premium and Enterprise accounts can integrate with Mailchimp, HubSpot, Constant Contact, Campaign Monitor, and Keap. Additionally, Enterprise users can integrate with Marketo.
  • If you use Mailchimp, Hubspot, Marketo, or Salesforce Sales Cloud we will also pass your registrant’s engagement metrics over to that CRM provider once you complete your event.
  • When completing the registration form, your viewers will also need to opt into Vimeo’s privacy policy.

How to create a backup stream

This feature requires an Enterprise account with the Events feature added.

With an Enterprise membership, you can produce two streams simultaneously to the same event, with one being your backup in case of a failure with your primary streams, such as a system crash or power failure.

  • What you need
  • Create an event
  • How to configure RTMP/RTMPS/SRT (primary and backup)
  • How to configure Livestream Studio (primary and backup)
  • Start streaming
  • Ending the stream

What you need

To use this feature, you must set up two separate encoders with video and audio inputs and network connections. You can use any two third-party encoders or stream directly to your Vimeo account using two licenses of Livestream Studio. You can also do both; for example, you can use Studio as your primary and an encoder as your backup, or vice versa.

You must determine which encoder will be your primary encoder and which will be your backup. How you configure the streaming settings for the backup encoder will vary slightly from the primary encoder.

Note that this feature does not require matching both encoders’ streaming resolutions, bitrates, frame rates, etc. (although you may want to consider matching as much as possible for the best viewing experience).

Create an event

  1. Start by creating an event on Vimeo. Select the Newdropdown in your library, and then select Host event.
  2. Choose Live broadcast or webinar.
  3. Choose a setup method. Regardless of which method you choose, select Stream with an external encoder as your broadcast method.
  4. Proceed with configuring the rest of your event settings as desired to finish creating your event.

How to configure RTMP/RTMPS/SRT

  1. Find the URL and Stream key in the Stream panel.
  2. Input this into any encoder as you normally would into your primary encoder. ⚠️Note: If your encoder does not support RTMPS, click Copy URL below the RTMPS field to get the standard RTMP URL.
  3. For your backup encoder, copy and paste the same URL(s), but instead of the standard Stream Key, copy and paste the Backup stream key into the Stream Key field in your backup encoder.

How to configure Livestream Studio

  1. First, make sure you are running Studio version 6.3.0. Earlier versions do not include this feature.
  2. In the Stream tab, select Vimeo as your provider.
  3. Choose your event from the drop-down menu. If Studio is a primary encoder, you will go live as normal. If you are using Studio as a backup encoder, you must ensure your primary stream is live first.
  4. Click Advanced Settings(below the Share With dropdown menu) and select the Backup streamcheckbox. ⚠️Note:This checkbox will remain greyed out until a primary stream is running to your event.

Start streaming

  1. Whether streaming via an encoder or Livestream Studio, go live from the primary encoder first.
  2. Once the primary encoder connects, you can start the stream from your backup encoder.
  3. You can then check the stream health monitor to confirm that Vimeo receives both streams.
  4. If your primary stream disconnects, the backup stream will automatically take over. The stream health monitor will indicate this.
  5. If you can bring back your primary stream, make sure the primary encoder is live (using the same URL and Stream Key as before) and then stop the stream from the backup encoder to switch back to the primary stream; the player will not automatically switch back. Once that’s done, you can reopen the backup encoder to have it ready.

Ending the stream

When you utilize primary and backup streams and are ready to end your stream entirely, click the red End event button from the Live Preview page. This will end the live video on Vimeo and start the archiving process.

Screenshot: to_stop_stream_end_event.png

How to create a live event

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article discusses how to create a live event on Vimeo. You can stream live events on Vimeo, whether using our in-browser production studio or a third-party encoder.

  • What to know before creating a live event
  • How to create a live event
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before creating a live event

Before creating a live event, take note of the following:

  • You can stream a live event in up to 1080p HD resolution.
  • 4K streaming is available as an add-on for Enterprise customers. Read more at About 4K Streaming.
  • Live events created by Contributor Plus team members are stored in the user’s Private folder and must be moved to a shared team folder to go live.
  • Additionally, Contributor Plus members can only activate or deactivate the logos and backgrounds in a live event
  • Read our recommended network configuration for live events
  • Visit Streaming Best Practices for additional recommendations about streaming live events on Vimeo.

How to create a live event

To create an event from the Vimeo home page:

  1. From the Vimeo homepage, start a new project in one of two ways:
  • Select + Createin the top navigation bar, then select Eventfrom the dropdown menu.
  • Select Host event or webinar from the menu located in the center of the Vimeo home page.
  1. If prompted, select Live Stream.
  2. Choose a setup option that best suits the needs of your event:
  • Set up from scratch: Start a new event from a blank canvas and manually configure all settings.
  • Choose event type: Choose from recommended settings that match different events, such as a Live Broadcast or Team Event.
  • Reuse Settings: Copy the settings you used in a previously created event.
  1. Follow the setup flow to configure the settings for your event.
  2. Select Create to create your new event. The new event will be stored in the Live Events folder of your library.

After creating a live event, you will enter the web-based production studio to manage and run your broadcast.

Suggested next steps

  • Learn howto navigate the web-based production tool.
  • You can also stream via an external encoder.
  • You can alsogo live from your mobile device using the Vimeo Android app or the Vimeo iOS app.

How to create a recurring live event

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

A recurring live event occurs at regular intervals, such as weekly meetings or monthly townhalls. This article discusses how to create a new recurring live event or edit a previously created live event to set a repeating schedule.

  • What to know before creating a recurring live event
  • How to create a new recurring live event
  • How to make a previously created live event a recurring event

What to know before creating a recurring live event

Before you create your recurring event, take note of the following:

  • If your event has a registration form, it will appear with each recurrence of the event.
  • Visit Troubleshooting: Unable to remove a registration form from a recurring live event for more information.
  • New live events created by Contributor Plus members are stored in their own personal folder and must be moved to a shared team folder to go live.
  • Duration is separate from recurrence end: the event duration field (the length of a single occurrence) is now independent from the recurrence end date (when the series stops repeating). The duration field is informational only — the stream will not be automatically stopped when the duration elapses, so the event owner must select End event to stop the broadcast.
  • Concurrent-stream limits: each occurrence of a recurring event is counted independently against your account’s concurrent-stream limit at its scheduled time. You can review your full schedule and any overlaps on the Live Events dashboard. If an occurrence cannot start because the limit is already in use, the event owner receives an email explaining why.

How to create a new recurring event

You can set a recurring schedule while creating a live event. To do so:

  1. From your Vimeo home page, select the Host button and choose your event type.
  2. On the Add event details step of the creation process, select the Recurring event toggle.
  3. Use the drop-down menu and checkboxes to set how often the event should recur (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly), then set the duration of each occurrence and the recurrence end date independently.
  4. Select Createto create your recurring live event.

How to make a previously created live event a recurring event

You can edit the schedule of a previously created event from your library. To do so:

  1. Select the event from your Live events folder to open the web-based production studio.
  2. Select the Settings gear icon in the top-right corner.
  3. Expand the Schedule pane and select the Recurring event toggle.
  4. Use the drop-down menus and checkboxes to set how often the event should recur (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly), and set the duration of each occurrence and the recurrence end date independently.
  5. The settings will save automatically. Screenshot: The web-based production studio settings showing the ‘Schedule’ pane with the ‘Recurring event’ toggle activated and a weekly frequency selected

How to create a webinar

This feature requires a Vimeo Advanced,Premium, or Enterprise account with the Events feature added.

You can utilize livestreaming, audience interaction, event registration, and viewer analytics tools to host webinars on Vimeo. This event type includes automated follow-up emails to your event attendees and the ability to sync your attendee information with marketing tools.

  • How to create webinar
  • Additional information

How to create webinar

  1. Go to your Library and select the New button in the upper righthand corner, then select Host event.
  2. A new modal will appear. Select Live broadcast or webinar and then Choose event type.
  3. On the next page, select Webinar.
  4. You will see some initial Webinar settingson the right side of the modal. You can choose your Broadcast method and Latency at this time.
  5. Using the corresponding toggles, you may disableRegistration, Chat, and automatic closed captions.
  6. Use the Language dropdown to set the language for your webinar.
  7. Select Next in the bottom right corner of the modal to add your event details including Title, Description, Start and End time, Time zone, and Privacy settings.
  8. Once you’ve set up your webinar, selectCreate. Note: You can also schedule this to happen automatically as described in the How to schedule and automatically start a simulated live event article.
  9. In the upper right corner of the page next to your avatar, you will see these components: analytics, settings, chat, the share link button, and the embed menu.
  10. Select thelink button to see your webinar’s URL, which you can copy to your clipboard and paste anywhere, such as marketing content and email campaigns to help promote it. You can also use it to preview what your webinar’s landing page will look like to your viewers.
  11. Select the Embed menu for options to embed the player and engagement tools. For more information, see Embed my event on my website.

Additional information

  • For more information on privacy settings for your webinar, see Change the privacy settings of your Live videos.
  • To customize the webinar player, see How to customize my live event’s player.
  • Advanced and Premium users are limited to 100 registrants and will not have access to attendee-specific analytics. If your event requires more than 100 attendees, you can turn off registration or upgrade to Enterprise.
  • If you are an Enterprise user and cannot create webinars or need more registrants than your account allows, please contact your account manager for the next steps.
  • Team account owners and admins can create webinars and link email providers; team contributors cannot create webinars but can manage and produce a webinar if it’s in a folder to which they have access.
  • Vimeo will auto-complete webinars that stop streaming for more than 6 hours after their scheduled end time. Upon auto-completion, you will get viewer-level analytics and event analytics.
  • After a live webinar has ended, the webinar is still available to watch on demand. Viewers can continue to register and watch the archived event.
  • If you are unable to create a webinar, it might be because of rate-limits. This limit has been implemented due to security concerns regarding misuse of the product. To navigate around it, please try again in a moment or edit one of the previously created but unedited webinars for your event.

How to create and manage live polls

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article discusses how to create, manage, and utilize polls during live events. You can boost viewer engagement during virtual events by opening an audience poll directly within the event. If you embed the engagement tools on your website, polls will be included.

  • Creating a poll
  • Adding a poll graphic to a scene
  • Opening a poll
  • Closing a poll
  • Export polls CSV during/after live events or Venues

Our polls feature allows you to insert questions into your livestream for viewers to respond to. Polls can be used to gather feedback from viewers (answers ranked by percentage) or as a quiz (one option being the correct response).

You can have as many polls as you’d like per stream, but only one poll may be open at a time.

Currently, you can only create and manage polls via a desktop browser; polls are not available via the Vimeo mobile app.

Creating a poll for a live event

💡Tip: You can also manage polls by navigating to the engagement tools link for your event.

Once you have set up your live event, you can find the Polls icon on the left side of the page.

Screenshot: polls live event.png

  1. Select Create poll.
  2. Type in the question and at least two options for viewers to choose from.
  • Click Add option if you need more than two answer choices. You can add up to four options per poll.
  1. (Optional) To mark one option as the correct choice (e.g., for a quiz), click the star iconassociated with that option.
  2. When you’re finished, click Save.
Character limit on a poll

The character limit for a live poll question and each of the answers is a maximum of 120 characters or 3 lines.

Adding a poll graphic to a scene

⚠️Note: This section is only relevant if you are streaming to a recurring event or a webinar via our web-based production tool page.

If you create a poll and you select Stream with Vimeo when setting up your event, you will need to add it to a scene on the web-based production tool page in order to show the poll graphics overlay.

  1. Below the preview player, select the scene you want the poll graphic to appear.
  2. SelectOpen poll in the left navigation menu.
  3. Select Show on scene.
  4. When Show on sceneis selected, the poll will appear on the selected scene as shown below:
  • Tip: You can add your poll graphic to multiple scenes, but you will need to make sure the Show on scene is selected for each scene if you want the graphic to remain in the player when you switch between them.
  • Scenes can only contain one poll each.

To remove a poll graphic from a scene:

  1. Select the scene below the player that has the poll.
  2. Open the Poll panel on the left.
  3. Open the poll that needs to be hidden.
  4. Click Hide from scene.

Opening a poll

Once you’ve created your poll, select the poll in the Polls panel and click Open poll to display the poll and allow your viewers to see it and choose a response.

The open poll will be pinned to the beginning of the live chat so it will be visible to all viewers. You can keep your poll open for as long as you’d like.

Closing a poll

Once your viewers have had enough time to submit their responses, clicking Publish results will close the poll so no more responses can be accepted. Results will be displayed in the chat window.

Once your poll has concluded and you no longer need the results, you can remove it by clicking Archive.

Keep in mind that the results will not be stored anywhere on your Vimeo account after your event so be sure to take note of them before removing them.

⚠️Note: If you’re on an Enterprise account and hosted a Webinar, you can access how each of your attendees answered any polls you conducted during your event. Read more at ‘Track your webinar’s attendee engagement and analytics’.

Export polls CSV during/after live events or Venues

To export CSV:

  1. Create and launch a poll during a live event.
  2. Open the poll for the audience to respond.
  3. Publish the poll results to the audience.
  4. Archive the poll.
  5. At the top-right of the poll menu, open the stacked dot menu and then Download.

How to customize my live event’s player

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise account with the Events feature enabled.

After you create an event, you can customize the appearance and features available on the live event player. You can change these settings at any time and the changes will reflect on the player without needing to re-embed the player on your site.

  • How to customize the live event player
  • What features can I customize in the live event player?

How to customize the live event player

To customize the live event player:

  1. First, create your event or select an event from your library.
  2. Select the settings gear at the top-right corner of the event settings page.
  3. From the menu on the right hand side, open the Destinations panel.
  4. Next to the Vimeo logo, select theCustomize button.
  5. A new page will open. Your settings will appear in the left side panel with a preview of your event’s player in the middle of the page. Configure each player setting as desired (more on which player settings you can change are discussed below).
  6. When you are done configuring player settings, click Save in the upper right corner to save your settings.

What features can I customize in the live event player?

Below are all the names and definitions of all the live player customization settings you can configure for any live event.

  • Before event: You can toggle on the following options to display in the player while your event is not live.
  • Show recurring schedule: An overlay will appear in the lower-left corner of the player showing your event’s recurring scheduled time. If you don’t schedule a start time, the message will say “This event hasn’t started yet.”
  • Show event schedule: The player will display the date and time of the next time your event is schedule to go live next in the middle of the player. If you don’t schedule a start time, the message will say “This event hasn’t started yet.”
  • Show latest video: Displays the most recent event archive video, which viewers can watch, rather than the event thumbnail or event schedule.
  • Playlist: The settings in this section are most relevant if your event is recurring.
  • Playlist: Will display a list of all videos streamed to that event in the upper right corner. Note that this cannot be display at the same time as your profile details.
  • Autoplay next video: Will automatically play the next video upon completion of the previous video in the event playlist.
  • Loop playlist: Will automatically play the first video upon completion of the last video in the playlist.
  • Play button: Settings for the play button on the live player.
  • Position: Changes where the play button is displayed. If Auto is selected, the play button will be at the bottom if you have Show latest video selected, and move to the center when the event is live.
  • Controls: These settings appear at the bottom of the player. The toggles determine whether or not viewers can access these controls on your event player.
  • Progress bar: Shows the progress bar and allows viewers to scrub back if DVR is enabled.
  • Volume: Allows viewers to adjust the player volume.
  • Picture-in-picture: Allows viewers to see the event player while browsing other tabs.
  • Full screen: Allows viewers to watch in full screen.
  • Vimeo logo: Displays the Vimeo logo
  • Customization: These settings allow you to adjust the appearance of elements on the player.
  • Primary color: The main color of the elements on the player; is black by default.
  • Accent color: The secondary color of elements on the player, such as the progress bar and hover states; is blue by default.
  • Icon/text color: The color of icons and text on the player; is white by default.
  • Thumbnail: Clicking on this allows you to upload a custom thumbnail to display when your event is not live.
  • Custom logo: Allows you to select or upload a custom logo to display on the player in place of the Vimeo logo.
  • Hide live label: Allows you to hide the red ‘Live’ label on the player when streaming.
  • Hide viewer count: Allows you to hide the live viewer count on the player when streaming.
  • Your details: You can choose which of your account or event details to overlay. Note that these cannot be displayed at the same time as the Playlist.
  • Profile picture: Displays your Vimeo profile picture. This does not display unless you also toggle on Title
  • Title: Displays your event title.
  • Byline: Displays your Vimeo account name. This does not display unless you also toggle on Title.

How to embed my live event on my website

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

When you stream an event on Vimeo, you can embed the live video player and viewer engagement tools onto your website, allowing your audience to watch and participate in your event directly on your site rather than only on Vimeo.com. This article explains how to customize and generate the embed code for your live event.

What to know before embedding a live event

  • Recurring Events: While widgets often work well for single videos, they generally do not work well for recurring events. If you need to embed a recurring live event, we recommend using the hosting service’s HTML block and pasting the iframe embed code described in the steps below.

How to embed a live event

You can generate specific embed codes for your player, engagement tools, or both. To do so:

  1. Create a live event or select one from your library.
  2. On the in-browser production tool, select Embed in the top right corner to customize your settings.
  3. Choose the content you would like to embed:
  • Player and engagement tools: Embeds the video player alongside chat, polls, and Q&A.
  • Player only: Embeds only the video player.
  1. Engagement tools only: Embeds only the engagement tools.
  2. Select your dimensions:
  • Responsive: The player will automatically adjust based on the container size (Default).
  • Fixed: Toggle on Set custom dimensions to enter the exact pixel size for the player.
  1. Under Where can this event be embedded?, choose where the event is allowed to appear and add custom domains if necessary.
  2. Select Copy embed code to copy the iframe code to your clipboard.
  3. Paste the code into your website’s HTML editor.
  4. Once embedded, the event will appear on your site. When you start your stream, the player will automatically load. When you stop your stream, the player will indicate that the event will be saved to your Library.
