How to enable extended streaming

This feature is only available as an add-on with an Enterprise plan. If you would like to enable extended streaming, please contact your account manager or our sales team.

With extended streaming, you can use an encoder to stream an event 24/7, or for as long as you wish. To see answers to frequently asked questions about this feature, see FAQ: Extended streaming mode.

  1. After you have created your live event, select the gear icon in the upper righthand corner of the event settings page.
  2. Open the Productiondropdown menu.
  3. Toggle off Record event and DVR in order to activate theExtended stream toggle. These options are not available for extended streaming.
  4. Toggle on Extended stream.
  5. Once you go live, your stream will remain active until you choose to end it manually.

⚠️Note:Extended streams will not be recorded, meaning your stream will not be archived or saved in your library. When recording is disabled for a recurring event, none of your future streams will be archived.

How to enable low-latency streaming

This feature requires an Advanced, Premium or Enterprise plan.

Vimeo Enterprise members have the option of reducing the delay of their streams from the source to their viewers by enabling low-latency streaming in their event settings.

  • How to enable low-latency streaming
  • What contributes to latency?
  • Why wouldn’t I always use low latency mode?

How to enable low-latency streaming

When you create a new event (or open an existing recurring event), you will be brought to the live settings page. Selec thegear icon in the upper righthand corner to open the Settings panel.

Within Settings, open the Production dropdown to findLatency options. Select theLatencydropdown to edit the selection for your event.

Notes:

  • If you enable low-latency streaming, you will not be able to enable auto-closed captions and vice versa.
  • If your organization also utilizes the corporate eCDN feature on the account, this will override the low-latency setting on your event. Currently, these features cannot be used together. If you wish to disable eCDN to use low latency, please contact us.

If you enable low-latency streaming for a recurring event, the setting will remain on for all future streams to that event (unless you manually disable it). Low-latency streaming cannot be turned on or off mid-event; you would need to toggle the switch before you start streaming.

What contributes to latency?

Latency–which is the term we use to refer to the time the camera captures the content to the time your viewers see it–has many varying factors that contribute to it. It generally comes down to the relationship between network congestion, CPU resources, and the stream’s quality (bitrate and resolution) throughout the stream’s journey from the source to the player.

A typical stream works like this:

  1. Production workflow: This is your camera(s), video mixer, encoder, and everything that you set up locally to produce your stream. It could be as simple as a webcam using our browser encoder or as complex as an external encoder with multiple camera inputs. The main factors here for latency are your encoder’s CPU capacity and network speed/bandwidth.
  2. Vimeo processes the stream: We ingest and decode the incoming stream, then re-encode it into multiple qualities and a more consumable format for viewing. The low-latency toggle does not impact this process.
  3. CDN sends content to the player: We use content delivery networks (CDNs) to distribute your content all over the world to then playback in the Vimeo player. As part of this process, the player keeps a certain amount of content pre-loaded (or “buffered”) to ensure a smooth playback experience should there be a network-related slowdown before this point. Enabling low-latency streaming will reduce the amount of content the player has prepared before playing back to the viewer.

At any point in this process, there is potential for stream back-up and network slowdown, which could be outside of your or Vimeo’s control. When we build up a buffer in the player, that allows time for any network-related slowdowns to catch up while still providing a smoother and high-quality playback experience for the viewer even if they are a little further behind. This also allows the player to download the highest possible quality when all systems are functioning without delay.

Why wouldn’t I always use low latency mode?

We know our users are eager to reduce the delay of their live events to their viewers. However, there is a trade-off when enabling low latency, in that when your stream moves from your encoder to our ingest servers and CDN to your viewers, it skips some of the steps we’d otherwise take to ensure a reliable and high-quality viewer experience.

Regardless of the latency setting, the player will create different qualities and pre-load video in the player before displaying it to the viewer. The difference between default latency and low latency is how much of the video is pre-loaded and prepared (also referred to as buffered) for playback. With low latency enabled, the player prepares less content at a more frequent rate, which can create less margin for error should there be a network issue in the process.

Your viewers may also see a reduction in video quality if there are network slowdowns in the process that prevent the player from quickly adapting to the highest possible bitrate if the highest quality isn’t yet buffered. Keeping the default latency setting would allow more time for higher-quality video to load.

If your content is more time-sensitive and/or requires closer to real-time interaction with your audience, that’s the ideal use case for enabling low latency. However, be mindful that if there is network congestion or CPU limitations along the way it’s more likely that your viewers will experience buffering or low-quality streaming in the player.

Events that do not need much interaction with viewers will not see any benefit of a low-latency stream, and as such we would recommend keeping low-latency turned off.

As always, we strongly recommend testing and rehearsing before your event.

How to hide the viewer count on my live event

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise account with the Events feature enabled.

To hide your live viewer count from the live event player:

  1. Select your event from your library.
  2. Navigate to Settings by selecting the gear icon from the upper right corner of the page.
  3. Go toDestinationsand select Customize next to the Vimeo logo.
  4. A new page will open. Scroll down to the Customization section.
  5. Toggle on Hide viewer count. Screenshot: hide viewer count.png
  6. Click Save in the upper right corner.
  7. The live viewer count will not be displayed in the live player for all future live streams on that event.

You can turn the viewer count back on for future streams on your event by returning to the Customize Player page and disabling the Hide viewer count toggle.

How to host a live event from my mobile device

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

The Vimeo mobile app for iOS and Android includes the ability to stream live directly from your mobile device, allowing you to go live on the go.

Ensure you have iOS 13 or later, or an Android version 6 or higher,installed on your device.

Due to variables outside of Vimeo’s control, Vimeo cannot guarantee streaming stability at all times for users connecting their mobile devices to 4G/5G mobile data or Wi-Fi connections.

  • Set up the app to stream
  • Start and stop streaming from the app
  • Adjust the streaming quality
  • Troubleshooting: Event doesn’t appear in the drop-down menu
  • Some things to note
  • iOS mobile App workflow

Set up the app to stream

Start by launching the app and make sure you are logged into your account. In the bottom navigation, tap the blue “Add” button in the center (Note: Some Android devices may display an”Upload” button instead).

Screenshot: PNG_image.png

Tap Live on the bottom right corner.

Screenshot: IMG_7819.PNG

The first time you use this feature, you will need to allow the Vimeo app to access your camera and microphone; this is required for streaming from the app to work.

After allowing these permissions, your camera will open. You can keep your phone in portrait mode to shoot a video in 9:16, or turn your device sideways to stream in landscape (16:9). If you do the latter, be sure your device’s portrait orientation lock is set to off, or the stream will appear sideways. Keep your device in the desired position (portrait or landscape) before going live to ensure you achieve the desired aspect ratio.

Screenshot: IMG_326F8B3E326E-1.png

Regardless of your video’s aspect ratio, you will see the option to enter an event title for a new event, or open the drop-down to choose an existing event.

Screenshot: IMG_7823.PNG

Below the event title, you can choose your streaming destinations. Tap the drop-down arrow to select your desired destinations. This is also where you can change your stream’s privacy settings on Vimeo by tapping Edit privacy. In addition, you can connect and add other simulcast destinations.

Screenshot: IMG_7822.PNG

Near the red go-live icon are additional settings. Tap the camera settings icon to adjust the following:

  • Sound: Mute and unmute your device’s microphone; it’s unmuted by default.

  • Note that the mobile app does not support external audio devices.

  • Light: Off by default, enabling this will turn on your device’s flashlight, which may be handy if you are in a dark environment.

  • Grid: If you want to get your framing precise, you can turn on the grid to evaluate your subjects’ positioning in the shot. Note that the grid lines will not appear on the stream. This is turned off by default.

  • Filter: You can choose among numerous camera filters to adjust the coloring of your shot. This is set to “Normal” by default.

Screenshot: IMG_7827.PNG

Screenshot: IMG_7828.PNG

You can also flip between the default front and rear cameras on your device by tapping the camera flip icon near the go-live button. Note that it’s not possible to select specific lenses (e.g., a wide-angle lens) that are included on some devices.

Screenshot: flip.png

Start and stop streaming from the app

When you’re ready to start streaming from your device, ensure you’re in the desired aspect ratio (landscape or portrait) before going live.

Portrait example - controls on the bottom of the screen:

Screenshot: IMG_8873.PNG

Landscape example - controls on the left side of the screen:

Screenshot: IMG_8874.PNG

Then tap the red button to start streaming. The icon will spin for a moment, then disappear, and a red “LIVE” box will appear in the upper right corner, alongside a viewer count and a timer. The camera settings are still accessible during your stream.

Screenshot: live_count_timer.png

⚠️Note: It is not possible to moderate or participate in your event’s live chat or use other interactive tools while streaming from the mobile app. This should be done from a separate browser.

You will see warning messages at the top of the screen if there is an issue, such as poor connectivity. Should this happen, check your connection or stop your stream and switch your connection type (e.g,. 4G to Wi-Fi).

You can also check the simulcast menu while live to share the URLs of your stream on those destinations; it will also inform you if there is a problem with the stream going to that destination.

Screenshot: destinations_menu_live.png

When your event is finished and you want to stop streaming, tap the red square icon. Your stream will then be archived as a video, and you can access it directly from the app as well as the Library when you log into your account on a desktop browser. The app will also display some basic analytics from your stream upon ending.

Screenshot: IMG_7830.PNG

Adjust the streaming quality

The quality of the stream will largely depend on the type of device you are using, based on the resolution that your camera and device’s hardware can support. That being said, you can adjust the default streaming quality that is available to your device in the app’s settings.

Navigate to Profile > Settings, where you can scroll down to find the Streaming settings menu.

Screenshot: profile_icon.png

Screenshot: settings_menu.png

Screenshot: streaming_quality.png

The quality you’re choosing here will be the highest available quality for playback. All lower qualities will still be present per our transcoding process. For example, if you choose 720p, your stream will be available in 720p, 540p, and 360p, but not 1080p. This can be useful if you are using a connection with poor upload speed or you are trying to reduce your data usage on a 4G/LTE connection.

Screenshot: quality_options.png

Troubleshooting: Event doesn’t appear in the drop-down menu

When you first create an event in your Vimeo account on your desktop, you’ll be brought to the event setup page. In there is a blue Next button in the upper right corner of the page.

Screenshot: next.png

If you click this, your event will not be available to select in the Vimeo app for 60 minutes. This is because clicking Next activates Vimeo’s web-based production tool, which remains active for 60 minutes before timing out. When it’s active, Vimeo cannot accept a stream from any other source, including the Vimeo mobile app.

To get around this, create your Vimeo event and then donot click Nexton the event setup page.

This will allow your event to appear in the Vimeo app as a streaming destination immediately and you can go live from the app to that event right away. The event will remain available in the app as long as you don’t select Next.

Alternatively, you can create a new event directly from the app by typing a title into the Event Title field as described above.

Some things to note

  • If you navigate away from the Vimeo app while streaming live, the stream will end and be archived as a video.
  • The same applies if you receive a phone call. Consider setting your device to Do Not Disturb to prevent your stream from being unexpectedly interrupted.
  • Streaming over a 4G/LTE connection will use data from your cellular provider’s data plan. Be mindful of how you connect your mobile device when going live.

Selecting Live events will take you to the New event creation process:

After selecting Create you will be taken back and it’ll be possible to go live.

Select the Camera settings symbol to get options for sound, light, grid, and filters:

Selecting the Simulcast symbol populates simulcast destinations and provides the ability to change the privacy settings.

If you click the circling arrows, it will switch to the forward-facing camera.

Clicking the red circle will start the live stream.

How to I customize the appearance of my live event teleprompter

In addition to the live event teleprompter window being resizable and repositionable, you can also customize the size of the text and the speed at which it scrolls.

Text Size

You can change the size of the text by selecting the “Increase Font Size”or “Decrease font size” buttons. This will adjust the font size to be either bigger or smaller.

How to install Livestream Studio

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can install Livestream Studio on your own Windows or macOS computer to access its production features. This article explains how to download and install the software.

  • How to install on macOS

What to know before installing

  • Administrator rights: If you are using Windows, you must be logged in as an Admin user to install and run Livestream Studio.
  • Internet connection:An active internet connection is required throughout the installation process.
  • Hardware units: If you purchased a Livestream Studio hardware product (e.g., HD31, HD51, HD550), the software is already pre-installed on your unit. You do not need to follow these steps.

How to install on Windows

  1. To download the installation file for Windows contact us and ask for the link to download the Livestream Studio app.
  2. Open the downloaded .exe file to launch the Livestream Studio Launcher wizard.
  3. Agree to the license terms and follow the on-screen prompts.
  4. Select Finish in the wizard.
  5. The Launcher will automatically open, download the full Studio software, and prompt you to install it via a second installation wizard.
  6. Follow the prompts to complete the second installation.
  7. When finished, the most recent version of Livestream Studio will launch automatically.

How to install on macOS

  1. To download the installation file for Mac contact us and ask for the link to download the Livestream Studio app.
  2. Open the downloaded .pkg file to launch the installation wizard.
  3. Follow the on-screen steps to complete the installation.
  4. Upon completion, Livestream Studio will launch automatically.

How to join a live event as a Remote Guest

Remote Guests lets you join a Live Event using your webcam or desktop source from a location different from the event host’s. This article explains how to join a live event as a Remote Guest and how to use the guest interface.

  • What to know before joining a live event as a Remote Guest
  • How to join a live event as a Remote Guest
  • How to use guest controls as a Remote Guest
  • Suggested next steps

What to know before joining a live event as a Remote Guest

Before joining a live event as a remote guest, note the following:

  • The host of the live event will provide you with a link to join as a Remote Guest.
  • Please contact the host of the live event if you need the link once more. Our support team cannot provide you with a new link.
  • Google Chrome is required to join as a Remote Guest.
  • View our hardware and network recommendations for Remote Guests.
  • A Vimeo account is not required to join a live event as a Remote Guest.
  • A Vimeo account with an Advanced, Premium, or Enterprise (with Events) plan is needed to host a live event.

How to join a live event as a Remote Guest

You can join a live event as a Remote Guest using Google Chrome and the link provided to you by the event host. To do so:

  1. Open the link provided by the host in Google Chrome.
  2. If this is your first time doing so, allow Chrome permission to access your camera and microphone when prompted.
  • Read how from Google Chrome support at Use your camera and microphone in Chrome.
  1. Enter your name and select Join Event.

Screenshot: A red box highlights the ‘Guest’ name in a input field and the ‘Join event’ button. This is under the instructions ‘Add your name to join as a guest’.

Once connected, you will see your camera feed in the bottom-right corner, see the Broadcast Preview, and hear the event audio.

How to use guest controls as a Remote Guest

While in the event, you have access to the following controls:

  • Share screen: Select the Share screen button to share your desktop, application window, or Chrome tab instead of your webcam.
  • Chat: Select the arrow in the upper-right corner to open the internal chat with the host and other guests.
  • Stop Video: Stops sending your video feed but keeps audio active.
  • Mute: Mutes your microphone.
  • Settings: Allows you to select a different webcam or audio source.
  • Leave: Disconnects you from the event.

Suggested next steps

  • If your camera or microphone is not appearing, visit Troubleshooting: Remote Guest’s camera and microphone not appearing.
  • Learn how to add Remote Gueststo your live event in Livestream Studio.

How to manually retrieve my Livestream Studio log files

If you’re experiencing problems with Livestream Studio and need help from our Support team, sending your log files when contacting uswill help us diagnose and resolve the issue more efficiently. This article explains how to collect Livestream Studio logs on Windows and macOS.

  • Which logs to send to Support
  • How to retrieve logs on Windows
  • How to retrieve logs on Mac

Which logs to send to Support

Please attach the following files and folders to your support ticket in a compressed .zip file: .

  • crisis_log.txt
  • launcher_config.xml
  • launcher_log.txt
  • primary_log.txt
  • previous_logs (folder)

How to retrieve Studio logs on Windows

  1. Press Windows Key + R on your keyboard to open the Run command window.
  2. In the text field of the Run command window, type %localappdata% and press Enter.
  3. In the File Explorer window, open the Livestream Studio folder. The necessary log files will be inside this folder.
  4. Compress your files into a compressed .zip file. Microsoft Support provides guidance on how to create a .zip file at Zip and unzip files.

How to retrieve Studio logs on Mac

  1. Open your Applications folder.
  2. Right-click on the Livestream Studio app icon and select Show Package Contents.
  3. Navigate into the Contents folder and into the Resources folder.
  4. The log files are stored in this directory.

Compress your files into a compressed .zip file. Apple Support provides guidance on how to create a .zip file at Zip and unzip files and folders on Mac.

How to monitor the health of your stream

Our stream health monitoring feature allows you to see how well your stream is performing in real-time. The information displayed in this tool comes directly from our Ingest server logs, which is the first point of contact your stream has with the Vimeo Live backend.

  • How to view your stream health
  • Stream Metrics
  • Advanced Analytics

How to view your stream health

If you are streaming via RTMP, you can find the stream health indicator by selecting the stream icon on the upper right of the live settings page and preview page.

Screenshot: Stream health current status.png

The indicator bar at the top displays one of the following statuses:

  • Ready: When your webcam has been connected and you are ready to go live.
  • Good connection: When your stream has connected (either through the browser, RTMP, or an integrated encoder) and our servers are receiving a stable frame rate/bitrate. (You can see this in the image above.)
  • Unstable connection: When our servers detect more than a 15% drop in frame rate/bitrate from the intended configuration. This means there may be a problem with your network connection or encoder.
  • Offline: When your stream has disconnected from our servers.

Stream Metrics

If you are streaming via an external encoder, you can view graphs and metrics of your stream. On the right navigation bar of the event settings page, click on the Streamicon to see more information about your broadcast.

Go to your stream metrics to view the data for your incoming bitrate and frame rate are displayed. The graph updates in real time and details the changes in bitrate/frame rate over the last ten minutes of your stream.

Screenshot: stream metrics.png

Below the graph, you’ll find the bitrate, average bitrate, frame rate, average frame rate, and video resolution for your stream. These metrics update in real time as well.

Please note: When screen sharing with the web-based production tool, the bitrate/frame rate will show 0fps and 0kbps. This does not mean there is an issue with your stream. The screen share functionality within the web-based production tool does not supply bitrate or frame rate data as other input sources do, thus there is no data to report in the graph. Once you end screen sharing and return to another input, the correct bitrate/frame rate will return.

Advanced Analytics

Below your stream metrics, you can click Show Analyticsto see additional information about your stream, namely Video codec, Audio codec, AVC profile, and AVC level. These inform you of your stream’s video and audio compression format (AVC stands for Advanced Video Coding), and the Session ID is a unique string that identifies your stream for Vimeo. If you’re noticing an issue with your stream you’d like us to investigate, include all the metrics listed here when you contact us so we can look into it.

How to navigate the web-based production tool

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article discusses the web-based production studio for live events. This allows you to stream directly from your browser without the need for additional tools or software.

The appearance of the studio may vary slightly depending on the type of production mode that you selected. This article outlines the Stream from your browser inproduction mode.

  • Accessing the web-based production studio
  • Top navigation bar
  • The stage
  • Scenes
  • Production elements toolbar
  • Other production modes

Accessing the web-based studio

You can access the web-based production studio after creating a live event or selecting a previously created event from your live events folder in your library.

Screenshot: The web-based streaming production studio. The layout shows a central canvas for video scenes, an asset menu on the left for speakers and media, and an open ‘Settings’ panel on the right for the event.

Top navigation bar

The top navigation bar displays the following:

  • Team- View your team that is working on your live event.
  • Analytics - View real-time analytics for your event.
  • Settings- Change the settings for your live event
  • Chat - Monitor and engage with viewers through the chat.
  • Share- Share the link to your stream.
  • Embed- Embed your live event on an external website.
  • Go Live- Launch your live event or switch the studio’s production mode.

The stage

The stage is at the center of the web-based production tool. The stage displays the currently selected scene, as shown to your viewers.

Screenshot: The stage of the live web production studio. The tool bar for changing background color and layout are at the top. Below it is an empty canvas. Below that is the scene selector showing a single scene plus the option to add a new scene.

Above the stage is the layout bar. Select the layout bar to choose the layout of your scene’s elements and speakers, or select Autofor the design to change automatically based on the production elements of your scene.

Screenshot: The Layouts menu option is selected and shows the open layouts menu, displaying all the options for displaying the chosen scene’s source arrangement

You can also change the background color of your scene. From the layout bar above the stage, select the background color button to choose a solid color, apply a predefined gradient, or select a custom color using a color picker for a personalized look for the scene.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the live web production stage with the background color selector open. The menu lets users choose solid colors, select gradient options, or input a HEX code for a custom color.

Scenes

Below the stage is the scenes panel. Learn how to add and manage scenes for your event at Creating and using scenes on a Vimeo event.

Below the scenes panel is the control bar. You can use the control panel bar to select and control your audio input, your camera input, share your screen, or open the teleprompter.

Screenshot: The controls toolbar with four icons: a muted microphone, an active camera, a share screen button, and a document button. The camera button is currently selected.

Production elements toolbar

On the left-hand toolbar, you’ll find various tools and production elements to help control and enhance your event.

  • Speakers: Invite and manage the speakers who will be presenting at your event.
  • Templates: Choose from various predefined layouts to enhance the visual presentation of your event.
  • Media: Add videos, images, and slides to your event.
  • Graphics: Add a lower-third overlay with information about the scene or the speaker
  • Brand: Incorporate your brand identity elements, such as colors and logos.
  • Q&A:Facilitate interaction by allowing viewers to submit questions during the livestream. You can moderate questions or allow anonymous Q&A.
  • Polls: Create and conduct polls to engage your audience and collect real-time feedback.

Differences with other production modes

As mentioned, changing to a different production mode for your live event will update the web-based production environment accordingly.

  • Pre-recorded event: Automatically go live with a pre-recorded segment.
  • Recording only: Record a video without an audience.
  • Use an external encoder: Go live with RTMP/RTMPS or SRT.

How to open and moderate my event’s engagement tools on a separate page

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise account with the Events feature enabled.

This article explains how to access a separate, full-page version of your event’s engagement tools for dedicated management of chat, polls, and Q&A.

In addition to embedding engagement tools or moderating audience engagement from your event settings page, you can access a separate full-page version of your event’s engagement tools.

This is helpful if you want someone on your team to solely focus on managing and moderating chat, polls, and Q&A.

To open engagement tools in a separate page:

  1. From the web-based production tool, select the Chatbutton located at the top right of the page. It is shaped like two overlapping speech bubbles.
  2. Select ⋮ > Engagement tools > Open in a new tab.
  3. This will open your engagement tools in a new tab in your browser.

How to prerecord an event in the web-based production tool

You can use our web-based production tool to record your camera, screen, and guest speakers without the need for an external application and without needing to go live. You can later share the recording as a video or set it up to stream live as a prerecorded event.

  1. Create an event, selecting Stream with your browser during the setup process.
  2. In the upper right corner of the web-based production tool, click the dropdown arrow next to Go live to open the Production mode menu.
  3. Select Recording only. This will remove audience engagement features such as chat, Q&A, and polls.
  4. Configure any other elements needed for your recording such as graphic overlays, videos, and guest speakers.
  5. When you are ready, select Start recording.
  6. While recording, you have three options in the upper right corner you can choose from. From left to right, they are:
  • Pause: This will pause the recording if you or your guest speakers need a break. Select the Play button that replaces it to resume recording where you left off.
  • Restart: This will stop and delete the active recording and immediately start a new recording.
  • Delete: This will stop and delete the current recording. You will have to manually click Start recording again to start a new recording.
  1. When you are ready to end the recording, select Stop recordingin the top right corner.
  2. A modal window will open to confirm that the recording has ended and give you two options:
  • Trim: This will open a new browser window allowing you to review your video’s transcript and trim unwanted sections of your video using our text-based video editor.
  • Review settings: This will open the video settings page for your event’s archived video.

How to preview your stream before going live

This article discusses how to preview your stream when using an external player encoder before going live to your audience

  • How to preview your stream
  • Troubleshooting: Go Live selection greyed out

How to preview your stream

When using an external encoder to stream over RTMP, RTMPS, or SRT, you can preview your stream before going live.

⚠️Note:This setting is not account-wide and must be configured for each event. If enabled for a recurring event, it will remain active for all associated streams.

To preview your stream before going live:

  1. Create a new live event or select a previously created event.
  2. Select Use an External encoderas your production mode.
  3. Select the Settings gear on the top right of the page to expand the settings panel.
  4. Select the toggle to Preview your streambefore going live.
  5. The preview will populate on the player before it is shown to your audience. Before broadcasting, you can open the Stream Healthpanel to check its status.
  6. Select Go Live in the upper right corner to begin streaming live to your audience.

If you use auto-closed captioning, those captions will not appear in this player, even after you go live. You must check the video page or the embedded player to see the captions.

Troubleshooting: Stream does not appear in preview player, “Go Live” button greyed out

If you enable the stream preview and the player fails to display your stream after launching your encoder (and you cannot select “Go Live”), it is usually because of blocked firewall ports.

Confirm that the following ports are open:

    • TCP/UDP 3478
  • TCP/UDP 19305-19307
  • TCP/UDP 19307 50000 - 64000

If these ports are unblocked and you still cannot preview your stream, please contact Support for additional assistance.

How to schedule a prerecorded event to start automatically

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can schedule prerecorded content to play automatically in a live event without needing to be present to start the stream. This article discusses how to schedule a prerecorded event, manage playback settings, and switch between production modes.

  • What to know before scheduling a prerecorded live event
  • How to schedule and configure a prerecorded event to start automatically
  • How to switch a scheduled prerecorded event back to manual control

What to know before scheduling a prerecorded live event

Before you schedule your event, take note of the following:

  • Encoder support:This feature is only supported when streaming via the web-based production tool and is not available for external encoders.
  • Event types availability: Prerecorded events are available for live events and webinars, but are not available for venues.
  • Minimum lead time: If the scheduled start time is set to under 1 minute from the current time, the automatic start will not work.
  • Concurrent-stream limits at start time: earlier scheduled start times take priority. If your account is already at its concurrent-stream limit when the prerecorded event is due to start, the prerecorded event will not begin and the event owner receives an automated email explaining why. You can review your full event schedule on the Live Events dashboard.
  • Video edits: Any videos you add to the live event will play back in their entirety, and all video scenes will auto-transition. This cannot be changed. Ensure you have made all necessary edits or trims before the event begins.
  • Audience interaction activation and availability:Whilechat, polls, and Q&Acan be added to the event, polls must be manually activated during the broadcast to ensure timing is accurate. Chat and Q&A can be scheduled automatically.
  • Time zones: Event settings display in the creator’s browser timezone, but viewers will see the start time automatically converted to their local timezone.
  • Contributor Plus folder location:New live events created by Contributor Plus team members are stored in their own folder and must be moved to a shared team folder to go live.
  • Subscription limitations: The number of concurrent events varies with the subscription plan. Read more at Simulcast concurrent events to different destinations.

How to schedule and configure a prerecorded event to start automatically

You can configure a live event to start automatically using prerecorded videos. To do so:

  1. Create a new live eventor select an existing one from your library.
  2. In the upper right corner of the web-based production tool, open the dropdown next to Go live and select Prerecorded event.
  3. Select the video(s) you want to stream from the modal that appears and select Add.These videos will be added to the Prerecorded segment.
  4. If you want to include a live portion at the end of the event, add scenes to the Live segmentlocated below the player. If live scenes are also added, the event will switch to manual mode after transitioning to the first live scene, requiring you to manually select End event to stop the stream.
  5. Navigate to theSettings Gear > Schedule to add the Start date and Time. A timer in the upper right corner will display the countdown to the scheduled start time.

Once the event begins at the scheduled time, prerecorded videos will play and proceed to the next scenes automatically.

How to switch a scheduled prerecorded event back to manual control

You can revert a prerecorded event to manual production mode if you decide to go live manually. To do so:

  1. Select your event from the Events library.
  2. In the upper right corner of the production tool, select the dropdown next to the scheduled date (or ‘Unscheduled’ if there’s no date set).
  3. Select Stream from your browser. Screenshot: Web production tool menu highlighting the dropdown arrow and the ’’Stream from your browser” option.
  4. Your segments will remain in order, but must now be switched manually. Additionally, the event will not start until you select Go live.

How to set the regional availability for live events

This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article discusses setting the regional availability for your live event on Vimeo. To learn how to set the geo-availability for your video, visit How do I set regional availability for my videos?

  • What is regional availability?
  • Setting regional availability by country/region
  • Setting regional availability by US-based city or zip code
  • Setting regional availability using a .csv file
  • What will my viewers experience?

What is regional availability?

Setting an event’s regional availability (geo-blocking or geo-allowing) lets hosts restrict access to their event based on viewers’ locations. Location is typically based on the viewer’s IP address.

When configuring Regional Availability for your live events, you can:

  • Allow Locations: Specify where the event can be viewed.
  • Deny Locations: Specify the locations where the event cannot be viewed.

Regional Availability helps content owners:

  • Comply with licensing agreements: Ensure that your event is only accessible in regions where you have the necessary rights to display it.
  • Protect content: Prevent unauthorized access to your event.

You can set an event’s regional availability by region or country. Regional availability for cities and zip codes based in the United States is also supported.

Setting regional availability by country or region

Team owners, admins, and contributor+ members can manage geoblocking settings on the Vimeo website. These settings are not accessible on the Vimeo mobile app.

  1. Visit the web-based production tool for your event.
  2. Select the Settings gear in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Regional Availabilityto expand the menu.
  4. Select Manageto open the Manage Regional Availability window.
  5. Use the dropdown menu to select whether you want to’ Block in specific regions’ or ‘Allow in particular regions.
  6. Select the checkmark next to each region or country to allow or block, depending on your setting type. You can also use the search bar to find specific countries and regions.
  7. Select Applywhen you are finished.

Setting regional availability by US-based cities or zip codes

You can also set regional availability by using zip codes. Support for city and zip/postal codes is currently limited to cities and zip codes in the United States.

To set regional availability for your event by zip/postal code:

  1. In the Manage Regional Availability window, select the World icon.
  2. Select Enter US zip codes.
  3. Enter each 5-digit ZIP code and press Enter.
  • You can add multiple ZIP codes by separating them by commas (e.g., 10001, 10002, 10003) and selecting Enter.
  1. Select Applyto save your settings.
  2. You can download your list of regions as a .csv file by selecting the download button at the bottom left of the window.

Setting regional availability using a .csv file

In addition, you can bulk allow or block regions using a .csv file. Learn how to format your file at ‘How do I format a .csv file to set regional availability for my video or live event?’

To import your .csv file:

  1. Select the Upload icon in the bottom-left corner of the Manage regional availability window.
  2. Select the CSV file from your device to upload.
  3. Review the imported data.
  4. Click “Apply” to save the settings.

What will viewers experience?

Viewers in geo-allowed regions can watch your event without any indication that regional access restrictions have been applied.

Viewers in restricted regions will not be able to access your live event. They will receive an error message indicating that it is unavailable in their area. Read more at ‘What does “This video is not available in your region” mean?’

How to set up a third-party encoder to stream with Fail-Safe Streaming

This feature requires an Enterprise account with the Events feature added.

This article discusses setting up a third-party encoder to stream with Fail-Safe Streaming.

If you stream your events using an external encoder, you must install our dedicated application on your local environment (i.e. the same device that runs your preferred encoding application) to stream using MPEG-DASH.

Read about MPEG-DASH streaming at ‘How to stream to your event with Fail-Safe Streaming’.

⚠️Note: Fail-safe streaming is not supported for SRT streams.

Download and install the transmitter service

  1. Select Use an External Encoder as your Production mode when creating your event.
  2. On the event setup page, navigate to Settings.
  3. Under Latency, choose Fail-safe streaming.
  4. Select the Download button to download the Vimeo Fail-Safe Streaming Transmitter Service application.
  5. Follow the onscreen steps to complete the installation.

Using the Vimeo transmitter service

Once the transmitter service is installed in your local environment:

  1. Copy the URL and Stream Key under the Fail-Safe Streamingtab on your event’s preview page.
  2. Paste the URL and Stream Key into the appropriate fields within your encoder.
  3. Launch the Fail-Safe StreamingTransmitter Service application.
  4. Start streaming from your encoder.
  5. The transmitter service will begin receiving your RTMP signal and will convert it to MPEG-DASH before sending it to Vimeo.

Is the fail-safe streaming transmitter service compatible with a third-party hardware encoder?

Yes. You can use fail-safe streaming with your chosen hardware encoder. To stream from your hardware encoder to the transmitter service, substitute the localhost part of your RTMP URL with the transmitter service’s local IP address.

How to set up and manage Live Q&A

You can boost viewer engagement during your virtual events by hosting Q&A sessions directly within your event. This feature is available alongside the live chat. If you embed the live chat on your website, the Q&A will be included as well. Live Q&A allows you to accept questions, let viewers vote to prioritize questions based on popularity, display questions on the stream, and eventually answer them live.

This article explains how to effectively set up and manage live Q&A sessions to improve viewer engagement during virtual events.

  • Setting up Q&A
  • Adding Q&A graphics to a scene
  • Displaying and answering questions
  • Q&A tools
  • Ending the Q&A session
  • Exporting the event Q&A

Setting up Q&A

The character limit for questions in a Live Q&A is a maximum of 240 characters or 3 lines.

You can set up Live Q&A in both the browser studio and when you are streaming through an encoder for your live event.

💡Tip: You can also manage and moderate Q&A from the engagement tools link.

To set up Q&A in the browser studio (‘Stream through your browser):

  1. In the browser studio, select the Q&A button from the left panel. It is indicated by a speech bubble with a question mark in the center.
  2. In the Q&A pane, you can set the following features as an Enterprise member:
  • Moderate questions:Select which questions are shown to the audience.
  • Allow anonymous:Allow viewers to hide their names when asking a question.
  1. Select Start Q&Ato begin the Q&A session. ⚠️Note:If you are adding Q&A while you Stream with Vimeo, you will need to select Show on scene on the web-based production tool page to show the questions’ graphics overlays.
  2. Select Export questions to export the questions from your event to a .csv file.

To set up Q&A when streaming with an encoder:

  1. Select the Q&A button from the left-side panel on the main event settings page.
  2. Enterprise only: Toggle the options for Moderate questions and/or Allow anonymous.
  3. Select Start Q&Ato begin the Q&A session.

Once you have set up your virtual event, you can see a Q&A tab on the left side of the page, where you can click Start Q&A to open your event up to questions. You can do this before your stream or while you’re live, although note that you cannot take action on a question until your event is broadcasting.

You can set up Q&A before your stream or while you’re live, however, you cannot take action on a question until your event is broadcasting.

After you’ve selected Start Q&A, your viewers will be notified that they can begin to submit questions on the on-site Vimeo event page or the embedded chat window. If you have enabled Anonymous Q&A, viewers can choose whether to submit questions anonymously or with their names attached.

An indicator below the chat box shows the number of characters remaining to the question-askers while typing questions.

Questions viewers ask will be posted to the Q&A window immediately upon submission unless you have moderation enabled. Viewers can click the thumbs-up icon to vote on questions they like.

Under the Active tab, questions will populate, which you can sort either by Recent or Popular.

💡Tip: If you want to add Q&A to your venues, refer to How to open a Q&A in a virtual venue.

Adding Q&A graphics to a scene

⚠️Note: This section is only relevant if you stream to a recurring event or a webinar via our web-based production tool page.

If you are adding Q&A and selecting Stream with Vimeo when setting up your recurring event, you will need to add it to a scene on the web-based production tool page to show the questions’ graphics overlays.

  1. Below the preview player, click on the scene with which you want the question graphics to appear.
  2. Click the Q&A icon in the left navigation menu.
  3. In the panel that opens, click Show on scene.
  4. An icon will appear in the selected scene thumbnail indicating that the poll graphic is included.
  5. The Q&A will be enabled for that scene, so when you display a question graphic (discussed below), it will appear when you click Show on scene for each question.

To disable the Q&A graphics, click Disable Q&A below the preview player.

Displaying and answering questions

⚠️ Note: It’s only possible to display question graphic overlays when streaming via the web-based production tool page. If you are streaming via an external encoder, questions will only appear in the chat window.

You, or other admins and contributors on your team, can reply to questions within the Q&A panel if you wish. However, if you prefer to answer a question as part of your live broadcast:

  1. A graphic overlay will appear as a lower third with the question. This is generally when you would be expected to address the question within the stream.
  2. You can hide (and re-show) the graphic overlay by clicking the corresponding Hide (Show) in the Active tab.
  3. When you’ve finished answering, go to the question in the Q&A panel and click Archiveto remove the question from the list. You may also archive questions without answering them or publishing them to the stream.

If you’ve archived a question by mistake, you can switch over to the Archived tab, hover the cursor over the questions, and click Unarchive. This will put the question back in the Active tab.

Q&A tools

Pin a question

Event hosts and broadcasters can pin a specific question to the top of the questions list. Only one question can be pinned at a time. Pinned questions will be visible to all event attendees, including viewers, moderators, and presenters. Event hosts and broadcasters can unpin the current question and pin a new one.

To pin a question:

  1. Open your Q&A panel, and select the question you would like to pin
  2. Click on the pin iconbeside the question to Pin to top. The question will now appear at the top of the list for all the viewers.
  3. You can click on the pin icon again to unpin the question.

Ending the Q&A session

To end your Q&A session, click End Q&A or End sessionin the Q&A panel (depending on how you’re streaming).

Please note that ending Q&A does not end the live chat. Live chat will end as soon as the broadcast ends and will not be available afterwards.

Exporting the event Q&A

Once you end the Q&A, you can export a CSV log of the Q&A by clicking Export in the Q&A panel.

  • If you streamed viaan external encoder, this is at the top of the Q&A panel.
  • If you streamed to a recurring event or webinar with Vimeo (using the web-based production tool page), this is below the Start Q&A button.

If you’re streaming to a recurring event, this button opens a drop-down menu with a list of the date/times of all streams in the last 30 days that you can archive; select Current event or Active Q&A sessionfor the active event.

The Q&A CSV includes the following information:

  • Name (person who asked it or “anonymous”)
  • The question
  • Time submitted
  • Number of upvotes
  • Answered (yes/no)
  • Archived (yes/no)
  • Approved (yes/no/N/A – this only applies to Enterprise customers who have access to moderation features)
  • Q&A number (if you held multiple Q&A sessions within one stream, i.e. you started a Q&A, then ended it, then started it again prior to ending your broadcast; this lets you know if the question was asked during which Q&A session during the course of the stream).

How to set up and use a teleprompter for my live event

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can write a script or talking points to use as a teleprompter for your live event in the web-based production tool. Guest Speakers can also use the teleprompter.

  • How to set up the teleprompter
  • How to use the teleprompter

How to set up the teleprompter

Before your event begins, set up the web-based teleprompter with the script you want to read.

To set up the teleprompter:

  1. In the web-based production tool, select the Open Teleprompterbutton.
  2. Type or paste your script or talking points in the teleprompter window.

💡 Tip:You can also use AI to generate a script for you. To learn how, visit ‘How to use AI to write a script for my live event’s teleprompter’

How to use the teleprompter

Once you have set up and customized the appearance of your teleprompter, it will be ready for use during your live event. Event runners and guest speakers can both use the teleprompter.

To use the teleprompter:

  1. Select the Playbutton in the Teleprompter window. This will cause the script to start scrolling.
  2. Select the Pausebutton to pause the scroll.
  3. Select the Reset button to restart the script from the beginning.

💡Tip:You can control the text size or the text speed while the teleprompter is scrolling to make the script easier to read.

How to share my archived live event

When you end a live event, the URL of each archive from that event will include a unique video ID, which is different from the general event ID. This allows for differentiating the individual videos within an event series after they are no longer live.

Keep this in mind when sharing links to your event versus a specific archive from that event.

  • When your recurring live event is streaming live, it will keep the same URL in the format of:
  • *0
  • The xxxx represents an event ID, which is different from a video ID.
  • After a stream belonging to a recurring event series ends, it will archive and the archived video will then have its unique URL with a unique video ID in the format of:
  • *0

When you share the general link to your event page on Vimeo, viewers can see past recordings of that event using the arrow buttons within the upper right corner of the player. Note that this only appears to viewers if you enablePlaylist in the live event player settings.

Screenshot: Screenshot 2024-03-29 at 2.50.50 PM.png

If you want to share one specific archive from an event:

  1. Navigate to your library.
  2. Locate the video within the library. It will have the same title as the event. Note that archives are not stored in the Live Events folder.
  3. Select the video to enter the video settings page.
  4. Select the Share button in the upper right corner.

How to simulcast concurrent events to different destinations

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

It’s possible to simulcast concurrent live events on Vimeo to different streaming destinations. For example, you can stream a webinar to LinkedIn at the same time as a product announcement on Facebook, all from different events on the same Vimeo account. This article discusses limitations and what to expect when simulcasting concurrent live events.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:While connections to social sites are user-specific, the ability to share andprivacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit “How to edit my Organization’s settings” or”How to edit my Workspace’s settings“.

  • How many concurrent events can I stream to?
  • How many simulcast destinations can I stream to?
  • Can I stream concurrent events to the same simulcast destination?

How many concurrent events can I stream to?

With an Advanced plan, you can stream up to two (2) different events on your account simultaneously using either our web-based production tool on each event or different external encoders. You can unlock access to more concurrent live events with an Enterprise account.

Each event can be configured to simulcast to different destinations, allowing you to reach different audiences with each stream. If those events are live at the same time, neither stream will interfere with or interact with the other.

How many simulcast destinations can I stream to?

For each event on your account, you can add up to 10 directly integrated simulcast destinations (Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn) and up to 20 custom destinations via RTMP.

Can I stream concurrent events to the same simulcast destination?

You can stream to the same destination from different concurrent Vimeo events. The specific experience depends on how you simulcast.

  • Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn integrations: If you stream separate events to the same destination simultaneously (e.g., both events simulcast to the same Facebook page), both events will stream concurrently in separate locations within that destination.
  • Facebook will create separate posts on the same page.
  • YouTube will create separate pages for each event on your account.
  • LinkedIn will create separate posts on the same page.
  • Custom destinations via RTMP: You should generate separate stream keys from the platform you’re simulcasting to if you wish to stream different events to that destination concurrently. This will ensure that one event does not override another.

How to simulcast my Vimeo event to Facebook

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

There are two ways to simulcast your event from Vimeo to Facebook: a direct integration with your Facebook account or via RTMP. This article will walk through the requirements and steps for each simulcasting method so that you can stream your Vimeo event to your Facebook audience with whichever method you prefer.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:While connections to social sites are user-specific, the ability to share andprivacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit “How to edit my Organization’s settings” or”How to edit my Workspace’s settings“.

  • Requirements for simulcasting to Facebook
  • Set up Facebook as a streaming destination: Direct integration
  • Set up Facebook as a streaming destination: RTMP

Requirements for simulcasting to Facebook

  • Direct integration:
  • You must be the Vimeo account owner to set up the initial account connection to Facebook. After the connection is made, a Vimeo account admin or contributor plus can configure an event to simulcast to that Facebook destination.
  • The direct integration does not support streaming to Facebook groups. If you want to stream to a Facebook group, you will need to use the RTMP method.
  • Either simulcasting method:
  • You must be able to log into the Facebook account that is either the owner or administrator of the desired profile or page.

Set up Facebook as a streaming destination: Direct integration

You can connect Vimeo to your Facebook account and simulcast to your Facebook Profile or any page of which you are an Admin, up to 10 destinations at once.

  1. To connect your Facebook account to Vimeo, first create or navigate to your live event.
  2. In the event production page, select Settings, then open the Destinations panel.
  3. Click Connect next to Facebook. Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting the gearwheel icon at the top of the live settings page, followed by the Facebook option under the Destinations panel on the right side of the page.
  4. Facebook will open in a new window prompting you to authenticate the Vimeo app. If your Facebook account does not automatically appear, make sure to log in to the Facebook account in the same web browser, then go back to your live event settings and click Connect again.
  5. Follow the onscreen prompts and choose the default privacy for the live events Vimeo posts to Facebook. These privacy settings only affect your stream on Facebook and do not change the event settings on Vimeo.
  6. Next, adjust the toggles to limit or grant permissions to post content in different places on the Facebook account, such as specific groups and pages. Select OK. You will be redirected back to the Destinations panel in your live event settings page on Vimeo.
  7. Click Add next to Facebook to add a Facebook destination for your stream.
  8. Select the Facebook destination you wish to simulcast to and adjust Facebook’s privacy setting as desired, then click Save.
  9. When you’re ready, go live to your Vimeo event; it will automatically simulcast to Facebook. Remember that your encoder settings should include the RTMP URL and Stream Key from Vimeo, not Facebook.

Set up Facebook as a streaming destination: RTMP

Another way to simulcast from Vimeo to Facebook is to get the RTMP URL and Stream Key from your desired Facebook destination and input them into your Vimeo event’s Destinations setting. This method allows for up to 20 simultaneous destinations.

  1. Follow Facebook’s instructions to Go live on Facebook using streaming software. This instructs you on Facebook’s requirements for going live on their platform and how to find the server URL and stream key, which Vimeo needs.
  2. On Vimeo, create or navigate to your event.
  3. In the production tool, select Settings at the top of the page.
  4. In the right-hand menu, open the Destinations panel.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the panel to find RTMP, then select Add.
  6. An RTMP streaming settings modal window will open on Vimeo. Input a Destination name (e.g. “My Facebook page”); this serves as a descriptive label for you.
  7. Copy and paste the Server URL and Stream key from Facebook into the corresponding fields on Vimeo. (On Facebook, the “Server URL” is the RTMP URL.) Then click Save.
  8. When you’re ready, go live on Vimeo from your encoder.
  9. Once you are streaming from your encoder, you will receive a live video and audio preview in Facebook. Confirm that the video and audio are correct and in sync. You must select Go live now in Facebook in order for your live video from Vimeo to be posted to your Facebook audience.
  10. As a best practice, stop the live feed on Facebook first. This will end the stream on Facebook and post it as a video. You can then end the stream on Vimeo.

How to simulcast my Vimeo event to Linkedin

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can simulcast your events from Vimeo to a LinkedIn profile or LinkedIn page, including scheduled events on LinkedIn. This article will walk through the requirements and steps for connecting to LinkedIn so that you can stream your Vimeo event to your LinkedIn audience.

Requirements for simulcasting to LinkedIn

  • You must be the Vimeo account owner to set up the initial connection from Vimeo to LinkedIn. After the connection is made, a Vimeo account admin or contributor plus can configure any event on the Vimeo account to simulcast to that LinkedIn destination.
  • If you want to stream to a company Page on LinkedIn, you must connect to the LinkedIn account of that page’s administrator.
  • LinkedIn requires that you meet their Live Video Access Criteria to stream to LinkedIn.
  • The use existing LinkedIn event option is available when the start time of the scheduled LinkedIn event is at least one hour from the current time.
  • For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:While connections to social sites are user-specific, the ability to share andprivacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit “How to edit my Organization’s settings” or”How to edit my Workspace’s settings“.

Set up LinkedIn as a streaming destination

To connect your Vimeo account to LinkedIn and add it as a streaming destination:

  1. Create or navigate to your live event.
  2. In the top of the production tool, select the Settings gearwheel
  3. Open the Destinations panel.
  4. Select Connect next to LinkedIn. Screenshot: Screenshot of the web production tool highlighting the gearwheel at the top right of the page and the open Destinations panel, pointing out the LinkedIn option.
  5. Log in to your LinkedIn account if necessary, and choose if you want to connect as a Member (to your own profile) or as an Admin (to your company page).
  6. Follow the onscreen prompts and allow the requested permissions to connect your Vimeo and LinkedIn accounts. Once connected, return to the event settings page on Vimeo.
  7. If you want to schedule the stream on LinkedIn so that your audience knows when you will go live, toggle on Schedule and set a start time and date for your event. Select Save.
  8. Ensure the toggle switch next to your preferred LinkedIn destination is on.
  9. When you’re ready, go live on Vimeo. Once live, your stream will automatically simulcast to LinkedIn (allow 20-30 seconds for the stream to appear). If you created or selected a scheduled event, the stream will appear in that event’s post.

How to simulcast my Vimeo event to other streaming destinations

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can simulcast your live event from Vimeo to any streaming destination that accepts RTMP, such as Instagram, TikTok, and Twitch, so your content reaches your audience on your preferred platform. This article discusses what you need from the streaming destination and how to configure your Vimeo event to simulcast to those other providers.

  • Requirements for simulcasting to custom destinations
  • Set up a custom streaming destination on my Vimeo event
  • How many custom destinations can I stream to at once?

Requirements for simulcasting to custom destinations

If your desired streaming destination does not have a direct integration with Vimeo, such as Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn, confirm that it can receive live broadcasts via RTMP.

If it can, locate the RTMP URL (sometimes referred to as the Server URL) and the Stream key for your account on that platform. Provided below are links to popular platforms’ documentation on how to do so:

  • Instagram
  • Twitch
  • X, formerly known as Twitter

Before your event, check with your provider for instructions and best practices for streaming to that platform using a software encoder, treating Vimeo as the software encoder.

For Enterprise accounts with Workspaces:While connections to social sites are user-specific, the ability to share andprivacy settings can be configured and managed at both the Workspace and Organization levels, with Organization settings taking precedence. For details, visit “How to edit my Organization’s settings” or”How to edit my Workspace’s settings“.

Set up a custom streaming destination on my Vimeo event

Once you have the RTMP URL and Stream Key for your streaming destination, you can add them to your Vimeo event settings so that Vimeo can push your live stream to that provider.

  1. On Vimeo, create or navigate to your event.
  2. In the production tool, select Settings at the top of the page.
  3. In the right-hand menu, open the Destinations panel.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the panel to find RTMP, then select Add.
  • If you are streaming to Instagram, TikTok, or X, you can select Add next to the corresponding icons, but the following steps are the same.
  1. An RTMP streaming settings modal window will open on Vimeo. Input a Destination name (e.g. “My Twitch Channel”); this serves as a descriptive label for you.
  2. Copy and paste the RTMP URL and Stream key from your destination into the corresponding fields on Vimeo, then click Save.
  3. When you’re ready, go live on Vimeo from your encoder.
  4. Once you are streaming from your encoder, confirm that the video and audio are also being received at your custom destination.
  5. When you end the stream on Vimeo, the stream will also end on the destination.

How many custom destinations can I stream to at once?

You can simulcast to up to 20 custom streaming destinations via RTMP per event.

How to simulcast my Vimeo event to YouTube

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

There are two ways you can simulcast from Vimeo to YouTube: a direct integration with your YouTube account, or via RTMP. This article will walk through the requirements and steps for each simulcasting method so that you can stream your Vimeo event to your YouTube audience with whichever method you prefer.

  • Requirements for simulcasting to YouTube
  • Set up YouTube as a streaming destination: Direct integration
  • Set up YouTube as a streaming destination: RTMP

Requirements for simulcasting to YouTube

For details, visit “How to edit my Organization’s settings” or”How to edit my Workspace’s settings“.

Set up YouTube as a streaming destination: Direct integration

You can connect your Vimeo account to your YouTube account and simulcast to your YouTube channel, up to 10 destinations at once.

  1. Create or navigate to your live event.
  2. In the production tool, select Settings then open the Destinations panel.
  3. Select Connect next to YouTube. Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting the gearwheel icon at the top of the live settings page, followed by the YouTube option under the Destinations panel on the right side of the page.

Set up YouTube as a streaming destination: RTMP

Another way to simulcast from Vimeo to YouTube is to get the RTMP URL and Stream Key from YouTube Studio and input them into your Vimeo event’s Destinations setting. This method allows for up to 20 simultaneous destinations for your event.

  1. Follow YouTube’s instructions to go live using an encoder. This guides you on YouTube’s requirements for going live on their platform and how to find the RTMP URL and stream key, which Vimeo needs.
  • Within YouTube, you can also choose to schedule your stream for later. If you miss your scheduled start time, nothing will happen; you can always go into your Live Control room and change the date, time, and whatever other details you’d like. Your event link and RTMP credentials will remain the same until you go live to that event.
  1. On Vimeo, create or navigate to your event.
  2. In the production tool, select Settings at the top of the page.
  3. In the right-hand menu, open the Destinations panel.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the panel to find RTMP, then select Add.
  5. An RTMP streaming settings modal window will open on Vimeo. Input a Destination name (e.g. “My YouTube channel”); this serves as a descriptive label for you.
  6. Copy and paste the RTMP URL and Stream key from YouTube into the corresponding fields on Vimeo. Then click Save.
  7. When you’re ready, go live on Vimeo from your encoder.
  8. Once you are streaming from your encoder, you will be live on your YouTube channel.
  • If you are broadcasting to a scheduled stream on YouTube, you will need to manually select Go live from the YouTube Live Control Room for the stream to be live on YouTube.

How to stream a live event over RTMP/RTMPS

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article explains how to stream a live event from a web-based production studio using RTMP or RTMPS.

  • What is the RTMP/RTMPS protocol?
  • How do I stream a live event using RTMP or RTMPS?
  • How can I monitor the health of my RTMP/RTMPS stream?

What is the RTMP/RTMPS protocol?

RTMP (Real-Time Messaging Protocol) and RTMPS (RTMP over a Transport Layer Security (TLS/SSL) connection) are transmission protocols used for streaming audio, video, and data over the internet.

How do I stream a live event using RTMP / RTMPS?

You can stream with an external encoder from the web browser while setting up your event. Learn which external encoders Vimeo supports at ‘About Encoders’.

To stream your live event with an external encoder in the web browser:

  1. Select your event from your Live Events folder in your Library, or create a new event to access the browser-based production studio.
  2. In the top right corner of the browser studio, select the drop-down arrow next to ‘Go Live’.
  3. Select ‘Use an external encoder’.
  4. In the settings pane on the right side of the screen, select RTMP/RTMPSin the header of the Streammenu.
  5. Copy your stream URL and stream ID into your external encoder.
  6. Add any additional information needed for your stream to the Settings pane.

When you’re ready to go live, select Go Live.To preview your stream before going live, select the toggle next to ‘Preview stream before going live’. This will allow you to preview your stream before it is visible to your audience. Your stream will not go live unless you select the “Go Live” button. Read more at Preview your stream before going live.

How can I monitor the health of my RTMP/RTMPS stream?

You can monitor your stream stability using the indicator bars above the stream output window in the production studio. The network indicator will change to yellow or red if the connection worsens. When the connection quality is good, the indicator will be hidden.

Select the stream health indicator button to open the stream health pane to monitor your stream’s health specifics.

How to stream a live event over SRT

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

This article discusses how to stream a live event from the web-based studio using the SRT protocol.

  • What is the SRT protocol?
  • What does Vimeo support and not support for the SRT protocol?
  • How do I stream a live event using SRT?
  • How can I monitor the health of my SRT stream?

What is the SRT protocol?

Secure Reliable Transport (SRT) is a widely adopted, open-source, encrypted video transport protocol developed by Haivison. This protocol enhances streaming performance on networks with inconsistent connectivity. SRT excels at delivering high-quality video even under less-than-ideal network conditions.

What does Vimeo support and not support for the SRT protocol?

We support the following when streaming over SRT:

  • Container: MPEG-TS
  • Video codec: H.264, H.265
  • Audio codec: AAC
  • Max frame rate: 1080p 30fps
  • Using thebackup stream feature
  • Low-latencymode
  • Simulcasting
  • One audio track on a single SRT stream

We do notsupport the following when streaming over SRT:

  • All available modes on SRT encoders
  • Our platform can only work in “Listener” mode, as the external encoder is expected to use “Caller” mode.
  • Extended stream mode
  • Fail-safe streaming
  • Multi-audio tracks

What configurations are required for my SRT stream?

Learn how to configure your SRT stream from Haivision’s Help Center at Configuring an SRT Stream.

How do I stream a live event using the SRT protocol with an external encoder?

You can stream with an external encoder from the web browser while setting up your event. Learn which external encoders we support at Supported external encoders.

To stream your live event with an external encoder in the web browser:

  1. Select your event from your Live Events folder in your Library, or create a new event to access the browser-based production studio.
  2. In the top right corner of the browser studio, select the drop-down arrow next to Go Live.
  3. Select Use an external encoder.
  4. In the settings pane on the right-hand side of the screen, select SRTfrom the Streammenu.
  5. Copy your stream URL and stream ID into your external encoder.
  6. If you wish to give your stream additional protection, toggle on Encryption, and paste the passphrase into your encoder.
  • Note that where and how you input your stream information will vary from encoder to encoder. Refer to your software’s documentation for detailed instructions on how to apply an SRT stream URL, stream ID, and passphrase for your encoder.
  1. Add in any additional information needed for your stream in the Settings pane.

When you’re ready to go live, select Go Live.To preview your stream before going live, select the toggle next to Preview stream before going live. This will allow you to preview your stream before it is visible to your audience. Your stream will not go live unless you select the “Go Live” button. Read how at Preview your stream before going live.

How can I monitor the health of my SRT stream?

Select the stream health indicator bars above the stream output window to open the stream health pane and monitor your stream stability. The network indicator will change to yellow or red if the connection worsens. When the connection quality is good, the indicator will be hidden.

How to stream a presentation or slideshow

This feature requires an Advanced or Premium plan, or an Enterprise plan with the Events feature added.

You can stream a presentation or a slideshow as a live event. This article discusses how to stream a presentation using the web-based production tool or Livestream Studio.

  • What to know before streaming a presentation or slideshow
  • How to stream a presentation or slideshow in the Web-based production tool
  • How to stream a presentation or slideshow in Livestream Studio

What to know before streaming a presentation or slideshow

  • Slideshows are converted to static slides. Any animations or effects will be removed, and videos that are part of the slides will not be playable.
  • You can upload presentations in .pdf and .pptx formats, up to 100MB.
  • Live events created by Contributor Plus team members are stored in the user’s Private folder and must be moved to a shared team folder to go live. Additionally, Contributor Plus members can only activate or deactivate the logos and backgrounds in a live event

How to stream a presentation or slideshow in the Web-based production tool

The web-based production tool features a Slides function, which lets you or a guest speaker upload slides and navigate through them during a presentation. To do so:

  1. Create your eventor select it from your library.
  2. From the top ‘Go Live’ drop-down menu, choose to stream via your browser to open the web-based production tool.
  3. On the left side toolbar, select Media and the Slidesheader in the expanded Media panel.
  4. Select Upload to upload your presentation file.
  5. Once uploaded, hover over the presentation’s thumbnail image on the media panel and select the plus sign to add it to a scene.
  6. Any speaker added to the scene can navigate through the slide deck using the arrows below the preview player.

Users added to the scene will appear in a picture-in-picture alongside the slide deck. You can hide them by turning off their video feed or selectingControls > Hide speaker, or use the built-in screen-sharing feature to control the screen shared with your audience.

How to stream a presentation or slideshow in Livestream Studio

Livestream Studio offers a few methods to bring your presentation in as a source. To do so, you can use:

  • Remote Guest(Recommended): Send an invite URL to the presenter to open in Google Chrome. They can select Share screen and choose their application window to replace their camera feed.
  • HDMI or Screen Capture: You can connect the presenting computer via HDMI capture or use screen capture on a second monitor if the presentation is controlled from the Studio desktop.

After the presentation is added as an input, you can use the graphics overlay designer to create a picture-in-picture experience. Read more at How to build a Picture-in-Picture Graphic.
