  • Watch Later

Comments

You can leave a comment on any video that has commenting enabled. You can enable or disable commenting on your own videos by navigating to your video, clicking Advanced to go to your advanced settings, then navigating to General> Privacy.

Note: If the video is set to Unlisted or Private, video recipients will see our cleaner recipient video page where the commenting interface varies depending on the video owner’s membership tier.

  • Videos owned by Free, Basic, and Plus members will display a Comments panel on the video page. Video owners currently cannot disable this method of commenting on videos with these privacy settings.
  • Videos owned by Starter, Standard, Advanced, Pro, Business, and Premium members will see a button for the Review Page on these videos. Video owners can choose to disable the review page if they wish.

Enterprise members using our Video Library product see a Comments button on the video page of their Unlisted and Private videos rather than the Review page link. Clicking that button will open the Comments panel along the right-hand side of the page. The comment panel for Enterprise users also supports time-coded notes, similar to review pages, as well as video comments.

You can leave a video comment by including a link to a public Vimeo video in your response, or by clicking the record icon to make a new video which will be embedded into your comment. You can reply to another user’s comment with a link to a public video but you can not record a video response in a reply to another user’s comment.

You can click the options menu (•••) on any comment in this panel to see more options, such as copying a link to that video’s comment to your clipboard (you can also click on a comment to select it, then copy the URL from your browser). This will allow you to send a link to that video with that comment open and highlighted to someone else.

If you’re an Enterprise team owner or a Contributor or Admin team member on an Enterprise team, you can resolve comments left on a video. Please note that if the comment has additional direct replies, resolving the initial comment will also resolve all of the replies. Your viewers can toggle on the option to see any resolved comments, but they won’t be able to interact with them.

If you want to fully remove a comment from your video, you can click the options menu (•••), then click Delete. This will also remove any replies to that comment.

All public and password-protected videos will continue to display the comments as demonstrated below.

If you made a typo while adding a comment, you can edit or delete your comment by hovering over it and clicking “Edit” or “Delete.” You can also remove someone else’s comment on your own video.

Screenshot: The edit and delete options at the top right corner of a comment

You can reply to a comment (or another reply) by clicking “Reply” in the lower right corner of the comment.

HTML won’t work in a comment, but you can share links. You can also use timestamps to send a viewer right to a specific section of your video. For example, writing “2:32” in the description will send a viewer to the two-minute, 32-second mark after the video loads. Please note: timestamps do not work for comments on Vimeo On Demand videos.

The general rule for commenting is simple: be cool and play nice. You are free to disagree and/or provide critical feedback in the comments section of Vimeo, but please keep it respectful. Also, don’t spam, and please be a person (not a robot). Check out our Community Guidelines for more info.

Likes

A Like is a quick and friendly way to let a video creator know that you appreciate, value, or maybe even love their video.

To like a video, just hover your mouse over the video player and click the heart icon in the top right corner. The heart will turn from white to blue to signify that your like has been registered. You can unlike a video by clicking on the heart logo in the top right hand corner of the video again.

It’s not possible to like your own videos.

To see all the videos you’ve liked, hover over your profile image in the top navigation bar and click Likes in the menu.

Please note that you won’t be able to comment or like videos if your profile is in Private Mode.

To access your liked videos on the mobile app, tap your avatar/icon in the top right of your screen, scroll down, and select Likes.

To access your likes on the mobile browser, you must go directly to this link: likes

Watch Later

Watch Later is a handy way to bookmark videos you don’t have time to watch right now. When you click the Watch Later button on any Vimeo player, it will be added to your private Watch Later page which you can access by clicking your avatar in the upper right corner, then click Watch Later. The owner of the video will not be notified when you add their video to your Watch Later queue.

You can remove a video from your Watch Later queue by hovering your cursor over the video player and clicking the Watch Later icon in the upper right corner of the player. To clear all of your Watch Later videos, go to your Watch Later page and click Clear All Videos on the right side of the page.

To access your Watch Later list using the mobile app, tap your avatar/icon in the top right of your screen, scroll down, and select Watch Later.

Download captions or subtitles for On Demand titles

To watch a downloaded VOD title with captions or subtitles, you’ll need to download both the video and the caption files to your computer.

⚠️Note: Not all VODs have caption file downloads enabled.

  • How to download captions or subtitles for On Demand titles
  • What if the VOD does not have a caption or subtitle file available to download?

How to download captions or subtitles for On Demand titles

Follow these steps to download the video and caption files and view them using VLC:

  1. You can download both the video and captions or subtitles of these files by going to the title’s VOD page, then clicking the Download button.
  2. In the window that appears, select the desired video file for download and the desired caption file for download. ⚠️Note: You can also download these files by hovering over the title in your Purchases and clicking the green download icon.
  3. Once you’ve downloaded both files, you’ll need to use them with a media player that supports caption files. We recommend VLC because it is compatible with a wide range of operating systems and file formats. You can download it for free here.
  4. Open the downloaded video file in VLC Media Player.
  5. From the menu, clickSubtitles, then Add Subtitle File.
  6. Select the downloaded .SRT file, click Open, and enjoy!

What if the VOD does not have a caption or subtitle file available to download?

If the caption or subtitle option is not available for the VOD you have purchased, you may contact the seller to request it.

To contact the seller, first log in to your Vimeo account and visit the VOD page. Scroll down and select theMessage button in order to reach the seller.

Screenshot: A VOD page interface showing video details, a mosaic art image, and user profile information. The Message button, located next to the Follow button beneath the user profile, is highlighted by a red arrow.

⚠️Note: You must follow at least one other person on Vimeo to message another user.

FAQ: Vimeo App for Vision Pro

Learn answers to common questions about the Vimeo App for the Vision Pro below.

  • What are the system requirements for the Vimeo app for Vision Pro?

What are the system requirements for the Vimeo app for Vision Pro?

The Vimeo app can be installed on any Vision Pro device running visionOS 1.0 or higher.

Can I upload a video using the Vimeo Vision Pro app?

Yes - you can upload a video using the Vimeo app for Vision Pro. Read how at ‘How do I upload videos on the Vimeo App for Vision Pro?’.

Can I subscribe to Vimeo through the Vision Pro app?

You can create a Basic Vimeo through the Vision Pro app with an email address or your Apple ID by selecting Join Vimeo on the app’s Watch page or Account menu. You can’t subscribe to a paid Vimeo plan through the Vision Pro app. To subscribe to a paid Vimeo subscription plan, visitPricing plans.

Why can’t I see the Library tab?

The Library tab will only display if you’re logged into your Vimeo account. Ensure that you are logged into your Vimeo account on the app.

Can I watch live events or showcases on the Vimeo app for Vision Pro?

No - live events or showcases are not available to watch on the Vimeo app for Vision Pro.

FAQ: Vimeo Staff Picks

This article provides an overview of Staff Picks and information about how they are selected.

What are Staff Picks?

As a Vimeo member, you’re automatically opted in to follow Staff Picks, which is a channel that our Curation team updates every day (Note: You can always unfollow any account on Vimeo). The goal of Staff Picks is to celebrate the best films on Vimeo for our global audiences to enjoy.

If you come across a Staff Pick on Vimeo, it will be indicated with a laurel badge. Screenshot: Circular black badge with laurel wreaths containing the text “Vimeo Staff Pick”

In addition to Staff Picks, you can find Best of the Year and Staff Pick Premieres. Staff Pick Premieres are global online film premieres, featuring a pre-selected Staff Pick each week.

How to find staff-pick videos

Click to find the Staff Pick videos on Vimeo.

Alternatively you can find Staff picks by selecting your profile icon on the top right. Select watchand you will find Staff Picks. Click on the Staff Picks option.

Screenshot: The Vimeo user menu, displaying content links (Staff Picks) and the Dark mode toggle switch.

How can my film become a Staff Pick?

There’s no formal submission process for how to become a staff pick on Vimeo, and any creator can have their video chosen. A good place to start is to make sure that your thumbnail and description are clear and pique a viewer’s interest. You can also seek out appropriate groups and channels to add your video to, and make sure it’s appropriately categorized and tagged as well as rated for content.

Check out these resources to help you improve your chances of being highlighted on Staff Picks:

  • Vimeo Curator Tips: Your Thumbnails and Descriptions
  • A Case Study in Gaining Exposure for your Film

Filter out mature content

When you’re watching videos on vimeo.com, you may see a Mature badge next to the video’s title, right underneath the player. This badge appears because the creator has indicated that the video contains violence, nudity, profanity, and/or illegal substances. If you don’t want mature videos to appear in your search results, you can filter them out.

If you are located in the United Kingdom or European Union and are not logged into a Vimeo account, you will be prompted to log in to watch an unrated video or a video rated Mature on vimeo.com.

Video overview

Here’s a video overview of how to filter out mature content:

Filter out mature videos

You can filter out videos that contain mature or explicit material by following these steps:

  1. Navigate to the Viewing preferences tab in your Account Settings.
  2. Under the Mature content filter, choose between Show me everything, Don’t show mature content, and Let me choose. If you select Let me choose, you can select specific types of content to filter, including unrated videos.
  3. Click Save. Videos with the rating you’ve chosen to filter out will no longer show up in your search results.

Screenshot: Warning icon. Note: If you come across a video that doesn’t match your mature content settings, eg. in a group or channel, the thumbnail of the video will be replaced by a warning. You can either heed this warning or click Show me the video to hide the warning.

Generate Console Logs/HAR Files for Troubleshooting

If you are experiencing technical difficulties using Vimeo in a supported browser, Vimeo Support may request that you attach screenshots or files to help troubleshoot and debug the issue. This may include console logs and HAR files.

  • Console logs help provide insight into how your browser interacts with the code of a webpage.
  • HAR files(HTTP ARchive format files) help provide insight into how your browser interacts with a website on the Network level.

⚠️ Note: HARfiles may contain the content and cookies of any pages you are recording, which may include sensitive information (including, but not limited to: passwords, user IDs, and credit card numbers). Please ensure that you clearany logs before and after capturing the data, as instructed for each browser below.

  • Apple Safari
  • Google Chrome
  • Microsoft Edge
  • Mozilla Firefox

Apple Safari

Console Log:

💡 Tip:By default, Safari hides the Developmenu from the menu bar, which you will need to enable to access the Developer Panel- home of Console. You will need to enable it in your browser if it does not appear in your menu bar.

To show the Develop menu:

  1. From the top menu, click Safariand navigate to the Settings menu (or select ⌘, on the keyboard)
  2. Select the Advancedtab.
  3. Click the checkbox next to Show features for web developersat the bottom of the windowif it is currently not selected.
  4. Exit the Settingsmenu after you’ve confirmed the Develop menu appears in the top bar (between Bookmarksand Window)

To access the Console log:

  1. In Apple Safari, click on the Developmenu
  2. Click on Show Web Inspectorto open the Developer panel.
  3. Click on the Consoletab, and make sure that the Allfilter is selected on the right-hand side of the panel.
  4. Right-click the Consolepanel and select ClearLog to clear any previous logs recorded.
  5. Select the filter icon and select Preserve Log to ensure it’s checked.
  6. Replicate the issue that you faced in the Safari browser. The Consolepanel will record the activity.
  7. Select all (use CTRL+A or CMD+A keyboard shortcuts), then click Save selectedto save as a file on your local drive. You can attach this file to your Vimeo Support ticket if the Support team requests it.
  8. Uncheck the Preserve Logcheckbox, right-click the Consolepanel, and click ClearLog to clear the console activity log from your browser.
HAR file:
  1. Click on the Developmenu in the top menu bar and click Show Web Inspector.
  2. In the Web Inspectorconsole, click the Networktab
  3. Click the garbage canicon on the far right of the Network Panel to clear any previous cache of network items.
  4. Select the filter icon, then select Preserve Log to ensure it’s checked. Screenshot: Safari Web Inspector Network panel showing the filter menu with Preserve Log selected.
  5. Replicate the issue that you faced in the Safari browser.
  6. Click Export at the top-right corner of the Networkpanel to export the HARfile and save it to your local drive. You can attach this file to your Vimeo Support ticket if the Support team requests it.
  7. Uncheck the Preserve Logcheckbox and click the garbage canicon to clear the log from the browser. 💡Tip: The Exportbutton may be hidden if your browser window is too small. If you are unable to see the Exportbutton, resize your browser window to a larger size.

Read about troubleshootingApple Safari at Apple Safari’s Help Center.

Guidelines for determining playback resolution

When you upload or stream a video on Vimeo, your video will be converted to other resolutions to ensure successful playback on different devices and different networks.

The resolutions your video converts to will depend largely on if the larger dimension or the smaller dimension of your source video meets the minimum requirements noted for each resolution below. These conversion specifications apply for videos that you upload as well as videos that were streamed live and archived, although please note that archived live videos will not exceed 1080p60.

Before uploading your video, be sure to check our compression guidelines to ensure it will upload and convert successfully.

Notes for all conversions:

  • The bitrates listed for each resolution are a maximum. This means your video could transcode at a lower bitrate depending on the complexity of the image. For example, a video with a lot of still images will have a lower bitrate than a video with a lot of fast-paced motion.

  • Regarding frame rates:

  • 720p60 and 1080p source files will only receive a 60fps conversion as 720p60 is ubiquitous enough that it should be playable anywhere.

  • Generally, we transcode to 30fps unless otherwise noted.

  • The audio sample rate for all conversions is 48kHz.

  • Resolution

  • Applies to

  • Details

  • 240p

  • Applies to all videos

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: HE-AAC V2 and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 0.3 Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 64 Kbps Maximum height: 240px Maximum width: 426px

  • 360p

  • Applies to all videos

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 0.5 Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 129 Kbps Maximum height: 360px Maximum width: 640px

  • 540p

  • Applies to all videos

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 1.5 Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256 Kbps Maximum height: 540px Maximum width: 960px

  • 720p

  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is at least 1216px OR smaller dimension is at least 684px.

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 2.5 Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256 Kbps Maximum height: 720px Maximum width: 1366px

  • 1080p 60fps

  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is 60FPS, has a higher bitrate, and whose larger dimension is at least 1824px OR smaller dimension is at least 1026px.

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 7 Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256 Kbps Maximum height: 1080px Maximum width: 2048px

  • 2K (30fps and 60fps)

  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is at least 2432px OR smaller dimension is at least 1368px. ⚠️Note : There are many different types of 2K video. Currently, our 2K profile is created for QUAD HD 2K (2560x1440). If your 2K video is DCI 2K (2048x1080), it will transcode up to 1080p, not 2K.

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 12 Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256Kbps Maximum height: 1440px Maximum width: 2732px

  • 4K (30fps and 60fps)

  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is at least 3648px OR smaller dimension is at least 2052px.

  • Video codec: H.264 Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 22Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 265Kbps Maximum height: 2160px Maximum width: 4096px

The following specifications will be used when converting source files that are HDR (such as HDR10 or Dolby Vision) or above 4K.

  • Resolution
  • Applies to
  • Details
  • 240p (HDR/>4K)
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: HE-AAC V2 and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 0.3Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 64Kbps Maximum height: 240px Maximum width: 426px
  • 360p (HDR/>4K)
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 0.5Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 128Kbps Maximum height: 360px Maximum width: 640px
  • 540p (HDR/>4K)
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 1.5Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256Kbps Maximum height: 540px Maximum width: 960px
  • 720p (HDR/>4K)
  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is at least 1216px OR smaller dimension is at least 684px.
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 2.2Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256Kbps Maximum frame rate: 60fps Maximum height: 720px Maximum width: 1366px
  • 1080p (HDR/>4K)
  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is at least 1824px OR smaller dimension is at least 1026px.
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 5Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256Kbps Maximum frame rate: 60fps Maximum height: 1080px Maximum width: 2048px
  • 2K (HDR/>4K)
  • Applies to videos whose source file’s larger dimension is at least 2432px OR smaller dimension is at least 1368px.
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 10Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 265Kbps Maximum frame rate: 60fps Maximum height: 1440px Maximum width: 2732px
  • 4K (HDR/>4K)
  • Applies to videos who source file’s larger dimension is at least 3648px OR smaller dimension is at least 2052px.
  • Video codec: HEVC Audio codec: AAC and Opus Maximum video bitrate: 16Mbps Maximum audio bitrate: 256Kbps Maximum frame rate: 60fps Maximum height: 2160px Maximum width: 4096px

How do I delete the Vimeo Android mobile app?

To delete the app from your Android device, follow the instructions from Google Support at ‘Delete, disable, and manage unused apps on Android’.

To reinstall the app, search for “Vimeo” in the Google Play Store or visit the Vimeo App listing. Read how to install apps on your Android device from Google Support at ‘Download apps to your Android device’.

⚠️Note:The Vimeo app is only supported when downloaded from the Google Play Store. Please exercise caution if downloading apps from unofficial sources.

How do I get support for the Vimeo Android app?

If you need help using the Vimeo Android app, contact our support team.

Please include information about the error or behavior you’re encountering, any troubleshooting steps you’ve taken, and any further details that would help us to troubleshoot.

How do I install the Vimeo app for Android?

The Vimeo Android mobile app is compatible with phones and tablets running Android 8.0 (Oreo) and newer. We do our best to support most Android mobile devices, but due to the open nature of Android, we’re unable to comprehensively test the app in all environments and markets.

  • Install the Vimeo android app
  • Vimeo app languages

Install the Vimeo android app

To install the Vimeo Android app, search for “Vimeo” in the Google Play Store or visit Google Play: Vimeo. The Vimeo app is only supported when downloaded from the Google Play Store. Please exercise caution when downloading apps from unofficial sources.

⚠️Note:

  • Uploading and live streaming from the app requires access to your device’s Storage, Microphone, and Camera. Push notifications must be enabled if you want alerts for new activity on Vimeo.
  • If your device connects to the internet through a VPN, proxy, or bonded internet connection, or if your device’s connection is routed through a content filtering service from your internet provider, the app may not be able to reliably connect to our servers. For a reliable experience, temporarily disable the service while using the Vimeo app.

To delete the app, follow the instructions outlined in the ‘Delete the Vimeo Android mobile app’ Help Center article.

Vimeo app languages

The Vimeo app is currently localized and translated into English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. The app will detect your device’s default language and will use one of these languages; it is not possible to manually select a preferred language within the app. If your preferred language is not available the app will default to English.

How do I install/uninstall the Vimeo app for Vision Pro?

The Vimeo app for Vision Pro can be downloaded from the App Store.

To install the Vimeo app for Vision Pro:

  1. Wear the Vision Pro. 💡Tip:For safety details about the Vision Pro, visit Apple Support at ‘Important safety information for Apple Vision Pro’.
  2. Access the App Store on Vision Pro.
  3. Download and install the Vimeo app.
  4. Open the app and log in to your Vimeo account, or register for a new one.

To uninstall the Vimeo app for Vision Pro:

Read about deleting or arranging apps on the Vision Pro from Apple Support at ‘Arrange or delete apps on Apple Vision Pro’.

How to @mention someone in a comment

You can use @mentions to notify other users within a comment. Read on to learn how to @mention someone and for additional information about how @mentions work on Vimeo.

  • How to use @mentions
  • How do @mentions work for Viewers?
  • How do @mentions work for Collaborators?
  • What happens if a user is @mentioned?

How to use @mentions

  1. Navigate to the comments panel by selecting theCommentsbutton or scrolling below the video player.
  2. In the comment text box, type the “**@**” symbol and at least one character to see the selectable user to auto-fill.
  3. Once you have found the user you would like to@mention, select their name and then type the rest of your comment.
  4. SelectPost to leave your comment on the video.

How do @mentions work for Viewers?

  • Viewers who are on a team can @mention other members of their team.
  • Viewers who are not on a team can @mention other users who have already commented.

How do @mentions work for Collaborators?

  • Team members can @mention other team members.
  • Guest members can @mention other users who have already commented. They can use @mentions in comments via a Review link or an Unlisted video link.

What happens if a user is @mentioned?

If a logged-inuser is @mentioned, they receive an email,bell, andpush notification (if enabled on mobile) from which they can click through to arrive at the video with the commenting panel opened and the relevant comment highlighted.

If aguestuser is @mentioned, they receive an email notification from which they can click through to arrive at the video with the commenting panel opened and the relevant comment highlighted.

How to access transcripts on the video page

While viewing a video on vimeo, you will see the Transcript button below the video player as long as the video owner has enabled a transcript.

How to navigate the transcript panel

To navigate the transcript panel:

  1. Select theTranscriptbutton on the player to view the entire video transcript in a panel to the right of the video player. If you don’t see this option, the video does not contain a transcript.

  3. You can click through the transcript to jump to specific timestamps within the video.
  4. Select the magnifying glass icon to search for specific words and find relevant sections within the video.
  5. If you scroll away from the currently playing section in the transcript, the Return to current timebutton will appear to bring you back to the current point in the video.

How to customize transcript settings

Transcript language

  • You can change the language of the transcript if multiple languages are available. Select the settingsmenu at the top right of the transcript menu to find additional languages.

Display timestamps

  • From thesettingsmenu, you can also choose to show or hide timestamps next to the transcript.

How to cast videos via AirPlay or Chromecast

You can cast videos to your Apple AirPlay or Google Chromecast-equipped TV or TV device by using the Vimeo app for iPhone, iPad, or Android mobile devices. Chromecast is also supported in embedded players in web browsers.

How to use DVR when watching a live event

If you are late to attend a live event, missed critical information, or need a break, you can use DVR to rewatch the live event while it is still streaming.

Note:This feature will not be available if the event host has turned off the DVR feature.

To watch an event using DVR:

  1. Go to the live event player.
  2. There are two ways you can view an earlier time of the live event:
  • Use your cursor to click or scrub back to an earlier time on the player timeline.
  • If the event has auto-generated captions, select the Transcript icon on the player to open the transcript drawer. Scroll back and click on the part of the transcript you want to watch. Playback will start from that time in the live event.
  1. When playback of the earlier content starts, you will see a Skip to live button on the top left corner of the player. Click this to jump to the currently live content.

Additional information:

  • If you are watching a long event, you will only be able to scrub back to the most recent four hours of the live broadcast to watch in DVR mode. Contact the event organizer if you would like to see a recording of the full event after it ends.
  • When you watch an event in DVR mode, you can adjust the playback speed by clicking on the gearwheel icon on the player and selecting Speed.
  • If you select the speed to be slower, the player speed will reduce. After it adjusts the speed, you will see the Skip to live button.
  • After you have scrubbed back, you can select the speed to be faster. It will revert to normal speed if you catch up to the live event’s current content.
  • If you see a notification in the player that the live broadcast has ended while watching in DVR mode, you can continue watching the event so that you don’t miss the ending.

How to watch 360 videos

This article explores how to watch and interact with 360 videos on Vimeo.

You can watch 360 videos on Vimeo on your desktop and mobile devices. Next to every 360 video’s title on vimeo.com, a 360 badge will appear. For example, thiscollection of 360 videos was handpicked by our curation team.

Visit System Requirements for viewing, browsing, and apps to learn our minimum requirements for playing videos across our website, iOS app, and Android apps.

  • 360 vs. VR
  • Watching 360 videos on a desktop device
  • Watching 360 videos on a mobile device
  • Vive Video and Vimeo

360 vs. VR

Vimeo supports 360 video (monoscopic and stereoscopic), not true VR. While the terms are often used interchangeably, 360 video and VR are considered two different experiences.

  • A 360 videois recorded from all angles using a special rig of multiple cameras or one omnidirectional camera. Users can dictate the direction or view of the video based on a central point in space, dictated by the camera.
  • VR (virtual reality) refers to a simulated digital environment in which a user can physically move around and interact using equipment such as a headset and body gear. Users can navigate, control, and influence the environment beyond their line of sight.

Vimeo supports both monoscopic and stereoscopic 360 video. Vimeo does not support mobile headset viewing for 360 videos in the Vimeo App (iOS or Android).

Watching 360 videos on a desktop device

On a desktop, you can explore a 360 video with your arrow keys, mouse, or trackpad. On the right side of the player, you’ll see a compass that indicates the direction you are facing in the video. Selecting the compass will reorient you to the original positioning of the video.

Watching 360 videos on a mobile device

You can watch 360 videos with the Vimeo app on Android and iOS.

Gyroscopic 360 playback is only on Android devices with gyroscopic sensors; the iOS app doesn’t support this.

On devices without a gyroscopic sensor or on the Vimeo iOS app, 360 videos won’t display in 360 degrees and will appear flat, requiring manual panning during playback. Vimeo doesn’t support mobile headset viewing on either platform.

Vive Video and Vimeo

Vive supports curated Vimeo content on their Vive Video app, which means that staff-picked Vimeo videos are available to watch on Vive and Oculus headsets. You can download the app on Steam and Viveport to discover staff-picked videos.

Inline playback on mobile

Learn more about Vimeo ending support for Internet Explorer

Vimeo has discontinued support for Internet Explorer due to its technical limitations and lack of modern features. In addition, Microsoft is ending support of their Internet Explorer desktop app in favor of Microsoft Edge. If you are attempting to access Vimeo.com while using Internet Explorer, we recommend switching to a supported browser, such as Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, or Mozilla Firefox.

  • How to switch browsers
  • What if my organization uses Internet Explorer?

How to switch browsers

If you don’t yet have another browser installed on your computer, you can click one of the links below to safely download and install a new browser:

  • Microsoft Edge
  • Google Chrome
  • Mozilla Firefox

Once you have successfully installed a new browser, you will be able to access Vimeo.com without any limitations.

What if my organization uses Internet Explorer?

Network and browser requirements for watching live events

This article discusses the minimum network and browser requirements for viewing live events on Vimeo, including recommended download speeds, compatible browsers, and firewall settings.

  • Download speeds
  • Desktop OS and browser
  • Supported mobile devices
  • Whitelisted domains and firewall ports

Download speeds

The quality of your live playback experience relies mainly on your Internet Service Provider (ISP) or mobile provider’s download speed. Please note that various factors can affect your overall internet speed.

The minimum speeds required for each playback quality are detailed in the table below:

  • Playback quality
  • Required Minimum Bandwidth
  • 240p
  • 500 kbps
  • 360p
  • 1 Mbps
  • 720p
  • 3 Mbps
  • 1080p
  • 7 Mbps
  • 2K
  • 12 Mbps
  • 4K & up
  • 22 Mbps

Desktop OS and browsers

We recommend using the following browsers and versions on Windows 7 or later, or macOS Sierra (10.12.6) or later:

  • Chrome 30+ (has automatic updates)
  • Firefox 27+ (has automatic updates)*
  • Microsoft Edge
  • Safari 9+

*H.264 video (required for viewing Vimeo videos) is only supported in Firefox for Windows 7 and later. Firefox versions on Windows XP are no longer supported for playback.

Supported mobile devices

  • Mobile viewers require a device running at least Android version 5.0 (Lollipop) or higher, or iOS version 12.4 or higher, to watch live events.
  • While live events on Vimeo may be viewable on Blackberry and Windows phones that support HTML5, we do not test our player in these environments and therefore cannot guarantee support.
  • The Samsung Internet browser (all versions) is not supported for live events on Vimeo. We recommend using a compatible browser instead.

Whitelisted domains and firewall ports

Viewers should ensure the following ports are open on their network for playback:

  • TCP/UDP 80 (HTTP)
  • TCP/UDP 443 (HTTPS)

Additionally, these domains should be whitelisted if you are on a network that may restrict access to websites or domains:

  • *.vimeo.com
  • *.vimeocdn.com
  • *.magisto.com
  • *.akamaized.net
  • *.cloudfront.net

Participate in a live event chat, poll, or Q&A session

When watching a live event, you may be allowed to participate in a live chat, a poll, or a Q&A session on the event page. In this article, we will outline what to expect and how to use each of these features as a viewer. Keep in mind there is no guarantee you will always see these features used as they are enabled and controlled by the event’s organizer.

  • Chat
  • Q&A
  • Poll

Chat

If the event’s organizer enabled chat, you would see a chat icon to the right of the video player on the desktop, below the player if you are viewing on a mobile browser, or at the bottom of the engagement tools modal window if you’re watching the event on a website other than Vimeo.

⚠️Note: If you are prompted to enter a password upon opening the event player or the chat embed window and you do not know the password, please contact the event organizer.

This is the event page on Vimeo with the chat enabled on a desktop browser.

Screenshot: Vimeo event page on a desktop browser displaying a video player with a central ‘E’ avatar. A red box highlights the Chat bubble icon located in the top right corner of the page.

This is the event page on Vimeo with chat enabled when watching on a mobile browser:

Screenshot: Vimeo event page on a mobile interface showing a live video of a hockey player. The interface includes a ‘Live’ badge in the top left and a ‘Chat’ tab active below the video player.

If you are watching an event on the organizer’s website, you may also see the chat embedded near the player.

If you are logged into a Vimeo account (or registered if the event is a webinar), you will automatically be logged into the chat and can open the chat panel to start posting messages or emojis. You can also paste links in the chat box, which will show up as hyperlinks and are clickable.

If you are not logged in you wish to participate, you must enter your name; if the event is a webinar, you may be prompted to re-enter your email address. By entering your name or email to join the chat, you accept Vimeo’s Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy before selecting Join.

Screenshot: Join to interact’ screen prompting the user to enter a name to chat. The ‘Name’ input field is filled with the text ‘Alex Doe’. Below are buttons to ‘Join’ or ‘Log in with Vimeo’

You can then type in your message or emojis and either press the Enter/Return key on your keyboard to send, or click the send button to the right to send your chat message, which may be up to 280 characters long. Your messages will appear on the right side of the chat window whereas others’ messages will appear alongside their names on the left side.

Screenshot: Chat sidebar interface. Messages from users ‘Steve’ and ‘Jay’ are visible. A navigation rail on the right displays icons for Chat, Polls, and Q&A

You can close the chat window at any time by clicking the X in the upper right corner. Closing the chat box will show only a chat bubble icon next to the player. This icon will display a red indicator when it’s first enabled or if there is new activity in the chat, such as new messages being posted.

Screenshot: Speech bubble with a small, red notification dot.

If you close the panel, you can re-open the chat window by clicking the chat bubble icon.

Note that the event chat is moderated by the event’s producer, who can delete or block comments from anyone. Also, chat is available in place of commenting until the stream ends.

You can also participate in chat if you are watching on the Vimeo mobile app provided that you are logged into a Vimeo account.

  • Once you locate the event in the app, open the event page and make sure you have the Chat tab toggled.
  • You can then send messages and see all the other messages others have posted in real-time (unless the owner disabled chat, in which case you will see a message indicating that chat is disabled).
  • Note that you will need to keep your device in portrait orientation as the chat will not be available in fullscreen/landscape mode.

Currently, some privacy settings on events will redirect you to the event’s page on vimeo.com on a mobile browser rather than the app.

Q&A

If the nature of the event involves answering questions from viewers, the event organizer may utilize our Q&A (Question and Answer) feature. When this feature is turned on, you and other viewers will see the Q&A icon appear with a notification indicator on the event page or embedded engagement tools; click the icon to participate.

Screenshot: Sidebar menu with a red box highlighting the ‘Q&A’ icon. It is shaped like a speech bubble and displays a small, red notification dot.

Toggle on the Anonymous switch if you don’t want your name displayed next to the question (note that the event organizer may choose to not enable this option).

Screenshot: Q&A panel featuring a text input field with the placeholder ‘Type your question here’. An ‘Anonymous’ toggle switch below the field is set to the ‘On’ position.

You can see your question and all other questions below, either in the order in which they were asked (Recent) or in the order of those with the most votes (Popular).

⚠️Note: The character limit for questions in a Live Q&A is a maximum of 240 characters or 3 lines.

An indicator below the text input box shows the number of characters remaining to the question-askers while typing the questions.

You can vote on any question by clicking the thumbs-up icon next to it.

When the event host is addressing a question, you may see it highlighted in the Q&A panel. You may also see it as a graphic overlay in the video player.

Screenshot: Graphic overlay on top of a video background displaying an anonymous question: “What’s the ETA on that product launch?” The question shows one thumbs-up vote.

The event host can then archive any questions, which will cause them to disappear from the list.

To close the Q&A panel, click the X in the upper right corner of the Q&A window. The Q&A icon will display a red indicator if there is a new activity, such as a new question being posted.

Poll

The event host can use the Polls feature to either get a vote on a topic or quiz their audience. If they do this, you will see the Polls icon appear with a notification indicator on the event page or embedded engagement tools. Select the icon to open the Polls panel.

Screenshot: Sidebar menu with a red box highlighting the ‘Polls’ icon, which displays a small red notification dot.

The polls panel will display the question and 2-4 possible response options (depending on how the event organizer created it). Click on a response to choose one.

Screenshot: Polls panel displaying the question “Which new feature are you most excited about?” followed by a list of four clickable text options: Text-based video editor, AI script generator, Teleprompter, and Record studio .

The event organizer may display the poll in a graphic in the player as well; this is mainly to raise awareness of the poll, as the options in the player cannot be clicked.

Screenshot: Poll results for “Which feature are you most excited about?”: AI script generator and Text based video editor are tied at 50%, while Record studio and Something else are at 0%. They are displayed as bars on a video overlay.

When the event organizer closes the poll and publishes the results, you will see the results in the polls panel; they may also appear in a graphic overlay.

Screenshot: Polls panel displaying results for the question “Which new feature are you most excited about?” Two bars show 50% for ‘AI script generator’ and 50% for ‘Text based video editing’, while other options show 0%.

To close the polls panel, click the X in the upper right corner. You will see a red notification indicator if there is new activity in the Polls panel, such as a new poll being opened.

Purchase On Demand videos with promo codes

If you’ve received a VOD promo code, you can redeem it directly on a title’s Vimeo On Demand page. On the title’s page, click the button for the type of purchase your code is good for (Buy, Rent, or Subscribe). Then, in the purchase window that appears, click Apply promo code, enter the code, and click the Apply button. The purchase window will then update to reflect the discounted price before you finalize the purchase.

A few notes about VOD promo codes:

  • As of September 21, 2026, new Vimeo On Demand purchases are disabled, so promo codes can no longer be redeemed. Access to previously purchased titles ends on November 20, 2026.
  • If your code is for 100% off a video, you’ll need to click “Continue” to complete the transaction.
  • If your code is for a partial discount, then you’ll need to enter valid payment information along with the code to complete the purchase.
  • Please note that currently, dollar-off promo codes can only be applied to VOD purchases made in USD.
  • Additionally, only VIP promo codes are applicable for more than one month of free or discounted viewing for Subscription-VODs. Any other promo code will apply towards the first month of purchase, after which you will be charged the listed price.

Troubleshooting promo codes

If you’re seeing an error message that says “Oops. Something is not right here” when trying to make a Vimeo On Demand purchase, it usually means there’s an issue with your payment method. If you’re still seeing the message after making sure all the information you entered is correct (or if you’re seeing the message with multiple payment methods), please contact us so we can take a look on our end and help you complete the purchase.

If you’re certain that you’re entering the promo code correctly and you’re seeing a message that says “Sorry, that discount code appears to be invalid,” please contact us so we can investigate further (please include the code you’re trying to use in your email).

Purchased VODs FAQ

We’ve compiled a list of the most frequently asked questions and answers about purchased Vimeo On Demand videos here to help you make the most of your VOD experience. You can also find more information regarding purchasing VODs in our Viewer Agreement.

  • How can I switch my purchase type from rent to buy?
  • How can I cancel a recurring VOD subscription?
  • How can I get a refund for a VOD I purchased?
  • Can I use the VOD I purchased for public screenings?
  • I am part of a tax-exempt organization; can you refund the tax on my VOD purchase?
  • What language options are there for On Demand titles?
  • Do VODs expire?

How can I switch my purchase type from rent to buy?

If you rent a title and like it so much that you want to buy it, that’s great! Just contact us and we’ll be happy to help you get that taken care of.

How can I cancel a recurring VOD subscription?

If you need to cancel a recurring VOD subscription, log in to your Vimeo account, then go to yourBilling Settings and choose thePurchases tab. From there, find the title you’d like to unsubscribe from, and click the Unsubscribe link below the renewal date.

How can I get a refund for a VOD I purchased?

For security reasons, we require approval from VOD sellers before granting refunds for VOD purchases. If you’d like to request a refund directly from the seller, follow these steps:

  1. Send the seller a message from the VOD page. To do this, log in to your Vimeo account and visit the VOD page.
  2. Scroll down and find the Message button to reach the seller. Please note that you must follow at least one other person on Vimeo to message another user.
  3. Explain that you were not satisfied with your purchase and that you’d like to request a refund. Let them know that if they wish to grant a refund, we need them to contact us with a) a link to your Vimeo profile, and b) a request to refund your purchase.

Can I use the VOD I purchased for public screenings?

The license issued to you when you rent or buy VOD work is for personal viewing only. It does not allow you to redistribute the work or show it publicly. You can find more information about this in our Payment Addendum.

With that said, you are welcome to reach out to the VOD seller directly to request their permission to share their work in this way. You can contact them by sending a private message through their profile page (please note that you must be following another Vimeo member to use the messaging feature, even if it’s just the seller).

What language options are there for On Demand titles?

Creators can choose to offer their Vimeo On Demand titles in as many languages as they want, so the responsibility falls on them to choose what languages (including captions/subtitles) they offer for their titles.

If a title you want to watch isn’t currently available in your language, feel free to reach out to the creator for more information using the Message button on the title’s Vimeo On Demand page.

Do VODs expire?

If you have bought a VOD, and not rented it, you will be able to view it until November 20, 2026. On that date, Vimeo On Demand will be discontinued and access to all purchased VOD titles will end. Before then, if the VOD seller deletes the VOD, you will have 30 days to watch or download the video.

If a VOD seller decides to delete their content or leaves Vimeo, you will have 30 days to back up your purchase. After 30 days, you won’t see a deleted VOD title in your purchases anymore. If you rented a VOD that gets deleted, you will have the entire rental period to view it.

Remove unwanted black bars in the player

Letterboxing is when black bars appear at the bottom and top of your video. Pillarboxing is when black bars appear on the left and right sides of your video. Read on to learn how to remove unwanted black areas.

  • Pillarboxing on vimeo.com clip page
  • How to remove unwanted black bars

Pillarboxing on vimeo.com clip page

If you notice what appears to be pillarboxing when you visit your video’s clip page on vimeo.com, note that this page’s design includes black on either side of the player. The screenshot below includes a video uploaded with a 16:9 aspect ratio; the black on either side is not from the video itself, it’s from the page design.

Screenshot: Vimeo clip page showing a 16:9 video with black areas on the left and right, illustrating pillarboxing.

You can confirm whether the black bars exist in your video by checking the video’s edit page from your Library or by checking the embedded player. If you see black bars in either of those environments, then the pillar or letter bars exist either within your video or due to your video’s aspect ratio in comparison to the player.

How to remove unwanted black bars

To remove unwanted letterboxing or pillar bars, try the following:

  • First, double-check the original source file for letterboxing or pillar bars. Vimeo does not automatically remove hard-coded black bars from uploaded videos. If the source is letterboxed or pillarboxed, you can fix it by cropping or reformatting the file in a video editing program.
  • If it’s due to the video’s aspect ratio, choose the embedded player size that matches the video’s native aspect ratio.
  • Check the video thumbnail. If you’re uploading a custom thumbnail image, make sure it does not include black bars. If your thumbnail does not contain black bars, make sure that the aspect ratio of your thumbnail matches the aspect ratio of your original video file. For example, if your video is 16:9, your thumbnail image should also be 16:9.

If you still can’t get rid of unwanted black bars, reach out to our support team for assistance.

System Requirements for viewing, browsing, and apps

This article discusses the supported browsers, operating systems, and app versions required for viewing videos and browsing the Vimeo site.

The Vimeo website and player are supported on the most popular desktop and mobile platforms. We strongly recommend keeping your device’s operating system and browser as up-to-date as possible to avoid any bugs or potential security vulnerabilities.

Below you’ll find our minimum requirements for accessing vimeo.com, playing videos, and using our official apps.

  • Bandwidth requirements - video playback
  • Supported browsers — video playback
  • Supported browsers — vimeo.com site
  • Advanced playback

  • Vimeo macOS app

Bandwidth requirements - video playback

You can view Vimeo videos in quality ranging from 360p to 8K. The following table shows the minimum speeds required for each playback quality:

  • Quality
  • Required Minimum Bandwidth
  • 240p

  • 360p
  • 1 Mbps
  • 720p
  • 3 Mbps
  • 1080p

Not sure what speeds your device is receiving? Perform the speed test (on mobile or desktop) for an estimate. We recommend performing this test a few times since bandwidth can change.

For more in-depth information about bandwidth and troubleshooting, visit Troubleshoot playback quality and buffering issues.

Supported browsers — video playback

Vimeo playback is supported in browsers that can decode H.264 videos in an HTML5 player.

The following browsers have guaranteed support:

  • Browser
  • Versions
  • Chrome
  • Current and two previous major versions
  • Edge
  • Current and two previous major versions
  • Firefox

Supported browsers — vimeo.com site

The vimeo.com website and all features on the website are supported when using the latest versions of these browsers:
