If you see a banner on vimeo.com asking you to upgrade your browser, you can check for the latest versionhere.

Advanced playback

5K, 6K, 7K, or 8K playback

To view our higher-resolution playback versions, you must use a browser that supports H.265 (HEVC) decoding in an HTML5 player.

These operating systems and browsers currently support the playback of videos with resolutions over 5K:

  • Safari 11+ on macOS 10.13 High Sierra or higher
  • Microsoft Edge 15+ on Windows 10 (with supported hardware)

We hope to support 5K and higher resolution playback on additional browsers and platforms as they become available.

HDR and Dolby Vision playback

To view an HDR video, you must have an HDR10-supported display and a system that supports H.265 (HEVC) playback.

HDR and Dolby Vision playback is currently supported on these platforms:

  • Safari 11+ on iPhone 8 and above, and iPad Pro 2nd generation and above
  • Apple TV 4K on tvOS 18+ connected to a display supporting HDR10.
  • Read additional information at About the Apple TV App
  • iOS devices at ’Play and record HDR video on iPhone or iPad’.
  • macOS devices at ‘Play HDR video on Mac’
360° playback

For monoscopic 360° playback on a desktop (i.e, on a monitor and not within a headset), we recommend using the latest version of the following browsers with WebGL and hardware acceleration enabled:

  • Chrome
  • Firefox
  • Edge
  • Safari (v11.0.2 or newer)

Playback of 360 videos on mobile devices is only possible with the official Vimeo app for Android or iOS. Mobile devices must have gyroscope sensors for the app to play 360 videos.

Vimeo mobile app

Native apps are available for mobile phones and tablets running Android and iOS. We recommend keeping your device’s operating system up-to-date. The minimum operating system version for each platform is listed below.

  • Android: Version 8.0 (Oreo)
  • iOS: Version 16.0

Additionally, iPhone 8 and above and 2nd generation iPad Pro and above can playback Dolby Vision videos on the Vimeo app.

Additional permissions may need to be enabled to access all mobile app features. See our Android and iOS mobile app requirement articles for further details.

Vimeo macOS app

The Vimeo macOS app requires macOS 10.12 (Sierra) or newer to operate. Older versions of macOS are not compatible with the app.

Troubleshoot 360 Playback

360 video requires more computer processing power than regular video. Here are some steps you can follow to troubleshoot issues with 360 Playback.

  • Switch quality to “auto”
  • Update browser (Safari)
  • Enable Hardware Acceleration (Chrome)
  • Enable WebGL (Chrome)

Switch quality to “auto”

You may need to switch to one of the lower-quality options for smooth playback on your system. We recommend setting the player to “auto” in the quality menu and viewing from a supported environment.

Update browser (Safari)

If your videos are not playing in 360 within Safari, please make sure you are using version 11.0.2 or higher. Older versions of Safari do not support 360 playback.

Enable Hardware Acceleration (Chrome)

If videos are not playing in 360 within Chrome, it’s likely that WebGL and hardware acceleration are disabled. These browser settings are usually on by default, but if they are disabled for any reason, videos will play as flat instead of in 360.

To enable hardware acceleration, follow these steps:

  1. In the address bar, go to chrome://settings.
  2. Select Systemfrom the panel on the right.
  3. In the System section, ensure Use hardware acceleration when available checkbox is toggled on (you’ll need to relaunch Chrome for any changes to take effect).

Enable WebGL (Chrome)

To enable WebGL, follow these steps:

  1. In the address bar, go to chrome://flags
  2. Ensure that WebGL 2.0 is enabled (you’ll need to relaunch Chrome for any changes to take effect)
  3. If the WebGL setting is missing, try installing a fresh version of Chrome or go to get.webgl for installation instructions.

Troubleshoot audio sync issues

The easiest way to avoid sync issues is to compress your video following our compression guidelines. However, if you continue to encounter issues, here are some common causes and fixes for the loss of audio sync.

  • Out-of-sync source files
  • Variation between decoding technologies
  • Video encoded with variable frame rate
  • Video contains multiple edit list entries
  • Conversion process issues

Out-of-sync source file

If the audio in your source file is out of sync, it will impact the uploaded video. Resolve any pre-existing audio sync issues in your editing software, then re-upload to Vimeo.

Variation between decoding technologies

There may be a slight variation between decoding technologies. Your video may look or sound different across different players and browsers (which is out of Vimeo’s control). To minimize playback variations, make sure your browser is up to date and close any additional programs running on your computer.

Video encoded with a variable frame rate

We recommend that you use a constantframe rate rather than a variable frame rate. Variable frame rates are commonly used in webinars or screencasts.

The video contains multiple edit list entries

This impacts videos edited with QuickTime technology. Use the Export feature instead of Save or Save Aswhen you are saving your video in QuickTime.

Conversion process issues

In rare cases, our conversion process will sometimes lead to variation between your source file and our playback versions.

To determine if that’s the case, try this test:

  1. Go to your video page.
  2. Download both your source file and the largest HD Vimeo version of your video using the Download button on your video page.
  3. Play both versions of the video in the same program on your computer (e.g., Quicktime, Windows Media Player, or VLC) and make note of whether there’s a difference between the two. If there are no differences, you may be experiencing a decoding issue in your browser.

If you’re not quite sure what’s causing your sync issue, please contact us so we can investigate further. Be sure to provide a link to the video(s) in question and a description of the places in the video where the loss of audio sync is especially apparent.

Troubleshoot color variation

There are many reasons why your video may look different once uploaded to Vimeo. Here are some common causes:

  • Decoding technology
  • Missing color properties
  • Hardware or software issues
  • Conversion process

Decoding technology

The primary cause for color variation is your browser’s decoding technology.

You can determine whether this is the cause by testing your video in different browsers. If the color of your video looks accurate in Safari, but not Firefox, you may be encountering a decoding variation. Unfortunately, Vimeo does not have any control over the decoding of your video.

Missing color properties

Another potential cause for color variation in your video is when one or more of thecolor propertiesare missing.

Color properties–color space, color range, color primaries, transfer characteristics, and matrix coefficients–are controlled by your editing software.

If any color properties such as Primaries, Transfer, or Matrix, are marked as “Unknown”, this may cause unexpected color variation in the uploaded video.

You will need to re-export your video file with these properties so that it can be encoded with the correct color variation.

Hardware or software issues

The viewer’s hardware (monitor, graphics card, etc.) and software play a big role in the viewer’s playback experience. Try testing your video on different setups and take note of the differences in color (if any).

Conversion process

In rare cases, our conversion process will lead to variations between your source file and our playback versions.

To test whether this is the case, follow these steps:

  1. Go to yourLibrary and then select your video.
  2. Use the Download button to download both your source file and the largest HD Vimeo version of your video.
  3. Compare the two versions of the video by playing them in the same program on your computer (e.g., Quicktime, Windows Media Player, or VLC).
  4. If you see any differences in color when comparing the videos, pleasecontact us and provide the following information:

Troubleshoot playback quality and buffering issues

If you’re having trouble viewing a video, such as frequent buffering, low video quality, or dropped frames, you should try some basic troubleshooting. This might involve adjusting your browser settings or checking your network connection. This article covers different ways to troubleshoot these issues.

  • What is causing poor playback and buffering?
  • How to fix playback quality and buffering issues?
  • How to check the bandwidth and the source file?
  • How to send debug results to Vimeo for analysis?

What is causing poor playback and buffering?

These are the most common reasons you may experience poor playback quality or buffering.

  • Insufficient bandwidth: Your current internet download speed (bandwidth) is not fast enough to support the selected video quality, causing the player to stop and buffer frequently. The Vimeo player requires network speeds of 500 kbps or higher to stream the lowest quality (240p).
  • Device processing limitations: Your computer or device may be unable to keep up with the video data transfer, leading to dropped frames (skipped video frames) and potential audio sync issues, especially if multiple applications or tabs are running.
  • Interference: Interference with the video player’s performance can result from outdated browser software, an old cache, or browser extensions.

How to fix playback quality and buffering issues?

Basic Troubleshooting Steps

These initial steps can often resolve temporary connectivity or browser issues:

  • Disable any browser extensions, plugins, or add-ons.
  • Third-party programs can sometimes cause issues during playback. Try disabling any active extensions one by one to find the culprit, or open the video in an incognito or private window for testing.
  • Restart your router and modem.
  • Try disconnecting the power cord and then reconnecting it to perform a hard reboot and refresh your connection.
  • Update your browser.
  • Make sure you are using the latest version of your browser for peak performance.
  • Close excess browser tabs or applications.
  • Keeping too many applications open can make everything run slower, especially video playback.
  • Clear your browser’s cache.
  • Refreshing your browser’s cache can help with different audio and video issues, including playback. Learn how to reset your browser’s cache for
  • Apple Safari
  • Google Chrome
  • Microsoft Edge
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Try disabling/Enabling Hardware acceleration.
  • Try changing this option within your browser settings, as it sometimes conflicts with older graphics cards.
Check Player Quality Settings

To fix frequent buffering or low-quality video:

  1. From the video player, select the gear icon in the lower right corner.
  2. Ensure the quality is set to Auto.
  • When in Auto mode, the Vimeo player will automatically adjust to the best quality of video for your current Internet connection and processing speed. This is the recommended default setting.
  • If Auto is not available, switch to one of the lower quality options (e.g., 540p or 360p). The video should start playing at a quality that your connection can support, reducing buffering.

How to check the bandwidth and the source file?

To fix unexpected low quality or buffering:

  1. Check your bandwidth with an online speed test.
  • We recommend using trusted HTML5 tests likedownload to get an estimate of your download speed.
  • If your speed is consistently low, we recommend getting in touch with your Internet Provider for more information.
  1. Check your source file (if you are the uploader).
  • If there are any quality issues visible in your source video, try re-exporting the file at a higher quality and re-uploading to Vimeo, as small issues can become amplified during compression.

How to send debug results to Vimeo for analysis?

To fix persistent, hard-to-diagnose issues or dropped frames, contact our Support team and be sure to include the following information:

  • Detailed description of the problem you’re experiencing (e.g., buffering, dropped frames).
  • Your results from this speed test:download
  • The URL of the page where your videos are embedded, including any necessary login credentials (if applicable).
  • The Debug Key/Payload associated with your playback session.
To get the Debug Key:
  • Desktop browser:
  1. Open any video you’re having trouble with, press play, and watch the video.
  2. Once the issue occurs, press “d” on your keyboard to open the debug panel.
  3. Click the blue Copy Debug Key button to obtain the unique ID associated with your playback session.

⚠️Note:If you aren’t seeing the option to copy a debug key, please make sure that your browser is not sending a “do not track” request.

  • Mobile browser (If the playbar is enabled):
  1. Start watching the video and wait for the issue to occur.
  2. Tap the playbar settings gear icon.
  3. Tap the small (i) icon.
  4. Tap Copy Debug Payload to paste the debug ID to your device’s clipboard.

Once you’ve copied the debug information, paste the entire key into your support ticket and send it our way for analysis.

⚠️Note:The debug key will be comprised of random characters, which will then be used to access playback information in our system.

Once you’ve gathered this information, contact us, and we’ll look into your issue.

Troubleshoot: Fullscreen button missing from the player

If the option to view a video in full-screen mode is missing from the player, it indicates that full-screen is unavailable. This article outlines the potential ways to resolve this issue.

  • Check player settings in Vimeo
  • Check the embedded code
  • Check for nested iframes or frames
  • Check for site-level overrides (no-fullscreen-support)

Check player settings in Vimeo

  1. Go to your Library, select the video, and navigate to the Appearance tab.
  2. Ensure the Full-screen button is toggled on under the Controls section.

Check the embedded code

The iframe embed code might be missing necessary fullscreen attributes.

  • Check if the following attributes are present in your iframe tag: mozallowfullscreen,webkitallowfullscreen, and allowfullscreen.
  • If you are pasting the embed code into another application, ensure these attributes are retained.

Example embed code

Check for nested iframes or frames

  • Nested Iframes:
  • The player iframe is contained within another iframe that is missing the fullscreen attributes (mozallowfullscreen,webkitallowfullscreen,allowfullscreen). Browsers prevent nested iframes from entering full-screen without these attributes on the container.
  • Try inserting the player outside of the container iframe or add the fullscreen attributes to the container iframe.
  • Frame Elements:
  • The iframe is contained within a element. Frame elements, and any iframes inside them, cannot enter full screen.
  • We recommend removing all tags from your page’s source code.

Check for site-level overrides (no-fullscreen-support)

  • Inspect the embedded site and search for the parameter ‘no-fullscreen-support’ in the browser’s Elements tab.
  • If this tag is present, it overrides the Fullscreen attribute. The user must contact the site developer to resolve this issue.

If you’ve checked all the steps above and are still experiencing the issue, pleasecontact us, and we will investigate further. Be sure to include a link to the page where the video is embedded so we can examine the page’s source code.

Troubleshooting: “Sorry, we couldn’t find that page”

If you followed a Vimeo link and landed on an error page displaying: “Sorry, we couldn’t find that page”instead of the video, it usually means the video can’t be shown at that address. Work through the checks below, most of the time the cause is a privacy setting, and there’s a quick fix.

1. Privacy settings (the most common cause)

Most error pages come from a video whose privacy settings don’t allow you to watch it from where you are, or with the account you’re using. Match your situation below.

Private video:access is limited to specific people

If you’re the viewer:

  • The owner has to add your email address to the video from Vimeo. Ask them to do this if they haven’t.
  • Make sure you’re logged in to the exact Vimeo account (email) the video was shared with, not a different or personal account.

If you’re the owner:

  • Open the video → Settings → Privacy, and add the viewer’s email under the people allowed to watch.
  • Confirm you shared the link with the same email you added.
Embed only: the video plays only when embedded

If you’re the viewer:

  • This video is set to play only inside a website where it’s embedded, not on its direct vimeo.com link. Watch it on the page where it was embedded instead of opening the raw link.

If you’re the owner:

  • If viewers should be able to open the direct link, change the privacy from “Embed only” to a setting that allows viewing on Vimeo (e.g. Unlisted or Public).
“My company only”: restricted to your organization

If you’re the viewer:

  • Make sure you’re logged in with your corporate email, the one tied to your company’s Vimeo organization. A personal account won’t have access.

If you’re the owner:

  • Confirm the viewer is a member of your Vimeo organization. If they’re external, either add them or switch the video to a privacy setting that allows people outside the company.

2. Other common causes

The video was deleted
  • Viewer: If the video was removed, the link will no longer work for anyone. Ask the owner whether it still exists or was re-uploaded elsewhere.
  • Owner: Deleted videos can’t be recovered from the link. If it was removed by mistake, re-upload it and share the new link.
The link is incomplete or mistyped
  • Viewer: Some links include an extra code (for example, an unlisted video needs its full link). Re-copy the complete, original link and make sure no characters are missing.
  • Owner: Share the full link straight from Vimeo’s share panel rather than typing or editing it by hand.
Region or country restriction
  • Viewer: The owner may allow playback only in certain regions. If you’re travelling or on a VPN, try again from an allowed location.
  • Owner: Check Settings → Privacy for any geo-restrictions and adjust them if viewers in that region should have access.
The link is old or has changed
  • Viewer: Links shared long ago may no longer point to the right place. Ask the owner for the current link.
  • Owner: If the video was moved or its address changed, re-share the up-to-date link.

Still stuck?

Quick checks for viewers:confirm you’re logged in to the right account, try a different browser or device, and ask the owner to re-share the link.

Owners:if the privacy settings look correct and viewers still can’t watch, contact Vimeo Support with the video link and the viewer’s email.

Troubleshooting: I can’t access a VOD title

There are several reasons why you might be having trouble accessing a Vimeo On Demand title. This article contains information about some restrictions as well as troubleshooting steps.

  • Why am I unable to access a VOD title?
  • Location restrictions
  • Streaming restrictions
  • Device amount restrictions
  • How to fix a device limit error

Why am I unable to access a VOD title?

These are the most common reasons you may be unable to access a VOD title:

Location restrictions

Some titles may have different distribution agreements for different global regions. For this reason, some of the titles on vimeo.com/ondemand are only available for purchase in certain countries.

If the title you want to watch isn’t currently available in your region, you’re welcome to reach out to the creator for more information (via the Message button on the title’s Vimeo On Demand page). They may be able to tell you where you can watch it in your country.

Streaming restrictions

Some Vimeo On Demand titles can only be viewed on one device at a time. There are also limits on how many different titles can be streamed concurrently on different devices. If you encounter the Stream limit: Too many streams are open at once error in the player, reduce the number of simultaneous streams occurring on your account.

Device amount restrictions

If you see the error message Device limit: You’ve reached the maximum number of authorized devices, you will need to deauthorize one of your current devices to authorize the new one.

How to fix a device limit error

Follow the steps below to deauthorize a device:

  1. Visit My Settings on Vimeo
  2. Authorized devices will appear at the bottom of this page
  3. Click the green button next to the authorized device you want to remove
  4. Now you’ll be able to authorize a new device

Please be aware that you can only deauthorize up to two devices within 90 days.

Troubleshooting: “This video is not available in your region”

If you encounter a message stating “This video is not available in your region”, it indicates that the video publisher or event host has applied regional restrictions to the content.

Screenshot: Black video player screen displaying the white text error message: “This video is not available in your region”.

This restriction prevents viewers in certain geographic locations from accessing the video or event.

Publishers and hosts use this feature for various reasons, including licensing agreements and legal requirements.

If you have questions about why a video or event is unavailable in your region, please contact the video publisher or event host directly.

Video owners and event hosts on Vimeo Enterprise accounts can read about restricting videos and events by region at the following articles:

  • How do I set regional availability for my video?
  • How do I set regional availability for my live event?

Viewer features available on the Vimeo app for Android

  • Watch and Search
  • Offline playlist
  • Content viewing preferences
  • 360/VR video playback
  • Live event playback and chat

Watch and Search

Your Feed and Staff Picks are available on the Watch tab of the app. Your “watch later” videos can be found in the app settings.

Users, channels, and videos that are public on vimeo.com as well as your videos, can be searched for and played using the app. If you have access to another user’s password-protected or unlisted video, it can be played in the app when opened from a link on the web or when the video is saved to your Watch Later queue.

Offline playlist

Spending time on the subway, on an airplane, or somewhere with limited internet access? You can save videos to an offline playlist and watch those videos when no internet connection is available. Any video that can be played back in the app can be saved to the offline playlist.

To save a video to your offline playlist, tap the icon in the upper right corner while the video is playing, or select Save video offline from the [•••] menu.

To access the offline videos, select the profile picture at the top right corner of the app and scroll down to ‘Library’, and select Offline videos.

Videos saved to the offline playlist can only be played within the Vimeo app and cannot be exported or played in other apps.

Content viewing preferences

The Vimeo app will respect your content viewing preferences while logged into your account. If you have set your preferences to hide certain content, those videos will be omitted from parts of the app, or displayed with a generic thumbnail; this includes videos on your own account.

To update your content viewing preferences within the app, tap your profile picture at the top corner of the app, then tap Account settings > Viewing preferences.

If you use the app without logging into an account, only content rated “All Audiences” will appear. Unrated content and videos marked “Mature” will be omitted or will display a generic thumbnail.

360/VR video playback

Videos marked 360 can be played and explored using the app. Read more about watching 360 videos at ‘Watch 360 videos.’

Live event playback and chat

Viewers can watch your live event on Vimeo and participate in the chat.

Watch videos above 4K (5K, 6K, 7K, 8K)

Videos beyond 4K will be delivered using the HEVC (H.265) video codec. Since support for HEVC playback only exists for newer generation devices and platforms, you’ll need to view them from specific hardware and software to view video qualities beyond 4K (e.g 5K, 6K, 8K). Note that we will only generate a 5-8K transcode if the creator uploaded it as an HDR video that has greater than 5K resolution.

  • Supported browsers
  • Supported operating systems
  • Offline viewing

Supported browsers

  • Safari 11+
  • Microsoft Edge 15+ (with supported hardware)
  • Note: Chromium versions of Edge do not support above 4K

Supported operating systems:

  • MacOS 10.13 High Sierra
  • Windows 10

The following viewing environments arenotcurrently supported for playback above 4K:

  • Mobile devices- iOS and Android (includes the Vimeo app and mobile browsers)

The following may be used while casting to TVs supporting 4K+ via Apple AirPlay and Google Chromecast:

  • Chrome
  • Firefox
  • Opera
  • iOS and Android (including the Vimeo app and mobile browsers)

💡Tip:For best results, TVs should be using the highest possible stream quality.

Offline viewing

If the content owner enables downloading, all playback versions will be available for download on desktop (in all browsers). To view it on your computer, you’ll need to use a player that supports HEVC playback. We recommend using the latest version of VLC media player.

Watching HDR and Dolby Vision Videos

HDR videos will be marked with an HDR badge in the player or on the video page. Videos created and uploaded in Dolby Vision will be marked with a Dolby Vision badge.

⚠️Note: Due to the many layers of transcoding that take place with HDR formats such as Dolby Vision, lower qualities of a video will be available first while additional transcoding takes place in the background. If you are uploading HDR10, HDR10+, or Dolby Vision videos, be sure to allow extra time for all of the renditions to be available.

  • Supported Viewing Environments
  • Supported Browsers
  • Supported Devices
  • Supported Operating Systems
  • Vimeo Mobile App

Supported Viewing Environments

HDR and Dolby Vision videos should be playable as long as HEVC is available and you have a compatible display. Check this site to verify if your browser supports HEVC: hevc.

If you view from an environment that does not support HDR10, HDR10+, or Dolby Vision, we’ll automatically default to standard SDR playback.

If your display supports HDR and has HDR enabled, you can view HDR renditions, regardless of the HDR type. If your display does not support dynamic HDR or does not support the same version as the video, it will be displayed using static HDR metadata.

Supported Browsers

  • Safari 14+ (iOS or macOS Big Sur only)
  • Supported Mac devices are listed by Apple at: Play HDR video on Mac
  • Chrome (HEVC, not Dolby Vision)
  • Edge (HEVC, not Dolby Vision)
  • Opera (HEVC, not Dolby Vision)

Supported Devices

  • Apple TV 4K and above (connected to an HDR10-supported TV or monitor, using the Vimeo Apple TV App, or while being cast to).
  • iPhone 8 and above
  • iPad Pro 2nd generation and above
  • A complete iOS device list from Apple can be found at ‘Play and record HDR video on iPhone or iPad’
  • Samsung Android (HDR10+)

Supported Operating Systems

  • iOS 11+/tvOS 18+
  • macOS Big Sur (11.1 and above)
  • Windows 10+

Note:This list will continue to grow as the video market continues to adopt HDR and HDR formats such as Dolby Vision.

Vimeo Mobile App

Dolby Vision and HDR10 playback are available in the Vimeo mobile app for iOS and Android.

What are the creator features on the Vimeo Android app?

The Vimeo Android app features a range of creator tools, some of which require a paid plan.

  • Analytics overview
  • Video-specific Analytics
  • Publishing to Social
  • Uploading and Trimming
  • Recording
  • Live Streaming
  • Showcases
  • Folder management
  • Team management
  • Creating Videos

Analytics overview

Your account’s analytics information is now also available via the Vimeo Android mobile app. The app provides an overview of your video’s performance for the past 30 days, with a breakdown of ‘Views’, ‘Impressions’, ‘View Rate’, ‘Likes’, and ‘Views by URL’.

Screenshot: Vimeo mobile app displaying the options menu for a video titled “New event”. The “Analytics” option in the menu is highlighted in a red box, and the “Analytics” tab on the bottom navigation bar is also highlighted in a red box.

You can view this Analytics section on your Android mobile app by tapping the ‘Analytics’ tab on the bottom menu of your screen. Once in the Analytics section, you can view the report by scrolling down on your Android mobile device.

Screenshot: Vimeo mobile app “Analytics” dashboard filtered by “All videos” and “Last 7 Days”. The screen displays data cards for Views, Impressions, and View rate, all currently showing zero activity.

Video-specific Analytics

To view the analytics for one of your videos, tap the [•••] menu next to the video you want to view and tap Analytics. Creators can see the video’s Views, Impressions, View rate, Vimeo Likes, and Views by URL for the past 30 days.

Publishing to Social

Creators can publish their videos to Facebook Pages or their YouTube accounts. To do so, tap the [•••] menu next to the video you want to publish, then tap Share > Publish to social, and select the platform where you want your video published.

Uploading and Trimming

Creators can upload videos from their device’s Camera Roll using the iOS app. To do so, tap the (+) icon in the navigation bar, select the video you want to upload, trim the video’s beginning or end if desired, tap Next or Skip, add a name or description, select the video’s privacy settings, and tap Upload.

For a quick and reliable upload, keep the app active and in the foreground while connected to Wi-Fi.

Recording

Creators can record video directly within the Vimeo app. To do so, tap the (+) icon in the navigation bar, tap the Record tab, hold your device horizontally or vertically as desired, and tap the Record button when ready. Tap the record button again when you’re finished.

WARNING: When recording with the app, upon completion your video is uploaded directly to Vimeo, the video will not be saved to your device. If your device has an unreliable internet connection, or if you want to be extra cautious in case anything happens during recording or uploading, we strongly recommend using the default camera app to record and save videos to your device first, then use the Vimeo app to upload.

Live Streaming

Vimeo Advanced, Vimeo Premium, and Vimeo Enterprise members can live stream directly from the app, no other equipment is required. Read about going live from your mobile device at ‘Go live from your mobile device’.

Showcases

Creators can access their Showcases within the app by tapping Home on the navigation bar and scrolling down to Showcases. From there, users can view and edit existing Showcases, and create new Showcases.

Folder management

Creators can view their personal and team Folders by tapping Home on the navigation bar, then tapping View all next to Recent videos, or by clicking the Videos tab in the toolbar at the bottom of the screen.

Creators will also be able to create new folders as well as rename, share, or delete existing folders from their mobile Library.

Team management

Creators can also invite new team members and manage their teams from the Videos tab in the app. To do so, tap either the Home or Videos tab on the navigation bar, then click the downward arrow next to your name to open the team switcher. Here is where you can switch into another team, or tap Manage team to manage your team, such as adding new team members.

Creating Videos

You can create and edit videos on your mobile device in the Vimeo app for Android. Read how at ’How do I make a new video in the Vimeo mobile apps?’

What are the requirements for the Vimeo iOS app?

The Vimeo app is supported on all Apple devices capable of running iOS 16, iPadOS 16, and newer.

Install the Vimeo app for iOS

To install the Vimeo iOS app, search for “Vimeo” in the App Store, or visit ‘Vimeo on the App Store’.

Please note:

  • Uploading and live streaming from the app will require access to your device’s Photos, Microphone, and Camera. Push notification access is also required if you want alerts for new activity on Vimeo.
  • Dark Mode is toggled automatically according to your device’s preferences. Read about Dark Mode from Apple Support at Use Dark Mode on your iPhone and iPad.
  • If your device connects to the internet through a VPN, proxy, or bonded internet connection, or if your device’s connection is routed through a content filtering service from your internet provider, the app may not be able to reliably connect to our servers. For a reliable experience, temporarily disable the service while using the Vimeo app.

To delete the Vimeo iOS app, tap and hold the Vimeo app icon until a menu pops up, then selectDelete app.

To reinstall the app, search for “Vimeo” in the App Store, or visit the Vimeo App listing at Vimeo on the App Store.

Vimeo app languages

The Vimeo app is currently localized and translated into English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish. The app will detect your device’s default language and will use one of these languages. It is not possible to manually select a preferred language within the app. If your preferred language is not available, the app will default to English.

Getting support for the Vimeo iOS app

If you need help with the Vimeo iOS app, please contact our support team.

Creators can record videos directly within the Vimeo app. To do so, tap the (+) icon in the navigation bar, tap the Record tab, hold your device horizontally or vertically as desired, and tap the Record button when ready. Tap the record button again when you’re finished.

WARNING: When recording with the app, upon completion your video is uploaded directly to Vimeo, the video will not be saved to your device’s Camera Roll. If your device has an unreliable internet connection, or if you want to be extra cautious in case anything happens during recording or uploading, we strongly recommend using the default Camera app to record and save videos to your Camera Roll, then use the Vimeo app to upload.

In addition to recording with your camera, the Vimeo iOS app also includes the ability to record your iOS device’s screen. Tap the (+)icon and select Record screen.

You will see a brief tutorial first; swipe through the screens or tap Start recording to go to the record screen. You can choose whether to keep your microphone on or off by tapping the microphone icon toward the bottom of the screen. Tap Start Broadcast and after a short countdown, your screen will begin recording.

A red dot will appear at the top of your device’s screen while you are recording (iPhone 8 and older will see a red bar); tap it to end your recording. You can then go back to the Vimeo app to access, edit, and upload your recording to your Vimeo account.

It’s currently not possible to record both your device’s camera and screen simultaneously due to iOS system limitations.

Live Streaming

Vimeo Premium and Enterprise users can live stream directly from the iOS app, no other equipment required! Learn how to go live from your mobile device at Go live from your mobile device.

Showcases

Creators can access their Showcases within the app by tapping Home on the navigation bar and scrolling down to Showcases. From there, users can view and edit existing Showcases, and create new Showcases. You can also view your Showcases by tapping on the ‘Showcases’ tab at the top of the Manage Videos screen.

While viewing your Showcases, you can click on the three horizontal dots to the right of the Showcase to make adjustments to your Showcase and view/update your settings:

Folder management

Creators can view recently created Folders by tapping Home on the navigation bar and tapping View All next to Recent videos. From there, you can edit your Folder’s settings by tapping on the three horizontal dots next to a folder and making adjustments from the settings menu that pops up:

You can also add a video to a folder by tapping on the three horizontal dots next to a video, and tapping the ‘Move to folder’ option, which will display a list of your Folders to choose from:

Teams on Mobile

Team owners and team members can now make changes to the videos they have permission to view on the iOS app.

Tap your profile icon in the upper right corner to find the team switcher. Open the team switcher to display the teams you’re a part of on Vimeo, then tap on the team account you wish to switch to.

Tapping a team’s name in the switcher will switch you out of your account and into the team account, displaying the videos you have permission to view and edit on the team account.

You can adjust your team members’ roles by first tapping on your avatar in the top right corner of your screen, then tapping on Manage Team. Read more about team member types and permissions.

In the Manage Team menu, tapping on (•••) to the right of a team member’s name will provide you with the option to change a team member’s role, or remove them from the team.

Review Notes

Team owners and team members can also leave time-coded review notes on videos via the app. After toggling to the comments tab on the clip, you’ll see an option to add a public comment or a review note.

Those with review access can reply to a time-coded note, share the review link, share the video file, save the video to their camera roll, and hide any resolved notes. You’ll also have the option to edit or delete your comment.

Creating Videos

You can create and edit videos on your mobile device in the Vimeo app for iOS. Learn how at ’How do I make a new video in the Vimeo mobile apps?’

Why do I need to log in to view certain videos?

To maintain a clear and safe viewing experience, content ratings are displayed prominently to viewers. This guide will walk you through how and where those ratings appear on Vimeo.

  • Why do I need to log in to watch a video?
  • How can I tell what rating a video has?

Why do I need to log in to watch a video?

  • If you are based in the UK or the EU, you may be prompted to log in to your Vimeo account to watch videos with a Mature content rating or videos that have not yet been rated. This also applies to watching live events on Vimeo.
  • You can also learn how to filter out mature contentfrom Vimeo search results.

How can I tell what rating a video has?

  • For videos with a Mature rating, you will see a Mature badge next to the video’s title.
  • For videos with an All Audiences rating, you won’t see a badge next to the video’s title.
  • For videos without a rating, you won’t see a badge unless it is your own video or a video on your team’s account.
  • Your own videos will have a Not Yet Rated badge.

Why is the Chromecast or Airplay button missing?

Video creators may choose to turn off the ability for their viewers to cast videos via Chromecast or AirPlay. If you are not seeing the options to cast on a video, this means the video owner has disabled them.

This feature can be customized in the video player settings.
